The sweet spot sits below maximum on purpose: max power is a trap, and the overcharge result is visibly worse than a good one.

props.name: onShot
props.description: Fires on release with the band and the value.

usageNotes: The release reads the needle's live motion value; a release always lands even if the pointer left the button.
The best marker stays pinned on the result bar — chasing your own best is the loop.
Reduced motion steps the needle on an interval while held, judging identically.

items.title: Reflex Light
items.tagline: Jump the start and it does not count.
items.description: Five lights arm one at a time, hold, and go out together — that blackout is the signal. Timing comes from event timestamps, never the wall clock, and a click before the lights drop is a jump start that voids the attempt. The penalty is what makes the wait tense.

props.name: delays
props.description: The hold before the lights drop, cycled in fixed order — reproducible, and learnable.

props.name: onReaction
props.description: Fires with the measured reaction.

usageNotes: Delays cycle a fixed table rather than rolling — a practised user can learn it, which is the fair price of reproducibility.
Every pending timer is cleared on a jump start, a reset, and unmount.
Reduced motion keeps the sequence — it is discrete state — and drops only the sparks and flashes.

items.title: Energy Pips
items.tagline: The wait is the mechanic. Say so.
items.description: The energy economy that decides when someone comes back: pips drain as they are spent and refill on a timer that only runs while the bank is below full. At zero the wait is stated plainly rather than hidden, because an honest countdown is the mechanic. Nothing here reads the wall clock — the countdown is an interval tick counter, so it renders the same on the server.

props.name: max / start
props.description: Bank size and opening balance.

props.name: refillSeconds
props.description: Seconds per regenerated pip.

usageNotes: The refill timer stops at full — a topped-up bank should not keep ticking.
The empty state names the wait instead of just disabling the button.
Reduced motion swaps pip states instantly and steps the refill bar.

items.title: Health Shield
items.tagline: The chip ghost shows what it cost.
items.description: A damage model built for legibility: shield absorbs first and shatters when it breaks, then health takes the rest — leaving a chip ghost at the old value that drains a beat later, so you can see exactly what the hit cost. Low health warms the fill and adds a pulse; healing refuses to overfill with a visible bounce at the cap.

props.name: max / start / shield
props.description: The two pools and the opening health.

props.name: hit
props.description: Damage per strike.

usageNotes: The lingering chip ghost is the single most important tell — without it a hit is just a smaller bar.
Overhealing is refused visibly; a silent cap teaches nothing.
Reduced motion snaps the bars and shows the ghost as a static beat.

items.title: Mana Orb
items.tagline: Two waves, never in step.
items.description: A glass orb of liquid mana whose surface actually moves: two wave layers at different periods, deliberately desynced, because a single sine reads as a machine and two read as liquid. Casting drops the level and sloshes it, an empty cast is refused as clearly as a successful one lands, and regen shimmers until full and then stops.

props.name: max / start / cost
props.description: The pool, its opening level, and the spell cost.

props.name: regenPerSecond
props.description: Refill rate, driven by a tick counter.

usageNotes: The desynced wave layers are the whole illusion — matching their periods kills it.
A full orb stops animating; an idle resource should not burn frames.
Reduced motion flattens the surface entirely and snaps the level.

items.title: Cooldown Dial
items.tagline: Four timers, one polyrhythm.
items.description: Four abilities with four different cooldowns, which is what gives an ability bar its polyrhythm: each casts, dims, and unwinds its own radial sweep back to ready, with a brief shared lockout after any cast so mashing gains nothing. The return to ready gets its own pop, because the wait is only worth it if the reward is felt.

props.name: abilities
props.description: Name, hotkey, and cooldown seconds per slot.

props.name: onCast
props.description: Fires per successful cast.

usageNotes: Q, W, E, and R cast from the keyboard when the group has focus.
Remaining time comes from an interval tick counter, never the wall clock.
Reduced motion shows a stepped numeral instead of an unwinding sweep.

items.title: Boss Meter
items.tagline: The pause is what makes it a phase.
items.description: A long fight made legible by its thresholds: the bar carries phase markers, and crossing one stops everything for a beat, stamps the numeral, warms the tint, and names what just changed. That pause is the device — without it a boss bar is just a slow health bar. The last phase enrages, and defeat shatters it.

props.name: max / hit
props.description: The pool and the damage per strike.

props.name: phases
props.description: Threshold percentages that trigger a transition.

usageNotes: The phase pause is deliberate dead time — it is what turns a threshold into an event.
Chip damage lingers here too, at boss scale, so a long fight still reads hit by hit.
Reduced motion keeps the tint step and stamp but drops the shudder, sweeps, and shatter.

items.title: Sticker Album
items.tagline: The gaps are the ask.
items.description: An album page whose empty slots do the asking: each collect flies a sticker to its place, presses it down at a slightly crooked angle, and solidifies the outline. Every fourth pull is a duplicate that slides off to the spares tray — a set you complete without ever pulling a double is not a collection, it is a checklist.

props.name: slots
props.description: Slots on the page (6–12).

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Fires when the page fills.

usageNotes: Sticker order is fixed, so the same page fills the same way for everyone.
Duplicates are deliberate: the spares tray is what makes the set feel collected rather than ticked off.
Reduced motion places stickers instantly and keeps the completion state.

items.title: Badge Case
items.tagline: Locked, but never unreadable.
items.description: A case of achievements where the locked ones still say what they are: a silhouette, a lock, and the hint that would earn it — because a hidden name teaches nothing about what to chase. One secret badge is the right number. Each unlock fills the medallion, flips the glyph, and prints the share of players who hold it.

props.name: badges
props.description: Name, hint, rarity share, and an optional secret flag.

props.name: unlocked
props.description: How many start earned.

usageNotes: Locked names and hints stay legible on purpose — the ask is the point of an achievement case.
Rarer badges get a warmer tint and a larger unlock reaction; the percentage is the social proof.
Reduced motion swaps badge states instantly and keeps the caption.

items.title: Passport Stamps
items.tagline: A perfectly aligned stamp looks printed.
items.description: A passport leaf that takes a stamp per destination: the head descends, the page shudders, the mark presses in a degree or two off true, and ink spreads at the edges. A filled page turns to a fresh one. Dates are pre-formatted strings and nothing reads a clock, so the page renders identically everywhere.

props.name: destinations
props.description: Name, a pre-formatted date string, and a stamp shape.

props.name: onPageComplete
props.description: Fires when a page fills and turns.

usageNotes: Stamps land deliberately imperfect — the slight misalignment is what makes them read as stamped.
Dates are strings in the data; the component never touches a Date object.
Reduced motion places marks at their final angle with no descent or page turn.

items.title: Set Complete
items.tagline: The fifth card changes everything.
items.description: Five cards and a bonus that stays locked until the last one lands. Empty frames show exactly what is missing, connectors draw between placed cards so the set visibly links up, and completion lights the chain, sheens every card, and breaks the lock off the bonus. Pulling a card back re-locks it just as clearly — the loss has to read or the set means nothing.

props.name: cards / bonus
props.description: The five slots and the reward the set grants.

props.name: start
props.description: How many begin placed.

usageNotes: Empty frames name the missing card; a set you cannot see the shape of is not a goal.
Breaking the set re-locks the bonus visibly — completion only matters if it can be lost.
Reduced motion fills frames instantly and swaps the bonus panel to active.

items.title: Pet Companion
items.tagline: It notices when you stop.
items.description: A companion that grows through four stages as your bond rises — and droops, curls up, and dims when it falls, because a pet that cannot be neglected is a toy rather than a companion. Feeding and playing restore it visibly, it blinks on its own, and the mood line always says plainly where you stand.

props.name: bond
props.description: Opening bond, 0 to 100, which drives the growth stage.

props.name: decayPerTick
props.description: Bond lost per idle tick.

usageNotes: Neglect is a designed state with its own poses — removing the decay removes the attachment.
Blinking is the cheapest aliveness cue in the component and worth every line of it.
Reduced motion swaps poses for feeding, playing, and stage-ups without bounces or sparks.

items.title: Journey Map
items.tagline: The road lights up behind you.
items.description: A winding campaign path where the road lights up behind you: the avatar travels an authored waypoint route while a dash-clipped overlay follows it exactly, so progress reads as ground covered rather than a bar filling. Each arrival pops its milestone, hands the pulse to the next, and names what was reached.

props.name: milestones
props.description: Label and hint per node; positions are authored, never measured.

props.name: at
props.description: Which milestone the avatar starts on.

usageNotes: Path geometry and node positions are fixed constants — identical on server and client.
The lit trail and the avatar share one duration so the road never leads or lags the traveller.
Reduced motion jumps the avatar and steps the trail to length.

items.title: Season Track
items.tagline: The window closes. That is the point.
items.description: A two-lane season pass with a closing window: free and premium rows across eight tiers, an unclaimed counter that nags, and a retroactive payout when premium unlocks — which is exactly why the pattern works, shown honestly. Ending the season expires everything unclaimed, in view, because the expiry is the whole point of a season.

props.name: tiers / perClick
props.description: Track length and progress per earn, at 100 per tier.

props.name: daysLeft
props.description: Shown in the header; a prop, never computed from a clock.

usageNotes: Unlocking premium pays out every passed tier at once — the retroactive drop is the mechanic, not a bug.
Expiry greys and strikes unclaimed rewards rather than quietly removing them.
The track scrolls inside its own container; the page never scrolls sideways.

items.title: Territory Grid
items.tagline: You can only grow from what you hold.
items.description: A board two sides expand across, where you may only claim tiles touching what you already hold — so the frontier, not the whole grid, is the decision. Claims ripple into their neighbours, surrounding an enemy tile captures it, and the opponent answers from a fixed sequence so the same board plays the same way for everyone.

props.name: cols / rows
props.description: Board size.

props.name: onCapture
props.description: Fires when a surround flips a tile.

usageNotes: Adjacency gating is the strategy — non-bordering neutrals are inert and look it.
The opponent replays a fixed sequence; a demo whose rival improvises cannot be reasoned about.
Reduced motion swaps tile colours instantly and keeps captures and captions.

items.title: Ladder Climb
items.tagline: Falling is faster than climbing.
items.description: A competitive ladder you can fall down, which is the only reason climbing it matters: promotions light the band and unfurl a banner, demotions dim it and say so plainly with no sparks and no ceremony. A demotion shield absorbs the first loss at the bottom of a division, so the fall reads as fair rather than arbitrary.

props.name: divisions
props.description: Bottom to top; six by default.

props.name: perWin / perLoss
props.description: Progress gained and lost per match.

usageNotes: Demotion is deliberately unglamorous — legible, but never celebrated.
The shield absorbs one loss at a division floor and regenerates after two wins.
Reduced motion jumps the marker and keeps both captions.

items.title: Checkpoint Run
items.tagline: Progress you cannot lose is a countdown.
items.description: A run measured in ground covered, with flags that plant as you pass them and a stumble that throws you back to the last one — quickly, and a little ugly, because losing ground should not look graceful. Progress that cannot be lost is not progress, it is a countdown; the best distance persists so you always have your own mark to beat.

props.name: checkpoints / segmentsPerLeg
props.description: Flags on the route and steps between them.

props.name: onCheckpoint / onFinish
props.description: Fires per flag planted, and at the line.

usageNotes: The stumble is faster than the crawl forward — asymmetry is what makes checkpoints valuable.
The best distance survives resets; chasing your own mark is the loop.
Reduced motion snaps the runner back with the caption and no tumble.

items.title: Crit Hit
items.tagline: A crush should not look like a graze.
items.description: Damage numbers that scale their weight with what they mean: a graze drifts, a hit rises, a crit punches in with a starburst and a shake, and a crush brings the whole card with it. Numbers fan out along a cycled vector table so a flurry stays readable instead of stacking into a smear. The tier order is fixed, so the same strikes always read the same.

props.name: tiers
props.description: Label, amount, and weight per tier; cycled in fixed order.

props.name: onCrit
props.description: Fires on the heavier tiers.

usageNotes: Outcomes cycle a fixed table — random crits make a component impossible to reason about or test.
The fan-out vector table is what keeps a fast flurry legible.
Reduced motion keeps tier differences in size, weight, and tint, and drops every arc and shake.

items.title: Streak Heat
items.tagline: Cooling is slower than heating.
items.description: Escalation you can feel: each multiplier tier warms the panel, grows the numeral, and adds one more ambient layer on top of the last — a pulse, then a shimmer, then a rotating glow, then heat haze. Breaking the streak cools everything down over a slower tween than it took to heat, because a loss should take its time.

props.name: thresholds
props.description: Streak counts at which the multiplier steps up.

props.name: onLevel
props.description: Fires on each new tier.

usageNotes: The ambient layers are cumulative, not swapped — that stacking is what reads as heat rather than a state change.
Colour, size, and weight carry the escalation on their own, which is why the reduced-motion fallback still works.
Reduced motion drops every ambient layer and keeps the ladder legible.

items.title: Perfect Stamp
items.tagline: Failure gets a thud, not a party.
items.description: The verdict, slammed onto the results card: it arrives fast and oversized, lands hard at a slight angle, throws a shockwave and dust, and shudders the card by an amount scaled to the grade. A perfect run earns a sweep and a glow. A failed one gets a dull thud and no celebration, because a results screen that congratulates failure teaches nothing.

props.name: grades
props.description: Label, tint, fleck count, and landing angle per grade.

props.name: onGrade
props.description: Fires with the stamped verdict.

usageNotes: Grades cycle a fixed order so the demo is reproducible and testable.
The stamp never lands perfectly straight — a true angle reads as printed rather than stamped.
Reduced motion places the verdict at rest with its tint and caption, and nothing else.

items.title: Impact Frame
items.tagline: The freeze is the feeling.
items.description: Hit-stop, demonstrated and measured: an impact freezes the scene for a set number of milliseconds, flashes, jolts within its own bounds, and prints the freeze duration so the effect can be studied rather than just felt. A compare toggle runs the same strike without the freeze, which is the fastest way to understand why it matters.

props.name: onImpact
props.description: Fires with the chosen intensity.

usageNotes: The jolt is contained inside the card — it never moves the page and cannot cause layout jank.
Reduced motion removes the freeze, flash, jolt, and lines entirely; there is no reduced-but-still-flashing middle ground.
The printed freeze duration makes this a teaching component as much as an effect.

items.title: XP Shower
items.tagline: The total climbs as they land.
items.description: Reward that arrives as objects: orbs burst from the source, hang for a beat, then stream to the counter on staggered arcs — and the total climbs in steps as each one lands, which is the entire reason to do this instead of animating a number. The big orbs are saved for last, because pacing is most of the payoff.

props.name: orbs
props.description: Orbs per claim (6–20).

props.name: onClaim
props.description: Fires with the batch total.

usageNotes: Each orb owns its own arrival, so overlapping claims keep counting correctly.
The hold before the flight is what makes the collection feel deliberate rather than instant.
Reduced motion ticks the counter once by the batch total and never renders an orb.

items.title: Avatar Forge
items.tagline: Only the changed layer moves.
items.description: A character maker where only the layer you changed moves — cycle a head, and the head pops while everything else holds, so the eye lands on the edit instead of hunting for it. A handle is derived from the current combination and rewrites itself as parts change, which is the small thing that turns a shape stack into someone. Saving stamps it into a roster of the last three busts.

props.name: onSave
props.description: Fires with the derived handle when a bust is saved.

usageNotes: Surprise me steps every slot by a fixed offset table — a randomiser nobody can reproduce makes bug reports impossible.
The handle is hashed from the slot indices, so the same avatar always carries the same name.
Reduced motion swaps parts instantly and keeps the handle, the roster, and the caption.

items.title: Guild Crest
items.tagline: The order is the ceremony.
items.description: Heraldry, assembled in order: the shield drops and settles, the field wipes across it, the charge stamps on with a ring, and the ribbon unfurls from the centre carrying the name. Each layer waits for the one before it, because a crest that arrives all at once is only an image — the sequence is the ceremony. Cycling a part re-runs that layer alone, and a mock blazon reads the whole device back in shorthand.

props.name: name
props.description: Guild name carried on the ribbon.

props.name: onStrike
props.description: Fires with the blazon once the crest finishes assembling.

usageNotes: Shape, field, charge, and colour come from fixed tables, so a given crest is always reproducible.
Colour changes ride CSS transitions rather than motion interpolation, which cannot cross token values.
Reduced motion presents the finished crest with its caption and swaps parts instantly.

items.title: Team Roster
items.tagline: Someone is always the slow one.
items.description: The lobby before the match, where the interesting state is always the person you are waiting on. Teammates ready themselves on a fixed schedule, one of them deliberately slow, one of them drifting away partway through — because readiness that ignores presence is a lie. When the last ring fills, the countdown runs and the rows pulse together.

props.name: members
props.description: Party members; one may be flagged as you and is pinned to the top.

props.name: onLaunch
props.description: Fires when the countdown reaches zero.

usageNotes: Teammate readiness runs off a fixed delay table, so the lobby behaves identically on every mount.
The slow teammate and the away drift are deliberate — a lobby where everyone is instantly ready teaches nothing.
Reduced motion keeps the countdown stepping on its timer and drops the pops, pulses, and sweep.

items.title: Duel Ready
items.tagline: The lean is the tell.
items.description: The face-off screen, which people remember better than the match. Two sides slide in from opposite edges, a divider wipes between them, and the versus mark stamps in the centre; locking in lights your frame and leans your fighter toward the middle, the physical tell that you are committed. When both sides are in, they lunge, the mark flares, and the count runs down to the word.

props.name: foeDelayMs
props.description: Fixed delay before the opponent locks in.

props.name: onFight
props.description: Fires when the countdown reaches zero.

usageNotes: The opponent answers on a fixed delay rather than a random one, so the sequence is testable.
Neither side can lock in twice; the button disables the moment it lands.
Reduced motion presents the panel assembled, steps the countdown on its timer, and drops every slide, lunge, and flare.

items.title: Emote Wheel
items.tagline: The centre is the way out.
items.description: Hold to bloom eight emotes out of the centre, sweep toward one, release to play it — and release near the middle to back out with nothing, because a wheel you cannot cancel is a trap. A cooldown unwinds on the trigger afterwards, which is not a limitation but the design that keeps the thing charming instead of turning it into a spam device.

props.name: emotes
props.description: Wedge labels; glyphs come from a fixed table by index.

props.name: cooldownMs
props.description: Trigger lockout after an emote plays.

props.name: onEmote
props.description: Fires with the played emote.

usageNotes: Wedge positions come from index maths, never measurement, so the wheel is correct on first paint.
Arrow keys move the highlight and the number row selects directly — a radial control still has to answer a keyboard.
Reduced motion opens the wheel already fanned, plays the emote at its end position, and steps the cooldown as a numeral.

items.title: Unlock Gate
items.tagline: A gate that never refuses is a door.
items.description: The feature that stayed greyed out for a week, finally opening: the requirement meter fills, the padlock lifts and falls away, the plate splits down the middle, and the blur drops off something that was genuinely there the whole time. Short of the threshold the plate refuses — a shake, a rattle, and a caption — because a gate that never says no has taught nobody anything.

props.name: requirement
props.description: Steps needed before the gate opens.

props.name: onUnlock
props.description: Fires once the plate clears.

usageNotes: What is revealed is a working panel with a real control, not a grey rectangle — the reveal only lands if something is behind it.
The refusal below the threshold is the design; it is what makes the opening mean anything.
Reduced motion removes the plate in one step and turns the refusal into a caption.

items.title: Prestige Reset
items.tagline: The pause before the star.
items.description: Trading everything you built for a mark that says you did it. The stats drain one row at a time, the level counts itself down, and then the whole panel goes quiet for a beat before the new star ignites — that held pause is the most important frame in the sequence. It confirms before it commits, which is not friction but the acknowledgement the ceremony runs on.

props.name: startLevel
props.description: The level a prestige trades away.

props.name: maxStars
props.description: Stars available before the button retires.

props.name: onPrestige
props.description: Fires with the new star count.

usageNotes: The two-step confirm is deliberate — a destructive ceremony with a one-click trigger is a bug report waiting to happen.
The countdown steps off an interval tick counter, never a clock, so it behaves identically everywhere.
Reduced motion swaps every value in one step and still requires the confirm.

items.title: Tier Upgrade
items.tagline: The reveal happens mid-flip.
items.description: Status made physical: a membership card that flips into its next self, where the new face only ever comes around mid-flip and is never visible early. Each rung changes the material, the perk, and the figure, because a flip that lands on the card you already had is the exact failure this component exists to avoid. Stepping back flips the other way, so the direction of travel reads.

props.name: holder
props.description: Name carried on the card.

props.name: startTier
props.description: Starting rung on the five-tier ladder.

props.name: onUpgrade
props.description: Fires with the tier just reached.

usageNotes: Sparks are held back for the top tier alone — spending them on every rung is what makes a ladder feel flat.
Both faces set backfaceVisibility, so the incoming tier cannot be read before the card turns.
Reduced motion swaps the card in place and sets the figure without rolling it.

items.title: Mission Board
items.tagline: Scarcity is what makes a choice a choice.
items.description: A board you take work FROM, which is a different instrument from a list of what you already hold: postings are pinned and unclaimed, the slots that hold them are few, and accepting one lifts it off its pin and carries it into a slot, leaving the hole behind so the board reads as depleted. With every slot full the board refuses — the card tugs against its pin and springs back.

props.name: slots
props.description: Active missions you may hold at once.

props.name: onTurnIn
props.description: Fires with the reward as a mission is turned in.

usageNotes: Pin angles and the refresh rotation come from fixed tables, so a board looks the same on every render.
The limited slots are the whole device — without them this is a quest log, and the catalog already has one.
Reduced motion moves cards in one step and turns the refusal into a caption.

items.title: Return Gift
items.tagline: Glad you are back, never guilt.
items.description: The loop reaching back out: a parcel waiting because you were gone, whose box visibly grows richer with the length of the absence, so the reward is legible before it is ever opened. The ribbon unties, the lid tips away, and the gifts rise one at a time with the best one held back for last — the order of a reveal is most of the reward. The greeting is glad you are back and never once mentions how long it took.

props.name: absenceOptions
props.description: Selectable absences; each carries the tier it unwraps.

props.name: onCollect
props.description: Fires with the collected total.

usageNotes: Gift contents come from a fixed per-tier table rather than a roll, so any tier can be demonstrated on demand.
The tone is a constraint, not decoration — a welcome-back that scolds is worse than no welcome at all.
Reduced motion presents the gifts in place at once and still rolls the collected total as a stepped figure.

items.title: Focus Rail
items.tagline: One panel is always open.
items.description: The primitive behind expanding galleries and team panels: a row of panels where the one under the pointer, or holding focus, grows on a spring while its siblings contract in place. Leaving the rail always restores an expanded panel, because a rail with nothing open reads as broken. Hover expands by default; a press mode waits for a click or Enter, and the keyboard roves either way.

props.name: items
props.description: Panels in order; each carries an id, a label, and optional detail content.

props.name: activeId
props.description: Controlled active panel; omit to let the rail manage it.

props.name: grow
props.description: Flex weight of the expanded panel.

props.name: expandOn
props.description: Whether hovering expands, or only a press.

usageNotes: Galleries and team sections compose this rather than re-deriving the flex spring.
Focus always expands the focused panel regardless of mode — keyboard intent is intent.
Reduced motion resizes panels instantly and swaps detail without fades.

items.title: Turn Modal
items.tagline: Two faces of one object.
items.description: A card that lifts, travels to the centre, and turns over on Y into a focus-trapped dialog — the flip and the travel are one motion, so the dialog face comes around mid-flight and is never visible early. Closing reverses the same path back to the card. Where morph-dialog reshapes the trigger into the dialog, this one turns it over, which is the right device when the card and the dialog are two faces of the same object.

props.name: front
props.description: The card face at rest.

props.name: title
props.description: Accessible name of the dialog face.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state; pair with onOpenChange.

usageNotes: Focus moves into the dialog once the flight lands and returns to the card on close.
Both faces hide their backface, so the dialog cannot be read before the turn passes ninety degrees.
Reduced motion drops the flight and the turn; the dialog fades in centred with the trap intact.

items.title: Elastic Type
items.tagline: Every letter its own spring.
items.description: Display text whose glyphs compress under the cursor and rebound when it leaves — each letter its own spring, so a word behaves like a row of rubber blocks. The rebound overshoot on the way back is the signature; without it the effect reads as a squash, not an elastic. Built for 404 numerals and one-word headlines.

props.name: text
props.description: The word or numeral to render.

props.name: radius
props.description: Pixel radius of the cursor's influence.

props.name: squash
props.description: Maximum horizontal compression at the cursor.

usageNotes: The text stays one accessible string; glyph spans are hidden from assistive tech.
Squash conserves volume — a letter gets taller as it gets narrower — which is what makes it read as material.
Reduced motion renders the text plainly with no deformation.

items.title: Echo Type
items.tagline: Closes like a deck.
items.description: Display text with echo layers stacked behind it that fan apart on hover and re-stack when the pointer leaves — fanning staggers outward from the lead, and closing reverses the stagger so the layers fold back like a deck. An always-on mode holds the fan open and breathes it. Built for 404 numerals and single-word headlines that need presence without a backdrop.

props.name: text
props.description: The word or numeral to render.

props.name: echoes
props.description: Echo layers behind the lead.

props.name: mode
props.description: Fan on hover and focus, or hold the fan open and breathe it.

usageNotes: Echoes inherit the text colour at falling opacity; nothing animates colour.
The wrapper is focusable, so a keyboard user fans it too.
Reduced motion renders the echoes at their fanned positions and holds still.

items.title: Band Type
items.tagline: Slipping, not leaning.
items.description: Display text sliced into horizontal bands that slip sideways under the cursor — the bands nearest the pointer travel furthest, and they alternate direction, which is what makes the word read as slipping rather than leaning. Leave, and the bands settle back top-down on a spring. Built for 404 numerals and one-word headlines.

props.name: text
props.description: The word or numeral to render.

props.name: bands
props.description: Horizontal slices.

props.name: slip
props.description: Maximum sideways travel in pixels at the cursor.

usageNotes: Bands are clipped copies of one word sized by a hidden reference, so they tile with no seams.
Touch behaves as a hover at the press point and settles on release.
Reduced motion renders the word whole and never slices it.

items.title: Vignette · Empty Drawer
items.tagline: Open, and nothing in it.
items.description: The illustration for an empty archive: a quiet isometric filing cabinet whose top drawer springs open on a loop to show there is nothing in it, and extends a little further under the pointer. Built from clipped faces rather than 3D transforms, so it holds in every browser, and it pauses the moment it scrolls out of view.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the scene; everything inside is decorative.

usageNotes: Seat it in an empty-state block through its art slot; the block keeps the copy honest and the vignette keeps it warm.
The loop pauses off-screen and when the tab is hidden, and rebases its clock on resume.
Reduced motion holds the drawer open with the empty tag visible.

items.title: Vignette · Search Sweep
items.tagline: The lines part for nothing.
items.description: The illustration for no results: a lens roams down a short stack of result lines, and the lines part as it passes — the parting is the picture of nothing being there — before a small zero settles at the end. Every element rides one clock of authored keyframes, so the scene cannot drift apart the way independently timed loops do.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the scene; everything inside is decorative.

usageNotes: Pairs with the no-matches empty state, which does the diagnosis while this does the mood.
Pauses off-screen and when the tab is hidden.
Reduced motion renders the final frame with the lines parted and the zero in place.

items.title: Vignette · Inbox Zero
items.tagline: The last one leaving.
items.description: The illustration for a cleared inbox: the flap opens, the last message lifts out and away, the badge counts down as each one leaves, and a check settles when it reads zero. The countdown is what makes the zero mean something — an envelope that is simply empty tells you nothing about the work that emptied it.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the scene; everything inside is decorative.

usageNotes: Pairs with the cleared-desk empty state.
The badge is state stepped on a tick counter aligned to the clock, so it pauses and resumes with the scene.
Reduced motion renders the closed envelope, the zero badge, and the check.

items.title: Vignette · Blank Board
items.tagline: The first card, carried across.
items.description: The illustration for a first run: three empty columns, one starter card, and a cursor that picks it up and carries it across the board, dropping it into the last column where a dashed slot fills to receive it. The cursor and the card share one set of keyframes, so they travel as one thing rather than two things pretending to.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the scene; everything inside is decorative.

usageNotes: Pairs with the first-light empty state.
Pauses off-screen and when the tab is hidden.
Reduced motion renders the card seated in the last column with the cursor gone.

items.title: Surface Paint
items.tagline: Real underneath, painted on top.
items.description: The stage every effect in this wing stands on: your interface renders real and interactive, the painter keeps a texture of it current, and an effect layer draws over it. Overlay mode keeps the DOM visible and draws only where the effect differs; replace mode holds the DOM at zero opacity — still in flow, still focusable, still in the accessibility tree — and shows the transformed texture in its place, with clicks passing straight through.

props.name: mode
props.description: Whether the DOM stays visible under the effect or is shown only through the texture.

props.name: effect
props.description: The effect layer, rendered above the painted root with pointer events off.

props.name: paint
props.description: Painter options: DPR cap, node budget, pseudo-element painting, focus ring, backdrop.

usageNotes: The DOM is never visibility-hidden: that drops it from assistive technology. Replace mode uses opacity, so focus, selection, and screen readers keep working.
A focus-visible ring is painted into the texture beneath the effect, so glass bends the ring like everything else.
Reduced motion in replace mode shows the real DOM and skips the canvas — show the real thing rather than freeze the fake one.

items.title: Crystal Lens
items.tagline: Optics over a live page.
items.description: A lens that follows the cursor and refracts the live interface like a crystal ball: the texture bends toward the centre, the edge disperses into colour fringes, and a touch of frost softens the rim. Hover a heading or a control and the lens zooms on it. The proving effect of the wing — the DOM stays real and clickable underneath while a shader does the optics.

props.name: radius
props.description: Lens radius in CSS pixels.

props.name: zoom / refraction / dispersion / frost
props.description: Magnification at the centre, bend strength, colour-fringe strength, and rim blur.

props.name: targets
props.description: A selector for elements the lens zooms on when hovered.

usageNotes: Everything under the lens is the real DOM: links click, fields focus, and the painted ring follows focus.
The optics are one fragment shader over the painted texture; the lens position is a spring on the wrapper's pointer, never the canvas.
Reduced motion shows the undistorted page with a still lens outline.

items.title: ASCII Lens
items.tagline: The page, set in type.
items.description: A soft lens that follows the cursor and redraws the live interface beneath it as characters — glyphs chosen by the shape of what they cover, not just its brightness, so an edge reads as a slash and a fill as a block. Outside the lens the page is itself; inside it, the page is type. The DOM stays real and clickable throughout.

props.name: radius / softness
props.description: Lens radius in CSS pixels and the feather of its edge.

props.name: cell / charset
props.description: Glyph cell size and the character ramp.

props.name: color / tint
props.description: Glyph colour and how far it replaces the page's own colour.

usageNotes: The glyph atlas is drawn once from the character ramp; the shader matches cells by luminance and edge direction.
Everything under the lens is the real DOM — links click and fields focus.
Reduced motion renders the whole surface as still glyphs with no lens motion.

items.title: Dither Lens
items.tagline: Retro, and exact about it.
items.description: A lens that pixelates the live interface into an ordered dither — Bayer, halftone, hatch, or dash — with a two-colour palette and a click that sends a degauss ripple through it. Retro on purpose and exact about it: the pattern is a fixed matrix, so the same page always dithers the same way.

props.name: radius / softness / pixelSize / levels
props.description: Lens size, edge feather, pixel size, and brightness quantisation.

props.name: pattern
props.description: The dither matrix.

props.name: darkColor / lightColor / colorize
props.description: The palette ends and how much of the page's own colour survives.

usageNotes: The dither matrix is a constant; nothing about the pattern is random.
A click fires a degauss ripple that fades on its own.
Reduced motion shows one dithered frame with no lens motion and no ripple.

items.title: Cipher Surface
items.tagline: Decoded where you look.
items.description: The interface renders as scrambled cipher glyphs until the cursor comes close, and decodes back into crisp, coloured UI behind a flickering wavefront. Idle glyphs reroll on a fixed cadence from a seeded table, so the scramble looks alive without ever being random. The real DOM is underneath the whole time.

props.name: radius / softness / edgeWidth
props.description: Decode radius, its feather, and the wavefront's thickness.

props.name: cell / charset / color
props.description: Glyph cell size, the cipher alphabet, and its colour.

props.name: scramble / scrambleSpeed
props.description: Fraction of idle glyphs rerolling, and how often.

usageNotes: Rerolls come from a seeded sequence keyed by cell, so a page decodes the same way every visit.
Passthrough lets a little of the real UI show through the cipher so structure still reads.
Reduced motion shows the surface fully decoded with no wavefront.

items.title: Scanner Lens
items.tagline: Instrumentation, not optics.
items.description: A scanner that follows the cursor and magnifies the live interface inside a HUD reticle — ring, crosshair, ticks, corner brackets, and a mono readout of what it is over — with clicks that send a ripple bending across the page. Where the crystal lens is optics, this one is instrumentation.

props.name: size / zoom / follow
props.description: Lens radius, magnification, and how tightly it tracks the pointer.

props.name: ring / crosshair / ticks / brackets / readout
props.description: Which HUD elements draw.

props.name: ripples / rippleSpeed / rippleBend
props.description: Click ripples and their travel and bend.

usageNotes: The readout names the element under the reticle from the real DOM, not from the texture.
Ripples are a ring of bend travelling outward; they never move the DOM.
Reduced motion snaps the reticle to the pointer and disables ripples.

items.title: Dust Reveal
items.tagline: It settles where you look.
items.description: The interface renders as fine grey dust — grains wandering from their home pixels, the brightest content scattering furthest — and coalesces into crisp, coloured UI where the cursor comes near, with a chromatic edge at the reveal. Idle grains drift on a seeded field, so the dust breathes without a single random number.

props.name: radius / softness / smoothing
props.description: Reveal radius, its feather, and how damped the cursor following is.

props.name: size / scatter / drift
props.description: Grain size, wander distance, and idle shimmer speed.

props.name: aberration / bend / fade
props.description: Chromatic edge, smear at the reveal edge, and grain contrast.

usageNotes: Grain offsets come from a seeded noise field keyed by pixel, so the dust is deterministic.
Pixels near the background colour are left alone; only content becomes dust.
Reduced motion renders the surface fully settled and crisp.

items.title: Pond Glass
items.tagline: Click, and the page ripples.
items.description: The interface under still water. A click drops a stone: rings spread across the page, refracting and highlighting everything they cross, then settle. The waves are a real height-field simulation on the GPU with a byte-precision fallback, so it runs where half-float buffers are missing, and the page beneath stays clickable.

props.name: refraction / highlight
props.description: How far a wave bends the view, in pixels, and the strength of its specular sheen.

props.name: damping / speed / settle
props.description: How quickly rings fade, how fast they travel, and how long the loop runs after the last drop.

props.name: dropRadius / dropStrength / hoverDrops
props.description: The stone: its size, its force, and whether moving the pointer drips as well.

usageNotes: The simulation runs at a fraction of the canvas resolution and stops on its own once the water is still.
Clicks reach the real DOM underneath — a button under the water still works.
Reduced motion shows the real, unrippled DOM.

items.title: Rain Glass
items.tagline: Wipe the pane to see.
items.description: Rain on a window, with the interface behind it. Droplets bead on the pane and run in trails that bend the view, a haze softens what they do not cover, and the cursor wipes a clear patch that fogs back over. Every droplet is seeded from its cell, so the same pane always rains the same way.

props.name: density / size / speed
props.description: How many droplets, how large, and how fast the running ones travel.

props.name: refraction / blur / fog
props.description: How far a droplet bends the view, how soft the un-wiped pane is, and how heavy the haze.

props.name: wipeRadius / refog
props.description: The clear patch the cursor leaves and how many seconds it takes to fog back.

usageNotes: Droplets and trails are procedural in the shader; nothing is random and nothing is stored.
The wipe is the last few pointer positions, aged in the shader, so it needs no extra texture.
Reduced motion shows the real, dry DOM.

items.title: Ice Pane
items.tagline: It melts where you rest.
items.description: Frost across the interface that melts where the cursor rests and creeps back when it leaves. The frost is a crystalline field that blurs and refracts the view with a cold tint and a few glints; the melt is a persistent map that the pointer warms and time refreezes, with a wet rim at the boundary. The DOM stays live under the ice.

props.name: frost / refraction / blur
props.description: How much of the pane starts frozen, how far the crystals bend the view, and how soft it is.

props.name: melt / meltSpeed / refreeze
props.description: The warm radius around the pointer, how fast it clears, and how fast the frost returns per second.

props.name: color / tint / sparkle
props.description: The cold cast and how strong it is, and the glints in the crystals.

usageNotes: The melt map is a small canvas, warmed by the pointer and faded every frame; the loop stops once the pane has refrozen.
Clicks reach the real DOM through the frost.
Reduced motion shows the real, clear DOM.

items.title: Warp Grid
items.tagline: Move fast and it shears.
items.description: The interface as a grid of cells on springs. Move slowly and nothing happens; move fast and the cells you pass shear in the direction of travel, edges splitting into colour, then spring back into place. The field is simulated on the CPU at grid resolution and read by the shader as a texture, so it costs almost nothing.

props.name: cols / rows / lines
props.description: The grid, and the opacity of the cell lines drawn with it.

props.name: strength / radius / maxShift
props.description: How hard pointer velocity pushes, how far its influence reaches, and the largest shift a cell may take.

props.name: stiffness / damping / aberration
props.description: The springs cells return on, and how far the colour channels split while sheared.

usageNotes: Push comes from pointer velocity between frames, never from position alone — a slow sweep leaves the page still.
The loop runs only while any cell has energy left.
Reduced motion shows the real, unwarped DOM.

items.title: Droplet Cursor
items.tagline: Liquid, behind the cursor.
items.description: A chain of droplets that trails the cursor and refracts the interface behind it. Each drop follows the one ahead, shrinking along the chain, and the drops merge as one liquid surface where they touch; light bends through them, catches on a highlight, and tints the rim. Draws only where the drops are, so the page is itself everywhere else.

props.name: count / size / taper
props.description: How many drops, the lead drop's radius, and how much each successive drop shrinks.

props.name: follow
props.description: How tightly each drop tracks the one ahead — lower is more liquid.

props.name: refraction / dispersion / color / tint / highlight
props.description: How far the drops bend the view, the colour split at their edges, and the rim tint and specular strength.

usageNotes: Drops are a metaball field in one fragment shader; merging is what the field does, not a special case.
The loop stops once the chain has caught up with the cursor.
Reduced motion shows a single still drop at the pointer with no trail.

items.title: Shield Field
items.tagline: Click, and it rings.
items.description: A faint lattice over the interface that rings out when clicked: a shockwave travels from the point of impact, lighting each cell as it passes and bending the page a little under the front, then fades. Cells near the pointer glow softly. Draws only the lattice and the waves, so the page is itself everywhere else.

props.name: cell / lattice / lineOpacity
props.description: The lattice geometry and how visible it is at rest.

props.name: waveSpeed / waveWidth / waveLife / maxWaves
props.description: How fast a shockwave travels in px/s, how thick its front is, how long it lives, and how many may run at once.

props.name: color / glow / refraction / hover
props.description: The field colour, the brightness of a lit cell, how far the front bends the page, and the pointer's glow radius.

usageNotes: Waves are ages in the shader, driven by a frame tick; the loop stops once the last one has faded.
Clicks reach the real DOM under the field — the button you ping still fires.
Reduced motion draws the still lattice with no waves and no pointer glow.

items.title: Signal Glitch
items.tagline: It tears, and comes back.
items.description: The interface as a weak signal. Bursts of interference tear it into shifted bands, split its colour channels, and speckle it with noise, then it reassembles — clean between bursts. The bursts are scheduled from a seeded clock, so the pattern is deterministic; a click forces one. Underneath, the page is live the whole time.

props.name: rate / duration / intensity
props.description: How often bursts come per second, how long each lasts, and how violent they are.

props.name: bands / shift / split
props.description: How many horizontal bands tear, how far they shift in px, and the colour-channel offset.

props.name: scanlines / noise / clickBurst
props.description: The resting scanline weight, the speckle during a burst, and whether a click forces one.

usageNotes: Burst timing comes from a hash of the frame clock, never from a random number.
Between bursts the shader passes the texture through untouched, so a still page costs almost nothing.
Reduced motion shows the real, clean DOM.

items.title: Tape Wear
items.tagline: Played back, worn.
items.description: The interface played back from a worn cassette: chroma bleeding sideways, a faint vertical jitter, a tracking band that drifts up the frame tearing what it crosses, dropout streaks, scanlines, and a soft vignette. Every flaw is seeded from the frame clock and the pixel, so the wear is the same on every play.

props.name: wear / bleed / jitter
props.description: Overall degradation, how far chroma bleeds in px, and the vertical shake.

props.name: tracking / trackingSpeed / dropouts
props.description: The tracking band's strength, how fast it climbs the frame, and how many dropout streaks appear.

props.name: scanlines / vignette / tint
props.description: Scanline weight, edge darkening, and the warm cast.

usageNotes: The tracking band is a function of the frame clock; the loop runs while the surface is on screen.
Clicks reach the real DOM through the playback.
Reduced motion shows the real, clean DOM.

items.title: Laser Print
items.tagline: Printed in, as you scroll.
items.description: A beam that prints the interface in as you scroll. Above the line the page is set; at the line a hot glow, sparks, and a heat shimmer; below it, blank stock. Progress follows the surface's position in the viewport by default, plays once on entry with `mode="auto"`, or takes a `progress` value directly.

props.name: mode / progress / duration
props.description: What drives the beam: the viewport, a one-shot play of `duration` seconds, or the `progress` prop.

props.name: color / beamWidth / glow / sparks
props.description: The beam's colour, thickness, glow radius, and spark density.

props.name: shimmer / scorch / direction
props.description: The heat band below the line, the faint burn above it, and which way the print runs.

usageNotes: Scroll progress is read from the host's bounding box on passive scroll events; the loop runs only while the beam is inside the surface.
The unprinted part still holds the real DOM — a link below the beam is clickable.
Reduced motion shows the real DOM fully printed.

items.title: Wet Canvas
items.tagline: Drag the paint.
items.description: The interface as wet paint on a woven ground. A weave and a paper grain sit under the page with their own lighting; moving the pointer drags the paint along the direction of travel, raising glossy ridges that catch the light and slowly dry back flat. The drag lives in a small map warmed by the pointer, so the shader stays one pass.

props.name: weave / grain / light
props.description: The woven ground's relief, the paper speckle, and the light angle in degrees.

props.name: brush / strength / dry
props.description: The smear's radius, how far it drags the paint in px, and how many seconds it takes to dry flat.

props.name: gloss / ridge
props.description: The specular sheen of wet paint and how strongly the smear raises ridges.

usageNotes: Smear direction is the pointer's velocity, so a slow drag pulls gently and a flick pulls hard.
Clicks reach the real DOM through the paint.
Reduced motion shows the real, dry DOM.

items.title: Bonfire Edge
items.tagline: Warm at the edge.
items.description: Fire along the bottom edge of the interface: flames that rise and lick, sparks that climb and die, and a heat shimmer that bends the page just above them. The flames lean with the pointer and grow where it comes near. Draws only the fire and the shimmer, so the rest of the page is itself.

props.name: height / intensity / speed
props.description: How tall the flames reach in px, how fierce, and how fast they move.

props.name: color / sparks / shimmer
props.description: The base colour of the fire, the spark density, and how far the heat bends the page above it.

props.name: wind / heat / edge
props.description: How far the flames lean with the pointer, how much they grow under it, and which edge burns.

usageNotes: Flames, sparks, and shimmer are one fragment shader on the frame clock; nothing is random.
The page under the shimmer is the real DOM — a control near the edge still works.
Reduced motion draws one still frame of the fire with no shimmer.

items.title: Flame Border
items.tagline: Wrapped in fire.
items.description: A ring of fire around an element, following its rounded corners. Flames lick inward from every edge with a warm glow on the interior; the middle of the page stays untouched. The border reads the host's corner radius, so it fits whatever shape it wraps.

props.name: width / intensity / speed
props.description: How far the flames reach inward in px, how fierce, and how fast.

props.name: color / glow
props.description: The fire's base colour and the warmth cast onto the interior.

props.name: corner
props.description: Corner radius override in px; by default the host's computed radius.

usageNotes: The flame band is a signed distance to the rounded rectangle, so corners burn as evenly as edges.
Draws only the border and the glow; the page inside is the real DOM.
Reduced motion draws one still ring of fire.

items.title: Fluid Wash
items.tagline: Stir it.
items.description: The interface under a sheet of fluid that the pointer stirs. A real velocity field on the GPU — advected, pressure-solved, dissipating — bends the page where it flows and washes a tint of colour along the current. Runs in half-float where the browser offers it and drops to byte buffers with fewer iterations where it does not.

props.name: resolution / pressureIterations
props.description: The simulation grid as a fraction of the canvas, and the pressure solver's iterations (halved on byte buffers).

props.name: viscosity / dissipation / force / splatRadius
props.description: How velocity persists, how the tint fades, how hard the pointer pushes, and how wide its stroke is.

props.name: refraction / color / tint
props.description: How far the flow bends the page, the colour it carries, and how strongly.

usageNotes: The loop runs while the field has energy and stops once the fluid is still.
Clicks reach the real DOM through the fluid.
Reduced motion shows the real, still DOM.

items.title: Glyph Sweep
items.tagline: Set the next one in type.
items.description: A transition between panels: change the index and a band of glyphs sweeps across the surface, dissolving the old panel into characters at its leading edge and setting the new one in crisp behind it. Both panels are painted textures, so the sweep is one shader pass; between sweeps the surface is the live panel.

props.name: index / children
props.description: Which panel shows; the children are the panels.

props.name: direction / duration / band
props.description: Which way the sweep travels, how long it takes in seconds, and how wide the glyph band is in px.

props.name: cell / charset / color
props.description: Glyph cell size, the character ramp, and the glyph colour.

usageNotes: The outgoing panel's texture is retained at the moment the index changes, so the sweep never waits on a paint.
Between sweeps the loop is off and the canvas shows the live panel.
Reduced motion switches panels instantly with the real DOM visible.

items.title: Type Rain
items.tagline: Lit by the rain.
items.description: Streams of glyphs fall over the interface and light it as they pass: the page is held dim, and where a stream crosses, the real colour and type show through around a bright head glyph. Every stream is seeded by its column, so the rain falls the same way each visit. The pointer parts the streams.

props.name: cell / density / speed / length
props.description: Glyph cell size, how many columns rain, how fast they fall, and how long each stream is in cells.

props.name: color / glow / dim
props.description: The glyph colour, the head's brightness, and how far the page is dimmed between streams.

props.name: charset / repel
props.description: The characters that fall, and the radius the pointer clears.

usageNotes: Streams are functions of column, time, and a seed; nothing is stored between frames.
The dim page is the real DOM underneath; its controls still work.
Reduced motion shows the real, undimmed DOM.

items.title: Sand Scroll
items.tagline: It settles as you scroll.
items.description: The interface dissolves into sand below a line and reassembles as you scroll. Grains stream down and drift from their home pixels, further the deeper they sit below the line, and settle back into crisp type as the line passes. Progress follows the surface's place in the viewport, plays once, or takes a value directly.

props.name: mode / progress / duration
props.description: What drives the line: the viewport, a one-shot play, or the progress prop.

props.name: grain / scatter / fall
props.description: Grain size in px, how far grains drift sideways, and how fast they stream down.

props.name: softness / fade / direction
props.description: How wide the settling band is, how much loose sand fades, and which way the line runs.

usageNotes: Grain offsets come from a seeded field keyed by pixel and time; nothing is stored between frames.
The loose part still holds the real DOM underneath.
Reduced motion shows the real DOM fully settled.

items.title: Cloth Drape
items.tagline: Hung like cloth.
items.description: The interface as a hanging cloth. A grid mesh carries the painted page; wind rolls slow waves through it, the cursor pushes a dent that springs back, and the shading follows the folds. The mesh is a few thousand vertices, so the drape costs almost nothing.

props.name: cols / rows
props.description: The mesh resolution.

props.name: wind / speed / amplitude
props.description: How much the cloth moves at rest, how fast the waves travel, and how deep they are in px.

props.name: push / radius / shading
props.description: How deep the cursor dents the cloth, how wide the dent is, and how strongly folds are lit.

usageNotes: Displacement happens in the vertex shader; the fragment shader only samples and shades.
Clicks reach the real DOM through the cloth.
Reduced motion shows the real, flat DOM.

items.title: Cube Fold
items.tagline: Folds as it passes.
items.description: The interface folds over cube edges as it scrolls. The top and bottom bands of the page hinge away in perspective as the surface enters and leaves the viewport, meeting flat in the middle of the scroll. One mesh, two hinges, real perspective.

props.name: mode / progress
props.description: What drives the fold: the viewport, or the progress prop.

props.name: band / angle / perspective
props.description: How tall each folding band is as a fraction of the height, the largest fold angle in degrees, and the camera distance.

props.name: shading
props.description: How much a folded face darkens.

usageNotes: Progress is read from the host's bounding box on passive scroll events; frames are requested only when it changes.
The folded bands still hold the real DOM underneath.
Reduced motion shows the real, flat DOM.

items.title: Tile Wave
items.tagline: Tiles, on springs.
items.description: The interface cut into tiles that tilt and lift as the cursor passes, a wave rolling out from the pointer and settling on springs. Each tile is a quad on a grid mesh with its own centre, so it rotates about itself; gaps between tiles show the ground behind. A click sends a ring through the whole grid.

props.name: cols / rows / gap
props.description: The tile grid and the gap between tiles in px.

props.name: tilt / lift / radius
props.description: The largest tilt in degrees, the largest lift in px, and how far the cursor's influence reaches.

props.name: stiffness / damping / ring
props.description: The springs tiles settle on, and the strength of the click ring.

usageNotes: Tilt and lift are simulated per tile on the CPU and read by the vertex shader from a small texture.
Clicks reach the real DOM through the tiles.
Reduced motion shows the real, flat DOM.

items.title: Hex Floor
items.tagline: Flat where you look.
items.description: The interface laid over a floor of hexagonal prisms seen from a slight angle. Each prism stands at a seeded height and breathes with a slow wave; near the cursor they flatten, so the page reads clearly wherever you look and stands in relief everywhere else.

props.name: cell / height / idle
props.description: Hex size in px, the largest prism height in px, and how much the floor breathes at rest.

props.name: radius / softness
props.description: How far around the cursor the floor flattens, and how gradually.

props.name: tilt / shading
props.description: The viewing angle in degrees and how strongly prism faces are shaded.

usageNotes: Extrusion is a parallax offset per hex in one fragment shader; there is no mesh.
Clicks reach the real DOM through the floor.
Reduced motion shows the real, flat DOM.

items.title: Glass Shards
items.tagline: Broken, and beautiful.
items.description: The interface as a pane broken into shards. Each shard tilts toward the cursor and refracts what is behind it a little differently from its neighbours, with a bright edge along every crack; near the pointer, shards lift and part, and the ground shows through the gaps. The fracture is a seeded cell pattern, so the pane breaks the same way every time.

props.name: shards / seed
props.description: How many shards the pane breaks into, and which break.

props.name: tilt / lift / radius
props.description: How far a shard tilts toward the cursor in degrees, how far the nearest lift in px, and how far the cursor reaches.

props.name: refraction / edge / color
props.description: How much a tilted shard bends the page, the brightness of the cracks, and their colour.

usageNotes: Shards settle on springs; the loop stops once every shard is at rest.
Clicks reach the real DOM through the pane.
Reduced motion shows the real, whole DOM.

items.title: ASCII Figure
items.tagline: A figure, set in type.
items.description: A 3D figure set in type: the lit render becomes a grid of glyphs chosen by luminance, in one colour, floating and rocking, and yours to orbit by dragging. A torus knot by default; any GLB, glTF, SVG, or image by URL. The 3D runtime loads lazily after mount.

props.name: preset / src / scale
props.description: A built-in shape, or a GLB, glTF, SVG, or image URL sniffed by its bytes, and how large it sits.

props.name: orbit / idle
props.description: Drag to orbit, and the resting float and rock.

props.name: cell / charset / color
props.description: Glyph cell size, the character ramp, and the ink colour.

usageNotes: The 3D runtime loads after mount, on demand; no page pays for it until a figure renders.
Presets ship no asset; a URL source is fetched and sniffed, never trusted by extension.
Reduced motion renders one still frame at the default camera with orbit and idle off.

items.title: Dither Figure
items.tagline: Lit, then dithered.
items.description: A 3D figure in ordered dither: the lit render quantised through a Bayer matrix into a two-colour palette at a chosen pixel size, floating and rocking, yours to orbit. Retro on purpose and exact about it. The 3D runtime loads lazily after mount.

props.name: preset / src / scale
props.description: A built-in shape, or a GLB, glTF, SVG, or image URL sniffed by its bytes, and how large it sits.

props.name: orbit / idle
props.description: Drag to orbit, and the resting float and rock.

props.name: pixelSize / levels / darkColor / lightColor
props.description: The dither cell, its brightness steps, and the palette ends.

usageNotes: The 3D runtime loads after mount, on demand; no page pays for it until a figure renders.
The matrix is fixed; the same figure always dithers the same way.
Reduced motion renders one still frame at the default camera with orbit and idle off.

items.title: Ink Figure
items.tagline: Drawn, not rendered.
items.description: A 3D figure drawn in ink: silhouette and crease lines from the depth and normal buffers, hatching that darkens with shade, on paper. Floats and rocks, yours to orbit. The 3D runtime loads lazily after mount.

props.name: preset / src / scale
props.description: A built-in shape, or a GLB, glTF, SVG, or image URL sniffed by its bytes, and how large it sits.

props.name: orbit / idle
props.description: Drag to orbit, and the resting float and rock.

props.name: lineWeight / hatch / color / paper
props.description: Outline thickness, hatch density, ink colour, and the paper colour.

usageNotes: The 3D runtime loads after mount, on demand; no page pays for it until a figure renders.
Lines come from depth and normal discontinuities, so they hold at any angle.
Reduced motion renders one still frame at the default camera with orbit and idle off.

items.title: Glass Figure
items.tagline: Bends what is behind it.
items.description: A 3D figure in glass: transmission, refraction, and dispersion through a physical material over a studio backdrop, so the figure bends what sits behind it. Floats and rocks, yours to orbit. The 3D runtime loads lazily after mount.

props.name: preset / src / scale
props.description: A built-in shape, or a GLB, glTF, SVG, or image URL sniffed by its bytes, and how large it sits.

props.name: orbit / idle
props.description: Drag to orbit, and the resting float and rock.

props.name: ior / dispersion / thickness / tint
props.description: Refractive index, colour split, apparent thickness, and the glass tint.

usageNotes: The 3D runtime loads after mount, on demand; no page pays for it until a figure renders.
A backdrop with type behind the figure makes the refraction legible.
Reduced motion renders one still frame at the default camera with orbit and idle off.

items.title: Particle Figure
items.tagline: Held together, barely.
items.description: A 3D figure as points on its surface: thousands of particles that hold the shape, scatter from the cursor, swirl, and spring home. Floats and rocks, yours to orbit. The 3D runtime loads lazily after mount.

props.name: preset / src / scale
props.description: A built-in shape, or a GLB, glTF, SVG, or image URL sniffed by its bytes, and how large it sits.

props.name: orbit / idle
props.description: Drag to orbit, and the resting float and rock.

props.name: count / size / color
props.description: How many points sample the surface, their size, and their colour.

props.name: push / swirl / spring
props.description: How far the cursor scatters them, the swirl around it, and how fast they return.

usageNotes: The 3D runtime loads after mount, on demand; no page pays for it until a figure renders.
Points are sampled from the surface once, seeded, so the figure is the same on every visit.
Reduced motion renders one still frame at the default camera with orbit and idle off.

items.title: Liquid Figure
items.tagline: Seen through water.
items.description: A 3D figure seen through liquid: the render is distorted by a flowing field that the cursor stirs, with a specular sheen on the ripples. Floats and rocks, yours to orbit. The 3D runtime loads lazily after mount.

props.name: preset / src / scale
props.description: A built-in shape, or a GLB, glTF, SVG, or image URL sniffed by its bytes, and how large it sits.

props.name: orbit / idle
props.description: Drag to orbit, and the resting float and rock.

props.name: strength / speed / stir / sheen
props.description: How far the liquid bends the render, how fast it flows, how hard the cursor stirs it, and the highlight strength.

usageNotes: The 3D runtime loads after mount, on demand; no page pays for it until a figure renders.
The distortion field is procedural; nothing is stored between frames.
Reduced motion renders one still frame at the default camera with orbit and idle off.

items.title: Thermal Lens
items.tagline: Warm where the page is dense.
items.description: A lens that reads the interface as heat: luminance becomes an ironbow palette — black through purple, red, orange, to white-hot — with a soft bloom on the hottest type and a cold blue ground, inside a feathered circle that follows the cursor. Outside it the page is itself.

props.name: radius / softness
props.description: Lens radius in CSS px and the feather of its edge.

props.name: palette
props.description: The heat ramp.

props.name: bloom / contrast / invert
props.description: Glow on the hottest tones, tone contrast, and whether ink or ground reads as hot.

usageNotes: The palette is a fixed ramp evaluated per pixel; nothing is stored between frames.
The DOM under the lens stays real — a link under the heat still clicks.
Reduced motion draws one still lens outline with no motion.

items.title: Negative Lens
items.tagline: The page, in negative.
items.description: An x-ray lens: inside the circle the interface inverts to a negative with bone-white edges lifted from the texture, a faint radiograph grain, and a soft blue cast; the rest of the page stays positive. The edges come from the painted texture, so type reads as structure rather than as a smear.

props.name: radius / softness
props.description: Lens radius in CSS px and the feather of its edge.

props.name: edge / cast / grain
props.description: Edge lift strength, the cast colour, and radiograph grain.

props.name: targets / targetZoom
props.description: A selector for elements the lens zooms on when hovered.

usageNotes: Edges are a Sobel over the texture's luminance, drawn additively over the inverted page.
The DOM under the lens stays real.
Reduced motion draws one still lens outline.

items.title: Blueprint Lens
items.tagline: Drafted, not printed.
items.description: A lens that turns the interface into a cyanotype blueprint: a Prussian-blue ground with the page's edges drawn as fine white lines, a drafting grid behind, and dimension ticks along the rim. Inside the circle the page is a drawing of itself; outside it is the page.

props.name: radius / softness
props.description: Lens radius in CSS px and the feather of its edge.

props.name: grid / lineWeight
props.description: Drafting grid pitch in px, and the line weight.

props.name: blue / paper
props.description: The ground colour and the line colour.

usageNotes: Lines are edges of the painted texture, so headings, borders, and seals all draft cleanly.
The DOM under the lens stays real.
Reduced motion draws one still lens outline.

items.title: Halftone Lens
items.tagline: Four screens, one rosette.
items.description: A lens that prints the interface as a four-colour halftone: cyan, magenta, yellow, and black dot screens at their classic angles, so overlaps form the rosette you see in a magazine under a loupe. Dot size follows each channel's density; the paper shows between dots.

props.name: radius / softness
props.description: Lens radius in CSS px and the feather of its edge.

props.name: pitch / gain
props.description: Dot screen pitch in px and dot gain.

props.name: angles / paper
props.description: The four screen angles and the paper colour.

usageNotes: Each channel is a rotated dot grid; dot radius is the channel's coverage at the cell centre.
The DOM under the lens stays real.
Reduced motion draws one still lens outline.

items.title: Nightscope Lens
items.tagline: Green, grainy, and awake.
items.description: A night-vision lens: inside the circle the interface is amplified into a green phosphor image with intensifier noise, a soft bloom on bright type, a faint scanline, and a dark vignette at the rim; a mono readout on the rim shows the pointer position. Outside it, daylight.

props.name: radius / softness
props.description: Lens radius in CSS px and the feather of its edge.

props.name: gain / noise / bloom
props.description: Amplification, intensifier noise, and glow on bright tones.

props.name: phosphor / readout
props.description: The phosphor colour and whether the rim readout draws.

usageNotes: Noise is a hash of the pixel and the frame clock; the image is the texture's luminance amplified into the phosphor.
The DOM under the lens stays real.
Reduced motion draws one still lens with no noise.

items.title: Comic Lens
items.tagline: Inked, dotted, done.
items.description: A lens that redraws the interface as a comic panel: colours posterised to a few flat tones, black ink outlines lifted from the texture's edges, and Ben-Day dots in the mid tones. Inside the circle the page is drawn; outside it is the page.

props.name: radius / softness
props.description: Lens radius in CSS px and the feather of its edge.

props.name: levels / outline / dots
props.description: Posterise steps, outline weight in px, and Ben-Day dot density.

props.name: ink
props.description: The outline colour.

usageNotes: Outlines are edges of the painted texture, so type and borders ink cleanly.
The DOM under the lens stays real.
Reduced motion draws one still lens outline.

items.title: Kaleido Lens
items.tagline: Six of everything.
items.description: A kaleidoscope on the cursor: inside the circle the interface is mirrored into six wedges around the pointer, rotating slowly, so a heading becomes a mandala of itself. The mirror geometry is exact, so seams meet without a gap.

props.name: radius / softness
props.description: Lens radius in CSS px and the feather of its edge.

props.name: wedges / spin
props.description: How many mirrored wedges and how fast they turn in rad/s.

props.name: zoom
props.description: Magnification of the source wedge.

usageNotes: The lens samples one wedge of the texture and mirrors it around the pointer; the DOM under it stays real.
Spin comes from the frame clock and stops under reduced motion.
Reduced motion draws one still kaleidoscope.

items.title: Pixel Sort Lens
items.tagline: Sorted by light.
items.description: A lens that pixel-sorts the interface: within the circle, runs of pixels along the sort axis are dragged into luminance order, so type streaks into bright-to-dark ribbons. The streak length follows the local contrast, and the sort is a deterministic approximation done in one pass.

props.name: radius / softness
props.description: Lens radius in CSS px and the feather of its edge.

props.name: axis / length / threshold
props.description: Sort direction, the longest streak in px, and the luminance threshold that starts a run.

usageNotes: The streaks are an approximation: each pixel takes the extreme of a window along the axis weighted by its position, which reads as sorting at a fraction of the cost.
The DOM under the lens stays real.
Reduced motion draws one still lens outline.

items.title: Reading Ruler
items.tagline: One line at a time.
items.description: A reading aid: a horizontal band follows the cursor and keeps the current line crisp and warm while everything above and below softens and dims. The band snaps to the line height under the pointer, read from the real DOM, so it always frames a whole line of type.

props.name: height / softness
props.description: Band height in px (auto from the line under the pointer when 0) and the feather above and below.

props.name: dim / blur / tint
props.description: How much the rest dims, how much it softens, and the band's warm tint.

props.name: snap
props.description: Snap the band to the line box under the pointer.

usageNotes: The band's height and position come from the element under the pointer via elementFromPoint, so it frames real lines.
The rest of the page stays live under the veil.
Reduced motion keeps the band still at the pointer with no spring.

items.title: Braille Lens
items.tagline: Raised, cell by cell.
items.description: A lens that embosses the interface into raised dots: the page is sampled in six-dot cells and each dot rises where there is ink, lit from the upper left so the dome reads as relief on paper. A quiet, tactile way to see the page as texture.

props.name: radius / softness
props.description: Lens radius in CSS px and the feather of its edge.

props.name: cell / dot / relief
props.description: Cell pitch in px, dot radius in px, and how strongly the dots are lit.

props.name: paper
props.description: The paper colour under the dots.

usageNotes: Dots are placed on a 2×3 cell grid and raised by the texture's ink coverage at each dot.
The DOM under the lens stays real.
Reduced motion draws one still lens outline.

items.title: Honey Glass
items.tagline: Slow to follow, slow to let go.
items.description: The interface under a sheet of honey: the refraction lags the pointer, pools where it rests, and relaxes slowly after it leaves, with a warm amber tint and a specular sheen on the bulge. The lag is a spring with heavy damping — viscosity as motion, not as a filter.

props.name: viscosity / bulge / radius
props.description: How slowly the bulge follows and relaxes, its height in px of refraction, and its width.

props.name: tint / sheen
props.description: The amber cast and the specular strength.

usageNotes: The bulge centre is a heavily damped spring on the pointer; the loop stops once it has settled.
Clicks reach the real DOM through the honey.
Reduced motion shows the real, still DOM.

items.title: Soap Film
items.tagline: Thin as a film, coloured by it.
items.description: A soap film stretched over the interface: thin-film interference colours drift across the page as the film's thickness flows, and the pointer thins it where it pushes. The colour is computed from the simulated thickness, so it has the true rainbow order of a real film.

props.name: strength / flow / speed
props.description: How strong the colour is, how much the thickness varies, and how fast it drifts.

props.name: push / radius
props.description: How much the pointer thins the film and how wide.
