props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Selection, shaped by mode; a range in progress carries a null end.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on selection; opening a range fires once with a null end, then again when it closes.

props.name: min / max
props.description: Bounds; days outside are disabled and refuse selection.

props.name: label
props.description: Group label; the grid is named from it and the month.

usageNotes: A real grid: arrows move a day and carry the month with them, PageUp and PageDown change month, Home and End jump to the ends of the week, Enter or Space selects, and the month name is a live region.
While a range is open the sweep follows the pointer or the focused day, so arrowing through the month reads exactly like hovering it.
Under reduced motion the months cross-fade in place and the day stops stamping; the range fill still fills, since progress is information.
Today is read after hydration, not during render, so the server and the client never disagree about which day wears the ring.

items.title: Slide Confirm
items.tagline: Slide all the way, or it slides back.
items.description: A track that asks for the whole gesture. The thumb tracks the pointer 1:1 while the label fades under it and a fill follows behind; past 85% it slams home on flick, the arrow morphs into a check and the copy swaps, and released short of that it springs back on snap. ArrowRight nudges 10% a press, ArrowLeft takes it back, End runs it to the top and Enter there confirms, so the keyboard drives the same physics.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Fires once when the slide completes.

props.name: label
props.description: Track copy while idle; it also names the slider.

props.name: confirmedLabel
props.description: Copy after confirming.

props.name: resetAfter
props.description: Milliseconds before the thumb returns; omit to stay confirmed.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Locks the track and takes the thumb out of the tab order.

props.name: onProgressChange
props.description: Fires with the whole-percent position on every change, spring-back included.

usageNotes: The thumb is a slider: ArrowRight and ArrowUp nudge 10%, ArrowLeft and ArrowDown take it back, End runs it to the top, Home and Escape return it, and Enter or Space confirms once the thumb is past 85%.
The pointer is captured only after 4px of travel, so a plain click on the thumb is not swallowed and never confirms by accident.
Under reduced motion the thumb moves directly and the fill has no spring, but it still fills and the percentage still reads: how far you have got is information.

items.title: Choice Cards
items.tagline: The chosen card lifts; the rest step back.
items.description: A plan picker built as a radiogroup of cards. Choosing lifts the card 2px on glide while a ring draws around its perimeter and a check stamps into the corner on recoil, and the unchosen cards step back in tone. Switching the billing period re-rolls every price digit by digit on glide; arrow keys move between cards, Home and End jump to the ends, and Space selects.

props.name: options
props.description: The plans: value, title, monthly and yearly price, blurb, optional badge.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial chosen plan; defaults to the first option.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on choice.

props.name: billing / defaultBilling
props.description: Controlled or initial billing period; switching it re-rolls every price.

props.name: onBillingChange
props.description: Fires when the billing period changes.

props.name: currency
props.description: Prefix for every price.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible group label, shown beside the billing toggle.

usageNotes: A radiogroup with a roving tabindex: Left and Right (or Up and Down) move and select with wrap, Home and End jump to the first and last plan, Space selects the focused card. The billing toggle is its own two-stop radiogroup.
Under reduced motion the ring and the corner check still appear — they are the answer to the click — but the card does not lift and prices swap without rolling.
Cards sit side by side from the small breakpoint up and stack to one column at phone width; the ring is drawn on a measured rect, so it follows the card's real size.

items.title: Size Tiles
items.tagline: The tile you pick inflates; the rest hold still.
items.description: A size chooser that answers with weight instead of layout. The chosen tile inflates to 1.06 on snap and its border thickens, both transform and colour, so nothing beside it shifts; unavailable tiles draw a diagonal strike through themselves on flick when hovered or focused and carry 'out of stock' for a screen reader. Arrow keys move and wrap, Home and End jump, Space selects, and the fit note beneath cross-fades over a measured height.

props.name: sizes
props.description: The sizes: value, label, availability, and an optional fit note.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial chosen size.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on choice; an unavailable size never fires it.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible group label; the chosen size reads out beside it.

usageNotes: A radiogroup with a roving tabindex: Left and Right (or Up and Down) move and select with wrap, Home and End jump to the first and last tile, Space selects the focused one.
Unavailable tiles stay in the group and stay focusable — they carry aria-disabled and an 'out of stock' description, so the strike has a keyboard path and is never news only to a mouse.
Under reduced motion the tile keeps its thickened border and drops the inflation; the strike and the fit note still appear, because availability is information.

items.title: Filter Ledge
items.tagline: Chips toggle; the count catches up.
items.description: A ledge of filter chips that keeps its arithmetic honest. Toggling a chip blooms its fill from the centre on snap while a check draws itself in on flick and widens a slot to sit in, and the result count beneath rolls its digits to the new number on glide. Clear all sweeps the fills off in a cascade, left to right; every chip is a toggle button carrying aria-pressed and its own tab stop.

props.name: filters
props.description: The chips: id, label, and an optional per-filter count.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial active filter ids.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on every toggle and on clear all.

props.name: resultCount
props.description: The number the readout rolls to; the owner derives it from the active filters.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Fires when clear all empties the ledge.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the chip group.

usageNotes: Chips are toggle buttons with aria-pressed, each its own tab stop, so Tab reaches them and Space or Enter flips one — there is no gesture the keyboard cannot reach. Clear all disables itself when the ledge is already empty.
Under reduced motion the fills and checks swap instantly and the count updates without rolling; the total still changes, because a filtered result is information rather than flourish.
At phone width the row scrolls sideways and each end fades only while something is hidden past it; the fade is a mask on the row, so it reads on any background.

items.title: Cadence Pick
items.tagline: Pick a rhythm; the calendar redraws.
items.description: A rhythm picker that shows the rhythm. Four stops share one knob that glides between them on snap, and beside them a seven by five calendar glyph re-patterns itself: every mark keeps its identity across cadences, so it travels to its new cell on glide in a cascade rather than blinking out and back. Custom unfolds an interval stepper over a measured height; arrows move and wrap, Home and End jump, Space selects.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial cadence.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on change; custom carries the interval it now means.

props.name: everyDays / defaultEveryDays
props.description: Custom interval in days, clamped to 1–30.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible group label, which also names the radiogroup.

usageNotes: The stops are a radiogroup with a roving tabindex: Left and Right (or Up and Down) move and select with wrap, Home and End jump, Space selects. The interval control is a spinbutton — arrows step a day, Page Up and Page Down step a week, Home and End take it to 1 and 30.
Under reduced motion the marks swap to their new cells instantly and the panel opens without a glide; the pattern still redraws, because the pattern is the answer.
The custom panel holds no room while it is closed: its height is measured from the controls inside it, and it is inert so nothing in it takes focus while it is shut.

items.title: Likert Scale
items.tagline: The bar fills to where you stand.
items.description: An agreement scale of five or seven nodes on a line. Choosing fills the line up to that node on glide and inflates the node on snap, while the anchors shift weight with it — the near one firms as the far one fades — and hovering previews the fill at a lower weight without committing. A radiogroup with a roving tabindex: arrows move and select, Home and End jump to the ends, Space selects.

props.name: question
props.description: The statement being rated; it names the radiogroup.

props.name: points
props.description: Node count.

props.name: anchors
props.description: Labels at the ends; the end nodes borrow them for their names.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial 1-based choice.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on choice, with the 1-based value.

usageNotes: A radiogroup with a roving tabindex: Left and Right (or Up and Down) move and select with wrap, Home and End jump to the ends, Space selects the focused node. Every node carries its position in its name, and the end nodes carry their anchor.
Under reduced motion the fill still fills — on a tween instead of the glide spring — and the chosen node marks itself by colour rather than by inflating.
Node geometry never changes: the selected node scales, so the line under the row stays true and nothing beside it moves.

items.title: Priority Flag
items.tagline: The flag climbs the mast.
items.description: Priority drawn as a signal mast: the flag climbs to the chosen rung on glide while its colour tweens up the muted → warn → danger ramp. Landing on the top rung it flutters once, a single two-keyframe skew on recoil. Up and Down step the mast and wrap, Home and End jump to the ends, Space and Enter select.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial level — low, medium, high or urgent by default.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires when the level changes, by pointer or by key.

props.name: levels
props.description: Overrides the rungs, ordered bottom to top; the colour ramp stretches to fit.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible group label. Omit it and pass aria-label to label the group invisibly.

usageNotes: A radio group with a roving tabindex: Up and Left climb the mast, Down and Right descend, both wrapping; Home and End jump to the ends; Space and Enter select.
Under reduced motion the flag jumps to its rung with no climb and no flutter — only the colour tweens, because the level's colour is information.
Rungs are 36px, the same as the row height, so the flag always lands on a label's centreline however many levels you pass.

items.title: Slot Grid
items.tagline: Free slots breathe; the picked one stamps.
items.description: Appointment slots as a real grid of day columns and time rows. Free slots lift a pixel on hover with glide, taken slots are hatched and inert, and picking stamps the slot from 1.3× on recoil while the summary beneath cross-fades to the new time. Arrow keys walk the cells, Home and End jump to the ends of a row, Enter and Space pick.

props.name: days
props.description: Column headers, left to right; each needs an id and a label.

props.name: times
props.description: Row labels, top to bottom.

props.name: taken
props.description: "dayId:time" keys that are unavailable; those cells hatch and stop accepting picks.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial "dayId:time" key. Empty means nothing is held.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the "dayId:time" key on every pick.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible group label. Omit it and pass aria-label to label the grid invisibly.

usageNotes: role=grid with gridcells: arrow keys move a roving focus in two dimensions without wrapping, Home and End jump to the ends of the row, Enter and Space pick.
Taken slots keep aria-disabled rather than disabled, so the keyboard can read the whole week while picks stay refused.
Under reduced motion the stamp appears with no landing and the summary swaps without the cross-fade; the hatch and the stamp both carry the state without colour alone.
Narrow viewports scroll the day columns horizontally under edge fades while the time column stays pinned.

items.title: Vote Pair
items.tagline: One thumb bounces; the tally rolls.
items.description: Up and down vote buttons with the tally rolling between them. The chosen thumb pops from 0.78 on recoil and holds an 8° tilt toward its own direction on snap, while the tally rolls in the direction it moved and travels further when a side switch swings it by two. Both halves are toggle buttons carrying aria-pressed, so Enter or Space on the side already chosen withdraws the vote.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial vote: up, none, or down.

props.name: score
props.description: The tally before the reader's own vote is added; the control shows score + value.

props.name: onVote
props.description: Fires on every change, including the withdrawal back to 0.

props.name: size
props.description: Control size; both halves and the tally share one height.

props.name: subject
props.description: Names what is being voted on inside each button's accessible label.

usageNotes: Two toggle buttons, each its own tab stop: Enter or Space casts, and pressing the side already chosen withdraws the vote back to 0.
The tally sits in a live region and announces the new number, so the count reaches a screen reader without the animation.
Under reduced motion nothing pops or tilts — the colours swap and the tally still updates, because the count is information rather than flourish.

items.title: Access Matrix
items.tagline: Flip a row; the cells follow in order.
items.description: A permission matrix with roles down, actions across and a switch in every cell. Flipping a row's master runs its cells in order on cascade(), each knob sliding on snap, so a bulk change reads as one act rather than five simultaneous blinks; a column header lights its column by hover or by focus. Arrow keys walk the grid in two dimensions, Home and End jump to the ends of a row, Space and Enter toggle.

props.name: roles
props.description: Rows, top to bottom; each needs an id and a label.

props.name: actions
props.description: Columns, left to right; each needs an id and a label.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial grants: the granted action ids per role id.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the whole grant map on any toggle, cell or row master.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible group label. Omit it and pass aria-label to label the grid invisibly.

usageNotes: role=grid with a roving tabindex: arrow keys move in two dimensions without wrapping, Home and End jump to the row's master and its last action, Space and Enter toggle.
Cells carry role=switch with aria-checked; the row master is a tri-state checkbox rather than a switch, because ARIA does not let a switch report mixed.
Under reduced motion the knobs jump to their end with no cascade and no slide — the grant state still changes, since that is the information.
Narrow viewports scroll the action columns horizontally under an edge fade while the role column stays pinned.

items.title: Avatar Pick
items.tagline: The ring travels; the chosen face puffs.
items.description: A face chooser where one ring travels between the tiles on snap, keyed by a shared layoutId so it is the same ring moving rather than nine rings blinking. The chosen face puffs to 1.08 on recoil while the rest lose a little saturation on a tween, and the last tile opens a real file picker and previews the image in place. Arrows step and wrap, Home and End jump to the ends, Space and Enter select.

props.name: options
props.description: The faces: an id, one or two initials, a tint (pass a theme token), and a label used as the accessible name.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial id. The uploaded face reserves the id "upload".

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on every choice, including the one an upload makes.

props.name: allowUpload
props.description: Shows the tile that opens a real file picker and previews the chosen image.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible group label. Omit it and pass aria-label to label the group invisibly.

usageNotes: A radio group with a roving tabindex: arrows step through the tiles and wrap, Home and End jump to the ends, Space and Enter select. On the upload tile Space and Enter open the file picker instead, so no gesture is pointer-only.
Faces are drawn, not fetched — initials on a disc tinted from the token you pass, so the set costs no image requests and reads in both themes.
The upload preview's object URL is revoked as soon as it is replaced and again on unmount.
Under reduced motion the ring jumps to the chosen tile and nothing puffs; the saturation still shifts, because it is what marks the choice.

items.title: Spy Index
items.tagline: The marker follows your reading.
items.description: A table of contents that watches the page. An IntersectionObserver keyed to the reading line marks the section in view, and the marker travels between entries on glide through a shared layoutId while the active entry steps 4px out of the column and the rail beside the list fills with reading progress. Entries are plain links, so Tab reaches them and Enter follows them; clicking scrolls the container smoothly and hands focus to the target.

props.name: sections
props.description: The entries, in document order; ids must match headings inside the container.

props.name: container
props.description: The scrolling element; defaults to the window.

props.name: offset
props.description: Pixels from the top of the container that count as in view.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the nav, shown above the list.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires when the section in view changes.

usageNotes: Entries are ordinary links inside a nav: Tab reaches them, Enter follows them, and the entry in view carries aria-current="location". Clicking scrolls the container to the heading and moves focus there when the target is focusable.
Under reduced motion the marker jumps to its entry, the 4px indent is dropped, the rail still fills, and the scroll is instant rather than smooth.
The observer only reports crossings of the reading line; the active entry is then read from geometry, so a heading sitting exactly on the line resolves the same way every time.

items.title: Tab Bar
items.tagline: The active icon fills; its label rises.
items.description: A bottom tab bar built for a thumb. The chosen tab fills its outline glyph — a solid path cross-fading over the stroked one, a tween because weight and colour have no physics — lifts its label 2px on snap, and the indicator pill travels under it through a shared layoutId rather than blinking out and in. A badge bumps on recoil when its number changes, and the bar is a real tablist: a roving tabindex, Left and Right around the bar, Home and End to the ends.

props.name: tabs
props.type: { id: string; label: string; icon: "home" | "search" | "inbox" | "wallet" | "me"; badge?: number }[]
props.description: Up to five tabs; the icons are built in and a badge shows when its count is above zero.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial active tab id.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on tap and whenever the keyboard moves the selection.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name for the tablist.

usageNotes: A roving tabindex over role="tablist": Left and Right (or Up and Down) wrap around the bar, Home and End jump to the ends, and activation follows focus as tabs should. A tab carrying a badge names its count in its accessible name.
Under reduced motion the glyph fill and the indicator pill swap instantly, the label holds still, and the badge number still updates — the count is information, not flourish.
The badge bumps only when its number changes, never on mount, so a first paint is quiet.

items.title: Fold Sidebar
items.tagline: Collapse to icons; the labels fold in.
items.description: An app sidebar that folds to a rail. The width travels between 224px and 56px on glide while each label fades and is clipped by its own row, and because every icon sits half a rail from the edge nothing shifts sideways as the panel narrows. The active pill travels between items through a shared layoutId, group panels animate to a measured height rather than a reserved one, the fold control's double chevron turns over on snap, and in rail mode a hovered or focused item names itself in a tooltip beside the rail.

props.name: groups
props.type: { label: string; items: { id: string; label: string; icon: string }[] }[]
props.description: Sections and their items; icons come from the built-in set (gauge, grid, bell, users, card, gear, dot).

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial active item id.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on select.

props.name: collapsed / defaultCollapsed
props.description: Rail mode, controlled or initial.

props.name: onCollapsedChange
props.description: Fires on fold.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the nav.

usageNotes: Items are buttons inside a nav and the active one carries aria-current="page"; group headers are aria-expanded toggles over the panel they own, and a closed panel is inert so Tab skips what is hidden behind a zero height.
Under reduced motion the width and the group heights swap instantly and the chevrons turn without a spring; the labels still fade, since a fade neither travels nor bounces.
In rail mode the group headers step aside for a hairline and every item stays reachable, naming itself in a tooltip anchored beside the rail on hover or focus.

items.title: Top Rise
items.tagline: Surfaces as you go deep; the ring shows how far.
items.description: A back-to-top control that surfaces from the bottom edge on recoil — two visible bounces, the physics of something landing — once the container has passed the threshold, and sinks away on the exit ease when the top comes back into reach. Its ring carries scroll depth, drawn with pathLength so the geometry follows the button's own box rather than a fixed radius. Pressing it scrolls to the top while the arrow lifts 4px on flick; Tab reaches it and Enter or Space presses it.

props.name: container
props.description: The scrolling element; defaults to the window.

props.name: threshold
props.description: Pixels scrolled before it surfaces.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name.

props.name: onDepthChange
props.description: Fires with whole-percent scroll depth, 0–100, when the percent changes.

props.name: className
props.description: Positioning is the caller's: absolute inside a relative frame, or fixed when the page itself scrolls.

usageNotes: A plain button with an accessible name: Tab reaches it, Enter or Space presses it, and below the threshold it leaves the DOM entirely so the keyboard never lands on something invisible.
Under reduced motion it fades in and out without travelling, the ring still fills, and the scroll to the top is instant rather than smooth.
Place it outside the scroll container, in a relative wrapper — an absolutely positioned child of a scroller scrolls away with the content.

items.title: Canopy Menu
items.tagline: The panel unfolds; the columns arrive in order.
items.description: A mega menu that stays one panel. Hovering or focusing an item unfolds the canopy beneath the bar — scaleY from the top on glide, clipped — and its columns cascade in inside the 600ms budget. Moving to another item morphs the same panel to the new content's measured width and height rather than closing and reopening; Left and Right walk the bar, Tab steps down into the open panel, and Escape closes and hands focus back.

props.name: items
props.type: { id: string; label: string; columns: { heading: string; links: { label: string; href: string }[] }[] }[]
props.description: The bar and the panel behind each item.

props.name: openDelay
props.description: Hover intent delay in ms before an unopened panel unfolds; moving between items once open is immediate.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the nav.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires with the open item's id, or null when the panel closes.

usageNotes: A roving tabindex of aria-expanded buttons over one region: Left and Right walk the bar, Home and End jump to its ends, Enter and Space toggle, Tab steps down into the open panel, and Escape — from the bar or from inside the panel — closes and returns focus to the item that opened it.
Under reduced motion the panel appears and disappears without scaling and the columns arrive with it, no cascade and no 8px rise.

The panel's contents are laid out absolutely so their natural size can be measured free of the box that is animating toward it; the measurement is clamped to the bar's width, so the columns wrap instead of overhanging a narrow viewport.

items.title: Swipe Tabs
items.tagline: Drag the panel; the indicator rides your thumb.
items.description: Tabs whose panels are a strip you can push: dragging moves the strip with the pointer while the underline rides the same value, so the indicator sits exactly where your thumb has taken it. Release settles to the nearest panel on snap and the strip's height glides to the new panel's measured height. Left and Right move and activate without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump.

props.name: tabs
props.type: { id: string; label: string; content: React.ReactNode }[]
props.description: Tabs and their panels, left to right.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial tab id.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires when the active tab changes.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the tablist for assistive technology.

usageNotes: A real tablist: Left and Right move and activate without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump to the first and last tab, and the active panel is focusable so it can be scrolled from the keyboard.
Pointer capture waits for 4px of horizontal travel and stands down when the travel is vertical, so a tap stays a tap and the surface behind the strip still scrolls.
Under reduced motion the panels swap: no travel, no springs, and dragging is off — the underline and the panel change instantly.

items.title: Route Bar
items.tagline: Trickles while it waits; finishes when the page lands.
items.description: The bar at the top of a page change. It appears at 8% and trickles toward 90% on a decaying schedule, so a slow route keeps moving without ever claiming to be nearly done; when the page lands it completes on glide and leaves on the exit ease, with a soft glow at its head. Purely presentational — hold active true while a navigation is pending, or call start() and done() on the ref.

props.name: active
props.description: True while a navigation is pending.

props.name: height
props.description: Bar height in px.

props.name: color
props.description: CSS colour for the bar and its head glow.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the progress bar for assistive technology.

props.name: ref
props.description: Imperative start() and done(), OR'd with the active prop.

usageNotes: No keyboard path of its own: the bar is presentational and never takes focus, reporting itself as role=progressbar with aria-valuenow rounded to whole percent.
Under reduced motion the head loses its glow and the bar still moves, because progress is information rather than flourish.
Repeated starts reset to 8% instead of stacking, and every timer and animation is stopped on unmount; it is absolutely positioned by default, so it reserves no space in the layout.

items.title: Section Dots
items.tagline: The active dot stretches into a pill.
items.description: A rail of dots down the side of a scrolling story. The active dot stretches into a pill on snap, a layout animation so the shape itself travels rather than a dot blinking on elsewhere, and its label slides out from the rail on hover or focus. The rail reads the container with an IntersectionObserver, and Up and Down move between dots while Enter scrolls the container to that section.

props.name: sections
props.description: Ids of the section elements inside the container, in document order.

props.name: container
props.description: The scrolling element the rail watches and scrolls.

props.name: side
props.description: Which edge of the container the rail sits on.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires when the section under the viewport changes.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the rail for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Roving tabindex over the dots: Up and Down (or Left and Right) move focus, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter and Space scroll the container to that section, and the active dot carries aria-current.
Under reduced motion the pill swaps instead of stretching, the label appears without travel, and the container jumps rather than scrolling smoothly.
The rail positions itself absolutely against the container's own relative parent, so it overlays the frame without reserving a column; keep the section text padded clear of it.

items.title: Burger Sheet
items.tagline: The burger becomes the cross as the sheet unfolds.
items.description: A menu button that turns into its own close button: the middle bar fades while the outer two travel to the centre and rotate on snap, the same spring the sheet's links land on. The sheet is a large surface, so it arrives on glide with its links cascading behind it and leaves on the exit ease. It is a real dialog while open — focus is trapped in the panel, Escape closes and returns focus to the button, and the frame passed as container stops scrolling.

props.name: items
props.description: Links in the sheet, top to bottom.

props.name: side
props.description: Which edge the sheet enters from.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial open state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires on open and on close.

props.name: container
props.description: The scrolling frame the sheet covers; its scroll locks while open.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading inside the sheet; also names the dialog.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the menu button, which carries aria-expanded.

usageNotes: Open moves focus to the panel's close button and traps Tab and Shift+Tab inside the dialog; Escape closes and returns focus to the menu button, as does clicking the scrim or a link.
Under reduced motion the sheet fades in place instead of sliding, the links arrive without travel or cascade, and the bars swap straight to the cross.
The sheet positions itself against the nearest positioned ancestor, so make the frame relative and leave the header static; scroll locking is applied to the container ref, never to the document.

items.title: Letter Index
items.tagline: Drag the letters; the current one pops out.
items.description: The A–Z rail beside a long list. Dragging it pops the letter under the pointer out into a bubble on recoil, two visible bounces, while the list jumps instantly because it is following your thumb; letters with no entries are muted and the pick falls to the nearest letter that has some. The rail is a listbox: Up and Down move the active letter past the muted ones, and Enter scrolls the list there.

props.name: groups
props.description: Sections that exist; every other letter of the rail is muted.

props.name: container
props.description: The scrolling list; its section headers carry data-letter="A".

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fires when the rail jumps the list to a letter.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the rail for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The rail is one tab stop with aria-activedescendant: Up and Down move the active letter and skip the muted ones, Home and End go to the first and last letter with entries, Enter or Space scrolls the list there.
Under reduced motion the bubble appears instead of popping, and the list jumps rather than scrolling smoothly on Enter.
Pointer capture waits for 4px of travel so a tap on a letter is still a tap; each section header inside the container must carry data-letter for the rail to find it.

items.title: Undo Toast
items.tagline: Undo, before the ring runs out.
items.description: A toast with an action and a countdown. It rises on recoil, whose two bounces read as something landing on the stack, while a ring beside the message drains linearly across the duration; hovering or focusing stops the ring where it stands and leaving resumes it from there. Taking the action cross-fades the panel to a restored line and lifts it away on the exit ease, and the action is a real button one Tab from the message.

props.name: open
props.description: Shows the toast. Raise it after the edit has already been applied.

props.name: message
props.description: What was done — one short line, past tense.

props.name: actionLabel
props.description: Action copy.

props.name: duration
props.description: Milliseconds until it dismisses itself; 0 or less keeps it up.

props.name: onAction
props.description: Fires when the action is taken — restore the thing here.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Fires when the ring runs out, the toast is closed, or a restore finishes.

props.name: className
props.description: Overrides the default bottom-centre placement inside the nearest relative parent.

usageNotes: role=status with two real buttons: Tab reaches the action and the dismiss control, and focusing either pauses the countdown exactly as hovering does.
Under reduced motion the panel fades in place instead of rising, and the ring still drains — a countdown is information, not flourish.
It renders absolutely inside the nearest positioned ancestor, so give the surface it belongs to relative; changing the message replaces the panel and restarts the countdown.

items.title: Light Box
items.tagline: The thumbnail becomes the picture.
items.description: A gallery whose thumbnail grows into the viewer. Tile and viewer share a layoutId, so opening morphs the thumbnail's rect into the picture on glide while the backdrop tweens in, and closing returns it to the tile it grew from. Moving is a different gesture: the old picture leaves on the exit ease and the new arrives from distances.shift, driven by arrows, a swipe, or the Left and Right keys, with focus trapped and Escape closing.

props.name: images
props.description: Items of { id, alt, caption?, art }; art renders in both the tile and the viewer, so make it fill its container.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial id of the open picture; null is closed.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires on open, on every move, and on close.

props.name: className
props.description: Applied to the gallery wrapper.

usageNotes: role=dialog with a focus trap: focus lands on the panel so the picture's name is read first, Left and Right move between pictures, Tab cycles the controls, and Escape closes and returns focus to the tile.
Under reduced motion nothing travels — the viewer cross-fades in, pictures cross-fade between each other, and the swipe is dropped in favour of the arrows.
The viewer is absolutely positioned inside the nearest positioned ancestor, so give the surface that owns the gallery relative; art is yours to supply, so no assets ship with it.
Closing returns the picture to the tile the session opened from, which keeps the morph pointed at one tile even after moving through the set.

items.title: Edit Bubble
items.tagline: Click the value; it becomes the field.
items.description: Inline editing without a modal. A pencil hint appears on hover, and clicking morphs the value into a field: reading state and bubble share a layoutId, so the box grows on snap with one crisp overshoot while the text keeps its place. Enter saves and the new value lands on recoil like a stamp, Escape restores, blurring saves, and a blocked save nudges the bubble four pixels and prints the reason where the label sits.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value. The reading state mirrors it; each edit starts from it.

props.name: onSave
props.description: Called on commit. Return a promise to hold the bubble open while it saves; a rejection keeps the edit and shows a reason.

props.name: validate
props.description: Return a reason to block the save; null lets it through.

props.name: type
props.description: Input type; number also sets a decimal inputMode.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the field, also shown above it.

props.name: className
props.description: Applied to the field wrapper.

usageNotes: Enter saves, Escape restores the previous value, and blurring the field saves as well, so tabbing onward never loses an edit; focus returns to the reading button on every close.
Under reduced motion the bubble swaps in with no morph, the saved tick appears without its flick, and a blocked save states its reason without the nudge.
Reading state and bubble are the same height and the label line doubles as the hint and error line, so nothing below the field ever jumps.

items.title: Bell Tray
items.tagline: The bell rings; the tray drops.
items.description: A notification bell and its tray. An arriving item swings the bell on recoil, rotated about its crown so it pivots where a bell hangs, and bumps the badge with the same spring; opening drops the tray on glide with its items cascading in under the 600ms budget. Marking all read sweeps the unread dots out one after another, dismissing an item collapses its row on the exit ease, and the bell is a button with aria-expanded whose tray answers to Up, Down and Escape.

props.name: items
props.description: Notifications of { id, title, time, unread }, newest first.

props.name: onRead
props.description: Fires with the ids that just became read — one id, or all of them.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Fires when an item is dismissed; remove it from items to collapse the row.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial tray state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires when the bell, Escape, or a click outside changes the tray.

props.name: className
props.description: Applied to the bell's positioned wrapper.

usageNotes: The bell is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls and the tray a labelled region: Tab moves into the tray, Up and Down walk the items, Enter dismisses one, and Escape closes and returns focus to the bell.
Under reduced motion nothing swings, drops or cascades — the badge, the dots and the counts still update, because a count is information.
The bell only rings for ids it has not seen before, so a tray that mounts with items stays still; nothing starts on mount.

items.title: Typed Confirm
items.tagline: Type the word; the button wakes as you match.
items.description: A destructive confirmation that has to be spelled out. Each character that agrees with the phrase lights where it stands on flick, the shortest spring in the set, and the danger button fills from the left in proportion to the match on a plain tween — nothing overshoots, because destruction does not celebrate. A character that disagrees dims the fill instead of clearing it, only an exact match enables the button, and it is an alertdialog with a focus trap where Escape cancels.

props.name: phrase
props.description: What must be typed exactly before the button wakes.

props.name: title / description
props.description: Dialog copy; the description says what is lost and is wired to aria-describedby.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: Button copy.

props.name: open / onOpenChange
props.description: Controlled state; the dialog closes through onOpenChange on cancel, Escape, backdrop and confirm.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Fires once, on a full match, when the button is pressed.

props.name: onMatchChange
props.description: Fires on every keystroke with the leading characters that match.

props.name: className
props.description: Applied to the overlay that fills the nearest positioned ancestor.

usageNotes: role=alertdialog with a focus trap: focus lands in the field, Tab cycles the controls, Enter confirms a full match, and Escape cancels and returns focus to whatever opened it.
Under reduced motion the letters and the fill swap to their new values with no travel, which still shows how far the match has come.
The dialog is absolutely positioned inside the nearest positioned ancestor, so give the surface it guards relative; the phrase wraps by character so a long name never pushes past a narrow edge.

items.title: Fab Fan
items.tagline: One button fans into five.
items.description: A floating action button that fans into five. Pressing turns the plus 45 degrees into a cross on snap while the actions travel a quarter arc and land on recoil in cascade; the label of whichever action the pointer or the keyboard is on slides in beside it from distances.step, pushed clear of its neighbours. Pressing again folds the cascade backwards on the exit ease. It is a menu button with aria-expanded: Up and Down walk the actions, Left and Right follow the arc, Home and End jump, Enter selects, and Escape folds the fan and returns focus to the trigger.

props.name: actions
props.description: Up to five actions; icons come from the built-in stroked set, and anything past the fifth is dropped so the arc stays legible.

props.name: placement
props.description: Corner the button sits in, and the direction the quarter arc sweeps.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial fan state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires whenever the fan opens or folds.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the trigger and the menu it controls.

usageNotes: Enter or Space on the trigger opens the fan and focuses the first action; Up and Down walk the list, Left and Right follow the arc's direction, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space selects, and Escape folds the fan and returns focus to the trigger.

One label shows at a time, on the action the pointer or the keyboard is on, pushed radially outward so it clears the neighbouring actions: five horizontal pills cannot share a quarter arc, whose vertical pitch near the top is under 10px. Every action still carries its label as its accessible name and its tooltip.
Under reduced motion nothing travels: the actions appear at their stops and fade out again, and the plus swaps to a cross instantly.
The component fills its nearest positioned ancestor, so give the surface it sits on position: relative; the backdrop is a labelled button so a pointer tap outside also folds it.

items.title: Keymap Sheet
items.tagline: Press ? and the keys drop in.
items.description: A shortcut sheet that opens on ? or its trigger. The panel rises on glide and every keycap pops from 0.7x on flick in a cascade, grouped by section; typing in the filter folds the rows that no longer match away on the exit ease, headings included. It is a modal dialog with a focus trap, the hotkey is ignored while focus sits in a field, and Escape closes the sheet and returns focus to the trigger.

props.name: groups
props.description: Sections of shortcuts; each shortcut carries a label and one string per keycap.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial sheet state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires whenever the sheet opens or closes.

props.name: hotkey
props.description: The key that opens the sheet, matched against event.key and shown on the trigger.

props.name: onFilterChange
props.description: Fires as the filter field is typed in, and with an empty string when the sheet opens.

usageNotes: The hotkey opens the sheet only when focus is not in an input, textarea, select or contenteditable, and its listener is added on mount and removed on unmount. Focus moves to the filter, Tab cycles inside the panel, and Escape closes the sheet and returns focus to the trigger.
Under reduced motion the sheet fades in place and the keycaps appear without popping; rows still fold, because a filtered list changing length is information.
The component fills its nearest positioned ancestor, so give the surface it sits on position: relative; the panel scrolls internally and shrinks to the rows that match.

items.title: Dock Player
items.tagline: Scroll past it; it docks in the corner.
items.description: A media card that docks. An IntersectionObserver watches its seat against the scrolling container, and once less than 40 percent of the seat is on screen the card shrinks into the corner along one shared layoutId, travelling on glide because a layout shift should not bounce. Play, progress and close ride along, the docked picture is a button that scrolls the seat back into view, and under reduced motion the two positions cross-fade.

props.name: container
props.description: The scrolling element whose viewport decides when the card docks; it is the observer's root.

props.name: title
props.description: Card title, and the accessible name of the play, close and return controls.

props.name: corner
props.description: Corner the card docks into.

props.name: children
props.description: The media surface; it is stretched to fill the card's picture area in both sizes.

props.name: onStateChange
props.description: Fires when the card moves between inline, docked and closed.

usageNotes: Every pointer path has a keyboard one: the docked picture is a button that scrolls the seat back into view, play toggles with Enter or Space, and close hands the seat a Show player button that brings the card back.
Under reduced motion the inline and docked cards cross-fade instead of travelling, while the timecode and progress bar keep running, because playback state is information rather than flourish.

Render the component directly in the scrolled column: it returns the seat plus a zero-height sticky rail that must share the column as its containing block. The seat holds the card's exact shape, so the article never reflows when the card leaves.

items.title: Share Tray
items.tagline: Tap share; the targets rise in turn.
items.description: A share sheet whose tray raises on glide while the targets rise from distances.step on recoil in a cascade, so each arrival gets its own two bounces inside the 600ms budget. Copy writes the clipboard and stamps: the link mark cross-fades to a check that draws on flick and the label lands from 1.15x, and where the browser has a native sheet a More target hands off to it. It is a modal dialog with a focus trap, a labelled backdrop, and Escape closing back to the trigger.

props.name: url
props.description: What is shared: written to the clipboard by the copy target and handed to the native sheet.

props.name: title
props.description: Share title, shown in the tray and passed to the native sheet.

props.name: targets
props.description: Custom destinations, each with an icon from the built-in set; the built-in copy target is always first.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial tray state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires whenever the tray opens or closes.

props.name: onAction
props.description: Fires with the id of whichever target was used, the built-in copy and more included.

usageNotes: Targets are plain buttons, so Tab walks them and Enter or Space selects; focus is trapped inside the tray and Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
Under reduced motion the tray fades in place and the targets appear without rising, but the copy stamp still swaps to a check, because a confirmation is information.

The More target appears only where navigator.share exists, and it is read after hydration through a store snapshot so the server and first client renders agree. A clipboard that refuses is reported as Copy failed rather than silently succeeding.

items.title: Consent Slab
items.tagline: It rises once; the choices unfold.
items.description: A consent slab that rises from the bottom of its frame on glide. Customise measures its own panel with a ResizeObserver and unfolds to exactly that height, with the necessary category locked on; a decision stamps into the button row and the slab sinks on the exit ease, leaving a Preferences chip to bring it back. It is a labelled region rather than a dialog, and each category is a switch with aria-checked that Enter or Space drives.

props.name: categories
props.description: Consent categories with a label and a blurb; mark the ones the product cannot run without as locked.

props.name: onDecision
props.description: Fires with every granted id, locked categories included.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial slab state; the Preferences chip re-raises it.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires when the slab rises or sinks, so a controlled parent can follow the stamp.

usageNotes: No focus trap and no backdrop: it is a labelled region, so the page behind it stays usable. Customise carries aria-expanded, each category is a switch driven by Enter or Space, and a locked category reports itself checked and disabled.
Under reduced motion the slab fades in and out and the panel unfolds instantly; the switches and the stamp still change, because a decision is information.

Accepting anything optional lands the stamp on recoil, while refusing everything lands it on snap — declining is not an occasion to celebrate. The decision is held in memory here; a product would persist it.

items.title: Transfer Bar
items.tagline: Fast at first, honest at the end.
items.description: A transfer progress bar that stays honest at the end: the fill runs linear to 90% and then approaches the finish asymptotically, so the last percent belongs to the transfer rather than to the animation, while a stripe rides the fill and the rate and remaining-time readouts roll on snap. Done stamps a check on recoil and folds the body away on glide to a one-line summary whose height is measured rather than reserved; error tints warn, stops the stripe and offers Retry. The track is a progressbar carrying aria-valuetext, Retry is a real button in the tab order, and under reduced motion the stripe never runs while the fill still fills.

props.name: progress
props.description: 0–1. Clamped, and compressed past 90% so the fill cannot claim a finish the transfer has not reached.

props.name: status
props.description: Active runs the stripe, done stamps and folds, error tints warn and offers Retry.

props.name: bytes
props.description: Feeds the byte, rate and remaining-time readouts; the rate is sampled on its own clock and smoothed.

props.name: label
props.description: File name. Truncates with a title attribute and labels the progressbar.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Fires from the Retry button in the error state.

usageNotes: The only control is the Retry button in the error state — a real button in the tab order, activated with Enter or Space.
Under reduced motion the stripe never runs and the check simply appears, but the fill still fills and the readouts still update: progress is information, not flourish.
Progress is driven entirely by props; the bar owns no clock but the one that samples the transfer rate, and folds to its measured height rather than reserving room for a state.

items.title: Save Mark
items.tagline: Saving, saved, and how long ago.
items.description: An autosave indicator that tells the truth about time. Unsaved breathes on drift, saving bounces three dots on snap a beat out of phase, saved draws its check with pathLength on flick, and error shakes once on a tween before offering Retry. "Saved just now" relaxes into a live "Saved 2m ago" from a timer that runs only while a save is on screen, and the chip is a polite status region whose spoken text changes on state rather than on every tick; Retry is a real button in the tab order, and under reduced motion nothing bounces or breathes while the check still appears.

props.name: state
props.description: Which of the five save states to show. Each has its own mark and its own physics.

props.name: savedAt
props.description: Epoch ms of the last save. Drives the relative time, which ticks from a timer and is never read during render.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Fires from the Retry action, which appears only in the error state.

usageNotes: The only control is Retry in the error state — a real button in the tab order, activated with Enter or Space.
Under reduced motion the dot does not breathe and the saving dots do not bounce; the states swap and the check appears complete, because a save confirmation is information rather than flourish.

The polite status region speaks the state, not the clock: "Saved 2m ago" shows on screen while assistive technology hears "Saved" once, so a live relative time never becomes a stream of announcements.

items.title: Expiry Ring
items.tagline: The ring drains; the last ten seconds pulse.
items.description: A countdown ring that drains linearly — the one place a tween is more honest than a spring, because no easing may borrow from a second. Inside it mm:ss rolls on snap, one wheel per digit so only the place that changed moves; under the warn threshold the ring pulses on drift and the digits warm to warn, and zero stamps Expired on recoil and swaps the line for a Resend button that restarts the run. The element is a timer with its live region off so a screen reader is not read a number every second, a polite region speaks only at the two thresholds, and Resend is a real button; under reduced motion the pulse never runs while the ring still drains.

props.name: seconds
props.description: Length of the countdown.

props.name: running
props.description: Pause and resume. Pausing keeps the elapsed time, so resuming carries on rather than restarting.

props.name: warnAt
props.description: Seconds left when the ring starts pulsing and the digits warm to warn.

props.name: onExpire
props.description: Fires once, from the tick that reaches zero.

props.name: onResend
props.description: Fires from the Resend button, which also restarts the countdown.

props.name: onTick
props.description: Whole seconds left, emitted from the tick that changed the number.

props.name: label
props.description: What is expiring. Names the timer and both threshold announcements.

usageNotes: Resend is a real button in the tab order, activated with Enter or Space; pause and resume are driven by the running prop, so the host decides what controls them.
Under reduced motion the ring does not pulse and the digits swap in place, but the ring still drains and the readout still counts: a countdown is information, not flourish.
The timer's own live region is off. A separate polite region announces exactly twice — on crossing warnAt and on expiring — so assistive technology is never read a number every second.

items.title: Copy Chip
items.tagline: Copy, and the icon says so.
items.description: A copy button that shows its own result. The glyph morphs rather than swaps — the two squares fade out on a tween while the tick draws over them with pathLength on flick — a wash flashes once across the chip and drains on the exit ease, the label swaps to the copied copy, and the chip reverts after its timeout. When the clipboard refuses, the chip selects the value in a field over its own box and asks for Ctrl/Cmd+C, with Escape or blur returning it to idle; a polite status line announces each outcome once, and under reduced motion the icon simply swaps because the result still has to be visible.

props.name: value
props.description: What is written to the clipboard, and what the fallback field selects.

props.name: label
props.description: Idle copy, and the accessible name in the icon variant.

props.name: copiedLabel
props.description: Copied copy, shown while the tick is drawn.

props.name: timeout
props.description: Milliseconds before the chip reverts to idle. A second copy restarts the clock.

props.name: variant
props.description: With or without a visible label; both are 32px tall so they sit in a row of controls.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Fires with the value once the clipboard has taken it.

usageNotes: A real button: Tab reaches it, Enter and Space copy. If the clipboard is refused, focus moves into a field holding the selected value so Ctrl/Cmd+C still works, and Escape or blur returns the chip to idle.
Under reduced motion the glyph swaps instead of morphing and the tick appears complete — the outcome is information, so it is never animated away.
The polite status line announces each outcome once; the chip itself carries no live region, so a rapid second copy does not stack announcements.

items.title: Task Tick
items.tagline: Strike it through; it sinks to the bottom.
items.description: A checklist that keeps its order honest. Checking draws a line through the label with pathLength on flick — the strike is the acknowledgement, so it lands before anything moves — and only after a beat does the row sink into the done section, a layout reorder on glide where the row travels rather than blinking from one place to another; unchecking floats it back and the progress pill counts on snap. The beat is what keeps a fast run of ticks pointing at the rows the reader meant. Every checkbox is a real input, so Tab reaches each one and Space toggles it, and under reduced motion the strike appears complete and rows move without springs, because the order is the information.

props.name: items
props.type: { id: string; label: string; done: boolean }[]
props.description: The tasks, in the order they should read while open. Done tasks sort to the bottom a beat after they are ticked.

props.name: onToggle
props.description: Fires from the checkbox that changed, with the value it is changing to.

props.name: label
props.description: List label. Names the list and sits beside the progress pill.

usageNotes: Real checkboxes: Tab reaches each row, Space toggles it, and the whole row is a label so a pointer can hit anywhere along it.
Under reduced motion the strike appears complete and rows move without springs — the reorder still happens, because where a task sits is information rather than flourish.
The reorder waits a beat after the tick. A row that leaves instantly takes the pointer's target with it, and the next tick lands on whatever slid underneath.

items.title: Quota Meter
items.tagline: Fills honestly; over the line, it warns.
items.description: A segmented quota meter whose bars fill left to right in a cascade() on glide, because a quantity settles rather than switches. Crossing warnAt tints the track warn and flashes the leading segment once, and usage past the limit opens a danger lane beyond the track's end while the track glides aside to make room. It is a role=meter carrying the overage in aria-valuetext, so the reading is spoken even though the rolling digits are decorative.

props.name: used
props.description: Current usage in unit. May exceed limit — the overage is drawn past the track's end.

props.name: limit
props.description: The quota the track represents.

props.name: warnAt
props.description: Fraction of the limit at which the meter turns warn and flashes its leading segment.

props.name: unit
props.description: Unit label printed after both numbers and spoken in the value text.

props.name: label
props.description: What is being measured; names the meter for assistive technology.

props.name: segments
props.description: Bars in the track; the cascade tightens automatically as the count grows.

usageNotes: role=meter with aria-valuenow clamped inside the quota (a meter may not report past its maximum) while aria-valuetext names the percentage, or the overage in words.
Under reduced motion the segments still fill — a quota is information, not flourish — but without the stagger, and the digits swap in place instead of rolling.
The threshold flash is mounted by the crossing itself, so a meter that loads already over the line does not flash at a viewer who crossed nothing.

items.title: Presence Row
items.tagline: Faces join with a squeeze; the count catches up.
items.description: A presence stack that makes room. A face arriving scales from 0.6 into a snap while its neighbours slide over on the same spring through layout, so the row squeezes open instead of reflowing in one frame; a face leaving fades on the exit ease and popLayout closes the row behind it. Hover or focus fans the stack apart so every face is legible — the row itself is focusable, and Escape closes the fan — and the overflow chip rolls its count.

props.name: people
props.description: Who is present, in stacking order; each needs an id, a name and a tint (pass a theme token so both themes read).

props.name: max
props.description: Faces shown before the overflow chip takes over.

props.name: onOverflowClick
props.description: Fires when the +N chip is pressed, from the click itself — the component keeps no list of its own to open.

props.name: context
props.description: What the presence is for; it completes the spoken sentence, as in "Ana and 2 others are on the Fernworks brief".

usageNotes: The row is one focus stop carrying the whole sentence as its name; focusing it fans the stack, Escape closes the fan without moving focus, and Tab reaches the +N chip.
Faces are procedural initials on a tinted disc — no image requests, and the tint is any CSS colour, so a token keeps both themes legible.
Under reduced motion nothing fans and the faces simply appear; the polite status line still lets the count catch up for a screen reader.

items.title: Typing Pill
items.tagline: Three dots, out of step on purpose.
items.description: A typing indicator whose pill lands on recoil — the two visible bounces of something arriving in a conversation — and leaves on the exit ease, because a departure should not celebrate itself. The three dots run one snap between two keyframes, reversed and repeated, each started a phase later than the last, so they are never at the same height at once. A polite live region holds only the caption, so a screen reader hears each change exactly once.

props.name: names
props.description: Who is typing, in the order they started. An empty array hides the pill and clears the announcement.

props.name: max
props.description: Names spelled out before the caption falls back to "and N others".

usageNotes: There is nothing to operate: the pill is driven entirely by names, and its role=status region is announced politely once per change rather than on every frame of the dots.
typingCaption(names, max) is exported so a host can mirror the exact wording elsewhere instead of reimplementing the grammar.
Under reduced motion the dots pulse their opacity in the same phases and nothing travels; the pill still appears and disappears, since who is typing is information.

items.title: Load Hem
items.tagline: The list's hem loads the next page.
items.description: Infinite scroll done honestly. A sentinel at the list's hem is watched by an IntersectionObserver rather than a scroll handler, so an idle list costs nothing and a hem that is off screen never fetches on mount; the observer is rebuilt after each page, and a status flag means one page is never fetched twice. Arriving rows cascade in from distances.step on glide, the last page stamps the end on recoil, and a failed page keeps what it has and offers Retry.

props.name: initial
props.description: The first page, already loaded. It is page 0, so the hem asks for page 1 next; it is captured once and never reset by a rebuilt array.

props.name: onLoadMore
props.type: (page: number) => Promise<{ items: T[]; hasMore: boolean }>
props.description: Fetches a page, called from the crossing that caused it. A rejection shows Retry instead of losing the rows already loaded.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Row renderer; the hem supplies the row box and its hairline.

props.name: container
props.description: The scroll container the sentinel is measured in. Omit it and the hem walks up to the list's own scrolling ancestor.

props.name: endLabel
props.description: The stamp that retires the loader on the last page.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Retry is a real button in the tab order, and the observer stays quiet after a failure until it is pressed — retrying a broken request on scroll is how a list hammers a server.
Pages, failures and the end are announced in a polite live region, and the list carries aria-busy while a page is in flight.
Under reduced motion the rows appear rather than cascading and the loader stops sweeping, but the loading and end states still show: that a list is still loading is information.

items.title: Offline Bar
items.tagline: Gone offline; counting down to try again.
items.description: A connection banner that keeps its own time. Going offline drops the bar in from distances.shift on glide in warn, with a ring counting the seconds down to the next check and a Retry now that runs it immediately; when the connection returns the bar turns success, says so, and lifts away on the exit ease after a beat, because a reconnection is a relief rather than a celebration. It follows the browser's online and offline events through useSyncExternalStore, or takes a controlled online prop from products with their own health check.

props.name: online
props.description: Controlled connection state. Omit it and the bar follows the browser's own online and offline events.

props.name: retryIn
props.description: Seconds between automatic retries; the ring sweeps once per period.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Runs on every retry, automatic or pressed, from the tick or the press that caused it. Resolving true counts as connected; false restarts the countdown.

props.name: offlineLabel
props.description: Copy while the connection is down.

props.name: onlineLabel
props.description: Copy for the beat before the bar lifts away.

usageNotes: Retry now is a real button in the tab order and is disabled while a check is in flight, so the countdown and the keyboard can never run two checks at once.
The bar sits inside a permanent role=status region and the ticking seconds are hidden from it — a live region that re-read itself every second would talk over everything else.
Under reduced motion the bar fades in place instead of dropping and the ring steps between seconds rather than sweeping; the countdown still counts, since it is information.

items.title: Uptime Strip
items.tagline: Ninety days, one bar each.
items.description: Ninety days of service history, one bar each: the bars grow from the baseline in a single cascade on glide, and incident days carry a second bar that swells and fades on drift so the bad days pulse once without anything blinking. The header percentage rolls its digits on glide rather than swapping. The strip is a listbox — the pointer reads whichever bar it is over, Left and Right walk the days, Home and End jump to the oldest and today, and the reading follows along the strip, clamped inside the strip's own box so nothing shifts.

props.name: days
props.description: Ninety entries, oldest first.

props.name: label
props.description: Service name.

props.name: uptime
props.description: Percentage shown in the header; it rolls to each new figure.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats the header percentage.

props.name: onReadChange
props.description: Fires with the day under the pointer or the keyboard cursor; null on leave.

usageNotes: The strip is a listbox with one tab stop: Left and Right (or Up and Down) walk the days, Home and End jump to the oldest day and today, Escape drops the reading, and the reading follows the keyboard cursor as it follows the pointer.
Under reduced motion the bars appear at full height and the incident pulse is dropped; the percentage still updates, because a reading is information rather than flourish.
The reading is measured against the strip with a ResizeObserver and clamped to it, so it never leaves the card and never shifts the layout; bars are fluid, so ninety of them fit a 342px phone column.

items.title: Poll Bars
items.tagline: Vote, and the bars find their share.
items.description: A poll that turns into its own result. Until the reader votes it is a plain radiogroup; the vote reveals the bars, each growing to its share on glide in one cascade while the percentages roll and the total climbs, and the chosen option stamps its check on recoil. Bars are drawn inside the option rows so revealing the results shifts nothing. Up and Down move and vote, Home and End jump to the ends, Space and Enter cast.

props.name: options
props.type: { id: string; label: string; votes: number }[]
props.description: Options and their counts, excluding this reader.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial vote.

props.name: onVote
props.description: Fires on vote.

props.name: allowChange
props.description: Let the reader move their vote after casting it.

props.name: question
props.description: The poll question; it labels the radiogroup.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats the vote counts.

usageNotes: A radiogroup with a roving tabindex: Up and Down (or Left and Right) move and vote without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump to the ends, Space and Enter cast. With allowChange false the arrows still read the options out but the vote holds.
Under reduced motion the bars are set without spring and the digits swap; the results still appear, because the outcome is the information the reader asked for.
The bar is drawn inside each option row and the percentage sits in a fixed gutter, so the reveal never moves a row.

items.title: Delta Tile
items.tagline: The number rolls; the arrow turns to meet it.
items.description: A KPI tile that answers three questions in one movement: the value rolls its digits on glide, the delta arrow turns to meet it on snap while its colour tweens danger to success, and the twelve-point sparkline redraws itself with pathLength on glide whenever the series changes. The tile is a button — hover or focus reads the previous period, Enter or Space pins that reading — and its accessible name is the whole sentence.

props.name: label
props.description: Metric name.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value; its digits roll to each new number.

props.name: previous
props.description: Prior period value; the delta is derived from it.

props.name: series
props.description: Sparkline points, oldest first; a new array redraws the path.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats the value, the previous reading, and the range.

props.name: lowerIsBetter
props.description: Set when a fall is the good outcome — churn, latency, cost.

usageNotes: The tile is a button: Tab reaches it, focus reads the previous period, and Enter or Space pins that reading so it can be studied without a pointer.
Under reduced motion the digits swap, the arrow flips instantly, and the sparkline is drawn at once; the delta colour still tweens, because colour carries no momentum.
The sparkline is a viewBox scaled by its container with a non-scaling stroke, and the previous-period reading is positioned inside the chart's own box, so neither can overhang a narrow column.

items.title: Activity Rings
items.tagline: Three rings, each closing on its own spring.
items.description: Three nested progress rings, each filling to its value on glide one cascade step apart so they read as three measurements arriving rather than one animation. A ring past its goal keeps going as a darker second lap over the first, and the centre figure rolls its digits to whichever ring is being read. Hovering or focusing a legend row isolates its ring and dims the others; arrows walk the rows and Enter pins the isolation.

props.name: rings
props.type: { id: string; label: string; value: number; goal: number; color: string }[]
props.description: Outer to inner, up to three.

props.name: size
props.description: Diameter in px; the figure scales down with its container.

props.name: thickness
props.description: Ring stroke width in px.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats values and goals in the legend.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the figure; a sentence per ring is appended to it.

usageNotes: The legend is a list of buttons with a roving tabindex: Up and Down move between rows, Home and End jump to the ends, and Enter or Space pins the isolation so it survives the pointer leaving.
Under reduced motion the rings are set without spring and only the dimming tweens; the fill still shows, because progress is information.
The figure is role=img carrying one sentence per ring, so the whole reading is available without sight or a pointer.

items.title: Budget Bar
items.tagline: Segments grow, then make room for each other.
items.description: A month's spending as one stacked bar. The segments grow to their share on glide in a single cascade, then hold: reading one expands it on snap while its neighbours compress, and the label and amount surface inside the segment rather than in a tooltip over the bar. Turning a legend chip off drops that category and the bar re-flows on glide. Arrows walk the segments, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter pins a reading.

props.name: segments
props.type: { id: string; label: string; value: number; color: string }[]
props.description: Categories and amounts, left to right.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats amounts in the bar, the legend, and the total.

props.name: label
props.description: Bar title.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires with the segment being read; null when the reading is dropped.

usageNotes: The segments are a group of buttons with a roving tabindex that skips hidden categories: Left and Right walk them, Home and End jump to the ends, and Enter or Space pins a reading so it survives the pointer leaving. Legend chips are toggle buttons carrying aria-pressed.
Under reduced motion the widths are set without spring and only the labels fade; the shares still show, because the breakdown is the information.
Each segment's wash is mixed into the surface colour, so the reading inside it keeps its contrast in both themes; the amount lives inside the segment, so nothing overlays the bar.

items.title: Crosshair Chart
items.tagline: The dot rides the line under your hand.
items.description: A line chart you read with your hand. The trace draws itself on mount with pathLength on glide and the area fades in a beat behind it; moving a pointer snaps a crosshair to the nearest sample and the dot rides the line on flick, with a readout whose digits roll from a motion value instead of a re-render. The plot is a slider: Left and Right step one sample, Home and End jump to the ends, Escape clears the crosshair.

props.name: points
props.description: The series, left to right; each sample carries a label and a value.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every number the chart says out loud, the rolling readout included.

props.name: height
props.description: Plot height in px. The width is fluid and measured, so nothing overhangs a phone.

props.name: label
props.description: Series name — the chart's accessible name and the readout's caption.

props.name: color
props.description: Trace and fill colour; any CSS colour, defaulting to the signal token.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires with the index under the crosshair, or null when it clears.

usageNotes: The plot carries role=slider: Left and Right step one sample, Up and Down do the same, Home and End jump to the ends, Escape clears the crosshair, and aria-valuetext speaks the point under it.
Under reduced motion the trace is painted whole with no self-draw and the dot jumps between samples — the reading still changes, because the reading is the information.

Every sample is also listed for assistive technology, so the chart means something with no pointer at all; the hover readout is absolutely placed and clamped inside the plot, so a rolling number never moves the page.
Touch keeps pan-y, so the page still scrolls through the chart while horizontal travel scrubs it.

items.title: Gantt Lane
items.tagline: Bars slide into their lanes; hover lights the chain.
items.description: A plan on three weeks of grid. Bars arrive a shift from their lane in cascade() order on glide, hovering or focusing one lights its whole chain and draws the connectors with pathLength on flick, and dragging a bar tracks the pointer 1:1, pushes any dependent it would overrun, then settles onto the whole day on snap. Left and Right nudge the focused bar a day, Up and Down walk the lanes, Enter pins the chain and Escape unpins it.

props.name: tasks
props.description: Seeds the lanes as day offsets from the chart start; the chart owns positions after that and reports through onChange.

props.name: days
props.description: Columns in the grid. The lanes scroll horizontally under edge fades when they outrun the viewport.

props.name: today
props.description: Day offset the today line stands on. Omit it and no line is drawn.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires with the whole plan after a drag settles or a keyboard nudge lands.

props.name: formatDay
props.description: Names a day offset for the header ticks, the bars' aria-describedby dates and the live readout.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires with the hovered or focused task id, or null when nothing is lit.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible chart label. Omit it and pass aria-label to name the chart invisibly.

usageNotes: Bars are buttons carrying their dates through aria-describedby: Left and Right nudge the focused bar one day, Up and Down walk the lanes, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter pins the chain lit and Escape unpins it.
Dragging captures the pointer only after 4px of travel, so a tap still reaches the click that pins a chain, and a synthetic sweep can never throw on capture.
Under reduced motion bars appear in place with no cascade and connectors are drawn already complete — the plan still moves, because the dates are the information.
The task-name column stays pinned while the lanes scroll horizontally under edge fades; nothing overhangs a 342px viewport.

items.title: Sort Table
items.tagline: Click a header; the rows trade places.
