Under reduced motion the marker and the fill swap to their positions on a tween with no spring; the flag still cross-fades and the months figure swaps in place.
Also exports projectGoalMonths(saved, goal, monthly) so a host can print the same projection the marker shows.

items.title: Pot Shuffle
items.tagline: Move money between pots.
items.description: A row of savings jars with a liquid level and a figure each. Dragging from one jar tilts it toward the pointer on glide and lifts a coin; releasing over another jar sends the coin along an arc on glide and drops it in on recoil, and only then do the levels glide and both figures roll their digits on snap. The keyboard runs the same move — Enter or Space lifts, Arrow keys walk the row, Enter or Space drops, Escape cancels — and every step is announced.

props.name: pots / defaultPots
props.description: { id, name, balance }[], controlled or initial.

props.name: onPotsChange
props.description: Fires when a move lands, with the whole new row.

props.name: onMove
props.type: (from: string, to: string, amount: number) => void
props.description: Fires alongside it with just the move.

props.name: step
props.description: Money moved by one drop, clamped to what the source holds.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every figure. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the row.

usageNotes: Each jar is a button named by the pot and its balance, in a roving tabindex: Left and Right walk the row, Home and End jump, Enter or Space lifts a coin and drops it on another jar, Escape puts it back. A hint line says what to do next and a status line announces each lift, move and cancel.

Under reduced motion there is no tilt and no arc: the coin waits on its jar and fades at the drop, whose completion still commits the move; the levels move on a tween and the figures swap their digits in place.
The move commits — and onPotsChange fires — when the coin lands, not when the pointer lets go, so the figures roll the moment the money arrives.

items.title: Streak Saver
items.tagline: Weeks in a row.
items.description: A weekly saving streak as a row of cells, oldest on the left and the current week on the right. Saving lights the current cell — the fill lands from 0.6× on snap, one crisp overshoot, a light switching on — while a halo blooms and fades on a tween and the streak count rolls to the new run on the same beat. When the calendar advances the oldest cell leaves on the exit ease, the rest glide left one column as a layout move, a new outlined cell arrives from the right, and a week left unsaved dims to a hatched cell on a colour tween: nothing celebrates a miss. The cells are a labelled list that reads as sentences, the Save button stays focusable once pressed, and a status line announces the run once per change.

props.name: weeks
props.description: Oldest first; the last entry is the current week. Each carries an id, a date label and whether it was saved: a past week unsaved is missed, the current week unsaved is open.

props.name: amount
props.description: The weekly contribution, printed on the Save button and used for the total put away.

props.name: onSave
props.description: Fires from the Save press for the current week.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the saver; printed as the heading and read as the list's label.

usageNotes: The Save button is a real button — Tab reaches it, Enter and Space press it — and once the week is saved it turns aria-disabled rather than disabled, so focus stays where the press was; each cell reads as a sentence and a status line announces the run once per change.

Under reduced motion a lit cell fades to its colour, the row's shift swaps positions, the missed cell still dims and the digits swap in place — the cell still lights and the count still updates, because the run is the information.
An open current week does not break the streak; it only leaves it at risk. The parent owns the calendar: append a new open week and drop the oldest to advance it.

items.title: Auto Sweep
items.tagline: Whatever is left, swept.
items.description: A month-end sweep: two tiles, Spending and Savings, and above them a lane where a dashed arc runs from one figure to the other. Pressing Sweep lifts the leftover out of the spending tile as a pill that travels the arc on glide — the curve is closed-form, so the pill's position is one progress value and the trail draws itself just ahead of it — while the spending figure rolls down on snap the moment the pill leaves and the savings figure rolls up only when it lands, dropping the last nudge on recoil as the tile's wash flashes once. Any increase in savings mounts the same flight, so a parent that sweeps on its own schedule animates the same way. The figures are a definition list, the button's name says what it sweeps, and a status line announces the landing.

props.name: balance
props.description: The spending balance. Rolls down when a sweep leaves.

props.name: savings
props.description: The savings balance. An increase mounts a flight carrying the difference; the figure rolls when it lands.

props.name: keep
props.description: The floor left in spending; the leftover is balance minus keep, never below zero.

props.name: period
props.description: The sweep's occasion, printed under the heading ("Month end · 30 Sep").

props.name: onSweep
props.description: Fires from the Sweep press with the leftover; move the money here.

props.name: onSettle
props.description: Fires when the pill lands in savings.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the control; printed as the heading and read as the group's label.

usageNotes: The Sweep button is a real button — Tab reaches it, Enter and Space press it — and with nothing above the floor it turns aria-disabled rather than disabled, so focus stays put; the two balances read as a definition list and a status line announces the landing.

Under reduced motion the pill fades in over the spending figure and out over the savings figure with no travel, the trail is skipped, the wash still flashes and the digits swap in place — the money still visibly moves from one figure to the other.
The parent owns the money: move it in onSweep and the component animates the difference, so a sweep triggered by a schedule looks exactly like one triggered by the button.

items.title: Goal Card
items.tagline: One goal, one card.
items.description: One card for one goal: a ring whose stroke is the share saved, the goal's name and figure beside it, an add control, and a details toggle that unfolds a panel underneath. Pressing Add mints a coin at the ring's rim that drops into the hub on recoil — the two visible bounces of a coin landing in a slot — and only when it lands does the ring grow to the new share on glide and the hub's percentage roll on snap, so the ring moves because the coin arrived; reaching the goal turns the ring success and draws a tick on flick. The panel's height is measured by a ResizeObserver and animated on glide with the chevron turning on snap. The ring is a meter that carries the share in words, the panel is inert while closed, and a status line announces each add once.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial amount saved. An increase mints a coin and the ring waits for it to land; a decrease shrinks the ring at once with no coin.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the Add press that changed the amount, with the new total and what was added.

props.name: goal
props.description: The target; the ring closes here and Add turns aria-disabled once it is reached.

props.name: step
props.description: The amount one Add press contributes, clamped so the last press lands exactly on the goal.

props.name: weekly
props.description: Planned contribution per week; the panel projects the weeks left from it.

props.name: deadline
props.description: A quiet line in the panel ("By 30 Nov").

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial state of the details panel.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the Details toggle press.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: The goal's name; printed as the heading and read as the meter's label.

usageNotes: Add and Details are real buttons — Tab reaches them, Enter and Space press them. Details carries aria-expanded and aria-controls for the panel, which is inert while closed so it never traps a Tab; the ring is a meter whose value text reads the share in words, and a status line announces each add and the moment the goal is reached.

Under reduced motion the coin fades in at the hub and out again so the add is still acknowledged, the ring and percentage move on a base tween, the tick appears complete and the panel's height tweens on fast — the ring still fills and the panel still opens.
Both the amount and the panel are controlled or uncontrolled: pass value and onValueChange to own the money, open and onOpenChange to own the disclosure, or defaults for either.

items.title: Rate Ladder
items.tagline: Longer terms, higher rungs.
items.description: A ladder of term deposits: two stiles with a rung per term, the shortest at the bottom and the longest at the top, so higher rungs pay more. Picking a rung lifts it off the stiles on snap — two pixels up, a raised surface and a cobalt edge, one crisp overshoot — while the rung it replaces settles back, and on the same beat the headline rate rolls its digits and, given a principal, the interest at maturity rolls beside it. Beneath the ladder a timeline runs from the deposit date to the longest term: a marker and its date flag slide on glide to the chosen maturity while the elapsed track fills to it, with the flag clamped inside the axis against measured widths. The ladder is a radio group with a roving tabindex where arrows select as they move, and the readout is a status line that announces a pick once.

props.name: rungs
props.description: Term deposits as { months, rate }, ascending by months; the rate is percent per year.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial term in months.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that picked a rung.

props.name: amount
props.description: Principal; given it, the interest at maturity (amount × rate ÷ 100 × months ÷ 12) is shown and read.

props.name: start
props.description: The deposit date as YYYY-MM-DD; the timeline starts here and maturities are computed in UTC, so no clock is read.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: formatDate
props.description: Formats the maturity date on the flag, the axis and in every sentence.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the ladder; printed as the heading and read as the radio group's label.

usageNotes: A radio group under the hood: Tab lands on the chosen rung, Up and Right step to a longer term and Down and Left to a shorter one without wrapping, Home is the shortest and End the longest, arrows select as they move, and Space or Enter select the focused rung. Each rung is named by its sentence and the readout is a status line, so a pick is announced once.

Under reduced motion the chosen rung changes colour and edge only, the rate and interest swap their digits in place, and the marker and track fill jump on a fast tween — which rung is chosen still shows.
Pass start as a fixed date rather than today's: the ladder never reads a clock, so server and client render the same maturities.

items.title: Nest Egg
items.tagline: The long view, compounding.
items.description: A chart of a balance compounding over the years: a principal plus a monthly contribution, compounded monthly at the chosen rate. On mount the curve draws itself from year zero with pathLength on glide over a dashed line of the contributions alone, so the gap between them — the growth — is the picture. The plot is a slider: pressing or dragging reads the value at the nearest year, a cursor and a dot travelling to it on snap while a callout above rolls the year's balance with the contributed and growth split beneath. The rate chips morph the path on glide — every path has the same point count, so the curve bends rather than blinks — against a vertical scale fixed to the highest offered rate, so a higher rate visibly lifts the curve. Arrows step a year, Page keys five, Home and End reach the ends, and a status line announces the settled year, never every year a drag passes through.

props.name: principal
props.description: The opening balance.

props.name: monthly
props.description: The monthly contribution, compounded monthly at the chosen rate.

props.name: years
props.description: The horizon; the plot has a point per year and the slider runs from 0 to here.

props.name: rates
props.description: The rate chips in percent per year; the vertical scale fits the highest so a higher rate lifts the curve rather than rescaling it.

props.name: rate / defaultRate
props.description: Controlled or initial annual rate in percent.

props.name: onRateChange
props.description: Fires from the chip press or key.

props.name: year / defaultYear
props.description: Controlled or initial scrub position in years.

props.name: onYearChange
props.description: Fires from the pointer or key that moved the cursor.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the chart; printed as the heading and read as the slider's label.

usageNotes: The plot is a slider: Tab reaches it, Left and Right (or Down and Up) step a year, Page Down and Page Up step five, Home and End reach year 0 and the horizon, and its value text reads the balance, the contributions and the growth as one sentence. The rate chips are a radio group with a roving tabindex where Left and Right step, Home and End jump, and Space selects.

Under reduced motion the curve is already drawn on mount, a rate change swaps the path in place, the cursor and dot jump, and the callout's digits swap without rolling — the value at the year still reads, because that is the information.

Pointer capture waits for four pixels of travel, so a plain press sets the nearest year and a synthetic sweep cannot throw; the status line holds the last settled year during a drag and catches up on release.

items.title: Mover List
items.tagline: Who moved most today.
items.description: A board of assets ranked by percent change. When prices tick, every row that changes seat travels to its new one with a position-only FLIP on glide while the rank column re-reads in place, and each updated chip mounts a wash keyed to that tick that flashes and fades on the exit ease. A radio pair swaps gainers for losers with Left and Right, Home and End, and Space; a polite live region names the leader once the tape goes quiet.

props.name: assets
props.description: The board: id, symbol, name, price and previousClose. Changing a price flashes that row's chip and re-sorts the rows.

props.name: view / defaultView
props.description: Controlled or initial sort direction.

props.name: onViewChange
props.description: Fires from the radio that changed the view.

props.name: limit
props.description: Rows shown; the rest leave on the exit ease.

props.name: format
props.description: Prints every price. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: flashMs
props.description: How long a chip's flash takes to fade, and the quiet the live region waits for before naming the leader.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the list for assistive technology and prints in the header.

props.name: onOrderChange
props.description: Fires from the effect that observed a new order, with the visible ids top to bottom.

usageNotes: The view control is a radio group with a roving tabindex: Left and Right step between gainers and losers, Home and End jump, Space selects. Each row reads rank, asset, price and change as one sentence, so the sign never rides on colour alone.
Under reduced motion rows swap seats without travel and chips still flash and fade in place — an update is information, the travel was the flourish.
Which chips flash is decided by comparing each incoming price with the last committed one, so a re-render that changes nothing flashes nothing and the first paint never flashes.

items.title: Price Sparkline
items.tagline: A day in one line.
items.description: A day's prices as one line that grows across its frame. Each arriving point draws only the newest segment with pathLength on glide while the points before it hold still, the last point's dot travels to its new place on glide with a halo that breathes on a slow reversing tween and a ring that expands on each arrival, and once the day overfills the frame the window slides. Hovering snaps a hairline to the nearest print and the header reads its time and price; the plot is a slider where Left and Right walk the points, Home and End jump, and Escape returns to the latest.

props.name: points
props.description: The day's prints as { time, price }, oldest first. Appending one extends the line by a segment.

props.name: capacity
props.description: Points across the full width; more than this slides the window to the last capacity points.

props.name: format
props.description: Prints every price. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: height
props.description: Plot height in px; the width is fluid and measured with a ResizeObserver.

props.name: label
props.description: The instrument; prints in the header and names the slider.

props.name: onReadChange
props.type: (point: SparkPricePoint | null, index: number | null) => void
props.description: Fires from the pointer or key that moved the reading to a point, or returned it to the latest (null).

usageNotes: The plot is a horizontal slider: Left and Right walk one print, Home and End jump to the ends, Escape returns the reading to the latest; aria-valuetext speaks the time and price of the point under the hairline.
Under reduced motion the newest segment appears fully drawn, the dot swaps position and no halo or ring plays — the hairline and readout still follow the pointer and the keys.
The polite live region names the latest print once the tape has been quiet for a beat, never per point.

items.title: Watchlist Row
items.tagline: Starred, and watched.
items.description: One row of a watchlist whose star is a switch: watching scales the fill up from the star's centre on recoil, two visible bounces of a stamp landing, while the price rolls to each print on snap and the change chip re-tones. Unstarring drains the fill, holds a beat so the empty star is read, then slides the content out on the exit ease and collapses the row's measured height behind it, firing onRemoved from the collapse's completion. Tab reaches the star, Space and Enter toggle it.

props.name: id
props.description: Identifies the row in onRemoved.

props.name: symbol
props.description: The ticker printed first and named in the star's label.

props.name: name
props.description: The asset's name, printed under the symbol.

props.name: price
props.description: The last print. Changing it rolls the digits on snap.

props.name: previousClose
props.description: Basis for the change chip.

props.name: watched / defaultWatched
props.description: Controlled or initial star state; false starts the leave after the beat.

props.name: onWatchedChange
props.description: Fires from the press that toggled the star.

props.name: onRemoved
props.description: Fires once the row has slid out and collapsed; drop it from the list here.

props.name: format
props.description: Prints the price. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: leaveDelayMs
props.description: The beat between unstarring and the slide-out, so the empty star is read; re-starring inside it cancels the leave.

usageNotes: The star is a real switch: Tab reaches it, Space and Enter toggle it, its name carries the symbol, and the row speaks price and change in words while the rolling columns stay hidden from assistive technology.
Under reduced motion the fill appears without scale, the digits swap without rolling, and the row still leaves — it fades and collapses without the sideways travel.
Renders as an li: compose rows inside a ul or ol, and remove a row from your list in onRemoved rather than on the star press, so the slide-out is seen.

items.title: Price Alert
items.tagline: Tell me when it crosses.
items.description: A threshold line dragged over a price chart. The line sits directly under the hand once a press has travelled four pixels, a plain click or a key moves it on snap, and the alert badge follows it through a spring on glide so the label trails the tool by a beat. When the last price lands on the other side of the line the badge pulses — landing from 1.25× on recoil with a ring that expands on the enter ease — and onCross fires; moving the line re-arms it without a pulse. The badge is a vertical slider: Up and Down step, Page keys jump ten, Home and End reach the bounds.

props.name: points
props.description: Prices oldest first; the last one is the live print the crossing is judged against.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial threshold.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, click or key that moved the line.

props.name: min / max
props.description: The chart's vertical range and the threshold's bounds.

props.name: step
props.description: Threshold granularity; arrow keys move one step, Page keys ten.

props.name: format
props.description: Prints the threshold and prices. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: height
props.description: Plot height in px; the width is fluid and measured with a ResizeObserver.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the slider and prints in the header.

props.name: onCross
props.description: Fires from the effect that observed the last price crossing the line, with the side it landed on.

usageNotes: The badge is a vertical slider: ArrowUp and ArrowDown move one step, PageUp and PageDown ten, Home and End jump to min and max; aria-valuetext says whether the alert is waiting for a rise or a fall, or has crossed.
Under reduced motion the line and the badge move together with no spring lag, and a crossing flips the tone and the words with a blink instead of a bounce and a ring.
Only a price movement counts as a crossing — dragging the line across the current price re-arms the alert quietly.

items.title: Heat Tiles
items.tagline: The market as a grid of heat.
items.description: A grid of asset tiles coloured by percent change: a success layer and a danger layer sit under each tile's text and their opacities tween on the move ease, so a tile warms as a gain grows, cools as it fades, and cross-fades on a sign flip. Pressing a tile opens it in place — it spans two columns and two rows while the rest of the grid re-lays around it with layout on glide, dense-packed so no hole opens — and reveals the name, price, a day sparkline and the high and low. Tiles are buttons with a roving tabindex: arrows move, Home and End jump, Enter and Space toggle, Escape closes.

props.name: assets
props.description: The board: id, symbol, name, price, previousClose and an optional history for the open tile's sparkline. Changing a price re-tints its tile.

props.name: columns
props.description: Tiles per row; an open tile spans two columns and two rows.

props.name: expanded / defaultExpanded
props.description: Controlled or initial open tile id.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that opened or closed a tile.

props.name: scale
props.description: Percent change at which a tile's tint saturates.

props.name: format
props.description: Prints the open tile's price, high and low. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the grid for assistive technology and prints above it.

usageNotes: Roving tabindex over real buttons: Left and Right move one tile, Up and Down move a row, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter and Space toggle a tile, Escape closes the open one and keeps focus. Each tile's name is a sentence with the change in words, so the tint is never the only signal.
Under reduced motion the tints still tween — colour is the information — but tiles swap seats without travel and the details fade in without a delay.
Tints saturate at scale percent; lower it for a quiet market so small moves still read, raise it for a volatile one so the grid is not all colour.

items.title: Index Dial
items.tagline: The whole market, one needle.
items.description: A half-dial for a market index, zeroed on the previous close: the needle stands straight up when the index is flat and swings left for a fall or right for a rise. Each print swings it on snap — one crisp overshoot, the way a real needle overshoots a new reading — and the arc from the zero mark to the needle is drawn from the same motion value, success on the up side and danger on the down side, so the sign is the reading. The level rolls its digit columns on the same spring and a chip carries the percent; it is a role=meter whose valuetext reads the move in words, and nothing takes focus.

props.name: value
props.description: The index level. Changing it swings the needle and rolls the figure.

props.name: previousClose
props.description: The basis; the dial's zero.

props.name: range
props.description: Percent each side of zero the dial spans; larger moves pin the needle at the rim.

props.name: format
props.description: Prints the index level. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: The index name; labels the meter.

props.name: caption
props.description: A quiet mono line beside the label — the venue.

props.name: swingOnMount
props.description: Start the needle at zero and swing it to the value on first paint.

props.name: onSettle
props.description: Fires from the spring's completion when the needle comes to rest.

usageNotes: The dial has no pointer gesture and takes no focus: it is a role=meter whose aria-valuetext reads the level and the move in words, and each settled print is announced once through a polite status line.
Under reduced motion the needle and arc set at once, the digits swap without a roll and the chip appears in place — the arc still colours by sign, because the reading is the information.
Moves beyond range pin the needle at the rim while the figure and chip print the full change.

items.title: Sector Wheel
items.tagline: Sectors, as wedges.
items.description: A ring of market sectors drawn as stroked wedges whose widths are their performance: each sector's share is its absolute move plus a small baseline, coloured success or danger by sign, and a change of data re-proportions every wedge's pathLength and pathOffset on one glide so the ring settles as a body. Choosing a sector spins the wheel on snap, the shorter way round, until that wedge sits under the notch at twelve o'clock, the hub cross-fades to its name and move, and a measured panel glides open on its movers in a cascade. The wheel can be grabbed after four pixels of travel and released onto a wedge; the chips beneath are a radiogroup with a roving tabindex, so the arrow keys spin it too.

props.name: sectors
props.description: Clockwise from the notch: { id, label, change, movers: { symbol, name, change }[] }, moves in percent.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial selected sector id.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press, key or release that chose a sector.

props.name: baseline
props.description: Percent points added to every wedge's magnitude so a flat sector keeps a readable slice.

props.name: formatChange
props.description: Prints a move.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible heading. Omit it and pass aria-label.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Invisible label when label is omitted.

usageNotes: The chips are a radiogroup with a roving tabindex: Right and Down step to the next sector, Left and Up to the previous, Home and End jump to the first and last, Space selects — and every step spins the wheel to that wedge's detent, the same spin the pointer makes by dragging the ring.

Under reduced motion the wedges set to their shares and the wheel rotates by an instant swap so the chosen sector still sits under the notch; the hub cross-fades by opacity and the movers appear without stagger or travel.

Each radio is named by the sector and its move in words, the mover list is a real ordered list labelled by the sector, and a polite status line announces the chosen sector and its top mover on each change.

items.title: Earnings Countdown
items.tagline: Results, in three days.
items.description: A card that counts down to a company's results: a ring drains toward the report, its fraction the seconds left over a window, while a mono readout rolls its digit columns on snap as each second lands. The clock is the component's own, seeded from a prop and ticking in an effect that halts while the document is hidden. When results land the ring closes on snap and turns success, the actual figures roll in beside the estimates on the same spring, and a verdict chip appears — Beat on recoil because a beat is a landing, Miss and In line on snap with no bounce. Reaching zero without results swaps the readout to Due and holds; nothing takes focus.

props.name: label
props.description: What is being reported; labels the card.

props.name: seconds
props.description: Seconds until the report when the clock is seeded; changing it re-seeds the clock.

props.name: window
props.description: Seconds the full ring represents; three days by default.

props.name: running
props.description: Ticks the clock.

props.name: estimate
props.description: The consensus figures.

props.name: actual
props.description: The reported figures; providing them lands the results.

props.name: format
props.description: Prints earnings per share.

props.name: formatRevenue
props.description: Prints revenue.

props.name: onElapsed
props.description: Fires from the tick that reached zero.

props.name: onLand
props.description: Fires from the effect that observed the actual figures arrive.

usageNotes: The card is a role="group" labelled by its label; the readout is a role="timer" with aria-live="off" whose aria-label carries the time in words, so a screen reader is never read every second. The figures are a definition list, unreported actuals are labelled Not yet reported, and a polite status line announces milestones only: the clock starting, results due, and results landing with the verdict in words.

Under reduced motion the digits swap without a roll, the ring still drains second by second because a countdown is information, the actual figures appear in place and the verdict chip fades in with no travel or bounce.
No pointer gesture and no wall clock: the clock ticks from its seed in an effect with its own interval, halts entirely while the document is hidden, and never reads the time during render.

items.title: News Ticker
items.tagline: Headlines that pass, and pause.
items.description: A single line of market headlines flowing right to left on one frame loop that integrates the tape's velocity toward a target with exponential friction: the cruising speed while playing, zero the moment a pointer is over it, a headline holds focus, or play is off, so the tape eases to a stop and eases back up rather than freezing. Headlines are real buttons; focusing one pauses the tape and glides it into view on glide. A new headline is spliced into the ring after the item under the right edge, arrives from distances.shift on snap behind a signal wash that fades on the exit ease, and the ring's ResizeObserver moves the tape by exactly the width it added so nothing already on screen jumps.

props.name: headlines
props.description: In arrival order: { id, text, source, time, tone? } where time is an already-formatted string and tone is "up" | "down" | "flat". A new id pushes in at the right edge.

props.name: playing / defaultPlaying
props.description: Controlled or initial play state. Off, the tape eases to a stop.

props.name: onPlayingChange
props.description: Fires from the tape's own Pause/Play toggle.

props.name: speed
props.description: Cruising speed in px/s.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fires from the press on a headline.

props.name: onPauseChange
props.description: Fires from the hover, focus or play change that paused or resumed the tape.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the region.

usageNotes: A visible Pause/Play toggle with aria-pressed is first in the tab order and last on screen; Tab then walks the headlines of the first ring copy, each focus pausing the tape and gliding that headline into view. The loop copies are aria-hidden and inert, so the tape reads once.

Under reduced motion there is no tape: the headlines render as a wrapped row of chips, newest first, a new one appears in place with the same flash in opacity only, and the pause control is not shown because nothing moves.

New headlines are announced once, politely, as "New: text, source" from the effect that observed the arrival, never per frame; tone is carried by a caret and the words in each button's name, not by colour alone. The loop halts entirely while the document is hidden.

items.title: Compare Lines
items.tagline: Two assets, one chart.
items.description: Two assets on one plate, each series normalised to its own first point so the lines share a scale of percent-since-start and a dashed baseline at zero. On mount both traces draw in together — pathLength from 0 to 1 on one durations.page tween with the enter ease — so they finish on the same frame and the eye reads the divergence as it happens. The legend is two toggles: hiding a series fades its line and area on the exit ease with no redraw, and the vertical domain is fixed across both series so a toggle never re-scales the plate. Pointing at the plate sets a cursor at the nearest sample — a hairline, a dot per visible series, a bar between them and a readout chip that prints both values and the gap in percentage points — and the chip moves on snap while keeping inside the plate; the plate is a focusable group where Left and Right step the cursor, Home and End jump to the ends and Escape clears it.

props.name: series
props.description: { id, label, points: number[] }, closes oldest first; both series share the same sample count.

props.name: labels
props.description: Already-formatted x labels, one per sample, for the readout.

props.name: hidden / defaultHidden
props.description: Controlled or initial set of hidden series ids.

props.name: onHiddenChange
props.description: Fires from the toggle that changed it.

props.name: onCursorChange
props.description: Fires from the pointer or key that moved the cursor.

props.name: format
props.description: Prints a raw close in the readout. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible heading. Omit it and pass aria-label.

props.name: height
props.description: Plate height in px; the width is fluid and measured.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Invisible label when label is omitted.

usageNotes: The plate is a focusable role="group" labelled by the heading and described by both series' final moves: Left and Right step the cursor, Home and End jump to the ends, Escape clears it, as does leaving or blurring the plate. The legend toggles are aria-pressed buttons named Show or Hide plus the series, and a polite status line reads the cursor's sample, each visible series in words and the gap in points.
Under reduced motion both traces are simply there, complete; toggling still fades because opacity is the one motion allowed, and the cursor readout swaps position without a spring.
The gap is the first series' percent minus the second's, positive when the first leads; lead is carried in words and a sign, and the two series use cobalt and warn so neither reads as up or down.

items.title: Tip Terminal
items.tagline: The customer's turn.
items.description: A customer-facing tip screen. Preset, no-tip and custom chips form one radio group whose highlight travels on snap; Custom opens a numeric pad grown to a measured height on glide, and the tip and total count to each figure on glide. The confirm is a slide: the knob follows the finger, springs back on snap from a short pull, and past 80% glides home and draws its check on flick. Arrows walk the chips; Enter, Space or End confirm.

props.name: subtotal
props.description: The bill before the tip.

props.name: presets
props.description: Percentages offered as chips, each printed with the money it comes to.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial choice: a preset percent, a custom amount, or none.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the chip or pad key that changed the tip.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Fires from the release or key that confirmed the payment.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount the terminal prints.

props.name: label
props.description: The merchant's name, printed above the subtotal.

usageNotes: The chips are a radio group with a roving tabindex: arrows move and select, Home and End jump, Space selects. The pad is a group of real buttons. The confirm knob is a button: Enter, Space or End confirm by keyboard, and a pointer must slide it past 80% of the track — a plain tap only nudges it.

Under reduced motion the pad still opens to its measured height on a fast tween, figures swap in place, the knob still tracks a drag and returns instantly, and the paid state swaps in by opacity alone.
Once confirmed every chip and key is disabled and the status region announces the paid total; mount a fresh terminal (a new key) for the next order.

items.title: Split Ways
items.tagline: Split the bill any way you like.
items.description: A bill split by count, by item, or by amount. The mode switch's knob rides its track on snap, and each mode re-lays the people at the table as FLIP on glide: equal cards in a grid, full-width rows holding item chips that travel between seats under a shared layoutId, or rows with a stepper and an unassigned line beneath. Every share counts to its figure on glide and the list's height is measured, never reserved. Arrows walk the modes; chips and steppers are buttons.

props.name: total
props.description: The bill.

props.name: people
props.description: Who is at the table, in seat order: { id, name }.

props.name: items
props.description: What was ordered, { id, label, amount }; the item mode hands these between seats.

props.name: mode / defaultMode
props.description: Controlled or initial mode.

props.name: onModeChange
props.description: Fires from the radio that changed the mode.

props.name: defaultAssignments
props.description: Item id to person id for the item mode; unlisted items start with the first seat.

props.name: defaultAmounts
props.description: Person id to amount for the amount mode.

props.name: onSharesChange
props.description: Fires from the event that changed any share, with every person's share and the mode they belong to.

props.name: step
props.description: Amount the stepper moves per press.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount the control prints.

props.name: label
props.description: Printed above the mode switch.

usageNotes: The mode switch is a radio group with a roving tabindex: arrows move and select, Home and End jump, Space selects. Each item chip is a button that hands the item to the next seat; each stepper is a pair of buttons named for the person.
Under reduced motion rows and chips swap position instantly and every figure swaps in place; the shares and the unassigned line still update.
By count always sums to the bill; by item and by amount print what is unassigned or over beneath the list, so a split that does not add up says so.

items.title: Refund Flow
items.tagline: Money going back.
items.description: A refund card for one charge. The amount slider cannot pass the original — the track ends where the charge does — and pressing Refund sends the figure back along a route: the line fills and a pill carrying the amount travels to the customer's card on glide, then a REFUNDED stamp lands on it on recoil as onRefund fires. The slider takes arrows, Page keys, Home and End; the button is a real button.

props.name: original
props.description: The original charge; the slider's cap.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial refund amount.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, click or key that moved the amount.

props.name: onRefund
props.description: Fires when the refund lands on the card.

props.name: step
props.description: Keyboard step and drag snap; Page keys move ten.

props.name: merchant
props.description: The payee the money leaves.

props.name: cardLabel
props.description: The customer's card, as it should print.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount the card prints.

usageNotes: The slider is a role="slider" capped at the original: arrows step, Page keys move ten steps, Home and End reach zero and the whole charge. Capture is taken only after 4px, so a plain click sets the amount.
Under reduced motion the pill appears at the card instead of travelling and the stamp fades in without bouncing; the refund still lands and the status region still announces it.
The landing timer runs only while the document is visible, and once refunded the card locks — mount a fresh card (a new key) for the next charge.

items.title: Receipt Print
items.tagline: Printed, torn, done.
items.description: A till receipt out of a printer mouth. When printing turns on, lines feed out one at a time on a timer that pauses while the tab is hidden, each arriving on flick as the paper grows to a measured height on glide; the last line is a procedural barcode. Once printed the receipt tears: pulling it down follows the hand with resistance and past the tear distance the sheet leaves on the exit ease, a short pull springs back on snap, and a Tear off button tears by keyboard.

props.name: lines
props.description: The lines, top to bottom: { id, label, amount?, kind?: "item" | "total" | "note" }.

props.name: printing
props.description: Turning it on prints from the first line; turning it off clears the mouth for the next receipt.

props.name: onPrinted
props.description: Fires from the timer that printed the last line.

props.name: onTear
props.description: Fires from the release or key that tore the receipt away.

props.name: interval
props.description: Milliseconds between lines.

props.name: header
props.description: The merchant's name at the head of the paper; it also seeds the barcode.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount the paper prints.

usageNotes: The paper is a labelled region of real list items; once printed, a Tear off button below it tears by keyboard, and the paper itself tears by a pull past 44px of resisted travel. Capture is taken only after 4px so the sweep of a pointer never throws.
Under reduced motion lines still appear on the same timer, opacity only, the paper still grows on a fast tween, and a tear fades the sheet out instead of dropping it.
The feed timer pauses while the document is hidden and resumes on the line it stopped at; flip printing off and on again to print a fresh receipt.

items.title: Queue Number
items.tagline: Your number, called.
items.description: A branch queue display for one customer. The now-serving figure is an odometer whose digit columns roll up to each new face on snap, wrapping 9 to 0 without changing direction; beneath it the customer's own card counts an estimated wait down one second at a time, re-syncs whenever the served number changes, and when called tints cobalt and breathes on drift. The board is a labelled group and the card's status sentence changes per call, never per second.

props.name: serving
props.description: The number now being served; the board rolls to it.

props.name: ticket
props.description: The customer's own number.

props.name: secondsPerTicket
props.description: Estimated seconds per ticket ahead; the wait is this times the tickets that remain.

props.name: running
props.description: Whether the estimate counts down.

props.name: format
props.description: How a number prints; digits become odometer columns, other characters print as they are.

props.name: label
props.description: The counter's name, printed above the figure.

usageNotes: The board is a role="group" labelled by the counter's name with a plain-text copy of the served number; the customer's card is decoration over an sr-only status sentence that reads the ticket, how many are before it and the wait in minutes — announced when the served number changes, never per second.
Under reduced motion digits swap in place, the called card tints and changes its text without breathing, and the countdown still ticks because the wait is information.
The countdown runs only while running is true and the document is visible; drive serving from your own queue feed and the estimate re-syncs on every change.

items.title: Cash Drawer
items.tagline: Open, count, close.
items.description: A till whose face plate stays put while the tray beneath it opens on snap: the tray's measured height springs from zero with one crisp overshoot, the latch popping, while the slots ride down from under the face. Count walks the denominations top to bottom on a timed tick that pauses while the tab is hidden, each slot climbing in steps so none takes longer than 600ms while its count, its subtotal and the drawer total roll on snap together; Close slides the tray back and the padlock's shackle drops on flick. Open, Count and Close are real buttons, the tray is an inert region while closed, and a status line announces open, counting, counted with the variance, and locked.

props.name: denominations
props.description: What is in the tray, largest first: value, count, and an optional kind of note or coin.

props.name: expected
props.description: The float the drawer should hold; enables the variance line (level, over, short).

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial drawer state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the Open or Close press.

props.name: onCount
props.description: Fires from the Count press, as the tally begins.

props.name: onTallied
props.description: Fires from the tick that finishes the count, with the drawer total.

props.name: onLock
props.description: Fires from the Close press with the tallied total, 0 if uncounted.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the drawer for the group and the tray region.

usageNotes: Open, Count and Close are real buttons in Tab order; Count is aria-disabled while the tally runs, and the tray is inert while the drawer is closed so nothing inside it can take focus.
Under reduced motion the tray's height tweens with no travel or overshoot, the counts still tick and the totals still update, but the digits swap in place and the shackle appears already dropped.
The tally lives in an effect with cleanup and stops while the document is hidden; onTallied fires from the tick that finishes it, never per tick, and the status line announces only phase changes.

items.title: Tap Reader
items.tagline: Ready, reading, approved.
items.description: A card reader's display: the amount above, a ring in the middle, one line of state below. Ready, a short arc at the top breathes on a mirrored opacity tween; the ring is a real button that squashes on flick, and the host answers the tap by moving status to reading, which sets the arc spinning on a linear tween. On approved the spinner finishes its turn to the top and grows into a full ring on glide while a check draws inside it on flick; on declined the ring turns danger, shakes on a five-keyframe tween and a cross draws. The button's accessible name carries the state and the amount, Enter and Space press it, and the state line is a status region announced once per outcome.

props.name: status
props.description: Controlled; the outcome comes from the host.

props.name: amount
props.description: The sale, in major units.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats the amount. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the reader, top left.

props.name: reference
props.description: A sale reference shown top right.

props.name: messages
props.description: Overrides the state line copy per status.

props.name: onTap
props.description: Fires from the press while ready.

props.name: onReset
props.description: Fires from the press after an outcome, when the button reads New sale or Try again.

usageNotes: The ring is one button: Enter and Space press it; while reading it is aria-disabled and aria-busy and presses are ignored; after an outcome the same press fires onReset.
Under reduced motion nothing breathes, spins, shakes or squashes: reading shows a still three-quarter arc, and each outcome shows its ring and glyph at once, by colour and opacity alone.
The reader never times anything itself: the host moves status from reading to approved or declined from its own effect or response.

items.title: Tender Switch
items.tagline: Card, cash, or split.
items.description: A three-stop radiogroup of tender methods whose one knob rides to the chosen stop on snap via a shared layoutId, while the chosen method's chip slides into the summary line from the left on snap as the old one leaves on the exit ease, so the method reads as having moved from the selector into the sale. Split unfolds two decimal fields below the summary, the region's measured height gliding open and the fields arriving in a cascade; they keep each other honest, editing one setting the other to the remainder clamped to the total, while a two-segment balance bar glides to the new proportion. Left and Right step without wrapping, Home and End jump, Space selects.

props.name: total
props.description: The sale total the tender must cover.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial method.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that changed the method.

props.name: cardAmount / defaultCardAmount
props.description: Controlled or initial card share when split; cash is always the remainder.

props.name: onCardAmountChange
props.description: Fires from the input that changed it, with the card share clamped to the total.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats the total and the summary amounts. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the radiogroup.

usageNotes: A radiogroup with a roving tabindex: Left and Right (or Up and Down) step without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump to card and split, Space selects; the split fields are labelled decimal inputs that join Tab order only while split is chosen, because the folded region is inert.
Under reduced motion the knob swaps stops with no travel, the chip cross-fades in place, the split region's height tweens on durations.base, and the bar widths tween.
Amounts are kept to cents and clamped to the total; the summary is a polite live region, and the balance bar is hidden from assistive technology because the fields already carry the numbers.

items.title: Line Item
items.tagline: Quantity that ticks.
items.description: One basket row with a stepper pill whose quantity digit rolls on snap at each press while the pressed button squashes on flick, and whose line total rolls in the same beat because the total moves only because the quantity did. At the minimum the minus cross-fades into a bin; pressing it collapses the row, its measured height tweening to zero on the exit ease with the content fading, and onRemove fires only when the collapse completes so the host can drop the item without a jump. The quantity is a spinbutton: Up and Down step, Home and End jump to the limits.

props.name: name
props.description: The item; also names the spinbutton and the remove control.

props.name: note
props.description: A variant or detail under the name.

props.name: unitPrice
props.description: Price per unit, in major units.

props.name: quantity / defaultQuantity
props.description: Controlled or initial quantity, clamped to min and max.

props.name: onQuantityChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that changed it.

props.name: min
props.description: The lowest quantity; at it the minus becomes remove when removable.

props.name: max
props.description: The highest quantity; also sets the width reserved for the rolling figures.

props.name: removable
props.description: At the minimum, minus becomes a remove control.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Fires when the collapse completes; drop the item from state here.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats the unit price and the line total. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

usageNotes: The quantity is a role=spinbutton with aria-valuenow, min and max: Up and Down step, Home and End jump to the limits; the buttons are named Decrease, Increase and Remove {name}, and a status line announces the quantity with its total, or Removed.
Under reduced motion the digits swap in place, the buttons do not squash, and removal fades the row on the exit ease before it collapses in one tween.
Render each LineItem inside its own li; onRemove fires after the collapse has finished, so dropping the item from state there causes no jump.

items.title: Day Close
items.tagline: The day, totalled.
items.description: An end-of-day card whose figures read as dashes until totalled, then reveal in sequence: each figure's digit columns mount at zero and roll up on snap, offset by cascade per figure and a shorter step per column, so the card reads as one sweep from top to bottom. Once the last column lands the category bars draw, each fill scaling from the left on glide in its own cascade with its share fading in behind, and closing stamps a rotated CLOSED over the figures on recoil, two bounces of ink hitting paper. One button carries the flow, Total the day, Close the day, Closed, and locks once closed.

props.name: figures
props.description: The figures top to bottom: id, label, value and an optional tone of neutral, success or danger. The last one is announced as the net.

props.name: categories
props.description: The bars: id, label and value; shares are computed from their sum.

props.name: state / defaultState
props.description: Controlled or initial state.

props.name: onStateChange
props.description: Fires from the press that advanced it.

props.name: heading
props.description: The day, as text.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every figure and bar amount. The default pins an explicit locale so server and client agree.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the card for the group.

usageNotes: One button carries the whole flow with a changing label and is disabled once closed; Enter and Space press it. The figures are a dl whose values carry the printed amount or not totalled as text, and the bars read label, amount and share.
Under reduced motion the figures appear complete with no roll and no stagger, the bars fill on a tween, and the stamp fades in without scale or bounce.
A card that mounts already totalled or closed shows its figures and stamp complete; only a change after mount earns the sweep, so a reopened day rolls again when it is totalled.

items.title: Bill Calendar
items.tagline: Every bill, on the day it lands.
items.description: A month of bills, each on the day it lands, over a balance line that shows what the account holds on every one of those days. The line is one column per day — a balance is piecewise-constant between bills — and each column's height animates on glide, so moving a bill re-plots the month with a layout's physics. Dragging a chip captures the pointer only after 4px of travel while a carry chip follows it inside the card's frame and the day beneath lights as the drop target; on release the bill lands on recoil. Arrows walk days, Enter lifts the bill on the focused day, arrows choose its new day, Enter drops it and Escape cancels.

props.name: bills / defaultBills
props.description: Controlled or initial bills, each with id, label, amount and day.

props.name: onBillsChange
props.description: Fires from the drop or the keyboard move that changed a day.

props.name: onBillMove
props.type: (bill: Bill, fromDay: number, toDay: number) => void
props.description: Fires alongside it with the move itself, for an undo line.

props.name: openingBalance
props.description: What the account holds before the first of the month.

props.name: days
props.description: Days in the month.

props.name: startWeekday
props.description: Column the 1st sits in, 0 = Monday.

props.name: monthLabel
props.description: Printed in the header and in every day's label.

props.name: floor
props.description: Balance under this reads danger and the day's label says overdrawn.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the grid for assistive technology.

usageNotes: A real grid with a roving tabindex: arrows walk days and Up and Down move by a week, Home and End reach the ends of a week, Enter lifts the bill on the focused day, arrows choose the new day, Enter drops it and Escape cancels — the drag, on the keyboard, narrated by a polite live region.
The pointer is captured only after 4px of travel, inside try/catch, so a plain press still selects a day and a synthetic sweep never throws.
Under reduced motion nothing lifts or bounces, but the carry chip still follows the pointer and the balance line still re-plots on a tween.

items.title: Cashflow River
items.tagline: In from the left, out to the right.
items.description: Income enters from the left, merges into one balance trunk and leaves to the right as spend, every stream a stroked ribbon whose width is its share of the month. Both sides stack to the same total, so a ribbon keeps one thickness from its node to its band on the trunk, and whatever spend does not take stays as a Kept band in the signal tone; when the amounts change the curve and its width re-form together on glide. Pointing at a ribbon reads its figure in the header and thickens it while the rest dim, pressing pins the reading and Escape releases it, and each stream is also a chip below with a roving tabindex where arrows step, Home and End jump and Enter and Space pin.

props.name: inflows
props.description: Income streams top to bottom; labels stay short, the gutters hold about nine characters.

props.name: outflows
props.description: Spend categories top to bottom; the surplus or shortfall band is added for you.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial pinned stream id.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press, Enter, Space or Escape that pinned or released a stream.

props.name: onReadChange
props.description: Fires from the pointer or focus that lit a stream.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every figure on the diagram.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the diagram for assistive technology and heads the card.

usageNotes: Every ribbon has a chip below the diagram: a roving tabindex where Left and Right and Up and Down step, Home and End jump, Enter and Space pin the reading and Escape releases it — the keyboard equal of the hover.
The hit target is a fat transparent stroke over each ribbon, so a four-unit ribbon is still catchable with a pointer.
Under reduced motion the widths still re-form, on a tween instead of the glide spring, and the lit ribbon brightens rather than thickening.

items.title: Token Stream
items.tagline: Words as they arrive, not after.
items.description: A response surface where the words arrive, not the answer. Each token mounts with a fast fade and no travel while a caret rides the inline flow and breathes on an ambient loop; Stop arrives in the header on snap, and when the host marks the stream stopped the caret morphs into a full stop on the same spring. Tab reaches Stop while the stream is open, Enter or Space cuts it, and the live region reads one completed sentence at a time.

props.name: chunks
props.description: Tokens that have arrived so far, in order, carrying their own leading spaces. Append-only.

props.name: streaming
props.description: The stream is open: the caret breathes and the Stop control shows.

props.name: stopped
props.description: The reader cut the stream: the caret becomes a full stop.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Fires from the Stop control. The host closes the stream and sets stopped.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the response region for assistive technology.

props.name: model
props.description: The model's name for the header chip.

props.name: stopLabel
props.description: Copy on the Stop control.

usageNotes: The frame is a labelled region and the text a real paragraph; Stop is a button reached by Tab while the stream is open, and cutting the stream parks focus on the region rather than the document body.

Under reduced motion the component appends in sentences: tokens are held until one closes a sentence, then the sentence appears at once with a fade; the caret holds still at mid opacity and the stop morph is an instant swap.
The component keeps no clock. Feed it the tokens so far from your own stream, and the live region announces one completed sentence at a time — never a token.

items.title: Thinking Fold
items.tagline: The reasoning, folded away until asked.
items.description: A collapsed strip that stands in for the reasoning while the model thinks. A cobalt wash breathes across the strip on an ambient loop and a mono readout counts tenths from an interval that pauses in a hidden tab; when the answer starts the wash fades, the lamp becomes a tick drawn on flick, and the label cross-fades to the time it took. Enter or Space unfolds the strip to a measured height on glide, and folded lines are inert.

props.name: thinking
props.description: The model is still reasoning: the strip pulses and the clock runs.

props.name: lines
props.description: Reasoning lines that have arrived so far, in order. Append-only.

props.name: elapsed
props.description: Seconds of thinking owned by the host. Omit to count from the moment thinking turns true.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial unfolded state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the strip's click or key press.

props.name: label
props.description: Copy while thinking.

props.name: idleLabel
props.description: Copy before any thinking has happened; also names the panel.

props.name: settledLabel
props.description: Copy once the answer has started.

usageNotes: The strip is a disclosure button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; the panel is a region that is aria-hidden and inert while folded, so folded lines are neither read nor tabbed into.

Under reduced motion the wash and lamp hold at mid opacity, the settle is a colour swap with the tick appearing complete, and the panel's height changes on a tween. The clock keeps counting, because elapsed time is information.

The live region says the label once when thinking starts and the settled sentence once when it ends — never a tick, never a line. The clock never reads a wall clock; it counts from the moment thinking turns true.

items.title: Answer Settle
items.tagline: Provisional, then final.
items.description: Streaming text that shows its own certainty. The paragraph still being written is provisional — lighter ink, raised two pixels — and settles the moment the next begins: the ink deepens on a slow colour tween while the paragraph drops into place on glide. When the stream closes a translucent wash travels over the whole answer on the move ease and onSettled fires from its completion; the live region reads each paragraph once as it settles, never a word.

props.name: text
props.description: The answer arrived so far; a blank line separates paragraphs. Append-only.

props.name: streaming
props.description: The stream is open: the last paragraph stays provisional.

props.name: onSettled
props.description: Fires when the final wash has finished crossing the answer.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the answer region for assistive technology.

props.name: model
props.description: The model's name for the header chip.

usageNotes: The frame is a labelled region and every paragraph a real element, so the answer so far is always readable; the wash is hidden decoration that never takes the pointer.

Under reduced motion provisional paragraphs are lighter ink only, a settle is a colour swap on a fast tween, and the wash blinks once in place instead of travelling — it still fires onSettled, because the settle is information.
Feed it the text so far from your own stream; the component keeps no clock and decides completeness from the blank lines and the streaming flag alone.

items.title: Stream Retry
items.tagline: Cut off; pick up where it stopped.
items.description: A stream that can fail mid-answer and pick itself back up. When the host marks it failed the tail frays — the last characters step down in opacity, five dots cascade in after them and an inline Retry control arrives on snap; nothing bounces, because a failure is not an event to celebrate. Retry is a button reached by Tab, and when the stream reopens the seam heals with a hairline that brightens and fades on a slow tween so the reader can see where the answer was joined.

props.name: text
props.description: The answer arrived so far. Append-only across a retry.

props.name: streaming
props.description: The stream is open and words are arriving.

props.name: failed
props.description: The stream dropped: the tail frays and Retry shows.

props.name: error
props.description: The short line beside the Retry control.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Fires from the Retry control. The host resumes from the seam.

props.name: retryLabel
props.description: Copy on the Retry control.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the answer region for assistive technology.

props.name: model
props.description: The model's name for the header chip.

usageNotes: The frame is a labelled region and the text one real paragraph whose frayed characters keep their content; Retry is a button reached by Tab, and pressing it parks focus on the region while the control leaves.
Under reduced motion the fray is applied at once, the dots and the control appear without cascade or travel, and the heal is an opacity swap with the seam hairline fading in place.

The live region reports the drop, the resume and the close as sentences with word counts — never a word. The component records the seam itself from the moment failed turns true; the host only resumes appending.

items.title: Speed Scrub
items.tagline: Replay at any pace.
items.description: A finished answer whose arrival can be replayed at a chosen pace. The thumb sits inline at the replay position, so it rides the text through every line wrap; play advances by characters from a fixed-step interval, pause holds mid-word with the thumb swelling on snap, and the speed row's indicator glides between stops on snap. Pressing or dragging on the text scrubs to the character under the pointer; on the slider Left and Right step a word, Up and Down five, Home and End jump, and Space toggles play.

props.name: text
props.description: The finished answer.

props.name: position / defaultPosition
props.description: Controlled or initial replay position in characters.

props.name: onPositionChange
props.description: Fires from the interval, a key press, or a pointer scrub.

props.name: playing / defaultPlaying
props.description: Controlled or initial play state.

props.name: onPlayingChange
props.description: Fires from the play control, Space, a press on the text, or reaching the end.

props.name: speed / defaultSpeed
props.description: Controlled or initial multiplier.

props.name: onSpeedChange
props.description: Fires from the speed row.

props.name: speeds
props.description: The multipliers offered.

props.name: charsPerSecond
props.description: Characters per second at 1×.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the answer and the scrubber for assistive technology.

props.name: model
props.description: The model's name for the header chip.

usageNotes: The paragraph is real text; a transparent slider sized by it carries the position with aria-valuetext in words (and the word it is held in). Left and Right step a word, Up and Down five, Home and End jump, Space toggles play; the play button and the speed radio group are real controls with a roving tabindex.
Under reduced motion the thumb marks the hold by opacity instead of scale, the speed indicator swaps without gliding, and the replay still runs — a replay is the content.

The interval is a fixed step that runs only while playing and the tab is visible; it never reads a clock, and reaching the end pauses through onPlayingChange. The live region announces play, pause and the end — never a character.

items.title: Cursor Lead
items.tagline: A caret that arrives a beat before the word.
items.description: A streaming caret that steps ahead into the next word's slot before the word fills it. The slot is an invisible copy of the coming word with a faint underline that draws on flick as the caret arrives on snap; when the word lands it fades up with a nudge while the underline shrinks away beneath it, and the surface glides to its measured height. Assistive technology hears one sentence at a time, never a token.

props.name: text
props.description: The full answer; words are split on whitespace.

props.name: landed
props.description: How many words have arrived, clamped to the word count. Drive it from your stream.

props.name: playing
props.description: Whether the stream is live; keeps the caret on the surface until the last word and sets aria-busy.

props.name: model
props.description: An invented model name for the header chip.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the surface for assistive technology.

usageNotes: A display surface with no pointer gestures: the host drives landed from its own stream, and the status region announces each sentence as its final word lands and Answer complete on settle, never a word at a time.
Under reduced motion the caret swaps to its new slot without the spring, words fade in without the nudge, the underline fades instead of shrinking, and the height changes with a short tween.
The surface's height is measured with a ResizeObserver and animated on glide, never reserved, so a new line grows it rather than jumping it.

items.title: Partial Table
items.tagline: Rows fill as the model writes them.
items.description: A real table that grows row by row as characters arrive: each row fades in with a nudge on glide, and every cell not yet whole shows a shimmer bar as long as its missing letters. The columns are held at equal widths while anything is incomplete, and only when the last character lands do the col widths glide to the measured proportions of their content. Assistive technology hears a row when it completes, never a character.

props.name: columns
props.description: Header labels, left to right.

props.name: rows
props.description: The complete cell text, row-major.

props.name: arrived
props.description: Characters received across the cells in row order. Drive it from your stream.

props.name: playing
props.description: Whether the stream is live; sets aria-busy on the table.

props.name: caption
props.description: Names the table; rendered as its caption.

props.name: model
props.description: An invented model name, shown beside the caption.

props.name: onSettle
props.description: Fires from the measurement observer once the columns have settled after completion.

usageNotes: A display surface with no pointer gestures: a table with a caption, column headers and a body, aria-busy while playing; the status region announces Row N complete as each row's last character lands and Table complete on settle.
Under reduced motion rows fade in without the nudge, the shimmer bars are still muted blocks, and the column widths change with a short tween instead of the spring.
The layout is table-fixed with equal col widths until completion, so arriving characters never jog a neighbouring column; natural widths are measured off the cells' inner spans, never guessed.

items.title: Stream Branch
items.tagline: Two answers, side by side, as they come.
items.description: Two answers to one prompt racing in split panes, each behind a rail that fills to its progress on glide; the pane that lands first takes a First stamp on recoil. Keep lifts the chosen pane on snap and folds the other away, its measured height gliding to zero while the grid closes to one column, and Compare again unfolds it. Keep and Compare again are real buttons, so Tab reaches them and Enter or Space presses.

props.name: branches
props.description: Exactly two branches: { id, model, text, landed }. Drive landed from your streams.

props.name: playing
props.description: Whether the streams are live; sets aria-busy on unfinished panes.

props.name: picked / defaultPicked
props.description: Controlled or initial kept branch id; null while comparing.

props.name: onPickedChange
props.description: Fires from the Keep press with the id, or from Compare again with null.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the pair for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Two articles labelled by their model names inside a labelled section; each Keep is a button with aria-pressed, and the folded pane is inert so its control leaves the tab order. The status region announces the first finish, the pick, and the unfold, never a word.
Under reduced motion the rails still fill on a short tween, nothing lifts, the stamp appears without bouncing, and the fold is a fade with a tweened height.

Panes measure their own content with a ResizeObserver; the fold animates that measured height to zero rather than guessing, and the pair sits side by side only when its container is at least 24rem wide.

items.title: Latency Bar
items.tagline: Time to the first word.
items.description: A slim bar that fills while waiting for the first token and then snaps to done. The fill follows an asymptote smoothed on glide, so it rises fast and never finishes on its own; the first token snaps it full on snap and draws a check on flick, the time reads beside it in tabular digits, and a wait past the warn line turns the bar and readout amber with the word slow. The host passes state and elapsed time from its own clock.

props.name: state
props.description: Where the wait is.

props.name: elapsedMs
props.description: Milliseconds since the request, from the host's clock; freeze it at done.

props.name: budgetMs
props.description: Sets the fill curve, t / (t + budgetMs / 4).

props.name: warnAfterMs
props.description: Past this the bar and readout turn warn and the readout gains the word slow.

props.name: typicalMs
props.description: Draws a tick on the track at the typical wait.

props.name: label
props.description: What is being waited on; names the timer.

usageNotes: A display instrument with no pointer gestures: the readout is a role="timer" with aria-live off so ticks are never spoken, and the status region announces First token in N s once on done, with slow appended when the wait crossed the warn line.
Under reduced motion the fill still fills on a short tween, done arrives without the snap, the check appears whole, and colour changes still tween.
The bar never reads a clock: drive elapsedMs from your own timer, pausing it when the document is hidden, and set state to done when the first token arrives.

items.title: Stop Slab
items.tagline: Stop, and keep what you have.
items.description: An answer surface whose stop control grows into being: a dot pops in on snap when streaming starts and a beat later grows on glide into a slab as wide as its measured label. Pressing it squashes on flick, halts the stream, and shrinks the slab on glide to a round Regenerate control whose arrow draws on flick, while the words stay and a kept mark lands after the last one on snap. Enter or Space presses the control and Escape inside the surface stops.

props.name: text
props.description: The words that have arrived so far. Drive it from your stream.

props.name: status
props.description: Where the stream is; streaming shows the slab, stopped and done show Regenerate.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Fires from the Stop press, or Escape inside the surface, while streaming.

props.name: onRegenerate
props.description: Fires from the Regenerate press once the stream has stopped or finished.

props.name: model
props.description: An invented model name for the header chip.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the surface for assistive technology.

usageNotes: One button the whole time, named Stop generating while streaming and Regenerate after; Enter and Space press it and Escape anywhere inside the surface stops. The status region announces Stopped, kept N words, or Answer complete, never a word.
Under reduced motion the control cross-fades between its sizes instead of growing or shrinking, nothing squashes, the arrow appears whole, and the kept mark fades in.
Both the surface's height and the slab's width are measured with ResizeObservers, never reserved; the host owns the stream and clears the text before restarting from onRegenerate.

items.title: Prompt Composer
items.tagline: A field that grows with the thought.
items.description: A composer that grows with the thought. A hidden mirror carries the draft in the field's own type and padding, so its measured height — read by a ResizeObserver — is the height the field needs, and the wrapper glides there on glide, holding at maxRows while the textarea scrolls inside. The footer's token estimate rolls its digits on snap, and the send control is one button whose shape says what it does: round with an arrow while idle, square with a stop mark while a run is live, the corners and glyph swapping on snap so focus never moves. Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line, and while live Enter is held so the draft stays.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial draft.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from every edit.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires from Enter or the send button with the trimmed draft; the parent clears or keeps it.

props.name: onStop
