props.name: model
props.description: The invented model that wrote it, printed in the header.

props.name: review
props.description: The approval on record — reviewer, team and a formatted time; present, the stamp is down.

props.name: onApprove
props.description: Fires from the Approve control; the host records who and when.

props.name: onRevoke
props.description: Fires from the Revoke control.

props.name: stampText
props.description: The word on the seal.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the card for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The seal is a button named "Reviewed by <reviewer>" and described by an always-mounted sr-only line with the team and time; Tab reaches the seal and then the footer control, Enter and Space toggle the tooltip, Escape closes it.
Under reduced motion the seal fades in and out at rest — no drop, no tilt landing, no peel — and the tooltip fades without scaling; the success tint still tweens.
The component never reads a clock: the host records who and when in the review it passes, and the sr-only status announces the review and its revocation once each.

items.title: Risk Meter
items.tagline: How risky the action is.
items.description: A meter beneath a proposed action that fills toward its risk: the fill is a scaleX on glide, toned cobalt, warn or danger by band, with two threshold ticks on the track, and a band label rides above it with its centre on the fill's leading edge while its word rolls up or down on snap. In the high band the action control arms a confirm — the first press rolls Run into Confirm on the destructive tone, the second runs, and Escape or a change of risk disarms.

props.name: risk
props.description: The action's risk, 0 to 1.

props.name: action
props.description: What the model proposes to do, printed above the meter.

props.name: thresholds
props.description: Where the moderate and high bands begin; the high band arms the confirm.

props.name: bands
props.description: The band words.

props.name: runLabel
props.description: Copy on the action control.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: Copy on the armed control.

props.name: onRun
props.description: Fires when the action runs: one press below the high band, the second press in it.

props.name: onArmChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that armed or disarmed the confirm.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the meter and its group for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The action control is one button: below the high band a press runs; in it the first press arms Confirm (described by an sr-only "Press again to confirm"), the second runs, and Escape disarms. The track is a role="meter" whose aria-valuetext reads the band and percentage.
Under reduced motion the fill still fills on a base tween, the label does not travel, and the band and control words cross-fade in place.
A new risk value disarms the confirm and clears the last run in the same commit, so a control never stays armed for an action it was not armed on.

items.title: Guard Rail
items.tagline: The line it will not cross.
items.description: A rail that shows how close a conversation stands to a boundary: a round marker and the fill behind it move on glide as each message raises the proximity, taking the warn tone past warnAt, and a value of 1 or more is a crossing — that last stretch runs on recoil so the marker hits the line, overshoots into it and bounces back to rest against it, while the line flashes and the reason unfolds beneath in a measured frame. It is a role="meter" with the distance in words, and an sr-only status announces near and crossed once each.

props.name: proximity
props.description: How close the conversation stands to the line: 0 is far, 1 or more has crossed.

props.name: boundary
props.description: The line's name, printed at the rail's end.

props.name: reason
props.description: Why the line stopped the thread, shown when crossed.

props.name: warnAt
props.description: Fraction past which the rail turns warn.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the rail for assistive technology.

usageNotes: A display instrument with no pointer gesture: the rail is a role="meter" whose aria-valuetext reads the percentage of the way to the boundary, or that it was crossed, and the reason is a plain paragraph beneath it.
Under reduced motion the marker and fill still move, on a base tween, because the distance is information; the crossing does not bounce, the line still flashes and the reason fades in.
The marker and fill are placed by percentage inside a lane one marker narrower than the rail, so nothing is measured for position and a value of 1 rests the marker exactly against the line.

items.title: Bubble Land
items.tagline: Sent, and it shows.
items.description: A message thread with a composer whose new bubble rises into the list from the composer's side on recoil, the two bounces of something landing. The bubble's delivery mark walks the states the parent reports: a ring while sending, one check drawn on flick once sent, a second check that walks out on snap when delivered, and both tinted cobalt when read; failure shakes the bubble on a tween and offers Retry beneath it. The composer is a textarea where Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks a line, every mark is an image with a sentence, and a status region speaks delivered, read, and failure once each.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first: id, from ("me" or "peer"), text, an optional formatted time, and for own messages a delivery of "sending", "sent", "delivered", "read", or "failed".

props.name: peerName
props.description: The other person; the mark's sentences name them ("Read by Marta").

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires from Enter or the Send control with the trimmed draft; append the message here with delivery "sending".

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Fires from a failed bubble's Retry control; set that message back to "sending".

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Composer placeholder.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds the composer while the parent is busy.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The composer is a real textarea: Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline, and the Send control disables while the draft is empty; Retry is a button named by the message's first words, and taking it hands focus to the composer.
Under reduced motion the bubble fades in place, the checks appear without drawing or walking, and failure changes colour without the shake; the thread's height still follows its content on a tween.

Delivery is the parent's to report: the component never reads a clock, so a real transport or a seeded script drives the walk through the delivery prop, and the status region speaks delivered, read, and failure once per hop.

items.title: Read Wave
items.tagline: Seen by whom, and when.
items.description: A sent message with a row of reader discs beneath it. Each new reader slides in from below on snap and tucks into the overlapping tail while the "Seen by" count rolls its digits on the same spring; hovering, focusing, or pressing the row fans the discs apart with a layout FLIP on snap and unfolds a list of names and times whose measured height glides. The row is a button with aria-expanded named by the count, Escape folds it, and a status region speaks each arrival once.

props.name: text
props.description: The message body.

props.name: time
props.description: When it was sent, printed under the bubble.

props.name: readers
props.description: Everyone who has read it, in read order: id, name, a formatted time, and optional initials (derived from the name when omitted). Append as people read.

props.name: total
props.description: People who could read it; the count then reads "Seen by 3 of 5".

props.name: maxAvatars
props.description: Discs shown before the rest collapse into a "+N" pip whose number also rolls.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial pinned state of the fan; hover and focus open it on their own.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires when a press or Escape pins or unpins the fan.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The readers row is a button: Tab reaches it, Enter or Space pins the fan open, Escape folds it and keeps focus, and focus or hover open it on their own; the fanned list is a real list of name and time rows.
Under reduced motion discs and rows fade in place, the digits swap instead of rolling, the fan does not spread, and the list's height changes on a tween.
Arrivals are the parent's to report through the readers prop; the component never reads a clock, and the status region speaks "Read by Marta at 15:02" once per reader.

items.title: Edit Trace
items.tagline: Edited, and what it said before.
items.description: A message that keeps its previous versions. When a new version lands the text wipes in over the old on a clip-path tween and an Edited mark pops in on flick; pressing the mark unfolds every previous version beneath the bubble with measured height on glide, each with a strike that draws left to right on the same spring, while the current text replays its wipe over the last one. The mark is a button with aria-expanded, previous versions are del elements in a real list, Escape folds the trace and returns focus, and a status region speaks each edit once.

props.name: versions
props.description: Oldest first, each with text and a formatted time; the last entry is what the message says now. A single entry means never edited and no mark.

props.name: author
props.description: Sender name printed above the bubble.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial trace state; it only shows once there is a previous version.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the mark or from Escape with the new trace state.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The Edited mark is a button: Tab reaches it, Enter or Space toggles the trace, and Escape anywhere in the message folds it and returns focus to the mark.
Under reduced motion the wipe becomes a cross-fade, the strikes and the mark appear without drawing or scaling, and the panel's height swaps on a tween.
Versions are the parent's: append a new one and the component notices the landing during render, wipes the text in, and speaks "Edited:" with the new text once.

items.title: Delete Fade
items.tagline: Gone, with a moment to undo.
items.description: A thread whose messages can be deleted with a moment to undo. Deleting dims the bubble on a tween while the row's measured height glides on glide down to a chip with a ring that drains linearly across the undo window, the word Deleted, and an Undo button; hovering or keyboard-focusing the chip holds the ring. Undo brings the bubble back with a rise on recoil, while running out tells the parent to drop the message and the row exits on the exit ease with no bounce. Delete controls are buttons named by sender and first words, focus moves to Undo and back, and a status region speaks deleted, restored, and removed.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first: id, from (a name, or "me" for the own bubble), text, and an optional formatted time. Drop a message here from onExpire.

props.name: undoWindow
props.description: Milliseconds the ring drains before the delete is final.

props.name: onDelete
props.description: Fires on the delete press; the message stays in the thread as a pending chip.

props.name: onUndo
props.description: Fires when Undo is pressed and the bubble is restored.

props.name: onExpire
props.description: Fires when the ring runs out; remove the message from messages here.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Every delete control is a button: Enter or Space deletes and focus lands on Undo, where Enter or Space restores and focus returns to the delete control; keyboard focus on the chip holds the ring, and if the ring runs out under focus, focus moves to the thread list.
Under reduced motion the bubble fades back without rising, heights swap on a tween, and the ring still drains at the same rate because the countdown is information.
The ring pauses while the tab is hidden and resumes from where it stood; the pending and gone marks follow the ids in messages, so a reset thread with fresh ids comes back clean.

items.title: Group Stack
items.tagline: Same sender, stacked tight.
items.description: A thread whose consecutive messages from one sender stack as a run: the gap inside a run is 2px and between runs 12px, so a bubble that joins a run tightens against the one above while the corners between them lose their radius. The run's disc renders once on its last message under a shared layoutId, sliding down on glide as the run grows; a new sender opens the gap and mounts a fresh disc with a pop on snap, and every arriving bubble rises on snap. Continuation messages carry a hidden sender prefix so each list item reads with its sender, and a status region speaks each arrival once.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first: id, sender (a display name; runs are cut wherever it changes), text, and an optional formatted time shown under the last bubble of a run.

props.name: self
props.description: The sender rendered as own messages, right-aligned and without a disc.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The thread has no controls of its own: it is a list whose items each read with their sender, so the keyboard path is whatever appends to messages; the list scrolls inside a capped frame that follows the newest bubble.
Under reduced motion the gaps swap without a FLIP, the disc re-renders on the new last message without travelling, and bubbles fade in place.
Arrivals are the parent's: append to messages and the component notices during render, tightens or opens the gap, hands the disc down the run, and speaks "Marta: …" once.

items.title: Time Divider
items.tagline: Yesterday, drawn between.
items.description: A thread that draws a line where the day changes. A divider that mounts because a new message crossed into a new day draws its rule from the centre outward on glide, the layout spring, and its label fades in over the line once it is most of the way out; messages arrive with a four-pixel rise on glide. Nothing inside is focusable: each divider is a separator labelled with its day, so a reader walking the list hears the change where it happens.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread in order: id, author, text, at as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm, optional mine.

props.name: today
props.description: The current day as YYYY-MM-DD; Today and Yesterday are measured from it.

props.name: formatDay
props.description: Overrides the divider wording; the default gives Today, Yesterday, a weekday inside the week, and a date beyond it.

props.name: onDayCross
props.description: Fires from an effect when a new day's divider mounts after the first render.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Nothing inside is focusable; each divider is an li with role separator and an aria-label of its day, and one polite sentence per arrival names the day only when that message opened it.
Under reduced motion the line does not draw: line and label fade in together on a short tween and messages fade in place.
Timestamps are strings and day labels come from UTC arithmetic against today, so a prerender in one zone and a browser in another print the same divider.

items.title: Message Glow
items.tagline: Jump to it; it glows.
items.description: A thread where a quote is a door. Pressing the quoted line in a reply, or the pinned chip at the head, drives the box's scrollTop on glide until the target bubble sits centred, and on settle the bubble glows once: a wash and a two-pixel ring at full strength that fade on the exit ease, keyed by a jump count so a repeat jump glows again. The target list item takes focus when the scroll settles, and a Back chip glides you to where you were.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread in order: id, author, text, at as HH:mm, optional mine, optional replyTo naming the message it answers.

props.name: pinned
props.description: Id of a message offered as a sticky Pinned chip at the head of the thread.

props.name: onJump
props.description: Fires from the press that starts a jump.

props.name: onBack
props.description: Fires from the Back chip.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the scroll region for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Quotes and the pinned chip are buttons: Enter or Space jumps, the target list item takes focus without scrolling again when the glide settles, and Back returns focus to the quote that started the jump.
Under reduced motion the scroll is set at once and the glow still fades, because it is the confirmation that the jump landed; the Back chip fades in place.
The scroll box is a labelled region with tabindex 0 so keyboard users can scroll it; it opens at the newest message.

items.title: Long Fold
items.tagline: A long message, folded.
items.description: A thread where a long message arrives folded. Any bubble taller than lines line boxes clamps to exactly that many, fades its last line out in the bubble's own colour and offers a read-more; unfolding joins the folded height to the measured one on glide while the fade lifts on a tween and the chevron turns on snap. Folding back runs the same spring in reverse and, if the bubble's top has scrolled away, glides the box to it at the same time, so the message you closed stays under your eye.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread in order: id, author, text with newlines kept, at as HH:mm, optional mine.

props.name: lines
props.description: Lines shown while folded; a message that fits shows no control.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial ids of unfolded messages.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the press that folds or unfolds a message.

props.name: moreLabel
props.description: Disclosure copy while folded.

props.name: lessLabel
props.description: Disclosure copy while open.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the scroll region for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The disclosure is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls: Enter and Space fold and unfold, and the folded text is never hidden from assistive technology, so a reader can hear the whole message without unfolding it.
Under reduced motion heights swap at once, the fade still lifts, the chevron flips without turning, and the scroll correction is set instantly.

Heights come from a ResizeObserver on the text's border box and the folded height from the line box, so nothing is reserved; scroll anchoring is off in the box so the fold-back correction owns the scroll position.

items.title: Forward Slip
items.tagline: Sent on, with a stamp.
items.description: A thread where a message can have come from somewhere else. A forwarded message rises on glide and then its stamp, Forwarded from and the source thread's name, slides in from the bubble's outer edge on recoil, because a stamp is pressed on and lands with two bounces. The source name is a button that lifts two pixels on snap and draws a rule under itself on flick when hovered or focused; pressing it jumps, the host swaps the thread in, the list cross-fades and the original message takes focus.

props.name: thread
props.description: The visible thread: id, name, and messages carrying id, author, text, at, optional mine and optional forwardedFrom (threadId, threadName, messageId, author, at). Swapping the id cross-fades the list.

props.name: arriveAt
props.description: A message id to focus once this thread mounts; the destination of a jump.

props.name: onJump
props.description: Fires from pressing a stamp's source name with the source threadId and messageId.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The source name in the stamp is a button: Tab reaches it, Enter or Space jumps, and the destination message takes focus without scrolling when the host mounts the source thread with arriveAt.
Under reduced motion the stamp fades in place with no travel or bounce, the name changes colour instead of lifting, and the thread swap is the same opacity cross-fade.
Everything present when a thread mounts is settled history; only a message added to that thread afterwards rises and gets its stamp slid in.

items.title: Bubble Tail
items.tagline: The last one gets the tail.
items.description: Only the last message of a run wears the tail. Consecutive messages from one sender form a run, and the tail is one element per run with a shared layoutId, so when a new message extends the run it hands off, travelling from the old last bubble to the new one on snap while its path morphs from a tucked curve to the full point and the old bubble's corner rounds back on glide. A new sender starts a new run with its own tail, and nothing inside is focusable.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread in order: id, author, text, at as HH:mm, optional mine.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Nothing inside is focusable; the run boundary is carried by the printed sender at the head of each run and an sr-only sender on every bubble, never by the tail, which is aria-hidden decoration.
Under reduced motion the tail does not travel or morph: it appears on the new last bubble on a short fade and the corner radius swaps.
The tail's layoutId is scoped to the run, the id of its first message, so two runs never share a tail and only a message that extends a run triggers the hand-off.

items.title: Compose Bar
items.tagline: A bar that makes room.
items.description: A chat composer that makes room. Two hidden mirrors measure the draft at the single-line and full columns, and the moment the narrow one wraps the well glides on glide to the full-width height plus a footer while the attach control slides on glide from beside send to the far left, so the two controls slide apart around the text. A dot beside the first line glows when the field is blurred with unsent text; Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks a line.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial draft.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from every keystroke and from the clear after a send.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires from Enter or the Send control with the trimmed draft.

props.name: onAttach
props.description: Fires from the Attach control.

props.name: onLinesChange
props.description: Fires from the observer whenever the measured line count changes.

props.name: onFocusChange
props.description: Fires as the textarea gains and loses focus.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: Lines the well grows to before the textarea scrolls.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Keep it short: a placeholder that wraps reads as a second line.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds the composer and both controls.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the textarea for assistive technology.

usageNotes: A real textarea: Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line, and the tab order runs textarea, Attach, Send; Send is aria-disabled while the draft is empty rather than removed from the order.
Under reduced motion the well's height and the attach control's position swap on fast tweens, and the draft dot holds a steady ring instead of pulsing.
An sr-only status announces "Draft kept, N words" once when the field blurs with text and "Message sent" on send.

items.title: Typing Echo
items.tagline: They are typing, honestly.
items.description: A typing indicator that lives in the thread. A slot under the message list is measured by a ResizeObserver and glides open on glide while an echo of the coming bubble, with the typers' initial avatars, rises on snap; three dots ride one staggered keyframe wave so no two are ever at the same height, and a caption names exactly who is typing. When they stop, the echo fades on the exit ease and the slot collapses to give the room back. It has no controls; a persistent live region speaks each change of caption once.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first: id, the sender's name, the text, and own for the viewer's messages.

props.name: typing
props.description: Who is typing now, in the order they started; an empty array collapses the slot.

props.name: max
props.description: Names spelled out before "and N others".

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The thread is an ordered list whose items carry "Marta: text" labels; the echo is decoration and hidden from assistive technology, while a persistent polite live region holds the caption so each change is announced exactly once and silence announces nothing.
Under reduced motion the slot height swaps on a fast tween, the echo fades in place, and the dots pulse opacity in the same stagger instead of travelling.
The dot wave is started in an effect, stopped on unmount, and held while the document is hidden; drive typing from your presence source, never from a clock in render.

items.title: Voice Bubble
items.tagline: Hold, speak, send.
items.description: Hold the mic and a waveform pill opens on snap; a 100ms tick advances a seeded level for each bar, re-targeted on flick so the wave reads as the voice, while a clock counts. Releasing after a real hold resamples the take into a 32-bar note that the parent appends, and its bubble rises on recoil with a play control and a wave that is a slider: press and drag scrub it, Arrow keys step a second, Home and End jump. No microphone is read; a tap shows a hold hint instead.

props.name: notes
props.description: The thread, oldest first: id, from (me or peer), whole seconds, a wave of 0..1 levels, and an optional time.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires from a release or a Space/Enter stop after a real hold, with the seconds and a 32-bar profile.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Fires from Escape during a take, or a release that was only a tap.

props.name: onRecording
props.description: Fires at the start of a take and on each whole second; null when the take ends.

props.name: onPlayChange
props.description: Fires with the note that started playing, or null when playback stops.

props.name: maxSeconds
props.description: The take stops itself here.

props.name: peerName
props.description: Names the other side in the bubbles' sentences.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The mic is a button with aria-pressed: pointer down holds and release sends, Space or Enter toggles the take, Escape discards it; each bubble's wave is a slider whose Arrow keys step one second and Home and End jump, and its play button is named Play or Pause.

Under reduced motion the pill fades in place, the live bars hold a static profile while the clock still counts, the bubble fades in without rising, and the playback fill still advances because position is information.
Both ticks live in effects with cleanup and hold while the document is hidden; the wave is procedural and the profile it records is seeded, so no microphone or clock is read during render.

items.title: Emoji Rise
items.tagline: Emoji that rise to meet the caret.
items.description: A composer that answers a colon. Typing `:` at the start of a word opens a picker in the slot above the field: the slot's measured height glides open on glide while the panel rises from distances.step on snap, and letters after the colon filter a named set whose survivors slide to their new cells on glide because every option is a layout item. Enter, Tab or a click replaces the token with the glyph and a space and pops a last-used tile on recoil; Escape closes the picker and keeps the text, and focus never leaves the textarea.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial draft.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from every keystroke, from an insert, and from the clear after a send.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires from Enter with the picker closed, or the Send control, with the trimmed draft.

props.name: onInsert
props.description: Fires with the item whose glyph was inserted.

props.name: onPickerChange
props.type: (state: { open: boolean; query: string; matches: number }) => void
props.description: Fires from an effect whenever the picker opens, closes, or its match count changes.

props.name: items
props.description: The set to search: glyph, name, and optional keywords. Defaults to the built-in sixteen.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The textarea's placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the textarea for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Focus never leaves the textarea: it carries aria-autocomplete, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant while the listbox is open. Left and Right step, Up and Down move a row of eight, Home and End jump, Enter or Tab insert, Escape closes; Enter with the picker closed sends and Shift+Enter breaks a line.

Under reduced motion the slot and the panel fade on fast tweens with no rise, layout is off so survivors swap cells in place, the highlight takes the wash without lifting, and the last-used tile fades in without the pop.
An sr-only status announces the match count once per query, each insert by name, and "No match for :xyz"; the last-used tile is a named button, so the repeat has a keyboard path.

items.title: Attach Preview
items.tagline: What you are about to send.
items.description: Attachments show themselves before they go. A strip above the composer is measured by a ResizeObserver and glides open on glide only when it holds something: a new slot widens from zero on glide while the drawn thumbnail inside rises from distances.step on snap. Removing one narrows its slot to zero and fades it on the exit ease so its neighbours slide together, and sending moves the files into a new own-side bubble in one commit, where a layoutId prefixed by useId flies each thumbnail from the strip into the thread on glide.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first: id, from (me or peer), optional text, attachments and time.

props.name: pending
props.description: The files waiting in the strip: id, name, kind (photo, doc or sheet) and the seed that draws the thumbnail.

props.name: onAttach
props.description: Fires from the Attach control; append the next file to pending.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Fires once a thumbnail's slot has finished narrowing to zero, so the removal is seen before the file is dropped.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires from Enter or Send; clear pending and append the message in the same commit so the thumbnails fly.

props.name: peerName
props.description: Names the other side in the composer's label and the thread's sentences.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The textarea's placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The thread is an ordered list whose own items read "You sent 2 attachments: pallet-a.jpg, pallet-b.jpg"; the strip is a labelled list of images named by kind and file, each with a named remove button, and focus moves to the next remove control or back to Attach as the strip empties.
The composer is a real textarea: Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks a line, and Send is disabled while there is neither text nor a pending file.

Under reduced motion nothing flies and nothing rises — thumbnails fade in place — but the slots and the strip still open and close on fast tweens, because a slot collapsing is feedback rather than flourish.

items.title: Draft Badge
items.tagline: An unsent thought, remembered.
items.description: A channel list that remembers what you did not send. Leaving a channel with unsent text puts a badge on its row — a pencil and the draft's first words rising from four pixels on snap in place of the topic line, so the row never changes height — and opening it again drops the badge out on the exit ease while the same text arrives in the composer from eight pixels above on glide, caret at the end. The rows are tabs with a roving tabindex: arrows move, Home and End jump, Enter or Space opens; Enter in the composer sends and Shift+Enter breaks the line.

props.name: channels
props.description: The rows: id, a name printed after a hash, and the topic shown while the channel holds no draft.

props.name: drafts / defaultDrafts
props.description: Controlled or initial draft text per channel id.

props.name: onDraftsChange
props.description: Fires from every keystroke and from the clear after a send.

props.name: active / defaultActive
props.description: Controlled or initial open channel id; defaults to the first channel.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires from a row press or the key that opened a channel.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires from Enter or the Send button with the trimmed text of the open channel.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Composer placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the channel list for assistive technology; the composer is named after the open channel.

usageNotes: The channel rows are a vertical tablist with a roving tabindex: Up and Down (or Left and Right) move focus without wrapping, Home and End jump, Enter or Space opens the channel and puts the caret at the end of its draft. Enter in the composer sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line.
Under reduced motion the badge fades in and out in place and the restored text fades into the field without travelling.
Each badge is an image whose sentence reads "Draft: <first words>", and a status region announces a kept, restored or sent draft once per event, never per keystroke.

items.title: Mention Pop
items.tagline: Names that complete as you type.
items.description: Names that complete as you type. An @ opens the room's members in a list that rises above the composer from eight pixels on snap, rows cascading in with a presence dot that says in words who is here; picking one wraps the typed name as a chip whose wash scales from the left edge on snap around glyphs the textarea already drew, and sending lands the message in the thread where its chips glow once — a fill flashes and a ring flares outward on a tween. Up and Down move the highlight, Home and End jump, Enter or Tab inserts, Escape closes; with the list shut Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks the line.

props.name: members
props.description: Who can be mentioned: id, name, a mono handle searched alongside it, and presence (online, away or offline).

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first: id, from ("me" or a sender's name) and text with @Name tokens. Append the sent message here from onSend.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial composer text.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on every edit and on the clear after a send.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires from Enter or the Send button with the trimmed text and the member ids mentioned in it.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Composer placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread and the composer for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The textarea is a combobox over a listbox driven by aria-activedescendant, so focus never leaves the text: Up and Down move the highlight, Home and End jump, Enter or Tab inserts the chip, Escape closes the list; with the list shut Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks the line.
Under reduced motion the list fades in place without the rise or the cascade, the chip's wash appears by opacity, and the glow on send is a single fade with nothing flaring outward.
Presence dots are images with sentences ("Marta, online"), and a status region announces "Mentioned Marta" on insert and "Sent, pinged Marta, Rui" on send — never per keystroke.

items.title: Send Swoosh
items.tagline: The send, felt.
items.description: A composer whose send is felt. Pressing Send fires the arrow forward — fourteen pixels right and gone on the exit ease — and a fresh one returns from ten pixels behind on snap, one crisp overshoot into place; in the same moment the composer clears with a wipe, a clip inset sweeping the words away over an already-empty textarea. A status of sending holds the button dimmed under a ring, and failed wipes the text back in from the right, turns the button danger and puts the caret at the end. Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line, and focus returns to the field on failure only when it was already inside the composer.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial composer text.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from every edit, the clear on send, and the return of the words on a failure.

props.name: status
props.description: The parent's report on the last send: sending holds the button, sent lets it go, failed returns the text.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires from Enter or the Send button with the trimmed text.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Composer placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the composer for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks the line; Send is a real button, aria-disabled while the text is empty or a send is in flight, and described by the failure line while there is one. On a failure focus returns to the textarea only if it was already inside the composer.
Under reduced motion the arrow does not travel — it dims and returns by opacity — the wipe is a straight fade of the ghost layer, and the failure tint and the returned words arrive on a fast fade.

The verdict is the parent's to give: hold `status` at "sending" while the request is out, then set "sent" or "failed". A status region announces Sending, Sent and "Not sent, text returned to the composer" once per outcome.

items.title: Reply Cite
items.tagline: Replying to this.
items.description: A thread that can point at itself. Reply on a message slides a cite card into the composer's head from eight pixels above on glide while the head's measured height glides open from nothing, and the original wears a cobalt bar that draws down its side on snap for as long as it is the target. Pressing the card carries the thread back to the original — scrollTop driven by glide rather than jumped — and moves focus onto the message, so it is both seen and read; Escape in the composer or on the card takes the target away, the card leaving upward on the exit ease as the head glides shut. Enter sends with the target id attached and the message that lands quotes what it answered.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first: id, from ("me" or a sender's name), text, an optional formatted time, and replyTo — the id of the message it answers, which draws its cite line. Append the sent message here from onSend.

props.name: replyTo / defaultReplyTo
props.description: Controlled or initial reply target. A target the thread no longer holds shuts the head rather than citing a missing message.

props.name: onReplyToChange
props.description: Fires from a Reply press, the remove button, Escape and a send.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires from Enter or the Send button with the trimmed text and the target it answers.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Composer placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread and the composer for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Every message carries a Reply button named after it ("Reply to Marta: first words"), and taking a target moves the caret to the composer. Escape in the textarea or on the cite card removes the target; Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks the line. Pressing the card scrolls the thread to the original and focuses it, so a screen reader lands on the message rather than on the space around it.
Under reduced motion the card fades in and out in place, the head's height swaps on a fast tween, the cited edge appears on a colour tween, and the thread jumps to the original instead of gliding.

The head reserves no room: a ResizeObserver measures the card's border box, so the composer is exactly as tall as the reply it holds and no taller when it holds none. A status region announces "Replying to Marta" and "Reply removed" once per change.

items.title: Schedule Chip
items.tagline: Send it at nine.
items.description: A composer whose send button can wear a clock. The schedule control opens a list of times that rises above the field from eight pixels on snap; choosing one puts the time in a chip on the composer's foot, scaling in from 0.9 on the same spring, and turns the send button into a clock — the arrow crosses out as a face crosses in and the two hands sweep from twelve to the hour and the minute on snap, each on its own rotation. Sending with a time queues instead: a card lands under the composer on glide with the text, the time in words, a ring that drains across the wait and a seconds readout, both holding where they are while the tab is hidden. Arrows move the list, Home and End jump, Enter or Space picks, Escape closes and hands focus back to the control.

props.name: options
props.description: The times offered: id, a label read on the chip and by the send button, the hour and minute the hands sweep to, and delayMs — the wait each one means.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial chosen option id. Null sends now.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from a pick, a clear, and after a queue clears the chip.

props.name: queue
props.description: The queued messages the parent holds, oldest first: id, text and the optionId that queued them. Each card runs its own wait.

props.name: draft / defaultDraft
props.description: Controlled or initial composer text.

props.name: onDraftChange
props.description: Fires from every edit and from the clear after a send or a queue.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires from Enter or Send with no time chosen.

props.name: onQueue
props.description: Fires from Enter or Send with a time chosen; append the message to queue.

props.name: onDeliver
props.description: Fires when a queued message's wait reaches zero; remove it from queue and deliver it.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Composer placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the composer for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The schedule control is a listbox trigger: Up and Down move the highlight, Home and End jump, Enter or Space picks, Escape closes and hands focus back to the control, and a pointer down outside shuts it. Enter in the textarea sends or queues, Shift+Enter breaks the line. The send button's name reads "Send" or "Schedule for tomorrow 9:00", and the clock itself is hidden from assistive technology.

Under reduced motion the list and the chip fade in place and the hands swap to the time without sweeping, but the ring still drains and the seconds still count down, because the wait is information rather than flourish.

Each queue card holds its remainder in a motion value, so the ring and the readout cost no re-renders and a hidden tab stops the wait where it stood rather than restarting it. Queue cards are labelled sentences ("Queued for tomorrow 9:00: first words") with a role="timer" readout, and a status region announces the queue, the send and the delivery once each.

items.title: React Burst
items.tagline: A reaction that bursts, then counts.
items.description: A row of reaction chips that answers the press. Taking a reaction bursts its drawn mark from 1.32 back to 1 on recoil while a ring the size of the chip drains on the exit ease and the count rolls in one grid cell on snap; withdrawing shrinks the mark on flick with no ring, and a chip that reaches zero leaves while the row re-flows on glide. Arrow keys move across the chips under a roving tabindex, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space toggles the reaction under the cursor.

props.name: reactions
props.description: The seeded tallies: id, label, glyph and the other people on each reaction.

props.name: mine / defaultMine
props.description: Controlled or initial list of reaction ids you have taken.

props.name: onMineChange
props.description: Fires with the whole next list on every press.

props.name: onReact
props.description: Fires with the reaction pressed and whether it is now yours.

props.name: maxNames
props.description: Names printed before the card reads "and 4 more".

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds every chip while the row stays readable.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the reaction row for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Roving tabindex: the row costs one Tab stop, Left/Right and Up/Down step without wrapping, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter and Space toggle. Withdrawing the last of a reaction walks focus to the neighbouring chip.
Under reduced motion nothing bursts or shrinks — the chip's fill swaps on a fast tween — but the count still rolls, because a count is information.
State is never colour alone: every chip carries aria-pressed and a sentence naming who reacted, and an sr-only status announces each change once, frozen at the press.

items.title: Reaction Picker
items.tagline: Quick reactions, on hover.
items.description: A quick-reaction bar that comes when you come near. Pointing at the message or focusing the React control raises the bar from eight pixels below on snap, and inside it the drawn marks lift toward the pointer on a measured 56px falloff; picking one sends a ghost of it flying to the reaction row on glide while the chip it lands on flashes. The tally commits at the press, so Arrow keys, Enter and Escape get the same instant truth as the pointer.

props.name: sender
props.description: Who wrote the message the picker sits on.

props.name: text
props.description: The message body.

props.name: time
props.description: Already formatted, printed beside the sender.

props.name: options
props.description: The pickable reactions: id, word and drawn mark.

props.name: baseCounts
props.description: Seeded counts from other people, added to yours in the row.

props.name: picked / defaultPicked
props.description: Controlled or initial list of reaction ids you have added.

props.name: onPickedChange
props.description: Fires with the whole next list on every pick or removal.

props.name: onPick
props.description: Fires with the reaction picked, before the ghost has landed.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial bar visibility; hover and focus drive it when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from hover, focus, Escape and a pick.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the message region for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The React control is always in the tab order: Enter or Arrow Down opens the bar and moves into it, Left/Right and Home/End walk the marks, Enter picks, and Escape closes and returns focus to the control.
Under reduced motion the bar cross-fades at its final position, the marks do not lift toward the pointer, and the pick lands on the chip at once instead of flying.
The row is a destination, not a control: each chip carries a sentence naming its reaction and count, and an sr-only status announces every pick once, frozen at the press.

items.title: Thread Open
items.tagline: A side conversation, opened.
items.description: A thread whose side conversations open beside it. Pressing a message's reply count slides a panel in from the right edge of the component's own frame on glide while a scrim fades the thread behind it and the replies cascade in from eight pixels below on snap at cascade(count). The panel is modal within the frame: Tab cycles inside it, Escape closes, and closing folds it back on the exit ease and returns focus to the count control that opened it.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first; a message's replies are its side conversation.

props.name: openId / defaultOpenId
props.description: Controlled or initial id of the message whose panel is open.

props.name: onOpenIdChange
props.description: Fires from a count press, Escape, the close control and the scrim.

props.name: onReply
props.description: Fires from Enter or Send in the panel with the trimmed text.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The panel composer's placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The count control is a button with aria-expanded and aria-haspopup="dialog"; the panel is aria-modal, takes focus on open, traps Tab and Shift+Tab, closes on Escape, and hands focus back to the control it came from.
Under reduced motion the panel does not travel: it cross-fades at its final position and the replies arrive together without stagger or offset, because the content is information.
The composer is a real textarea — Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line — and an sr-only status names each change once: opened, reply sent, closed.

items.title: Quote Block
items.tagline: Their words, in your message.
items.description: A message that carries someone else's words. The quote sits in the bubble as a card with a cobalt rule down its side, folded to one line until its disclosure glides it open on glide to a height a ResizeObserver measured; pointing at the card, or focusing either control, draws the wash across the matched words in the original with a scaleX from its left edge on snap. The second control carries the thread back to the source on glide and lands focus on it, and a quote whose words are not in the original says so in its own label.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first; a message's quote names its source and the words taken from it.

props.name: expandedId / defaultExpandedId
props.description: Controlled or initial id of the message whose quote card is unfolded; one at a time.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Fires from the disclosure control with the next unfolded id.

props.name: onShowSource
props.description: Fires when the thread is carried back to the original.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The card holds two controls: a disclosure with aria-expanded and aria-controls that folds and unfolds the passage, and a jump that scrolls the thread to the source and lands focus on it. The quote is a real blockquote with a cite, and the marked run in the original is a real mark.
Under reduced motion the height swaps on a fast tween, the wash appears at full width rather than wiping, and the jump sets scrollTop directly — focus still lands on the source.
An sr-only status names each change once: the quote folded or unfolded, and whose message is being shown.

items.title: Reply Line
items.tagline: Connected to the message it answers.
items.description: A thread that shows what a reply answers. Pointing at a reply, or walking to it with the arrow keys, draws a measured connector from its own edge up to its parent — one path of a fixed command count whose pathLength runs 0 to 1 on glide — while the answered message lifts four pixels on snap and takes a hairline ring. Leaving fades the line on the exit ease, and Enter on a reply moves focus to the message it answers.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first; replyTo names the message a reply answers.

props.name: activeId / defaultActiveId
props.description: Controlled or initial id of the reply whose line is drawn.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires from hover, focus, blur and Escape.

props.name: onJumpToParent
props.description: Fires when Enter on a reply moves focus to the message it answers.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Roving tabindex: the thread costs one Tab stop, Arrow Up and Down step between messages, Home and End jump, Enter on a reply moves focus to its parent, and Escape clears the line.
Under reduced motion the line appears at full length with a fade and the answered message takes its ring without travelling, because which message is answered is information.

Every message carries a sentence rather than a colour — "Rui at 07:44, replying to Marta at 07:12" — and the visible reading cross-fades in one grid cell so rapid arrow keys never leave it a step behind.

items.title: Reaction Tally
items.tagline: Every reaction, tallied.
items.description: A tally row that keeps reactions in standing order. A vote that overtakes reorders the row and every chip travels to its new slot as a layout FLIP on glide, while the chip in front pulses a cobalt ring on each new vote and the counts roll to their new face on snap. The chips are aria-pressed buttons on a roving tabindex: Left and Right step without wrapping, Home and End jump to the loudest and the quietest, Space toggles your own vote, and focus rides the chip rather than the slot so the chip you are on keeps focus while it moves.

props.name: reactions
props.description: The kinds and other people's counts, in first-reacted order; ties keep that order so a level row never churns.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial set of ids you have reacted to; your vote adds one to that kind's total.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from a chip press or Space with the next set of your ids.

props.name: onRankChange
props.description: Fires with the order, the leader, its total and the margin over second place after every change.

props.name: text
props.description: The message body the tally hangs under.

props.name: author
props.description: Printed above the bubble.

props.name: time
props.description: Sent time, printed under the bubble, already formatted.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: A roving tabindex across the chips: Left and Right step without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump to the loudest and the quietest, Space and Enter toggle your vote, and each chip's name is a sentence carrying its count and whether you reacted.
Under reduced motion the row reorders instantly and the leader holds a steady cobalt ring instead of pulsing — the standing still reads, only the travel is dropped.
Marks are drawn in a 16-unit box rather than typed, so a chip never depends on the reader's emoji font, and the count is spoken by the button's name rather than by the rolling digits.

items.title: Reply Count
items.tagline: Replies, and the last one's face.
items.description: A thread badge that carries the count and the last replier's face. An arrival bumps the badge from 1.06 back to rest on recoil — two keyframes, driven imperatively, because a spring drops anything in between — while the disc and the number swap on snap, each pair stacked in one grid cell so the outgoing face cross-fades under the incoming one instead of being shoved sideways. Replies past the ones you have read open a chip out of the badge's edge on snap; Enter or Space opens the thread and collapses it.

props.name: replies
props.description: The thread's replies, oldest first; append to it as they land.

props.name: seenCount / defaultSeenCount
props.description: Controlled or initial count of replies you have already read; the gap becomes the new chip.

props.name: onSeenCountChange
props.description: Fires when opening the thread marks everything read.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Fires from a press or Enter with the reply count.

props.name: text
props.description: The parent message's body.

props.name: author
props.description: Printed above the bubble.

props.name: time
props.description: The parent's sent time, already formatted.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: What the badge reads with no replies yet, beside a drawn reply arrow.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: One button in the tab order: Enter and Space open the thread and mark it read, and its name is a sentence — count, unread, last replier and time — so nothing is carried by colour or by a glyph.
Under reduced motion nothing bumps or slides: the disc and the number cross-fade in place and the new chip appears at full width rather than opening out of the edge.
An sr-only polite status speaks each arrival once, frozen at the moment it lands, so a host that later trims the list cannot make the region repeat a stale sentence.

items.title: Pin Message
items.tagline: Pinned to the top.
items.description: A thread with a bar at the top and a flight between them. Pressing a message's pin measures the gap between that row and the bar's floor at the moment of the press, and the copy enters the bar from exactly there, riding y to zero on glide, so it reads as lifted out of the thread rather than faded into a list; unpinning sends it back down the same distance on the exit ease. The bar's height comes from a ResizeObserver bound to its content, so an empty bar occupies nothing, and at the cap the remaining pin controls go aria-disabled with names that say why rather than leaving the tab order.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first; each carries an id, author, text and formatted time.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial pinned ids, most recently pinned first.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from a pin or an unpin with the next pinned set.

props.name: onPinChange
props.description: Fires with the message that changed and its new state.

props.name: onJump
props.description: Fires when a bar row sends focus down to its message.

props.name: maxPinned
props.description: How many the bar holds before the remaining pin controls refuse.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

props.name: barLabel
props.description: Names the pinned bar and heads it.

usageNotes: Every control is a real button in the tab order: each message's pin is aria-pressed and names the message it holds, each bar row carries a jump button that moves focus to that message — which takes aria-current while it is the jumped-to row — and its own unpin.
At the cap the unpinned messages' controls are aria-disabled rather than removed, and their names read "Bar full, unpin one first"; a polite status says the same.
Under reduced motion nothing flies: the copy appears with a fade and the bar's measured height changes on a fast tween, because what is pinned is information rather than flourish.

items.title: Star Mark
items.tagline: Saved for later.
items.description: A star, a folded corner, and the list that keeps them. Pressing a message's star grows a solid star out of the outline on recoil — two visible bounces, the one thing here that celebrates — while the bubble takes a corner mark scaling from its own corner on flick and the saved list gains the message, sliding in from 16px on glide with the newest save at the top. Unsaving reverses all three on the exit ease, and the panel's height comes from a ResizeObserver bound to its content so it is only ever as tall as what it holds.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first; each carries an id, author, text and formatted time.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial saved ids, most recently saved first.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from a star press or Space with the next saved set.

props.name: onSaveChange
props.description: Fires with the message that changed and its new state.

props.name: onJump
props.description: Fires when a saved row sends focus back to its message.

props.name: savedLabel
props.description: Names the saved list and heads it, beside the count.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: The panel's designed zero state, shown rather than reserved.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Each star is an aria-pressed button named for the message it saves, and each saved row carries a jump that moves focus back to that message — which takes aria-current while it is the jumped-to row — and its own remove control.

Under reduced motion the star fills in colour, the corner mark appears without a stamp and the saved row cross-fades in; the panel's height still changes, because the list is the record of what you saved.
The star's points are solved once and rounded to three decimals, so the same path string is drawn on the server and in the browser.

items.title: Translate Flip
items.tagline: Their language, then yours.
items.description: A message that turns over into its translation. The card rotates about its horizontal axis on snap — one crisp overshoot, two keyframes — with the original and the translation as the two faces of one card, each hiding its back, while observers measure both faces so the card glides to the active one's height on glide rather than reserving room for the longer text. The original stays under a fold that opens at a measured height, Escape closes it and hands focus back, and a language chip rides the corner rail from one corner to the other as a layout FLIP.

props.name: text
props.description: The message as it arrived, in the source language.

props.name: translation
props.description: The rendering in the reader's language.

props.name: source / target
props.description: Where it came from and the reader's language; each is a code for the chip and a name for every control.

props.name: translated / defaultTranslated
props.description: Controlled or initial face.

props.name: onTranslatedChange
props.description: Fires from the control or Space with the next face.

props.name: originalOpen / defaultOriginalOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial state of the fold that holds the original.

props.name: onOriginalOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the fold control, from Escape, and when turning back closes the fold.

props.name: pending
props.description: The host is still producing the translation: the chip turns an arc and the control refuses with aria-disabled.

props.name: author
props.description: Printed above the card.

props.name: time
props.description: Sent time, already formatted.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Translate is an aria-pressed button named for the language it will show; the fold is aria-expanded and aria-controls its region, and Escape anywhere in the card closes the fold and returns focus to the fold control.
Both faces stay in the DOM and the one that is turned away is aria-hidden and inert to the pointer, so a screen reader never reads the same message twice.

Under reduced motion the card does not turn: the faces cross-fade in place, the chip swaps corners at once and the pending arc holds still, while the measured height still changes because which language you are reading is information.

items.title: Presence Dot
items.tagline: Here, away, or gone.
items.description: Four states drawn as four shapes, so colour is never the only signal: online fills, away takes a crescent bite, busy is crossed by a bar, offline is a hollow dimmed ring. The bite and the bar are holes in one SVG mask that scale in on snap, away breathes a slow mirrored ring, and every change rings once from a key rather than a timer. The sentence is frozen at the moment of the change and spoken once by a polite status region.

props.name: status
props.description: The state; drives the shape, the colour, the breath and the ring.

props.name: name
props.description: Whose presence it is; opens the spoken sentence.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible text beside the mark. Omit it and the status word is drawn instead.

props.name: detail
props.description: A quieter trailing clause ("back at 15:30"), spoken with the status.

props.name: size
props.description: 8, 10 or 14px marks; the breath and the ring scale with it.

props.name: showWord
props.description: Draws the status word beside the mark, so the shape is never alone.

props.name: ring
props.description: The one-shot ring on a change; turn it off in dense rosters.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: Fires from an effect once per frozen sentence, after a change.

usageNotes: No pointer gesture and no keyboard path of its own: the mark is role="img" naming the state, the status word is drawn beside it by default, and with no visible label the mark carries the whole sentence — so the colour is never alone.
Under reduced motion the shapes still swap and offline still dims — shape is information — but nothing breathes, rings or scales.
A polite sr-only status region speaks the frozen sentence once per change; onAnnounce fires alongside it, never from a state updater or during render.

items.title: Member List
items.tagline: Who is in the room.
items.description: A roster in two groups whose rows carry layout, so a change of state re-sorts them on glide, and a useId-prefixed layoutId, so a member crossing from offline to online travels between the two lists as one row instead of blinking. Arrivals slide in from distances.step under a cobalt wash replayed by a key, departures only fade on the exit ease, and the frame's height comes from a ResizeObserver so an empty group reserves nothing. Rows are buttons under a roving tabindex: Down and Up step through both groups, Home and End jump to the ends.

props.name: members
props.description: The room; sorted into two groups, with ties keeping the array's order.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the roster for assistive technology; opens each group's list label.

props.name: groupLabels
props.description: The two headings.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fires from a row's click, Enter or Space.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: Fires once per frozen change sentence ("Rui Baptista is online").

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Drawn when the room is empty.

usageNotes: Roving tabindex over both groups in visual order: ArrowDown and ArrowUp step, Home and End jump to the first and last member, Enter and Space select the focused row.
Under reduced motion nothing travels — rows cross-fade, the wash becomes one steady tint, and the measured frame changes height on a tween.
Every row's accessible name is a sentence ("Marta Ferreira, away, on dock three") and each state prints its word beside the dot, so presence is never carried by colour alone.

items.title: Avatar Cluster
items.tagline: The room, at a glance.
items.description: Faces overlap by ten pixels until the cluster is hovered or holds focus, and then each face's own margin glides apart on glide so the cluster widens rather than sliding faces out from under each other. Avatars are procedural — initials over a rim signature hashed from the id into pathLength fractions, rounded before they reach an attribute — and the speaking member lifts on snap under a cobalt ring that breathes. The overflow count rolls in the direction it moved, and a roving tabindex over the faces is the keyboard's path to the spread.

props.name: people
props.description: The room, in stacking order; the first face sits on top.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the cluster and the overflow chip ("Coldbrook standup").

props.name: max
props.description: Faces drawn before the overflow chip.

props.name: speakingId
props.description: Who is speaking; that face lifts, rings and rises above its neighbours.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fires from a face's click, Enter or Space.

props.name: onOverflowSelect
props.description: Fires from the overflow chip.

usageNotes: Roving tabindex over the faces and the overflow chip: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight step, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter and Space select, Escape collapses the spread without moving focus.
Under reduced motion the spread is instant, the speaking ring holds steady instead of breathing, and the overflow count cross-fades in place.
Every face is a button whose accessible name is a sentence ("Rui Baptista, speaking"), and a polite status region speaks a change of speaker or of the head count once.

items.title: Status Line
items.tagline: What they are up to.
items.description: A custom status under a name that types itself out from an effect with cleanup, holding where it stands while the tab is hidden, with a caret blinking beside the last character until it settles. Clearing wipes the line away left to right on an animated clipPath, and because the exiting node keeps the text it last drew the wipe erases the real sentence. An expiry ring drains on glide toward each remaining fraction the parent reports, rounded before it reaches the attribute, and the measured frame means no status reserves no room.

props.name: name
props.description: The person the status belongs to; drawn as initials and spoken with the clear control.

props.name: roleLabel
props.description: A quiet second line under the name ("Coldbrook dispatch").

props.name: status
props.description: The custom line. A new value types itself; null wipes the old one away.

props.name: expiry
props.type: { label: string; remaining: number; total: number }
props.description: Ring plus printed remainder; the label is already formatted, and no clock is read.

props.name: typeSpeed
props.description: Milliseconds per character while typing.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Copy for the clear control.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Fires from the Clear control and from Escape; set status to null here.

props.name: onSettle
props.description: Fires once when the line finishes typing.

props.name: onExpire
props.description: Fires from an effect when expiry.remaining reaches zero.

usageNotes: Clear is a real button in the tab order; Escape from anywhere inside the block clears too, and the control names the person it clears for.
Under reduced motion the line is drawn whole with no caret and fades instead of wiping, while the expiry ring still drains — a countdown is information.
A polite status region speaks "Status set: …" once on settle and "Status cleared" once on the wipe, never per character.

items.title: Last Seen
items.tagline: Seen, minutes ago.
items.description: A wording rather than a clock: minutes arrive as a prop and the component only adds to them from a ticker it is asked to run, in an effect with cleanup that stops while the tab is hidden. As the total crosses a threshold the label re-writes itself — just now, a minute ago, an hour ago — with the old words leaving upward and the new arriving from below on glide, stacked in one grid cell and cross-faded so a fast ticker never leaves the reading behind. Coming online swaps the label for a dot that lands on recoil beside the word Online.

props.name: name
props.description: Whose presence it is; opens the spoken sentence.

props.name: minutesAgo
props.description: Minutes since they were last seen, from the host — never from a clock.

props.name: online
props.description: Swaps the label for a dot and the word Online.

props.name: at
props.description: An already-formatted wall time ("14:52"), printed after the wording.

props.name: ticking
props.description: Runs the internal count-up; the host owns the decision.

props.name: tickMs
props.description: Milliseconds per added minute; a demo can shorten it to make the climb visible.

props.name: label
props.description: Leading words while offline.

props.name: format
props.description: Overrides the wording ladder for other locales.

props.name: onWordingChange
props.description: Fires from an effect whenever the drawn reading changes.

usageNotes: A label with no pointer gesture and so no keyboard path of its own: the reading is role="img" with a full sentence, and the word Online is always drawn beside the dot.
Under reduced motion the wording cross-fades in place and the dot lands at full size, while the count still runs and still re-words itself.
The ticker stops while the tab is hidden and while the person is online, and a polite status region announces only the online swap and unit crossings — never the minute-by-minute climb.

items.title: Typing Cluster
items.tagline: Several people, typing.
items.description: One typer gets a row of their own, and so does a second; the moment a third starts the rows merge into one cluster, every disc keeping its own element and sliding into the overlapped stack on glide. The merged row's name slot rotates through the typers on snap, and pressing it spreads the stack back into the named rows — Escape re-merges without moving focus. The whole strip lives in a ResizeObserver-measured height, so one row, three rows and none of them are all the same glide.

props.name: typing
props.description: Who is typing, in the order they started. Empty collapses the strip.

props.name: mergeAt
props.description: Typers needed before the separate rows merge into one cluster.

props.name: rotateMs
props.description: Milliseconds each name holds the merged row's slot.

props.name: maxFaces
props.description: Discs drawn in the stack before the rest become a rolling +N.

props.name: expanded / defaultExpanded
props.description: Controlled or initial spread state of the merged cluster.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Fires when the cluster is spread or re-merged.

props.name: onFocusNameChange
props.description: Fires when the rotating slot lands on a different name; null when nobody types.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the strip for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Tab reaches the merged cluster, Enter or Space spreads it into the named rows, and Escape re-merges it without moving focus.
Under reduced motion nothing travels: the discs take their stacked or spread positions directly, the names cross-fade in the slot, and the caret holds steady instead of blinking.
Each spread row carries its own sentence and a polite status line speaks once per roster change, so the rotating name is decoration rather than the only way to know who is typing.

items.title: Join Toast
items.tagline: Someone arrived.
items.description: A card lands above the room's own content on recoil when a member joins, while the cards already there glide down through layout so the stack opens instead of reflowing. Each card drains a linear hairline timer and clears itself on the exit ease; past max the older arrivals fold into one summary line whose count rolls on snap and whose timers keep running. Pointer or focus holds every timer, Escape clears the stack, and the whole thing sits in a ResizeObserver-measured height inside the component's own box.

props.name: arrivals
props.description: Who has joined, oldest first; { id, name, note? }. The host removes them in onDismiss.

props.name: room
props.description: The room's name, spoken in every card's sentence.

props.name: duration
props.description: Milliseconds a card stays before it clears itself; 0 or less keeps it up.

props.name: max
props.description: Cards shown before the older ones fold into the summary line.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Fires when a card's timer runs out or its close control is pressed.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Fires when Escape clears the whole stack.

props.name: onHoldChange
props.description: Fires as the pointer or focus enters and leaves the stack.

props.name: children
props.description: The room content the stack sits above and pushes down.

usageNotes: Every card is an li whose accessible name is a sentence, each carries a real dismiss button in newest-first tab order, and Escape anywhere in the stack clears it.
Focus inside the stack holds every timer, which is the keyboard's path to the hover pause.
Under reduced motion the cards fade in place with no travel and no bounce and the height swaps on a tween, but the timers still run because an arrival's expiry is information.

items.title: Role Badge
items.tagline: Admin, mod, member.
items.description: A role pill beside a member's name that morphs rather than swaps: the glyph and the word stack in one grid cell and cross-fade, the incoming glyph arriving from 0.6 on snap while the ink transitions on a colour tween. A promotion glints — a sheen sweeps the pill once while it lands from 1.06 on recoil — and a demotion only dims, because a demotion never celebrates. The pill opens the ladder as a real listbox in flow beneath the row, where arrows move, Enter chooses, and Escape returns focus to the pill.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial role value; defaults to the first role.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the chosen role's value.

props.name: onRoleChange
props.description: Fires with { value, label, direction } where direction is promoted, demoted or changed.

props.name: roles
props.description: The ladder, lowest rank first; { value, label, rank, description? }.

props.name: name
props.description: The member's name, shown and spoken in the change sentence.

props.name: handle
props.description: The member's handle, shown under the name.

props.name: editable
props.description: False renders the pill as a label with no list and no tab stop.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds the pill; the role still reads.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial state of the role list.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires as the list opens and closes.

usageNotes: The pill is a listbox button: Enter or Space opens the ladder, Arrow keys move the active option, Home and End jump, Enter or Space chooses, and Escape closes and returns focus to the pill.
The list opens in flow under the row inside a ResizeObserver-measured height, so it never floats over what the host wrote below it.
Under reduced motion nothing sweeps or bounces, but a promotion still flashes its ink and a demotion still dims, because the direction of a role change is information.

items.title: Online Count
items.tagline: How many are here now.
items.description: The figure is a row of ten-face wheels, so only the place that changed travels — up when the count rose, down when it fell, on snap. Beside it a graph of the window extends: one bar per sample, the newest growing in on snap while the rest slide left on glide through layout and the oldest pops out on the exit ease. Pressing the figure pins a name list open in flow inside the card, in a ResizeObserver-measured height, and Escape closes it.

props.name: names
props.description: Who is here now, in the order the list should read them.

props.name: count
props.description: The figure, when the host counts more people than it can name.

props.name: history
props.description: Samples across the window, oldest first; the graph draws the last `samples` of them.

props.name: samples
props.description: Bars kept in the graph.

props.name: windowLabel
props.description: Names the graph's span in the caption and in the spoken sentence.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the instrument for assistive technology.

props.name: maxNames
props.description: Names listed before the rest become an "and N more" line.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
