props.description: The house rule the removal cited.

props.name: steps
props.description: The review's stages: value, label and an optional note.

props.name: step / defaultStep
props.description: Controlled or initial count of stamped stages.

props.name: onStepChange
props.description: Fires when sending the appeal stamps the first stage.

props.name: note / defaultNote
props.description: Controlled or initial appeal note.

props.name: onNoteChange
props.description: Fires from every keystroke in the textarea.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Fires from Send appeal with the trimmed note.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Cap on the note; the remainder reads beside the control.

props.name: decision
props.description: The outcome. Only the host sets it.

props.name: decisionNote
props.description: One line under the decision.

props.name: onDecisionShown
props.description: Fires once when a decision first lands, after the state settles.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds the textarea and the control.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes on the card.

usageNotes: Tab reaches the textarea then Send appeal; Send is genuinely disabled while the note is empty or the appeal has already gone, and each stage carries its own sr-only sentence rather than a colour.
Under reduced motion the stamps still stamp and approval still restores — on fast tweens, with no scale and no travel — because a completed stage is information.
The decision only ever comes from the `decision` prop, so the polite status region can never announce an outcome before the host has answered with it.

items.title: Filter Mask
items.tagline: Words, masked.
items.description: Words a room filter caught, kept in place under opaque hatched blocks so uncovering one never reflows the line. Each cover is a motion span with its origin on the right whose scaleX runs to zero on snap, so it retreats rightward and the word appears in reading order; revealing everything runs the same wipe in a cascade, and masking again grows the covers back on glide. Every block is a real button with a whole-sentence label, and the count above the bubble reads as a pluralised sentence that cross-fades in one grid cell.

props.name: text
props.description: The message. Caught words are matched inside it.

props.name: terms
props.description: The words the room filter catches, matched whole-word and case-insensitively.

props.name: author
props.description: The sender, shown above the bubble.

props.name: time
props.description: A plain string: the component never reads a clock.

props.name: filterName
props.description: Who masked the words; named in the header sentence.

props.name: revealed / defaultRevealed
props.description: Controlled or initial reveal-all state.

props.name: onRevealedChange
props.description: Fires from the header toggle.

props.name: onWordReveal
props.description: Fires when a single block is uncovered.

props.name: onMaskedCountChange
props.description: Fires from an effect whenever the masked count changes.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds the toggle and every block.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes on the wrapper.

usageNotes: Every masked word is an ordinary tab stop with aria-pressed: Space and Enter uncover one word, and the header toggle uncovers or covers them all.
A masked word is never readable while it is masked — the block's label names nothing until it is uncovered, and then names the word — so a screen reader hears what the sighted reader sees.
Under reduced motion the covers cross-fade instead of wiping and the cascade collapses, but the count and the header sentence still update.

items.title: Mod Queue
items.tagline: Waiting for a moderator.
items.description: Reported messages one at a time, with the rest of the queue named underneath and a toolbar that does not move. A verdict slides the card out on the exit ease — right for Keep, left for Hide and Time out — while the next rises from 8px on glide, so the button you pressed keeps your focus and a whole queue clears without re-finding it. The waiting count and the tallies roll their digits on snap, and the card area is a ResizeObserver-measured height that closes onto a cleared line rather than reserving room.

props.name: items
props.description: The reported messages: id, author, text, reason and report count, front of the queue first.

props.name: label
props.description: The queue's heading.

props.name: index / defaultIndex
props.description: Controlled or initial position in the queue.

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Fires each time the front card changes.

props.name: onAct
props.description: Fires with "keep", "hide" or "timeout" and the item it was passed on.

props.name: onEmpty
props.description: Fires once when the last card leaves.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: The cleared line.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds the toolbar; the queue still reads.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes on the panel.

usageNotes: The verdicts are a role="toolbar" with a roving tabindex: Left and Right step without wrapping, Home and End jump, Space and Enter act, and each button's name is a sentence naming the member it would act on.
An empty queue marks the buttons aria-disabled rather than disabled, because a disabled button is blurred by the browser and clearing the last card must not cost you your place.
Under reduced motion nothing slides and the digits swap instead of rolling, but the queue still empties and the measured height still closes.

items.title: Trust Level
items.tagline: Earned, over time.
items.description: A ladder of level pips on a rail whose fill glides to the level held plus the way through the next one, its width rounded before it becomes a string motion paints. A level up stamps — the pip lands from 1.6 on recoil with its tick drawing on flick, and the bar badge beside the name cross-fades in one grid cell and lands on the same spring — while a level lost only dims, because losing standing must not celebrate. Hovering or focusing a pip reads what that level unlocked in a panel that opens in flow in a measured height, and the pips are a real tablist with Arrow, Home and End keys.

props.name: name
props.description: The member, shown and spoken.

props.name: handle
props.description: The member's handle, shown under the name.

props.name: room
props.description: The room the trust is held in; named in the sentences.

props.name: levels
props.description: The ladder, lowest first: a label and what it unlocks.

props.name: level
props.description: The level reached, as an index into levels. Only the host earns it.

props.name: progress
props.description: How far through the next level, 0 to 1.

props.name: onLevelChange
props.description: Fires after a level settles with its level, label and direction.

props.name: shownLevel / defaultShownLevel
props.description: Controlled or initial index of the level being read; defaults to the level held.

props.name: onShownLevelChange
props.description: Fires from hover, focus and the Arrow keys.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds the pips; the ladder and the fill still read.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes on the card.

usageNotes: The pips are a role="tablist" with a roving tabindex: Left and Right step without wrapping, Home and End jump, and selection follows focus, so the hover reveal is never a mouse-only feature.

The value lives on a role="meter" whose aria-valuetext is a whole sentence — "Level 3 of 4, Trusted, 62 percent of the way to Guide." — and the panel opens in flow in a measured height rather than floating over the host's content.
Under reduced motion the fill still fills and the panel still opens on fast tweens; nothing stamps, but a level lost still dims once so the direction of the change survives.

items.title: Poll Builder
items.tagline: Ask the room.
items.description: A poll written in the composer and watched from the thread. Each option added slides in from 8px on glide while the composer's box takes its new height from a ResizeObserver on its own content on the same spring, and the multiple-answers switch morphs the preview's marks between circles and squares on snap. Posting is the rise: the draft's dashed edge goes solid and the bubble comes up on recoil while the box closes to a posted line. Enter inside an option adds a row and takes focus into it, Backspace in an empty one removes it, and Control or Command with Enter posts.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial draft: question, options and whether multiple answers are allowed.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from every keystroke, add, remove and switch, from the setter that made the change.

props.name: posted / defaultPosted
props.description: Controlled or initial posted state; the composer closes while it is true.

props.name: onPostedChange
props.description: Fires from Post and from the New poll control.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires with the trimmed draft the moment Post is pressed.

props.name: maxOptions
props.description: Options the poll may carry before Add option locks.

props.name: minOptions
props.description: Rows the builder will not go below, and the count Post requires.

props.name: sender
props.description: Name used in the preview bubble's sentence.

props.name: time
props.description: Already formatted; printed under the posted bubble. The component never reads a clock.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread for assistive technology.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds every field and control; the preview still reads.

usageNotes: Real inputs throughout: Tab runs question, option, its Remove, the next option, then Multiple, Add option and Post. Enter inside an option adds a row below and moves focus into it, Backspace in an empty option removes that row and returns focus above, and Control or Command with Enter posts from anywhere in the composer.
Post stays in the tab order while the draft is incomplete, carrying aria-disabled and an aria-label sentence naming what is missing rather than going silent.
Under reduced motion rows appear and vanish on opacity alone, the box resizes on a fast tween, and posting swaps the bubble's edge without the rise.

items.title: Event Card
items.tagline: Are you coming?
items.description: An invitation sent into a thread, answered in the room. Your tile waits at the end of the attendee strip behind a dashed edge, and choosing moves it — motion reorders the same node into the going or maybe run on glide, ζ0.98, because joining a list is a layout shift and not a pop — while the going count rolls to its new figure on snap. The three controls are a real radio group: Left and Right move and select without wrapping, Home and End jump, and pressing the answer you already gave withdraws it.

props.name: event
props.description: The invitation: id, from, title, when, where, and an optional time and delivery mark.

props.name: attendees
props.description: Everyone but you, each already going or a maybe.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial RSVP: going, maybe, no, or nothing yet.

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: (status: RsvpStatus | null, previous: RsvpStatus | null) => void
props.description: Fires from the press or key that answers, and from the press that withdraws.

props.name: you
props.description: Your display name; the initials on your own tile.

props.name: capacity
props.description: How many the event holds. Set, the chip reads 5 of 8 and Going locks with a sentence once it fills.

props.name: peerName
props.description: Names the sender in the delivery sentence.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread for assistive technology.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds the three controls; the card still reads.

usageNotes: A radio group with a roving tabindex: Left and Up, Right and Down move and select without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump, Space selects, and pressing the answer you already gave withdraws it.
Every control carries an aria-label sentence with the count in it and every attendee's name is real text, so no state rests on a fill or a tint.
Under reduced motion your tile does not travel — it is simply in its new place — and the count still changes, because a guest list is information.

items.title: Pay Request
items.tagline: Money, asked for in chat.
items.description: A request for money sent as a message — a record of an ask, never a transfer. The amount rolls: each digit column takes its new position on snap so a re-split reads as the figure changing rather than the row redrawing. Under it a confirm track takes a deliberate gesture — the knob follows the pointer and captures it only after 4px of travel, returns on snap short of the threshold, and commits past it — and committing stamps a PAID mark from 1.16× on recoil while the track cross-fades to a settled row in one shared grid cell. The knob is a real slider: arrows step it, End commits, Escape abandons, Enter commits from where it stands.

props.name: request
props.description: The message: id, from, who is asking, the amount, an optional note, time and delivery mark.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats the amount; the figure is rounded to cents before it reaches it.

props.name: currency
props.description: The unit printed beside the amount; it never rolls.

props.name: paid / defaultPaid
props.description: Controlled or initial settled state; the track gives way to the settled row.

props.name: onPay
props.description: Fires once, the moment the gesture or key commits.

props.name: onProgressChange
props.description: Fires with the knob's whole-percent position as it moves.

props.name: threshold
props.description: Share of the track the knob must pass to commit; short of it the knob returns.

props.name: paidAt
props.description: Already formatted; printed in the settled row. The component never reads a clock.

props.name: provider
props.description: Printed in the footer beside the note that this is a request and not a transfer.

props.name: peerName
props.description: Names the sender in the delivery sentence.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread for assistive technology.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds the track; the card still reads.

usageNotes: The knob is a real role=slider with aria-valuenow and an aria-label sentence: Right and Up step it 10 percent, Left and Down step back, Home returns it, End takes it to the far end and commits, Escape abandons the gesture, and Enter or Space commits from where it stands.
The pointer is captured only after 4px of travel, inside try/catch, so a plain click is never swallowed and a synthetic sweep cannot throw.
Under reduced motion the knob still follows the pointer but returns instantly, and the stamp fades on in place instead of bouncing — the outcome still shows, because it is information.

items.title: Chat Task
items.tagline: A task that ticks.
items.description: A job handed to somebody in a thread, and the moment it is finished. The tick is drawn rather than revealed — its pathLength runs 0 to 1 on flick, the stroke arriving in the time a pen would take — then a rule strikes the line as a background wipe cloned onto every line fragment, so a wrapped title is struck line by line, and last the assignee's tile takes a check badge landing from 1.18× on recoil. The due line and the done line share one grid cell and cross-fade, so checking never moves the card. Space or Enter toggles the real checkbox.

props.name: task
props.description: The message: id, from, title, assignee, and an optional due phrase, time and delivery mark.

props.name: checked / defaultChecked
props.description: Controlled or initial done state.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that toggles the box, from the setter that made the change.

props.name: doneAt
props.description: Already formatted; printed in the done line. The component never reads a clock.

props.name: overdue
props.description: Warms the due line and rewords it, so lateness is a sentence rather than a colour.

props.name: doneBy
props.description: Who is credited in the done line.

props.name: peerName
props.description: Names the sender in the delivery sentence.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread for assistive technology.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds the checkbox; it keeps its place in the tab order and the card still reads.

usageNotes: A real role=checkbox named by the task line and described by the line under it, so its name is the job and its description is the deadline; Space or Enter toggles it and it stays in the tab order while disabled, carrying aria-disabled.
The done state is spoken by aria-checked and by a real line of text, and lateness is worded rather than tinted, so nothing rests on the grey.
Under reduced motion the tick appears whole, the rule appears at full width and the badge fades on — all three still show, because a finished task is information.

items.title: Countdown Card
items.tagline: Until the thing.
items.description: A message that is counting, and the moment it stops. Each digit column is ten faces tall and takes its new position on snap, so the seconds column rolls every second while the minutes column sits still until it is its turn, and a rail under the digits drains linearly across the whole span. Reaching zero turns the card: the countdown face rotates from 0 to 90 degrees while the event face rotates from -90 to 0, both on glide with their back faces hidden, so one card turns over rather than two swapping. The run is one motion value started by a prop, held while the document is hidden, and never reads a clock.

props.name: event
props.description: The message: id, from, title, the line the event face shows on arrival, and an optional place, time and delivery mark.

props.name: seconds
props.description: The run's length in seconds. Changing it is the reset: the run remounts and starts over.

props.name: running
props.description: Runs the countdown. The timing belongs to the host, never to a clock the card reads.

props.name: onRemainingChange
props.description: Fires from the run each time the whole second changes.

props.name: onReached
props.description: Fires once, when the remainder reaches zero and the card turns.

props.name: showHours
props.description: Forces the hours column for a run shorter than an hour.

props.name: peerName
props.description: Names the sender in the delivery sentence.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The readout is a role=timer whose aria-label is a sentence rebuilt each second but never announced; an sr-only status speaks only on settle and at coarse milestones — the run starting or being held, one minute left, ten seconds left, and zero.
The run lives in an effect with cleanup, holds where it stands while the document is hidden, and takes its length only from the seconds prop, so the card never reads Date.now().
Under reduced motion the card does not turn: the faces cross-fade in place and the digits swap without rolling, while the rail keeps draining at the same linear rate.

items.title: Carousel Card
items.tagline: Several cards, one message.
items.description: A deck of cards carried by one message. The track glides to the chosen slide on glide while the dot row's pill travels between dots on snap through a useId-prefixed layoutId, so one pill moves rather than four dots blinking. A finger drags the rail one-to-one and the release snaps to the nearest card; Left and Right step the dots without wrapping, Home and End jump to the first and last, and focusing a card's control brings that card in.

props.name: items
props.description: The slides in rail order; each is { id, title, note?, price?, meta? } and draws a procedural swatch seeded from its id.

props.name: index / defaultIndex
props.description: Controlled or initial slide index.

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Fires from the setter that moved the rail: an arrow, a dot, a key, or a settled drag.

props.name: onCardAction
props.description: Fires from a slide's control with that slide's item.

props.name: actionLabel
props.description: The word on each slide's control.

props.name: format
props.description: Money formatter for an item's price; the locale is pinned so the server's string matches the client's.

props.name: peek
props.description: Pixels of the next card left showing, subtracted from the measured viewport width.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the carousel for assistive technology.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes on the bubble.

usageNotes: Three tab stops: Previous, the dot row (roving tabindex, Left and Right step without wrapping, Home and End jump to the ends), and Next; every card's action control stays in the tab order and brings its card into view on focus.
Under reduced motion the track swaps on a fast tween instead of gliding and the dot pill drops its layoutId to fill in place; dragging still tracks the hand, because that motion is the viewer's own.
Pointer capture is taken only after 4px of travel and inside a try/catch, so a tap on a card's control still lands and a synthetic drag sweep never throws.

items.title: Form Card
items.tagline: A form, in the thread.
items.description: A real form that lives in a thread and keeps its answer. Sending collapses the fields and stamps the values into a summary whose rows arrive from 8px on snap in a cascade while the box glides on glide to the height a ResizeObserver measured, and a Sent chip lands on recoil. An empty required field refuses the send instead of celebrating: it takes aria-invalid with a named message and focus, and Edit returns the fields with their values and puts focus back in the first one.

props.name: fields
props.description: The questions in order; each is { id, label, kind?, options?, placeholder?, required?, hint? } and renders a real input or select.

props.name: values / defaultValues
props.description: Controlled or initial answers, keyed by field id.

props.name: onValuesChange
props.description: Fires from the change handler that caused it, with the next whole record.

props.name: submitted / defaultSubmitted
props.description: Controlled or initial face: true shows the summary, false the fields.

props.name: onSubmittedChange
props.description: Fires from Send and from Edit, in that direction.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Fires once from a send that passed, with the frozen answers.

props.name: title
props.description: The card's heading, which names the form for assistive technology.

props.name: note
props.description: One quieter line under the heading.

props.name: submitLabel
props.description: The word on the submit control.

props.name: editLabel
props.description: The word on the summary's control.

props.name: sentLabel
props.description: The chip's word once the card is sent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds every field and control.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes on the card.

usageNotes: A real form: every field has a real label, Enter inside a text field submits, a refused send moves focus to the first field that still needs an answer, and Edit returns focus to the first field once the faces have swapped.
Under reduced motion the two faces cross-fade on a fast tween, the summary rows arrive together instead of cascading, and the Sent chip appears at full size with no bounce.
The box measures whichever face is live with a ResizeObserver and ignores the zero reading taken mid-swap, so no height is reserved for the taller face and the card never collapses for a frame.

items.title: Location Share
items.tagline: Where I am, live.
items.description: A live location in the thread. The pin glides across a procedural map on glide as each new position arrives, the walked path draws behind it, and an accuracy halo breathes on a slow reversing tween. A ring around the sharer's initials empties as the share runs out, driven from a secondsLeft prop rather than a clock read during render, and stopping dims the pin to a last-seen marker; a polite region speaks one sentence per place change, never per tick.

props.name: person
props.description: Who is sharing; the puck's initials are taken from it.

props.name: position
props.description: The pin, normalised 0 to 1 inside the map box; every derived coordinate is rounded before it reaches an attribute.

props.name: trail
props.description: The path already walked, oldest first, drawn as a polyline behind the pin.

props.name: place
props.description: The nearest landmark in words; a change here is what the live region announces.

props.name: secondsLeft
props.description: Seconds of sharing left. The host counts it down; the card never reads a clock.

props.name: totalSeconds
props.description: The share's full length, which the countdown ring is drawn against.

props.name: status
props.description: Ended dims the pin, stops the halo and replaces the controls with a last-seen line.

props.name: lastSeenTime
props.description: A preformatted time shown once the share has ended.

props.name: accuracyMeters
props.description: Sizes the halo and is spoken in the map's accessible name.

props.name: seed
props.description: Picks the procedural map: streets, river and park all come from integers.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Fires from the Stop control.

props.name: onExtend
props.description: Fires from Add 15 minutes with 900.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the card for assistive technology.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes on the card.

usageNotes: The map is a role=img named by one whole sentence, the countdown is a role=timer with aria-live off, and a polite status speaks only on a place change, on the last minute, and at the end.
Under reduced motion the pin swaps to its new position instantly and the halo holds a steady disc, but the countdown ring still empties: how long is left is information, not flourish.
Nothing here reads a clock. The host owns the tick and passes secondsLeft, so a demo's interval can live in an effect with cleanup and pause while the document is hidden.

items.title: Receipt Card
items.tagline: Paid, and here is the proof.
items.description: A paid receipt folded into one line of a thread. Pressing it unrolls the paper: the body's height is measured through a callback ref and glides open on glide while the item lines arrive from 4px up in a cascade, and the total lands last and rolls its digits up from zero on snap. Enter and Space fold and unfold it, Escape folds it from anywhere inside and returns focus to the summary control, and the torn bottom edge is drawn from integer teeth sized by its container.

props.name: merchant
props.description: Who was paid; it heads the summary and names the card.

props.name: date
props.description: A preformatted date. The card never reads a clock.

props.name: method
props.description: How it was paid, in words, printed beside the date.

props.name: reference
props.description: A reference code printed under the total.

props.name: lines
props.description: The item lines as { id, label, qty?, amount }, printed in order and summed into the total.

props.name: extras
props.description: Service, delivery and the like, printed under a dashed rule and summed with the rest.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial fold state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the summary control and from Escape, with the next state.

props.name: format
props.description: Money formatter for every figure; amounts are rounded to cents before they are summed or spoken.

props.name: paidLabel
props.description: The chip's word, which says the state in words rather than in a colour.

props.name: totalLabel
props.description: The total row's word.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the receipt for assistive technology; falls back to a sentence naming the merchant.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes on the card.

usageNotes: The summary is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls whose name is one whole sentence carrying the merchant, the total and the date; Enter and Space toggle it and Escape folds it from anywhere inside, returning focus to the control.
Under reduced motion the lines fade in together with no cascade and no travel, the height swaps on a fast tween, and the total appears at its value instead of rolling.

The body is unmounted while the receipt is folded, so its height is measured through a callback ref that attaches the observer when the node arrives rather than in a mount-only effect that would find nothing.

items.title: Availability Grid
items.tagline: When everyone is free.
items.description: A message that asks a room when it is free and answers itself as the answers arrive. Each cell fills from its bottom edge on glide by the share of the room that can make that slot, the figure rolls to its new value on snap, and the crown ring travels from the old leader to the new one on snap through a useId-prefixed layoutId. It is a real role=grid with a roving tabindex — arrows move a cell, Home and End jump along the row, Space toggles your answer — and posting the leader stamps a tick on recoil.

props.name: days
props.description: Column headings in order; long names truncate with a title.

props.name: times
props.description: Row headings in order, one per time band.

props.name: people
props.description: The room's size. Every count is out of it, and it sizes each fill's share.

props.name: votes
props.description: Everyone else's answers, keyed "<dayIndex>-<timeIndex>".

props.name: mine / defaultMine
props.description: Controlled or initial list of slot keys you said yes to — the only vote a viewer can change.

props.name: onMineChange
props.description: Fires from the setter that toggled a cell, with the next whole list.

props.name: decided
props.description: The posted slot key. Only the host sets it; it locks the grid and stamps the chosen cell.

props.name: onPost
props.description: Fires from the post control with the leading slot's key.

props.name: postLabel
props.description: The word on the post control.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Holds every cell and the post control.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the grid for assistive technology.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes on the card.

usageNotes: A real role=grid with columnheaders, rowheaders and a roving tabindex: arrows move one cell, Home and End jump to the ends of the row, and Space or Enter toggles your answer. Each cell's name is one whole sentence naming the slot, the count and your own answer.

Under reduced motion the fills still fill and the figures still change — a count is information — but nothing travels, the crown appears on the leader rather than flying to it, and the posted tick lands at full size.

Ties break by the earliest slot, so the crown never flickers between two equal cells, and the spoken sentence is worked out by diffing the answer that actually arrived, never the one the press hoped for.

items.title: Mention List
items.tagline: Where you were named.
items.description: The inbox of every place your name came up, with the line you were named in and your handle set as a chip inside it. Rows arrive from distances.step on snap in a cascade while layout on glide carries the rows already there down to make room, and opening one flares its own wash and drains it over durations.page on the exit ease before dimming the row to read. A roving tabindex moves with Down and Up, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space opens.

props.name: mentions
props.description: Newest first: id, author, room, time and the line you were named in.

props.name: handle
props.description: The token marked as a chip inside each line.

props.name: openId / defaultOpenId
props.description: Controlled or initial open row.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that opened a row.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Fires with the whole mention so the host can jump its thread.

props.name: readIds / defaultReadIds
props.description: Controlled or initial read set.

props.name: onReadIdsChange
props.description: Fires from an open, or from the header's mark-all action.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: The frozen sentence the polite region just spoke.

props.name: label
props.description: Heads the card and names the list.

props.name: markAllLabel
props.description: Copy for the header action.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Scroll ceiling for the list, in px.

usageNotes: An ol of li whose rows are real buttons with a roving tabindex: Down and Up move, Home and End jump, Enter and Space open, and Mark all read keeps its own place in the tab order.
Each row is named as one sentence carrying its state in words — "Marta Ferreira named you in #coldbrook-yard, 02:14. … New." — so nothing depends on the dimmed ink alone.
Under reduced motion nothing travels or staggers; the glow still flares briefly, because it is the answer to where you just landed.

items.title: Digest Fold
items.tagline: What you missed, folded.
items.description: What you missed, folded into one line: a count, the rooms and the hour it starts from, beside procedural author marks hashed from their names. Pressing the header unfolds the body against a ResizeObserver-measured height on glide while the chevron turns on snap and the rows fade in on a cascade, and pressing a row jumps to it, drawing a tick on flick before the row dims to opened. The header is a real disclosure, rows carry a roving tabindex, and Escape folds the card back to the header.

props.name: groups
props.description: What you missed, grouped by room, oldest first.

props.name: since
props.description: The time the digest starts from; printed and spoken.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial fold state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the header press or from Escape.

props.name: onJump
props.description: Fires with the pressed row and the room it came from.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: The frozen sentence the polite region just spoke.

props.name: title
props.description: The card's heading.

usageNotes: The header is a disclosure with aria-expanded and aria-controls named as one sentence; the folded body is hidden from assistive technology and out of the tab order rather than merely clipped.
Rows carry a roving tabindex: Down and Up move, Home and End jump, Enter and Space jump to the message, and Escape folds the card and returns focus to the header.
Under reduced motion the height swaps, nothing cascades and the tick appears rather than drawing, but every count and mark still updates.

items.title: Notify Toggle
items.tagline: All, mentions, nothing.
items.description: The three honest answers to how much of a room you want: everything, only when you are named, nothing. One knob rides the three-stop track on a shared layoutId joined on glide, while under it a wheel of descriptions slides to match — a single ResizeObserver measures all three lines, so the strip travels by the heights above the chosen one and the window joins that line's own height with nothing reserved for the longest. The bell morphs on flick, drawing and undrawing its arcs, its at-mark and its clapper rather than interpolating a path; Left and Right step without wrapping, Home and End jump, and Space selects.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial level: all, mentions or none.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that chose the level, never from an effect.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: The frozen sentence the polite region just spoke.

props.name: room
props.description: The room the setting belongs to; printed and spoken after a hash.

props.name: stops
props.description: Label and description per stop; defaults to All / Mentions / Nothing.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's visible heading.

usageNotes: A real radio group with a roving tabindex: Left and Right (or Up and Down) step without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump to all and nothing, Space and Enter select.
Each radio is named as one sentence including its description, so the description wheel stays out of the accessibility tree and a reader is never read all three.
Under reduced motion no knob travels — the checked stop draws its own pill — the wheel swaps, and the bell's marks cross-fade at full length rather than drawing.

items.title: Catchup Scroll
items.tagline: Read it all, at a pace.
items.description: A catch-up control that reads the backlog to you at a stated pace: the run animates the box's own scrollTop imperatively across the words still to be read, linearly, because a reading speed that accelerates is a lie. Beside the thread a rail joins its fill on glide and marks a tick per message boundary, both measured from the rows themselves, and messages the rail has passed dim to read. Any touch stops it — a wheel, a pointer or a key inside the box — reported from the handler that caused it; Home and End jump to the top and the floor.

props.name: messages
props.description: The backlog, oldest first: id, author, time and text.

props.name: playing / defaultPlaying
props.description: Controlled or initial run state.

props.name: onPlayingChange
props.description: Fires from the control, from an interruption, and from the finish.

props.name: onProgressChange
props.description: Fires as the rail passes each message.

props.name: onFinish
props.description: Fires once when the run reaches the floor.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: The frozen sentence the polite region just spoke.

props.name: wordsPerMinute
props.description: Reading pace; sets how long the run takes.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the region and the control.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Scroll ceiling for the thread, in px.

usageNotes: The box is a region with tabIndex 0 so it scrolls from the keyboard: Home and End jump to the top and the floor, and any key, wheel or pointer press inside it stops the run where it stands.
The rail is a real progressbar with an aria-valuetext sentence, and a polite region speaks once per settle — on start, on stop, on finish — never once per row.
Under reduced motion the catch-up still runs but in steps: the box is seated on the next message at that message's reading time, so progress happens and nothing travels.

items.title: Badge Count
items.tagline: Unread, on the icon.
items.description: An app badge that behaves like one. The tile draws a procedural mark hashed from its own name, and an arrival bumps the pill from 1.25 back to 1 on recoil while the digits roll in strips of ten and a ResizeObserver-measured width joins on glide, so gaining a place widens the badge rather than jumping it. A count that falls never bumps, past max the strips hold at the cap and a plus arrives from distances.nudge on snap, and reading everything collapses the badge on the exit ease.

props.name: app
props.description: The app's name: seeds the mark, captions the tile, and names the button.

props.name: count
props.description: Unread items. Zero collapses the badge.

props.name: max
props.description: Cap; anything above reads as 99+.

props.name: noun
props.description: Pluralised into the spoken sentences.

props.name: tone
props.description: The badge's ink.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Fires from the press; clear the count in the host.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: The frozen sentence the polite region just spoke.

usageNotes: The tile is a real button named as one properly pluralised sentence — "Coldbrook Threads, 12 unread messages." — so the badge itself stays aria-hidden and the number is never heard twice.
Enter and Space open the app; a polite region speaks one frozen sentence per change of the count.
Under reduced motion nothing bumps and nothing travels: the digits swap, the width swaps and the badge fades, but the number always updates.

items.title: Priority Ping
items.tagline: Marked urgent.
items.description: A thread whose urgent messages arrive louder and quieten when somebody says they have seen them. An urgent message settles into place on glide while a danger rail draws down its leading edge from scaleY 0 and a wash behind it breathes on a repeating tween, since a spring takes exactly two keyframes and a pulse has to come back. Acknowledging stops the wash, cools the rail to hairline, and swaps the flag's pennant for a tick on flick; the controls are one tab stop under a roving tabindex where Down and Up step, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space acknowledges without the control losing its place or its focus.

props.name: messages
props.description: The thread, oldest first: id, author, text, and the optional urgent, acknowledged and acknowledgedBy flags.

props.name: onAcknowledge
props.description: Fires from a row's control and from Enter or Space on it; set acknowledged on that message here.

props.name: onPendingChange
props.description: Fires when the number of unacknowledged urgent messages changes.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: Fires once per frozen change sentence, the same one the status region speaks.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the thread for assistive technology.

props.name: acknowledgeLabel
props.description: Copy for the row control.

props.name: heading
props.description: The strip above the thread.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: How tall the thread grows before it scrolls inside its own box.

usageNotes: One tab stop into the thread: Down and Up step between urgent rows, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter and Space acknowledge. An acknowledged control keeps its place and its focus and becomes aria-disabled rather than leaving the tab order.
Urgency is a sentence, never colour alone: an urgent bubble carries a hidden "Urgent message." and the control is named "Acknowledge the urgent message from Ines."
Under reduced motion nothing travels and nothing breathes — the rail is drawn whole and the wash holds one steady tint — but it still cools on acknowledgement, because urgency is information.

items.title: Quiet Hours
items.tagline: Silent after ten.
items.description: A nightly window on a 24-hour rail, shaded as two segments when it crosses midnight because a night past the date line is still one window. Dragging a handle moves it 1:1 with the pointer and captures only after four pixels of travel, while a settled or keyed change re-shades on glide; inside the window the bell's two sound arcs retract by pathLength on flick and it dims, and underneath the next change counts down over a draining hairline. Each handle is a real slider: Arrow keys move by step, Page Up and Page Down by an hour, Home and End jump to the ends of the day.

props.name: start / defaultStart
props.description: Minutes past midnight when quiet begins.

props.name: end / defaultEnd
props.description: Minutes past midnight when quiet ends.

props.name: onRangeChange
props.description: Fires from the setter that moved a handle, with both ends.

props.name: enabled / defaultEnabled
props.description: Whether the window applies; the switch drives it.

props.name: onEnabledChange
props.description: Fires from the switch.

props.name: nowMinutes
props.description: The host's minute of the day, 0 to 1439. The component never reads a clock.

props.name: step
props.description: Minutes per keyboard nudge and per pointer snap.

props.name: onQuietChange
props.description: Fires each time the window opens or closes around nowMinutes.

props.name: label
props.description: The strip's heading, and the switch's name.

usageNotes: Two role="slider" handles: Arrow keys move by step, Page Up and Page Down by an hour, Home and End jump to midnight and a quarter to midnight, and each speaks its value as "Quiet starts at 10:00 pm."
Nothing is scheduled in here: pass the minute of the day as nowMinutes and the countdown, the shade and the bell all derive from it.
Under reduced motion the handles and the shade repaint at once and the arcs swap without drawing, but the countdown and the draining hairline still run, because a countdown is information.

items.title: Summary Strip
items.tagline: The thread, in a line.
items.description: The gist of a long thread, sitting above it. A new summary types itself from an effect that holds while the tab is hidden, with the rest of the sentence laid out invisibly ahead of the caret so the box stays still, and the old line is wiped left to right by an animated clipPath on the exit ease rather than faded. A ResizeObserver measures the content and the strip's height joins it on glide, the refresh arrow turns one full turn per press on glide, and Enter or Space on that control refreshes while it stays aria-disabled rather than leaving the tab order.

props.name: summary
props.description: The current summary. A new value wipes the old one and types itself.

props.name: covers
props.description: How many messages this reading covers; printed and spoken, pluralised.

props.name: refreshing
props.description: The host is writing a new one; the strip sweeps and reads busy.

props.name: typeSpeed
props.description: Milliseconds per character.

props.name: onRefresh
props.description: Fires from the refresh control.

props.name: onSettle
props.description: Fires once, from an effect, when a summary finishes typing.

props.name: label
props.description: The strip's small heading.

props.name: refreshLabel
props.description: The control's spoken name.

usageNotes: The refresh control is a real button reached by Tab and pressed with Enter or Space; while the host is writing it is aria-disabled rather than removed from the order.

While a summary types the strip is aria-busy and its text is hidden from assistive technology, and a status region says the whole sentence once when it settles — never a half-written word, never one announcement per character.
Under reduced motion the summary arrives whole, the old line cross-fades instead of wiping and the sweep holds steady, because the words are the information and the typing is the flourish.

items.title: Thread Digest
items.tagline: Which threads moved.
items.description: What moved while you were away, ordered by what moved last. Each row carries a column sparkline of when its messages landed, animated by each column's y and height on glide rather than by a path, and a thread that receives something climbs the list while every row it passes trades places on the same spring through position-only layout projection. The busiest column is tinted, a thread with nothing new dims and keeps its shape, and the list is one tab stop under a roving tabindex where Down and Up step, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space opens the focused thread.

props.name: threads
props.description: The threads: id, name, optional preview, unread, a monotonic activity rank, and one count per bucket.

props.name: bucketLabels
props.description: Names for the buckets ("6 am", "7 am"), used in the row's spoken sentence.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Fires from a row's press, and from Enter or Space on it.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: Fires once per frozen change sentence, the same one the status region speaks.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the list for assistive technology.

props.name: heading
props.description: The strip above the list.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Drawn when there are no threads.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: How tall the list grows before it scrolls inside its own box.

usageNotes: One tab stop into the list: Down and Up step rows, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter and Space open the focused thread. The roving index follows the row's identity, so a row that climbs while it holds focus keeps it.
The sparkline is aria-hidden and the row's name is one whole sentence — "Coldbrook yard, six new messages, busiest around 9 am." — so the shape is never the only copy of the information.
Sort by the activity rank you raise, never by a clock; under reduced motion the re-sort lands instantly and the columns still step to their new heights.

items.title: Snooze Chip
items.tagline: Remind me later.
items.description: One notification, put off until a stated time. The chip unfolds its durations in flow on a ResizeObserver-measured height joined on glide, and picking one slides the card sixteen pixels away on the exit ease while the block collapses to the stamp's own measured height and the stamp lands on recoil with a clock whose hands turn to the wake time. The wake time is arithmetic on a minute the host passes in, never a clock read: Left and Right rove the chips, Home and End jump, Escape folds and returns focus to the chip, and choosing one moves focus to Undo.

props.name: title
props.description: Who or what the notification is from.

props.name: body
props.description: The one line of the notification.

props.name: meta
props.description: A quiet third line, such as the room it came from.

props.name: durations
props.description: The fold's stops: minutes from now, or an `at` minute of the day to wake at instead.

props.name: nowMinutes
props.description: The host's minute of the day, 0 to 1439. The component never reads a clock.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial state of the duration fold.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the chip, from Escape, and from a chosen duration.

props.name: onSnooze
props.type: (snooze: { id: string; label: string; wakeMinutes: number } | null) => void
props.description: Fires with the chosen snooze, or null from Undo.

props.name: onWake
props.description: Fires once when nowMinutes reaches the wake time.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats a minute of the day; defaults to a 12-hour clock.

props.name: snoozeLabel
props.description: Copy for the chip.

usageNotes: The chip is a disclosure with aria-expanded; inside the fold Left and Right rove the chips, Home and End jump to the ends, and Escape folds it and returns focus to the chip. Each chip is named with the time it produces, so the outcome is known before the press.

Choosing a duration moves focus to Undo, because the control that had it has just left with the card; Undo hands focus back to the chip. Whichever layer is not showing is out of the tab order and hidden from assistive technology.
Under reduced motion the two layers cross-fade in place, the block's height swaps rather than gliding and the clock's hands are drawn at the wake time without turning.

items.title: Log Tail
items.tagline: Lines as they arrive, held when you look.
items.description: A log that follows its own floor. While it tails, each arriving line is pinned into view in a layout effect and travels 8px up on glide with its level rail drawing down beside it; scroll up and the tail breaks, holding the box where you left it while an opaque strip rises off the floor on snap counting what has arrived. The strip, End, and the Follow control all run scrollTop back down, and scrolling to the floor by hand latches the tail on again.

props.name: lines
props.description: The buffer, oldest first; each line carries id, level, service, time and text. Cap it in the host — nothing here virtualises.

props.name: tailing / defaultTailing
props.description: Controlled or initial follow state.

props.name: onTailingChange
props.description: Fires from the break, the strip, the Follow control, and End.

props.name: onPendingChange
props.description: Fires when the count of lines that arrived while held changes.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: The sentence the polite region just spoke.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Scroll ceiling for the box, in px.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the log region and heads the card.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Printed while the buffer is empty.

usageNotes: The box is a role="log" with tabIndex 0: End jumps to the floor and resumes the tail, Home goes to the top and holds it, and the Follow control is a pressed-state button reachable by Tab.
The live region is polite while the tail follows and off while it is held; a second polite region speaks the held count on settle ("4 new lines below.") rather than once per arrival.
Under reduced motion lines still arrive and rails still mark the level, but nothing travels and the jump to the floor is seated in one step.
Arrivals belong to the host: pass lines from your own feed — the component never reads a clock.

items.title: Level Filter
items.tagline: Show only what matters.
items.description: Four level chips and the log lines they let through. Turn a level off and its lines leave on a fast tween while everything below travels up under layout on glide — a FLIP, because the list is moving rather than repainting — and the box's measured height glides with it; each chip's count rolls a digit at a time on snap. Where a run has been hidden a rule opens in the gap and says what is missing, its hairlines growing outward from the centre.

props.name: lines
props.description: The buffer, oldest first; each line carries id, level, service, time and text.

props.name: levels / defaultLevels
props.description: Controlled or initial set of shown levels.

props.name: onLevelsChange
props.description: Fires from a chip press with the new set, in level order.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: The sentence the polite region just spoke.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Scroll ceiling for the list box, in px.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the toolbar ("<label> levels") and the list ("<label> lines").

usageNotes: The chips are a role="toolbar" with one roving tabindex: Left and Right step without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump, Space and Enter toggle; each chip's name is a sentence ("Error, 3 lines, shown.") so the state never depends on colour.
Hidden runs are never closed over: a rule stays in the gap as its own list item, carrying a sentence that names what was removed.
Under reduced motion nothing FLIPs and no digit rolls, but the counts, the gaps and the list all still change.
The set is reported from the press that caused it, and the spoken summary is frozen from the settled set, so a controlled host is never announced ahead of its answer.

items.title: Log Expand
items.tagline: One line, opened.
items.description: One log line that opens in place. The panel unfolds in flow against a height a ResizeObserver measured from the content's own border box, joined on glide behind overflow-clip, while the chevron turns a quarter on snap. Inside, the fields are a real key-value list and the JSON is the same record printed whole; the two cross-fade with the leaving view taken out of flow, so the height is always the height of what is being read, and a secret field stays masked in both until an explicit reveal.

props.name: entry
props.description: The line and everything behind it: time, level, service, message, and its fields (a field may be marked secret).

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial disclosure state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the summary press and from Escape.

props.name: view / defaultView
props.description: Controlled or initial body view.

props.name: onViewChange
props.description: Fires from the view toggle.

props.name: onRevealChange
props.description: Fires when the masked field is shown or hidden again.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: The sentence the polite region just spoke.

usageNotes: The summary is a real disclosure (aria-expanded, aria-controls) named as one sentence; the view toggle is a radio group with a roving tabindex where Left and Right move, Home and End jump, and Space selects.
Escape closes the panel from wherever focus is — the handler sits on the wrapper, not inside the panel — and returns focus to the summary; a folded body is inert as well as aria-hidden.
Secrets are masked by default in both views and revealed only by the explicit control, which announces "Token shown." politely.
Under reduced motion the panel still opens and every field still shows, but the height swaps in one step and the views change without the fade.

items.title: Search Highlight
items.tagline: Matches, lit in order.
items.description: A search field over a log, and the log lights up under it. Every match becomes a mark whose wash sweeps in from its left edge by its own background size — never a transform, so the text is not scaled — on snap, staggered by cascade so a screenful lights inside the choreography budget; the current match is ringed and seated into view by its own offset. The counter rolls a digit at a time and shares one grid cell with the pattern error, and Enter steps forward, Shift+Enter back, Escape clears.

props.name: lines
props.description: The buffer, oldest first; matches are found in each line's text.

props.name: query / defaultQuery
props.description: Controlled or initial query.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.description: Fires from every keystroke and from the Escape clear.

props.name: regex / defaultRegex
props.description: Controlled or initial regular-expression mode.

props.name: onRegexChange
props.description: Fires from the pattern chip.

props.name: onMatchesChange
props.description: Fires when the number of matches changes.

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Fires when the cursor steps; -1 when there is nothing to step to.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: The sentence the polite region just spoke.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Scroll ceiling for the log box, in px.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the search field.

usageNotes: A real input type="search": Enter steps to the next match, Shift+Enter to the previous, Escape clears the query where focus actually is; the steppers stay in the tab order as aria-disabled when there is nothing to step to.

An unparseable regular expression marks the field aria-invalid and stops the highlighting rather than throwing; the reason and the counter share one grid cell and cross-fade, so a fast typist never sees a blank readout.
The polite region speaks on settle — once typing stops — with the count pluralised, and each step speaks "Match 3 of 12."
Under reduced motion matches still light, but the wash appears without the sweep or the stagger and stepping seats the box in one move.

items.title: Trace Waterfall
items.tagline: Spans, stacked in time.
items.description: A request drawn as the time each of its parts took. Every span is a bar on one shared axis — left is its start as a share of the trace, width is its duration — drawn in from its own left edge on glide and staggered by cascade, with every percentage rounded to three decimals before it reaches a style. Hover or focus reads a span back in a header whose two readings cross-fade in one grid cell, and collapsing a parent folds its descendants out under layout while the parent grows a quieter bar spanning what it now hides.

props.name: spans
props.description: The trace in start order; each span carries id, optional parentId, name, service, start and duration in ms, and an optional status.

props.name: collapsed / defaultCollapsed
props.description: Controlled or initial set of collapsed parent ids.

props.name: onCollapsedChange
props.description: Fires from a press and from the Left and Right keys.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires as hover or focus moves to a span, and with null when both leave.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.description: The sentence the polite region just spoke.

props.name: unit
props.description: Printed after every duration.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the tree.

usageNotes: A real role="tree" with one roving tabindex: Up and Down move between visible rows, Right opens a parent or steps into it, Left closes it or steps out, Home and End jump, Enter and Space fold.

Each row names itself as one sentence — duration, start, status, children — so a failed span says "error" rather than only turning red, and the header readout stays out of the accessibility tree because the row already carries it.
Folding never hides time: a collapsed parent draws a second, quieter bar across the extent of everything beneath it.
Under reduced motion the bars are still drawn to full width, but they appear rather than draw and nothing FLIPs.

items.title: Span Detail
items.tagline: One span, in full.
items.description: One span's own record, opened. A track draws the trace window with the span's extent laid on it at its offset, scaling from its left origin on glide, and the event ticks draw afterwards on flick in a cascade; pressing the head unfolds a ResizeObserver-measured body whose attribute rows and event list arrive from 4px away. Attributes marked secret stay masked until their own Reveal control is pressed, an errored span stamps on snap rather than recoil, and the event list is a roving-tabindex ol where Arrow keys step and Home and End jump.

props.name: span
props.description: The one span: service, operation, startMs, durationMs, status, attributes and events.

props.name: windowMs
props.description: The trace window the track represents; the extent is drawn as a share of it.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial unfolded state of the record.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the press that folded or unfolded the record.

props.name: onReveal
props.description: Fires when a masked attribute is revealed by its own control.

props.name: onEventSelect
props.description: Fires when an event row is activated by pointer or keyboard.

props.name: formatMs
props.defaultValue: ms under a second, seconds above
props.description: Renders every duration in the card, so a host changes units in one place.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the card for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The head is a real disclosure button with aria-expanded; inside the record the event rows carry a roving tabindex where Arrow Up and Down step, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space selects.
Secrets are masked by default: an attribute marked secret prints as dots until its Reveal control is pressed, and Mask puts it back.
Under reduced motion the extent bar still fills and the ticks still appear, on tweens with no stagger, and the error stamp arrives at full size as a colour wash.
Every millisecond comes from props — the card never reads a clock, so it renders the same on the server and the client.

items.title: Log Group
items.tagline: Repeated lines, folded.
items.description: Consecutive lines carrying the same level and message fold into one row whose count rolls on snap when the run grows, with a ring popping off the badge so the change reads without the row moving. Pressing a folded row unfolds it: a ResizeObserver measures the member list, the wrapper glides to that height, and the members cascade in from 4px away inside the choreography budget. The rows are a roving tabindex — Arrow Up and Down step, Home and End jump, Right unfolds and Left folds.

props.name: lines
props.description: The log in order: id, level, a printed clock string, and the message.

props.name: openIds / defaultOpenIds
props.description: Controlled or initial unfolded runs, keyed by each run's first line.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the press that folded or unfolded a run.

props.name: onGroupToggle
props.type: (id: string, open: boolean, count: number) => void
props.description: Fires with the run that changed and its length, for a host's own readout.

props.name: minRun
props.description: Repeats needed before a run folds; below it every line prints on its own.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The log is an ol of li with a roving tabindex over the folded rows: Arrow Up and Down step, Home and End jump, Right unfolds, Left folds, Enter and Space toggle.
This folds repetition rather than filtering it — every line stays in the list, and each row's name says how many times it repeated and between which two clocks.
Under reduced motion the count still rolls to its new value and the run still opens, on tweens, with no badge pop and no stagger.

items.title: Timestamp Rail
items.tagline: When each line happened.
items.description: A gutter of clocks beside a log that a switch condenses to elapsed offsets, both readings sharing one grid cell so the column never changes width and the rows never move. Where two lines sit further apart than gapMs the rail grows a dashed stem sized to that gap's share of the largest; hovering or focusing one lifts it on snap, swaps its compact reading for a spoken one, and tints the lines it spans. Pressing a gap scrolls the box to the line after it and washes that row on a three-keyframe tween, and the gaps carry a roving tabindex.

props.name: lines
props.description: The log in order: id, a printed clock, ms from the first line, level and message.

props.name: mode / defaultMode
props.description: Controlled or initial reading in the gutter.

props.name: onModeChange
props.description: Fires from the press that flipped the reading.

props.name: gapMs
props.description: Distance between two lines before the rail draws a gap marker.

props.name: onJump
props.description: Fires when a gap is activated, with the line it landed on.

props.name: onGapFocus
props.description: Fires as a gap is hovered or focused, and with null when it is released.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: The scroller's height in pixels; the log scrolls inside it, never the page.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the scrollable log for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The gaps are real buttons under a roving tabindex: Arrow Up and Down step between them, Home and End jump to the first and last, Enter and Space land on the line after the gap; the scroller itself is a tab stop so the log can be scrolled from the keyboard.
The ref exposes jumpToLongestGap() so a host control outside the rail can land on the longest wait.
Under reduced motion the stems still size themselves to their durations, the jump scrolls without smoothing, and the landing wash only fades.
Every time comes from props — the rail never reads a clock, so it renders the same on the server and the client.

items.title: Error Pin
items.tagline: Errors, pinned in the scrollbar.
items.description: A rail down the right edge of a log stands for the whole file: every error line puts a pin on it at its own share of the length, and a thumb tracks the visible slice from motion values written in the scroll handler, so scrolling never re-renders the list. A pin that arrives while you watch pops in on snap rather than recoil, because an error is not a landing to celebrate; pressing one scrolls the box to that line and washes the row on a three-keyframe tween. The pins are buttons under a roving tabindex.

props.name: lines
props.description: The log in order; every line at level "error" puts a pin on the rail.

props.name: activeId / defaultActiveId
props.description: Controlled or initial pinned error the rail treats as current.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires from the press that made a pin current.

props.name: onJump
props.description: Fires when a pin is activated, with its position among the errors.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: The scroller's height in pixels; the log scrolls inside it, never the page.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the scrollable log for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The rail is a labelled group of real buttons under a roving tabindex: Arrow Up and Down step between errors, Home and End jump to the first and last, Enter and Space land; each pin's name reads "Error 2 of 3 at 09:41:12, hold rejected. Jump to it."
The ref exposes jumpToNextError() so a host control outside the rail can advance through the errors.
A new error announces itself once, politely, at the moment the lines prop brings it in; the current row also carries aria-current.
Under reduced motion a pin fades in at full size and the jump scrolls without smoothing — the pin still appears, because an error is information.

items.title: Context Lines
items.tagline: The lines around it.
items.description: A search result that opens its neighbourhood. Pressing a matched line reveals the lines above and below: a ResizeObserver measures each side and both wrappers glide to their own heights, while the lines cascade outward from the match — nearest neighbour first, the ones above arriving from overhead and the ones below from under. A spinbutton sets how many lines each side shows, growing or trimming both wrappers on the same glide while the count rolls on snap, and the before block hangs from its bottom edge so trimming takes the far lines rather than the neighbours.

props.name: matches
props.description: The results: id, line number, text, and the surrounding before and after arrays.

props.name: openIds / defaultOpenIds
props.description: Controlled or initial ids of the opened matches.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the press that opened or folded a match.

props.name: context / defaultContext
props.description: Controlled or initial number of lines shown on each side.

props.name: onContextChange
props.description: Fires from the step that changed the count.

props.name: maxContext
props.description: The stepper's ceiling; the supplied arrays cap it further.

props.name: query
props.description: The matched term, marked inside the matched line.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the list of matches for assistive technology.

usageNotes: Each match is a disclosure button whose aria-controls names both context wrappers, and whose name reads "Line 204, …. Show 4 lines of context."; while a match is folded its wrappers are aria-hidden, so a reader never meets lines that are not on screen.
The stepper is a role="spinbutton" with two buttons either side: Arrow Up and Right add a line, Arrow Down and Left take one, Home goes to none and End to the ceiling.
Under reduced motion the wrappers change height on tweens, the lines arrive on opacity with no stagger or travel, and the count swaps in place.

items.title: Latency Histogram
items.tagline: Where the requests fall.
items.description: A distribution of response times whose bars scale up from their baselines on glide in a cascade sweep, so a new window re-shapes the same bars rather than mounting a new chart. The p50, p95 and p99 marks stand on the same axis and slide to their places on snap; pressing a percentile chip pins it, washing the plot to the mark and dropping every bar past it to the hairline. The bars are a roving-tabindex list of buttons where Left and Right step, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space latches a bucket's reading.

props.name: buckets
props.description: Ordered buckets of { from, to, count }; the last may leave `to` off to run open-ended.

props.name: pinned / defaultPinned
props.description: Controlled or initial pinned percentile.

props.name: onPinnedChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that pinned or released a percentile.

props.name: onPercentilesChange
props.description: The computed p50, p95 and p99 — a reading, so it also fires on the first commit.

props.name: onBucketChange
props.description: The bucket under pointer or focus; also fires on the first commit.

props.name: unit
props.description: Printed after every latency figure.

props.name: unitLong
props.description: The same unit spoken in full, so every accessible name is a sentence.

props.name: windowLabel
props.description: The window these buckets cover, printed in the header.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the chart and its bar list.

props.name: height
props.description: Plot height in px; the width is fluid.

usageNotes: The bars carry a roving tabindex: Left and Right step, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space latches a bucket so its reading survives the pointer leaving.
Each bar names itself as one sentence — range, count and share of the window — so the distribution is available in words, and the percentile chips are aria-pressed toggles in the normal tab order.
Under reduced motion the bars still take their heights, because a distribution is information, but on a tween with no stagger and with the marks swapping in place.
Every percentage is rounded to three decimals before it reaches a style, so the chart hydrates against the markup the server sent.

items.title: SLO Burn
items.tagline: How fast the budget goes.
items.description: An error budget drawn as the minutes it has left and the pace it is spending them at. The bar drains from the right on glide — a budget settling, never a bounce — while a pace rule slides on snap to where the budget should stand at this point in the window, and a burn-rate line carries its marker past a ticked fast mark. Above the fast rate the bar and chip turn warn and the chip pulses on a mirrored tween, and the Project switch, flipped with Enter or Space, opens the slice this rate would take by window end.

props.name: remaining
props.description: Share of the error budget left, 0 to 1.

props.name: elapsed
props.description: Share of the compliance window elapsed, 0 to 1; the pace rule stands at what is left of it.

props.name: budgetMinutes
props.description: The whole budget in minutes, so the readout names real minutes.

props.name: windowHours
props.description: Length of the compliance window, used for the time to exhaustion.

props.name: objective
props.description: The objective, printed in the header.

props.name: fastAt
props.description: Burn rate at or above which the meter reads fast.

props.name: maxRate
props.description: Top of the burn-rate line; the marker clamps there and the reading says so.

props.name: projected / defaultProjected
props.description: Controlled or initial state of the projection switch.

props.name: onProjectedChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that flipped the switch.

props.name: onBurnChange
props.description: Rate, state, minutes left, minutes projected at window end and hours to exhaustion — a state, so it also fires on the first commit.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the meter.

usageNotes: Both bars are real role="meter"s whose aria-valuetext is a sentence, and the projection control is a role="switch" reached by Tab and flipped with Enter or Space.
The state word — Ahead, On pace, Fast, Spent — is printed beside the rate, so the reading never rests on colour alone, and a polite region speaks only threshold crossings.
Every figure comes from props: the meter never reads a clock, so it renders the same on the server as after hydration.
Under reduced motion the fill still drains and the markers still take their places on tweens, and the fast-burn pulse does not run.

items.title: Heat Week
items.tagline: Every hour of the week, coloured.
items.description: Seven days by twenty-four hours, each cell carrying an hour's reading as opacity over one token — cobalt below the hot mark, warn at or above it. The cells warm in column by column, staggered by cascade across the 24 hours rather than all 168 cells, and hovering or focusing one lifts it on flick while the header reads it back in a cross-faded cell. It is a real grid: Arrow keys move in two dimensions, Home and End reach the ends of a row, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End the corners, and Enter or Space isolates a day so the other six fade.

props.name: values
props.description: One row per day, one reading per hour; a short row reads as gaps.

props.name: days
props.description: Row names in full — spoken whole, abbreviated for the rail.

props.name: hotAt
props.description: Value at or above which a cell reads warn rather than cobalt.

props.name: unit
props.description: Printed after every value.

props.name: unitLong
props.description: The same unit spoken in full, so every cell name is a sentence.

props.name: day / defaultDay
props.description: Controlled or initial isolated row index.

props.name: onDayChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that isolated or released a day.

props.name: onCellChange
props.description: The cell under pointer or focus; a reading, so it also fires on the first commit.

props.name: format
props.description: Renders every value, so a host changes units in one place.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the grid.

usageNotes: A real role="grid": each row is a role="row", its first cell a role="rowheader" that carries the isolation with aria-selected, and the rest role="gridcell". Arrow keys move in two dimensions, Home and End reach the ends of a row, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End the corners of the week, and Enter or Space isolates the focused cell's day.
Every cell names itself as one sentence — day, hour and value — so the heat is available in words and not only as colour.
The stagger runs across the 24 columns rather than all 168 cells, which keeps the sweep inside the 600ms choreography budget.
Under reduced motion the cells arrive at their intensity with no stagger and no lift, and isolation is a plain opacity change.

items.title: Percentile Lines
items.tagline: p50, p95, p99, drawn together.
items.description: Three percentiles over one window, drawn together: each line arrives by pathLength on glide, offset by cascade so they read as three strokes rather than one. The gap between neighbouring lines is the point — hovering a band shades it and thickens its two boundary lines on flick, and the spread row below names the same gap in words as roving-tabindex buttons where Left and Right step, Home and End jump, and a press latches the shading. Every path's d is set and never animated, because a hidden series re-pairs the bands.

props.name: series
props.description: Ordered low to high: id, label and one value per sample.

props.name: samples
props.description: The x labels, one per value — the chart never reads a clock.

props.name: hidden / defaultHidden
props.description: Controlled or initial ids of the hidden series.

props.name: onHiddenChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that hid or showed a series.

props.name: onBandChange
props.description: The band under pointer or focus, with its widest spread; also fires on the first commit.

props.name: unit
props.description: Printed after every figure.

props.name: unitLong
props.description: The same unit spoken in full, so every name and table cell is a sentence.

props.name: format
props.description: Renders every value in the chart and its hidden table.

props.name: height
props.description: Plot height in px; the width is fluid.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the chart and its hidden table.

usageNotes: The legend is a group of aria-pressed toggles; the spread row is a roving-tabindex group where Left and Right step, Home and End jump, focus shades a band and Enter or Space latches it.
Every number behind the picture lives in a visually hidden table with a caption, a header row of series names and one row per sample, so a screen reader can walk the whole window.
No path's d is animated: motion cannot interpolate a path whose command count changes, and hiding a series re-pairs the bands.
