Under reduced motion the lines arrive already drawn and only fade in, and the shading is a plain opacity change.

items.title: Rate Dial
items.tagline: Requests per second.
items.description: Requests per second, read as a position. The needle swings to the rate on snap around a 240° arc whose every coordinate is rounded before it reaches an attribute, and the figure under the hub rolls its digits on the same spring, keyed from the right so the units column keeps its identity. A peak marker holds the highest reading seen, moving only outward and flaring once on a three-keyframe tween when it is beaten; the dial is a focusable role="meter" whose value text is a sentence, and Reset peak drops the mark back to the current rate.

props.name: value
props.description: The current rate; the host owns it, so the dial never reads a clock.

props.name: max
props.description: Full scale of the arc.

props.name: warnAt
props.description: Value at or above which the dial reads busy and the warn band bites.

props.name: defaultPeak
props.description: Peak the dial mounts with, so a host with history shows its high at once.

props.name: onPeakChange
props.description: The held high — a reading, so it also fires on the first commit.

props.name: onZoneChange
props.description: Calm, busy or over scale; a reading, so it also fires on the first commit.

props.name: unit
props.description: Printed under the rolling figure.

props.name: unitLong
props.description: The same unit spoken in full, so the value text is a sentence.

props.name: format
props.description: Renders the figure and every spoken number.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the dial.

usageNotes: The dial is a role="meter" carrying tabIndex 0, so a keyboard reader can land on the reading itself; Reset peak is a real button, disabled while the peak equals the current rate.
The zone word — Calm, Busy, Over scale — is printed beside the figure, so the band never rests on colour alone, and a polite region speaks a new peak from a sentence frozen at the moment it moved.
Every arc coordinate is rounded to three decimals before it reaches an attribute, because trig differs in its last digits between Node and the browser.
Under reduced motion the needle takes its angle instantly and the digits swap in place, but the peak still moves and still holds — a held high is information.

items.title: Error Ratio
items.tagline: Good against bad.
items.description: Good against bad on one rail. The two runs re-proportion on glide as each window arrives and the error ratio's digits roll on snap beside them, while a window whose bad share rose washes the bad run once on a three-keyframe tween and prints the word rising. The two legend controls are a roving-tabindex group where Left and Right step, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space latches the header reading to one side.

props.name: good
props.description: Requests answered successfully in this window.

props.name: bad
props.description: Requests that failed in this window.

props.name: warnAt
props.description: Error ratio at which the level word becomes elevated.

props.name: failAt
props.description: Error ratio at which the level word becomes breaking.

props.name: windowLabel
props.description: The window's printed name; the meter never computes one from a clock.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the meter for assistive technology.

props.name: held / defaultHeld
props.description: Controlled or initial side the header reading is latched to.

props.name: onHeldChange
props.description: Fires from the press that latched or released the header reading.

props.name: onLevelChange
props.description: Reports the level from the first commit as well as every change, because a level is a state.

props.name: onRise
props.description: A settled event: fires when a window's bad share sits above the last one's.

props.name: format
props.description: Renders every request count, so a host changes units in one place.

usageNotes: The legend is a roving-tabindex group: Left and Right step without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space latches the header reading to that side or releases it.
Under reduced motion the runs still re-proportion and the ratio still updates, on a tween rather than a spring, and the rise wash is dropped in favour of the printed word rising.
Every count arrives as a prop from a seeded script, so the meter never reads a clock and renders the same on the server and the client.

items.title: Apdex Ring
items.tagline: Satisfied, tolerating, frustrated.
items.description: A satisfaction score drawn as one ring cut into three. The component cuts the latency distribution it is handed by its threshold and draws satisfied, tolerating and frustrated as three stacked arcs of the same circle whose lengths ease on glide, while the score rolls on snap in the middle. The threshold's own radiogroup lives inside the ring: Left and Right step and select without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump, and the selected pill travels behind the words on snap.

props.name: samples
props.description: The seeded distribution the ring cuts: a response time and how many requests landed there.

props.name: thresholdMs / defaultThresholdMs
props.description: Controlled or initial T; satisfied is at or under it, tolerating up to four times it.

props.name: onThresholdChange
props.description: Fires from the press or arrow key that chose a preset, never from an effect.

props.name: presets
props.description: The thresholds the radiogroup offers.

props.name: onScoreChange
props.description: Reports the score from the first commit as well as every re-cut, because a score is a state.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the ring for assistive technology and opens its spoken sentence.

props.name: formatMs
props.defaultValue: ms under a second, seconds above
props.description: Renders every threshold, so a host changes units in one place.

usageNotes: The presets are a real radiogroup: Left and Right step and select as they go without wrapping past the ends, Home and End jump to the first and last, and Space or Enter selects.
Under reduced motion the arcs still re-proportion, on a tween rather than glide, the score's digits swap in place, and the selected pill appears rather than travelling.
Every band is printed in a definition list under the ring, so the arcs' colours are never the only way to read the cut.

items.title: Sparkline Grid
items.tagline: Many metrics, small.
items.description: Many metrics, each one tile. Every line draws itself left to right on glide, staggered across the grid by cascade, and draws again whenever a new window replaces its readings; pressing a tile expands it in place, growing its line and gliding open a ResizeObserver-measured body of low, high, mean and sample count. It is a real grid: Left and Right step within a row, Up and Down keep the column, Home and End reach the row's ends, Control with them reaches the first or last tile, and Enter or Space opens.

props.name: metrics
props.description: The tiles: id, name, unit, seeded series, an optional anomaly flag and note.

props.name: columns
props.description: Tiles per row; the arrow-key geometry follows it exactly.

props.name: expandedId / defaultExpandedId
props.description: Controlled or initial expanded tile.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that expanded or folded a tile, never from an effect.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires as hover or focus moves between tiles, and with null when both leave.

props.name: format
props.description: Renders every reading in the grid, so a host changes units in one place.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the grid for assistive technology.

usageNotes: One roving tabindex across a real grid: Left and Right step within a row, Up and Down move a row keeping the column, Home and End jump to the row's ends, Control with Home or End jumps to the first or last tile, and Enter or Space expands or folds.

Under reduced motion the lines still arrive at full length with a fade and no stagger, the tile expands to its measured height on a tween, and the anomaly wash is dropped in favour of the printed word.
The expanded body is measured by a ResizeObserver on the node when it arrives, so a shut tile reserves no space at all.

items.title: Capacity Bar
items.tagline: Used, reserved, free.
items.description: Used, reserved and free share one rail, each run easing its own width on glide so a filling pool reads as the free run giving ground. A threshold rides the rail as a real slider whose handle captures the pointer only after four pixels of travel, and the moment committed capacity reaches the line the overhang past it shades warn on a tween while the printed state turns to over the line. Hovering a run names it in the header reading, which cross-fades in one cell inside the component's own box; arrow keys, Page keys and Home or End move the line and name the run it now sits in.

props.name: used
props.description: Cores in use.

props.name: reserved
props.description: Cores held for reservations but not running.

props.name: total
props.description: The pool's size; the rail is this wide.

props.name: unit
props.description: Printed after every figure, and made singular when the figure is one.

props.name: threshold / defaultThreshold
props.description: Controlled or initial line, as a share of total from 0 to 1.

props.name: onThresholdChange
props.description: Fires from the drag or key that moved the line, never from an effect.

props.name: onOverChange
props.description: A settled event: committed capacity crossing the line.

props.name: onSegmentChange
props.description: Fires as a run is hovered, or as the line enters one while the handle is held.

props.name: format
props.description: Renders every core figure, so a host changes units in one place.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the rail and its line for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The line is a real slider: Left and Down step one percent, Right and Up step one, Shift with an arrow steps five, Page Up and Page Down step ten, and Home and End go to the ends.
Under reduced motion the runs still re-size, on a tween rather than glide, the handle jumps to its place with no spring, and the overhang's shade cross-fades rather than growing.
Every run is printed in a definition list under the rail, so the hover tint never carries a reading on its own.

items.title: Anomaly Band
items.tagline: What normal looks like.
items.description: A metric line with normal drawn behind it: the band is the mean plus and minus sigma standard deviations of the readings handed in, and it glides to new bounds whenever the window or the width changes, while the line draws itself left to right on glide. Readings outside the band pop on snap and ring out on a tween staggered by cascade, and a selected outlier draws its whisker from the band's edge to the point. Every reading is also a row in a scroller with a roving tabindex where the arrows step, Home and End jump, Enter or Space selects and Escape clears.

props.name: series
props.description: The window, oldest first: an id, the printed clock and the value.

props.name: sigma
props.description: Half-width of the normal band, in standard deviations.

props.name: unit
props.description: Printed after every value.

props.name: selectedId / defaultSelectedId
props.description: Controlled or initial selected reading, shared by the chart and the list.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that selected or cleared a reading, never from an effect.

props.name: onOutliersChange
props.description: Reports the count from the first commit as well as every window, because a count is a state.

props.name: format
props.description: Renders every value in the chart and the list.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the chart and the list for assistive technology.

usageNotes: The readings carry a roving tabindex: Arrow Up and Left step back, Arrow Down and Right step on, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space selects and Escape clears the selection.

Under reduced motion the band still moves to its bounds and the line still reaches full length, on a tween rather than glide, the outlier dots arrive with a fade and no stagger, and the ring pulse does not play.
Every clock comes from props, so the chart never reads one; the mean, the band and every deviation are rounded before they reach an attribute.

items.title: Pipeline Rail
items.tagline: Stage by stage.
items.description: A build's stages on one rail, filling in the order they ran: a landed stage's fill scales from its own left origin on glide while the segments arrive in a cascade, and the stage in flight washes its whole segment and pulses between two opacities on a mirrored tween. A failed stage stops the rail, dims every stage after it, and unfolds a ResizeObserver-measured strip on glide whose failure sentence and rerun control rise in on snap. The segments are a roving-tabindex list where Arrow keys step, Home and End jump, and selection moves with focus.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root group element.

props.name: stages
props.description: The rail, in run order: id, name, status, seconds, an optional progress share and an optional failure note.

props.name: selected / defaultSelected
props.description: Controlled or initial selected stage id; without one the rail follows the stage in flight until a stage is chosen.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that moved the selection.

props.name: onRerun
props.description: Fires from the press on the rerun control, with the stage it restarts; without it the failure strip shows no control.

props.name: onRailChange
props.description: The whole reading — phase, stage, index, passed count and total seconds — reported from the first commit as well, because it is a state.

props.name: formatSeconds
props.description: Renders every duration on the rail.

props.name: rerunLabel
props.description: Verb on the rerun control, before the stage name.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the rail for assistive technology and prints above it.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: The segments carry a roving tabindex: Arrow Left and Up step back, Arrow Right and Down step on, Home and End jump, and each button names itself as one sentence with its position, status and time.

A phase change is announced once through a polite live region, and a failure reads back the host's note; the rerun control hands focus to that stage's segment before the strip leaves, so the keyboard is never dropped on the page.
Under reduced motion the fills still fill — how far a build got is information — on tweens, with no stagger and no running pulse.
Every second comes from props, so the rail never reads a clock; pass progress only for a stage that can actually measure it, and a running stage without one washes its whole segment instead.

items.title: Rollout Wave
items.tagline: Ten percent, then more.
items.description: A release reaching a fleet one wave at a time: the track carries the share of machines on the new build and scales from its left origin on glide, with a hairline tick at each wave's boundary so the plan shows before it happens. Under it every machine is a dot, and a landing wave lights its own dots in a cascade on snap while a rollback runs the same dots dark in reverse order, because a rollback is the wave run backwards. Holding stops the track where it stands and draws a rule at the current edge; Hold is a real switch and Roll back a plain button reached with Tab.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root element.

props.name: waves
props.description: Cumulative shares of the fleet each wave reaches, in order.

props.name: hosts
props.description: Machines in the fleet; the grid draws one dot each.

props.name: wave / defaultWave
props.description: Controlled or initial index of the last landed wave; -1 means the fleet is still on the previous build.

props.name: onWaveChange
props.description: Fires from the setter behind the roll-back press.

props.name: paused / defaultPaused
props.description: Controlled or initial held state.

props.name: onPausedChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that held or resumed the rollout.

props.name: onRolloutChange
props.description: The whole reading — wave, share, machines and phase — reported from the first commit as well, because it is a state.

props.name: version
props.description: The build being rolled out; printed in the header and spoken.

props.name: hostName
props.description: Names each machine for its dot.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the rollout and labels the meter.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: The track is a role="meter" whose aria-valuetext is a sentence, each dot is a list item naming its own machine and build, and Hold is a role="switch" toggled with Space or Enter; a wave landing, a hold and a rollback are each announced once through a polite live region.
The wave index comes from props, so the host's own timer drives the advance and the component never reads a clock; pause that timer while paused is true and when the tab is hidden.
Under reduced motion the track still fills and the dots still light — how far a release has reached is information — on tweens, with no scale and no stagger.
Roll back never bounces on arrival and nothing pulses while the rollout is held, because neither is progress.

items.title: Deploy Diff
items.tagline: What this deploy changes.
items.description: The card you read before you ship: the head carries the route, the release and a commit count whose digits roll on snap in a fixed-width column, and pressing it unfolds a ResizeObserver-measured body on glide where the service chips and commits cascade in from 4px away. The deploy control is a slide track whose knob is dragged, with the pointer captured only after 4px of travel, or driven from the keyboard as a real slider; only a full sweep fires the deploy, and a short one springs home on snap. The status comes from the host, so the strip that replaces the track arrives only when the parent answers, and takes focus after this card's own confirm.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root group element.

props.name: release
props.description: The build being deployed; printed in the head.

props.name: from
props.description: The environment this deploy runs from.

props.name: to
props.description: The environment this deploy runs to; named in every status sentence.

props.name: commits
props.description: Newest first, each with a short hash, subject and author; the count in the head rolls.

props.name: services
props.description: The changed services, one chip each with lines added and removed.

props.name: status
props.description: Comes from the host — the card never advances it on its own.

props.name: blockedNote
props.description: Why the deploy is held; printed and spoken when the status is blocked.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial unfolded state of the body.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that folded or unfolded the body.

props.name: onDeploy
props.description: Fires once, from the gesture that carried the knob to the end.

props.name: onArmChange
props.description: How far the knob has travelled, 0–1 — a reading, so it also fires on the first commit.

props.name: slideLabel
props.description: Names the slide control and prints on its track.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the card for assistive technology.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: The head is a disclosure button with aria-expanded; the knob is a role="slider" where Arrow keys move it a tenth, Page Up and Page Down a quarter, Home sends it back and End confirms — only a full sweep fires onDeploy, and a press on the bare track never moves it.

Set status to deploying from onDeploy and to deployed or blocked when the work really lands: the card never claims a deploy happened, and each status change is announced once through a polite live region.
Under reduced motion the knob still tracks the pointer and the keys but returns home instantly, the digits swap in place, and the rows fade in with no travel or stagger.
The body's height is measured, never reserved, so a folded card holds no room for its commits and a list that grows while open re-measures on its own.

items.title: Canary Split
items.tagline: A slice of traffic, watched.
items.description: How much traffic the new build is taking, and what it is doing with it: the canary holds the left of a split bar whose boundary is a real slider, dragged with the pointer after 4px of travel or driven with the arrow keys, and both shares settle on glide. Under the bar the baseline's error rate and the canary's share one fixed viewBox, and the canary's line draws itself as a clip rect sweeps across the box on a tween, so the stroke keeps an even width to its last sample. When the host's verdict settles, Promote and Abort slide in from 8px away on snap into a ResizeObserver-measured region, and nothing is announced until the host answers.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root group element.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial share of traffic on the canary, in whole percent.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the setter behind the drag or key.

props.name: max
props.description: The most traffic the canary may take.

props.name: baseline
props.description: The current build's line, drawn quiet: a label, error-rate samples oldest first, and the rate now.

props.name: canary
props.description: The new build's line, drawn live in the verdict's colour.

props.name: verdict
props.description: Comes from the host; decides which controls are in.

props.name: note
props.description: One sentence explaining the verdict; printed and spoken.

props.name: onPromote
props.description: Fires from the press on Promote.

props.name: onAbort
props.description: Fires from the press on Abort.

props.name: onSplitChange
props.description: The whole reading — canary share, baseline share and verdict — reported from the first commit as well, because it is a state.

props.name: formatRate
props.defaultValue: two decimals and a percent sign
props.description: Renders both error rates.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the control for assistive technology and prints above it.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: The boundary is a role="slider" whose value text names both shares: Arrow keys move it one percent, Page Up and Page Down ten, Home drops the canary to zero and End takes it to max; a press on the bar jumps there, while a press on the boundary waits for travel.

Promote and Abort only fire callbacks: set the verdict from the host once the change has really happened, and the card speaks the new verdict once through a polite live region, with focus handed to the decision region rather than dropped on the page.
Under reduced motion both lines are painted whole, the shares change without springing, and the controls fade in where they will stand.
The plot is a role="img" with a sentence naming both rates and the verdict, so the colour of the canary's line never carries the reading on its own.

items.title: Build Log
items.tagline: The build, as it runs.
items.description: A build read the way an engineer reads one: step headers that fold, with the step in flight opening itself and tailing, so new lines arrive at the bottom from 4px away on glide while the oldest leave the tail window and the body holds one steady, ResizeObserver-measured height. A step that finishes folds back to its header unless the reader has pressed one, because a reader's choice outranks the script. When the build settles the summary stamps its duration: a pass lands from 1.2× on recoil, and a failure arrives on snap with no bounce at all.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root group element.

props.name: steps
props.description: The build, in order: id, name, status, seconds and every line the step has printed, oldest first.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial set of open step ids; without one the log follows the step in flight.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that folded or unfolded a step.

props.name: onBuildChange
props.description: The whole reading — phase, step, index, passed count and total seconds — reported from the first commit as well, because it is a state.

props.name: tailLines
props.description: How many lines a running step shows.

props.name: totalSeconds
props.description: What the summary stamps.

props.name: formatSeconds
props.description: Renders every duration.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the log for assistive technology and prints above it.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: Every header is a disclosure button with aria-expanded in the tab order: Arrow Up and Down move between headers, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space folds or unfolds.

The polite live region speaks settled steps and the final verdict only, with the last error line read back on a failure; the tail itself is never announced, because several lines a second would drown a reader.
Under reduced motion the lines still arrive and the heights still change, on tweens, the running dot does not pulse, and the summary appears at full size.
Every duration comes from props, so the log never reads a clock; a warn or error line prints its level as a word, and wide lines scroll inside their own box rather than widening the card.

items.title: Env Switch
items.tagline: Staging, then production.
items.description: Where the next command lands: the environments share one rail, and the knob travels between them on glide under a useId-prefixed layoutId, while the head washes as the stop changes — a tinted layer cross-fading on a tween, quiet for the first stop, cobalt between, warn for a guarded one. A guarded stop never commits on the first press; it arms, and a confirm row unfolds in flow beneath the rail on glide to a ResizeObserver-measured height, its button focused as it arrives. The stops are a radio group where Arrow keys move and commit unguarded stops, and Escape or Cancel disarms and hands focus back.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root element.

props.name: stops
props.description: The environments, left to right: id, a short name, the host it points at, and an optional guarded flag.

props.name: service
props.description: What is being pointed somewhere; printed in the head.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial committed stop id.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that committed a stop.

props.name: onArmedChange
props.description: The armed guarded stop, or null — a state, so it also fires on mount.

props.name: armLabel
props.description: Copy on the confirm control.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the rail for assistive technology.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: The rail is a role="radiogroup" with a roving tabindex: Arrow keys step and commit an unguarded stop as they land, Home and End jump, and arrowing onto a guarded stop only moves focus — Enter or Space arms it, and Escape or Cancel disarms and returns focus to that stop.

Mark production-like stops guarded so they arm a confirm instead of committing on the first press; a value committed from outside clears any pending confirm, and every arm, confirm and cancel is announced through a polite live region.

Under reduced motion the knob does not travel — the selected fill fades in where it belongs — while the head wash and the host line still swap, because which environment you are pointed at is information.
The confirm row sits in flow inside the component's own box rather than as an overlay, so it never escapes a clipped or scrolled container.

items.title: Release Notes
items.tagline: Written as it ships.
items.description: The note a release writes about itself while it is still being cut: commits arrive as props and the card groups them into added, changed, fixed and removed, each group with a count that cross-fades in one cell. A landing line arrives from 4px away on glide, staggered inside its group by cascade, while the lines already there travel under layout on the same spring, so a new entry pushing the rest down reads as a shift rather than a bounce. Pressing a line swaps it for an input in the same cell, focused as it arrives; Enter or blur commits, Escape reverts, and an edited line keeps a quiet edited mark.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root group element.

props.name: commits
props.description: The landed commits, in the order they landed: id, kind, the line as written, and an optional scope.

props.name: version
props.description: The release being written.

props.name: service
props.description: What the release is of; printed before the version.

props.name: dateLabel
props.description: The release date as a string — the card never reads a clock.

props.name: edits / defaultEdits
props.description: Controlled or initial per-commit text overrides, keyed by commit id.

props.name: onEditsChange
props.description: Fires from the setter that committed an edit.

props.name: onEntryCommit
props.description: Fires once per committed line, with the text it now reads.

props.name: onEditingChange
props.description: Which line is open for editing — a state, so it also fires on mount.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the card for assistive technology.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: The lines read as one list with a roving tabindex across every group: Arrow Up and Down step, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space opens the line for editing; in the field Enter commits, Escape reverts, and focus returns to the line's button either way, while a blur commits without pulling focus back.
An edit overrides the commit's text without losing it: editing a line back to the original drops its override, and landings and edits share one polite live region where the newest sentence wins.
Under reduced motion entries appear with opacity only, layout travel is off, and the counts still change — what the release contains is information.
Commits land from the host in the order they landed; the card groups them itself, so feed it the raw list rather than pre-sorted groups.

items.title: Health Check
items.tagline: Every check, ticked.
items.description: The list a deploy has to get through before anyone believes it: a running probe turns its ring at a constant rate, because a spring would imply it is nearly done, a pass stamps on snap from 1.06 and draws its tick on flick, and a failure stamps its cross on snap and unfolds its own detail to a ResizeObserver-measured height on glide. Under the head a rule fills on glide to the share of checks that have settled, and the counts beside it cross-fade in one cell so a fast sequence never blanks the number. The checks are a roving-tabindex list where Arrow Up and Down step, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space folds a row.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root group element.

props.name: checks
props.description: The checks, in run order: id, probe name, target, status, and once settled the latency, response and an optional detail line.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial set of expanded check ids.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that folded or unfolded a check.

props.name: onSummaryChange
props.description: The whole reading — passed, failed, running, waiting, settled and total — reported from the first commit as well, because it is a state.

props.name: onCheckSelect
props.description: Fires when a row is activated by pointer or keyboard.

props.name: formatMs
props.defaultValue: ms under a second, seconds to two decimals above
props.description: Renders every latency, so a host changes units in one place.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the list for assistive technology.

props.name: className

usageNotes: Each row is a disclosure button with aria-expanded that names itself as one sentence — probe, target and how it went — under a roving tabindex: Arrow Up and Down step, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space folds or unfolds.

An uncontrolled list opens a check the moment it settles to fail, because a failed check must not stay shut; a controlled host keeps its own set and should open the failed id itself from onOpenChange or its own state.
A failure and the final tally are announced once through a polite live region, and the settled rule is a role="meter" whose value text is a sentence.
Under reduced motion the ring holds still while the row still prints running, and ticks and crosses appear at full size, because a settled check is information.

items.title: Rollback Arc
items.tagline: Back to the last good one.
items.description: Every version a service has worn, laid on one static arc with the newest at the frontier and each node's coordinates rounded before they reach an attribute. The deployed marker rides the curve rather than cutting the chord: one scalar motion value carries its position between version indices and useTransform derives cx and cy from it, so a rollback across three versions travels the arc on glide. Choosing an earlier node moves a hollow caret to it on snap and unfolds a roll-back row at a ResizeObserver-measured height, and only when the marker has settled does the version become current and the sentence get spoken.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root group element.

props.name: versions
props.description: Oldest first, frontier last: id, label, a good, bad or unknown status, and an optional note.

props.name: service
props.description: Whose versions these are; printed in the head.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial deployed version id.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires when a rollback settles, from the setter that committed it.

props.name: onChosenChange
props.description: The caret's version — a state, so it also fires on the first commit.

props.name: onRollbackStart
props.description: Fires from the press that started the travel.

props.name: rollbackLabel
props.description: Copy on the confirm control; the default names the direction.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the arc for assistive technology.

props.name: className

usageNotes: The nodes are a role="listbox" of options under a roving tabindex: Arrow Left and Down step toward older versions, Arrow Right and Up toward the frontier, Home and End jump, Enter or Space chooses, and Escape cancels a pending rollback and returns focus to the node.

The confirm button is focused as its row arrives and uses aria-disabled while the marker travels, so it never drops the keyboard mid-press; onValueChange fires only once the marker has settled, so drive the real rollback from onRollbackStart and treat onValueChange as done.
Under reduced motion the marker does not travel — it jumps and the arrival is spoken at once — because where the service now stands is information.
Each version carries its verdict as a word as well as a colour, in the node's own label and in the deployed and chosen readout under the arc.

items.title: Queue Depth
items.tagline: Waiting to deploy.
items.description: What is waiting to go out, in the order it will go: the head carries a rule that drains on glide to its share of the seconds left, and a Hold switch stops it, because a queue you cannot stop is not a queue. Pressing a row promotes it one place and the two neighbours exchange under layout on glide, a FLIP rather than a re-render; two adjacent rows for the same service can be merged, the lower leaving on a fast exit while the upper takes its changes and its count cross-fades in one grid cell. Depth reads as a count and a total wait in the head, and every row is a real button under a roving tabindex whose name says where it sits and where pressing would put it.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root group element.

props.name: deploys
props.description: The queue as the host knows it: id, service, change, author and seconds waited so far.

props.name: headSeconds
props.description: Seconds left on the head; the rule drains to its share of the total.

props.name: headTotalSeconds
props.description: What the head's countdown started from.

props.name: held / defaultHeld
props.description: Controlled or initial hold on the head of the queue.

props.name: onHeldChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that flipped the Hold switch.

props.name: onQueueChange
props.description: The settled order — a state, so it also fires on the first commit.

props.name: onPromote
props.description: Fires from the press that moved a row up one place.

props.name: onMerge
props.description: Fires when a row is folded into the one above it.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the queue for assistive technology.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: The rows carry a roving tabindex: Arrow Up and Down step, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space promotes the focused row one place; the head uses aria-disabled rather than disabled so the keyboard is never locked out of the list, Hold is a role="switch", and each promotion, merge and hold is announced through a polite live region.

The order and the merges are the queue's own state, reconciled against deploys during render: ids that leave the prop drop out of both and new ids join the back, so the host ships the head by removing it — along with anything merged into it — and reads the order back from onQueueChange.
The countdown comes from headSeconds, so the queue never reads a clock; stop the host's timer while held is true.
Under reduced motion nothing FLIPs and a promotion is an instant exchange, while the rule still drains and the counts still change, because how much is waiting is information.

items.title: Underline Peek
items.tagline: The underline opens into the page.
items.description: A link whose underline opens into its preview: after a short rest the line drops away from the word as a ribbon its exact width on snap, then spreads into a card that hangs from a tab under the word, one outline rebuilt each frame with concave fillets where tab and card meet. While open, the card slides along beneath the link toward the pointer on a lagging glide (drift when soft), and it folds back into the line on exit tweens when the pointer leaves, focus moves on or Escape is pressed. Focus opens it after the same delay and the preview is the link's description; on touch the first tap shows the preview and the second follows the link.

props.name: href
props.description: Where the link goes.

props.name: children
props.description: The link text.

props.name: preview
props.description: The card's content. Phrasing content only (spans styled as blocks), since the link usually sits inside a paragraph.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds the pointer or keyboard focus must rest on the link before the preview drops.

props.name: follow
props.description: The open card slides along beneath the link toward the pointer, on a lag; off, it sits centred under the word.

props.name: width
props.description: Card width in px, capped to the boundary.

props.name: stiffness
props.description: Firm drops on snap and follows on glide; soft drops on glide and follows on drift, a longer lag.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled / uncontrolled open state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the hover, focus, tap or key that opened or closed the preview.

props.name: boundary
props.description: The box the card must stay inside; it opens below the word, or above when only that side has room.

props.name: target
props.description: Passed to the anchor.

props.name: rel
props.description: Passed to the anchor.

props.name: onClick
props.description: The link's click, after the touch first-tap guard.

props.name: sound
props.description: A soft swish as it unfurls and a paper fold as it closes, panned to the link.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The preview never opens; the link still works.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the link itself.

usageNotes: Keyboard: focusing the link opens the preview after `delay`; Escape folds it and is marked handled, so a dialog around it stays open; Enter follows the link. The preview is the link's accessible description.
Touch: the first tap opens the preview instead of navigating, the second tap follows the link, and a tap anywhere else folds it.
Under reduced motion the finished card cross-fades in place: no drop, no spread, no sliding with the pointer.
Pass the surrounding text block as `boundary` so the card never leaves it; the card is clamped to cover the whole word, so the tab always lands on it.

items.title: Edge Peek
items.tagline: It leans out as you come near.
items.description: A side panel tucked into the edge of a surface whose handle leans out as the pointer comes near: distance from the edge is mapped continuously to a lean and sprung on drift (soft) or snap (firm), and past the handle's own width the lean pulls the panel's edge out behind it. A press slides the panel open on glide or snap; the handle can also be dragged 1:1, rubber-bands at both ends and commits by projection with its release velocity, while a plain close accelerates home on an exit tween. The handle is a real disclosure button: keyboard focus leans it out as a near pointer does, Enter or Space opens it, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the handle.

props.name: label
props.description: The panel's name: the handle's and the panel's accessible name, and the panel's heading.

props.name: panel
props.description: What the panel holds.

props.name: children
props.description: The surface the panel is tucked into.

props.name: reach
props.description: How far from the edge, in px, the handle starts to notice the pointer.

props.name: lean
props.description: How far the handle leans out at its closest, in px; past the handle's width it pulls the panel's edge out too.

props.name: side
props.description: Which edge the panel lives on.

props.name: pull
props.description: Soft leans on drift and opens on glide; firm leans and opens on snap.

props.name: panelWidth
props.description: Panel width in px, capped to the surface width less 56.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled / uncontrolled open state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the press, drag, key or tint press that changed it.

props.name: sound
props.description: A hum that tracks the lean while the pointer is within reach, a whoosh as it opens and a clack as it lands home.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The handle neither leans nor opens.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface frame; the host sizes it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab to the handle leans it out; Enter or Space opens the panel; Tab moves into it; Escape closes it from anywhere inside and returns focus to the handle. The panel is inert while closed.
Touch: a first tap near the edge, or on the handle's sliver, leans the handle out; the second tap opens. Dragging the handle pulls the panel directly.
Under reduced motion nothing travels: the handle sits fully out and proximity only brightens it, and the panel cross-fades in and out in place.
Size the surface with `className` (for example `h-52 w-full`); the handle and panel are clipped to it.

items.title: Cross Grid
items.tagline: The row and the column meet where you point.
items.description: A data table with a crosshair: the pointed cell lights a band along its row and a band down its column, and moving from cell to cell slides both on a spring at the house snap ratio (stiffness is a prop; its default is snap itself) rather than jumping. With followLabels, copies of the column header and the row label detach from their home and travel to sit just above and just left of the cell, so a far corner reads without tracing; appear and disappear are opacity tweens. It is a real grid: one cell is the tab stop, arrow keys, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End and PageUp/PageDown move focus, and focus drives the same crosshair, labels and tick.

props.name: label
props.description: The table's accessible name.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column headers, in order.

props.name: rows
props.type: { id: string; label: string; values: number[] }[]
props.description: Row labels and one value per column, in column order.

props.name: corner
props.description: Text for the top-left header cell, over the row labels.

props.name: format
props.description: How a value is printed.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height (28 or 36px) and type size.

props.name: followLabels
props.description: Copies of the column header and row label travel to sit beside the pointed cell.

props.name: highlight
props.description: Uniform bands, or bands that glow brightest where they cross.

props.name: stiffness
props.description: Spring stiffness for the crosshair and the travelling labels, at the house snap damping ratio.

props.name: active / defaultActive
props.description: Controlled / uncontrolled crosshair cell, by row and column id.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.type: (cell: { row: string; column: string } | null) => void
props.description: Fires from the pointer, tap or key that moved or cleared the crosshair.

props.name: sound
props.description: A tick per cell, climbing a pentatonic step per column and panned by the column's place.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the table's frame.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab reaches one cell; arrow keys move, Home/End go to the row's ends, Ctrl+Home/End to the first and last cells, PageUp/PageDown to the column's ends. Focus drives the crosshair; leaving the grid clears it.
Touch: a tap puts the crosshair on a cell, another tap moves it, and a tap outside the table clears it.
Under reduced motion nothing slides: the crosshair and the travelling labels appear at the cell and cross-fade.
Keep ids stable: the crosshair, focus and the label chips are keyed by row and column id.

items.title: Overflow Glide
items.tagline: The rest of the line, when you ask.
items.description: A line cut to its box that, pointed at or tabbed to, glides left at reading speed until its last character reaches the edge, holds there, and eases home on the glide spring, which takes the pan's velocity, so a line let go mid-read slows, turns and returns. Speed is words per second, a word being five characters, and the ellipsis dissolves within its own width of travel while masked edges follow what is hidden on each side. It answers to the hover and keyboard focus of the link, button or row around it; on touch the first tap reads and the second acts.

props.name: children
props.description: The line. Cut to its box at rest; the rest glides into view when asked for.

props.name: speed
props.description: Reading pace in words per second, where a word is five characters, so a name with no spaces reads at the same pace as a sentence.

props.name: pause
props.description: Seconds held at the end of the line before it eases home.

props.name: fade
props.description: Soft ramps at the cut edges, following how much text is hidden on each side, instead of hard edges.

props.name: loop
props.description: Keep reading, again and again, while the line is pointed at or focused.

props.name: active
props.description: Drive the glide from outside. Leave undefined and the line follows the hover and keyboard focus of the nearest link, button, option, tab, menu item, row or label around it, or its own.

props.name: onPhaseChange
props.description: Reports each phase of the glide as it begins.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a soft swish as a glide starts. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on; a hover-born swish also waits for the page's first press.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: Keyboard: tabbing to the host (a row button, a link) starts the glide on focus-visible and tabbing away sends it home. A cut line with no interactive host is itself a tab stop; a line that fits is never one, and never glides.

The full text is always in the DOM and the ellipsis is aria-hidden, so assistive technology reads the whole name through the host; the glide is for eyes. On touch, the first tap on a cut line is stopped before the host's handler and reads it; the second tap acts.
Under reduced motion the line does not travel: it pages through with fades, one window less 15% at a time, holding each page for its reading time at the same words per second, then fades home.
The window is masked, never covered, so the line sits on any background, a hovered row included.

items.title: Try On
items.tagline: Hover to try it; click to keep.
items.description: A picker whose options preview on a sample the moment you point at them: the look wipes over the sample from the swatch's own side, as a straight edge sweeping away from it or a circle grown from it, on the enter curve, and draws back into its swatch on the exit curve when you move off. Click and it stays: a stamp lands on the sample on the recoil spring, the sample dips under it on a flick and snaps back, and the kept ring slides over on the snap spring. The swatches are a listbox: arrow keys move focus and focus previews, Enter or Space keeps, Escape puts the tried look back.

props.name: options
props.type: { value: string; label: string; color: string }[]
props.description: What can be tried on. color is any CSS colour; text laid on it uses var(--background).

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial kept option.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the click, key or tap that kept a new option.

props.name: onPreviewChange
props.description: The option being tried on, as it changes; null when the sample is back to the kept one. For previewing the choice somewhere else as well.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the list of swatches and heads the caption.

props.name: sampleText
props.description: The card's title, the button's label, the badge's text.

props.name: renderSample
props.description: Draw your own sample for an option instead of the built-in ones.

props.name: wipe
props.description: How a preview arrives: a straight edge from the swatch's side, or a circle grown from the swatch.

props.name: speed
props.description: Wipe speed as a multiple of the house pace, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: sample
props.description: What the options are tried on.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a swish as each preview wipes in (a softer one as it draws back) and a click as a keep lands. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every swatch and dims the picker; the kept look stays.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the swatches are a role="listbox" with roving focus. Arrow keys move focus (wrapping) and Home/End jump; focus previews, Enter or Space keeps through the button's own click, Escape puts a tried look back (and is left alone when nothing is being tried), and leaving the list reverts and returns the tab stop to the kept swatch.
On touch the first tap tries an option on and holds it, a second tap on the same swatch keeps it, and a press anywhere else puts the kept look back.

Controlled use reports the keep from the gesture and waits for the host: the stamp and the new resting state arrive with the new value, so a refused change never stamps. A value the host sets itself wipes in from its own swatch.
Under reduced motion there is no travelling edge and no bounce: previews cross-fade in and out, the stamp fades without scaling, the sample does not dip, and the kept ring moves at once.

items.title: Eyedropper
items.tagline: Point at a colour; it reads it.
items.description: A loupe over a picture drawn in code that shows the pixels under the pointer as a magnified grid, the one being read framed at its centre and its value on a tag pinned to the loupe; the loupe follows the pointer 1:1 and pips as the colour changes, pitched by lightness. Click and the colour drops out of the loupe onto a swatch shelf: the droplet falls on the exit curve while the shelf glides open a slot, and the swatch lands on the recoil spring. Arrow keys move the loupe one pixel (Shift, ten) and Enter picks.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial shelf of picked colours, newest first, as #rrggbb.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the pick that changed the shelf, with the new shelf. Picking a colour already on it moves it to the front.

props.name: max
props.description: How many colours the shelf keeps; the oldest drops off.

props.name: label
props.description: The picture's accessible name.

props.name: zoom
props.description: How many times larger a pixel is in the loupe, 4 to 16.

props.name: grid
props.description: Lines between the magnified pixels.

props.name: loupe
props.description: The loupe's side in px, 80 to 160.

props.name: format
props.description: How a colour is written: on the tag, the shelf, copies and announcements.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a pip for each new pixel, pitched by lightness, and a drop for each pick. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on; pointer pips also wait for the page's first press.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Stops sampling and picking and dims the eyedropper.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the picture is a button. Arrow keys move the loupe one pixel (Shift moves ten) without scrolling the page, and Enter or Space picks through the button's own click. A polite live region names each reading once the keys settle ("muted violet, #583C71, at 76, 122.") and each pick and copy; each shelf swatch is a button that copies its value.

On touch, a tap places the loupe and reads, dragging the loupe moves it by the finger's travel so the finger never hides the pixel, and a tap on the loupe picks. The picture itself still scrolls the page.

The picture is painted once per size, one image pixel per CSS pixel, with the device pixel ratio capped at 2, only while it is on screen and the page is visible, and nothing loops. Its colours are its own, the same in light and dark; everything themed (frame, grid, reticle, tag) is DOM with tokens.
Under reduced motion the loupe still follows the pointer, which is direct manipulation, but the drop does not fly: the swatch fades into its slot and the shelf reorders without gliding.

items.title: Gel Switch
items.tagline: A droplet that crosses.
items.description: A switch whose knob is a drop of gel. Pressed, the droplet reaches toward its new side while the rest holds back, a neck forms and pinches, and the tail lets go and catches up; it lands with a jiggle and the track fills with liquid behind it. It can be dragged 1:1, rubber-bands past either end, and a thrown release commits to the side it was heading for.

props.name: checked / defaultChecked
props.description: Controlled or initial on/off state.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Fires from the press, key or drag that changed it, with the new state.

props.name: label
props.description: What the switch controls: its accessible name, and shown beside it unless hideLabel.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive technology only.

props.name: viscosity
props.description: How thick the gel is, 0 to 1: runny gel is quick and splashy, thick gel slow and composed.

props.name: stretch
props.description: How far the droplet reaches toward its new side before the rest of it follows, 0 to 1.

props.name: wobble
props.description: How much the droplet jiggles when it lands, 0 to 1.

props.name: fill
props.description: Fill the track with liquid behind the droplet while on.

props.name: size
props.description: The switch's size; the droplet's sounds pitch with it.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the droplet's synthesised sounds. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the switch and dims its label.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: It is a real role="switch" button labelled by its label: Space and Enter toggle it through the same path as a tap, so the droplet and the sound match whichever way it was pressed.

Controlled use reports the change from the press and then waits for the host: if the host takes the new value the droplet crosses, and if it refuses the droplet settles back, so the switch never shows a state the app does not hold.
The droplet is two circles and the metaball bridge between them, rebuilt each frame from two springs — no blur filter — so its edge stays crisp at every size and in both themes.
Under reduced motion the droplet moves in one piece on a short tween with no neck and no jiggle, and the colour still changes, because on and off are information.

items.title: Conjure Button
items.tagline: The words come apart, then come back finished.
items.description: A generate button whose own label is the material. Pressed, its letters lift off one after another and become glyph particles orbiting inside the pill on a glide spring while a band of light scans it; when the host's status says done, every particle condenses onto a letter of the new label on the same spring and a spark flares from the icon, and when it says error the orbit scatters and the pill shakes once on a tween. It is a native button: Space and Enter press it, its name is the current label, and it stays busy and focusable while the host works.

props.name: status / defaultStatus
props.description: The run's state, owned by the host (controlled), or its initial state when uncontrolled. The button never decides it is finished.

props.name: onStatusChange
props.description: Reports "working" from the press; uncontrolled, also "done" or "error" when the promise from onConjure settles.

props.name: onConjure
props.description: The work. Uncontrolled, a returned promise settles the run (resolve for done, reject for error); a plain return means the work is already done.

props.name: label
props.description: The label at rest, before a run, and the button's accessible name then.

props.name: workingLabel
props.description: The accessible name and spoken status while the host works.

props.name: doneLabel
props.description: The finished label the particles condense into.

props.name: errorLabel
props.description: The label after a failed run.

props.name: particles
props.description: How many glyphs the label comes apart into, 12 to 48.

props.name: orbit
props.description: Orbit speed in laps per second; the shimmer band sweeps with it.

props.name: palette
props.description: The particles' colours: accent to signal, the button's own ink, or warn to danger.

props.name: shimmer
props.description: Scan a band of light across the button while the host works.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the run's synthesised sounds: a shimmer and a rise on the lift, a chime on the spark, a thud on a failure. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the button.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: It is a native button: Space and Enter press it through the same path as a click. While the host works it is aria-busy and ignores presses but keeps focus, and a polite status announces the working, done or error label once the host has set it.

Under reduced motion nothing travels: the letters cross-fade, the glyphs appear in place on the orbit and twinkle in opacity, the shimmer breathes instead of sweeping, and a failure turns the border red instead of shaking. The sounds are unchanged.

The particles are DOM glyphs placed by motion values from one clock and four shared progresses, each mapped through a seeded delay, so nothing re-renders per frame, nothing is random, and the clock runs only while the swarm is alive.

items.title: Split Confirm
items.tagline: It splits into yes and no.
items.description: A destructive button that asks by coming apart. Pressed, a crack runs down its middle and the halves part on a snap spring into Cancel and Confirm, with the crack left in the gap as a hairline countdown that heals from both ends; when it runs out the halves are thrown shut on the same snap and meet with a clack. Confirm fires once and latches, closing on a flick spring into a muted button that no longer presses. Focus moves to Confirm as it arrives, the arrow keys cross the halves, and Escape closes the question.

props.name: label
props.description: The action, as the button reads before it is pressed.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: The right half's answer.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description: The left half's answer.

props.name: confirmedLabel
props.description: What the latched button reads once the action is confirmed.

props.name: confirmed / defaultConfirmed
props.description: Controlled or initial latch. Controlled, the latched face appears only once the host sets it; setting it back to false (an undo) restores the live button.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Fires once, from the Confirm press.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Fires when the question closes unanswered, with why.

props.name: timeout
props.description: Seconds the halves stay apart before they rejoin on their own.

props.name: split
props.description: A zigzag crack that snaps apart, or a clean seam that glides.

props.name: tone
props.description: Destructive red, or the primary accent for confirms that are serious but not destructive.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the synthesised tink of the crack, the clack of the rejoin and the thock of the confirm. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the button.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: Every state is native buttons. Pressing the whole button moves focus to Confirm as it arrives; Left/Right (and Home/End) cross between the halves, Escape cancels and returns focus to the whole button, and a timeout returns focus only if it was inside. Confirm arms about 320ms after the split and ignores key repeat, so a double press or a held Enter cannot confirm by accident.

Under reduced motion the gap appears at once, the halves cross-fade their colours and labels, and the rejoin is an instant close; the countdown hairline still shortens, because the time left is information. The sounds are unchanged.

The halves open inside the control's own box (sized for its widest state), so neighbours never move. The countdown pauses while the page is hidden, and a polite status says what is being asked, then Timed out or Cancelled, then the confirmed label once the host holds it.

items.title: Clicker Count
items.tagline: Every press, counted by hand.
items.description: A hand tally counter. Pressing the body sinks the plunger on a flick spring while the units wheel turns one notch on the same spring, then the plunger returns on a snap spring and the wheel stays; with carry on the wheels are geared, so 099 to 100 turns three wheels in one stroke. A long press on the reset knob turns it and winds every wheel back toward zero as the hold fills, and letting go early springs them home. Space and Enter count, and holding Space or Enter on the knob is the long press.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial count. It rolls over past the last wheel, like the real thing.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press or the finished reset, with the new count.

props.name: label
props.description: What is being counted. Names the counter and its buttons, and is spoken with the count.

props.name: digits
props.description: Number wheels in the window, 3 to 5.

props.name: travel
props.description: How far the plunger sinks, in px: short and snappy, or long and heavy. The click pitches with it.

props.name: finish
props.description: The body's finish, built from theme tokens so it reads on a light or a dark stage.

props.name: carry
props.description: Geared wheels: a rollover turns the next wheel in the same stroke and a reset rewinds through every number. Off, the wheels above the units turn freely to their own digits.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the synthesised click and clack of each press, a whir that rises while the knob is held, and the landing on zero. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the plunger and the knob.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: A group named by its label holds two native buttons. The body counts: Space and Enter make a full stroke with both sounds, and a held Enter keeps counting like a held plunger. The knob resets: hold Space or Enter for the same 800ms as a pointer (key repeat is ignored, Escape or blur lets go), and an assistive-technology click, which cannot hold, runs the full reset. A polite status speaks the count.

Under reduced motion the plunger darkens instead of travelling, the digits swap in place, and the knob does not turn; its progress ring still fills while it is held and the wheels swap to zero when it completes. The sounds are unchanged.

Controlled, the press and the finished hold report through onValueChange and the wheels turn when the host's value arrives; if the host refuses a reset, the knob lets go and the wheels run back to the count it still holds.

items.title: Keycap Press
items.tagline: It goes down when you press the real key.
items.description: A mechanical keycap that is a real button: it goes down when it is clicked, when Space or Enter presses it, and when its own shortcut is typed anywhere on the page, and it stays down for as long as the key is held. The switch sets the stroke — a clicky cap holds at the jacket on a decelerating tween then slams to the floor on an underdamped spring that rattles off the bottom, a tactile cap hitches at a softer bump and lands composed, a linear cap falls in one smooth stroke — and every cap returns on the same stem spring carrying its release velocity. The legend lights at actuation, and the switch sounds on the frame the cap passes each point.

props.name: label
props.description: The action, in a word or two: the key's accessible name, and the label legend.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: The real key that presses it from anywhere on the page: "e", "shift+r", "mod+enter", "space", "/". mod is Command on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Fires once per press, with what pressed it: on the click for pointer and keyboard presses, on keydown for the shortcut.

props.name: switch
props.description: Sets the travel curve and the sound: a jacket that gives and slams with a click, a rounded bump and a thock, or one smooth stroke and a muted thud.

props.name: height
props.description: The cap's skirt height in px, 4 to 14. Travel is 0.7 of it, and a taller cap sounds deeper.

props.name: legend
props.description: What is printed on the cap: the key glyph over the label on a 1.5u cap, the key glyph alone on a 1u cap, or the label alone on a cap that widens to fit.

props.name: glow
props.description: A backlight halo in the well around the cap, faint at rest and blooming with the legend on actuation.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the switch's synthesised sounds. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the key, blocks presses and stops listening for the shortcut.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the button's classes.

usageNotes: It is a native button named by its label, with aria-keyshortcuts: Space and Enter hold it down for as long as they are held and press it through the native click, a click from assistive technology plays a whole tap, and a held Enter does not repeat the action.

The shortcut listens on the document but never takes a key the page already handled (defaultPrevented) or one typed into a field, a select or editable text; it claims the key when it acts, so a second key with the same shortcut does not also fire, and a key that is disabled, hidden, inert or behind an open dialog does not listen.
Under reduced motion the cap swaps straight between up and down with no curve, and the legend, the halo and the sound still answer, because a press is information.
Keep the label to a word or two: the cap is sized by its legend and does not wrap.

items.title: Copy Slip
items.tagline: The text slips out and into the clipboard.
items.description: A copy field whose Copy button is a clipboard with its clip standing open. Pressed, a paper slip carrying the text lifts off the value and flies in a true throw — x linear, y a measured arc that never leaves the component — into the clipboard, where the clip clamps shut on snap and the glyph takes the landing on recoil; the button says Copied until the clip reopens. The slip only goes in if the clipboard took the text: a refusal bounces it back out on recoil, selects the text and says why in words, and Enter and Space copy through the same press.

props.name: value
props.description: What is copied, and shown in the field.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the field. The button is named by its word plus this: "Copy Payment link".

props.name: arc
props.description: How high the slip is lobbed, 0 to 1: 0 slides it straight along the row, 1 uses all the room above it. The swish rises with it.

props.name: slip
props.description: How light the paper is, 0 to 1: a stiff card thrown straight and fast, or a slip that hangs, leans along its path, flutters and takes its time.

props.name: hold
props.description: Seconds the clip stays shut and the button says Copied. The clock pauses while the page is hidden.

props.name: showText
props.description: Print the copied text on the slip; off draws ruled lines, for values that should not fly past a shared screen.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Fires once the clipboard has taken the value.

props.name: onCopyError
props.description: Fires when the clipboard refused: an insecure page, a denied permission, or a writer that failed or did not answer.

props.name: writer
props.description: Writes the text. Defaults to the system clipboard's writeText; swap in rich copy or a test double.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the paper and the clip. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the button and dims the field.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root element's classes.

usageNotes: The Copy button is a native button named by its visible word and the field's label ("Copy Payment link", then "Copied Payment link"); Enter and Space copy through the same press, and one polite status line says "Payment link copied." only after the clipboard has answered.

A refusal is said in words, not colour alone: the button reads Failed, a line under the field names the reason (an insecure page, a blocked clipboard) and the value is selected so ⌘C or Ctrl+C copies it by hand; the line is measured and grows in, never reserved.
Under reduced motion there is no flight and no clamp travel: the sheet appears in the clipboard and the clip shows shut, and the words, the hold and the sounds are unchanged.
Presses during a flight are absorbed, since the same copy is already on its way; a press while the clip is shut starts the whole thing over, hold clock included.

items.title: Pour Hold
items.tagline: Hold to pour; let go to stop.
items.description: A value input you fill by pouring: holding tips a carafe on a weighted spring, and once it passes the pour angle a stream leaves the mouth in a real ballistic arc, lands in the glass, and from that frame the level (the value) rises. Letting go rights the carafe, the stream's tail falls and lands as the last drop, and the surface rocks back to level on a spring whose damping is the liquid's viscosity, while the glass's own shape turns volume into height so a flute climbs fast and a jar slowly. It is a slider: arrow keys pour or lower one step, Page keys ten, End pours to the brim, Home empties, and Space or Enter held pours for as long as they are held.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The amount poured, 0 to max. Controlled or uncontrolled; the level follows a pour as it happens and settles on whatever the host says once it ends.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the pour or the key that changed it: once for each step a pour crosses, and once for each key step or empty.

props.name: max
props.description: What a full glass is worth.

props.name: step
props.description: The value's resolution, what one arrow key pours, and what a tap pours.

props.name: label
props.description: What is being poured: the slider's accessible name, also shown over the reading.

props.name: format
props.description: The reading under the glass and the slider's spoken value. Defaults to a percentage of max.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: The text of the button that empties the glass.

props.name: rate
props.description: How hard it pours, 0 to 1: the tilt, the stream's thickness, the flow (about 6 s to fill at 0, 1.6 s at 1) and the loudness.

props.name: viscosity
props.description: Water to syrup, 0 to 1: slower flow, a thicker and denser stream, a lower pour note, and a surface that barely sloshes.

props.name: glass
props.description: The glass's shape, which sets both the drawing and how fast the level climbs for the same pour.

props.name: overflow
props.description: Let a held pour run over the brim: the surface domes, a sheet runs down the outside and pools, and the value stays at max. Off, the carafe rights itself at the brim and a further hold is refused.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the pour, whose pitch rises as the glass fills, and the last drop. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the instrument, takes it out of the tab order and stops any pour.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: The instrument is a vertical role="slider" with aria-valuetext from format: ArrowUp/ArrowRight pour one step (held, they keep pouring), ArrowDown/ArrowLeft lower one, PageUp/PageDown move ten, End pours to the brim, Home empties, and Space or Enter held pours exactly like a held pointer, sounds included. The Empty button is a real button.

Under reduced motion the carafe swaps poses with no swing, the stream appears and goes whole and the surface stays flat, while the level still rises for as long as you hold and stops when you let go, because the level is the value.
A hold never selects text or opens the browser's menu, and a pour stops at once on pointer cancel, window blur or a hidden page. A tap pours one step.

items.title: Peek Hold
items.tagline: Hold to look before you open.
items.description: A list whose rows you can look into before you open them: a long press charges while the rest of the list starts to blur, then the row lifts out of the page on the snap spring and grows into a floating preview on the glide spring, with its actions beside it. Without letting go, sliding onto an action highlights it on a snap-spring pill and releasing chooses it; releasing on nothing cancels, and the card glides back down into its row, while a still release leaves the preview open. Right-click, the menu key and Shift+F10 open the same preview, and its actions are a menu driven by the arrow keys, Enter, Escape and Tab.

props.name: items
props.type: { id: string; title: string; subtitle?: string; meta?: string; leading?: ReactNode; badge?: ReactNode; preview: ReactNode }[]
props.description: The rows. The row's own header becomes the top of its preview, and preview is revealed under it.

props.name: menu
props.description: The actions offered under a preview ({ id, label, icon?, tone?: "default" | "danger" }), or a function of the item that picks them.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: A plain tap or click on a row, or Enter or Space on it.

props.name: onAction
props.description: An action chosen from a preview, by release, click or Enter. Fires before the preview closes.

props.name: onPeekChange
props.description: A preview opened, with its item's id, or closed, with null.

props.name: label
props.description: The list's accessible name.

props.name: delay
props.description: How long a press charges before the row lifts, in ms. The charge (the row sinking, the list blurring) runs exactly this long.

props.name: lift
props.description: How far the row rises as it comes free, in px; its scale and shadow grow with it, and 0 is a flat, in-place expansion.

props.name: blur
props.description: How hard the list behind a preview blurs, in px.

props.name: actions
props.description: The actions as a vertical menu of icon and label, or as one row of icon-over-label buttons.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a swell as the row lifts, a tick as the highlight moves between actions, and a pop when one is chosen. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the list, disables its rows and closes any preview.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: Rows are buttons with aria-haspopup="menu" and a shared hint: Enter opens a row, and Shift+F10 or the menu key opens its preview with focus on the first action. The actions are role="menu" items with roving focus: the arrow keys move, Home and End jump, Enter or Space chooses, and Escape or Tab closes and returns focus to the row.

Under reduced motion nothing rises, grows or slides: the preview fades in where it will sit and fades out over its row, the charge shows only as the blur building, and the highlight swaps without travelling.

A hold never selects text or opens the browser's own menu, and rows keep touch-pan-y, so a swipe still scrolls the page; once a preview is open, touch moves are held so the finger can slide to an action. Pointer cancel, window blur and a hidden page end the hold, and a press outside the list closes the preview.
