props.description: A framed field with a notch cut under the tag, a filled field whose tag reads as a raised tab, or an underline.

props.name: budget
props.description: Show the budget as a thread filling under the field, cobalt, then warn in the last 20%, with a count. Needs maxLength.

props.name: type
props.description: The input's type.

props.name: name
props.description: The input's name, for forms.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: The input's autocomplete hint. Autofill lifts the label, even before the page has had a key.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: The on-screen keyboard to offer.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown inside the field only once the label has lifted out of the way.

props.name: required
props.description: The input's native required.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: The input's focus event.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: The input's blur event, e.g. to validate on leaving the field.

props.name: ref
props.description: The input element, e.g. to focus the field when a submit is refused.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a tick on the frame the tag lands (only while the field has focus), a shrug with the error shake, and a detent on the key that fills the budget. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the field and disables the input; the label stays where the text puts it.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: A real <input> named by a real <label for>: Tab into the field and the label lifts, flips and hangs with the same tick a click gives; typing, selection, IME composition, paste and autofill are native. The field's own frame is the focus indicator (a 2px ring-coloured border, or a 2px rule), deliberately not an outline ring, which would run through the hanging tag. The error and hint are linked with aria-describedby, and the budget is spoken only at thresholds ("6 characters left.", "No characters left.").

Under reduced motion the label cross-fades between the placeholder spot and the edge with no travel, flip, swing or shake, while the notch, the colours, the error message and the budget thread still answer.
Pass the form's submit count as shakeKey (and focus the field through ref) so each refused submit shakes the label again on the edge where it hangs.

items.title: Roll Search
items.tagline: The lens rolls open into a field.
items.description: A search that lives as a round lens at the right end of its slot: pressed, or with / typed anywhere on the page, the lens rolls to the left end like a wheel on the snap spring while the field unrolls behind it like a strip of carpet, one motion value driving the pill's width, the lens's place and its turn, so the wheel never slips and always lands upright. Results drop in below on snap in a cascade, in a panel whose height is measured and glides, with the query lit in each; Escape rolls it back up on glide. The input is a real combobox: arrows move through the results, Enter picks one, Escape rolls it up and returns focus to the lens.

props.name: items
props.type: { id: string; label: string; meta?: string; keywords?: readonly string[] }[]
props.description: What is searched: the label and meta are shown and lit, keywords only searched.

props.name: label
props.description: What is being searched, as "Search docs": the lens button's name and the input's visible label, which heads the results panel.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The input's placeholder.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The query. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the new query on every edit, and with "" when the search rolls up.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the field is rolled open. Controlled or uncontrolled; a host change rolls it silently.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the press, key or blur that opened or closed it.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Enter, or a press on a result. The search then rolls up and focus returns to the lens.

props.name: filter
props.description: Whether an item answers a query. Defaults to every word of the query appearing in its label, meta or keywords.

props.name: limit
props.description: The most results shown at once; the panel says "4 of 9" when there are more.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: The key that opens it from anywhere on the page, shown as a small key cap beside the lens; null for none. It never fires while typing in a field, with a modifier, during composition, or behind a dialog.

props.name: width
props.description: How far the field unrolls, in px, 200 to 400. It shrinks to fit a narrower box.

props.name: roll
props.description: The lens turns as it travels, like a wheel, rocking slightly against the end; off, it slides.

props.name: results
props.description: Compact rows with a page glyph and the meta at the end, or small cards in two columns.

props.name: highlight
props.description: Light every occurrence of the query's words in each result.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a whir while the lens rolls, its gain and pitch following the lens's speed (a swish when it slides), and a tick as each arriving result lands. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the lens, the input and the shortcut.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: Closed, the lens is a button with aria-expanded and aria-keyshortcuts="/"; Enter, Space or / open it and focus lands in the input within the same press, so a phone raises its keyboard. Open, the input is a role="combobox" with aria-activedescendant over a listbox: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active result, Enter picks it (the first when none is active), Escape rolls it back up wherever focus is inside the component and returns focus to the lens. Leaving an empty search rolls it up too, and the result count is spoken politely once typing pauses.
Under reduced motion nothing rolls or drops: the slot cross-fades between closed and open, results fade in place and the panel height changes on a short tween; the result ticks still mark arrivals.
The results panel sits in the flow under the field and its height is measured, so give the component room below it, or place it where the page can grow.

items.title: Sift Filter
items.tagline: Type; what doesn't match falls away.
items.description: A filter field over a two-column set of cards: as you type, every card that stops matching drops off the bottom under constant acceleration with a slight spin, while the matches close ranks on the glide spring, and the set's floor waits for the last faller to pass through it before it glides up to fit. Deleting back or clearing brings the fallen up from below the floor on the snap spring, their spin unwinding, in a stagger that stays inside the choreography budget. The field is a real input: Escape clears it with the same rise as deleting, fallen cards leave the tab order and the accessibility tree at once, and IME composition filters on what was committed.

props.name: items
props.type: { id: string; title: string; meta?: string; tags?: readonly string[] }[]
props.description: The cards: a title and a short second line, both searched and lit; tags only searched.

props.name: label
props.description: What the field filters: its visible label and accessible name.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The input's placeholder.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The query. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the new query on every edit, and with "" when cleared.

props.name: filter
props.description: Whether a card answers a query. Defaults to every word of the query appearing in its title, meta or tags.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Makes each card a button, and fires with the card pressed.

props.name: gravity
props.description: How hard cards fall, in px/s², 1000 to 6000: a fall of d px takes √(2d/g). Also how hard the fallen are thrown back up.

props.name: spin
props.description: How far a card turns on its way down, in degrees, 0 to 40. Each card falls its own way, the same way every time.

props.name: stagger
props.description: The gap between one card leaving (or returning) and the next, in ms, 0 to 100, tightened so a whole cascade stays within 600ms.

props.name: highlight
props.description: Light the query's words in each card's title and meta.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a patter, a soft plip as each card passes through the floor (pitched per card, panned by column), and a rise when an edit brings cards back. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field and the clear button, and makes cards plain.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: A real <input> with a visible <label for>; Escape clears it (and only claims the key when there is text to clear), as does the Clear filter button, with the same rise and sound as deleting. The set is a list; fallen cards are aria-hidden and inert from the moment they start to fall, and "3 of 10 match." is spoken politely once typing pauses.

Under reduced motion nothing falls, spins or travels: cards that stop matching fade out in place, survivors dip and reappear in their new slots, returning cards fade in, and the floor changes height on a short tween; the count, the spoken summary and the patter still answer.

Cards are a fixed 64px tall in two percentage columns, so the set's height is known before anything is measured and it renders the same on the server; titles and metas truncate with their full text in a tooltip.

items.title: Plain Date
items.tagline: Type it the way you say it.
items.description: A date field you type in words: it reads today, tomorrow, next fri 3pm, in 2 weeks or oct 23 against a now you pass, lights the words it used, slides the date out of the end of the phrase as a chip on the snap spring, and lights the day in a mini calendar whose light hops on snap and whose page turns on glide when the month changes. A phrase with two readings offers both chips; ArrowDown and ArrowUp choose, Enter or a click sets, Escape puts back the last set phrase. It is a real input with the combobox pattern, so typing, selection, IME, paste and undo stay native.

props.name: label
props.description: What the date is for. Shown above the field and tied to it by id.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment phrases are read against. Required. Pass a fixed moment or one taken in an effect, never new Date() during render.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The committed date. Controlled or uncontrolled; a host that sets a date the field did not report sees it written back as a phrase the field reads ("fri 23 oct 3:00pm").

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: (value: Date | null, detail: { hasTime: boolean }) => void
props.description: Fires from the Enter, chip click or blur that committed it, with whether a time was given. null when the field is cleared and Enter pressed.

props.name: defaultText
props.description: The phrase the field starts with, read but not committed.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The field's placeholder.

props.name: weekStart
props.description: The calendar's first column, each day's chime on the scale, and where "this week" ends, which decides whether next <weekday> has two readings.

props.name: format
props.description: How the chip writes the date: Fri 23 Oct, Friday 23 October, 2026-10-23 with a 24-hour time, or In 10 days with the date underneath.

props.name: calendar
props.description: Show the mini calendar beside the field.

props.name: strict
props.description: Read only the exact grammar and guess nothing: no short forms or prefixes, no bare hours, unknown words stop the parse, and a phrase with two readings has none chosen until you pick.

props.name: sound
props.description: A soft chime when the chosen date changes, pitched by weekday and panned by its calendar column, and a click when it is set. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field and its chips and dims the calendar.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: The grammar: today, tomorrow, in <n> days or weeks, <weekday>, this <weekday>, next <weekday>, <month> <day> [<year>] or <day> <month> [<year>], and a time anywhere (3pm, 3:30pm, 15:00, noon); "at", "on", "the", "of" are filler. next <weekday> has two readings while that day is still ahead this week. The input is a combobox whose options are the reading chips: ArrowDown and ArrowUp choose, Enter commits (and is left alone when the chosen date is already set, so a form can submit), Escape restores the last committed phrase undoably, and blur commits an unambiguous reading. Readings are announced once typing settles.

Under reduced motion the chips and the calendar light fade in place instead of travelling, the month changes with a cross-fade and the check appears without drawing; every reading, highlight, ring and chime still happens.
Nothing reads the clock during render: every date is local-time arithmetic on the now you pass, so server and browser render the same markup.

items.title: Calc Field
items.tagline: Type the sum; the answer keeps up.
items.description: An amount field that takes arithmetic: type 1240/3, 12*4+3 or 15% and the answer rides in a bubble just past the last character, kept up with on the snap spring, its digits rolling up as the answer grows and down as it shrinks. Enter or leaving the field commits: the sum folds away, or down into a receipt, on the exit tween while the answer folds down into place on snap; a character that can never be arithmetic is refused with a soft shake. The parser is a small recursive descent with no eval, and the input stays native, so typing, IME, paste and undo work, and undo brings a committed sum back.

props.name: label
props.description: What the amount is. Shown above the field and tied to it by id.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The committed amount, already rounded. Controlled or uncontrolled; a host that sets an amount the field did not report sees it written into the field.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the Enter or blur that committed it, with the rounded amount; null when the field is emptied and committed.

props.name: defaultText
props.description: A sum the field starts with, worked out but not committed.

props.name: percentOf
props.description: What a bare percentage is a share of: with 1240, 15% is 186. Without it a bare percentage is its fraction.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The field's placeholder.

props.name: precision
props.description: Decimals in the answer and the committed amount, 0 to 3 — the range currencies use.

props.name: currency
props.description: An ISO currency code whose symbol sits before the field and in the bubble, or "none" for a plain number.

props.name: expression
props.description: Write the sum out under the field while you type (× ÷ −, and which way it was rounded when it was), fold it down into a receipt on commit, and make the receipt a button that brings the sum back. Off, the sum folds away with nothing kept.

props.name: rounding
props.description: How the answer is brought to precision, on its decimal digits (1.005 is 1.01 half up). "up" and "down" are away from and toward zero. A rounded answer shows ≈, and the tape names the mode.

props.name: sound
props.description: A tick as the answer changes, pitched by its size and panned by the bubble's place, a click on commit, and a quiet shrug with each shake. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field and the receipt.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: Arithmetic: + − × ÷ (also * / x), brackets, unary signs, decimals, thousands commas and %, where a + b% adds b% of a and a bare b% is b% of percentOf. Enter commits and is claimed only when there is something to commit, so a form still submits on a second Enter; blur commits too; Escape restores the last committed text; undo after a commit brings the sum back. An unfinished sum keeps its last answer, dimmed. The answer is in the input's description and announced once typing settles, never per keystroke.

Under reduced motion the bubble moves without travel, digits cross-fade instead of rolling, the commit is a cross-fade and a failed commit turns the border danger instead of shaking; the answer, receipt and sounds still arrive.

The parser never throws and never evaluates code: anything it cannot work out comes back as a sentence ("Two operators in a row", "Can’t divide by zero") shown under the field and set as aria-invalid.

items.title: Glide Caret
items.tagline: The caret glides to where you type.
items.description: A native textarea whose caret glides: its place is read from a mirror of the text, a head springs there at the chosen stiffness while a softer, critically damped tail follows, and the caret is drawn as a solid bar with a translucent streak between the two that thins with distance and shrinks back to a bar as the tail catches up. Selecting text draws one highlight per line that springs out from the caret's column, rippling outward on the house cascade, with the caret riding the active end. Everything else — typing, selection, IME, paste, undo, spellcheck, the keyboard — is the textarea's own, and the native caret returns during composition and in forced colours.

props.name: label
props.description: What the text is. Shown above the field and tied to the textarea by id.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The text. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on every edit, with the new text.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The textarea's placeholder.

props.name: rows
props.description: Visible lines, 2 to 12. The textarea scrolls past them, and the caret and selection move with the text.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name, passed to the textarea.

props.name: stiffness
props.description: The caret's spring, 150 to 1200: floaty and lagging at the low end, tight at the top. The selection's growing edge uses it too.

props.name: stretch
props.description: How far the caret's tail lags, 0 to 1: at 0 a plain bar glides; toward 1 it trails a long streak.

props.name: width
props.description: The caret's thickness in px, 1 to 4.

props.name: blink
props.description: How the caret blinks at rest: a breathing fade, the classic hard on and off, or solid. It restarts solid after every move and runs on the compositor.

props.name: sound
props.description: Faint taps as the caret lands: a tick per character with its own small pitch, a lower one for deletions, a detent for a new line and a lighter tick for a click or arrow jump, panned by the caret's place. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the textarea; the drawn caret never shows.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: It is a real textarea with a visible label: every key, shortcut, selection gesture, IME, paste and undo is native, and so is its focus ring. The native caret is hidden only while the drawn caret is showing and focus is inside; during IME composition, before the first measurement, when disabled and in forced-colours mode the native caret and highlight come back. Placing the caret with the arrow keys taps exactly as a click does.
Under reduced motion the caret moves to each place at once with no streak and does not blink, and a selection fades in line by line instead of growing; the caret and the highlight are still drawn.

Measurement is coalesced to one read per frame and only runs on input, selection, focus, scroll and resize, so nothing runs while the text sits still; scrolling and resizing move the caret with the text, without travel.

items.title: Ratio Morph
items.tagline: Pick a shape; the picture reframes.
items.description: An aspect-ratio picker that reframes a picture: choosing a shape glides the frame's width and height to the new ratio on the glide spring, with four corner brackets riding its corners, while the picture is re-laid every frame so its focal point stays as near the centre as its edges allow. Pressing the stage brings the focal reticle to the finger 1:1 (it swells on flick) while a ghost of the whole picture fades in round the frame; past the picture's edge the reticle rubber-bands, and on release the throw is projected and the picture glides to re-centre on the new point. The chips are a radiogroup whose arrows choose and whose Home and End jump; the stage takes arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps) to move the focal point with the same glide and sounds.

props.name: ratios
props.description: The shapes offered, in chip order: social is 1:1, 4:5, 16:9 and 9:16; photo is 3:2, 4:3, 1:1 and 2:3; screen is 16:9, 16:10, 21:9 and 4:3. Or your own list of "w:h" strings. RATIO_MORPH_SETS exports the named sets.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The chosen ratio, as "w:h". A value that is not in the list shows the first ratio.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that chose a new ratio. In controlled mode the frame morphs once the host passes the new value back.

props.name: focalPoint / defaultFocalPoint
props.description: The point the frame keeps in view as it changes shape, as fractions of the picture's width and height.

props.name: onFocalPointChange
props.description: Fires once per drag release, tap or arrow key, with the new point rounded to three places.

props.name: brackets
props.description: The corner brackets' arm length in px, 6 to 40: short ticks to nearly closed corners.

props.name: focal
props.description: Marks the focal point with a reticle on the picture.

props.name: grid
props.description: Rule-of-thirds lines inside the frame that ride the morph; faint at rest, brighter while the picture is held.

props.name: picture
props.description: What is framed. It is laid out in a box of pictureRatio and scaled, so pass something that fills its box, such as an img with object-cover.

props.name: pictureRatio
props.description: The picture's own width over its height.

props.name: alt
props.description: What the picture shows, read with the stage's instructions. Defaults to a description of the built-in harbour.

props.name: label
props.description: The ratio chips' accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: A detent when a ratio is chosen and a click on the frame the morph lands, both pitched by the shape; a detent when a drag meets the picture's edge and a click on release. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the picker and blocks the chips, drags, taps and keys.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the wrapper that holds the stage and the chips.

usageNotes: The chips are a role=radiogroup of radios with one tab stop: any arrow moves and chooses (wrapping), Home and End jump, and each is named as a shape ("4 by 5, portrait"). The stage is a focusable role=application ("picture frame") described by the alt text and its instructions; arrows move the focal point 5%, Shift+arrows 20%, and a polite live region says the new point once per move.

Under reduced motion the frame changes shape at once and its brackets fade in at the new corners; the picture re-lays at once. A drag still follows the finger 1:1 but lands without a projected glide, and keys jump. The reticle, grid, ghost fade and sounds are unchanged.

The stage is touch-action: none, since the drag is two-dimensional. Its width is measured, so the frame is as large as the column allows; the server and the first client render use a 320px stage, then it resizes without a morph or a sound.

items.title: Seat Map
items.tagline: Pick your seats; the row makes room.
items.description: A seating chart for one booking: pressing a free seat flips it over on its centre line to its chosen face on the snap spring, with a clack as it lands flat, and the row makes room as its neighbours in the block are kicked aside by a velocity whose target is their own place, so each sways away and back on snap. While picks remain, the free seats beside yours light as together suggestions; taken seats are hatched, and the total rolls digit by digit on glide with a tick. It is a multi-select grid with one tab stop: arrows roam seat by seat over the aisles, Home, End, Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+End, PageUp and PageDown jump, and Space or Enter picks with the same flip and sounds.

props.name: rows
props.description: Rows of seats, 1 to 12, lettered from the stage back with I and O skipped. More rows make smaller seats (at most 22px) so the grid stays within about 172px.

props.name: columns
props.description: Seats in each row, 4 to 16, numbered from the left.

props.name: aisles
props.description: Aisles splitting each row, 0 to 3. Two make the classic short-long-short blocks; otherwise the blocks are even with any spare seats in the middle.

props.name: tiers
props.description: Prices the rows in three bands (front, centre and rear by thirds, the centre taking the remainder), each with its own tint and named in the readout.

props.name: maxPicks
props.description: The most seats one booking may hold, 1 to 12. At the limit the other free seats dim and a press is refused with a shrug.

props.name: taken
props.description: Seats already sold, by id (row letter and seat number, "C7"). seatMapId(rowIndex, seatNumber) builds an id the way the map does.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The chosen seats' ids in the order they were chosen. Ids that are off the map or taken are ignored.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that chose or released a seat. A seat flips only once the value that is shown includes it.

props.name: price
props.description: Every seat's price when tiers is off.

props.name: tierPrices
props.description: Front, centre and rear prices when tiers is on.

props.name: format
props.description: How prices and the total are printed. The total's digits roll; any other characters stay put.

props.name: label
props.description: The grid's accessible name.

props.name: stageLabel
props.description: Printed under the curve at the top of the map.

props.name: sound
props.description: A clack as a seat lands flat, pitched up with each seat you hold and panned by its column; a softer one as a released seat lands back; a tick as the total rolls; a quiet shrug for a refused seat. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the map and blocks picks; no seat takes focus.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the wrapper, whose max width is set from the seat size so the footer lines up with the grid.

usageNotes: The map is role=grid with aria-multiselectable; each row has a rowheader letter, and each seat is a gridcell with aria-selected (aria-disabled when taken) and a one-string name such as "Row C, seat 7, centre, $36.00, suggested". One seat is the tab stop. Arrows move a seat at a time, stepping over aisles; Home and End go to the row's ends, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End to the corners, PageUp and PageDown to the first and last rows; Space or Enter picks or releases. A polite live region says each change once, from the value actually shown.

Under reduced motion seats cross-fade from their free face to their chosen face instead of flipping, nothing sways, and the total swaps in place. Suggestions, dimming, sounds and announcements are unchanged.

The footer reads out the seat under the pointer or focus (its band and price, or that it is taken or yours), else the suggestions or your seats. Seats are touch-manipulation, so the page still scrolls from the map.

items.title: Tool Dock
items.tagline: Pick a tool; its options unfold beside it.
items.description: The tool rail of a drawing canvas and the canvas it drives: the active tool sits on an indicator that slides to each new choice on the snap spring with a tick pitched up the rail, and a tool with variants unfolds its options beside it with a swish — a panel revealed from the rail's edge whose entries step out on snap, or a drawer that glides open inside the rail on glide. Single-letter shortcuts switch tools while focus or the pointer is on the dock (never while typing), the key of the active tool cycles its variants, and the canvas shows the tool's own cursor, drawn 1:1 under the pointer and popping to each new shape on snap. The rail is a toolbar of pressed buttons with one tab stop: arrows move, Space or Enter choose, and the arrow toward the options opens them as a menu of radio items with focus inside.

props.name: tools
props.type: { id: string; label: string; glyph?: ToolDockGlyph; icon?: ReactNode; cursor?: ReactNode; key?: string; variants?: { id: string; label: string; glyph?: ToolDockGlyph; icon?: ReactNode; cursor?: ReactNode; key?: string }[] }[]
props.description: The rail, top to bottom (or left to right). A tool with variants shows the last one used; key is a single letter. Built-in glyphs, each with a cursor: move, hand, frame, rect, ellipse, line, polygon, pen, pencil, brush, text, eraser, comment.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The active tool's id, or the active variant's id for a tool that has them.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press, key or shortcut that changed the tool.

props.name: orientation
props.description: A rail down the canvas's left, or centred along its foot.

props.name: shortcuts
props.description: Single-letter keys switch tools and each button shows its letter (and names it in aria-keyshortcuts). Keys act while focus is in the dock, or while the pointer is over it and nothing else has focus; never in a field or with Ctrl, Cmd or Alt, and a handled key is claimed.

props.name: flyout
props.description: A tool's options float in a panel beside the rail (over the canvas, placed inside the component's box), or open as a drawer inside the rail that pushes the tools after it.

props.name: labels
props.description: A label under each icon; the rail widens to fit. Off, the name is still each button's accessible name.

props.name: children
props.description: What is on the canvas, laid out inside it (position it absolutely to fill).

props.name: canvasHeight
props.description: The canvas's height in px.

props.name: label
props.description: The rail's accessible name.

props.name: canvasLabel
props.description: The canvas's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: A tick on every tool or variant change, pitched up the rail on a pentatonic scale and panned to the button; a swish as options unfold and a lower, quieter one as they fold. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the dock, disables its buttons and stops the shortcuts; the system cursor comes back over the canvas.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the wrapper that holds the rail and the canvas.

usageNotes: The rail is role=toolbar (with aria-orientation) of buttons with aria-pressed and one tab stop: arrows along the rail move focus, Home and End jump, Space or Enter choose. A tool with variants has aria-haspopup=menu and aria-expanded; Space, Enter or the arrow toward the options (Right on a vertical rail, Up on a horizontal one) opens them as a role=menu of menuitemradio with focus on the checked one. There arrows move, Space or Enter choose and fold back to the tool, Escape or the arrow back folds without choosing, and focus leaving folds them. A shortcut's change is announced once in a polite live region.

Under reduced motion the indicator moves at once, options fade in and out with no reveal or step (a tray opens at full height), and the canvas cursor still follows the pointer but parks at once and swaps its shape with a fade. Sounds are unchanged.

The canvas hides the system cursor and draws the tool's own with its hotspot under the pointer, parking it at the centre when the pointer leaves so a keyboard or touch user still sees the tool change; a tap moves it to the finger. A press anywhere outside the rail and its options folds them.

items.title: Lasso Grid
items.tagline: Draw around what you want.
items.description: A file grid with rubber-band selection: drag anywhere and a box (or, with Alt or mode="lasso", a freehand loop) follows the pointer 1:1, lighting every tile it catches and squeezing it a little on the snap spring while the band holds it. Let go and the band contracts onto what it caught on the same snap spring, one crisp overshoot like a rubber band let go around a bundle, while a count badge glides after the selection's corner on the glide spring. Arrow keys move and select in two dimensions, Shift+Arrow draws the same band from the keyboard and snaps it tight when Shift is released, Space toggles, Cmd/Ctrl+A selects all and Escape clears.

props.name: items
props.description: The files, in reading order: id, name (the label and accessible name) and an optional kind — folder, image, doc, sheet, audio or video — that picks the glyph.

props.name: label
props.description: The grid's accessible name.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The selected ids, controlled or uncontrolled. A controlled grid shows the host's answer after each band, tap or key.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires once per band (on release), per tap and per key, with the new selection in item order.

props.name: mode
props.description: The band's shape: a rectangle, or a freehand loop that tightens into a box on release. Alt held as a drag starts draws the other one.

props.name: hit
props.description: Whether a tile is caught as soon as the band touches it, or only once the band encloses it.

props.name: badge
props.description: A count badge that rides the top-right corner of the selection, gliding after it as it changes, its figure rolling.

props.name: sound
props.description: A tick per tile as the band catches it, climbing a pentatonic step each time, and a tock on release. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the grid and blocks selection; arrow keys still move focus.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: It is a multi-select listbox of options with roving focus: Arrow keys move in two dimensions and select the tile they land on, Ctrl/Cmd+Arrow moves focus only, Space toggles a tile, Shift+Arrow grows a box from the anchor tile — drawn on screen like the pointer's band — and releasing Shift snaps it tight with the tock, Cmd/Ctrl+A selects all, and Escape clears a selection or cancels a band in flight (with nothing selected it is left for the page).

A plain band replaces the selection, Shift adds to it and Cmd or Ctrl toggles against it; a click selects one tile, Shift+click a block from the anchor, Cmd/Ctrl+click toggles one. On touch there are no modifiers, so a tap toggles a tile and a band adds.

Under reduced motion the band still draws under the pointer and fades on release instead of tightening, tiles do not squeeze and the badge moves without gliding; every tile still lights and every sound still plays.
The grid takes touch-action: none so a band can be drawn with a finger; keep it a modest block on long mobile pages.

items.title: Brush Select
items.tagline: Paint across to pick many.
items.description: Filter chips you select by painting: a click toggles one chip, but press on a chip and drag and the press becomes a brush — the first chip flips, and every chip the stroke passes takes its new state (or flips, in toggle mode), once per stroke. The paint wipes across each chip from the side the brush came in on an enter tween, each chip dips under the bristles on an impulse given to the snap spring, and its check draws on the flick; the stroke reports once, on release. Space toggles the focused chip, Shift+Arrow carries its state onto the next chip with the same wipe and tick, and Shift+Home/End or Cmd/Ctrl+A paint a whole run on one staggered beat.

props.name: items
props.description: The chips, in order: id and label.

props.name: label
props.description: The chip set's accessible name.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The selected ids, controlled or uncontrolled. During a stroke the chips show its draft; a controlled set then shows the host's answer.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires once on the release of a stroke, on a tap and on each key, with the new selection in item order.

props.name: mode
props.description: Paint the first chip's new state onto every chip the stroke passes, or flip each one.

props.name: layout
props.description: Pills of their natural width in wrapping rows, or equal rounded cells in a grid.

props.name: check
props.description: A round indicator on every chip that fills and draws a check when the chip turns on. Off, colour alone carries the state.

props.name: sound
props.description: A tick per chip the brush passes, climbing a pentatonic scale through the stroke (falling when the paint takes chips off). Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the chips and blocks taps, strokes and keys that change them; arrow keys still move focus.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: It is a multi-select listbox of options with roving focus: Left/Right move along the chips, Up/Down to the nearest chip in the row above or below, Home/End to the ends. Space or Enter toggles the focused chip; Shift+Arrow then carries its state onto each chip it moves to (or flips it, in toggle mode) with the next tick of the scale, Shift+Home/End paints to the end, and Cmd/Ctrl+A paints every chip on, or off when all are on.
A stroke is sampled every few pixels along its path, so a quick flick across a row still paints every chip it crosses; Escape during a stroke takes it back.
Under reduced motion the on face cross-fades instead of wiping, the check appears whole and nothing dips; the painting, the ticks and the result are unchanged.
The chip set takes touch-action: none so a finger can paint across it; keep it to a modest block on long mobile pages.

items.title: Zone Map
items.tagline: Tap the regions you cover.
items.description: A stylised map of invented regions, drawn procedurally and identically on server and browser, with a list beside it that keeps the selection in words. Hover or keyboard focus lifts a region above a flat shadow on the snap spring; a click selects it with a fill that floods out from the click point to the coast on an enter tween timed to its reach and an outline that draws both ways round from the nearest vertex, and a second click drains it back into the point you tapped, while list rows arrive and make room on the glide spring. Arrow keys move to the nearest region in that direction, Home and End to the first and last, and Space or Enter toggles with the same flood, from the region's centre, and the same tock.

props.name: label
props.description: The map's accessible name.

props.name: names
props.description: Region names in map order, top-left first. They are also the ids in value; regions beyond the list are called Region 8, Region 9 and so on.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The selected region names in the order they were picked, controlled or uncontrolled. Names not on the current map are ignored.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the click, key or remove button that changed the selection, with the new list.

props.name: regions
props.description: How many regions the island is cut into. The same count and seed always draw the same map.

props.name: lift
props.description: How far hover and keyboard focus lift a region, in map units (the map is 200 wide). 0 leaves only the tint.

props.name: flood
props.description: The fill floods out from the click point with a swish; off, it fades in whole and silently.

props.name: palette
props.description: The two theme colours every selected region's shade is mixed from: accent and signal, warn and danger, success and warn, or ink and ink-3.

props.name: seed
props.description: Another map for the same count.

props.name: listLabel
props.description: The heading over the list beside the map, and the list's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: A tock on every select (lower and softer on a deselect) and a swish riding the flood. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the map, stops the lift and blocks changes from clicks, keys and the remove buttons.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: The map is a multi-select listbox of regions with roving focus: arrow keys move to the nearest region in that direction, Home and End to the first and last, and Space or Enter adds or removes the focused one. The keyboard-focused region lifts like a hovered one and is ringed along its own edge. Each list row has a Remove button named for its region; removing a row moves focus to the row that takes its place.

Every coordinate is built with arithmetic alone from constant directions and a seeded integer generator, never trigonometry, so the server's markup and the browser's first render match to the last digit.
Under reduced motion nothing lifts, floods or draws: the raised region is tinted, the fill and outline fade in whole and list rows cross-fade; the selection, the list and every sound are unchanged.
The component is a row — the map and a 120px list that scrolls inside the map's height — so give it at least about 300px of width.

items.title: Pattern Lock
items.tagline: Draw the path through the dots.
items.description: A pattern pad whose line's live end is 1:1 under the finger and snaps through every dot its path crosses, taking any free dot lying straight between two it joins; each caught dot pops on a flick up and a springs.snap back and plays the next note of a rising pentatonic phrase, so the pattern is also a melody. A refused pattern shakes and fades after the clear delay, and an accepted one locks with a ripple that runs along the path in the order it was drawn, with a chord. Arrow keys move between the dots, Space or a number key adds one, Backspace takes the last back, Enter finishes as a lift does and Escape clears.

props.name: label
props.description: The pad's accessible name, e.g. "Unlock pattern".

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The pattern as dot numbers from 1 (reading order), in drawing order. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the catch that added a dot, the key that removed one, and the clear, with the whole pattern.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Asked when a pattern of at least minLength dots is finished. Return true to accept it (ripple and chord), false to refuse it (shake and buzz), nothing to record it neutrally, or a promise of one of those while the pad waits.

props.name: minLength
props.description: Shorter patterns are refused before onComplete is asked.

props.name: grid
props.description: Dots per side: a 3 × 3 or a 4 × 4 pad. Changing it clears the pattern.

props.name: path
props.description: Draw the line and keep caught dots lit. Off is the private mode: each catch only flashes and pops, the melody is the only trail, and success ripples from the centre so nothing of the pattern shows.

props.name: line
props.description: The line's weight in px, 2 to 10.

props.name: clearDelay
props.description: How long a wrong, short or recorded pattern stays on the pad before it fades, in ms.

props.name: size
props.description: The pad's side in px.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a rising note for each dot, a chord when accepted and a buzz when refused. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the pad and blocks drawing and keys.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the pad's classes.

usageNotes: Every dot is a real button with roving focus: Arrow keys move between dots, Home and End jump, Space adds the focused dot and number keys 1 to 9 add a dot by number (with the same skip rule, pop and note), Backspace removes the last dot, Enter finishes exactly as lifting the finger does, and Escape clears (it is left for the page when the pad is empty). Keyboard additions and every verdict are announced in a polite live region.

Under reduced motion the line still follows the finger, but no dot pops, nothing shakes and no ring travels: a refused pattern turns danger and fades, an accepted one turns success with its rings filled in place; notes, chord, buzz and verdicts are unchanged.

onComplete may be async: the pad holds the pattern (aria-busy) until the promise settles, and a new press before then wins. With nothing returned the pattern is recorded and fades after clearDelay, which is the first step of setting a new pattern.

items.title: Stroke Command
items.tagline: Draw a shape; it runs the command.
items.description: A gesture pad that runs a command when you draw its shape: a small unistroke matcher resamples the stroke, turns it to its indicative angle, scales it into a square and searches the leftover rotation against a check, a circle, an arrow and a zigzag. A match morphs the stroke you drew, point for point, into the clean shape laid over it on springs.glide, and the command's label lands on springs.recoil with its own chime; a stroke that is no shape shrugs and fades. The command chips are a real toolbar: Arrow keys move along it, and Enter or Space makes the pad draw that shape itself, through the same matcher, morph and sound.

props.name: commands
props.description: The commands in chip order, each bound to "check", "circle", "arrow" or "zigzag". Only these shapes are recognised; a shape bound twice keeps its first command.

props.name: onCommand
props.description: Fires from the release (or the chip) that ran a command, with the match score from 0 to 1 and how it was run: "stroke", "keyboard" or "pointer".

props.name: onMiss
props.type: (best: { shape, score } | null, threshold: number) => void
props.description: Fires when a stroke matched no command, with the nearest upright shape (or null for a line or a scribble too short to judge) and the score it needed.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the whole control; the toolbar is named after it.

props.name: tolerance
props.description: How forgiving the matcher is, 0 (strict: a score of 0.92 needed) to 1 (loose: 0.74).

props.name: trail
props.description: Show the ink while drawing. Off, only the pen tip moves, and the stroke appears as it is judged.

props.name: width
props.description: The ink's weight in px, 2 to 10.

props.name: templates
props.description: ghost fits the leading template faintly under the stroke while you draw, solid once it would match, and warms its chip; off shows nothing until release.

props.name: height
props.description: The pad's height in px; it fills the available width.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a pencil scratch that follows the pen's speed, a chime for a match (a different step of one chord per command) and a shrug for a miss. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the pad and the chips and blocks drawing and commands.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: The chips are a role="toolbar" with one tab stop: Arrow keys (and Home and End) move between commands, and Enter or Space makes the pad trace that shape and run it through the same matcher, morph, chime and onCommand. The pad itself is a pointer surface hidden from assistive technology; results are announced in a polite live region.

Under reduced motion drawing still follows the pen, but nothing is traced, morphed or shrugged: the clean shape and the label cross-fade in, an unmatched stroke simply fades, and every sound, callback and announcement is the same.
Check, arrow and zigzag are recognised only upright (within 50°); circles in either direction and zigzags from either end both count. A straight stroke or one shorter than 24px is never a command.

items.title: Guess Line
items.tagline: Draw what you think; then see.
items.description: A line chart whose latest stretch is hidden: the reader draws what they think comes next across the shaded band, the pen steadied by the smoothing and the drawn line bending through it 1:1 between points, and letting go with every point guessed reveals the truth. The real line continues from the anchor under a clip whose edge sweeps across the band, the gap between guess and truth shades as it passes, a hum follows the real value under the sweep, and on landing the score rolls up on springs.recoil. Every hidden point is also a slider: Up and Down set it, Left and Right move between points carrying the guess on, Enter reveals and Escape clears.

props.name: series
props.description: The charts on offer, by key. Each is { title, caption?, unit?, decimals?, hide?, step?, points: { label, value }[] }; hide is how many of the latest points are hidden (a third by default).

props.name: dataset
props.description: Which of series is shown; the first key by default. Switching clears the guess.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The guess, one value per hidden point, oldest first, null where nothing is drawn yet. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the move, tap or key that changed the guess (while drawing, once a point moves by half a step), and from the reset.

props.name: onReveal
props.description: Fires when the real line has finished drawing in, with the score from 0 to 100 and both sets of values.

props.name: smoothing
props.description: 0 to 1: how much the pen is steadied and the guess rounded into a curve. 0 is a raw pen and a straight polyline.

props.name: reveal
props.description: How long the real line takes to sweep in, in ms.

props.name: score
props.description: Show and announce the score. Off, the gap still shades, without a number.

props.name: height
props.description: The plot's height in px; the chart fills the available width.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a pencil scratch that follows the pen, a tick per keyboard step, and the reveal: a swish and then a hum whose pitch follows the real line under the sweep. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the chart and blocks drawing and keys.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: Each hidden point is a role="slider" on the plot with one tab stop for the set: Up and Down change the guess by one step (Page Up and Page Down by five), Left and Right move between points and moving right onto an empty point carries the guess on, Home and End jump, Enter reveals the real line with the same sweep and sound, and Escape clears the guess. Values read as "52k", "not guessed yet", or after the reveal "guessed 52k, actual 61k"; the reveal and the score are announced in a polite live region.

Under reduced motion the pen still draws, but the real line and the shaded gap fade in rather than sweep, the score appears without rolling, and the hum that follows the sweep is left out; the swish, the guess, the score and every callback are unchanged.

The plot is one SVG stretched to the width with non-scaling strokes, so it reads the same at 320px and 720px; the reveal is a clip rectangle, never a dash offset. A new press on the plot, the Guess again button or Escape starts over.

items.title: Loop Lift
items.tagline: Circle it to lift it out.
items.description: Draw a loop around part of a picture and the loop closes and smooths on one glide spring — the gap between the pen's end and its start grows shut while the wobble relaxes through a Fourier low-pass — then exactly that part lifts out: a copy of the picture clipped by the loop rises on the snap spring with a geometric glow, a shadow and a caption naming what it caught, while the rest dims. Escape, a tap or a new loop drops it back on glide. The things in the picture are a listbox: the arrow keys walk them, and Enter draws the loop around the chosen one with the same marker squeak, close and lift.

props.name: children
props.description: The picture. It is drawn twice: once as itself, and once as the lifted copy, which is aria-hidden and inert.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the list of things in the picture.

props.name: regions
props.type: { id: string; label: string; x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }[]
props.description: The things in the picture, as fractions (0 to 1) of its box: what a loop can catch, what the caption names and what the keyboard walks.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.type: { points: [number, number][]; regions: string[]; area: number } | null
props.description: The lifted selection: the closed, smoothed loop as fractions of the picture, the ids of the regions it encloses, and the enclosed share of the picture. null when nothing is lifted.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the loop, tap or key that changed the selection. Controlled, the piece lifts when the value comes back; a refused selection's outline fades.

props.name: smoothing
props.description: How much the loop relaxes when it closes, 0 to 1: the harmonics kept run from 14 (every wobble of the hand survives) down to 1 (an ellipse).

props.name: lift
props.description: How high the lifted piece rises, in px, 0 to 24: its offset, its scale and how far its shadow falls. 0 is a flat highlight.

props.name: glow
props.description: Strength and reach of the halo around the lifted piece, 0 to 1, drawn as layered strokes of the loop rather than a blur.

props.name: dim
props.description: How dark the rest of the picture goes while a piece is lifted, 0 to 0.8.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the marker's squeak (following the pen's speed), the tick as the loop closes, the lift's shimmer (higher for a smaller piece) and the drop. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Blocks drawing and takes the things in the picture out of the tab order.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the frame's classes.

usageNotes: The regions are a listbox with roving focus: the arrow keys and Home and End move between them, each one's focus ring outlines it, Enter or Space draws the loop around it (the same close, lift and sounds as a drawn loop) or drops it if it is already lifted, and Escape drops whatever is lifted — Escape is only claimed when there is something to drop.

Under reduced motion the stroke still follows the pen, the loop snaps to its smoothed shape without the morph, and the piece is picked out by outline, glow and dim alone, with no rise, scale or shadow; the caption and the announcement are unchanged.

Because the picture is rendered twice, avoid ids inside it (an SVG gradient with an id would be duplicated); the lifted copy is clipped with a polygon, so any picture that lays out the same at the same width works.
A polite status line speaks what was lifted and how much of the picture it is, and when it is dropped.

items.title: Measure Line
items.tagline: Drag across; it reads the distance.
items.description: A plan you measure by dragging: the finger draws a dimension line with end bars, a ruler of ticks and a live length label in real units that stays upright at any angle, hopping over the line on the snap spring when it swings through vertical. The end follows 1:1, catches corners and the ends of other lines, rubber-bands past the sheet and springs back on snap with the release velocity, and every tick the length crosses ratchets. The keyboard walks a cursor corner to corner, Enter anchors a line, the arrows carry its end on the flick spring with the same ratchet, and after any line the arrows adjust its last point.

props.name: width
props.description: The sheet's width in drawing units (millimetres on paper, say). Lines and corners are in these units.

props.name: height
props.description: The sheet's height in drawing units.

props.name: children
props.description: The plan: SVG elements in drawing units, drawn over a scale grid and under the lines.

props.name: corners
props.description: Points the ends snap to — wall corners, door jambs — in drawing units. The ends of lines already drawn are snap points too.

props.name: label
props.description: The plan's accessible name.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.type: { id: string; a: [number, number]; b: [number, number] }[]
props.description: The lines, each from a to b in drawing units.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, key or tap that changed the lines. Controlled, a refused change puts the live end back where the host says it is.

props.name: units
props.description: How lengths read ("3.42 m", "342 cm", "11′ 3″"), and the spacing of the ticks and the grid.

props.name: snap
props.description: Ends catch corners and the ends of other lines within 14px, with a catch ring and a snap; the keyboard cursor jumps corner to corner.

props.name: scale
props.description: The drawing's scale, 1:n: one drawing unit is n real ones. The same line reads longer at 1:100, and ticks and grid re-space.

props.name: keep
props.description: Keep every line (six at most, the oldest goes first), or let each new line replace the last.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the ratchet (a detent per tick crossed, rising with the length, louder on long ticks) and the snap as an end catches. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Blocks drawing and removing, and takes the plan out of the tab order.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the wrapper's classes.

usageNotes: The plan is a focusable application: the arrow keys walk a cursor between corners (or one tick at a time, Shift for a long tick), Enter anchors a line and the arrows carry its end, Enter finishes and the next Enter starts from there; after any line, drawn or typed, the arrows adjust its last point. Escape stops adjusting or discards an empty line and is only claimed then; Backspace removes the newest line. A tap on a kept line's label removes that line.

Under reduced motion drawing stays 1:1, and the label's hop, the snap ring's pop, the spring back from past the edge and keyboard moves become jumps; the ratchet and snap sounds and every number are unchanged.
A polite status line speaks each line's length as it is drawn or adjusted and each removal, and the lines are also listed for assistive technology outside the drawing surface.
formatMeasure(mm, units) and measureLength(line, scale) are exported so a host can print totals in the same format.

items.title: Scratch Card
items.tagline: Scratch it; see what's under.
items.description: A reward under scratch-off foil: the pointer scrapes the foil away with a ragged brush while flakes of the foil that actually came off tumble and fall, and the scrape's sound follows the brush's speed. Once enough is cleared a glint crosses the card, the rest of the foil crumbles behind its front, and the reward settles on the recoil spring with a chime. The foil is a canvas that reads its colours from its own computed style and repaints when the theme changes; before the reveal it is a real button, and Enter or Space sweeps the same brush across the card with the same sound.

props.name: children
props.description: The reward under the foil. It is inert and hidden from assistive technology until revealed, so it cannot be read or tabbed to through the foil.

props.name: label
props.description: What is under the foil, e.g. "Weekly reward". The foil button is named "Scratch to reveal: {label}" and the revealed reward is a group with this name.

props.name: revealed / defaultRevealed
props.description: Whether the foil is gone. Setting it back to false lays fresh foil over the reward before the next frame is painted.

props.name: onRevealedChange
props.description: Fires with true from the scratch or sweep that cleared enough foil. Controlled, the foil dissolves when the host answers.

props.name: onProgress
props.description: The share of foil cleared, 0 to 1 (two decimals), each time it moves by a whole percent.

props.name: brush
props.description: Brush radius in px, 10 to 34: a wider brush clears more per stroke and throws more flakes.

props.name: autoReveal
props.description: The percentage cleared, 40 to 80, at which the rest of the foil dissolves by itself.

props.name: flakes
props.description: Flakes of the foil that comes off tumble and fall out of the card. The frame loop runs only while flakes are falling, on screen, in a visible page.

props.name: foil
props.description: The foil's colours, mixed from the theme's ink or warning hue, and the chime's pitch (gold rings a fourth higher).

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the scrape (noise whose pitch and level follow the brush's speed), a paper crinkle for a single dab, and the reveal's chime and shimmer. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the foil button: nothing scratches.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the card's classes.

usageNotes: Before the reveal the foil is a native button: Space or Enter, or a click from assistive technology, sweeps the brush across the card in rows with the same scrape, flakes and reveal. Once revealed the button leaves, the reward becomes reachable, focus that was on the foil moves to the reward, and a polite status line says it was revealed.

Under reduced motion scratching still works, but there are no flakes, no glint and no settle: at the threshold the rest of the foil fades on a short tween, the keyboard reveals at once, and the chime still plays.

The foil paints on a canvas at the device pixel ratio capped at 2, with its colours read from the canvas's own computed style, so it follows a light or dark stage; the scratches are replayed after a resize or a theme change, and coverage is counted on a coarse grid rather than by reading pixels back.
The card clips to its rounded box; give the reward its own size (an aspect ratio or a height), since the foil covers exactly what the children lay out.

items.title: Jog Shuttle
items.tagline: Turn to step; twist the ring to fly.
items.description: An edit deck's transport control: a jog wheel that turns 1:1 under the finger and steps the playhead one frame per detent, inside a spring-loaded shuttle ring whose twist sets a speed that doubles zone by zone up to shuttleMax. Let go spinning, the wheel is a flywheel: its landing is projected from the release spin, snapped to a detent and reached on a critically damped spring with the same time constant, so it slows exponentially and stops on a detent, stepping and ticking as it goes; let go of the ring and the playhead stops while the ring swings home on the return spring with the release's spin. Arrows jog a frame (Shift ten, PageUp and PageDown a second) by turning the wheel through the same detents, and J, K and L shuttle reverse, stop and forward, faster each press, with the ring twisting and holding to show it.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The playhead, in frames. Controlled or uncontrolled; a frame the host refuses is not where the next step starts.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the jog detent, the shuttle frame or the key that moved the playhead.

props.name: onSpeedChange
props.description: Fires when the shuttle speed changes, from the twist or key that changed it: signed (negative in reverse), 0 when stopped.

props.name: min
props.description: The first frame.

props.name: max
props.description: The last frame.

props.name: fps
props.description: Frames per second: the timecode, how far PageUp and PageDown jump, and the shuttle's rate (a 4× shuttle runs 4 × fps frames a second).

props.name: label
props.description: What is being scrubbed: the control's accessible name, shown over the timecode.

props.name: detents
props.description: Detents per revolution of the jog wheel, 12 to 48. One detent is one frame, so fewer detents are further apart under the finger.

props.name: inertia
props.description: How far the jog wheel coasts when let go spinning, 0 to 1: at 0 it stops dead in the nearest detent, at 1 it runs on like a heavy flywheel.

props.name: shuttleMax
props.description: The shuttle's top speed. The ring's travel is split into zones that double from 1× up to it (16 gives 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16×), marked on the collar.

props.name: spring
props.description: The ring's return spring, 0 to 1: soft swings past centre and back, firm goes straight home. Key twists move the ring on the same spring.

props.name: sound
props.description: A detent tick per frame jogged (a clack at either end), a click as the ring enters each zone, and a whir while shuttling whose pitch rises with the speed. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the control, stops any shuttle, takes both parts out of the tab order and ignores drags and keys.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: The root is a group named by the label holding two sliders. Jog: ArrowRight/ArrowUp a frame forward, ArrowLeft/ArrowDown back, Shift for ten, PageUp/PageDown a second, Home and End to the first and last frame, its value text a sentence ("1 minute 12 seconds and 5 frames, frame 1733"). Shuttle: arrows one zone toward forward or reverse, Home and End to full reverse and full forward. On both, L shuttles forward and J in reverse (again: faster), K stops and Space toggles, with the ring twisting and holding at that zone.

Under reduced motion the wheel and ring still follow the finger 1:1, but a released wheel settles in its detent at once with no coast, key jogs jump the wheel in one step, and the ring snaps home; the playhead still shuttles and the readout, collar arc and sounds still answer.

The shuttle's frame loop exists only while the speed is not zero, stops when the page is hidden, and stops at either end of the clip. Turning the jog wheel cancels a shuttle first. Both parts are touch-none, since a rotary drag is two-dimensional.

items.title: Thumb Wheel
items.tagline: Roll the edge to set it.
items.description: A value set by rolling a knurled wheel seen edge-on in a slot: the knurl scrolls 1:1 under the finger, its ridges bunching toward the top and bottom as the cylinder turns away, while the value sits beside it level with a fixed notch and a gauge shows where the wheel is between its stops. Rolled past a stop it rubber-bands; flicked, its landing is projected at a rate set by friction, snapped to a step when detents are on, and reached on a critically damped spring with that time constant, so it slows exponentially and stops on the step, while a throw past a stop hits it on the snap spring. Arrows step, PageUp and PageDown move ten steps and Home and End go to the stops, rolling the wheel there through the same fine ratchet; the scroll wheel rolls it as it would scroll content.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The value the wheel is set to. Controlled or uncontrolled; a value the host refuses rolls back.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the roll, flick, scroll, tap or key that changed it: per step while rolling, and once with the value it lands on.

props.name: min
props.description: The bottom stop.

props.name: max
props.description: The top stop.

props.name: step
props.description: One detent's worth of value, and what a key or a tap moves it by.

props.name: label
props.description: What the wheel sets: the slider's accessible name, shown over the value.

props.name: unit
props.description: Printed after the value and read in its value text, as in "%" or "dB".

props.name: knurl
props.description: The pattern cut in the wheel's edge: fine straight ridges, coarse ones twice as far apart, or a diamond crosshatch drawn as the two helices a real knurl leaves.

props.name: friction
props.description: How soon a flicked wheel stops, 0 to 1: at 0 it coasts a long way, at 1 it stops almost at once.

props.name: detents
props.description: Click and settle on whole steps. Off, the wheel rolls freely and stops wherever it coasts, and the value shows one more decimal; keys and taps still land on whole steps.

props.name: range
props.description: How far the wheel turns from one stop to the other, in turns, 0.5 to 3: short is quick and coarse, long is slow and fine. The gauge shows one mark per quarter turn.

props.name: sound
props.description: A fine ratchet tick per step as the wheel rolls (per ridge, softer, with detents off), rising with the value, and a clack when it meets a stop. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the wheel, takes it out of the tab order and ignores drags, scrolls and keys.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: The housing is a vertical role="slider" named by its label, with the value and unit in aria-valuetext ("60%"): ArrowUp/ArrowRight one step up, ArrowDown/ArrowLeft one down, PageUp/PageDown ten steps, Home and End to the stops. The wheel rolls there and ratchets past every step, as a drag would. A tap above the notch steps up, below it steps down.

Under reduced motion the wheel still follows the finger 1:1, but every settle, flick, scroll and key jumps straight to its value with no coast or spring, while the reading, the gauge and the ratchet still answer.

The scroll wheel is claimed only while the wheel can still move that way, so a scroll that reaches a stop carries on to the page. The drag is touch-pan-x, so a horizontal swipe over the wheel still pans. The reading reserves the width of its widest value, so rolling from 99 to 100 never moves the layout.

items.title: Rotary Dial
items.tagline: Drag to the stop; it winds back.
items.description: A number input drawn as a telephone rotary dial: put a finger in a hole and drag it clockwise to the finger stop, and the wheel turns 1:1 with the pointer, ratcheting as it winds and giving only a few degrees at rest and at the stop. Let go at the stop and it winds back at the constant speed a governor holds, a linear run at returnSpeed pulses a second rather than a spring, ticking once per pulse while the next slot counts them up; it knocks against its rest stop on a stiff, loose spring and the digit lands with a flick. The holes are real buttons in one tab stop: arrows move round the dial, Enter or Space dials the focused hole, number keys dial directly (queued while it is busy), Backspace removes a digit and Escape clears.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The number dialled so far, digits only; anything longer than digits is cut. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the whole number when a digit lands, on Backspace and on clear.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Fires when the digit that fills the last slot lands.

props.name: label
props.description: What is being dialled: the dial's accessible name.

props.name: returnSpeed
props.description: How fast the wheel winds back, in pulses per second (30° each), 6 to 20: the pace of the pulse ticks and of the counting slot.

props.name: finish
props.description: A glossy black wheel over a cream plate with black digits, or a spun-metal wheel over a black plate with white digits. Physical colours mixed from black, white and the theme's ink, so the dial reads the same on a light or dark page.

props.name: digits
props.description: How many digits the number has, 3 to 10: the slot count. When every slot is full the holes stop engaging and number keys are ignored.

props.name: display
props.description: Show the number above the dial in slots, with a clear button and a polite live region. Off, only the dial renders and the host shows and announces the number.

props.name: sound
props.description: A ratchet tick every 10° as the wheel winds, rising as it goes, a clack at the finger stop, a tick per pulse on the way back and a knock when it comes to rest. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the dial, disables its holes and the clear button, and ignores drags and keys.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: The dial is a group named by its label; its ten holes are buttons named by their digit in one tab stop. ArrowRight/ArrowDown move to the next hole round the dial, ArrowLeft/ArrowUp back, Home to 1 and End to 0; Enter or Space dials the focused hole and number keys dial directly, with the same wind, pulses and sounds as a finger. Backspace removes the last digit, Escape clears the number (and is left alone when there is nothing to clear).

Under reduced motion a finger still turns the wheel 1:1, but a released, tapped or typed wheel is shown at rest at once while the governed return runs unseen, so the pulses still tick, the slot still counts up and the digit lands on the same beat.

Releasing short of the stop winds the wheel back silently and dials nothing. Digits typed while the wheel is busy queue, up to the free slots, and dial in turn. The live region speaks the number the host accepted: "5 5 5 0, 4 of 7 digits."

items.title: Straighten Dial
items.tagline: Level the horizon.
items.description: A photo editor's straighten control: a degree ruler under the picture scrolls 1:1 under the finger and turns the picture about its centre, while a thirds grid fades in for as long as it turns and the crop scales, frame by frame from the same angle, just enough to keep the corners covered. Zero is magnetic: the ruler holds at exactly 0 inside the magnet and catches up at double rate beyond it, the ends rubber-band, and a flick coasts to its projected landing on a critically damped spring while a slow release stays put; rubber-banded releases and keys move on the glide spring. Arrows turn a degree (Shift a tenth), PageUp and PageDown five, Home and End to the ends, with the same ticks and the same snap at zero.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The rotation in degrees, clockwise positive, in tenths. Controlled or uncontrolled; a value the host refuses is turned back to once the finger lets go.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, key, throw or reset that turned the picture, with the new rotation.

props.name: children
props.description: The picture to straighten. It fills the frame and turns inside it.

props.name: aspect
props.description: The frame's width over its height. The crop scale is worked out from it.

props.name: label
props.description: The ruler's accessible name, shown left of the reading.

props.name: range
props.description: How far it turns either way. The 15° ruler is also the finer one: 12 px a degree against 6, labelled every 5° rather than every 15°.

props.name: grid
props.description: Fade a thirds grid over the picture while it turns, and away again once it stops.

props.name: magnet
props.description: How wide the sticky zone around zero is, 0 to 3 degrees, drawn on the ruler. Inside it the ruler holds at exactly 0; 0 makes zero an ordinary degree.

props.name: crop
props.description: Scale the picture by the least amount that keeps the frame covered as it turns. Off, it turns at its own size and the empty corners show a checkerboard.

props.name: sound
props.description: A fine tick as each degree passes the needle, pitched up the further it is from level, and a snap as zero does. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the control, takes the ruler out of the tab order and ignores drags, keys and the reset.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root's classes.

usageNotes: The ruler is a slider named by the label, its value text a sentence ("3.4 degrees clockwise", "Level"). ArrowRight/ArrowUp turn a degree clockwise, ArrowLeft/ArrowDown back, Shift+Arrow a tenth, PageUp/PageDown five, Home and End to the ends; keys chain from where the last one aimed and are caught by the magnet only on the way in, so they can always step back out. A Reset button turns back to level the same way.

Under reduced motion the ruler and picture still follow the finger 1:1 and the crop still scales with the angle, but releases, keys and the reset land at once with no coast or spring; the grid still fades in and out.
The ruler is touch-pan-y, so the page still scrolls vertically over it. The picture and the ruler strip are both clipped to the component's own box however far it turns.

items.title: Vinyl Scrub
items.tagline: Spin the record to scrub the track.
items.description: A turntable as a track's playhead: at 33⅓ the platter turns 200° a second and one second of the track is exactly that much groove, so while it plays the record spins and the time runs, and turned by hand the time follows the hand, backwards too, with a scratch whose pitch follows the hand's speed. A finger brakes the record under it as hard as grip says, a drag turns it 1:1 about the spindle, and a release keeps the hand's spin while the motor pulls it back to speed on a time constant set by inertia, with a whir; the tonearm's stylus is solved onto the groove for the time and glides to a new groove on the glide spring after a needle drop. An arrow key is a hand on the record, holding it and scrubbing a second of groove per press on the glide spring, and letting go on key-up.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The playhead in seconds, in tenths. Controlled or uncontrolled; a time the host sets by itself is a needle drop.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the play clock, the scrub or the key that moved the playhead, at tenth-of-a-second steps.

props.name: duration
props.description: The track's length in seconds. The stylus runs from the outer groove at 0 to the inner one here.

props.name: playing / defaultPlaying
props.description: Whether the motor is on. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onPlayingChange
props.description: Fires from start/stop, Space or K, and when the track runs out.

props.name: onScrubChange
props.description: True while a hand, or a held arrow key, is on the record; false when it lets go. Pause real audio output while it is true.

props.name: label
props.description: What is on the deck. The control's accessible name.

props.name: rpm
