Choosing turns the ring the short way on snap so the chosen key hangs at the front, a click ticking as each key passes; the keys are pendulums that trail the ring, swing and knock when it stops with a damping set by jingle, and a new workspace threads on at the split and slides round to its place on glide. The ring is a focusable listbox: arrow keys turn it and choose, Home and End go to the ends, a letter turns to the next workspace with that initial, and a horizontal drag spins it 1:1 and settles on the key the throw was heading for.

props.name: workspaces
props.type: { id: string; name: string; detail?: string; initial?: string; color?: string }[]
props.description: The workspaces, one key each. detail is the second line under the chosen name; color is any CSS colour for the bow, one of six pigments by default.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The chosen workspace's id, whose key hangs at the front.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the key, click or drag that chose a workspace, with its id. A controlled ring that is refused turns back.

props.name: onAdd
props.description: Shows an Add button at the ring's split end. A workspace the host then adds threads onto the ring there.

props.name: addLabel
props.description: The Add button's accessible name.

props.name: label
props.description: The listbox's accessible name.

props.name: keys
props.description: How many keys hang on the ring at once, 3 to 7. With more workspaces the ring turns through all of them, a key re-cut for the next one as it passes behind.

props.name: ring
props.description: The metal of the ring and the blades, drawn as fixed pigments so both themes read the same.

props.name: jingle
props.description: How freely the keys swing and knock when the ring turns, 0 (stiff and silent) to 1.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a click as keys pass the front and when a key is threaded, and a clack when keys knock, only after the visitor's own turn.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The ring cannot be turned and Add is off.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root: a 272 px drawing over the chosen name.

usageNotes: A focusable listbox with one option per workspace and aria-activedescendant on the chosen one: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight (or Up and Down) turn the ring one key and choose, Home and End go to the first and last workspace, and a letter turns to the next workspace with that initial. Pointer and drag choices are said once in a polite live region.

Under reduced motion the ring does not turn and nothing swings: keys fade into their new places, a threaded key fades in where it hangs, and the chosen key is still the front one. A drag still turns the ring under the finger.
The swing runs on a small frame loop only while the ring moves or a key still swings, and stops on a hidden page.

items.title: Blind Menu
items.tagline: Opens slat by slat.
items.description: An account menu that hangs from its button like a window blind. Opened, the frame lowers to its length on glide while each slat, one item each, turns from nearly edge-on to face you on snap from the top down, stagger apart; the slat under the pointer or the focus leans toward you and catches the light, and closing draws the blind back up, slats turning shut from the bottom and rising into a stack under the headrail on exit tweens. It is the menu-button pattern: arrows move and wrap, Home and End jump, typing jumps to an item, Enter or Space chooses, and Escape closes and hands focus back to the trigger.

props.name: items
props.type: { id: string; label: string; icon?: ReactNode; shortcut?: string; tone?: "default" | "danger"; disabled?: boolean }[]
props.description: The menu, one slat per item. A danger item is drawn in the danger colour; a disabled one is skipped by the arrows.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: An item was chosen. Fires before the blind goes up.

props.name: label
props.description: The account's name: the trigger's text and the menu's name.

props.name: detail
props.description: A second line under the name: an email, a plan, a role.

props.name: avatar
props.description: Before the name, 28 px. Defaults to the name's initials in a circle.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the blind is down.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the press, key or outside press that opened or closed it.

props.name: slats
props.description: The most slats the blind lowers, 4 to 8. A longer menu scrolls inside it a slat at a time, with a mark on the bottom rail while there is more.

props.name: stagger
props.description: How far apart the slats turn open, 0 (all at once) to 1 (a slow wave), kept inside the 600 ms budget.

props.name: finish
props.description: What the slats are made of: grained wood and curved aluminium are fixed pigments; fabric is woven from the menu's own surface colours.

props.name: align
props.description: Which edge of the trigger the blind hangs from.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a swish when the visitor lowers or raises the blind (pitched down going up) and a click when an item is chosen.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The trigger cannot be pressed.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, which wraps the trigger; the blind hangs below it.

usageNotes: The trigger has aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded and aria-controls; Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens with focus on the first item and ArrowUp on the last. Inside the menu of menuitems with a roving tabindex, arrows move and wrap, Home and End jump, typed letters jump, Enter or Space chooses, Escape closes with preventDefault and returns focus to the trigger, and Tab or a press outside closes it.
Under reduced motion the blind fades in and out without lowering or turning, and a hovered or focused slat changes shade instead of leaning.
Focus moves into the menu when its node arrives, and only when the visitor opened it: a host that opens it does not steal focus.

items.title: Jukebox Menu
items.tagline: Pick a record.
items.description: A single-choice picker dressed as a jukebox: the catalogue sits on title strips in a book-style rack whose leaves turn about the spine on glide, riffling a leaf at a time across several pages, and every record has a letter-and-number code. A pick sends the changer arm round the fan of edge-on records on glide while its motor whirs, reaches in and grips the record, pulls it down to the spindle as it turns from edge-on to lying flat, and drops it on the platter on recoil before the tonearm swings on with snap. Under the chrome it is a listbox: arrows walk the strips and turn pages at the ends, Page keys turn a spread, a page letter and a strip number pick by code, and Enter picks the active strip.

props.name: records
props.type: { id: string; title: string; artist?: string }[]
props.description: The catalogue, in rack order. Each record gets a code from its page letter and strip number.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The id of the record on the turntable, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the strip, key or code that picked a record, with its id.

props.name: label
props.description: The listbox's accessible name.

props.name: pages
props.description: How many pages the rack splits the catalogue across, 2 to 4; a page holds up to eight strips, and a longer catalogue adds pages.

props.name: finish
props.description: The cabinet's trim, rack frame and key tops, as pigments that read the same in both themes.

props.name: arm
props.description: A changer arm fetches each record; off, the record rises from its slot and travels to the turntable by itself.

props.name: sound
props.description: Clack for keys, strips and landings, and a whir while the arm travels. Only for the visitor's own picks and keys.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The rack and keys can be read but not used.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the cabinet, which is w-full up to 360px.

usageNotes: The rack is a listbox with aria-activedescendant: ArrowUp and ArrowDown step through the strips and turn the page at either end, ArrowLeft and ArrowRight cross the spine, PageUp and PageDown turn a spread, Home and End jump, Enter or Space picks. Typing a page letter turns to that spread and waits; a digit then picks that strip. Escape clears a waiting letter. The selector keys are a toolbar with one tab stop.

Under reduced motion nothing travels, turns or spins: the rack cross-fades between pages and the record appears on the platter, while the readout, the lit strip and the spoken 'Now playing' still change.
Use jukeboxCodes(records, pages) to show the same codes elsewhere. The label turns only while the jukebox is on screen and the page is visible; a host changing value animates the arm silently.

items.title: View Morph
items.tagline: Grid, list, board — the items move themselves.
items.description: A collection with a switch for its layout: choosing Grid, List or Board re-lays every entry, and each one travels to its new place on the glide spring through motion's shared layout while its cover grows into a tile, shrinks to a thumbnail or thins to a colour strip, the details only one view has fading in and out and the measured height gliding with them. The switch is a radiogroup whose thumb slides on snap, and the chosen view's glyph starts as the view being left and morphs its six bars into its own shape on the same spring. Arrow keys move and choose a view, Home and End jump, and each entry is a button when onOpen is given.

props.name: collection
props.type: { id: string; title: string; meta?: string; status?: string; tone?: "accent" | "signal" | "warn" | "danger" | "success" | "ink" }[]
props.description: The entries. meta is the second line, status the board column's id, tone the cover's colour.

props.name: columns
props.description: The board's columns, in order. Defaults to the statuses in order of appearance.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The view, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that chose a view.

props.name: label
props.description: The collection's heading and the name of its list and view switch.

props.name: stagger
props.description: How far apart the entries set off, 0 (all at once) to 1 (a ripple inside the 600ms budget).

props.name: items
props.description: How many entries of the collection show; the header counts them against the whole. Defaults to all.

props.name: views
props.description: Offer grid and list, or grid, list and board.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: The most the collection grows to, in px; past it, it scrolls with a fade at the bottom edge.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: An entry was opened. When given, every entry is a button named by its title, meta and status.

props.name: sound
props.description: A click for the switch and a swish as the entries move, only when the visitor chose the view.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The switch and the entries cannot be used.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, a container-query box that fills its width.

usageNotes: The switch is a radiogroup with one tab stop: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight (or Up and Down) move and choose, Home and End jump, and each radio is named by its view; labels beside the glyphs hide below 26rem and stay for assistive technology. A polite status says the new view and how many entries show.

Under reduced motion the entries do not travel and the glyph does not morph: the collection fades up in its new layout and the height changes at once, while the chosen view and the announcement still change.
Every entry stays one element across the three views, so focus on an entry survives a change of view; the list takes two columns above 34rem.

items.title: Pocket Nav
items.tagline: What doesn't fit tucks away.
items.description: A navigation bar that never wraps or scrolls: a ResizeObserver reads its room and every link's natural width, and the links that no longer fit slide along the bar into a pocket at its end on the exit ease, shrinking as they go, in priority order and a cascade apart, while the links behind them close the gap on glide. The pocket takes each one with a squeeze on snap as its count rolls, links slide back out on snap as room returns, and the current page is never tucked. The bar is one tab stop whose arrows move between links and the pocket; the pocket is a menu button whose menu of tucked links opens on ArrowDown, Enter or Space, moves with arrows, Home, End and first letters, and closes on Escape or Tab with focus back on the pocket.

props.name: links
props.type: { id: string; label: string; href?: string; usage?: number }[]
props.description: The links, in bar order. With href a link is an anchor; usage ranks it for priority="usage".

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The current link's id, controlled or initial. It carries aria-current="page" and is never tucked.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press, key or menu choice that made a link current.

props.name: onPocketChange
props.description: The links in the pocket, in bar order: once measured, then each time the set changes.

props.name: label
props.description: The navigation's accessible name.

props.name: items
props.description: The most links the bar shows at once, 4 to 9; the rest wait in the pocket even with room to spare. Defaults to all.

props.name: priority
props.description: Tuck from the end of the bar backwards, or the least used links first wherever they sit.

props.name: pocket
props.description: A More button with a count and chevron, or a round three-dot button with a count dot.

props.name: sound
props.description: A swish for each link that slides into or out of the pocket and a tick as its count moves, only while the visitor is dragging or pressing keys; a swish when the pocket opens.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The links and the pocket can be read but not used.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the nav, which fills its width.

usageNotes: The bar is one tab stop with a roving tabindex over its links and the pocket: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move, Home and End jump, Enter or Space follows a link. On the pocket, ArrowDown, Enter or Space open the menu on its first item and ArrowUp on its last; in the menu, arrows, Home, End and first letters move, Enter chooses, and Escape or Tab close it with preventDefault and hand focus back. A press outside closes it; a chosen link takes focus once it has arrived in the bar.
Under reduced motion links fade out and in where they stand, the gap closes at once and the pocket does not squeeze, while its count and the announcement still change.

Widths come from a clipped, zero-height measuring row, so late-loading fonts re-measure and nothing hidden adds scroll width. The first fit after measuring is instant and silent; when even the current link and the pocket cannot fit, the current link's label truncates.

items.title: Liquid Tab Bar
items.tagline: The indicator flows between tabs.
items.description: A bottom tab bar whose indicator is a drop of liquid behind the chosen icon: choosing a tab sends the drop's head racing there on a spring that keeps its velocity while the tail holds back on a softer, later spring, and the neck between them is drawn every frame as a metaball bridge that thins as it stretches and pinches off when stretched too far. The head squashes along its speed and lands with a jiggle whose size is set by the viscosity, and the icon it lands on bounces on recoil; the icons are drawn a second time in the tint's contrast colour, clipped to the drop's live shape. The drop can be dragged 1:1 and thrown to a tab, and the tablist's arrows move and choose, Home and End jump.

props.name: items
props.description: The tabs, in order, each with a label and a built-in glyph.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The chosen tab's id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the tap, drag or key that chose a tab.

props.name: label
props.description: The tablist's accessible name.

props.name: panelId
props.description: The id of the panel the tabs control, for aria-controls.

props.name: viscosity
props.description: Runny (0) to thick (1): quick and splashy with a short neck and more jiggle, or slow and composed with a neck that stretches much further before it pinches.

props.name: tabs
props.description: How many of items the bar holds, 3 to 5. Defaults to all, up to 5.

props.name: tint
props.description: The drop's colour and the contrast colour of the icon it covers; accent and signal are fixed pigments, ink follows the theme.

props.name: sound
props.description: A blup when the drop lands on a tab the visitor chose, pitched by the tab and the viscosity.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The tabs and the drag cannot be used.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, which is w-full up to max-w-md.

usageNotes: It is a tablist with one tab stop: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move and choose (wrapping), Home and End jump, Enter and Space choose the focused tab. Dragging the drop along the bar follows the finger, rubber-bands past either end, and a release commits to the tab the throw was heading for; the bar uses touch-action pan-y so the page still scrolls.
Under reduced motion the drop moves in one piece on a short tween with no neck, squash or bounce; the tint and the tinted icon still move, because which tab is chosen is the information.
The drop is geometry, not a blur filter, so its edge stays crisp at any size; before the bar is measured (the server's render) a still drop sits on the chosen tab.

items.title: Ink Bleed
items.tagline: Words soak in, then dry.
items.description: A status line written in ink: each phrase soaks into the paper letter by letter on a seeded pen rhythm, landing as a drop on the baseline and wicking up through the glyph behind a feathered front, glossy while wet and drying to a lighter matte, and when it has rested a pad of blotting paper sweeps across and lifts it for the next phrase. Pressing the paper brings the blotter down under the pointer on springs.flick and dragging rubs it along 1:1, blotting every letter still wet under it lighter (and smeared when the pass was fast); the paper's height follows a wrapping phrase on springs.glide. The paper is a real button — Enter or Space runs the same pad along the whole line — and each phrase is announced once.

props.name: phrases
props.description: The status phrases, written one after another and cycled in order.

props.name: active
props.description: Writing. False lifts the line, writes doneText in dry ink and stops every loop.

props.name: doneText
props.description: What stays written once inactive. Defaults to the last phrase.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the pen, the drying, the rest and the blotter run, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: spread
props.description: How far the ink feathers into the paper, 0 (a crisp nib) to 1 (blotting paper): the soak front's softness, the halo, the drop and the smear.

props.name: paper
props.description: The stock and how ink behaves on it: plain is coated and dries slowly with a long gloss, laid is cream with laid and chain lines, kraft is brown and thirsty — fast, matte and feathered.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the blotter: a soft rustle as the pad comes down, a paper rustle for each letter it blots and a swish for the keyboard's pass or a flicked release. Writing and lifting are silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The line keeps writing but cannot be blotted.

props.name: onPhraseChange
props.description: A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; it is w-full by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the paper is a button — Enter or Space runs the blotter along the line and blots every letter still wet, the same end state as dragging it across. A lift already under way completes first.

Reduced motion: the whole phrase soaks in at once and keeps the reading time the pen would have given it, wet to dry is a colour change with no glint or drop, the lift is a fade and the keyboard blot dries the line in place; the dragged pad still follows the pointer and still lightens what it blots.
The phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root and is announced once per phrase; the clock runs only while the paper is on screen in a visible page.

items.title: Platen Print
items.tagline: Every letter struck by hand.
items.description: A status line printed by a platen press: a small head rides a rail over a strip of card stock, and for each letter its plunger falls with the letter, which squashes onto its baseline and springs back on springs.snap while the carriage steps on a stiff spring, every impression a little uneven in density, tilt and inking. A rested phrase is wiped to a ghost as the carriage returns on springs.glide and the next prints over it; hovering or focusing slows the press on springs.drift so each strike reads. The strip is a real button — a press, a tap, Enter or Space strikes the next letter by hand, and on a finished line sends the carriage home — and each phrase is announced once.

props.name: phrases
props.description: The status phrases, printed one after another and cycled in order.

props.name: active
props.description: Printing. False wipes the line, prints doneText and stops every timer.

props.name: doneText
props.description: What stays printed once inactive. Defaults to the last phrase.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the press strikes, rests and returns, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: pressure
props.description: How hard the platen strikes, 0 (a kiss) to 1 (a bite): the drop, the squash, ink squeezed at the edges, the deboss, how even the ink lies and the weight of the thock.

props.name: ink
props.description: The pigment on the letters and on the plunger's face.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the strikes the visitor makes: a thock at contact with the escapement's click, and a lower click for a carriage return asked for by hand. The press's own rhythm is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The line prints on its own but cannot be struck by hand.

props.name: onPhraseChange
props.description: A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; it is w-full by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the strip is a button — Enter or Space strikes the next letter (Enter held repeats), and on a finished line sends the carriage home, the same as a press or a tap. Focus slows the press the way hovering does.

Reduced motion: letters appear in place one at a time with their uneven ink (opacity only), the head stays parked at the rail's start, and the wipe is a fade to the ghost; hover still slows the rate and presses still strike.
The phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root and is announced once per phrase; the press's timer runs only while the strip is on screen in a visible page.

items.title: Neon Strike
items.tagline: A sign warming up, tube by tube.
items.description: A status line in bent neon tube on a dark sign board: each phrase warms up tube by tube in an uneven, seeded order, every tube trying once or twice, striking with a white flash and flickering on keyframed tweens before it settles to a steady glow, while the board takes on the colour as more of it lights and one faulty tube keeps a stutter. Lit phrases hold, power down on an exit tween and hand over to the next; given progress, the sign becomes a meter that lights the share of each phrase its band has reached, mostly left to right. The sign is a real button — the pointer near a tube makes it flicker, a press knocks the glass and sends a flicker outward, Left and Right walk a probe along the letters and Space or Enter knocks from it — and each phrase is announced once.

props.name: phrases
props.description: The status phrases, lit one after another and cycled in order.

props.name: active
props.description: Warming. False powers the sign down, lights doneText steady and stops every timer and the stutter.

props.name: doneText
props.description: What stays lit once inactive. Defaults to the last phrase.

props.name: progress
props.description: Determinate, 0 to 1: phrase i owns the band [i/n, (i+1)/n), and the share of its letters lit is the progress through that band; entering the next band powers the sign down and shows the next phrase.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast tubes strike, hold, power down and stutter, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: glow
props.description: How far the glow spills, 0 (bare tubes) to 1: the halo's layers and the wash the lit sign throws on its board.

props.name: colour
props.description: The gas in the tubes, as fixed pigments that read the same in both themes.

props.name: faulty
props.description: One seeded tube keeps a stutter while the sign runs.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play what the visitor causes: a buzz for a tube the pointer or the probe flickers, a click for a knock. Warming, the fault and power-downs are silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The sign keeps lighting but cannot be knocked or flickered.

props.name: onPhraseChange
props.description: A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; it is w-full by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the sign is a button — Left and Right move a probe along the letters (Home and End to the ends), flickering each one as the pointer would, with a tick under it while focus is visible; Space or Enter knocks the glass from the probe, as a press does.

Reduced motion: no flash, flicker or stutter — tubes light with a colour-and-glow fade in the same order, so the warm-up and the determinate share still show; power-down is a fade, the pointer's proximity does nothing and a knock is a gentle swell.

The phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root and is announced once per phrase; the timers run only while the sign is on screen in a visible page, and a beat's deadline survives progress updates so a fast-reporting host never starves it.

items.title: Crossword Guess
items.tagline: Pencilled in, then inked.
items.description: A status line solved into a crossword: each phrase fills a row of squares under its clue numbers while the next phrase waits below as empty squares. A drawn pencil writes the letters in graphite, a few of them near misses; once the row is pencilled it flips end over end on springs.snap, rubs each wrong guess out with crumbs falling, writes the right letter, and a pen then inks the row, the phrase is announced and the grid scrolls up a row on springs.glide, the tool following its targets on springs.flick. The pointer over a square lights its entry and the clue bar reads its number; pressing a square checks it — a wrong guess is rubbed out on the spot, a right one inked — and the keyboard does the same with a cursor square moved by the arrow keys.

props.name: phrases
props.description: The status phrases, solved into the grid one row each and cycled in order.

props.name: active
props.description: Solving. False finishes the row being solved briskly, then solves doneText with no wrong guesses and rests; nothing loops.

props.name: doneText
props.description: The row that stays once inactive. Defaults to the last phrase.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the solver works, 0.5 to 2: the pencil's rhythm, the rubs, the ink and the rest.

props.name: guesses
props.description: Wrong guesses pencilled into each phrase before they are rubbed out, 0 to 3 (never more than a third of its letters). Dealt as each row begins.

props.name: grid
props.description: How the grid is printed: news is cream squares, black blocks and black ink; pastel gives each entry its own tint with violet ink; ink is a night edition with indigo squares, silver pencil and cream ink.

props.name: progress
props.description: Determinate progress, 0 to 1. The phrases share it in equal bands, and within its band a row is pencilled, corrected and inked in step with it; entering the next band finishes the row and scrolls on.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the visitor's ticks as the pointer or cursor crosses squares and as a check inks a letter, and the scratch of a rub the visitor started. The solver's own work is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The grid keeps solving, but squares cannot be checked.

props.name: onPhraseChange
props.description: A row began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; it is w-full and sizes its squares from its own width.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the grid is a button. While it has focus a cursor square shows; Left and Right move it (blocks are skipped), Home and End jump to the ends, and Enter or Space checks it — a wrong guess is rubbed out, a right one inked, an empty one revealed — exactly as a press on that square does. A polite region reads the cursor square and the result of each check.

Reduced motion: no tool travels and nothing scrolls. A row is pencilled at once and keeps the reading time the pencil would have given it, corrections and the ink are cross-fades in place, rows swap by cross-fade, and hover, checks and the determinate fill all still work.
The phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root and is announced once, when its row is inked; the clock runs only while the grid is on screen in a visible page.

items.title: Sand Script
items.tagline: Written in sand, smoothed by a wave.
items.description: A status line written in sand on a canvas: a thin stream pours along the line and its grains fall and land in the letter shapes, the lowest first, so each letter heaps up in relief; when the phrase has rested, a wave runs up the beach with a foam lace, loosens every grain it reaches and drains back, leaving wet sand that dries as the next phrase pours. The pointer draws in the sand — a passing mouse leaves a shallow trail and a press digs a channel that pushes the grains aside, then refills — while the tray's height follows the type on springs.glide. The tray is a real button: Enter or Space draws the same finger through the words, and each phrase is announced once.

props.name: phrases
props.description: The status phrases, written in the sand one after another and cycled in order.

props.name: active
props.description: Writing. False finishes the pour briskly, sends the wave, writes doneText and stops; the canvas then rests as one still frame.

props.name: doneText
props.description: What stays written once inactive. Defaults to the last phrase.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the sand pours, rests and the wave runs, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: grain
props.description: Grain size in px, 1 (fine silt) to 3 (coarse): the grains, how densely the letters are sampled and the bed's speckle. Coarser grain sets larger type so a letter still reads.

props.name: tone
props.description: The beach: golden dune sand with a green-blue sea, grey volcanic ash glinting with mica under a slate sea, or pale pink coral sand with a turquoise sea.

props.name: progress
props.description: Determinate progress, 0 to 1. The phrases share it in equal bands; within its band the settled share of a phrase's grains follows it, and entering the next band sends the wave for the next phrase.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a swish when a pressed finger moves fast through the sand and when the keyboard's finger starts. The pour and the wave are silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The sand keeps being written, but cannot be drawn in.

props.name: onPhraseChange
props.description: A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; it is w-full and the tray is sized for the longest phrase at its width.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the tray is a button — Enter or Space draws a finger through the words along the line, the same channel a drag digs, and it refills the same way.

Reduced motion: no stream, falling grains or travelling water. A phrase fades in whole and keeps the reading time the pour would have given it, the wave becomes the old phrase fading while the sand darkens and dries, and trails still draw under the pointer and refill as a fade without pushing grains.

The phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root and is announced once, as it starts to be written. The canvas (device pixel ratio capped at 2) draws only while something moves and only on screen in a visible page.

items.title: Redline Draft
items.tagline: Drafted, struck through, rewritten.
items.description: A status line with an editor at work: each phrase arrives as a rough draft typed in behind a text cursor, then a pen nib, following its marks on springs.flick, strikes weak words through with a swept clip, writes better ones above over a caret, puts a missing word in and curls a filler out. Then the clean version slides into place on springs.glide — struck words and marks fade where they are, kept words glide to their new spots and each written word comes down from above the line as its ink turns to text — and the clean phrase is announced once. The visitor edits too: a drag strikes words under the pointer and a tap or Enter strikes one; a weak word struck is taken and rewritten at once, a good one is marked stet; arrow keys choose the word.

props.name: phrases
props.description: The status phrases, each drafted, marked up and set clean, cycled in order.

props.name: drafts
props.description: The rough draft each phrase starts as, index for index; a word diff finds the edits. Without it a draft is made from the phrase (weaker word choices, a small word left out, a filler to strike), seeded so the same phrase always gets the same draft.

props.name: active
props.description: Editing. False sets doneText clean in place of the draft and stops; nothing loops.

props.name: doneText
props.description: What stays once inactive. Defaults to the last phrase.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the draft is typed, marked up and rested, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: ink
props.description: The editor's pen: the danger, accent or success text colour, so every mark reads in both themes.

props.name: marks
props.description: How rough a made draft is: one or two edits, or three or four. Applies from the next phrase; drafts given in drafts are used as they are.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the scratch of the visitor's strike (following its speed), a tick when an edit is taken or the chosen word moves, and a lower tick for stet. The editor's own marks are silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The editor keeps working, but the visitor cannot strike.

props.name: onPhraseChange
props.description: A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; it is w-full, and the page's height follows its lines.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the page is a button. Left and Right choose a word (Home and End jump), shown with a tinted box while focused, and Enter or Space strikes it with the same stroke a tap draws — a weak word is taken and rewritten, a good one marked stet. A polite region reads the chosen word and the outcome.

Reduced motion: the draft appears whole and keeps its typing time as reading time, each edit appears in turn with no sweep, the clean line cross-fades in with nothing gliding, and the nib is hidden; a visitor's drag still draws its strike under the pointer.
The clean phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root and is announced once per phrase; the clock runs only while the page is on screen in a visible document.

items.title: Morse Status
items.tagline: Tapped out, then spelled.
items.description: A status line that is tapped out in Morse before it is spelled: a signal lamp sends each word with real ratios, and a head travelling the track under the line draws every dot and dash as long as the lamp was lit, so a dash is three dots long because it was on three times as long. When a word is complete each letter's marks lift off the track and condense into the printed letter on the glide spring while the letter resolves out of them, and the head glides on to the next word. The telegraph key is a real button whose lever dips on flick and springs back on snap; a tap, or Space or Enter, adds the visitor's own dot to the line and a hold draws a dash.

props.name: phrases
props.description: The status phrases, tapped out one after another and cycled in order.

props.name: active
props.description: Sending. False clears the line, spells doneText and stops the clock and every timer.

props.name: doneText
props.description: What stays spelled once inactive. Defaults to the last phrase.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the code is sent, 0.5 to 2: one unit is 50ms at 1, and the hold and fades scale with it.

props.name: lamp
props.description: Show the signal lamp, which flashes with the code and lights the mark being drawn. Off, the head and the marks carry the signal alone.

props.name: trail
props.description: How long the marks stay lit on the track, 0 (each fades to a ghost within a moment) to 1 (every mark stays until its word is spelled); also the length of the light streak behind the head.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the key under the visitor's hand: a click as the contact closes and a tick as the lever returns. The automatic sending is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The line keeps sending, but the key cannot be pressed.

props.name: onPhraseChange
props.description: A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.

props.name: onWordChange
props.description: A word of the phrase began to be sent: its index within the phrase. Also reported on the first commit.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; it is w-full by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the telegraph key is a button — Space or Enter held closes the line for as long as it is held (a dash), tapped sends a dot, exactly as the pointer does; a click from assistive technology sends one dot.

Reduced motion: the lamp glows steadily instead of flashing, each letter's code appears whole on the track in the same rhythm, and a spelled word cross-fades in rather than condensing out of its marks; the key's lever does not travel.
The phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root and is announced once per phrase, never per word or mark; the clock runs only while the line is on screen in a visible page.

items.title: Braille Rise
items.tagline: Felt first, then read.
items.description: A status line felt before it is read: each letter first rises as its real six-dot braille cell, the dots coming up out of the paper on the snap spring so each dome brightens as it overshoots, and a moment behind the dots sink back on a tween while the printed letter comes up out of them, so a band of raised cells rides across the line ahead of the print. Moving the pointer along the line lifts the cells under it again like a finger reading, and a press pops one up on the recoil spring. The line is a slider over its letters: Left and Right move a reading caret that raises the cell under it and names the letter and its dots, Space or Enter presses it, and the phrase waits while someone is reading it.

props.name: phrases
props.description: The status phrases, embossed and printed one after another, cycled in order.

props.name: active
props.description: Printing. False clears the line, prints doneText flat and stops every clock and timer.

props.name: doneText
props.description: What stays printed once inactive. Defaults to the last phrase.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the cells rise and print and how long a printed phrase rests, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: emboss
props.description: How deep the paper is pressed, 0 (flat ink dots, no shadow or swell) to 1 (paper-coloured domes with a long shadow and a bright rim).

props.name: cells
props.description: Show each unprinted letter's whole six-dot cell as faint pits, so the blank slate is visible before the dots rise.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the reading: a tick for each cell that comes under the finger or the caret, pitched by its dot count, and a pop for a press. The printing itself is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The line keeps printing, but it cannot be read by hand or by key.

props.name: onPhraseChange
props.description: A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; it is w-full by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the line is a slider over its letters — arriving by Tab rests the caret on the first letter and raises its cell, Left and Right (Home, End) move it a letter at a time exactly as a finger would, and its value text names the letter and its dots; Space or Enter presses the cell. While a finger or the caret is on the line, a printed phrase waits instead of changing under the reader.
Reduced motion: dots appear and sink with short fades in the same order and nothing swells or overshoots, so the phrase still arrives letter by letter and reading by hand still raises the cells.

Each letter's height is one motion value written as a CSS variable, and every dot of its cell is a background layer shaded in calc() from it; the phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root, announced once, and the print clock runs only on screen in a visible page.

items.title: Kiln Glow
items.tagline: Fired until it's done.
items.description: A determinate text loader fired like a glaze: the phrase stands in a kiln's spy window and its heat is the progress, climbing from dark iron through dull red, cherry, orange and yellow to white, each letter following on the drift spring with its own thermal mass so the heat arrives unevenly, while the letters light their own air, the back wall glows and a band of heat haze wavers above the words. At done the kiln goes out and the letters cool back down through the same colours to the glaze's fired colour, and every loop stops. A quick sweep of the pointer across the window cools the letters it passes for a moment, deeper the faster it goes, with a wisp of steam from the hot ones; the window is a button, and Space or Enter sweeps across every letter.

props.name: phrases
props.description: The status phrases. Without progress each fires by itself in turn, cycled in order.

props.name: active
props.description: Firing. False lets the kiln go out: doneText arrives as hot as the last phrase was, cools to its glaze, and every timer and loop stops.

props.name: doneText
props.description: What stays, fired, once inactive. Defaults to the last phrase.

props.name: progress
props.description: Determinate, 0 to 1: the letters' heat follows it, phrase i owns the band [i/n, (i+1)/n) and arrives at the current heat, and at 1 the kiln soaks for a moment and cools to the glaze.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the letters take and lose heat, the self-firing cycle and the haze's pace, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: heat
props.description: How hot the kiln gets at full progress, 0 (a dull red) to 1 (white heat), and with it the glow's reach, the wall's light and the haze.

props.name: glaze
props.description: The colour the letters cool to once fired, as fixed pigments that read the same in both themes.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the quench under the visitor's sweep: a sizzle while hot letters are cooled and a snap of thermal shock for the hottest. Firing and cooling are silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The kiln keeps firing, but the letters cannot be cooled by hand or by key.

props.name: onPhraseChange
props.description: A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; it is w-full by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the window is a button named Cool the letters — Space or Enter sends the same draught a quick pointer sweep does across every letter, left to right, with the same sound. With progress, a visually hidden progressbar carries the value, labelled by the phrase.

Reduced motion: no haze, steam or springs; the letters' colours still follow the heat on short tweens and a self-firing phrase still takes its time, because the heat is the progress, and a quench still darkens the letters and lets them warm back.

The kiln's chamber is fixed dark art in both themes; the phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root, announced once, and the haze runs only while the kiln is warm, on screen and in a visible page.

items.title: Lens Sweep
items.tagline: Reading it over.
items.description: A status line read over by a loupe: outside the lens the words are soft and faint, under it they are sharp, full ink and magnified about the lens's centre. The lens reads in saccades, gliding from word to word on the glide spring from rest to rest and pausing on each as if checking it, with a small nod and a hairline check drawn under the word that stays as it moves on; a read phrase rests, fades, and the lens sweeps back for the next. The lens follows a finger 1:1 anywhere along the line, ticking as it enters each word, and on release settles onto the word the throw was heading for and reads on from there; a tap on a word sends it there, and as a slider Left, Right, Home and End move it a word at a time.

props.name: phrases
props.description: The status phrases, read over one after another and cycled in order.

props.name: active
props.description: Reading. False puts the lens down beside the line and leaves doneText sharp, full ink and still; every timer stops.

props.name: doneText
props.description: What stays, read, once inactive. Defaults to the last phrase.

props.name: speed
props.description: How long the lens checks each word and rests on a read phrase, 0.5 to 2; the glide itself stays the house glide.

props.name: zoom
props.description: How much the lens magnifies, 1.2 to 2.

props.name: blur
props.description: How soft the words outside the lens are, 0 to 4 px.

props.name: lens
props.description: A jeweller's loupe, or a reading bar that magnifies a wider span of the line.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the lens under the visitor's hand: a tick for each word it enters while dragged, tapped to or moved by key, pitched along the line. The automatic reading is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The lens keeps reading, but it cannot be moved by hand or by key.

props.name: onPhraseChange
props.description: A phrase began: its index in phrases, or -1 for doneText. Also reported on the first commit.

props.name: onWordChange
props.description: The lens came to rest on a word and checked it: its index in the phrase.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; it is w-full by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the lens is a slider over the words — Left and Right move it a word, Home and End to the ends, the same end state as putting it down there by hand; its value text names the word, and reading waits a second after each key before going on from there.
Reduced motion: the lens does not glide — it appears at each word in turn with a short fade and the check appears whole; dragging is still 1:1 and a drop places it on the word directly.

Two copies of the line share one layout: a still, blurred page copy, and a copy clipped to the lens, scaled from its corner and shifted by the centre times one minus the zoom, so the point under the lens stays put. The phrase sits in a polite live region outside the busy root, announced once, and reading runs only on screen in a visible page.

items.title: Hourglass Turn
items.tagline: Sand runs out, then it turns itself.
items.description: An inline loader drawn as a small hourglass: sand runs from the top bulb onto a growing pile as a falling thread, conserved as drawn area so the top's level races where the bulb narrows, and when the top is empty the glass rests a beat and turns itself over on the snap spring while the sand rides the turn and slumps onto the neck. Drag it sideways and it follows the pointer, the thread breaks, and a release past a quarter turn completes the half turn with the release velocity so the sand stays where it was; with progress the pile is the progress and a turn by hand is a full tumble on glide. It is a real button — Enter or Space turns it — beside a status or progressbar label, and the landing thocks only when the visitor turned it.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible text beside the glyph, and the loader's accessible name ("Loading" when omitted).

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive technology only.

props.name: size
props.description: The glyph's box in px, 16 to 64. Detail is chosen by size: posts and a pile shadow from 24, falling grains from 32, a glass highlight from 40.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the sand runs (3.2 s a run at 1) and how long it rests before turning, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: sand
props.description: The sand's pigment, at a fixed lightness so it reads the same in both themes.

props.name: progress
props.description: Determinate share run through, 0 to 1: the pile holds that share and the sand runs to each new value at the glass's own rate. Omit for a glass that keeps turning.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a thock when the glass lands after the visitor turned it (and a quiet one when a short drag rocks back). The self-turn is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Keeps running, but cannot be turned by hand or key.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the inline root; the label inherits its font size and colour.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the glass is a button — Enter or Space turns it over, exactly as a drag past a quarter turn does; the loader's role (status, or progressbar with a value) sits on the label beside it, so no control is nested in a progressbar.

Reduced motion: the sand still runs, because the level is the information, but the thread is a still line, nothing rotates or slumps, and every turn is a quick cross-fade to the other way up; a drag still tilts under the finger and settles with a short tween.
Nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page; the run picks up from the same grain when it returns. Give it `size` to match the text it sits in — it reads at 16 px.

items.title: Knot Tie
items.tagline: A rope that ties itself.
items.description: An inline loader drawn as a short rope that ties itself: one Catmull-Rom path through a fixed set of points is blended every frame through four stages of the knot — slack, the first loop lifted over, loosely tied, snug — on move tweens, cinched on the rope's own spring (jute glides, nylon snaps one overshoot past, silk flicks), then loosened and untied. Where the rope crosses itself the upper strand is redrawn on top with its lay continuing unbroken, so the overhand, bow and figure-eight alternate over and under like real knots. Dragging the rope sideways tightens it early 1:1 with the pull, rubber-banding past snug, and a release cinches it with the release velocity; Enter or Space on the rope's button tugs it snug the same way, and the rope creaks only while the visitor pulls.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible text beside the glyph, and the loader's accessible name ("Loading" when omitted).

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive technology only.

props.name: size
props.description: The glyph's box in px, 16 to 64. Detail is chosen by size: crossings from 20, the rope's lay from 28, frayed or sealed ends and a shadow from 40.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast it ties, holds, loosens and lets go, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: knot
props.description: Which knot it ties: an overhand, a shoelace bow or a figure eight.

props.name: rope
props.description: What the rope is: its thickness, pigment, lay, end finish, snug spring and how quickly it slides loose.

props.name: progress
props.description: Determinate share done, 0 to 1: the knot is tied that far and snug at 1. Omit for a rope that keeps tying and untying.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a creak loop while the visitor pulls the rope, pitched by the tension and loud as the rope moves; it stops on release. The self-tying cycle is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Keeps tying itself, but cannot be tugged.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the inline root; the label inherits its font size and colour.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the rope is a button — Enter or Space tugs it snug on the rope's spring, the same end state as a drag; the loader's role (status, or progressbar with a value) sits on the label beside it.

Reduced motion: the rope does not morph; it holds whole stages — slack, loose, snug — and cross-fades between them on the same beats, and with progress it shows the whole stage the progress has reached.
The creak loop stops on release, on cancel, when sound is switched off, on disable and on unmount; nothing animates off screen or in a hidden page.

items.title: Radio Tune
items.tagline: Searching the dial.
items.description: An inline loader drawn as a small tabletop radio whose needle scans the dial like a seek radio: it sweeps up the band, catches each strong station with a hunting settle on the snap spring, dwells while the signal bars stand up, sweeps on and glides back to the bottom on glide, while the meter — the signal at the needle plus the band's own seeded static — wavers between stations. With progress the needle travels to the home station as the work goes on and at 1 locks on, a hair past the mark and back on snap, with the meter full and the backlight warm. It is a real slider: a drag moves the needle 1:1 under the pointer while the knob turns, a release coasts and is pulled onto a station within reach, arrow keys turn it finely, Page Up and Page Down seek, Home and End reach the ends, and focus stops the search.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible text beside the glyph, and the loader's accessible name ("Loading" when omitted).

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive technology only.

props.name: size
props.description: The glyph's box in px, 16 to 64. Detail is chosen by size: scale marks, stations and five signal bars from 24, scale numbers, band name, feet and walnut grain from 40.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast it sweeps, dwells and flickers, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: band
props.description: The waveband: FM 88–108 MHz with evenly spread stations and hiss, AM 530–1700 kHz on a compressed scale with stations crowded low and crackle, or SW 5.9–18 MHz with stations bunched in broadcast bands and a fading warble.

props.name: dial
props.description: The cabinet: cream bakelite, walnut or black bakelite, fixed pigments that read the same in both themes.

props.name: progress
props.description: Determinate share done, 0 to 1: the needle travels toward the home station and locks on at 1. Omit for a radio that keeps searching.

props.name: sound
props.description: While the visitor drags, play a hum loop as a heterodyne whistle that falls toward zero-beat on a station, a click for each scale mark passed and a brighter click when a hand, key or tap lands on a station. The search and the final lock are silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Keeps searching, but cannot be tuned by hand or key.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the inline root; the label inherits its font size and colour.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the radio is role="slider" named "Tuning" with the frequency as its value and text ("97.5 MHz, on a station") — Left and Right step finely, Page Up and Page Down seek the next or previous station, Home and End reach the ends of the band, and while it has keyboard focus the search pauses; the loader's role sits on the label beside it.

Reduced motion: the needle steps from mark to mark on the same rhythm instead of sweeping, the static holds still, the lock is an instant move plus a fade of the backlight, and a release lands at once — on a station when within reach.
After a hand has tuned it the search resumes 1.4 s later from where it was left; nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page, and the hum stops on release, blur, disable and unmount.

items.title: Abacus Count
items.tagline: Beads slide as the work counts up.
items.description: An inline loader drawn as a small counting frame: ten beads on each wire, the highest place on the left, one motion value per bead. The work counts up a bead at a time — each rises to the beam on the spring its material calls for (wood on springs.snap, glass on springs.recoil, stone on springs.glide) — and at ten the wire clears in a rattle while a bead rises on the next wire, so a determinate count (rows of a total, or percent) reads as beads and big jumps glide on springs.glide; without progress it counts to a seeded number and clears. The frame is a button: drag up and the next units bead follows the finger 1:1, a release past halfway flicks it home with the throw's velocity, and a tap, Enter, Space or the Up arrow does the same — free-running the flick adds one, determinate the bead is only lent and slides home if the work has not reached it.

props.name: label
props.description: What is loading. Shown beside the glyph and the loader's accessible name: the status's, or the progressbar's when progress is given.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive technology only, for a glyph inline in a sentence or a row.

props.name: size
props.description: The glyph's box in px, crisp from 16 to 64: detail simplifies below 40 and below 24 so it still reads at text size.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast it counts, 0.5 to 2: the pace between beads, the hold and the clear.

props.name: rods
props.description: Wires on the frame, 2 to 5: the places the count can show (fewer are drawn below 40px and 24px). The leftmost wire can hold all ten, which reads as full.

props.name: beads
props.description: What the beads are made of: how they look and how they land — wood snaps with one overshoot, glass rings in two bounces, stone lands dead.

props.name: progress
props.description: Determinate, 0 to 1: the frame shows round(progress × min(total, 10^rods)) in beads, stepping bead by bead for small moves and gliding for big ones. Without it the frame counts and clears on its own.

props.name: total
props.description: What a full progress counts to, so rows read as rows (480 rows on three wires shows 212 as 2·1·2) and the progressbar's value text reads "212 of 480".

props.name: onFlick
props.description: A bead was flicked across by hand, tap or key.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play what the visitor causes: a click as a flicked bead lands (pitched by material), a tick at the drag's halfway detent and a rattle of ticks for a carry the flick causes. Counting and clearing are silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Keep counting, but refuse the hand: the frame is drawn as a picture with no button, for loaders that should not be a tab stop.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the inline root; text size set here reaches the label.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the frame is a button named "Flick a bead" — Enter, Space or the Up arrow flick the next units bead across, the same end state as a drag up past halfway or a tap. The label sits beside it as role="progressbar" (with the percent and a value text) when progress is given, otherwise as a polite role="status"; it is a sibling of the button because a progressbar's children are presentational.

Reduced motion: beads swap into place instead of sliding and carries clear at once, but the count still steps (at a third of the pace) and determinate counts still update, because the count is the information; a drag still moves the bead under the finger and settles at once.
The count loop runs only while the frame is on screen in a visible page, and stopping always lands every bead where the count says, so a scroll or a StrictMode re-run resumes cleanly.

items.title: Yarn Knit
items.tagline: Knitting while it thinks.
items.description: An inline loader drawn as knitting: a needle holds a row of stitches, the working needle crosses it at the last one, and the yarn hangs from there to a ball on the floor. Each stitch the working needle stabs in and back on two tweens, the new V grows down from the needle on the fibre's spring (wool springs.snap, cotton springs.flick, mohair springs.drift), and the yarn tugs the ball, which jerks toward the work and rolls back on springs.snap, turning as it unwinds and shrinking as the row grows; given progress the row is that share knitted and glides on springs.glide, otherwise it knits to the end, holds and unravels. The glyph is a button: drag the yarn and its middle follows the finger 1:1 with a loop forming where it is pinched, and letting go of a long pull has the needles take the loop with a click — the next stitch when free-running, wound back when determinate — while a tap, Enter or Space pulls one loop.

props.name: label
props.description: What is loading. Shown beside the glyph and the loader's accessible name: the status's, or the progressbar's when progress is given.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive technology only, for a glyph inline in a sentence or a row.

props.name: size
props.description: The glyph's box in px, crisp from 16 to 64: detail simplifies below 40 and below 24 so it still reads at text size.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast it knits, 0.5 to 2: the stitch rhythm, the stab, the hold and the unravel.

props.name: yarn
props.description: The fibre, which sets the look and the spring: wool is springy with a ply twist, cotton thin, taut and quick, mohair soft and lazy with a halo and loose fibres.

props.name: colour
props.description: The yarn's dye, as fixed pigments that look the same in both themes; the needles are theme ink.

props.name: progress
props.description: Determinate, 0 to 1: how much of the row is knitted, the partial stitch growing smoothly and the needle stabbing as each whole stitch completes. Without it the row knits, holds and unravels on its own.

props.name: onTug
props.description: A loop was pulled by hand, tap or key.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the needles taking a pulled loop (pitched by fibre), and a softer knock when a determinate loop is wound back. Knitting and unravelling are silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Keep knitting, but refuse the hand: the glyph is drawn as a picture with no button, for loaders that should not be a tab stop.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the inline root; text size set here reaches the label.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the glyph is a button named "Pull a loop" — Enter or Space draws the yarn out and lets it go, the same end state as a long drag or a tap; a key's tug interrupted by a scroll or a hidden page is finished at once, never lost. The label beside it is role="progressbar" with the percent when progress is given, otherwise a polite role="status".

Reduced motion: no stab, roll or spring — stitches appear with an instant swap at half the pace and the row clears at once after its hold, while determinate progress still sets the row, because the row is the information; a drag still moves the yarn under the finger and it returns at once.

Everything that moves is derived from five motion values (stitches, stab, tug and the pull's x and y), so there is no React state per frame; the knitting rhythm runs only while the glyph is on screen in a visible page.

items.title: Geared Pen
items.tagline: A pen that never draws the same loop twice.
items.description: An inline loader drawn by a geared pen: a wheel rolls inside a toothed ring and its pen traces a hypotrochoid with as many lobes as the ratio, the wheel's own turn accumulated rather than computed so a changing ratio never makes the pen jump. Free-running, a frame loop writes the geometry into motion values, the trail fades behind the pen in tapered chunks, and the ratio drifts on a slow sine so the rosette precesses and never quite repeats; given progress, the ratio holds and the figure is drawn solid on springs.glide, closing at 1 as the pen lifts. The glyph is a button: drag around its centre and the wheel follows the pointer's angle 1:1, a free wheel keeps the throw and eases back to its pace while a determinate one glides home on springs.glide with the release velocity, and arrow keys turn it a notch (springs.snap) while Enter or Space spins it round.

props.name: label
props.description: What is loading. Shown beside the glyph and the loader's accessible name: the status's, or the progressbar's when progress is given.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive technology only, for a glyph inline in a sentence or a row.

props.name: size
props.description: The glyph's box in px, crisp from 16 to 64: detail simplifies below 40 and below 24 so it still reads at text size.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the wheel goes round, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: ratio
props.description: The ring's size over the wheel's, 2 to 9: the figure's lobes. Half steps weave two orbits before the figure closes.

props.name: trail
props.description: How long the fading trail is, 0 (a short comet) to 1 (three orbits), and the length of the comet a hand's turn leaves on a determinate figure.

props.name: ink
props.description: The pen's colour: the theme's bright accent, or the danger and success tokens' lightness and chroma at the ink's own hue, so the thin line keeps its contrast in both themes.

props.name: progress
props.description: Determinate, 0 to 1: how much of the closed figure is drawn, solid, with the pen at its head. Without it the pen never stops.

props.name: onTurn
props.description: The wheel was turned by hand, tap or key.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Keep drawing, but refuse the hand: the glyph is drawn as a picture with no button, for loaders that should not be a tab stop.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the inline root; text size set here reaches the label.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the glyph is a button named "Turn the wheel" — ArrowRight or ArrowUp turn it an eighth forward, ArrowLeft or ArrowDown back, Enter or Space spin it a full turn; free-running these are impulses that ease back into the wheel's pace, determinate the pen turns away and glides home, the same end states as a drag. The label beside it is role="progressbar" with the percent when progress is given, otherwise a polite role="status".

Reduced motion: no frame loop and no drift — the whole figure is drawn faintly and a bright stretch the trail's length steps along it every 650ms / speed, the wheel and pen jumping with it; a determinate figure updates at once. Dragging still turns the wheel 1:1.

The frame loop runs only while the glyph is on screen in a visible page and a determinate figure draws only while it changes; stopping gives a spin still easing out all at once, so a scroll never loses a turn.

items.title: Kettle Steam
items.tagline: Nearly boiled.
items.description: An inline loader drawn as a stovetop kettle coming to the boil: bubbles rise in its round sight glass, faster and more of them as it heats, and steam curls from the spout as filled ribbons whose curl travels up them, leaning away from the pointer on the drift spring. Given progress, heat is the progress — the bezel round the glass fills like a dial and the lid rattles near the top — and at 1 the whistle flips open on the recoil spring while the steam straightens into a jet, then settles into a still wisp and the frame loop stops; without it, the kettle simmers. The kettle is a real button: held with the pointer, Space or Enter it turns up the flame (a boost in on snap, out on drift, the body dipping on flick), and pressed at the boil it blows the whistle.

props.name: label
props.description: What is on the boil: the loader's accessible name, shown beside the kettle unless hideLabel.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive technology only.

props.name: size
props.description: The glyph's box in px, crisp from 16 to 64. Below 24 the sight glass, knob and handle grip drop out; below 44 the whistle flap, sheen and third wisp.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the water churns, the steam curls and the jet runs, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: progress
props.description: How close to the boil, 0 to 1; the label becomes a progressbar. Omitted, the kettle simmers. At 1 the whistle flips open and the steam jets, then everything comes to rest.

props.name: steam
props.description: How much steam, 0 (a faint thread) to 1 (a dense plume of three wisps at 44 px and up).

props.name: body
props.description: The kettle's finish, as fixed pigments that read the same in both themes.

props.name: sound
props.description: A hum while the kettle is held, pitched by the heat, and the whistle when it is pressed at the boil. Reaching the boil by itself is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The kettle keeps boiling but takes no presses and the steam ignores the pointer.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, an inline-flex row of the kettle and its label.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the kettle is a button — hold Space or Enter to turn up the flame (released on key up or blur), and at the boil press either to blow the whistle; assistive-technology activation is a short tap.

Reduced motion: nothing travels — the steam is one still ribbon whose opacity breathes while it heats, the bubbles are still dots whose count follows the heat, the bezel still fills, and the jet fades in as a still plume with the flap shown open.

The label lives in a role="progressbar" (aria-valuenow 0–100) when progress is given, otherwise a role="status" named by it; the frame loop runs only while the kettle is on screen in a visible page and stops once the boiled kettle is still.

items.title: Tape Reels
items.tagline: Tape winding from one reel to the other.
items.description: An inline loader drawn as a cassette whose tape winds from one reel to the other. The two packs are sized from the tape itself — their areas always add up to the same length — and each reel turns by the tape that moves over its own pack's radius, so the emptying reel speeds up while the filling one slows, as real tape does; given progress the tape follows it on the glide spring, and without it a motor winds at a steady tape speed and rewinds fast on a move ease. Dragging the cassette sideways pulls the tape 1:1, rubber-banded at the ends, and a release coasts to where the throw would rest on glide with the release velocity (or glides back to the progress, since the job owns the tape); holding Left or Right winds it the same way.

props.name: label
props.description: What is loading: the loader's accessible name, shown beside the cassette unless hideLabel. On this glyph label is the cassette's paper label, so the text is the label.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive technology only.

props.name: size
props.description: The glyph's box in px, crisp from 16 to 64. Below 24 each hub shows one notch and the tape path drops out; below 44 the screws, rollers' detail, handwriting and window glint.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the motor winds (about 9 s for the whole tape at 1) and rewinds, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: progress
props.description: How much tape is on the take-up reel, 0 to 1; the caption becomes a progressbar. Omitted, the tape winds and rewinds on a loop.

props.name: shell
props.description: The cassette's plastic: clear shows the whole mechanism in the page's own tint, smoke darkens it, ivory is opaque so only the window shows the packs.

props.name: sticker
props.description: The paper label across the shell — a colour band, ruled lines and handwriting at 44 px and up — with the window cut through it.

props.name: sound
props.description: A click when a scrub grabs and lets go of the tape (and on a jog), and a whir while it is pulled that follows the faster reel's spin. The motor is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The tape keeps winding but cannot be scrubbed or jogged.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, an inline-flex row of the cassette and its caption.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the cassette is a button — hold Left or Right to wind the tape by hand (key up lets go, as releasing a drag does), Home and End rewind or wind it through, and Space or Enter jogs it forward.

Reduced motion: the reels do not turn and nothing coasts — the motor advances the packs in steps and resets at the end, determinate packs jump to the progress, and a scrub still follows the hand 1:1 and returns at once.

The glyph set's text prop is label on every other glyph; here label is the cassette's paper label (a tweak), so the text is caption. The caption lives in a role="progressbar" (aria-valuenow 0–100) or a role="status"; the motor's frame loop runs only on screen in a visible page.

items.title: Lava Drift
items.tagline: Warm blobs rising and falling.
items.description: An inline loader drawn as a small lava lamp whose wax really convects: each blob carries a temperature, heats on the bulb, floats once it is half-warm and loses heat as it climbs — faster near the cool cap — so it rises, lingers, cools and sinks back into the pool, every blob on its own time, and blobs that touch pull their speed and heat together and travel as one mass until their heat parts them. The wax is circles joined by analytic metaball necks, so it merges and splits crisply with no blur. The pointer is a warm hand that heats the nearest blob while the glass glows under it (a warmth that rises on the drift spring), Space or Enter warms the blob on the bulb, and given progress the pool drains into a cap under the top on the glide spring while blobs ride up between them until the lamp goes still.

props.name: label
props.description: What is warming up: the loader's accessible name, shown beside the lamp unless hideLabel.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive technology only.

props.name: size
props.description: The glyph's box in px, crisp from 16 to 64. Below 24 at most three blobs and no halo; below 44 no shine, glass highlight or base band.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the wax heats, rises, cools and sinks (a cycle of about seven seconds at 1), 0.5 to 2.

props.name: progress
props.description: The share of the wax that has risen, 0 to 1; the label becomes a progressbar. The pool drains, a cap gathers under the top and blobs ride up between them; at 1 the lamp goes still. Omitted, the blobs rise and fall on their own.

props.name: wax
props.description: The wax and the liquid it floats in — amber in red, rose in violet, teal in blue — as fixed pigments that read the same in both themes.

props.name: blobs
props.description: How many blobs rise and fall, 2 to 6; with progress, how many ride up at once.

props.name: glow
props.description: How much the lamp glows, 0 to 1: the halo round the glass, the bulb's light up the liquid and the shine on the wax.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The lamp keeps flowing but cannot be warmed by the pointer or a press.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, an inline-flex row of the lamp and its label.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the lamp is a button — Space or Enter warms the blob sitting on the bulb (or hurries the lowest rising blob while it fills), the same heat the pointer gives the blob nearest it.

Reduced motion: the wax does not travel — it is drawn still, the glow breathes while the lamp works, the pool and cap still follow the progress at once, and a warm brightens the glow instead of moving wax.
No sound. The label lives in a role="progressbar" (aria-valuenow 0–100) or a role="status"; the frame loop runs only on screen in a visible page and stops once a filled lamp is still.

items.title: Sundial
items.tagline: The shadow walks the hours.
items.description: An inline loader drawn as a garden sundial seen from above. The time of day — the progress, or a looping day — sets the gnomon's shadow by the real horizontal-dial formula, so hour lines crowd towards noon, and the sun's altitude sets its length: long and faint at morning and evening, short and dark at noon; a small sun rides the rim opposite, lighting that side of the plate, and the light warms from a cool dawn to a gold evening before a short dusk. With progress the time follows it on the drift spring and rests in the evening at 1. Dragging on the dial walks the shadow — a flick swing to the finger, then 1:1, ticking at every hour line it crosses — and letting go drifts it back to the real hour, or lets the looping day carry on from there; Left and Right walk it an hour at a time on glide.

props.name: label
props.description: What is waiting on the day: the loader's accessible name, shown beside the dial unless hideLabel.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive technology only.

props.name: size
props.description: The glyph's box in px, crisp from 16 to 64. Below 24 only the plate, fin, shadow and sun; below 44 plain hour lines with no numerals, ticks or penumbra.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the looping day passes (about eight seconds and a short dusk at 1), 0.5 to 2.

props.name: progress
props.description: How far through the day, 0 (06:00) to 1 (18:00); the label becomes a progressbar and the dial rests in the evening light at 1. Omitted, a day passes on a loop.

props.name: dial
props.description: The plate: weathered stone, polished brass or dark slate with light engraving, as fixed pigments that read the same in both themes.

props.name: numerals
props.description: How the quarters are marked round the rim at 44 px and up: VI IX XII III VI, 6 9 12 3 6, or longer ticks.

props.name: sound
props.description: A tick for every hour line the shadow crosses while the visitor walks it, bright in the morning and low in the evening, loudest at noon. The running day is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The day keeps passing but the shadow cannot be walked.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, an inline-flex row of the dial and its label.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the dial is a button — Left/Right (or Down/Up) walk the shadow an hour, Page Up and Page Down three, Home and End to morning and evening, held keys keep walking and key up lets go, as releasing a drag does; Space or Enter walks it one hour on. With progress the shadow then drifts back to the real hour after a beat.
