props.description: Whether the band is snapped on. A host that changes it moves the band silently; one that refuses a snap gets the band back.

props.name: onSnappedChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, tap or key whose clasp caught, or from Unsnap.

props.name: onScan
props.description: Fires when a worn band is held to the reader: a tap, Enter or Space on it.

props.name: fabric
props.description: What the band is made of: woven twill with stitched edges and a soft curl, glossy silicone with a travelling highlight and a lively curl, or paper with fibres, die-cut slits and a crisp curl. Each has its own height.

props.name: tier
props.description: The ticket tier: the band's colour (cobalt, gold, red), the word printed on it, the default access and the chime's pitch.

props.name: wrap
props.description: How much depth the band shows, 0 to 1: worn, 0 is straight on and nearly flat and 1 looks down into the loop with strong perspective; off, it is how much of the wrist's curve the band keeps as it rests.

props.name: sound
props.description: A snap as the clasp catches (lower as it opens) and a chime on a scan, pitched by tier. Only ever in answer to the visitor.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the band but takes no drags, taps or keys.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the band is one real button whose name says what a press does — "Put on the wristband: VIP, Teo Bramhall" or "Scan the wristband: …" — so Enter or Space wraps it on or scans it; Unsnap is a real button shown while it is worn, and focus returns to the band after it. Drags are pointer mirrors of the button.

Reduced motion: nothing curls, lifts or ripples outward — the flat and worn bands cross-fade, the print still runs on (a clip, not a movement), and a scan shows one ring fading in place while the print panel glows. A drag still follows the finger and lands where it commits.

The band's length follows its measured width (between 260 and 600px), and the view only tips down into the loop as it closes, so a half-wrapped band never rises out of its box. A polite live region says when the band goes on or off and each scan.

items.title: Emboss Card
items.tagline: Letterpress you can feel.
items.description: A business card lying on the table with its name blind-debossed and a blind-embossed roundel, lit by one lamp that follows the pointer on the glide spring and drifts back to rest on drift: bevels are shaded analytically (a cosine around each ring, the letters masked against themselves shifted along the light), so the impression turns as the lamp moves. Tap, drag or press Details and the card turns over to its contact details, following the finger 1:1 and committing by projection on the snap spring as it lifts off the table; Copy writes the contact to the clipboard and draws a check on flick. The keyboard reaches the same turn through the Details toggle, and a keyboard arrival sweeps the lamp once across the card.

props.name: name
props.description: The name, blind-debossed on the front.

props.name: title
props.description: The job title, printed under the name.

props.name: company
props.description: The company, printed in spaced capitals at the top right.

props.name: details
props.type: { label: string; value: string; href?: string }[]
props.description: Contact lines printed on the back; up to four fit the card. An href makes the value a link.

props.name: monogram
props.description: One or two letters debossed into the roundel. Defaults to the name's initials.

props.name: flipped / defaultFlipped
props.description: Whether the back (the contact details) faces up; controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onFlippedChange
props.description: Fires from the tap, drag or button that turned the card, with the new side.

props.name: copyText
props.description: What Copy puts on the clipboard. Defaults to the name, title, company and every detail, one per line.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Fires once the contact is on the clipboard, with the text that was copied.

props.name: depth
props.description: How deep the press is, 0 to 1: the bevel's angle, the walls' width and the rim's cast shadow.

props.name: stock
props.description: The board the card is pressed into; black prints its details in white ink.

props.name: light
props.description: A lamp that follows the pointer, with a sheen on the board. Off: a fixed light from the upper left.

props.name: sound
props.description: The copy click and the soft click of the card landing after a turn the visitor asked for.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The card can be read but not turned or copied, and the lamp stays at rest.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Details is a toggle button (aria-pressed) that turns the card through the same spring as a drag, and Copy is a button; the face turned away is inert and hidden from assistive technology, and links on the back (mailto:, tel:, https:) are reachable once it faces up. A keyboard arrival sweeps the lamp once across the card.

Reduced motion: the card never rotates or lifts — the faces cross-fade on a short tween after a tap, a drag past a third of the card or Details — and the lamp still follows the pointer, directly, because shading is not travel. The check appears without drawing; status and sound are unchanged.

The lighting is analytic: conic gradients sampled from a cosine for each bevel and masks for the debossed letters, so it stays crisp at any size and costs a few style strings per frame. Copy falls back to a hidden textarea where the clipboard is refused, and says so if both fail.

items.title: Punch Card
items.tagline: Nine punches, one free.
items.description: A loyalty card you punch: each press sinks the next printed spot under the die on the flick spring, then cuts a real hole through the card (an SVG mask, so the table and the card's own shadow show through), the card jolts and recovers on recoil, and a paper chad carrying its piece of the print pops toward you and falls away under gravity on an ease-in tween. The final punch lights the reward with a recoil landing and a ring, then the card turns over on the snap spring to its redeem side; Redeem turns it back, and the holes give way to a fresh card at the instant it is edge-on. The count is a role="meter" and the punch is a real button, so Space or Enter presses and cuts through the same path, and focus follows the card when it turns.

props.name: brand
props.description: The café or shop, printed on the card's band.

props.name: reward
props.description: What a full card is worth.

props.name: member
props.description: The holder's name, printed at the foot of the card.

props.name: number
props.description: The card's number, printed on the band.

props.name: code
props.description: The redeem code on the back. Defaults to a deterministic code from the brand, the member and the cycle.

props.name: label
props.description: The card's accessible name. Defaults to "{brand} loyalty card".

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: How many spots are punched, 0 to holes; controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press that punched a spot, or from Redeem with 0.

props.name: onRedeem
props.description: Fires when the reward is redeemed.

props.name: holes
props.description: How many punches earn the reward, 6 to 12; the grid re-lays out in two rows.

props.name: shape
props.description: The printed spot, the hole and the chad.

props.name: chad
props.description: A paper chad pops out of each hole and falls away. Off: a clean cut.

props.name: sound
props.description: A click at each cut, rising in pitch across the card, a pop as the reward lights, and a click on Redeem.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The card can be read but not punched or redeemed.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the Punch button lies over the spots; Space or Enter dimples on key down and cuts on release, exactly as a press does, and once the card is full it reads "Card full. Turn over to redeem". When the card turns, focus moves to the arriving face's button (Redeem, or the Punch button again after a redeem). The count is a role="meter" with aria-valuetext such as "6 of 9 punched, 3 to go", and each punch is announced politely.
Reduced motion: no dimple travel, jolt, chad flight, ring or turn — the chad fades in its hole and the faces cross-fade — while the hole, the count, the reward's colour and every sound still arrive.
Controlled: onValueChange reports the press; a host that raises value animates the punches without sound, and a host that sets 0 while the redeem side is up turns the card back to a fresh front.

items.title: Award Seal
items.tagline: Signed, sealed, awarded.
items.description: A certificate that is signed and sealed in front of you: a signature generated from the signer's name writes itself along its own path, then an embosser presses a crimped foil rosette onto the paper on an accelerating tween, settling on the flick spring as the paper dimples around it, the foil flashes as the light sweeps round its crimps, and two ribbon tails unfurl on glide and swing as damped pendulums whose looseness is the swing tweak. The foil is lit analytically from one light — pleats square to it flash in stripes, the medallion's rim follows a cosine, the laurel is raised by shifted highlight and shadow copies — and hovering the seal moves that light with the pointer. The seal is a real button: Space or Enter signs and seals it, then burnishes it, Left and Right swing the ribbons, and Replay plays the whole ceremony again.

props.name: issuer
props.description: Who awards it, printed in spaced capitals at the top.

props.name: award
props.description: The award itself, e.g. "Certificate of Completion".

props.name: recipient
props.description: Who receives it.

props.name: citation
props.description: One or two lines on what it is for.

props.name: date
props.description: The date as it should be printed.

props.name: signer
props.description: Whose signature writes itself on the line; the signature is generated from this name.

props.name: signerTitle
props.description: Printed after the signer's name.

props.name: sealed / defaultSealed
props.description: Whether the certificate is signed and sealed; controlled or uncontrolled. Sealing plays the ceremony.

props.name: onSealedChange
props.description: Fires from the press that signs and seals it, with true.

props.name: foil
props.description: The rosette's foil, its printed accents and its ribbons' satin.

props.name: ribbons
props.description: Two ribbon tails hang from the seal and swing; they can be brushed, grabbed and thrown.

props.name: swing
props.description: How loosely the ribbons swing, 0 to 1: their damping, the size of every kick and the whip of their lower half.

props.name: sound
props.description: A thud as the seal meets the paper, a shimmer with the foil's flash, a softer thud when it is burnished.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The certificate can be read but not sealed, burnished or replayed.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the seal is a button — unsealed, "Sign and seal the certificate"; sealed, it burnishes the foil — and Left and Right swing its ribbons, the keyboard path for a drag. Replay is a button once the certificate is sealed. "Signed by", "Sealed" and "Replaying the seal" are announced politely.

Reduced motion: the signature fades in instead of writing, the seal fades in at rest with the paper's dimple, and the ribbons hang still; the light still follows a hovering pointer, directly, because shading is not travel. Sounds and announcements are unchanged.
Printable: every word is real text, and a sealed certificate prints with its signature and seal whatever the animation was doing; Replay is hidden in print.

items.title: Booth Strip
items.tagline: Four frames, and shake it dry.
items.description: A photo booth's panel and the strip it prints: for each shot the readout counts down, the reflector charges and fires a white wash over the booth, and the strip feeds out of the slot by one frame on a tween stepped into roller lines, newest shot nearest the slot. A fresh strip is wet — darker and glossy, the gloss shrinking from the edges as it dries — and shaking it dries it faster: it pivots at the slot, follows the finger 1:1 with rubber-banded edges, then swings as a pendulum spring taking the release velocity. Any frame enlarges into a viewer that grows out of the frame's own box on the glide spring and shrinks back on the exit ease; the frames are buttons in one tab stop where Up and Down move, Enter enlarges and Left and Right shake.

props.name: caption
props.description: Printed on the strip's tail, e.g. "Fernworks 01.10.26".

props.name: photos
props.description: Your own frame contents, used in turn; by default each frame is a drawn booth portrait, new poses every strip.

props.name: label
props.description: The booth's accessible name.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The shot shown enlarged (0 is the first shot), or null; controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the pick, key or button that opened, stepped or closed a shot.

props.name: defaultPrinted
props.description: A dry strip already hangs from the slot at first.

props.name: onPrint
props.description: Fires when a new strip has finished printing.

props.name: onPhaseChange
props.description: Fires as the booth moves between phases.

props.name: frames
props.description: Shots per strip, 3 or 4.

props.name: tone
props.description: The print's chemistry, applied to whatever is in the frames.

props.name: flash
props.description: The booth flashes white on each shot (never more than once a second). Off: only the reflector lights.

props.name: sound
props.description: A shutter snap on each shot and the print feed's whir while the strip feeds, only during a strip the visitor started.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The strip can be looked at but not taken, shaken or enlarged.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the shutter is a button; the frames are one tab stop where Up and Down move between shots in their visual order, Home and End jump, Enter or Space enlarges, and Left and Right shake the strip (each a kick that dries it a step). The viewer's Close takes focus when it arrives; Escape closes it and returns focus to the frame, and Left and Right step through the shots.

Reduced motion: no white wash (the reflector still lights), no feed travel and no swing — the strip stands at full length and each shot fades into its frame, a drag or Left and Right dry it without moving it, and the viewer fades in place. Sounds and announcements are unchanged.
The timeline and the drying clock pause in a hidden tab, and the drying clock runs only while the strip is wet and on screen.

items.title: Pocket Phone
items.tagline: A phone that tilts, turns and wakes.
items.description: A phone frame that holds any screen and leans toward the pointer under a sheet of glass glare on the glide spring. A corner toggle turns it to landscape on glide while the screen counter-rotates and re-lays its content out in real pixels; its keys sink into the frame on flick, the volume keys raise a level on the glass that slides out on snap, the side key sleeps and wakes the screen, and the island opens on snap into a live activity. Every key is a real button reached by Tab and pressed with Enter or Space (Enter repeats on the volume keys), the island is a disclosure that Escape closes, and keyboard focus tilts the phone toward the key it is on.

props.name: children
props.description: The screen's content, laid out in a size container the shape of the screen; use @container (orientation: landscape) for the turned layout.

props.name: label
props.description: The device's accessible name.

props.name: island
props.description: What the island shows when it opens. Without it the island is only the camera and is not a control.

props.name: islandLabel
props.description: The island button's accessible name.

props.name: time
props.description: The clock in the status bar.

props.name: orientation / defaultOrientation
props.description: Controlled or initial orientation.

props.name: onOrientationChange
props.description: Fires from the turn toggle with the orientation asked for.

props.name: volume / defaultVolume
props.description: Controlled or initial volume, 0 to 1 in sixteenths.

props.name: onVolumeChange
props.description: Fires from the volume keys with the new level.

props.name: awake / defaultAwake
props.description: Controlled or initial screen state.

props.name: onAwakeChange
props.description: Fires from the side key, or a tap on the dark glass, with the new state.

props.name: islandOpen / defaultIslandOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial island state.

props.name: onIslandOpenChange
props.description: Fires from a tap on the island, Escape, or a press outside it.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far the phone leans toward the pointer, in degrees, 0 to 15; 0 holds it flat.

props.name: finish
props.description: The metal band and keys.

props.name: glare
props.description: Light across the glass that moves with the tilt.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the keys' clicks. Nothing plays, and no audio context exists, unless this is on; sounds only answer the visitor.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every key and the lean, and dims the phone.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root; the default box is aspect-[3/5] at full width.

usageNotes: Volume up, Volume down and Side button are real buttons on the frame: Tab reaches each, Enter or Space presses it (the key sinks), Enter held repeats on the volume keys. The island is a button with aria-expanded; Enter opens it and Escape (with preventDefault) or a press outside closes it. Landscape is a toggle button with aria-pressed. Keyboard focus on any of them tilts the phone toward that key.

Under reduced motion nothing leans or travels: turning cross-fades the phone to the other orientation, the island opens to size and its content fades, keys darken instead of sinking, and the volume level, screen state and orientation all still show and are announced.
The frame is sized from one CSS min() of its container, so it fits any box without measurement; while it turns it eases back mid-turn so the rotated body never leaves the box.

items.title: Lid Laptop
items.tagline: Opens when you get close.
items.description: A laptop in real CSS 3D that holds any screen on its lid: the first time it is mostly in view the lid opens on the drift spring, a click opens or shuts it, and a vertical drag turns the hinge with the finger, rubber-bands past its stop and commits by projection on the glide spring with the release velocity. As the lid passes 60° the screen wakes from black; shutting is a landing, a glide fall that strikes the deck and bounces off it on the recoil spring with a thock at each contact, while a sheen slides along the deck after the pointer on drift and the screen's light spills onto it. A real button over the laptop is the keyboard's lid: Enter or Space toggles it, ArrowUp or End opens and ArrowDown or Home shuts.

props.name: children
props.description: The screen's content, laid out in a size container the shape of the screen.

props.name: label
props.description: The device's accessible name; the lid control is named after it ("Laptop lid").

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial lid state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from a tap, a drag, a key, or the laptop coming into view, with the state asked for.

props.name: openOnView
props.description: Open a shut lid the first time the laptop is mostly on screen, silently.

props.name: angle
props.description: Where the lid rests open, in degrees from the deck, 90 to 130.

props.name: finish
props.description: The aluminium of the deck, lip and lid shell.

props.name: wake
props.description: The screen wakes from black as the lid rises past 60° and sleeps below 40°; off, it is always lit.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the latch and the landing thocks. Only the visitor's own taps, drags and keys make a sound; the open on view never does.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the lid, its keys and its gestures, and dims the laptop.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root; the default box is aspect-[4/3] at full width.

usageNotes: The lid is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the screen, laid over the laptop's footprint so its focus ring outlines the laptop: Enter or Space opens and shuts it, ArrowUp or End opens, ArrowDown or Home shuts, and a polite status says "Lid open." or "Lid closed.". Screen content is inert while the lid is shut.
Under reduced motion the lid is drawn at its new angle at once with no fall or bounce, a drag still follows the finger, the deck's sheen holds still, and the screen still fades from black.
Pointer gestures start on the laptop itself, never on the empty box around it or on live content on an open screen, which keeps its own presses.

items.title: Slate Tablet
items.tagline: A tablet with its pencil.
items.description: A tablet frame with its pencil docked magnetically on the long edge: drag the pencil off and it follows the finger 1:1, turning to the writing angle and foreshortening toward the eye as it leaves the magnet, and with it out the screen takes ink whose width follows the hand's speed while the pencil rides the pointer and its shadow closes in. Thrown or brought back to the edge it snaps into the dock on the snap spring with the release velocity and a snap at contact, and the ink fades away on the exit ease; picked up by key it glides to the middle of the screen. The pencil is a real toggle button: Enter or Space picks it up and puts it back, arrow keys write while it is out (Shift moves without ink), and Escape docks it.

props.name: children
props.description: The screen's content, laid out in a size container the shape of the screen, under the ink.

props.name: label
props.description: The device's accessible name.

props.name: docked / defaultDocked
props.description: Controlled or initial pencil state.

props.name: onDockedChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, tap or key that picked the pencil up or put it back.

props.name: onStroke
props.description: Each stroke as it is finished, in fractions of the screen's width from its top left.

props.name: ink
props.description: The ink and the pencil's nib; black follows the theme's ink, blue and red are fixed pigments.

props.name: bezel
props.description: The black glass around the screen, in px, 8 to 24.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Lying down with the pencil on top, or standing with it on the right.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the nib's scratch while writing and the magnet's snap. The scratch loop runs only while a stroke moves and stops on lift.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the pencil and the ink, and dims the tablet.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root; the default box is aspect-[4/3] at full width.

usageNotes: The pencil is a button with aria-pressed (pressed is in hand): Enter or Space picks it up onto the middle of the screen and docks it again; while it is out, each arrow key writes a short line in that direction, Shift with an arrow moves without ink, and Escape (with preventDefault) docks it and clears the ink. A polite status announces each change.
Under reduced motion the pencil changes pose without travelling, a drag still follows the finger, and the ink still fades when it docks.
With the pencil docked the screen's content keeps its own pointer and keyboard; with it out, the screen becomes the ink layer (touch-action none) until the pencil goes back.

items.title: Crown Watch
items.tagline: Turn the crown to scroll.
items.description: A watch frame whose crown scrolls its screen: drag or wheel over the crown and its knurl turns 1:1 under the finger, a cylinder seen edge-on whose ridges crowd toward its top and bottom, geared so one notch is one step of content, and a swipe on the glass turns the crown with it. With detents the crown sticks at each notch and jumps through the middle while the content steps on springs.snap with a tick; without them the content follows the crown 1:1 and a flick coasts to its projected landing on springs.glide with the release velocity, and either way the ends rubber-band and spring back on snap. The crown is a vertical slider whose arrow keys turn it a notch, Page keys a screen and Home and End to the ends, and Enter or Space press it, which pushes it in on springs.flick and glides the screen home as the crown unwinds; the whole watch leans toward the pointer under a glare on its crystal.

props.name: children
props.description: The screen's content, in real px, scrolled by the crown. It wears the dark theme: a watch screen is black glass.

props.name: label
props.description: The watch's accessible name; the screen region is named after it.

props.name: title
props.description: The app's name, shown at the top left of the screen's header.

props.name: time
props.description: The clock at the top right of the screen's header.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The scroll offset in px from the top of the content (controlled / initial). Clamped to the content's measured range.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the turn, swipe, wheel, key or press that scrolled it, with the new offset in whole px: each notch as it lands with detents, the landing of a coast without.

props.name: step
props.description: Content per notch of the crown, in px (8 or more). Make it your row height so every notch lands on a row.

props.name: detents
props.description: The crown ratchets, a notch, a step and a tick at a time. Off, it turns smoothly, the content follows 1:1 and a flick coasts.

props.name: case
props.description: The case and crown metal (and a mesh band's), fixed pigments that read the same in either theme.

props.name: band
props.description: The strap: a moulded sport band with holes, stitched leather, or a fine metal mesh.

props.name: onCrownPress
props.description: The crown was pressed (tap, Enter or Space). The press also takes the screen back to the top.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the crown's detents: a tick per notch it turns through (with detents on) and a low knock at an end stop, only ever in answer to the visitor.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The crown and glass stop answering and the screen's content is inert.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, which keeps a 25:27 aspect ratio and sizes everything from its width.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the crown is a vertical role="slider" named "Crown" that controls the screen region. ArrowDown/ArrowRight turn it a notch down and ArrowUp/ArrowLeft up, PageDown/PageUp move a screen, Home and End go to the top and the end, and Enter or Space press it (back to the top). Focus that lands on content scrolled out of view brings it into view.

Reduced motion: nothing leans, springs or coasts. Content and crown go straight to each step (the knurl still turns under a dragging finger, since it is the visitor's own hand), a press darkens the crown instead of pushing it in, the ends clamp, and the scroll indicator still shows where the content is.

The wheel over the glass is only kept while the content can still move that way, so the page scrolls on past either end; over the crown it always turns the crown. The frame scales with its container's width and renders the same on the server: give it a width (around 200–260 px reads as a watch).

items.title: Tab Browser
items.tagline: A browser that behaves like one.
items.description: A browser window around a small site that behaves like one: tabs select on press and drag to reorder, the dragged tab lifting on springs.flick and following the finger 1:1 while the tabs it passes slide aside on springs.glide, each tab keeps its own Back and Forward history, page links navigate in the tab (or open a background tab with Ctrl, Cmd or the middle button), and a link or a host navigation types the new address into the bar from where it first differs. With loading on, a bar runs across under the toolbar on an ease-out for a seeded time per address while the tab's icon spins, then completes and fades as the new page cross-fades in with a short rise on glide; the light and dark skins wear those themes whatever the page does, and glass frosts the chrome over the page scrolling beneath it. The tabs are a tablist whose arrows move and select, Shift with an arrow moves a tab and Delete closes it, the address bar is a real input that takes an address, a path or a page's name, and Alt with an arrow goes back and forward.

props.name: pages
props.type: { url: string; title: string; content: React.ReactNode; icon?: React.ReactNode }[]
props.description: The site the browser can show; the first page is home, where new tabs open. Plain <a href> links to these addresses (with or without the protocol, or as /paths) navigate inside the frame; any other address shows a built-in nothing-here page, and nothing ever leaves the frame.

props.name: label
props.description: The browser's accessible name.

props.name: tabs
props.description: How many tabs are open, 1 to 4, on the first pages in order. Changing it opens or closes tabs at the end of the strip (never the one in use); the visitor can still open up to six and close them.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The address: the active tab's URL (controlled / initial). A new value from the host navigates the active tab there, typing it into the bar.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the link, address bar, Back, Forward or tab switch that asked for a new address. Controlled, the navigation is carried out when the host's value arrives, so a refused address never shows.

props.name: skin
props.description: Light or dark chrome and pages whatever the page's theme, or translucent, blurred chrome in the page's theme with the page scrolling beneath it.

props.name: loading
props.description: Navigations take a moment: a loading bar, a spinning tab icon, then the page cross-fades in. Off, pages change at once.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play clicks for the visitor's presses: tabs, each slot a dragged tab crosses, Back, Forward, Reload, links, Enter in the address bar, new and closed tabs. A page finishing loading is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Every control is disabled and the page is inert.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, a container: the window is 8:5 below 480 px wide and 12:5 above.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the tabs are a role="tablist" with roving focus; ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move to and select a tab, Home and End jump, Shift with an arrow moves the focused tab one place and Delete or Backspace closes it (the × beside each tab is a pointer convenience). Back, Forward, Reload and New tab are buttons; Back and Forward stay focusable when there is nowhere to go (aria-disabled). The address bar is a labelled input: Enter goes there, Escape restores the current address. Alt with an arrow goes back and forward from anywhere in the browser but the address bar.

Reduced motion: tabs swap places at once (a drag still follows the finger), the address appears whole instead of typing, the spinner holds still and pages cross-fade on opacity alone, while the loading bar still fills because it is information.

A polite live region says "Loading Routes." and "Routes loaded." once each per navigation, and where a moved tab now sits. The pages scroll inside the window, and each tab keeps its own scroll and history while another is in front.

items.title: Fold Phone
items.tagline: Open it up for more room.
items.description: A book-style foldable phone frame: folded it is a tall cover screen, and a sideways drag anywhere on it swings the front half round its hinge in real CSS perspective, the half's free edge following the finger 1:1 (the angle is solved from the finger's position) while its face darkens as it turns edge-on and its shadow falls across the other half, into a wide inner screen whose crease catches the light as the halves pass 150°. The hinge is a free-stop: a slow release rests where it is unless an end is near, a flick commits the way it was thrown, closing snaps shut on springs.snap with its overshoot reflected off the other half and a thock, and opening runs to the flat stop on springs.glide with the release velocity; the content re-flows between the cover's narrow size container and the wide one. The hinge is a slider in degrees whose arrows turn it 30°, Page keys 90°, Home folds, End opens flat and Enter toggles, and the Unfold button under the phone does the same.

props.name: children
props.description: The screen, laid out in a size container: narrow on the cover, wide inside, so container queries re-flow it. It takes input when the phone is folded or open flat; while it moves or rests part-open it is drawn more than once as a picture, so keep it presentational.

props.name: label
props.description: The phone's accessible name.

props.name: time
props.description: The clock in both screens' status bars.

props.name: fold / defaultFold
props.description: The posture, 0 folded shut to 1 open flat, anything between a hinge angle (controlled / initial). A new value from the host moves the hinge there silently.

props.name: onFoldChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, key or button that moved the hinge, with the posture it comes to rest at (three decimals).

props.name: finish
props.description: The frame and hinge, fixed pigments that read the same in either theme.

props.name: crease
props.description: A crease down the inner screen: a hairline, and a highlight that peaks as the halves pass 150° and fades to a faint line when flat. Off, the inner screen is seamless.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a thock as the halves clap shut (and a soft second one if they bounce) and a lighter one at the flat stop, only for the visitor's own drag, key or press.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The hinge, button and drag stop answering and the screens are inert.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, a column of the phone's 100:114 stage and the Unfold button; the phone is sized from the root's width.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the hinge is a horizontal role="slider" named "Hinge", valued in degrees with text "Folded", "Open flat" or "Open 120°". ArrowRight/ArrowUp open it 30°, ArrowLeft/ArrowDown close it 30°, PageUp/PageDown move 90°, Home folds, End opens flat, and Enter or Space open or fold it all the way. The button under the phone says what it will do (Unfold or Fold).

Reduced motion: no swing and no springs. The button and keys cross-fade the phone between postures; a drag still turns the half under the finger, since it is the visitor's own hand, and the release rests or commits at once. The crease light holds at the posture's strength, and the posture is still announced.

Only one copy of the content is exposed to assistive technology at a time — the cover's while the cover faces the viewer, the inner screen's after — and a polite live region says "Folded, cover screen.", "Open flat, wide screen." or the angle when the hinge comes to rest.

items.title: Pocket Console
items.tagline: Buttons that really press.
items.description: A handheld console frame whose keys travel: each cap goes down into its well on the flick spring as its side wall disappears, and the dome pushes it back up on snap with one crisp overshoot; the d-pad is one cross on a pivot that rocks toward the arm under the thumb, and sliding a finger round it rolls through all eight directions. Every press reaches the screen as a real keydown and keyup, so content written for a keyboard runs unchanged, while the LCD shows a pixel grid and backlight and the power light breathes on a slow tween only while it is on and on screen. From any key the arrow keys press the d-pad and A and B press A and B for as long as they are held, and Enter or Space hold the focused key.

props.name: children
props.description: The screen: any content, in a size container the shape of the LCD. It receives every press as a key event.

props.name: label
props.description: The console's accessible name.

props.name: power / defaultPower
props.description: Whether the console is switched on; the content is inert while it is off.

props.name: onPowerChange
props.description: Fires from the power switch with the state asked for.

props.name: onPress
props.description: A key went down (pointer, keyboard or assistive technology) while the console is on.

props.name: onRelease
props.description: A key came back up.

props.name: keyMap
props.description: The key each button sends into the screen. Escape is never sent.

props.name: shell
props.description: The plastic: warm grey, teal, or a smoked clear shell that shows the board inside.

props.name: grid
props.description: How strongly the LCD's pixel grid shows, 0 to 1.

props.name: backlight
props.description: How lit the LCD is, 0 (unlit, under a dark film) to 1 (glowing).

props.name: sound
props.description: Each key clicks going down and, quieter, coming up. Nothing plays on its own.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Keys take no presses and anything held is let go.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the 5:8 root; size it by width.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the d-pad is one Tab stop of four buttons with a roving tabindex; from any console control the arrow keys press the d-pad and the A and B keys press A and B for as long as they are held, Enter or Space hold the focused key, and an arrow on the d-pad moves focus to that arm. The power switch is a role=switch.
Reduced motion: no cap travels and the d-pad does not rock — a pressed key darkens at once — and the power light holds steady; every press still reaches the content and clicks.

Each press is dispatched as a KeyboardEvent at the element focused inside the screen, or at the content's first element, so an ordinary onKeyDown on the content's root hears it; the console never handles the events it sends.

items.title: Viewfinder
items.tagline: Frame it, focus, shoot.
items.description: A camera viewfinder over any scene with a two-stage shutter: holding it sinks the cap to its first stage on flick and racks the lens to the focus point's subject on the recoil spring, hunting through sharp twice before the brackets close on snap and turn green. Letting go fires — two curtains meet and part on a tween, and the frame, with the blur, exposure and roll it was taken with, shrinks out of the finder on snap and arcs into the corner slot on glide; released before the lock, the photo is soft. The nine focus points are a radiogroup the arrow keys move through, re-metering the scene and changing the shutter speed, and Space or Enter held on the shutter is the half-press, released the shot, with Escape to cancel.

props.name: children
props.description: The scene: any content, framed 3:2 in a size container.

props.name: label
props.description: The camera's accessible name.

props.name: point / defaultPoint
props.description: The focus point, 0 to 8, row by row from the top left.

props.name: onPointChange
props.description: Fires from a tap on the scene or an arrow key with the point chosen.

props.name: onShoot
props.description: Fires as the shutter falls, with the photo's count, point and whether focus had locked.

props.name: grid
props.description: The framing grid.

props.name: level
props.description: Show the electronic level, which turns green when the frame is level.

props.name: focus
props.description: Depth of field, 0 (deep, f/11) to 1 (shallow, f/1.4): how soft the scene starts, how far the lens hunts, and the aperture and shutter speed read out.

props.name: sound
props.description: The half-press detent, the focus beep and the shutter's two curtains. Nothing plays on its own.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Takes no presses; a half-press held is cancelled.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the 2:1 root; size it by width.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the focus points are a role=radiogroup with a roving tabindex — arrow keys move in two dimensions and Home/End jump; on the Shutter, Space or Enter held is the half-press and releasing takes the photo, Escape cancels a half-press (handled with preventDefault) and losing focus cancels it too. An assistive-technology click focuses first and then shoots.

Reduced motion: no hunting, rolling or flying — focus eases in on a short tween, the brackets turn green without closing, the curtains become one dim, and the photo appears in its slot; the lock, the count and the readout still change.
A polite live region says Focused. on each lock and Photo 3, sharp. or Photo 3, soft. on each shot. The photo in the slot is a copy of the scene, inert and hidden from assistive technology.

items.title: Ink Reader
items.tagline: Pages that refresh like paper.
items.description: An e-reader that lays any long text out in pages exactly as wide as its screen, measured, so a narrower reader has more pages; every turn is an e-ink refresh rather than a slide — the new page shows inverted, snaps to white and clears in three grey steps, or with a fast refresh draws at once and leaves the old page as a ghost that clears the same way, and a full flash never repeats within half a second. A swipe, a tap, the chin's keys (which press on flick and return on snap) or the keyboard turn the page, and the front-light slider follows the finger 1:1 and settles on snap, bringing the paper up from the room's own light and tinting it cool to amber while the ink stays black. On the focused page the arrow, Page and Space keys turn and Home and End jump; the slider takes arrows, Page keys, Home and End.

props.name: children
props.description: The text: any long content, laid out in pages the size of the screen.

props.name: label
props.description: The reader's accessible name.

props.name: title
props.description: The book or chapter, shown at the top of the screen.

props.name: page / defaultPage
props.description: The page shown, from 1.

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: Fires from a swipe, a tap, a key or a page key with the page asked for.

props.name: onPageCountChange
props.description: Fires when the text has been laid out, and again whenever a new size changes its page count.

props.name: light
props.description: The front light, 0 (off) to 1. The slider starts here and follows a new value.

props.name: onLightChange
props.description: Fires from the slider with the new level.

props.name: warmth
props.description: The light's colour, 0 (cool white) to 1 (amber).

props.name: refresh
props.description: A full flash (inverted, then clean) or a fast draw that leaves a ghost of the last page.

props.name: sound
props.description: A page turn's paper crinkle, a little higher going forward. Nothing plays at either end or on its own.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Takes no turns and no light changes.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the 5:7 root; size it by width.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the page is a focusable region named Page 3 of 12 — Right, Down, Page Down and Space turn forward, Left, Up, Page Up and Shift+Space turn back, Home and End go to the first and last page; Previous page and Next page are real buttons; the front light is a role=slider in percent.

Reduced motion: no inversion flash and no ghost — the new page appears under a paper wash that fades on a short tween — and the keys darken instead of travelling; the page number and the light still change.

The whole text stays in the DOM, so a screen reader reads it whatever page is shown, and a polite live region says Page 4 of 12. (or Last page.) at each turn. Inside the screen every token is redrawn in grey ink, so content styled with tokens reads as print.

items.title: Stand Monitor
items.tagline: Raise it, tilt it, rotate it.
items.description: A desktop display on a height-adjustable stand: dragging the screen lifts the panel on its column 1:1 under the finger, rubber-banding at the stops, and a heavy counterbalanced arm coasts it to where the throw would stop on the glide spring with the release velocity; dragging its top edge tilts it back in 3D on a friction hinge that holds where it is left and snaps to the nearest degree. The turn button pivots it to portrait on glide while the stand lifts it clear of the desk, the pivot height worked out each frame from the turned panel's reach, and once it settles the picture re-orients upright in a container the new shape; a cable hanging from its back swings at every move on a soft underdamped spring. The screen and its top edge are sliders for height and tilt that take arrow, Page, Home and End keys, and the turn button is a toggle.

props.name: children
props.description: The screen: any content, in a size container the shape of the screen in its current orientation.

props.name: label
props.description: The display's accessible name.

props.name: height
props.description: Where the panel sits on the column, 0 (lowest) to 1 (highest). Drags start from here, and a new value moves it.

props.name: onHeightChange
props.description: Fires from a drag or a key with the height the panel settles at.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far the top leans back, 0 to 15 degrees. Drags start from here, and a new value moves it.

props.name: onTiltChange
props.description: Fires from a drag or a key with the tilt the hinge settles at.

props.name: orientation / defaultOrientation
props.description: Which way the panel stands.

props.name: onOrientationChange
props.description: Fires from the turn button with the orientation asked for.

props.name: finish
props.description: Stand, back and bezel.

props.name: sound
props.description: The hinge creaks while the panel is dragged or turning, with the speed of the hand; the loop always stops.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Takes no drags, keys or turns.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the 16:9 root; size it by width.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the screen is a vertical role=slider for height (arrows 5%, Page keys 25%, Home/End) and its top edge one for tilt (arrows 1°, Page keys 5°, Home/End); Portrait is a toggle button with aria-pressed. The screen's content sits under the handles, not inside them, so it is read as itself.
Reduced motion: drags still follow the hand 1:1 and land where they are let go, keys jump, the turn is a cross-fade to the other orientation and the cable hangs still.
A polite live region says Portrait. or Landscape. on a turn and the reading once at the end of a drag (Height 60%., Tilt 9°.).

items.title: Loom Field
items.tagline: A weave that ripples under the hand.
items.description: A background of woven cloth, warp and weft interlaced thread by thread in a plain, twill or basket weave, with your content on top; a hovering hand is a light touch and a press goes in deep, opening an eye in the weave as the warps part sideways and the wefts up and down. Every crossing is a spring held straight along its thread by tension, so the threads lag the finger, a flick runs a ripple down them, and a lifted hand lets the eye close with two small overshoots near the recoil spring's damping, while the press itself eases in over a blink and out over the base duration. A transparent button behind the content is the keyboard's way in: arrow keys move the hand and Space or Enter held presses into the cloth.

props.name: children
props.description: The content on top of the cloth, in its own layer that fills the box: a hero, a heading, a call to action.

props.name: weave
props.description: How the threads interlace: a checker, a 3/1 diagonal rib like denim, or threads working in pairs.

props.name: press
props.description: How hard the hand presses, 0 to 1: how wide the threads part (0.7 to 3.2 thread pitches) and how deep the dent's shade reads.

props.name: thread
props.description: The warp's dye, a fixed pigment; the weft is the same dye washed into the page, so it follows the theme.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the cloth's keyboard surface.

props.name: onPressChange
props.description: The hand pressed into the cloth (true) or let go (false), reported from the pointer or keys that did it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The cloth is drawn and holds still; the hand is ignored and touch scrolling is left to the page.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box; the default is h-full w-full, so it fills its container.

usageNotes: Keyboard: a transparent button behind the content, after it in tab order, named by label and described by a hint. Focused from the keyboard the hand rests at the centre as a light touch with a ring; arrow keys move it 16 px (Shift: 48), Space or Enter held presses in and releasing lets go, and a click from assistive technology presses for a moment. A polite status says Pressed into the cloth once per press.

Reduced motion: no springs, ripple or wake; the threads part to the eye's exact shape on every pointer or key move, redrawn directly, and close at once when the hand lifts. Nothing runs between events.
The frame loop runs only while threads are moving, on screen and in a visible page; a still cloth costs nothing. Presses on the content's own links, buttons and fields are left to them.

items.title: Ink Marble
items.tagline: Comb the ink.
items.description: A background of marbled paper still on the bath, bands of ink floating on the size with your content on top; a drag pulls a comb through the ink, its tines standing across the stroke, and the ink near each tine is carried along, so a stroke across the bands feathers them into chevrons and a second one back makes a nonpareil. Nothing here springs: the comb is direct manipulation, the ink relaxes back into its bands on a seven-second exponential, the sheet sways a few pixels on slow currents while it is on screen, and a keyboard pass travels on a linear tween. A transparent button behind the content is the keyboard's way in: arrow keys comb from the hand and Enter or Space combs a full pass across the sheet.

props.name: children
props.description: The content on top of the paper, in its own layer that fills the box: a hero, a heading, a call to action.

props.name: bands
props.description: How many bands of ink float across the sheet, 4 to 10.

props.name: comb
props.description: The tool, 0 to 1: a single stylus at 0, nine fine tines 12 px apart at 1.

props.name: palette
props.description: The four inks on the bath, fixed pigments mixed a little into the page, with veins of paper between the bands.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the paper's keyboard surface.

props.name: onCombChange
props.description: A stroke of the comb began (true) or ended (false), reported from the pointer or keys that made it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The ink still drifts; it cannot be combed, and touch scrolling is left to the page.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box; the default is h-full w-full, so it fills its container.

usageNotes: Keyboard: a transparent button behind the content, after it in tab order, named by label and described by a hint. Focused from the keyboard the comb shows at the centre; each arrow key combs 24 px that way (Shift: 72) and a held arrow keeps combing; Enter, Space or a click from assistive technology combs one pass right across the sheet through the hand in the last direction. A polite status says Combed across the paper after a pass.

Reduced motion: no drift and no continuous relaxing; combing still redraws as the hand moves and a keyboard pass is applied at once. The ink settles in still steps, the marks halving 1.6 s after the last stroke and every 1.6 s after, with no motion between steps.

The sheet is a map from each 2 px cell to where its ink came from, resampled by the comb and looked up through prefiltered band tables, so combing never repaints colours and squeezed bands blend instead of flickering. The loop runs only on screen in a visible page, drawing at 30 fps when idle.

items.title: Koi Pond
items.tagline: They scatter, then return.
items.description: A background that is a garden pond seen from above, koi gliding in loose schools under a gently rippling surface while lily pads drift on it, with your content on top; the pointer is a hand over the water, whose shadow makes nearby koi edge away and whose stillness draws the bolder ones back to mill around it. A touch spreads a ring and scatters every koi within reach: they steer away at up to seven radians a second with a burst of speed, glide as the fright fades over a second and a half, then return; the koi steer rather than spring, each body rebuilt every frame from a spine that follows its head, and under reduced motion the scatter is a cross-fade on the base duration. A transparent button behind the content is the keyboard's way in: arrow keys move the hand and Space or Enter touches the water.

props.name: children
props.description: The content on top of the water, in its own layer that fills the box: a hero, a heading, a call to action.

props.name: fish
props.description: How many koi live in the pond, 3 to 12; changing it adds or removes koi without disturbing the others.

props.name: ripple
props.description: How alive the surface is, 0 to 1: the glints, the rings, the shimmer over the koi and the pads' bob. At 0 the water is glass.

props.name: water
props.description: The pond's water, pigments mixed a little into the page so the pond sits in its theme.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the pond's keyboard surface.

props.name: onScatter
props.description: A touch on the water scattered this many koi, reported from the press or key that touched it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The koi swim on; the hand is ignored and touch scrolling is left to the page.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box; the default is h-full w-full, so it fills its container.

usageNotes: Keyboard: a transparent button behind the content, after it in tab order, named by label and described by a hint. Focused from the keyboard the hand hovers at the centre with its shadow and a ring; arrow keys move it 16 px (Shift: 48), Space or Enter touches the water and, held, keeps the hand in so arrow moves sweep a wake; a click from assistive technology touches once. A polite status says how many koi scattered, once per touch.

Reduced motion: a still pond with the koi at their places, pads and glints still and no loop. The hand's shadow follows as a direct redraw; a touch cross-fades the near koi to places three body lengths away and a ring outline fades in place, and 2.6 s later they cross-fade back. Nothing travels.

The loop runs only while the pond is on screen in a visible page, about a couple of milliseconds a frame for twelve koi. Koi length scales with the box, so a small card has smaller koi rather than fewer.

items.title: Stained Glass
items.tagline: Light through leaded glass.
items.description: A backdrop of leaded glass whose irregular panes, cut from a seed, glow where the light falls: the pointer is the light, trailing the hand on the glide spring and drifting home to its resting place on the drift spring, while the panes' own colours spill over the leads as soft cast light and the came glints along the side that faces it. A new seed, pane count or palette re-leads the window from the light outward, and frames run only while the light moves and the window is on screen. The light is a real 2D slider under the content: arrow keys move it, Home and End go to the side edges, Page Up and Page Down to the top and bottom.

props.name: children
props.description: What sits over the window: a hero, a heading, a call to action.

props.name: panes
props.description: How many panes the window is cut into, 12 to 60.

props.name: glow
props.description: How hot the light is, 0 to 1: a soft wash, or a bright core whose coloured light spills over the leads.

props.name: palette
props.description: The glass.

props.name: seed
props.description: Leads the window: the same seed always cuts the same panes. A new one re-leads it, from the light outward.

props.name: rest
props.description: Where the light rests when nobody is moving it, as fractions of the box.

props.name: onLightChange
props.type: (light: { x: number; y: number } | null) => void
props.description: Fires when the visitor moves the light (pointer, touch or keys), and with null when it goes back to rest.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Let the pointer and the keyboard move the light. Off, the window is decoration only: no tab stop, no pointer handling.

props.name: label
props.description: The light control's accessible name.

props.name: className
props.description: Sets the size.

usageNotes: The light is a role="slider" with aria-roledescription "2D slider" under the content: arrow keys move it 5% (Shift 20%), Home/End go to the left/right edge, Page Up/Page Down to the top/bottom, and keyboard focus lights the window just as hover does.
Under reduced motion the light jumps to the pointer instead of gliding, home is instant and a new window cross-fades; nothing runs between moves, and the glow, cast light and glints still show.
Content sits in a relative layer over the window; a busy window reads best behind a frosted panel. On touch, a tap or a sideways drag places the light and vertical swipes still scroll the page.

items.title: Paper Facets
items.tagline: Folded light.
items.description: A backdrop of folded card: a low-poly field of flat facets lit by a lamp the pointer carries over the sheet, each facet shaded from its own normal so faces turned toward the lamp brighten, faces turned away fall into shadow and glints run across the folds. The lamp trails the hand on the glide spring and drifts home on the drift spring when the pointer leaves, and a new seed refolds the sheet on the drift spring as the card relaxes and creases again. The lamp is a real 2D slider under the content: arrow keys move it, Home and End go to the side edges, Page Up and Page Down to the top and bottom.

props.name: children
props.description: What sits on the paper: a hero, a heading, a call to action. Its text takes an ink that reads on the paper.

props.name: facets
props.description: About how many facets show, 20 to 120: broad folds or a fine crumple.

props.name: relief
props.description: How deep the folds are, 0 to 1: flat card, or hard creases with dark valleys.

props.name: paper
props.description: The card.

props.name: seed
props.description: Folds the sheet: the same seed always makes the same folds. A new one refolds it.

props.name: rest
props.description: Where the lamp rests when nobody is moving it, as fractions of the box.

props.name: onLightChange
props.type: (light: { x: number; y: number } | null) => void
props.description: Fires when the visitor moves the lamp (pointer, touch or keys), and with null when it goes back to rest.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Let the pointer and the keyboard move the lamp. Off, the sheet is decoration only: no tab stop, no pointer handling.

props.name: label
props.description: The lamp control's accessible name.

props.name: className
props.description: Sets the size.

usageNotes: The lamp is a role="slider" with aria-roledescription "2D slider" under the content: arrow keys move it 5% (Shift 20%), Home/End go to the left/right edge, Page Up/Page Down to the top/bottom, and keyboard focus lights the sheet just as hover does.

Under reduced motion the lamp jumps to the pointer instead of gliding, home is instant and a refold cross-fades with no vertex travel; nothing runs between moves, and the shading still follows the lamp.
The content layer's text colour is set to an ink that reads on the chosen paper (dark on white and kraft, pale on ink), also exposed as --paper-ink.

items.title: Bokeh Night
items.tagline: City lights out of focus.
items.description: A backdrop of a seeded night street seen through a fast lens, every lamp, headlight, sign and far window drawn as the disc a real lens makes of it, sized by the circle-of-confusion law so near lights balloon when the focus is far and the far city blooms when it is near; discs at the frame's edge are cut into cat's-eyes and street-level lights shine back from the wet road. The pointer's height sets the focus plane and the lens racks to it on the glide spring while the traffic drifts and the camera sways, only on screen. The focus is a real vertical slider under the content: arrow keys rack it nearer or farther, Page Up and Page Down by a quarter, Home to the nearest lights and End to infinity.

props.name: children
props.description: What sits over the street: a hero, a heading, a call to action. Its text takes a lamp-white that reads on the night.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The focus plane: 0 focuses on the nearest lights (2 m), 1 at infinity.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the pointer, tap or key that moved the focus, with the new value.

props.name: aperture
props.description: The lens's aperture: round discs, or six-bladed hexagons.

props.name: density
props.description: How busy the street is, 0 to 1: a quiet side street to a busy avenue.

props.name: warmth
props.description: The share of sodium lamps, tungsten headlights and warm signs, 0 to 1, against LED white and teal.

props.name: seed
props.description: Lays out the street: the same seed always makes the same street.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Let the pointer and the keyboard move the focus. Off, the street is decoration only: no tab stop, no pointer handling.

props.name: label
props.description: The focus control's accessible name.

props.name: className
props.description: Sets the size.

usageNotes: The focus is a vertical role="slider" under the content with aria-valuetext such as "Focus at 8 m": ArrowUp/ArrowRight rack it 5% farther, ArrowDown/ArrowLeft nearer, Page Up/Page Down by 25%, Home to the nearest lights and End to infinity; on touch a tap focuses at that height.
Under reduced motion nothing drifts, sways or twinkles: one still frame that refocuses instantly, one redraw per pointer move or key, because the focus is the value.
Controlled: the lens racks only when the host's value changes, so a host that refuses a move keeps its focus. The content layer's text is set to a lamp-white exposed as --bokeh-ink.

items.title: Quilt Grid
items.tagline: A patchwork that re-stitches.
items.description: A backdrop sewn from twelve classic quilt blocks — half-square triangles, pinwheels, flying geese, log cabins, Ohio stars — in printed fabrics with seams and running stitches, drawn in SVG and re-coloured by the theme. Waves re-stitch it from the pointer: ring by ring on a cascade delay, each block either turns a quarter turn on the snap spring or trades places with its outward neighbour on the glide spring, lifting with a soft shadow mid-move and landing flat, while a click re-stitches with a wave where half the blocks swap and a gentle ambient wave starts somewhere every few seconds. The keyboard path is a role="application" surface where arrow keys move a stitched marker and turn the blocks round it and Enter or Space re-stitch from it, announced once.

props.name: blocks
props.description: Blocks across the width, 6 to 16. A block is never drawn smaller than 32px, so a narrow quilt has fewer; the motifs stay seeded by cell when it is re-cut.

props.name: wave
props.description: How far a wave carries, 0 to 1: the block and its four neighbours at 0, the whole quilt at 1. Ambient waves carry half as far. A change sends one wave from the middle at the new reach.

props.name: palette
props.description: The fabrics, as pigments whose lightness follows the theme (full dye on light, dimmed on dark). A change re-dyes the quilt as a wave from the centre.

props.name: seed
props.description: Which quilt: every block's motif, fabrics, print and starting turn follow from it, the same on the server and the client.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the keyboard surface.

props.name: onWave
props.description: A hover, an arrow key or a re-stitch started a wave: its origin block (col, row from 0), how many blocks turned and swapped, and press: true for a re-stitch. Ambient waves are not reported.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Ambient only: the quilt ignores the pointer and the keyboard and leaves the tab order.

props.name: children
props.description: What sits on the quilt — a hero, a heading — in a layer above it. Presses on its own controls never start a wave.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, which fills its container (h-full w-full); set its size and radius here.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab reaches the quilt's role="application" surface; arrow keys move a stitched marker and turn the blocks round it (the same wave a pointer starts entering that block), Home and End jump along the row, Enter or Space re-stitch from it, and a polite live region announces each re-stitch once.

Reduced motion: nothing turns, slides or wanders and there are no ambient waves — a wave changes every block in its reach at once and each changed block dips in opacity and comes back, so the new pattern is still seen; palette changes cross-fade.

Ambient waves run only while the quilt is on screen in a visible page and nobody is pointing at it; touch uses touch-action: pan-y, so a sideways slide sends waves and a vertical one scrolls the page.

items.title: Cloud Chamber
items.tagline: Tracks of invisible particles.
items.description: A canvas backdrop of a side-lit cloud chamber: invisible particles leave vapour trails that condense just behind them, then broaden, break into droplets, drift down with the gas and curl in its currents until they fade — fat alphas from a source needle, thin betas that wander and tighten into spirals as they slow, long muons from above with the small curls they knock loose. The pointer is a magnet: every particle is integrated a step at a time in the field of the moment (κ = qB/p, falling off like a pole's), so betas hook round it and slow ones are caught in a spiral, while a glow and a curl arrow mark it and its presence eases in on a short tween; a press flips its pole. The keyboard path is a role="application" surface where focus brings the magnet in, arrow keys move it and Enter or Space flip it, with the new pole announced once.

props.name: rate
props.description: How many particles cross the chamber, 0 to 1: from one every second or so up to about ten a second on a 760×232 box, scaled by area.

props.name: field
props.description: The magnet's strength, 0 to 1, with the chamber's own weak field: 0 leaves every track straight, 1 coils slow electrons tight round the pointer. The chamber's own field alone curls slow electrons at the ends of their tracks.

props.name: tint
props.description: The vapour and the chamber's lamp. The trails mix it with the page's foreground: dark ink on the light theme, lit vapour on the dark one.

props.name: pole / defaultPole
props.description: Which way the magnet bends the tracks, controlled or uncontrolled. The curl arrow round the magnet shows the way an electron turns.

props.name: onPoleChange
props.description: Fires from the press or the key that flipped the pole, with the new pole.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the keyboard surface.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Ambient only: the chamber keeps running but ignores the pointer and the keyboard and leaves the tab order.

props.name: children
props.description: What sits over the chamber — a hero, a heading — in a layer above it. Presses on its own controls never flip the pole.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, which fills its container (h-full w-full); set its size and radius here.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab reaches the chamber's role="application" surface and brings the magnet in at the middle with a visible mark; arrow keys move it (Shift for larger steps), Enter or Space flip its pole, and a polite live region says the new pole once. Touch uses touch-action: pan-y: a sideways slide drags the magnet, a tap places it for a moment and a second tap flips it.

Reduced motion: the chamber is a still photograph of a seeded set of tracks at assorted ages — no drift, no curl, no new tracks, no frame loop — and moving the magnet re-runs those same tracks in its field and redraws once, so they still bend round it.
The canvas is at most 2× resolution, reads its colours from its own computed style (re-read on a theme or tint change) and runs its frame loop only while on screen in a visible page.

items.title: Ferro Pool
items.tagline: Spikes that reach for the magnet.
items.description: A canvas backdrop of a ferrofluid pool seen at a low angle — glossy near-black at the front, reflecting more of the room toward the back, with a softbox lying on it as a long soft band. The pointer is a magnet: its footprint is found through the same perspective that draws the pool, every site of a jittered hexagonal lattice feels its field, and above a threshold each rises into a spike on its own underdamped spring, so the crown jiggles up, leans along the field lines toward the magnet, stands on a mound that bulges beneath it and sinks back with a wobble when the magnet leaves, every spike shaded by a lit flank, a specular line and a rim on the side the slowly drifting light comes from. A click pulses the field — it surges and a ring runs out across the pool kicking every spike it passes — and the keyboard path is a role="application" surface where focus brings the magnet in, arrow keys move it and Enter or Space pulse.

props.name: strength
props.description: The magnet, 0 to 1: how far its field reaches across the pool, how tall the spikes grow and how far they lean toward it. On a resting pool a change holds the magnet over the middle for a moment, so the new crown shows.

props.name: spikes
props.description: Spikes across the pool's front edge, 8 to 32: a few tall cones or a dense bristle. The lattice is seeded, so it is the same pool every time. On a resting pool a change shows itself the same way.

props.name: sheen
props.description: How much the fluid shines, 0 to 1: the lit flanks, specular lines, rims and the softbox's reflection. 0 is matte ink, and a matte pool stops drawing once it is flat.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the keyboard surface.

props.name: onPulse
props.description: A click, a tap, Enter or Space pulsed the field.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Ambient only: the pool ignores the pointer and the keyboard and leaves the tab order.

props.name: children
props.description: What sits over the pool — a hero, a heading — in a layer above it. Presses on its own controls never pulse the field.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, which fills its container (h-full w-full); set its size and radius here.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab reaches the pool's role="application" surface and brings the magnet over its middle with a visible mark; arrow keys move it (Shift for larger steps), Enter or Space pulse the field, and leaving takes the magnet away. Touch uses touch-action: pan-y: a tap places the magnet and pulses, a sideways slide drags it, and it lifts away 1.6 seconds after the finger does.

Reduced motion: no springs, no wobble, no ripple and a light that stays put — the spikes are drawn exactly where the field puts them, once per move, a pulse shows its surged spikes for a moment and leaving draws the flat pool; no frame loop runs.

The canvas is at most 2× resolution, reads its colours from its own computed style (re-read on a theme change) and runs its frame loop only while on screen in a visible page; springs are integrated only while something is moving.

items.title: Tartan Shift
items.tagline: A plaid that slides into place.
items.description: A tartan cloth as a backdrop, built the way a weaver builds it from layered SVG patterns: a symmetric sett laid as the weft, the same sett as the warp, and the warp shown only through a stepped 2/2 twill so crossing colours blend on the diagonal, with shaded wales and a broad light across the cloth. When the palette or the sett changes, all sixteen stripes glide from their old places and widths to their new ones on the glide spring while the new colours are laid in behind a diagonal front that crosses the cloth along the twill on a tween, a bright thread in the new pinstripe colour running along it like a shuttle. It drifts gently with scroll — its travel through the viewport, in any scroll container, becomes a diagonal offset the patterns follow on the drift spring — and slides very slowly by itself while on screen; it is decorative, with no gesture of its own, so nothing needs a keyboard path.

props.name: sett
props.description: The pattern's scale and character: fine is a 96px repeat of 2px threads with narrow lines and overchecks, bold a 180px repeat of 2.5px threads with broad blocks. A change slides the stripes and re-threads the cloth.

props.name: palette
props.description: The cloth's dyes — green, navy, black, red and yellow; grey, charcoal, cream, coral and teal; brown, rust, ochre, olive and cream — as pigments whose lightness follows the theme. A change slides the stripes into the new sett and re-threads it; a change mid-crossing finishes from where it is.

props.name: drift
props.description: How far scrolling carries the cloth and how fast it slides by itself, 0 to 1. 0 holds it still.

props.name: children
props.description: What sits on the cloth — a hero, a heading — in a normal layer above it.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root, which fills its container (h-full w-full); set its size and radius here.

usageNotes: Decorative: the drawing is aria-hidden and has no gesture of its own. Its two motions are answered by the host (a palette or sett change) and by scrolling, both of which already work from the keyboard; the demo's cloth picker is a role="radiogroup" with arrow keys.
Reduced motion: nothing slides or drifts — no scroll drift and no slow slide — and a palette or sett change cross-fades the new cloth over the old one, already in its new sett.

Every motion moves the patterns' own x, y, width and height attributes, so nothing lays out again; the slow slide runs only while the cloth is on screen in a visible page and repaints only when it has moved a quarter of a pixel.

items.title: Follow Knot
items.tagline: The plus ties itself into a check.
items.description: A follow button whose plus is one rope: pressed, its free end sweeps round on a tween into a loop that crosses over the standing part, and the loop cinches into a knot at the vertex of a check on the snap spring, thrown hard enough by tension that its one overshoot reads as the knot pulling past tight. The label slides from Follow to Following on snap inside a slot as wide as the longest word, and the follower figure rolls one on, units first; hovering or keyboard-focusing a followed button loosens and turns the knot and offers Unfollow in danger ink, and a press unties it rope-first before the words and figure follow. It is a button with aria-pressed and a constant name, Space and Enter press it, and under reduced motion the rope swaps between plus and check with a short fade while the digits change in place.

props.name: pressed / defaultPressed
props.description: Whether the viewer follows, controlled or initial.

props.name: onPressedChange
props.description: Fires from the press that changed it, with the new state; the rope moves once the state actually changes, so a refused press never shows a false knot.

props.name: label
props.description: The word before following, and the start of the accessible name.

props.name: pressedLabel
props.description: The word once following; the slot keeps the longest word's width.

props.name: releaseLabel
props.description: The word while a followed button is hovered or keyboard-focused: what a press will do.

props.name: target
props.description: Who or what is followed, appended to the accessible name ("Follow Fieldline Journal").

props.name: count
props.description: Followers without this viewer; the button adds one while followed. Omit to hide the figure.

props.name: formatCount
props.description: How the figure is written; digits roll, other characters swap.

props.name: describeCount
props.description: The figure as spoken, read as the button's description.

props.name: tension
props.description: How hard the knot is pulled, 0 to 1: a loose eye that settles softly, or a hard bead that snaps past tight.

props.name: untieAngle
props.description: How far the knot turns as it loosens under a hover, in degrees.

props.name: tieDuration
props.description: How long the free end takes to sweep its loop, in ms; the cinch starts 60% of the way in.

props.name: previewDelay
props.description: How long a pointer rests on a followed button before it offers to unfollow, in ms.

props.name: compact
props.description: Icon only: the knot alone in a round button, the words in its accessible name.

props.name: size
props.description: 32, 36 or 44px tall.

props.name: accent
props.description: The unfollowed pill's fill, any CSS colour.

props.name: accentInk
props.description: Words and rope on that fill.

props.name: danger
props.description: Ink of the unfollow preview.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a tick as the free end crosses over and a snap as the knot pulls tight; only ever for the visitor's own press.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Not pressable, drawn at half strength.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the button.

usageNotes: Space and Enter press it through the native click; the accessible name stays label + target in both states, aria-pressed carries the state and the figure is the button's description.

Under reduced motion the rope swaps between plus and check with a 150ms fade, the words cross-fade in place and the digits change without rolling; the fill and ink still change, because following is information.
Controlled: pass pressed and onPressedChange. The press reports first and the knot ties only when the host answers, so a refused follow never shows a check.
The Unfollow offer never appears under the pointer that just followed; it waits until the pointer leaves and comes back, or for keyboard focus to arrive.
count is the figure without this viewer, so a host can pass its server count before the viewer's own follow is counted.

items.title: Mute Cone
items.tagline: Sound folds back into the speaker.
