props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the timeline and stops every gesture and control.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root (a rounded, clipped container-query box).

usageNotes: Keyboard: the markers (free events and bubbles, in time order) are one tab stop; Left and Right step between them and glide the view to keep them in sight, Home and End jump, + and - zoom about the focused marker, Enter or Space selects an event or opens a bubble (focus follows its first member once it has split out), Page Up and Page Down pan a screen, and Escape clears a selection with preventDefault.

Only Ctrl or Cmd with the wheel (and a trackpad pinch) zooms, and a horizontal or Shift wheel pans; a plain vertical wheel is left to the page. The viewport is touch-pan-y, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the page while a horizontal one pans and two fingers pinch.

Times are UTC (plus utcOffset) and labels are formatted by hand, never from the locale, so the server render and the hydrated page match; the server lays out the axis for 1600px and the browser corrects it once measured.
Under reduced motion steps and pans jump, a throw stops under the finger and bubbles swap in place; labels still cross-fade by spacing because which labels are legible is information.
Every per-frame value — ticks, labels, markers, bubbles — is a motion value; React re-renders only when a bubble forms or splits or the axis changes unit, and nothing runs while the view is still.

items.title: Snap Board
items.tagline: Drag a widget; the others make way.
items.description: A dashboard layout editor on a grid of columns and rows: a widget dragged by its header lifts on the flick spring and follows the finger 1:1, rubber-banding past the board's edges, and each time the cell under it changes a detent clicks, the ghost moves to the landing cell on snap and every widget in the way glides aside on glide. Let go, it flies to the ghost with the throw's own velocity and lands with a thock, and the layout is reported once; the corner resizes the same way, and push decides whether the others float back up, stay where they land or trade places. Every grip is a button: Space or Enter picks a widget up, arrows move it a cell (the widget snapping along with its ghost), Shift and arrows resize it, Enter drops and Escape puts everything back.

props.name: widgets
props.description: The widgets on the board: id, title, icon, content, and min and max size in cells. Content sits in a container-query box so it can lay itself out for the size it is given.

props.name: layout / defaultLayout
props.description: One item per widget: id, x and y of its top-left cell, w and h in cells. Anything wider than the columns or overlapping is clamped and settled.

props.name: onLayoutChange
props.description: Fires from the drop, resize or key that changed the layout, with all of it. A drop that changes nothing is not reported.

props.name: onMove
props.description: A drop that changed the layout: the widget dropped and the ids of the others that made way.

props.name: onDragChange
props.description: A widget picked up by pointer or key, its landing cell (id, mode and item) each time it changes, and null when it is put down.

props.name: columns
props.description: The grid's columns. Column guides fade in under the widgets while one is held.

props.name: push
props.description: How the others make way: pushed and floated back up into any gap, pushed and left where they land, or the widget under the drop trades places with the dragged one.

props.name: ghost
props.description: The landing preview: a dashed accent outline, an accent wash with a solid edge, or nothing but the others making way.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: One row's height, px.

props.name: gap
props.description: The space between cells, px.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: The tallest the board gets before it scrolls inside itself, px or any CSS length.

props.name: editable
props.description: Off: no grips and no corners, a plain dashboard.

props.name: label
props.description: The board's accessible name.

props.name: moveLabel
props.description: Each grip's accessible name.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: Each corner's accessible name.

props.name: accent
props.description: The ghost, the picked-up ring, the column guides and the default widgets' charts. Any CSS colour.

props.name: sound
props.description: A detent click at every cell the target crosses and a thock on every drop (louder for a longer flight). Nothing sounds when the host changes the layout.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the board and stops every drag, resize and key.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root (the labelled region that clips the board).

usageNotes: Keyboard: each widget's grip is a button (aria-pressed while held). Space or Enter picks it up; arrow keys move it a cell and the widget snaps along with its ghost while the others make way; Shift with arrows resizes (the corner button picks up in resize mode); Enter or Space drops; Escape puts everything back with preventDefault; Tab or blur drops it where it is. Each step is spoken once in a polite live region.

A drag is tracked in the board's own frame, so the widget stays under the finger even if the board grows or the page scrolls; only the header and the corner are touch-none, so the widget bodies still scroll the page.

With push="compact" a widget dragged down onto another by that one's height hops it above, so any order is reachable; "free" leaves gaps where you leave them; "swap" trades places with the widget under the drop when it fits.

Under reduced motion nothing lifts, flies or glides: widgets and the ghost jump to their cells (the dragged one still follows the finger), the board's height jumps; the layout and every announcement are unchanged.
Before the board is measured (and on the server) widgets are placed with the same geometry as CSS percentages, so the first paint is already the final layout.

items.title: Collapse Header
items.tagline: The title docks as you scroll.
items.description: A scroll container with a large header whose title is one heading floating over the page: as you scroll it moves 1:1 with the page toward the toolbar, easing across to its docked place beside the back button (or centred) and down to toolbar size, while the cover parallaxes and fades behind it and the actions fold into the overflow button as they slide up to meet the bar. Past the threshold the title lets go of the scroll and docks by itself on the snap spring; docked, the header stays compact however you scroll until you come back to the very top, where it re-expands on glide. The scroll area is a focusable region, so arrow, Page, Home and End keys reach the same states, and the overflow button is a menu button whose menu holds the folded actions.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading that docks in the toolbar. Large it may wrap to two lines; docked it is always one clean line.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: The line under the title; it scrolls away with the page.

props.name: eyebrow
props.description: A small label above the title.

props.name: cover
props.description: Fills the cover; the default is drawn in the accent and mixed toward the page, so it reads in both themes.

props.name: actions
props.description: The row of actions under the title (id, label, icon); they fold into the overflow menu as they reach the toolbar.

props.name: onAction
props.description: An action pressed, inline or from the overflow menu.

props.name: onBack
props.description: The back button. Without it the button is still drawn, for the docked title to sit beside.

props.name: backLabel
props.description: The back button's accessible name.

props.name: overflowLabel
props.description: The overflow button's and its menu's accessible name.

props.name: onDockChange
props.description: Fires from the scroll that docked the title (true) or re-expanded the header at the top (false).

props.name: parallax
props.description: How much slower than the page the cover moves, 0 to 1: 0 scrolls with the page, 1 stays put behind it.

props.name: dock
props.description: Where the title docks in the toolbar: beside the back button, or centred.

props.name: threshold
props.description: How far through its travel (0.3 to 1) the title lets go of the scroll and docks by itself on the snap spring; 1 never lets go early.

props.name: coverHeight
props.description: The cover's height in px; a fifth taller when the header is 560px wide or more.

props.name: height
props.description: The container's height, px or any CSS length. It scrolls inside itself.

props.name: size
props.description: The large title: 24, 28 or 34 px. It docks at 17 px.

props.name: accent
props.description: The cover drawing and the docked toolbar's rule. Any CSS colour.

props.name: children
props.description: The page under the header.

props.name: sound
props.description: A swish as the visitor's scroll docks the title (higher) and as it re-expands the header at the top (lower). Nothing else plays.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root (a rounded, clipped container-query box that carries data-state="expanded" or "docked").

usageNotes: The scroll area is a focusable region labelled by the title: arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down, Space, Home and End scroll it, so docking (scroll down) and re-expanding (Home) have the same keyboard path as a finger. The toolbar comes first in the DOM, so Tab meets the back button before the page.

The overflow button is inert until the actions have folded into it; it is a menu button (Enter, Space or ArrowDown open it) whose items move with arrows, Home and End, and Escape or Tab close it with focus back on the button. Focus on an action that folds moves to the overflow button, and back to the first action when they unfold.
There is one h2 throughout: the floating title is the heading, and the one-line docked copy inside it is aria-hidden. A polite live region says "Title docked" and "Header expanded" once per change.

Under reduced motion nothing flies or parallaxes: the title scrolls with the page and a docked copy cross-fades into the toolbar when the threshold is passed, the actions cross-fade as the overflow button fades in, and the cover only fades.
Every per-frame value is a motion value read from the scroll; React hears only when the title docks or re-expands and when the actions finish folding, and nothing runs while the page is still.

items.title: Answer Panel
items.tagline: Read it while it is still being written.
items.description: An AI answer you can read while it is written: thoughts arrive one at a time on snap, then the answer streams token by token behind a caret, its numbered citation pills scaling in on snap where each claim is made and lifting their source card on snap when hovered or focused. When the text is done the Thinking block collapses on glide into a one-line summary, the actions and follow-ups rise in a cascade, a pressed thumb lands on recoil, and Regenerate rewinds the text on the move ease before writing again. Tab reaches every pill, thumb and follow-up; focusing a pill opens its card, Enter opens the source and Escape closes the card.

props.name: question
props.description: What was asked; names the panel.

props.name: answer
props.description: The answer. Blank lines split paragraphs, "- " starts a bullet, and [n] cites sources[n - 1].

props.name: sources
props.description: The sources the answer can cite, in citation order: title, site, snippet, meta.

props.name: thoughts
props.description: The steps taken before writing, each with its duration in ms.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: Follow-up questions offered once the answer is done.

props.name: model
props.description: The model that wrote it, printed in the action row.

props.name: status / defaultStatus
props.description: The lifecycle. Controlled, the panel asks for the next status and waits for the host.

props.name: onStatusChange
props.description: Fires when the panel moves on: thinking finished, text finished, or Regenerate pressed.

props.name: speed
props.description: Tokens per second the answer is written at; thoughts hold longer when it is slow.

props.name: citations
props.description: Citation markers as numbered pills, bare superscript numbers, or not at all.

props.name: followups
props.description: Follow-ups as full-width rows, wrapping chips, or not at all.

props.name: feedback / defaultFeedback
props.description: The visitor's rating of the answer.

props.name: onFeedbackChange
props.description: Fires from the thumb that changed it, and with null when Regenerate clears it.

props.name: onFeedbackReason
props.description: The reason picked after Not helpful.

props.name: reasons
props.description: Reasons offered after Not helpful.

props.name: onRegenerate
props.description: Regenerate or Retry was pressed. Swap `answer` here; the old text rewinds first.

props.name: onFollowup
props.description: A follow-up was chosen.

props.name: onSourceOpen
props.description: A citation or a listed source was opened.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Copy was pressed, with the plain text sent to the clipboard (markers out, sources listed after).

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: What the error line says.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the thumbs, the copy, the disclosure and the rewind. The stream itself is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the actions, feedback and follow-ups; the answer still reads.

props.name: className
props.description: Give the panel a height (h-[32rem]) and its body scrolls inside it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab reaches the Thinking disclosure, each citation pill, the actions, thumbs, reasons and follow-ups. Focusing a pill opens its source card (described by it); Enter opens the source, Escape closes the card.

Drive it live by controlling `status` and appending to `answer` as chunks arrive: the panel paces bursty chunks into a steady stream, and setting `status="done"` flushes the rest quickly. Uncontrolled, it plays `thoughts` and `answer` by itself.
The body follows the caret only while the reader is at the bottom; scrolling up keeps their place and shows a Jump to latest pill.
Reduced motion: tokens still arrive (without fades), the caret does not blink, cards and pills appear on opacity, lists open at once and Regenerate clears instantly before re-streaming.
Pacing runs on requestAnimationFrame only while the panel is on screen and the page is visible; a polite status announces each phase once, never per token.

items.title: Agent Run
items.tagline: Watch the plan; approve the risky step.
items.description: An agent's run watched as it happens: steps move from pending to running to done or failed with live durations, nodes filling and ticking on flick, tool calls opening to a measured height on glide, and a time and cost meter whose digits run with the clock. A risky step halts the run behind an inline gate that glides open; holding Approve sweeps a linear fill, drains on the exit ease if let go early, and lands on recoil before the gate folds into a stamp. The timeline scrubs 1:1 and rubber-bands against its ends and any undecided gate, springing back on glide; arrow keys move the playhead and the plan, Space or Enter held approves.

props.name: run
props.description: The run log: title, agent, model, budget in cents, and each step's title, tool, ms, cost, input, output, error and gate.

props.name: now
props.description: Controlled clock in ms since the run started. The host owns time; scrubs and Replay ask through onNowChange.

props.name: defaultNow
props.description: Where the console's own clock starts.

props.name: onNowChange
props.description: A scrub, a seek, a key or Replay asked for a new time.

props.name: playing / defaultPlaying
props.description: Whether the console's own clock runs. It also pauses by itself off screen and in a hidden tab.

props.name: onPlayingChange
props.description: Play, Pause, Replay or the run reaching its end.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the console's clock runs, as a multiple of real time.

props.name: detail
props.description: Titles only, a one-line call under each step, or every call opened.

props.name: approval
props.description: Approve a gated step with a press and hold, a plain click, or let policy approve it without pausing.

props.name: holdMs
props.description: How long the approve button has to be held.

props.name: onDecision
props.description: A gated step was approved or denied.

props.name: onStateChange
props.description: The run moved on (running, paused, waiting, finished, failed, stopped) from its own clock, a scrub, a decision or play and pause.

props.name: onReplay
props.description: Replay was pressed: decisions clear and the clock rewinds to zero.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the run log is there yet: skeleton rows while loading, a Retry when it failed, and an empty plan says so.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry on the error state.

props.name: formatCost
props.description: How a cost in cents is shown in the meter and the log.

props.name: label
props.description: The console's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the approval chime, scrub ticks and control clicks. The run playing on its own is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the controls, the gate and the timeline.

props.name: className
props.description: Give the console a height (h-[34rem]) and the plan scrolls inside it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the plan is one tab stop; Up and Down move between steps, Home and End jump, Enter or Space opens a step's call. The approve button charges while Space or Enter is held; assistive technology that clicks it gets a 'Press again' confirm instead.
The timeline is a slider: arrows move the playhead a second, Shift with an arrow jumps step to step, Page keys five seconds, Home and End to the start and to the furthest point the run can reach.
Drive it live by passing `now` (ms since start) and appending steps to `run`; a gated step with no decision holds the run until onDecision answers. Uncontrolled, it replays the log on its own clock.
Reduced motion: the clock still runs and every state still changes; nothing spins, panels open at once, seeks and Replay jump, and the hold still fills because the fill is the feedback.
Only step boundaries re-render: durations, meters and the playhead are motion values. The plan and the activity log scroll their own boxes, never the page.

items.title: Prompt Dock
items.tagline: Everything you need, around the box you type in.
items.description: A prompt box with its context around it: a tray of pinned files and snippets that collapses into a count as each chip's icon flies into a stack on glide, files dropped on the dock flying from the drop point into the tray (x on glide, y on snap, so the path bows), and an @ menu whose chosen row flies in the same way. A model pill opens in place into every model with a highlight sliding on snap, the token meter fills and warms toward the limit and bumps on recoil as it crosses 90% and the limit, and Send's arrow folds into a stop square on snap while a reply is written. The box is a real textarea and combobox: arrows walk the @ menu, Enter or Tab attaches, Escape closes it or stops a reply, and Backspace in an empty box removes the last chip.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The prompt text.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the keystroke, the @ choice or the send that changed the text.

props.name: context / defaultContext
props.description: The items in the tray: id, kind, name, tokens and an optional detail.

props.name: onContextChange
props.description: Fires from the drop, the attach, the @ choice or the remove that changed the tray.

props.name: sources
props.description: What the @ menu offers, filtered as you type.

props.name: models
props.description: The models the pill switches between: id, name, short name, note.

props.name: model
props.description: The selected model's id. A new value slides the pill to it; the visitor's own switch is reported through onModelChange.

props.name: onModelChange
props.description: The visitor chose a model.

props.name: tray
props.description: The tray starts open, starts collapsed into a count, or collapses itself while there is text in the box.

props.name: limit
props.description: The context budget in tokens: the meter warms toward it and Send stops past it.

props.name: generating / defaultGenerating
props.description: A reply is being written, so Send is Stop. Uncontrolled, Send turns it on and Stop off.

props.name: onGeneratingChange
props.description: Send or Stop changed it.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Send or Enter, with what was sent. The box clears.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Stop was pressed, or Escape while a reply is written.

props.name: onFilesAdd
props.description: Files dropped on the dock or picked with Attach.

props.name: accept
props.description: File types the Attach picker offers, as for an input's accept.

props.name: placeholder
props.defaultValue: "Ask anything, or type @ to add context"
props.description: The empty box's hint.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: How many lines the box grows to before it scrolls.

props.name: label
props.description: The dock's and the box's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the chip landings, the switches, Stop and the send.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the box, the tray, the picker and Send.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the dock's outer box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: type @ (or press the @ button) to open the menu; Up and Down move, Enter or Tab attaches, Escape closes. Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line, Escape stops a reply, and Backspace in an empty box removes the last chip.
The model pill opens a horizontal listbox: Left and Right move, Home and End jump, Enter chooses, Escape returns focus to the pill. The tray toggle keeps focus as it collapses and opens.
Drops and Attach report the raw files through onFilesAdd and add a chip each, with tokens estimated from size; give `context` and `onContextChange` to own the list.
Reduced motion: nothing flies or slides; chips appear in their slots, the model label swaps, the send icon changes at once, nothing spins, and the token meter still fills and warms.
The dock's height is measured and glides; every flyer flies inside the dock's own box.

items.title: Thread View
items.tagline: A conversation you can branch.
items.description: A complete assistant thread over a tree of messages: runs from one author share an avatar, each message's toolbar rises into place on snap, copy morphs into a check on flick and a reaction lands on recoil. Editing a sent message forks the thread, and the version switcher slides the message and every reply under it — the old branch out on the exit ease, the new one in on glide — while its counter rolls on snap and the edited bubble's measured height glides. Scrolled up, a pill counts the replies that land and glides the log to the newest on glide; End does the same, Enter sends or saves, Shift+Enter breaks a line and Escape cancels an edit.

props.name: messages / defaultMessages
props.description: Every version of every turn as one flat list: messages that share a parentId are versions of one turn. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onMessagesChange
props.description: Fires from the send, edit or reaction that changed the list, with the whole new list.

props.name: leaf / defaultLeaf
props.description: Any message on the branch to show. The thread runs from the first turn through it, then on down the newest replies. Defaults to the newest version of every turn.

props.name: onLeafChange
props.description: Fires when a version switch, a send or an edit moves the visible branch.

props.name: density
props.description: How tightly the thread is set: type size, bubble padding, avatar size and the gap between runs.

props.name: branches
props.description: Edits keep every version, with a switcher to move between them. Off: the data still forks, but an edit reads as a replacement.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: Each message's actions: a pill on hover, focus or tap, a row always shown, or none for a read-only transcript.

props.name: onSend
props.description: A message was sent from the composer. It is already in the list; stream the reply in as a child of message.id.

props.name: onEdit
props.description: A message was edited: version is the new sibling of original and the branch now shows it.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: A message or one of its code blocks was copied to the clipboard.

props.name: onReact
props.description: A reply was marked good or bad, or the mark was cleared.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed on a reply whose status is "error".

props.name: onReload
props.description: Try again was pressed while status is "error".

props.name: now
props.description: The moment relative times count from. Defaults to the newest message's time, so the thread renders the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: author
props.description: The name new messages are sent under. Defaults to the newest user message's author, else "You".

props.name: title
props.description: The thread's name in the header; also its accessible name unless label is given.

props.name: model
props.description: The model answering, shown in the header and the composer's placeholder.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the thread's data has arrived: a skeleton while loading, a message with Try again on error.

props.name: composer
props.description: Show the composer: a textarea that grows to five lines, Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The composer's placeholder. Defaults to "Message" and the model's name.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: Prompts offered while the thread is empty; pressing one fills the composer.

props.name: label
props.description: The thread's accessible name. Defaults to the title.

props.name: sound
props.description: A pop for a send, a saved edit or a reaction; a tick for a version switch, a copy and the jump to the latest.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be sent, edited or reacted to.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root. It is 560px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab reaches each message's tools (the hover pill shows while focus is inside), Enter on Edit opens the editor, Enter saves and Escape cancels with focus back on Edit; the version switcher's Previous and Next say which version is shown; End in the focused log glides to the newest message.

Streaming is the host's: append an assistant message with status "streaming", grow its text as tokens arrive and clear the status when done. The log stays on its floor while you are there, and the live region announces each finished reply once, never per token.

Under reduced motion nothing travels: version swaps, arrivals, the toolbar and the pill cross-fade, the jump to the latest is instant and the caret holds still, while counts, checks and reactions still show.
Lays out by its own width: a phone layout below 30rem (tools on tap, wider bubbles), and from 60rem a rail listing the visible turns, with fork counts, that glides the log to each one.
Times are relative to now, never the clock, and new messages are stamped after the newest one — pass at yourself through onMessagesChange if you need wall-clock times.

items.title: Usage Ledger
items.tagline: Where the tokens went.
items.description: An AI usage panel built from daily records: each day is a column stacked by model, by kind or as one total that grows up from the baseline on glide, the whole period sweeping in inside 360ms, while the month's spend sweeps round a budget gauge on drift toward its projected month end. The daily alert is a line you drag: it follows the finger 1:1 with a magnetic pull onto round numbers, rubber-bands past the plot, re-colours every day above it to warn as it passes, and springs onto its value on snap with the release velocity. The plot is a slider over the days (arrows step, Home and End jump, Enter selects), the line's grip a slider over the threshold (arrows one step, Page keys four), and the period a radio group.

props.name: threshold / defaultThreshold
props.description: The daily alert in tokens: the line you drag. Days above it turn warn. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onThresholdChange
props.description: Fires from the drag or key that moved the line, once for each round value it lands on.

props.name: stack
props.description: What each day's column is split by: each model, input / output / cached, or one total. The legend follows.

props.name: range / defaultRange
props.description: The period shown: the last 7, 30 or 90 days up to now. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onRangeChange
props.description: Fires from the period control with the new period.

props.name: thresholdStep
props.description: The round number the line snaps to. Defaults to a nice twelfth of the axis (250k on a 3M axis).

props.name: models
props.description: The models billed: id, name, an optional colour, and a price per million input, output and cached tokens.

props.name: days
props.description: One record per day (date as YYYY-MM-DD), with tokens per model id. The default is ninety seeded days.

props.name: now
props.description: Today: where the period ends and the month's spend is counted to. Defaults to the last day in days.

props.name: budget
props.description: The monthly budget. The gauge shows the month's spend against it and where the month is heading.

props.name: onDaySelect
props.description: Enter on the focused day, or a click on a column.

props.name: format
props.description: Money in the gauge and its caption. Defaults to US dollars in locale.

props.name: formatTokens
props.description: Token counts on the axis, the grip, the readouts and the legend. Defaults to compact: 820k, 1.5M.

props.name: formatDate
props.description: Day labels from a YYYY-MM-DD date. Defaults to "Sep 14".

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale of the default money format. Fixed, so the server and the browser print the same.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the usage has arrived: a skeleton while loading, a message with Try again on error.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed while status is "error".

props.name: title
props.description: The panel's heading; also its accessible name unless label is given.

props.name: label
props.description: The panel's accessible name. Defaults to the title.

props.name: sound
props.description: A detent for each round value the line lands on, pitched by height; a tick for each day the keyboard steps and for a period change.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: the line, the days and the period cannot be moved.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root. It is 560px tall and scrolls inside itself; pass a height class to change it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the plot is a slider over the days — Left and Right step a day, Page keys a week, Home and End jump, Enter fires onDaySelect, Escape clears the readout; the alert grip is a vertical slider — Up and Down one round step, Page keys four, Home and End the ends; the period is a radio group on the arrow keys.
The threshold reports once per round value it lands on, from the drag or key that moved it. A controlled host that refuses a value sees the line spring back to its own value on release.

Under reduced motion the columns, the gauge and the sparklines appear drawn, and the line follows the finger without springs or rubber-band; it still snaps, and the days still change colour, because that is the information.
Lays out by its own width: one column on a phone (scrolling inside its box), the gauge beside the chart from 40rem, and the legend as a third column from 68rem.
Bars are pigment: each series takes a token's hue at a fixed lightness, so a model reads the same colour in light and dark. Pass a model colour as a CSS colour string to override it.

items.title: Side by Side
items.tagline: Two models, one prompt, you decide.
items.description: Two models answer one prompt in parallel columns, each streaming at its own pace — its time to first token, then its token rate, scaled by speed — with a live clock, a progress hairline and a Done stamp that lands on flick. Once both finish, a highlighter sweeps across what each says that the other does not, in reading order within 600ms, and the stats tally beneath them with bars that grow on glide. The vote puck drags 1:1, rubber-bands past the ends and settles on snap at the stop the throw was heading for, the preferred column takes its hue as a badge lands on recoil, and the reason you pick moves into the summary on glide; the stops are a radio group on the arrow keys, and on a phone the answers become two tabs.

props.name: speed
props.description: Playback speed of both streams as a multiple of real time. The clocks and stats still read in the models' real time.

props.name: diff
props.description: What is marked once both finish: runs of two or more words the other answer never uses, whole sentences with under half their words in common, or nothing.

props.name: vote
props.description: The vote bar: three stops (A better, tie, B better), or five with much better at each end.

props.name: prompt
props.description: The prompt both models answered, shown above the columns.

props.name: answers
props.description: The two answers: id, model, text, latencyMs and tokensPerSecond. Set an answer's status to drive its column yourself as text arrives; leave it unset and the column plays the text in at its own pace.

props.name: autoPlay
props.description: Start streaming when the surface first scrolls into view. Off: both answers show complete, with their marks.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The vote: choice ("a", "b" or "tie"), margin (1 or 2) and an optional reason. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, key or press that changed the vote or its reason.

props.name: reasons
props.description: Why a winner won, offered after a vote for a side. Defaults to More accurate, Clearer, More concise, Safer advice.

props.name: onRerun
props.description: Run again was pressed: both streams replay from the start and an uncontrolled vote clears.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed on a column whose answer has status "error".

props.name: onFinish
props.description: A column finished playing, with its first-token time, total time, token count and rate.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the run has data yet: skeleton columns while loading, a message with Run again on error.

props.name: labels
props.description: The two columns' short names, used on their badges, the stats and the vote stops.

props.name: label
props.description: The surface's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: A tick for each stop the puck crosses and each reason picked; a chime when a vote lands, pitched by side.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: no vote, no reason, no re-run.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root. It is 560px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the vote stops are a radio group — Left and Right move and vote, Home and End jump — enabled once both answers finish; reason chips are a second radio group; each answer's text box is focusable and scrolls with the arrow keys; on a phone the two answers are tabs on the arrow keys.
The live region speaks each column's finish once and the number of marked differences once, never per token.

Under reduced motion the text still streams (it is the data) but without the per-token fade, the highlights appear without the sweep, and the puck follows the finger without springs or rubber-band; the vote, the badge and the reason still land.

Lays out by its own width: two tabs over one answer below 30rem (the whole surface scrolls), two columns with the stats and the vote beneath from 30rem, and a third column holding the stats and the vote from 64rem.
Playback runs only while the surface is in view and the page is visible, and the clock carries on from where it stood when it resumes.

items.title: Artifact Pane
items.tagline: The thing it made, beside the chat.
items.description: A generated file beside the conversation that made it. Switching versions applies the diff in place: shared lines keep their element, dropped lines are struck and fold away on the exit ease, and new lines open on glide under a wash that sweeps across them in a cascade, on the Preview block by block and on the Code tab line by line, while the change count rolls on snap and the Preview / Code panels slide 16px on glide. Dock folds the pane into a chip in the thread: a ghost of its frame flies into the chip on glide, homing on its live box while the pane's column closes, and lands on recoil; the tabs and version pills take arrow keys, and Escape anywhere in the pane docks it.

props.name: versions
props.description: How the version history is offered: a segmented control whose indicator slides on snap, Previous and Next around a rolling readout, or a strip of dots under the header whose rail fills on glide.

props.name: diff
props.description: What a version switch shows: marks that flash and fold away, marks that stay (with a Changes toggle) until cleared, or a plain swap.

props.name: dock
props.description: Where the docked pane lands: as a card inside the message that made the shown version, or on a bar pinned to the foot of the conversation.

props.name: artifact
props.description: The file and every version of it, oldest first: title, filename, kind ("document" renders its Markdown, "code" shows a preview node when a version has one) and versions with summary, time and source.

props.name: conversation
props.description: The turns beside it. An assistant turn with a version id carries a chip that opens that version.

props.name: version / defaultVersion
props.description: The shown version's id. Uncontrolled, an appended version is followed when the reader was on the newest one.

props.name: onVersionChange
props.description: Fires from the control, chip or arrow key that chose another version.

props.name: tab / defaultTab
props.description: The shown view. A code artifact whose version has no preview shows Code only.

props.name: onTabChange
props.description: Fires from the tab or arrow key that switched the view.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the pane is open beside the conversation or docked into it as a chip. Controlled or uncontrolled; a host change flies the same way a press does.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the Dock button, the chip, a version chip or Escape, with the new state.

props.name: status
props.description: A new version is being written (a badge, a running hairline and a typing row in the thread), or the last revision failed (a strip with Retry).

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed after a failed revision.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: The shown version's source was copied to the clipboard.

props.name: onDownload
props.description: The shown version is being saved, as { name, text, type }. Return false to save it yourself; otherwise the pane saves it through the browser.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment relative times count from, so the surface renders the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: label
props.description: The surface's accessible name. Defaults to the artifact's title and "the conversation".

props.name: sound
props.description: A swish when the visitor docks or opens the pane, a click on copy, download, tabs and versions.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: versions, tabs, copy, download and dock do nothing; the panels still scroll.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root. It is 540px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab reaches the version chips, Copy, Download, Dock, the tabs and the version control; Left and Right (or Home and End) move the tabs and the version pills or dots with selection following focus; Escape anywhere in the pane docks it, and focus lands on the chip, then back on Dock when the chip opens it.

Versions are whole sources: the pane computes a line diff between whatever was shown and whatever is chosen, so jumping from v1 to v4 shows the full change. Append a version to `artifact.versions` while `status` is "writing" and set `version` to it to play the new diff.

Under reduced motion the diff marks still show, because they are information, but lines appear and leave without folding, panels cross-fade without travel, and docking cross-fades the pane and the chip with no flight.

Lays out by its own width: under 40rem the conversation fills the box and the open pane covers it as a sheet; from 40rem the two sit side by side; from 60rem the thread widens, turns show their times and Copy and Download are labelled.
Relative times count from `now`, never the clock. A Markdown document renders headings, paragraphs, "- " lists, **bold**, `code` and {template_variables} as chips.

items.title: Voice Mode
items.tagline: Talk; watch it listen.
items.description: A voice call with an assistant, drawn around an orb that breathes with whoever is talking: one level, smoothed each frame with a fast attack and a slower release, ripples a blob, pushes a ring of dots or trails two rings, while the orb's resting size moves between listening, thinking and speaking on snap, shrinks away on glide when the call ends, and its pigment cross-fades with the state. The conversation plays from data at speaking pace, the caller's words arriving in light ink and firming as each line settles and every new line rising 8px on snap, and Interrupt halts the reply mid-word, tracked to the character. Mute, Interrupt and End are real buttons (Mute a toggle with aria-pressed), and each finished line is announced once, never per word.

props.name: orb
props.description: How the orb draws the voice: a closed curve rippling on three seeded harmonics, a disc with two rings trailing the level on slower smoothings, or 28 dots each pushed out on its own phase.

props.name: captions
props.description: What is shown of the words: the conversation as lines (beside the orb from 40rem), only the current utterance large under the orb, or nothing (lines are still announced).

props.name: level
props.description: How far the orb swells with the voice, 0 to 1. At 0 it stays round and only its colour changes.

props.name: turns
props.description: The conversation, { id, role: "user" | "assistant", text }, played in order at speaking pace. Append turns as they are transcribed and the call carries on from where it is.

props.name: live / defaultLive
props.description: Whether the call is on. Turning it back on starts the conversation from the top.

props.name: onLiveChange
props.description: Fires from End and Call again.

props.name: muted / defaultMuted
props.description: The microphone is muted: the orb greys and stills, and the caller's turn waits until it is unmuted.

props.name: onMutedChange
props.description: Fires from the Mute button.

props.name: onInterrupt
props.description: The reply was cut off, with the part of it already said (empty when it was cut while thinking). Stop your speech output here.

props.name: onPhaseChange
props.description: The call moved between listening, thinking, speaking and ended.

props.name: meter
props.description: Reads the live input level, 0 to 1, each frame while listening, for example from an analyser on the microphone. Without it a seeded voice is simulated; nothing is ever recorded.

props.name: pace
props.description: Speaking pace in words a second. Longer words take longer and punctuation adds a breath.

props.name: agent
props.description: Who is on the other end: the header, the speaker names and the announcements.

props.name: status
props.description: The line is still connecting (a faint orb with a turning arc), or the microphone could not be reached (a message with Retry).

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed after an error.

props.name: label
props.description: The surface's accessible name. Defaults to "Voice call with" and the agent.

props.name: sound
props.description: A blup when the visitor interrupts, a click on Mute, End and Call again. The call itself is silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The controls do nothing; the call still plays.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root. It is 540px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Mute, Interrupt and End are buttons in that order; Interrupt is aria-disabled (never disabled) outside speaking and thinking, so focus is never dropped, and End becomes Call again in place with focus kept on it.
The call plays only while the surface is on screen and the page is visible: the word timer, the clock and the orb's frame loop all stop otherwise, and stop for good when the call ends.

Under reduced motion the orb keeps its round shape and size; the level shows as the strength of its halo and the state as its colour. Words still arrive and Interrupt still cuts them mid-word, because the conversation is information.
To drive it from a real session, append each transcribed turn to `turns`, pass `meter` reading your microphone analyser, and stop your speech output in `onInterrupt`.
Lays out by its own width: one column under 40rem; with the transcript, two columns from 40rem (orb and controls beside the lines), and from 60rem the speaker sits beside each line.

items.title: Source Search
items.tagline: Choose what the answer stands on.
items.description: A retrieval surface where you choose what an answer is grounded on. The query scores the sources as you type: rows that stay glide to their new rank, new rows rise 8px on snap in a cascade, leaving rows fade on the exit ease, every relevance bar or ring eases to its score on glide, and facet counts roll on snap. Checking a result flies a ghost chip from its title into the tray, x on glide and y on a softer spring so it travels on a shallow curve while homing on its slot, landing on recoil as the tray's count and the Answer button's count roll; checkboxes are native with Up and Down between them, the tray's remove buttons are a roving toolbar where Delete removes, and Escape clears the query.

props.name: relevance
props.description: How each result's score is shown: a bar that fills from the left, a ring gauge whose arc sweeps, or not at all (the rank still carries it).

props.name: facets
props.description: How the filters are offered: toggle chips under the query, a column of checkboxes beside the results (chips below 40rem), or none. Within a group facets OR, across groups they AND.

props.name: tray
props.description: How the chosen sources sit in the tray: numbered chips with titles, a fanned stack of small numbered cards that spreads on hover or focus, or one count with a dot per source.

props.name: sources
props.description: Everything that can be found: { id, title, site, snippet, kind: "doc" | "ticket" | "code" | "thread", space?, updated, relevance }.

props.name: query / defaultQuery
props.description: The search text. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.description: Fires on every keystroke in the query and when it is cleared.

props.name: onSearch
props.description: Enter was pressed in the query: run your search here.

props.name: matching
props.description: Score and filter sources against the query in the browser (relevance times the share of query words found, title words counting double). Turn off when the host searches and passes ranked results.

props.name: selected / defaultSelected
props.description: The ids in the tray, in tray order. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.description: Fires from the checkbox, the chip's remove button, Delete or Clear that changed the tray.

props.name: filters / defaultFilters
props.description: Active facets as "kind:doc", "updated:week" | "updated:month" | "updated:older", "space:<name>".

props.name: onFiltersChange
props.description: Fires from the chip or checkbox that changed the filters.

props.name: max
props.description: The most sources the tray holds. When full, further checkboxes are aria-disabled and the tray says so.

props.name: onAnswer
props.description: Answer was pressed, with the tray's sources in order and the query.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: A result's title was pressed. Without it, titles are plain text.

props.name: status
props.description: The host is searching (skeleton rows) or the search failed (a message with Retry).

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed after a failed search.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment "updated" times and the age facets count from, so results render the same everywhere.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The query's placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: The surface's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: A tick when the visitor checks, unchecks, filters or answers (rising with the tray's count), a pop when a flown chip lands.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be searched, filtered or chosen.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root. It is 540px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: ArrowDown in the query enters the results; Up and Down move between the native checkboxes and Space toggles; the tray's remove buttons are one tab stop with Left, Right, Home and End between them and Delete or Backspace to remove (focus moves to the next chip, then to Answer); Escape in a non-empty query clears it.
Counts follow the landings: the tray's count and the Answer button's count change when a flown chip lands, not when the box is checked, so the number never runs ahead of what the reader sees.
Under reduced motion nothing flies or slides: chips fade into the tray, rows re-rank and leave at once, scores are drawn at their values and skeletons hold still.
With your own search, pass ranked `sources`, set `matching={false}`, drive `status` while it runs, and use `onSearch` for Enter; the tray keeps any chosen id that is still in `sources`.

Lays out by its own width: under 40rem the facets are one scrolling chip row and the tray scrolls sideways above a full-width Answer; from 40rem the rail sits beside the results and tray chips wrap; from 60rem results show their updated time beside the score.

items.title: Agent Inbox
items.tagline: What your agents need you to look at.
items.description: A review queue for work agents have finished: each card carries the change (summary, area, a diff summary with its proportion bar, checks and risk) and two decisions. A card follows the finger 1:1 sideways while the decision it is heading for shows underneath and arms on snap past the threshold; the release is projected, so a flick commits and a short throw springs home on snap with its velocity, an approved card leaves on the exit ease while the cards under it close the gap on glide, and sending back opens a note on glide first. Checkboxes select several and a toolbar slides down over the header on snap, the header's counts roll on snap as the queue empties into an inbox-zero state whose check draws on flick and whose badge lands on recoil; the cards are a roving list where Up and Down move, A approves, R sends back, X selects, Enter opens the files and Escape closes a note.

props.name: swipe
props.description: What a sideways swipe does: right approves and left sends back, only right approves (left rubber-bands), or nothing (buttons and keys only).

props.name: batch
props.description: Cards carry checkboxes, and a toolbar slides in to approve or send back several at once.

props.name: density
props.description: How much each card says: one line with icon actions, a summary and the diff bar with labelled actions, or a two-line summary with every file and the risk spelled out.

props.name: tasks / defaultTasks
props.description: Every task, waiting and decided: { id, title, agent, area, summary, files: { path, added, removed }[], checks?, risk?, at, status?, note?, decidedAt? }. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onTasksChange
props.description: Fires from the swipe, button, key or undo that changed a task, with the whole new list.

props.name: onApprove
props.description: Tasks were approved: one, or a batch.

props.name: onReturn
props.description: Tasks were sent back with this note.

props.name: onUndo
props.description: A decision was undone; the task is waiting again.

props.name: threshold
props.description: How far a card must travel to commit, as a share of its width, 0.2 to 0.8. A flick that would carry it that far commits too.

props.name: notes
props.description: Quick notes offered when sending back; pressing one fills the note.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment relative times count from, and the time decisions are stamped with.

props.name: status
props.description: The queue is loading (skeleton cards) or failed to load (a message with Retry).

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed after the queue failed to load.

props.name: title
props.description: The queue's name, shown in the header.

props.name: label
props.description: The surface's accessible name. Defaults to the title.

props.name: sound
props.description: A swish for every decision the visitor makes (up for approve, down for send back), and a chime when their decision empties the queue.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be decided, selected or undone.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root. It is 540px tall by default; pass a height class to change it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the cards are one tab stop with Up, Down, Home and End between them; A approves, R opens the send-back note (Enter sends it, Escape closes it and returns to the card), X or Space selects, and Enter opens the file list. Approve and Send back are also real buttons on every card, and the batch toolbar takes Left and Right.
Focus never drops: when a card leaves, focus moves to the card that took its place, and to the inbox-zero heading when the queue empties.

Under reduced motion a drag still follows the finger, because the visitor is moving it, but nothing else travels: cards fade out and back, the list closes at once, counts swap without rolling, the toolbar fades in place and the inbox-zero check is drawn.
Sending back always needs a note: a left swipe springs the card home and opens the note rather than deciding on its own.

Lays out by its own width: under 40rem the actions sit as a full-width row under each card and the header counts wrap; from 40rem the actions sit at the card's right; from 60rem a Reviewed column logs every decision with its note, with Undo on the newest.

items.title: App Shell
items.tagline: The frame every screen lives in.
items.description: The frame a product's screens live in: a sidebar whose width is one motion value on glide, so its labels tuck away row by row and leave a 56px icon rail with tooltips, its edge dragged 1:1 and committed by projection with the release velocity; below 640px it becomes a drawer that slides over a scrim on glide and can be pushed back out. A pill under the current row travels on snap, pages change by slide, fade or zoom with the last crumb cross-fading in the same beat, and search is a combobox over the pages. Arrow keys walk the sidebar, [ or Cmd/Ctrl+B folds it, 1–9 change page and / goes to search.

props.name: pages
props.description: The destinations in sidebar order, each with its label, icon, optional badge and section, crumbs, heading, summary, search keywords and content.

props.name: page / defaultPage
props.description: The current page's id. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: Fires from the row, crumb, shortcut or search result that chose a page.

props.name: collapsed / defaultCollapsed
props.description: The sidebar folded to its rail (or hidden without rail). Controlled or uncontrolled; left unset it follows the shell's width.

props.name: onCollapsedChange
props.description: Fires from the toggle, the edge drag, the edge's arrow keys or the shortcut, with the new fold.

props.name: rail
props.description: Fold to a 56px icon rail whose labels become tooltips. Off: the sidebar slides away entirely and the content takes the width.

props.name: transition
props.description: How the content changes page: rising 16px in the direction of travel through the nav, a cross-fade, or settling from 0.98 scale.

props.name: density
props.description: Row heights (28/32/36px), the top bar (44/48/56px), paddings and the heading size.

props.name: workspace
props.description: The product at the top of the sidebar: name, detail line and an optional 28px mark.

props.name: user
props.description: Who is signed in, at the foot of the sidebar.

props.name: navLabel
props.description: The sidebar navigation's accessible name.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.description: The search field's placeholder and accessible name.

props.name: onSearch
props.description: Enter in search when no page matches, with the query.

props.name: shortcuts
props.description: [ or Cmd/Ctrl+B folds the sidebar, 1–9 go to a page and / focuses search, while focus is in the shell or it is hovered with nothing focused; never while typing.

props.name: status
props.description: The content area's state: a skeleton while loading, a message with Retry on error. The sidebar keeps working.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: The error state's Retry button.

props.name: label
props.description: The shell's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: A swish as the visitor folds or opens the sidebar or drawer, a click pitched by place as they choose a page.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root. It is 560px tall by default; pass a height (h-full, h-dvh) to fill a screen.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the sidebar is one tab stop — Up and Down walk the pages, Home and End jump, Enter or Space open. The edge is a separator: Left folds, Right opens, Enter toggles. In the drawer Tab is trapped and Escape closes it, handing focus back to the menu button.

Reduced motion: widths and the drawer change at once, pages cross-fade on opacity whatever transition says, the pill and tooltips appear in place; every change is still announced in the polite status.

The shell arranges itself by its own measured width — drawer below 640px, rail from 640px, open from 1024px — and server-renders that arrangement with container queries, so the first paint already matches.
Page content is yours: anything in a page's content renders in a scrolling region named by the page heading, and it reads --shell-row, --shell-pad and --shell-gap if it wants to follow density.

Search finds pages by label, heading, summary and keywords; give a page the names of its records (ids, people, sites) as keywords and a search for one lands on the page that holds it, with focus on its heading.

items.title: Command Center
items.tagline: Every action, one keystroke away.
items.description: A command palette that lives inside its frame: Cmd+K or Ctrl+K, pressed anywhere in the frame, lands it from 8px above on snap over a fading scrim, and it leaves on the exit ease. Commands are a tree — choosing one with sub-commands slides its page in on glide (or raises it over its parent like a sheet) while a chip with the parent's name pops into the field on snap and the list's measured height glides to the new page's; Backspace slides back. Fuzzy matching lights the letters it found across the whole tree, a pill follows the highlight on snap, Recent leads an empty field and a preview pane follows the highlight from 640px; the field is a combobox where arrows move, Enter runs or opens and Escape clears, then goes back, then closes.

props.name: commands
props.description: The command tree: each command has a label, group, icon, keywords, shortcut, hint, preview, placeholder and tone, and may hold children that open as a page of their own.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: The palette is open. Controlled or uncontrolled; opening by default never takes focus.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the shortcut, trigger, Escape, scrim or run that opened or closed it.

props.name: recent / defaultRecent
props.description: Ids of recently run commands, newest first. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onRecentChange
props.description: Fires with the new list whenever a run changes it.

props.name: onRun
props.description: A command was run, with the pages it was reached through.

props.name: nesting
props.description: How sub-commands open: a page sliding in from the side, a sheet rising over its receding parent, or no pages at all with every sub-command listed under its parent's heading.

props.name: preview
props.description: A pane beside the list previews the highlighted command — its facts, a sentence, or the choices it opens — where the frame is 640px or wider.

props.name: fuzzy
props.description: Letters match in order anywhere, scored for word starts and runs, and light up. Off: the query must appear as typed.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The field's placeholder on the first page; each sub-page uses its command's own placeholder.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: Cmd+K or Ctrl+K, pressed while focus is anywhere in the frame, opens and closes the palette; the key press is consumed there.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Show the search trigger along the top of the frame.

props.name: triggerLabel
props.description: The trigger's text.

props.name: maxRecent
props.description: How many recent commands are kept.

props.name: status
props.description: Commands still arriving show skeleton rows and a spinner in the field; a failed fetch shows a line with Retry.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: The error state's Retry button.

props.name: label
props.description: The palette's accessible name.

props.name: children
props.description: The app behind the palette, inert while it is open.

props.name: sound
props.description: A tick pitched down the list as the highlight moves, a swish as pages and the palette open and close. Typing is silent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the frame. It is 560px tall by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Up and Down move (wrapping), Page Up and Page Down jump five, Enter runs or opens, Tab or ArrowRight at the end of the text opens a command's page, Backspace or ArrowLeft in an empty field goes back, and Escape clears, then goes back, then closes — every key handled with preventDefault where focus is.
Reduced motion: the palette, its pages and the preview cross-fade on opacity, the list's height and the pill jump, and the run flash and choice check still show.
Give every command a stable id: recents are ids, and with nothing typed Recent leads with each command's path shown, so a deep command runs in one keystroke.
Searching at the top level reaches the whole tree; a deep result shows its path with the matched letters lit in it and runs directly, without opening its pages.
keepOpen commands behave as a choice among their siblings: running one leaves the palette open and moves the check to it, which suits settings like a theme.

items.title: Swim Board
items.tagline: Pick it up, carry it over.
items.description: A kanban board with swimlanes. A dragged card comes up into a carried copy 1:1 under the pointer, scaled on flick and leaning into its horizontal speed up to tilt degrees on a glide-tuned spring; the cell under it opens a gap of the card's exact height on glide while the cards below slide down, and on release it flies into the gap on snap with the release velocity and straightens as it lands. A move past a column's work-in-progress limit shakes its header on a five-beat tween and turns it warn (or is refused, the gap staying home), lanes group by priority or owner and fold on glide, and moving a card between lanes rewrites that field. Space picks a focused card up, arrows carry it a place or a column at a time, Enter drops and Escape puts it back, every step announced.

props.name: cards / defaultCards
props.description: Every card in board order — a cell lists its cards in the order they appear here. Each has a title, column, priority, owner, and optional tag and points. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onCardsChange
props.description: Fires from the drop that moved a card, with every card and the move (from and to as column, lane and index, and whether it came from the pointer or the keyboard).

props.name: columns
props.description: The columns left to right, each with an optional work-in-progress limit.

props.name: people
props.description: Everyone a card can belong to; owner lanes follow this order.

props.name: onMove
props.description: A card was dropped somewhere new.

props.name: onCardOpen
props.description: A card was tapped, clicked, or had Enter pressed on it while not picked up.

props.name: onLaneToggle
props.description: A lane was folded or unfolded, with its new state.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far a carried card leans into its travel, in degrees: its angle is the pointer's horizontal speed, clamped to this. 0 keeps it level.

props.name: limit
props.description: Work-in-progress limits: a move past one shakes the header and turns it warn, is refused with the card going home, or limits are hidden.

props.name: lanes
props.description: What the rows group by. Moving a card between lanes rewrites that field on the card.

props.name: collapsedLanes / defaultCollapsedLanes
props.description: Folded lanes by id. Controlled (with onLaneToggle) or uncontrolled.

props.name: title
props.description: The board's heading.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: A quieter line beside the heading, from 480px.

props.name: status
props.description: Skeleton cards while loading; a message with Retry on error.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: The error state's Retry button.

props.name: label
props.description: The board's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: A click as a card comes up or a lane folds, a thock pitched by column as it lands — duller when a drop is refused.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Cards can still be read and walked with the arrow keys, but not carried or opened.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root. It is 560px tall by default; the lanes scroll inside it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the board is one tab stop for cards (plus each lane's fold button). Arrows walk between cards, Space picks the focused card up, arrows then carry it a place at a time (crossing into the next lane past either end) or a column at a time, Enter or Space drops it and Escape puts it back; every pick-up, step, refusal and drop is announced.

Reduced motion: the carried card follows the pointer but never leans, the gap opens at once, landings and keyboard steps are instant and nothing shakes — the warn colour, Over limit, counts and announcements still show.

On touch screens a card is carried by its grip (the six dots at its corner), so a finger anywhere else on a card scrolls the board; on a phone the columns scroll sideways and the column chips above jump to one, and holding a card near an edge scrolls the board under it.
Controlled boards stay honest: the drop is reported with onCardsChange and the card flies to wherever the host's next cards put it — the new place if it accepted the move, home if it did not.
Moving a card between lanes rewrites the field the lanes group by (priority or owner) in the cards you get back.

items.title: Mail Inbox
items.tagline: Triage with a flick.
items.description: An inbox built for triage: a row's face follows the finger 1:1 and reveals its action from the edge it leaves, archive on a green pigment and snooze on an amber one, arming with a pop on snap at the commit line; a release past it (or a throw, by projection) runs the row out on glide with its release velocity before its height closes, and a short one springs home on snap. Selecting a thread slides a batch toolbar down over the header on snap with a rolling count, opening one fades its unread dot and glides its messages open under the row (or into a reading pane when the inbox is wide), and every archive leaves an Undo toast that lands on recoil. j and k move, x selects, Enter opens, e archives, b snoozes, s stars, u toggles unread, z undoes and Escape backs out.

props.name: swipe
props.description: How a swipe commits: past 42% of the row, resting open on its action (a long swipe still commits), or not at all, leaving the hover tools and keys.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height and type size: single-line compact rows, cozy, or roomy with larger avatars.

props.name: preview
props.description: Lines of message preview under the subject, 0 to 2.

props.name: threads / defaultThreads
props.description: Every thread in every folder, each a subject and its messages oldest first. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onThreadsChange
props.description: Fires from the swipe, key or button that changed the threads, with all of them.

props.name: folder / defaultFolder
props.description: The folder on screen. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onFolderChange
props.description: Fires when a folder is chosen on the rail or the folder chips.

props.name: selected / defaultSelected
props.description: Selected thread ids. A selection brings in the batch toolbar.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.description: Fires from the checkbox, x, select-all or batch action that changed the selection.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: The open thread: expanded under its row, or in the reading pane once the inbox is 68rem wide.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires when a thread opens or closes.

props.name: swipeActions
props.type: { right: MailAction | null; left: MailAction | null }
props.description: Which action each swipe direction runs; null leaves that direction rubber-banding. In the archive or snoozed folder the action that would send a thread where it is moves it back to the inbox.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment times are read against (09:12, Yesterday, Tue, 25 Sep). Never read from the clock during render.

props.name: zoneOffset
props.description: Minutes east of UTC that times are shown in, so the server and the browser draw the same inbox.

props.name: snoozeUntil
props.description: When a snooze ends, from now. Defaults to the next day at 08:00.

props.name: account
props.description: Whose inbox it is: shown on the rail, and their messages read as "me".

props.name: label
props.description: The inbox's accessible name.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading draws placeholder rows; error offers Retry.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed on the error state.

props.name: onArchive
props.description: Threads were sent to the archive, by swipe, key, hover tool or batch.

props.name: onSnooze
props.description: Threads were snoozed, and until when.

props.name: onRestore
props.description: Threads were moved back to the inbox from the archive or a snooze.

props.name: onReadChange
props.description: Threads were marked read by opening them, or toggled with u or the mail tool.

props.name: onStarChange
props.description: A thread was starred or unstarred.

props.name: onReply
props.description: Reply was pressed on an open thread.

props.name: onCompose
props.description: Compose was pressed on the rail.

props.name: onUndo
props.description: The last archive or snooze was undone from the toast or with z.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a pop when a swipe arms, a pick or a star lands, and a swish as rows leave. Off unless asked for.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Makes the whole inbox inert.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; it is 560px tall by default and lays out by its own width.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the rows are one tab stop. j and k (or the arrows) move, Home and End jump, x selects, Enter or o opens, e archives, b snoozes, s stars, u toggles unread, z undoes, Ctrl or Cmd with A selects all, and Escape clears the selection, closes the open thread or a revealed row.

Reduced motion: the row still follows the finger, but it fades rather than flies when it commits and every settle is a short tween; the toolbar, toast and pane cross-fade, and read state, counts and selections still change.

Data: pass threads (with folder, unread, starred, labels, snoozedUntil) and keep them in your store through onThreadsChange; the specific callbacks (onArchive, onSnooze, onRestore, onReadChange) say what happened. A controlled host that keeps a thread where it was gets its row back.
Layout follows the inbox's own width: one column with folder chips under 40rem, a rail with folders and label filters from 40rem, and a reading pane from 68rem.
Times come from now and zoneOffset, never the machine's clock or locale, so the server and the browser render the same markup.
Touch: rows are touch-pan-y, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the list and a horizontal one throws the row.

items.title: Week Planner
items.tagline: Draw an event where it belongs.
items.description: A week drawn on its hours. Pressing empty time and dragging rubber-bands a block out of the pressed slot, its far edge 1:1 under the pointer with a snapped line and a live time label, ticking at every new slot; on release the edge springs onto the snapped time on snap with the pointer's velocity and the event thocks down with its title ready to type. Events drag across time and days and stretch from either edge the same way, landing on snap with the release velocity while a dashed placeholder shows the landing and overlapping events re-divide their columns on glide; a now line moves through today on drift. The grid is one tab stop with a slot cursor (arrows, Shift for a range, Enter to create), and each event moves with the arrows, stretches with Shift, renames with Enter and goes with Delete.

props.name: snap
props.description: Minutes every drag, resize and cursor step snaps to; also the gutter's tick marks.

props.name: density
props.description: Height of an hour (40, 52 or 68px), with type and padding to match. A change glides every event to its new place.

props.name: now
props.description: The current moment, which draws the now line and shades time already gone: a Date or epoch ms, or a number from 0 to 24 read as that hour of today (13.5 is 13:30).

props.name: events / defaultEvents
props.description: Events with epoch-ms start and end, a title, an optional calendar id and location. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onEventsChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, key or field that changed the events, with all of them.

props.name: calendars
props.description: The calendars events belong to, each with a label and a tint (a CSS colour token).

props.name: day / defaultDay
props.description: The focused day: its week is shown, and on a phone the day itself. Controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onDayChange
props.description: Fires with the new day's midnight (epoch ms) from the arrows, the day strip, the headers or the keys.

props.name: selected / defaultSelected
props.description: The selected event, shown with a stronger tint and, from 68rem, in the details panel.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.description: Fires when an event is picked, created or let go.

props.name: today
props.description: The date marked as today; an hour-form now falls on it.

props.name: hours
props.description: The hours the grid draws. Events outside are clipped to them.

props.name: workHours
props.description: Working hours, drawn on the lighter ground; the keyboard cursor starts at their first hour when now is elsewhere.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: 1 starts weeks on Monday, 0 on Sunday.

props.name: zoneOffset
props.description: Minutes east of UTC that times are drawn in, never the machine's own zone, so the server and the browser draw the same week.

props.name: defaultDuration
props.description: Minutes an event made with Enter or New lasts when no range is selected.

props.name: newTitle
props.description: A new event's title, selected in its field so typing replaces it.

props.name: defaultCalendar
props.description: The calendar new events join. Defaults to the first calendar.

props.name: onCreate
props.description: An event was drawn, made with Enter, or added with New.

props.name: onUpdate
props.description: An event moved, was resized, renamed or changed calendar.

props.name: onDelete
props.description: An event was removed with Delete, its close button or the details panel.

props.name: label
props.description: The planner's accessible name.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading covers the hours with a note; error offers Retry.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed on the error state.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a tick at every new slot a drag or key reaches and a thock when an event lands. Off unless asked for.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Makes the whole planner inert.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; it is 560px tall by default and lays out by its own width.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the grid is one tab stop with a slot cursor. Up and Down move it a snap step, Left and Right a day, Page Up and Page Down an hour, Home and End the first and last slot, t jumps to now; Shift with Up or Down selects a range and Enter (or n) creates an event over it. Events are tab stops: Up and Down move them, Shift changes their end, Left and Right move a day, Enter or F2 renames, Delete removes, Escape returns to the grid.
Reduced motion: drags still follow the pointer, but landings, column re-divisions, week changes and the now line move at once; the placeholder, the snapped label and every time readout still show.
Times are absolute (epoch ms) and drawn in zoneOffset, never the machine's zone, so server and browser agree. now can be an hour of today, which keeps a fixed demo readable.

Layout follows the planner's own width: one day with a day strip under 40rem, the whole week from 40rem (drags cross days), and a details panel with a title field, calendar radio group and duration stepper from 68rem.
Touch: the hours scroll with touch-pan-y; a finger rests 300ms before it draws a new event or lifts one, so a swipe still scrolls.
Overlapping events share their day side by side and widen into free columns; a controlled host that refuses a move gets the event back where it was.

items.title: File Browser
items.tagline: Lasso, drag, drop into folders.
