The canvas caps its backing store at a device pixel ratio of 2 (dpr lowers it) and re-reads its colour when the theme changes, so it reads in light and dark.
Under reduced motion the grains appear already home and fade in; the hand and the throw are off.
The wrapper is focusable when interactive: Enter or Space scatters the grains from the centre and they regather, the same end state as a press. A drag over the words still selects the text.

items.title: Depot Board
items.tagline: Split-flap letters clatter to the message.
items.description: A split-flap departure board: each cell flips its top flap down over a hinge with real flap physics — integrated under gravity, slow off the top and fast at the bottom, landing on the stop with a small bounce before it rests — through its character ring one flap at a time until it reaches its letter, columns a ripple apart so the board settles in a wave, and only the cells whose letter changes move at all. Messages cycle once the board has settled and rested; the board is a button, so a press, Enter or Space shows the next message and Left/Right step back and forth, with the visitor's flips clacking when sound is on and the message announced once it settles.

props.name: messages
props.description: The messages the board cycles through; "\n" forces a new row and longer rows wrap between words.

props.name: index / defaultIndex
props.description: The message showing, controlled or initial.

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Fires from whatever changed the message — the timer, a press or a key — with the new index.

props.name: interval
props.description: How long a settled message stays before the next, ms; 0 changes only by hand.

props.name: speed
props.description: Flip speed, 0.5 to 2: how fast each flap falls and how fast the motor feeds the next.

props.name: cells
props.description: Columns on the board; the type scales so they always fit.

props.name: rows
props.description: Rows on the board; by default as many as the longest message needs.

props.name: ripple
props.description: Delay from one column to the next, ms, so the board settles in a wave.

props.name: ring
props.description: The characters each cell's flaps carry, in order: letters, digits, or both with punctuation.

props.name: size
props.description: The tallest a cell may be, px; narrow boards scale cells down to fit.

props.name: align
props.description: Where a row's words sit.

props.name: color
props.description: The letters.

props.name: flapColor
props.description: The flaps.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the current message: the timer stops, a press still changes it.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The board is a button: a press or Enter shows the next message, Left and Right step through them.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the first message clatters in from blank: on mount, when scrolled into view, on hover or keyboard focus, or — manual — when you control index or on the first press.

props.name: once
props.description: Cycle through the messages once and rest on the last.

props.name: delay
props.description: Wait before the first clatter, ms.

props.name: sound
props.description: Clack each flap the visitor sets falling, throttled; the timer's changes are silent.

props.name: caption
props.description: A line set into the housing above the cells — a title, a clock; it takes the board's width and never widens it.

props.name: label
props.description: The board's accessible name.

props.name: as
props.description: The element rendered around the board.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Fires each time the board settles on a message, with its index.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer element.

usageNotes: The current message is in an sr-only paragraph and the cells are aria-hidden; a polite status speaks a message only when the visitor changed it, once the board has settled, so automatic cycling is never announced.
One rAF loop integrates every moving flap and stops when the board is still, off screen or in a hidden page; the cycle timer waits for the board to settle and holds off screen.
Cells are sized from the board's own width with container units, so any number of columns fits from a phone to a desktop, up to size.
Under reduced motion no flap falls: each changing cell crossfades once to its letter, still a ripple apart, and cycling and announcements are unchanged.
Characters outside the ring become blanks; choose ring="digits" for clocks and counters, which also makes every change fewer flips.

items.title: Lens Warp
items.tagline: Letters bend under a glass bead.
items.description: A headline under a moving glass bead: letters near its centre magnify and are pushed outward with a smooth radial falloff, letters at its rim are squeezed and drawn in, and a faint highlight rides the glass — per-letter offsets and scale only, no filters. Every letter follows its target on its own spring, integrated in one loop: the springs.snap constants while the bead is on the words, so the type tracks it crisply, and a softer under-damped spring when it leaves, so the type relaxes with a wobble. The bead follows a mouse or pen 1:1, comes down under a finger, and makes one pass across the words when the trigger fires; with keyboard focus it lands on the first word, Left and Right walk it word by word on springs.glide, Home/End jump and Escape lifts it.

props.name: text
props.description: The headline under the glass.

props.name: as
props.description: The text element rendered.

props.name: radius
props.description: The bead's radius, px — never more than 1.5 times the type size; the piece reserves room above and below the words for it.

props.name: power
props.description: Magnification and bulge, 0 to 1.

props.name: specular
props.description: The highlight riding the bead, 0 to 1.

props.name: rim
props.description: How much the letters at the bead's rim are squeezed, 0 to 1.

props.name: wobble
props.description: How much the type wobbles as it relaxes when the bead leaves, 0 (none) to 1.

props.name: bead
props.description: Draw the glass disc itself; off leaves only the letters bending.

props.name: tint
props.description: The colour letters lean toward at the bead's centre.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and the keyboard move the bead.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the bead makes its one pass across the words: on mount, when scrolled into view, never (hover only), or when active turns true.

props.name: once
props.description: Make the pass only the first time.

props.name: delay
props.description: Wait before the pass, ms.

props.name: duration
props.description: How long the pass takes to cross the words, ms.

props.name: active
props.description: For trigger="manual": true runs the pass.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Fires when the pass is over and the type has relaxed.

props.name: onWordChange
props.description: Fires when the visitor moves the bead onto another word — by pointer or keys — and with null when it lifts; the automatic pass is not reported.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the wrapper; set the type size, weight and colour here.

usageNotes: The text is read once from an sr-only copy; the letters are aria-hidden but real text, so selecting and copying the headline gives the real words, and the transforms never touch layout.

The wrapper is focusable: focus brings the bead to the first word, Left and Right walk it word by word, Home/End jump and Escape lifts it; the word under the lens is spoken politely only when the keyboard moves it.

One rAF loop runs the letter springs only while the bead is present or a letter is still moving, and only on screen in a visible page; rest centres come from layout offsets, re-measured on resize and font load.
Under reduced motion nothing moves or scales: the bead appears in place and the letters under it lean toward tint by the same falloff, and the pass becomes a brief tint on the first word.
The piece reserves padding for the bead (0.3em at the sides, enough above and below for its radius) and clips to it, so neither the glass nor a magnified letter ever draws outside its box.

items.title: Pen Outline
items.tagline: A nib draws the outline, then the ink floods in.
items.description: A small nib travels the contour of every letter — outlines traced from the glyphs the browser actually rendered — while the stroke's dash offset grows under its tip, letter after letter, lifting between loops; when the last stroke closes, ink floods each letter from the bottom up behind a gentle wave on springs.drift, one after another. The pen runs on a linear clock (a hand at constant speed) that pauses off screen, and the flood is the real, selectable text clipped by a per-letter wave. Focused, Enter or Space drains the ink, rewinds the outline on the exit ease and writes it again.

props.name: text
props.description: The words the pen writes.

props.name: as
props.description: The element rendered.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the pen writes and the ink floods, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: stroke
props.description: Outline width, px.

props.name: flood
props.description: How much ink floods in once the outline closes: 0 leaves a pure outline, 1 is solid ink.

props.name: ink
props.description: Outline colour, any CSS colour.

props.name: floodColor
props.description: The colour the letters flood with.

props.name: guide
props.description: Opacity of the pencil guide shown before the pen arrives, 0 to 1.

props.name: wave
props.description: Height of the flood's wave front, 0 (flat) to 1.

props.name: nib
props.description: Show the travelling nib; the box reserves a quarter em above and right for it.

props.name: keepOutline
props.description: Keep the inked edge once the flood settles; false dissolves it into the fill.

props.name: trigger
props.description: What starts the drawing.

props.name: once

props.name: interactive

usageNotes: Keyboard: the headline is focusable when interactive; Enter or Space redraws it, and the full text is read once from a hidden copy while the drawing is aria-hidden.
Reduced motion: no nib and no wave — the outline fades in on a slow tween, then the ink fades up letter by letter; phases and onComplete still report.

Outlines are traced once per text, size or font change (one reused offscreen canvas, raster capped near 128px per em), so any inherited font works; nothing runs once the ink settles, and drawing pauses off screen and in hidden tabs.
The flood is the real text, so selection and copy return the words; colours default to tokens and read in both themes.
Set the size with className (it inherits otherwise); the root keeps a quarter em of room above and to the right for the nib, or pass nib={false} to drop it.

items.title: Stack Extrude
items.tagline: Type that lifts off the page in layered depth.
items.description: Every word is a real 3D block — a stack of copies at true translateZ depths under an em-based perspective, the sides in a pigment that darkens toward the back — and on arrival the words peel up off the page one after another, each word's height on springs.recoil and its stack spreading on springs.glide while a soft contact shadow widens and pales. The blocks turn to face the pointer on springs.glide and drift home on springs.drift; a press pushes them into the page on springs.flick, nearest first, and they pop back on recoil in a ripple. Arrow keys turn them, holding Space or Enter presses them, and Home or Escape squares them up.

props.name: as

props.name: layers

usageNotes: Keyboard: focusable when interactive — Arrow keys turn the blocks a third of `tilt` per press, holding Space or Enter presses them into the page, Home or Escape returns them to rest.
Reduced motion: the blocks hold `angle` without following the pointer; the sides fade in behind faces that never move, and a press darkens rather than moves.
Each frame writes two CSS variables per word plus the shared rotation; layer depths are static calc() strings, and nothing runs at rest.
The box reserves room below and right for the sides and the shadow; face and side colours default to tokens and a fixed-lightness pigment so both themes read.
The face copy is the real text for layout; the visual stack is aria-hidden and a hidden copy carries the words for assistive technology.

items.title: Paper Crease
items.tagline: A headline unfolds like a letter.
items.description: Each line of the headline is a strip of paper cut into panels along horizontal creases, nested hinges rolled toward the reader so only the blank back of the first flap shows; unfolding opens crease after crease on springs.snap, each panel's back darkening toward edge-on and its face catching a crease shadow and a glare that slides down it, with a faint crease left in the paper. Under the pointer or with focus the creases refold a few degrees like paper with memory (snap in, glide out). A press — or Enter or Space — folds the letter up on the exit ease, last crease first, and opens it again with a crinkle per crease when sound is on.

props.name: ink

props.name: sound

Reduced motion: nothing turns — the folded paper strip and the open text cross-fade, and the creases stay as faint lines.
Sound plays only for the visitor's press, one paper crinkle per crease as it opens, and only when `sound` is true.
Keep each line short enough to sit on one row at your narrowest width: a wrapped line still folds, but its creases then cut across two rows.
Every motion is a finite spring or tween on one motion value per crease; nothing runs at rest. The paper defaults to the card token, so both themes read.

items.title: After Image
items.tagline: Every word leaves a fading echo.
items.description: Every word keeps a short timestamped history of where it has been, and its echoes are placed where it was a few lag milliseconds ago — fainter and turned further round the hue circle the older they are — so motion fans out behind it as a chromatic afterglow that folds back in when it stops. Words arrive on curved paths (x on springs.glide, y on springs.snap), a dragged word follows 1:1 with its neighbours trailing, and on release every word springs home on springs.recoil with the throw's velocity while one faint echo breathes at rest. Arrow keys throw the words the same way and Enter brings them in again.

props.name: text
props.description: The words; each one trails its own echoes.

props.name: as
props.description: The element rendered.

props.name: echoes

props.name: lag

props.name: color

props.name: fade

props.name: glow

usageNotes: Keyboard: focusable when interactive — Arrow keys throw every word in that direction and recoil brings them home, the same end state as a drag; Enter or Space replays the arrival.
Reduced motion: words never travel; they fade in while a still afterglow at fixed offsets fades out, and drags or keys flash that afterglow instead of moving anything.

One rAF loop per instance runs only while a word moves or an echo is catching up, writing preallocated history rings (no per-frame allocation); the idle breath is a single tween that stops off screen, in hidden tabs and under reduced motion.
Drag is horizontal-friendly on touch (touch-action: pan-y keeps vertical scrolling); echoes are clipped to a short margin round the box, so they never spill far.
The echoes are aria-hidden copies; a hidden copy carries the words once for assistive technology. Echo colours derive from a token via relative oklch, so both themes read.

items.title: Cascade Split
items.tagline: Letters arrive on springs, word by word.
items.description: The text splits into letters, words or the lines it wraps to, and each piece arrives on a spring in one of three ways: rising through an edge just under its baseline on springs.snap, dropping in and settling on springs.recoil, or swinging down from a pin at its top-left corner like a hanging tile, past rest and back on recoil. The gaps between pieces follow an easing curve rather than a fixed step, and leaving replays the curve in reverse, last piece first, on the exit ease. Pointer passes nudge each piece in its own idiom through a second transform; focused, Left and Right walk a probe that nudges each piece and Enter or Space plays it again.

Reduced motion: nothing travels or turns; pieces fade in along the same curve in half the time and leave by fading in reverse.
Splits by grapheme, so emoji and combining marks stay whole, and words never break inside; line mode reads the wrap from layout when the cascade starts.
Long texts are soft-capped so the whole cascade stays brief; pass your own curve for custom choreography. Every motion is a finite spring or tween — nothing runs at rest.

items.title: Depth of Field
items.tagline: Words rack into focus like a lens.
items.description: A line shot through a fast lens: every word starts soft, a little smaller and faded, and a focal plane sweeps along the line kicking each word sharp on a spring that runs from snap to recoil with breath, so focus breathes past the word before it settles, with a focus-peaking edge flashing as it lands. Pointing at a word racks focus to it — the plane itself travels on a glide-weight spring, so a long pull passes through the words between and the rest fall off with distance — and leaving stops the lens down again. A keyboard handle racks word to word with Left and Right, Escape brings everything into focus and Enter plays the pull again.

Reduced motion: no plane travel, scale or breathing; soft words cross-fade to sharp in reading order and a re-rack fades straight to the new depth, so where focus sits still reads.
The text is read once from an sr-only copy; the word spans are aria-hidden but selectable, so copy gives the real words.
Blur and peaking are in em, so the effect holds from a caption to a hero; it only ever shrinks words, so nothing reaches past its box.
One rAF integrator drives the plane and every word through motion values; it runs only while something moves, on screen, in a visible page.

items.title: Orbit Script
items.tagline: A ring of text that turns, and turns to face you.
items.description: Text set round a ring at its measured advances, turning at a cruising speed: a pointer over it brakes it to a stop with friction while the nearest letter lifts off the ring on the snap spring and turns upright to face the reader, a drag spins it 1:1 about its centre and a flick coasts down by the same friction back to cruise, and on arrival the letters lay themselves onto the ring clockwise as it spools up. It is a slider in the tab order: the arrow keys step it one letter at a time on the snap spring, Page Up and Page Down a quarter turn, and Space pauses the turn.

Reduced motion: the ring stands still, a drag turns it 1:1 without coasting, keys step instantly, and the nearest letter takes the accent colour instead of lifting.
The box is 2 × (radius + 1.25) em square, so it scales with the inherited font size; text longer than the ring is set tighter rather than overlapping.
One rAF loop owns the angle and the lifted letters; it runs while the ring turns on screen in a visible page and stops when it is braked and still. Only lifted letters are rewritten per frame.
touch-none on the ring: it is a 2D drag. Sound is off unless sound is set, and only answers a drag, a flick or a key.

items.title: Live Caption
items.tagline: Words land as they're spoken, then settle.
items.description: Live captions that behave like the real thing: a script plays at a seeded speaking rhythm, each word landing in draft ink with a small drop on the snap spring, uncertain words shimmering, and a misheard word revising in place once two more words are in — the old word lifts away as the right one rises while the word's box springs to its new width on glide, so the line reflows instead of jumping. When a sentence is complete it settles into solid ink as a left-to-right wash staggered under the 600 ms budget, and the box rolls up on glide like broadcast captions. There is no gesture to answer; a host pauses it through paused.

Reduced motion keeps the speaking rhythm (the words are the information) but drops the travel: words fade in, corrections cross-fade at their final width, nothing shimmers and the roll-up jumps.
The box is lines × 1.5em tall and reserved from the start, so arriving words never move the page; older lines roll up and fade out at the top edge.
One timer walks a seeded event list and stops off screen, while the tab is hidden, while paused and at the end without loop; the shared shimmer runs only while a shimmering word shows.
No keyboard path is needed — there is no gesture — so give readers a Pause control (paused) next to fast captions.

items.title: Deck Shuffle
items.tagline: Letters riffle like cards before they settle.

Pointing at a word riffles it again, a tap does on touch, and a keyboard handle riffles the whole line with Enter or one word at a time with Left and Right.

Reduced motion: no turns, lift or bounce — each card cross-fades from its back to its letter in reading order, and a re-riffle is a brief cross-fade to the back and back.
The true letter is always each card's own in-flow text, so the line's box never changes during a riffle and copying gives the real words; the random faces live on a select-none overlay.
Faces change only when a card turns edge-on (a write to its overlay, not a render); nothing runs between riffles, and a riffle caught off screen or in a hidden tab lands at once.
Sound is off unless sound is set, plays only for riffles the visitor caused, and stays silent until the page has had a click, tap or key.

items.title: Foil Sheen
items.tagline: Gold-leaf light runs across the letters.

The pointer tilts the light on the glide spring and shifts the foil's broad reflections, and a press catches the light with a sweep from the side you pressed. A keyboard handle tilts the light with Left and Right and sends a sweep with Enter.

props.name: emboss

props.name: interactive

usageNotes: Keyboard: one tab stop, a slider for the light's angle; Left and Right tilt it 5 degrees, Home and End to the extremes, Enter or Space sends a sweep, Escape lets the light drift back.
Reduced motion: no sweep — the light rests a third of the way across the line, still and grainy, the pointer tilts nothing, and Enter swells the light in place.
The foil layer is the real text: it reads, selects (in the foreground colour) and copies as itself; the two light layers are aria-hidden and select-none.
Pigments sit at fixed lightness and lean toward the page's ink, so the foil keeps its edge in both themes; any CSS colour works as a tint through relative colour syntax.
Idle between sweeps (one timer); none are scheduled off screen or in a hidden tab. The micro-texture is a 96 px tile drawn once per seed and shared.

items.title: Weight Field
items.tagline: The weight swells where the pointer leans.
items.description: Text pressure with a body: each letter's tension is drawn through the inherited variable font's weight and width axes, and the pointer is a field — letters near it swell along a smooth bell of the distance, tensing on the snap spring and relaxing on a spring between snap and drift, so a pass across the word leaves a wake of weight relaxing behind the pointer; a press leans harder, and a flex wave runs once across the line on arrival. On touch a press-and-drag leans the same way, and a keyboard handle leans on one letter at a time with Left and Right.

props.name: text

props.name: as

props.name: radius

props.name: minWeight

props.name: maxWeight

props.name: minWidth

props.name: maxWidth

props.name: lean

props.name: relax

props.name: axes

props.name: align
props.description: Where the relaxed line sits in the room the swollen line needs.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer, a touch drag and the keys lean on the letters.

props.name: trigger

props.name: once

props.name: delay

props.name: duration

props.name: play

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: one tab stop, a slider; Left and Right lean on the letters one at a time (spaces skipped), Home and End jump, Escape or leaving the handle lets go.
Reduced motion: no wave and no springs — each letter takes its weight directly from the pointer or keys, with no overshoot or wake, because the swell is the feedback.

The axes are measured on the client from a hidden probe; with no wght or wdth axis the swell falls back to a stroke for weight and a stretch for width. An invisible copy set at the maximum reserves the box, so size the type for the swollen line to fit.
One rAF loop integrates every letter and stops when they are all at rest; rest centres are re-read only while the line is relaxed, so a swelling line never chases itself.
touch-pan-y: a horizontal drag leans on the letters and a vertical swipe still scrolls the page.

items.title: Contour Marquee
items.tagline: A sentence that rides any curve.
items.description: A marquee whose rail is a curve: the sentence repeats seamlessly along a wave, an arch, a loop that passes behind itself, or any path you give it, every glyph turned to the curve's tangent. One phase is integrated from a velocity that only ever eases — to cruise, to a crawl under the pointer or focus, to rest when paused — on a critically damped spring that is springs.drift at the default coast; grabbing the line scrubs it 1:1 along the curve by projecting the pointer onto the path, and a flick hands its speed back to that spring. The rail is a button: Space or Enter pauses, Left and Right glide a word on springs.glide (Shift a whole sentence), Home re-centres it.

props.name: as

props.name: curve

props.name: viewBox

props.name: speed

props.name: coast

props.name: separator

props.name: spacing

props.name: guide

props.name: fade

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: the rail is a toggle button named 'Pause the moving text'. Space or Enter pauses and resumes, Left and Right glide one word, Shift with an arrow a whole sentence, Home re-centres the sentence. Moving text needs a way to stop it, so leave the button reachable.
Reduced motion: nothing cruises — the sentence rests centred on the curve. Dragging still scrubs it 1:1, a release does not coast, arrows step instantly.

Size comes from the inherited font size (the box is measured in em), so set the type with a text class or clamp() on a parent; the preset curves regenerate for the measured width, about one wave crest per 13em.
A custom curve is any path d in its own viewBox; the box takes the viewBox's proportions and the type keeps its page size. Leave about 1em of room around the path for the glyphs.
The sentence is read once from an sr-only copy (as); the SVG is aria-hidden. The frame loop runs only on screen, in a visible tab, and while the line is moving — paused and settled it costs nothing.

items.title: Static Fuzz
items.tagline: Text frayed by analog noise.
items.description: Type received over a weak analog signal: the real words stay in the DOM while a WebGL2 canvas draws them frayed, every pixel row pushed sideways by a slow hum that bends whole bands of type, a per-row jitter that changes thirty times a second, the odd torn row and rolling bands that pass down through the words. Hovering opens a calm disc around the pointer on springs.snap, so the rows lock into register outward from it, while the whole line settles on springs.drift; leaving closes the disc on an exit tween and sends a band through as the signal frays again. Keyboard focus on, inside or around the element steadies it completely, and the arrival comes in from full static on springs.drift.

props.name: text

props.name: as
props.description: The element the text lives in.

props.name: intensity

props.name: bands
props.description: Rolling bands that pass through every ten seconds, 0 to 6.

props.name: calm

props.name: settle
props.description: How far the whole line steadies while hovered, 0 to 1. Keyboard focus steadies it fully.

props.name: grain
props.description: Ink dropping out in speckle, 0 to 1.

props.name: ghost

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the noise moves, 0.25 to 2.

props.name: color
props.description: Ink colour, any CSS colour; resolved on the element so it follows the theme.

props.name: seed

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the signal comes in from full static.

props.name: active

props.name: once

props.name: delay

props.name: onComplete

props.name: paused

props.name: interactive

props.name: focusable

props.name: dpr
props.description: Device pixel ratio cap for the canvas.

props.name: onCalmChange

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the element; set the type here (size, weight, colour).

usageNotes: The words are the element's own DOM text, so they wrap, select, copy and read exactly once; the canvas over them is aria-hidden and ignores the pointer. Set the font with ordinary text classes — the canvas rasterises whatever the page laid out.
The element carries a 0.28em horizontal gutter so torn rows stay inside its box; give it a matching negative margin (-mx-[0.28em]) to align the type with its column.
Keyboard: focus on the element (with focusable), on a link or button around it, or inside it steadies the whole line. Touch steadies it while a finger rests on the words.
Reduced motion: a still frame of mild fuzz with no bands; hover or focus cross-fades it to crisp type and back.

Cost: one WebGL2 draw per changed field (30 a second at most), only on screen in a visible tab; fully steadied, paused or at zero intensity it stops. DPR is capped at dpr. Without WebGL2 the plain text shows with a faint echo; after a lost context it shows until the context is restored.

items.title: Pigment Flow
items.tagline: Ink colours that drift through the letters.
items.description: Gradient text that behaves like pigment let into water: soft clouds of each colour wander seeded paths through the letters over a thinner wash of them all, every gradient mixed in oklab, all of it pure CSS on clipped text with motion values driving the stops. On arrival a drop blooms from the middle of the plain ink on a critically damped spring sized by duration (springs.drift at the default), and the pointer stirs a swirl of the pigments around a centre that trails it on springs.glide — circling winds it up, and it unwinds and fades as the water stills while the clouds it pushed drift home. Keyboard focus on, inside or around the element stirs the middle once, and with focusable the Left and Right keys stir the ink round either way.

props.name: as

props.name: colors

props.name: speed

props.name: stir

props.name: radius

props.name: diffusion

props.name: angle

props.name: seed
props.description: Seed for the clouds' paths, so two lines never drift in step.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the drop of pigment blooms into the ink.

props.name: active
props.description: With trigger="manual", the pigment blooms when this turns true.

props.name: once

props.name: delay

props.name: duration

props.name: onComplete

props.name: onStirChange

props.name: paused

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer, touch and focus stir the flow.

props.name: focusable

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the element; set the type here (size, weight, leading).

usageNotes: The words are real DOM text clipped to their background, so they wrap, select, copy and read once; the stir layer is an aria-hidden copy that ignores the pointer. Browsers without oklab gradients keep the plain text colour.

The palettes are text-tuned tokens, so the type keeps its contrast in both themes. Your own colours work too — pick ones that read as text on your surface, and mix toward var(--foreground) to deepen them.

Keyboard: with focusable, the words take focus and Left and Right stir the ink one way or the other; focus on the element, on a link or button around it, or inside it sends one slow stir through the middle. Touch stirs with a horizontal drag; vertical swipes still scroll the page.
Reduced motion: a still composition; the bloom is a cross-fade from ink, and the pointer leaves a soft drop of pigment that fades in and out.
Cost: no canvas. The ambient drift repaints at most 30 times a second, only on screen in a visible tab; paused or at speed 0 it stops, and a stir runs at frame rate only until the water stills.

items.title: Letter Rain
items.tagline: Letters drop, tumble and pile up.
items.description: A headline whose letters fall off the line: on its trigger each letter lets go — nearest the press first, cascade-staggered inside 600ms — and drops as a rigid box the size of its own ink, landing on corners, toppling, bouncing and piling at the foot of the box under a small real engine (separating-axis contacts, sequential impulses with friction, restitution and warm starting, sleep). Any letter can be picked up and follows the pointer 1:1, shoving the pile, then leaves with the release velocity and spin; Reassemble flies every letter home in reading order, x on springs.glide and y and rotation on springs.snap, each starting from its own velocity. The stage is a button: Enter drops the line or knocks the pile, Left and Right shove it, Up tosses it, and the Reassemble button brings it home.

props.name: text
props.description: The line whose letters fall.

props.name: as
props.description: The element that carries the line for assistive technology.

props.name: gravity

props.name: bounce

props.name: friction
props.description: How much letters grip each other and the floor, 0 (ice) to 1 (felt).

props.name: trigger

props.name: fallen / defaultFallen

props.name: onFallenChange
props.description: Fires from the press, key or gesture that dropped or reassembled the line.

props.name: depth
props.description: How far below the line the floor sits, em.

props.name: floor
props.description: Draw the floor the letters land on, as a hairline.

props.name: throwable
props.description: Letters can be picked up and thrown.

props.name: delay
props.description: Wait before an automatic drop (hover, in view, mount), ms.

props.name: stagger
props.description: Between letters letting go of the line, ms; capped so the whole line goes inside 600ms.

props.name: once
props.description: Automatic triggers drop the line only once.

props.name: reassembleAfter
props.description: Reassemble on its own this long after the pile comes to rest, ms; 0 waits for a press.

props.name: reassembleLabel

props.name: onComplete
props.description: The pile has come to rest, or the line has reassembled.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the landings the visitor causes. Off unless asked for.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No dropping, throwing or reassembling.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; set the type here — the physics scales with the font size.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the stage is a button. Enter or Space drops the line from its middle, or knocks the pile once it is down; Left and Right shove the pile, Up tosses it; the Reassemble button (shown while letters are loose) flies them home and hands focus back to the stage.

Reduced motion: nothing falls on screen. The same seeded pile is simulated out of sight and the letters cross-fade into it; throws, shoves and Reassemble cross-fade too. Dragging a letter still follows the finger.

The line is read once from an sr-only copy (as); the letters are aria-hidden spans in the line, so the box never shifts. The box is the line plus depth em of floor — leave it room. Letters are split by grapheme, so emoji and accents fall whole; scripts that join their letters (Arabic, Devanagari) are better left on the line.

Cost: the simulation runs at 120Hz (more when something is fast) only while a letter is awake, on screen and in a visible tab; a settled pile sleeps and costs nothing. Up to a few dozen letters is comfortable.
Sound (thud) only answers the visitor — a press, a key, a throw or a knock — never a hover, scroll-in or mount drop, and never before the page has had a click or key.

items.title: Type Trail
items.tagline: Your cursor writes as it moves.
items.description: A container whose pointer writes a phrase: the letters are laid along the pointer's recent path, spaced by arc length and turned to its tangent, leaving their resting line one by one on springs.glide as the pen reaches them, wet in the accent colour at the nib and fading and shrinking down the tail. When the pointer rests the phrase gathers into a neat line under it on springs.snap — one crisp overshoot as each letter rights itself, staggered from the nib back — and moving again releases it onto the path on springs.glide; leaving sends it home. The container takes focus: the arrow keys walk a visible pen that writes the same trail, Enter gathers under it and Escape sends the phrase back.

props.name: text

props.name: children

props.name: as

props.name: spacing

props.name: tail

props.name: smoothing

props.name: accent

usageNotes: The trail is bounded to the container and drawn in an aria-hidden, pointer-events-none layer, so links and buttons inside stay fully usable; the system cursor is never hidden. Give the container a height — the phrase rests inside it.

Keyboard: with keyboard on, the container is a focusable group named by the phrase. The arrow keys move a visible pen that writes the trail (Shift for 4em steps), Enter gathers the phrase under it, Escape sends it back to rest.
Touch: a sideways drag writes the trail and lifting the finger gathers it; vertical swipes still scroll the page (touch-action: pan-y).
Reduced motion: no letter travels. The phrase steps out of sight while the pointer moves and fades in as a neat line wherever it comes to rest; there is no ghost pen.

Cost: frames run only while the pen is moving or letters are settling, on screen in a visible tab; at rest it costs nothing. Letter widths are measured once per phrase, size and font; the path is a fixed typed-array ring.

items.title: Cipher Wheel
items.tagline: Each letter turns its dial until it reads.
items.description: A headline that decrypts on a row of rotary dials: every letter turns its own drum through the character set with a ratchet feel — each notch a springs.flick step, summed in closed form from one clock — and locks onto its letter on springs.snap with one clean overshoot and a hairline flash, the locks cascading left to right, at random or from the middle before the housings dissolve into plain type. Pressing the headline, or Enter or Space on it, turns the dials again from their own letters, and the pointer thumbs a resting dial that the detent pulls back.

props.name: as

props.name: order

props.name: speed

props.name: delay

props.name: trigger

props.name: once
props.description: With inView, decrypt only the first time it is seen.

props.name: active

props.name: interactive

props.name: housing

props.name: flashColor

props.name: seed

props.name: sound

props.name: onLock

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: with interactive on, the headline is focusable and Enter or Space turns the dials again; trigger="hover" also turns them when the headline takes focus. A drag that selects words never triggers a replay, and selection copies the real text.

Reduced motion: nothing travels — each housing shows its scrambled glyph, which cross-fades to the true letter at its lock in the same order, with the same hairline flash; the pointer does not thumb the dials.

Accessibility: the full headline is read once from an sr-only copy inside the element; the dial layer is aria-hidden. The hint for the keyboard path is referenced with aria-describedby, outside the heading so it never joins its name.

Performance: one linear clock per run drives every dial through motion values — no per-letter animation objects, no React render per frame — and the clock pauses off screen and in a hidden tab. Settled, nothing runs.
Size and colour inherit from the element (em-based), so the same dials work from a caption to a hero; the housings and the shading are drawn from currentColor, so both themes read.
Sound, when on, ticks once per lock with the pitch rising along the cascade, and only for runs started by a press, Enter or Space; hovering, thumbing a dial and the automatic triggers stay silent.

items.title: Word Bracket
items.tagline: A focus frame hops from word to word.
items.description: True-focus text: four corner brackets frame one sharp, full-ink word while the rest of the sentence sits blurred and dimmed, and on a timer the frame hops on like an inchworm — the leading edge leaves on springs.snap and bites the next word with one crisp overshoot, the trailing edge follows a beat later on springs.glide, and a hop to another line glides the whole frame. Hovering or tapping a word takes the frame there and holds the cycle; with the sentence focused, Left and Right move it a word, Home and End jump to the ends.

props.name: as

props.name: interval

props.name: frame

props.description: The frame moved to a word: the cycle, the pointer or a key chose it. Also reported on arrival.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the frame where it is.

props.name: loop
props.description: Wrap from the last word back to the first.

props.name: hoverControl
props.description: Hovering a word, tapping it or the arrow keys take the frame; the cycle resumes after.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: The cycle reached the last word (only without loop).

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the sentence element; size, weight and colour are inherited.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the sentence is focusable; Left/Up and Right/Down move the frame a word (skipping words shorter than minLength), Home and End jump to the ends, and the cycle waits while it has focus and resumes one interval after it leaves.
Pointer: hovering a word takes the frame there and holds the cycle until the pointer leaves the sentence; on touch a tap focuses the tapped word and the cycle resumes after two intervals.
Reduced motion: the frame does not travel or stretch — it fades out at one word and in at the next, and the words' sharpness changes with a short fade.
Accessibility: the sentence is read once from an sr-only copy; the blurred word layer and the brackets are aria-hidden, and the visible words still select and copy as written.

Performance: the cycle is a single timer that runs only while the sentence is on screen in a visible page and nothing holds it; the frame's four edges are motion values moved by transforms, and word boxes are re-measured only on resize and font load.
Size and colour inherit from the element; pass any CSS colour (a token is best) to frame so the brackets read in both themes.

items.title: Buoyant Line
items.tagline: Letters rise into place as you scroll.
items.description: Scroll-float text: as the line scrolls up through its container's viewport, its letters float up from below their places left to right, each on its own share of the scroll and its own spring — from springs.snap toward springs.drift as the lag grows, with a bob at the surface — swaying, tinted and faded while submerged, and they sink back if you scroll up. Progress is read from the nearest scroll container, or set directly, and the element's bottom edge is the waterline; the keyboard path is the container's own scrolling.

props.name: text
props.description: The line. Read once by assistive technology, and copied as written.

props.name: as
props.description: The element the line renders as.

props.name: rise
props.description: How deep the letters start below their places, em.

props.name: lag
props.description: How strung out the rise is, 0 (together, brisk) to 1 (one after another, slow to follow).

props.name: range
props.description: How much of the viewport's height the line scrolls through while its letters rise, 0.1 to 1.

props.name: start
props.description: Where the rise begins, as a fraction of the viewport's height from its top (1 is the bottom edge).

props.name: sway
props.description: How far a submerged letter tilts as it sways, degrees.

props.name: bob
props.description: How much the letters bob as they reach the surface, 0 (none) to 1.

props.name: tint
props.description: The colour a submerged letter takes before it surfaces into ink.

props.name: fade
props.description: Fade the letters with depth.

props.name: progress
props.description: Drive the rise yourself, 0 to 1; overrides scrolling.

props.name: once
props.description: Once every letter has surfaced, stay surfaced.

props.name: scrollContainer
props.description: The scroll container to read; defaults to the nearest scrollable ancestor, or the window.

props.name: onProgressChange
props.description: The line's progress through its rise, 0 to 1 in steps of 0.01, as it changes.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Every letter has surfaced (again).

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the line element; size, weight and colour are inherited.

usageNotes: Keyboard: there is no gesture of its own — the rise follows the scroll container, so make that container focusable (tabIndex 0 and a label) and the arrow, Page and Space keys drive it.
Reduced motion: nothing rises, sways or bobs; the letters fade in place from faint to full ink in reading order, still tied to the scroll, because how far the reader has come is information.
Accessibility: the line is read once from an sr-only copy; the letter layer is aria-hidden but its letters still select and copy as written.

Performance: one passive scroll listener on the container does work only while the line is near view (an IntersectionObserver gates it, and a last reading lands as it leaves), every letter is a spring on a motion value with no React render per frame, and the springs settle and stop.
The element's bottom edge is the waterline (a clip on that edge only): give the line a little room below it if its letters should be seen rising from further down.
Colour and size inherit; tint takes any CSS colour, so a token keeps the water readable in both themes.

items.title: Read Along
items.tagline: Words darken as you read them.
items.description: Scroll-reveal for long paragraphs: every word starts in faint ink and the words darken in reading order as the paragraph scrolls past the reading line, a long word taking longer than a short one, with the reading position gliding on springs.glide between scroll events so scrolling back reverses it just as smoothly. A soft underline draws itself through the word being read — its tail follows the word's start on glide, so between words it slides on like a finger under the line — or a caret marks the place; the keyboard path is the scroll container's own scrolling.

props.name: text
props.description: The paragraph. It stays real text, read and copied in order.

props.name: as
props.description: The element the paragraph renders as.

props.name: faint
props.description: How faint unread words are, as opacity 0 to 1.

props.name: range
props.description: Where reading ends, as a share of the viewport's height below start: the paragraph is read once its bottom edge has risen to start − range. 0.1 to 1.

props.name: start
props.description: Where reading begins: the paragraph's top at this fraction of the viewport's height from its top.

props.name: cursor
props.description: What marks the reading position: a soft underline drawn through the word, a caret, or nothing.

props.name: cursorColor
props.description: The cursor's colour.

props.name: softness
props.description: How many characters the darkening front is spread over.

props.name: pace
props.description: Whether a long word takes longer to read (length) or every word the same (even).

props.name: smooth
props.description: Glide the reading position between scroll events.

props.name: progress
props.description: Drive the reading yourself, 0 to 1; overrides scrolling.

props.name: scrollContainer
props.description: The scroll container to read; defaults to the nearest scrollable ancestor, or the window.

props.name: onProgressChange
props.description: How far through the paragraph reading is, 0 to 1 in steps of 0.01, as it changes.

props.name: onWordChange
props.description: The word being read changed: its index among the paragraph's words. Also reported on arrival.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: The paragraph has been read to its end (again).

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the paragraph element; size, leading and colour are inherited.

usageNotes: Keyboard: reading follows the scroll container, so make that container focusable (tabIndex 0 and a label) and the arrow, Page and Space keys read the paragraph forward and back.
Reduced motion: the reading position does not glide and the underline does not slide; words still darken with the scroll, because where the reader is is information.

Accessibility: the words stay real text in order — there is no duplicate copy — so the paragraph reads and copies normally; the cursor is aria-hidden and faint ink never drops below the opacity you set.

Performance: one passive scroll listener does work only while the paragraph is near view; one smoothed motion value drives every word's opacity and the cursor, and once the glide settles nothing runs. Word boxes are measured on resize and font load only.
Progress runs from the paragraph's top reaching start until its bottom reaches start − range, so a long paragraph is read over more scrolling than a short one.
Colours inherit; cursorColor takes any CSS colour, so a token keeps the underline readable in both themes.

items.title: Char Cast
items.tagline: Your headline cast in characters.
items.description: Your headline recast in characters: the real text is rasterised from its own layout and redrawn on a canvas as a grid of glyphs picked by a density ramp, with a slow value noise drifting through them, and it casts in on a seeded sweep where each cell's density follows the springs.snap step response — one step heavier, then settled. The pointer carries a soft light that trails the hand on springs.glide, inside which finer characters resolve the true letterforms; with the headline focused the arrow keys walk the light, and touch drags it.

props.name: text
props.description: The headline. It stays real text — transparent over the characters — so it reads, selects and copies.

props.name: as
props.description: The element the headline renders as.

props.name: cell
props.description: The character cell's width, px; rows are 1.4 times taller, as mono glyphs are.

props.name: ramp
props.description: The density ramp the coverage is cast through, light to dense.

props.name: characters
props.description: A custom ramp, lightest first (start with a space); overrides ramp.

props.name: light
props.description: The radius of the light the pointer carries, px; 0 turns it off.

props.name: tint
props.description: The colour the finer characters warm toward at the light's centre.

props.name: drift
props.description: How fast the noise drifts through the glyphs, 0 (still) to 2.

props.name: contrast
props.description: The coverage curve: above 1 thins the strokes, below 1 fattens them; 0.5 to 2.

props.name: trigger
props.description: What casts the headline.

props.name: once
props.description: With inView, cast only the first time it is seen.

props.name: active
props.description: With manual: true casts the headline, false shows it as plain type.

props.name: duration
props.description: How long the cast takes to sweep across, ms.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer, a touch or the arrow keys carry the light.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Caps the canvas's device pixel ratio; never above 2.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the noise and the cast's order.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: The cast has settled.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the headline element; its font, size, weight and colour are what get cast.

usageNotes: Keyboard: with interactive on, the headline is focusable; keyboard focus brings the light to the first letter, the arrow keys move it a few cells or a line at a time, Home and End jump along the line, and leaving puts it out. Touch drags it horizontally (vertical drags still scroll) and a tap leaves it a moment.
Reduced motion: no drift, the cast is a single fade, and the light follows the pointer directly rather than trailing it on a spring.

Accessibility: the headline is real text in the element — transparent once cast, so it reads, selects and copies — and the canvas is aria-hidden. Before the cast (and without script) it shows as plain type.

Performance: the canvas draws only while the light moves or the cast runs, at about 12 frames a second while it only drifts (drift 0 stops it entirely), and never off screen or in a hidden tab. Rasterising happens on layout, font load and text changes only; the backing store follows ResizeObserver with its pixel ratio capped at 2, and a lost 2D context redraws when restored.

Colour comes from the element's own text colour and tint, resolved on the element and re-read when the theme changes, so it reads in both themes. Use a heavy weight at display sizes: the bolder the strokes, the clearer the cast.

items.title: Scramble Brush
items.tagline: Your cursor scrambles what it touches.
items.description: Text you can brush: letters within a radius of the pointer turn to re-rolling noise, hot at the brush's core and cooling toward muted ink, and each returns to its letter a moment after the pointer last touched it — the core holding longer than the rim — so the cursor drags a tapering wake through the paragraph. Every true letter drops back in from a nudge above on springs.snap, so the wake settles in a ripple; with the text focused, the arrow keys hold one word scrambled and the word left behind ripples back to type.

props.name: text
props.description: The text. Read once by assistive technology, and copied as written.

props.name: as
props.description: The element the text renders as.

props.name: radius
props.description: How far from the pointer letters scramble, px.

props.name: restore
props.description: How long a letter stays scrambled after the pointer last touched it, ms.

props.name: glyphs
props.description: The noise a scrambled letter shows.

props.name: characters
props.description: A custom glyph set; overrides glyphs.

props.name: rate
props.description: How often a scrambled letter re-rolls its glyph, ms.

props.name: falloff
props.description: How much longer the brush's core holds its noise than its rim, 0 to 1.

props.name: color
props.description: The noise's colour at the brush's core; it cools toward muted ink.

props.name: keyboard
props.description: The text is focusable and the arrow keys brush it word by word.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing scrambles.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the noise.

props.name: onScrambleChange
props.description: How many letters are scrambled, as it changes.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the text element; size, leading and colour are inherited.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the text is focusable; keyboard focus scrambles the first word and holds it while focused, Left/Up and Right/Down move to the previous or next word (the one left behind ripples back to type, letter by letter), Home and End jump to the ends, and a thin underline marks the held word.
Touch: a horizontal drag brushes (touch-action pan-y, so vertical drags still scroll) and a tap brushes one spot.
Reduced motion: no re-rolling flicker and no drop — a touched letter shows one still glyph and cross-fades back to its letter after the same delay.
Accessibility: the text is read once from an sr-only copy; the letter layer is aria-hidden, and the true letters stay in it so a selection still copies the real words.

Performance: frames run only while some letter is scrambled and stop when the last one is back; each frame writes straight to the letters' noise layer with no React render, letter centres are measured on resize and font load, and the noise comes from a seeded generator.
Colours inherit; color takes any CSS colour, and the cooling noise is mixed from the text's own colour, so it reads in both themes.

items.title: Stamp Cycle
items.tagline: Each word is pressed in like a rubber stamp.
items.description: A rotating word that is stamped into its slot: the old impression lifts off on the exit ease while the slot's width springs to the new word on springs.glide, the stamp's shadow falls, and at contact the ink prints across the word from the edge the stamp rocked onto first while the slot squashes and recovers on springs.recoil and a ring of displaced ink spreads and settles to a residue. The ink carries the rubber's grain, so a firm press prints solid and a light one patchy and dry. The slot is a button: pressing lowers the stamp and letting go stamps the next word (holding prints firmer), and Enter or Space stamps through the native click.

props.name: words
props.description: The words stamped into the slot, one after another.

props.name: index / defaultIndex
props.description: Which word is stamped; controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Fires from the timer or the press that stamped a new word.

props.name: interval
props.description: Rest between automatic stamps, ms.

props.name: ink
props.description: A named token ink, or any CSS colour.

props.name: press
props.description: How firmly the stamp lands, 0 to 1: squash depth, ink coverage, ring size and fall speed.

props.name: texture
props.description: How much of the rubber's grain shows in the ink, 0 (flat) to 1.

props.name: tilt
props.description: The largest seeded tilt a word lands at, degrees.

props.name: frame
props.description: A border printed around the word with the same ink and grain.

props.name: ring
props.description: The spatter of displaced ink at contact and the residue it leaves.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the automatic cycle runs.

props.name: once
props.description: One pass through the words, resting on the last.

props.name: delay
props.description: Wait after the trigger before the first stamp, ms.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the automatic cycle.

props.name: pauseOnHover
props.description: Hover and keyboard focus hold the cycle so the word can be read.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The slot is a button: pressing it stamps the next word.

props.name: sound
props.description: A thock when the visitor stamps, pitched by how firmly.

props.name: as
props.description: The root element.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: A once pass has stamped its last word.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; case and tracking carry into the slot.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the slot is a real button named by the current word; Enter or Space stamps the next word through the native click, and focus holds the automatic cycle so the word can be read.
Reduced motion: no fall, squash or rock; the old word fades out, the new ink fades in at its seeded tilt with the residue already printed, and presses still stamp.
Performance: there is no animation loop; one timeout per beat, armed only while the slot is on screen in a visible page and not held, and each stamp is a few springs and tweens that end.
Place it inline in your own sentence; it inherits the font, size, case and tracking, and the frame gives back its padding so the line keeps its leading.
Ink is a token by default so it reads in both themes; pass any CSS colour to brand it. Only stamps the visitor makes are announced and heard.

items.title: Datamosh Type
items.tagline: A headline corrupted by compression.
items.description: A headline that fails the way compressed video fails: between bursts it is plain, selectable DOM text, and a burst swaps it for a canvas picture of the same glyphs that is corrupted frame by frame at a codec's frame rate — grid-aligned rows of macro-blocks slip sideways and drag a pixel run behind them, blocks freeze on the previous frame, drift to another block's pixels or quantise into a mosaic, and the two colour channels split apart behind the ink. Each burst ramps in, holds and decays on its own envelope rather than a spring, then a clean key frame puts the real text back in one frame. Bursts come on an interval while on screen, on pointer entry (clustered where the pointer came in), a tap, keyboard focus on the headline (a tab stop by default) or the link around it, and each change of burstKey.

props.name: children
props.description: The headline; it stays real, selectable text between bursts.

props.name: as
props.description: The root element.

props.name: intensity
props.description: How many artefacts a burst throws and how far they shift, 0 to 1.

props.name: burst
props.description: Length of one burst, ms.

props.name: split
props.description: How far apart the two colour channels drift, em.

props.name: block
props.description: The macro-block size, em.

props.name: smear
props.description: How often and how far a pixel run drags behind a slipped row, 0 to 1.

props.name: freeze
props.description: The share of corrupted blocks that hold a stale frame, 0 to 1.

props.name: fps
props.description: The codec's frame rate inside a burst, 8 to 60.

props.name: interval
props.description: Rest between automatic bursts, ms; 0 turns them off.

props.name: channels
props.description: The two channel colours, any CSS colour; tokens follow the theme.

props.name: hover
props.description: Pointer entry, a tap and keyboard focus each fire a burst.

props.name: focusable
props.description: A tab stop of its own, so the keyboard can fire a burst or, under reduced motion, clear the still frame; turn off inside a link or button, which is focused instead.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When automatic bursts run; hover and manual turn the interval off.

props.name: once
props.description: One automatic burst, then rest.

props.name: delay
props.description: Wait before the first automatic burst, ms.

props.name: burstKey
props.description: Each change fires one burst: the host's own trigger.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds every burst's corruption, so a page breaks the same way each visit.

props.name: paused
props.description: No bursts at all; one under way ends clean.

props.name: dpr
props.description: The most device pixels per CSS pixel the canvas may use, capped at 2.

props.name: onBurstStart
props.description: A burst began.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: A burst ended on a clean key frame.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; the canvas copies its font and colour.

usageNotes: Accessibility: the DOM text is always the real text, read once and selectable; the canvas is aria-hidden and ignores the pointer. The headline is a tab stop by default and focusing it plays a burst; inside a link or button, set focusable={false} and the host's focus does the same.
Reduced motion: one still corrupted frame stands in, drawn once and redrawn on resize, font load or theme change; hover or focus clears it to the clean text and leaving puts it back.

Performance: nothing runs between bursts but one timeout, and only while on screen in a visible page; a burst redraws only on codec frames, reusing six offscreen buffers capped at device pixel ratio 2 and released on unmount.
Theme changes are caught by a 1 ms colour transition on a hidden sentinel, so the canvas re-reads its ink and channel colours without reading the document; no 2D context simply means no corruption.
Keep bursts short and infrequent for reading comfort (the defaults are 0.52 s every 3.6 s), and give the host a visible control, as the demo's Corrupt button does, when a burst should be on demand.

items.title: Speed Banner
items.tagline: A marquee that answers how fast you scroll.
items.description: A marquee that answers the scroll: rows of repeated display type cruise in alternating directions, and the page's scroll velocity feeds one amount carried on springs.glide that runs the rows faster, leans each toward its own direction of travel and opens the letter spacing, the stretch anchored mid-row so the type elongates rather than slides. Scrolling up reverses every row through springs.drift, so the rows slow, stop and pull away the other way, and when scrolling stops everything eases back to the cruise. The banner is a focusable region: Space or Enter holds and releases it, Left and Right push it the way a scroll would, and Up, Down and the page keys scroll the page as usual.

props.name: text

props.name: as
props.description: The root element.

props.name: rows

props.name: speed

props.name: skew
props.description: The largest lean at full scroll speed, degrees.

props.name: stretch

props.name: boost
props.description: How many times their base speed the rows reach at full scroll speed.

props.name: sensitivity
props.description: The scroll speed that counts as full, px per second.

props.name: direction
props.description: The first row's direction; the next runs the other way.

props.name: flip
props.description: Scrolling up reverses every row.

props.name: outline
props.description: Which rows are drawn in outline.

props.name: separator
props.description: Set between items.

props.name: fade
props.description: Fade the ends of the rows.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between rows, em.

props.name: label
props.description: The region's name for assistive technology.

props.name: paused / defaultPaused
props.description: Hold the banner; the rows coast to a stop on the drift spring.

props.name: onPausedChange
props.description: Fires from the key press that held or released the banner.

props.name: onDirectionChange
props.description: Scrolling flipped the rows: 1 their own way, -1 reversed.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; type size, weight, case and tracking carry into the rows.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the banner is a focusable region; Space or Enter pauses and resumes it (announced politely), Left and Right push it backward or forward like a scroll, and the page's own scroll keys still scroll and still drive it.
Reduced motion: the rows rest at staggered offsets with no drift, lean or stretch, and scrolling leaves them still; outline and fades stay so it still reads as a banner.

Performance: one rAF loop runs only while the banner is on screen in a visible page, writing transforms and one CSS variable; when paused it stops as soon as the rows have coasted to rest. Scroll and wheel listeners are passive.
It reads the velocity of whichever scroller holds it, including the window; over a banner where nothing scrolls, the wheel stands in for a scroll.
Moving text can always be stopped: wire paused to a visible control as the demo does, and the items are read once from a hidden line while every row copy is hidden from assistive technology.

items.title: Breath Type
items.tagline: Letters inhale toward your cursor.
items.description: A word that breathes toward the pointer: letters within the radius open their tracking and grow along the inherited font's width, weight or optical size, while letters further away compress, and the line's width is conserved, so the space the near letters take is given up by the far ones and the word draws breath toward the cursor. The breath fills on springs.glide and empties on the slower springs.drift, its point trails the pointer on a critically damped spring, and on its trigger one breath passes along the line. Mouse hovers, touch presses and drags, and the keyboard breathes in at the middle on focus, walks the breath with Left and Right, jumps with Home and End and lets it go with Escape.

props.name: children
props.description: The text; it is read once and stays copyable.

props.name: as
props.description: The root element.

props.name: radius
props.description: How far the breath reaches from its point, em.

props.name: falloff
props.description: The curve from the breath point out to the radius.

props.name: axis
props.description: What breathes besides the tracking; the font's own axis when it has one, a transform or stroke when not.

props.name: depth
props.description: How deep the breath is, 0 to 1.

props.name: spread
props.description: Extra tracking at the breath point, em.

props.name: lag
props.description: How far the breath trails the pointer, 0 (none) to 1.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the intro breath plays; hover means never, manual means on breathKey.

props.name: once
props.description: Play the intro breath only the first time it is seen; otherwise again each time it comes back into view.

props.name: delay
props.description: Wait before the intro breath, ms.

props.name: duration
props.description: Length of the intro breath, ms.

props.name: breathKey
props.description: Each change plays the intro breath: the host's own trigger.

props.name: breathing
props.description: A slow resting breath while on screen and untouched.

props.name: focusable
props.description: A tab stop with a keyboard path: arrows move the breath, Escape lets it go.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Ignore the pointer and the keys.

props.name: onBreathChange
props.description: The letter at the breath point changed (grapheme index); null once exhaled.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: The intro breath finished.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; the letters inherit its font, size and weight.

usageNotes: Keyboard: focusing the text breathes in at its middle; Left and Right walk the breath a letter at a time (mirrored in right-to-left text), Home and End jump to the ends, and Escape lets it go. Touch presses and drags along the line while vertical scrolling still works.
Reduced motion: no intro or resting breath and nothing travels or scales; the pointer and keys still change the font's own axis (or ink weight when it has none) on a short tween.

Variable fonts: the axes and their ranges are read from the inherited font's faces, so a self-hosted variable family whose faces declare weight or width ranges is used as is; a static font falls back to transforms and stroke.
Layout never shifts: every letter keeps its rest width and the tracking is laid out as transforms whose sum is zero on each line, so the line's ends hold still.
Performance: letter positions are measured on resize and font load only, and each frame of a moving breath is one pass over preallocated buffers; when the breath settles nothing runs.

items.title: Tally Roll
items.tagline: Numbers that roll up like a meter.
items.description: A count-up figure built from mechanical digit wheels in little housings: every wheel runs its own ease-in-out drive and is coupled to it by a detent spring whose stiffness is a prop (damping ratio 0.62), so it lags a touch as it spins up and rocks into its detent as it lands; lower places spin extra turns and land first, and each higher place lands a stagger later, like carries arriving up a meter. The figure is laid out from Intl's own parts (number, currency, percent, or a hand-built compact form that server and browser agree on), a change mid-roll bends every wheel to the new figure without a jump, and fast wheels blur while leading zeros stay dim. The tally is a button: a press or Enter or Space spins the wheels forward to zero, as a tally's reset knob does, and counts again.

props.name: value
props.description: The figure the wheels roll to; a change mid-roll bends the roll.

props.name: from
props.description: Where the first roll starts.

props.name: format
props.description: How the figure is written; compact is built by hand so server and browser agree.

props.name: decimals
props.description: Fraction digits: 0 for number and currency, 1 for percent and compact.

props.name: currency
props.description: The ISO currency for the currency format.

props.name: locale
props.description: The formatting locale; digits are always Latin so they fit the wheels.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Fixed text before the figure.

props.name: suffix
props.description: Fixed text after the figure.

props.name: duration
props.description: Until the highest place lands, ms.

props.name: stiffness
props.description: The detent spring each wheel is coupled to its drive by: low rocks, high clicks dead.

props.name: stagger
props.description: Each higher place lands this much after the one below it, ms.

props.name: revolutions
props.description: The most extra turns a lower wheel makes on a long roll.

props.name: housing

props.name: dimZeros
props.description: Dim the leading zero wheels, so 01,248 reads as 1,248.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the first roll runs; manual shows the figure and only rolls on change or press.

props.name: once
props.description: Roll only the first time it is seen; otherwise it counts again from `from` each time it comes back into view.

props.name: delay
props.description: Wait before the first roll, ms.

props.name: replayOnPress
props.description: The tally is a button: pressing resets the wheels and counts again.

props.name: sound
props.description: Ticks as faces pass and as each wheel lands, only for rolls the visitor caused.

props.name: as
props.description: The root element.

props.name: onRollStart
props.description: A roll began.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Every wheel has landed.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; the wheels inherit its size, weight and colour.

usageNotes: Accessibility: the formatted figure (with prefix and suffix) is read once and copies as plain text; as a button it is named by the figure and described as counting again on Enter or Space, and a changed figure is announced politely once it has landed.
Reduced motion: the wheels change to their faces at once under a short cross-fade, with no spin, blur or rock; the figure is always right.
Performance: one rAF loop runs only while a wheel is moving and stops the moment every wheel has settled exactly on its detent; off screen or in a hidden tab a roll lands at once.
Server and client render the same wheels: formatting is Intl with Latin digits and a hand-built compact form, and the wheels start on `from` so a count-up never flashes the final figure first.
Sound only answers the visitor: a press, or a value change that follows the visitor's own action (transient user activation); a roll that starts because the tally scrolled into view is silent.

items.title: Glass Orb
items.tagline: A crystal sphere that holds its own weather.
items.description: A glass sphere on a table that holds its own weather, drawn in one WebGL2 pass: each pixel follows the view ray in through the front of the ball and out of the back, so the room behind comes back inverted and magnified, tinted where the glass is thick, with a window highlight, a caustic rim and a focused caustic in its shadow. Dragged, the orb follows the hand 1:1 along the table and off it; released, it rolls home on a spring between springs.glide and springs.recoil that takes the throw's velocity, and a lifted orb falls under gravity and lands with a small bounce, while the mist or snow inside is dragged after the glass and thrown up by the landing. Left and Right roll it, Up lifts and drops it, and Enter or Space shakes it.

props.name: weather
props.description: What is inside the glass: nothing, a drifting mist, snow, or a dark storm with rain.

props.name: refraction
props.description: How hard the glass bends light, 0 to 1: a clear bubble at 0, a solid crystal that shows the room upside down at 1.

props.name: tint
props.description: How deeply the glass is coloured by glassColor, 0 to 1; the thick middle colours more than the rim.

props.name: glassColor
props.description: The colour of the glass, any CSS colour, resolved on the element so it follows the theme.

props.name: weatherColor
props.description: The colour of the snow and mist; a pigment, so it reads the same in both themes.

props.name: backdropText
props.description: A word set large on the wall behind the orb; the glass shows it flipped and magnified.

props.name: size
props.description: The orb's diameter as a share of the box height, 0.4 to 0.9, never more than 72% of the width.

props.name: swirl
props.description: How strongly rolling, lifting and landing stir the weather, 0 to 1.

props.name: wobble
props.description: How much the orb rocks as it rolls home, from a glide at 0 to two visible rocks at 1.

props.name: drift
props.description: The slow circulation of the weather while nobody touches it, 0 to 1; 0 lets everything settle and the loop stop.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Drag, tap and keys move the orb.

props.name: alt
props.description: Describes the scene for assistive technology.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seed for the weather's arrangement and the mist's grain.

props.name: dpr
props.description: The highest device pixel ratio the canvas draws at (never above 2).

props.name: paused
props.description: Freeze the weather where it is.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a swish when the visitor rolls, lifts or shakes the orb.

props.name: onStir
props.description: Fires when the visitor moves the orb: a drag, a tap or a key.

props.name: onSettle
props.description: Fires when, after a stir, the orb is home and the weather has calmed.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the scene box; set its height here (default h-56).

usageNotes: The orb is a real round button that moves with the drawn ball: Left and Right roll it, Up lifts and drops it, Enter or Space shakes it, and its focus ring is the orb's own outline. The scene is a group labelled by alt; the canvas is aria-hidden.

One WebGL2 context and one draw per frame. The loop runs only while something moves (or, for mist and storm with drift above 0, at a rationed 30 fps), never off screen or in a hidden tab; snow stops it once the last flake has landed. The backing store caps its device pixel ratio at 2.
The room is painted from tokens on the component's own element and repainted when the theme changes; without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still life of the same room and orb stands in.
Under reduced motion nothing travels: the weather is a still, settled arrangement, and a key or a tap shows a new one.
Give the box a height with className; the orb's size follows the height and never takes more than 72% of the width, so it fits a 258px phone plate.

items.title: Live Wire Mark
items.tagline: Current crawls around your logo.
items.description: An electric outline for any SVG mark: the path is rendered as a faint wire and sampled into canvas points, and arcs of current crawl it both ways as jagged, tapering polylines re-kinked about thirty times a second, throwing forks that flicker and die over a glow that breathes underneath. Hover or keyboard focus charges it on springs.drift — more arcs, hotter, and sparks crackling off the corners past 0.6 — and a press discharges it in one flash on an exit tween, after which the charge climbs back on springs.drift from the point nearest the press. Enter or Space discharges it from the keyboard.

props.name: path
props.description: The mark as SVG path data in viewBox units; any number of subpaths, with corners and open ends found for you.

props.name: viewBox
props.description: The viewBox the path is drawn in.

props.name: voltage
props.description: How hot the current runs, 0 to 1: the arcs' reach, speed and brightness.

props.name: arcs
props.description: How many arcs crawl the outline at rest; hover and focus add more.

props.name: glow
