usageNotes: Only the field lives in the tube: children render in front of it as ordinary DOM, crisp and fully interactive. The tube itself is aria-hidden and never a focus stop or a click target.
Keyboard: a control inside that gains keyboard focus leans the curve toward itself and degausses softly; blur lets the tube settle back to centre.
Reduced motion: a still picture, centred, with scanlines, grille, a steady bloom and the reflection; no roll, breath, lean, warm-up or degauss.

Cost: the colour field renders at half resolution and the tube pass adds the fine detail at full resolution; nothing runs off screen, in a hidden tab, or when paused and settled. DPR capped at dpr. Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still of the field with scanlines and a rim stands in.
Theming: the named palettes are pigments at fixed lightness, because a lit tube looks the same by day or night; the bezel and rim are the page's own background, so the tube sits in either theme.

items.title: Forge Flow
items.tagline: Molten metal moving under a cooling crust.
items.description: A background of molten metal moving under a cooling crust: a heat field carried along a swirling flow and coloured from ember red through molten orange to white heat, and wherever it cools a crust of dark plates closes over it, cracked along borders that glow with the heat beneath and re-heal as the metal moves, the glow breathing in patches. The hand is heat — the spot follows on springs.glide and warms on springs.drift, opening the crust into a bright pool and leaving a trail that crusts over behind it — and a press stokes it, the pool heaving open on springs.recoil; the first time it is seen the surface is poured molten, every current running hot, and cools into its crust on springs.drift. Keyboard focus on content inside it brings the heat to the focused element.

props.name: paused

There is no tab stop of its own: when a child receives keyboard focus the heat glides to that element, as a hovering hand would. On touch a tap heats the spot for a moment and page scrolling is never taken.

One WebGL2 fragment pass that renders only while on screen, in a visible page and moving; paused or reduced it draws on change only. The backing store is capped at dpr (and softened past about 1.4 million pixels) and follows ResizeObserver.
A lost context or a browser without WebGL2 shows a static gradient in the same colours; a restored context repaints. Everything is disposed on unmount.

Colours are read from the component's own element and re-read when the theme or the colors prop changes. Under reduced motion it is a still frame with the crust set, and the hand's heat appears at once with no spring or trail.

items.title: Dune Gradient
items.tagline: Colour laid in drifting dunes.
items.description: A background of colour laid in drifting dunes: soft-edged bands stacked from the horizon down, each a leaning ridge with a steep lee face and a long windward slope, lit from a low sun with a fine highlight on every crest and a little sand grain over everything; far bands dissolve into the page colour and each travels at its own pace while its shape slowly changes. The hand leans the landscape by depth on springs.drift, a press sends a gust whose front brightens the crests as it runs outward and lifts wisps of sand off the lee faces, and the first time it is seen the dunes are laid back to front on springs.glide in a cascade. Keyboard focus on content inside it leans the dunes toward the focused element.

There is no tab stop of its own: when a child receives keyboard focus the dunes lean toward it, as they do toward a hovering hand. On touch a tap sends a gust and scrolling stays with the page.

One WebGL2 fragment pass that renders only while on screen, in a visible page and moving; with drift at 0 or paused it draws on change only. Lengths are in CSS px, so a dune is the same size at any DPR; the backing store is capped at dpr and follows ResizeObserver.

Layer colours are mixed in oklab from the palette and haze, read from the component's own element and re-read when the theme or palette changes, so the far dunes dissolve into the page in light and dark alike.
A lost context or a browser without WebGL2 shows the same bands as a static gradient. Under reduced motion the landscape stands still with no lean, and a gust is a haze along the crests that fades.

items.title: Dew Web
items.tagline: Silk threads strung with glints of dew.
items.description: A background of an orb-weaver's web at first light: radials from a hub to a frame moored off the edges, a capture spiral drooping between them under its own weight, and dew beaded on the silk; a light travels slowly round, droplets whose facets face it flash into small stars and silk lying across it carries a sheen, so bright arcs sweep the web while the anchors sway. Every crossing is a mass on springs tied to its neighbours, so a moving hand brushes the silk into a travelling tremble and a press plucks the nearest thread, which rings through the web — under-damped like the recoil spring, as long as ring asks — and settles; the first time it is seen the capture spiral is spun onto the standing scaffold ring by ring and the dew beads in. Keyboard focus arriving on content inside it gives the web a gentle pluck beside the focused element.

props.description: Picks the web: the same seed spins the same web with the same dew.

props.name: paused
props.description: Holds the sway and the light still; the hand still disturbs the silk.

props.name: intro
props.description: Spin the capture spiral onto the web, then bead the dew, the first time it is seen.

props.name: dpr
props.description: The highest device pixel ratio the web is drawn at, never above 2.

props.name: onPluck
props.description: Fires when the web is plucked: by a press, or by keyboard focus arriving inside it.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Classes for the content layer above the web.

usageNotes: The painted layer is aria-hidden and pointer-events-none; children render above it untouched, and a press on a button or link inside never plucks the web.
There is no tab stop of its own: keyboard focus arriving on a child gives the web a gentle pluck beside it. On touch a tap plucks, and page scrolling stays with the page.

Canvas 2D over a CSS mist the server renders too. The loop runs only on screen and in a visible page: full rate while the silk trembles, half rate for the slow sway and light, and not at all once paused and still. Node arrays are allocated when the web is spun, never per frame; DPR is capped at dpr.
Silk, glint and page colours are read from the component's own element and re-read when the theme changes; on a light page each glint carries a faint silk shadow so the light still reads.
Under reduced motion the web is a still frame with the light fixed so a handful of drops glint; a press brightens the dew near the hand for a moment instead of shaking it.

items.title: Survey Contours
items.tagline: A landscape drawn in contour lines.
items.description: A background that is a living topographic sheet: contour lines traced from a slowly breathing height field, every fifth an index contour drawn heavier with its elevation printed small along it and the line broken under the figures, spot heights on the highest summits, over a faint tint that leans toward the high ground. The hand raises a hill — the land under it rises on springs.drift, new rings bloom round it in the hill colour and a spot height rides the summit with its figure rolling as it climbs — and a press heaves it higher on springs.recoil, the rings rippling out and back with each bounce; the lowlands stand from the first frame and, the first time it is seen, the rest of the survey inks in from lower to higher in a cascade. Keyboard focus on content inside the sheet raises the hill under the focused element.

props.name: children
props.description: The content above the sheet: a hero, a heading, a call to action.

props.name: interval
props.description: The height between one contour line and the next, in the sheet's units.

props.name: weight
props.description: How heavy the lines are drawn, 0.5 to 2; every fifth line is heavier still.

props.name: labels

props.name: relief
props.description: How far the land rises from its lowest point to its highest, in the sheet's units.

props.name: scale

props.name: breathe

props.name: speed

props.name: tint

props.name: lineColor
props.description: The contour lines' colour, as a CSS colour.

props.name: hillColor
props.description: The colour the lines take round the raised hill, as a CSS colour.

props.name: tintColor
props.description: The colour the high ground leans toward, as a CSS colour.

props.name: unit
props.description: The unit printed after the spot height.

props.name: interactive

props.name: pointerStrength

props.name: radius
props.description: The width of the raised hill, in CSS px.

props.name: seed

props.name: paused

props.name: intro
props.description: Ink the higher contours in, lower to higher, the first time the sheet is seen; the lowlands are drawn from the start.

props.name: dpr
props.description: The highest device pixel ratio the lines are drawn at, never above 2.

props.name: onSummitChange
props.description: Reports the raised hill's summit once it settles, and null once it has subsided.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

props.name: contentClassName

usageNotes: The painted layers are aria-hidden and pointer-events-none, labels included (they are paint, not text); children render above them untouched, and a press on a button inside never heaves the hill.

There is no tab stop of its own: when a child receives keyboard focus the hill rises under it, as it does under a hovering hand. On touch a press raises and heaves the hill under the finger; page scrolling stays with the page.

Three height fields are surveyed once per size, seed and scale, then blended each frame, so the land breathes with no noise per frame; marching squares visit only the levels each cell spans, and the grid cell grows with the box so the cost stays bounded. The loop runs only on screen, in a visible page, and while the land breathes or the hill moves.

Colours and the label font are read from the component's own element, re-read when the theme changes and when web fonts arrive. onSummitChange reports a settled summit once, not every frame, so it can drive a live region.
Under reduced motion the sheet is still, the survey is drawn at once, and the hill stands under the hand immediately with its spot height.

items.title: Light Corridor
items.tagline: An endless corridor of soft light.
items.description: A background that is an endless corridor of rounded frames of soft light receding to a vanishing point: the frames glide toward you and fade as they pass, each a fine bright line inside a wide glow, mirrored in the floor with a reflection that fades from its own contact and joined to the next by faint rails, with a pool of light where the corridor ends. The vanishing point follows the hand on springs.drift, so the corridor turns to look where you point, and a held press rushes it — the speed swelling on springs.drift to three and a half times with faint light trails — while the first time it is seen the lights come on from near to far in a cascade, each with a small flash. Keyboard focus on content inside it turns the corridor toward the focused element.

props.name: speed

props.name: spacing

props.name: backdrop

props.name: glow

props.name: onIntroEnd
props.description: Fires when the last light is on — at once when there is no intro (intro off, reduced motion).

props.name: onRushChange
props.description: Fires when a held press starts the rush (true) and when it lets go (false).

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

props.name: contentClassName

usageNotes: The painted layer is aria-hidden and pointer-events-none; children render above it untouched, and pressing a button or link inside never starts a rush.

There is no tab stop of its own: when a child receives keyboard focus the corridor turns toward it, as it does toward a hovering hand. On touch a held press rushes and turns toward the finger; page scrolling stays with the page.

Canvas 2D with a few strokes and one gradient per frame and no per-frame paths; the loop runs only on screen, in a visible page, and while the frames travel or a spring settles. The server renders a still corridor of CSS frames that the canvas fades in over.

Light is added on dark backdrops so overlapping glows build, and laid normally on light ones; colours are read from the component's own element and re-read when the theme or color changes. Use vanish to keep the far end clear of your headline.
Under reduced motion the corridor is a still frame, there is no rush or light-up, and the vanishing point stands where the hand puts it at once.

items.title: Sliced Horizon
items.tagline: A sunset cut into sliding bands.
items.description: A background that is a sunset poster cut into horizontal strips: a sky running into a warm glow, a sun standing on the horizon and cut by it, and a sea with a path of glitter, painted once and drawn strip by strip, each slid sideways by a wave running down the stack so the sun breaks into offset bars. Moving the hand riffles the strips near it on the springs.snap constants; when the hand rests the strips pull into register one after another, radiating from its strip in a cascade, each on springs.snap with one crisp overshoot through alignment, and moving again lets the wave back in on springs.drift. The poster first arrives in register, as the server drew it, and breaks loose from the top; keyboard focus on content inside it brings the strips into register.

props.name: children

props.name: slices
props.description: How many horizontal strips the scene is cut into, 6 to 28.

props.name: offset
props.description: How far the strips slide sideways, 0 (in register) to 1.

props.name: palette

props.name: gap
props.description: The cut between strips, in CSS px.

props.name: horizon

props.name: sun
props.description: How large the sun is, 0 to 1.

props.name: sunX
props.description: Where the sun stands across the scene, as a fraction of the width.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the wave runs down the strips, 0 to 2; 0 holds them still.

props.name: waves

props.name: banded
props.description: Print each strip's sky as one flat colour, like screen-printed bands.

props.name: restDelay
props.description: How long a resting pointer waits before the strips pull into register, in ms.

props.name: interactive

props.name: pointerStrength
props.description: How hard a moving hand shoves the strips near it, 0 to 1.

props.name: seed
props.description: Picks the glitter on the sea: the same seed lays the same light.

props.name: paused
props.description: Holds the wave still; the hand still riffles and aligns the strips.

props.name: intro
props.description: Show the poster in register first, then let the strips break loose from the top, the first time it is seen.

props.name: dpr
props.description: The highest device pixel ratio the poster is drawn at, never above 2.

props.name: onAlignChange
props.description: Fires when the strips come into register (true), from a resting hand or keyboard focus, and when they start to drift again (false).

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Classes for the content layer above the poster.

usageNotes: The painted layer is aria-hidden and pointer-events-none; children render above it untouched and keep every click.

There is no tab stop of its own: when a child receives keyboard focus the strips come into register, the same end state as a resting hand, and drift again when focus leaves. On touch a tap brings them into register for a moment; page scrolling stays with the page.

The scene is painted once per size, palette and theme into a cached canvas wider than the box, so a frame is one image draw per strip with edges snapped to device pixels. The loop runs only on screen, in a visible page, and while the wave runs or a strip moves; in register and settled it stops.

Presets lean their deepest colours into the page colour so the poster sits in either theme; colours are read from the component's own element and re-read when the theme or palette changes. The server renders the poster in register, so the first paint matches it.
Under reduced motion the poster is still with its sun broken at a designed phase; resting or focus aligns it at once and moving breaks it again, with no riffle and no intro.

items.title: Pulse Tiles
items.tagline: A grid of tiles keeping time.
items.description: A background grid of rounded tiles lit by a beat: four beats to a bar at the tempo you set, and on the beats the grid plays diagonal waves, rings, a checkerboard answering itself and a curled spiral arm, each wave carrying the next palette colour. A struck tile flares, eases its colour into the wave's, swells inside its gap on the springs.recoil constants so the grid visibly taps in time, blooms into the gaps and fades; a press sends a ripple of the next colour out from that tile, and keyboard focus on a control inside parks the highlight there and sends a softer one.

props.name: children
props.description: The content on top of the tiles: a hero line, a heading, a call to action.

props.name: tile

props.name: gap

props.name: radius
props.description: A tile's corner radius, px.

props.name: tempo
props.description: Beats per minute, 30 to 200; four beats make a bar.

props.name: palette
props.description: A named palette, or 2 to 6 CSS colours of your own; each wave carries the next.

props.name: patterns
props.description: The patterns the grid plays, in turn.

props.name: bars
props.description: How many bars each pattern plays before the next one takes over.

props.name: decay
props.description: How long a struck tile takes to fade back to rest, ms.

props.name: glow
props.description: How far lit tiles bloom into the gaps around them, 0 to 1.

props.name: pop
props.description: How much a struck tile swells inside its gap, 0 to 1.

props.name: interactive
props.description: A hovering pointer lifts the tile under it and a press sends a ripple.

props.name: pointerStrength
props.description: How far and how brightly a ripple from a press travels, 0 to 1.

props.name: paused
props.description: Stop the beat: lit tiles fade and the grid rests until it is touched.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds where each pattern starts, which way it runs and the colour order.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onPatternChange
props.description: Fires with the pattern now playing: once when the beat starts, then at every change.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the box.

usageNotes: The tiles are decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with their focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never ripple.
Keyboard: when a control inside takes keyboard focus the highlight parks on it and a soft ripple leaves from it; blur releases it. The background adds no tab stop of its own.

Under reduced motion the grid holds a still chord of colour (the first pattern frozen mid-wave) with no beat and no swell; hover lights a tile at once and a press lights every tile in reach together, then lets them fade.

One WebGL2 draw a frame from a small per-tile texture. The beat runs only while the grid is on screen in a visible page; paused, it fades out and stops until touched. The canvas caps its device pixel ratio at 2 and resizes with its box.
Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still frame of the grid stands in; the palette resolves on the element itself and is re-read when the theme changes, so it reads in light and dark.

items.title: Scan Bed
items.tagline: A beam reads the surface line by line.
items.description: A background that is a scanner bed seen at a low angle: a dark surface ruled with a perspective grid and an object lying on it — a pebble, wind ridges or a crater — sampled as a point cloud you cannot see until it is read. A sheet of light sweeps across the bed line by line; every point it meets flares white-hot, cools and fades over the afterglow, so the read line bows up over every rise and the relief hangs behind it for a moment. The pointer tilts the bed on the springs.glide constants and a press restarts the pass from that row with a flare on the springs.flick constants; keyboard focus on a control inside does the same from that control.

props.name: density

props.name: interactive

props.name: paused

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the subject's shape and the sampling jitter.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onActiveChange

props.name: className

usageNotes: The bed is decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never restart the pass.
Keyboard: a control inside taking keyboard focus tilts the bed toward it and restarts the pass from its row; blur lets the bed settle. No tab stop of its own.

The bed stays dark in both themes (the page mixed toward black), so put light-on-dark or a panel over it; the beam and point colours are pigments that read the same either way, and they are re-read when the theme changes.
Under reduced motion the whole reconstruction stands still with the beam parked across it; the pointer's tilt is applied exactly on each move with no easing, and presses do nothing.
Canvas 2D with a few batched fills a frame and no allocation per frame; it runs only on screen in a visible page, caps its device pixel ratio at 2 and re-samples the subject when its box resizes.

items.title: Iron Sand
items.tagline: Grains that line up along an unseen field.
items.description: A background of iron sand on a plate with magnets hidden under it: the grains are laid along the field and each is a short needle on its own angular spring that turns to the field wherever it is strong enough to beat friction, so the sand lines up in flowing lines between the poles and stands up into small tufts of spikes at each one while the magnets wander slowly. The pointer carries a pole (position on the springs.glide constants, presence on springs.drift) and the sand streams after it; a press taps the plate, so every grain hops, lets go of friction and snaps to the field on the springs.recoil constants. Keyboard focus on a control inside carries the pole there and taps from it.

props.name: pointerStrength

Keyboard: a control inside taking keyboard focus carries the pole to it and taps the plate from there; blur lifts the pole. The background adds no tab stop.
Under reduced motion every grain lies at home with its needle laid along the field and the magnets hold still; the carried pole turns the needles around it at once and nothing slides.

Canvas 2D in five batched strokes over a plate drawn once per size and theme. It runs only on screen in a visible page, at thirty frames a second while the magnets merely wander, and stops entirely once the sand is still when drift is 0 or paused.

Colours resolve on the element itself and are re-read when the theme changes: graphite follows your ink (dark grains on a light page, silver on a dark one); rust and cobalt are pigments that read the same in both.

items.title: Glow Rain
items.tagline: Soft streaks of light falling slowly.
items.description: A background of soft light falling slowly: each streak sits at its own depth, far ones thin, dim and slow, near ones longer, wider and blurred as if out of focus, each a bright head with a body fading into a faint trail, and now and then a brighter one. The rain leans with the wind, near streaks more than far, and the pointer sets the wind while a quick sweep adds a gust, all through one spring with the springs.drift constants so it swings in and settles without a bounce. A press drops a bright streak that lands where you touched; keyboard focus on a control inside leans the rain toward it and drops one above it.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast it falls, 0.1 to 3.

props.name: color
props.description: The light's colour: a named one, or any CSS colour.

props.name: length
props.description: A far streak's length, px; near ones are longer.

props.name: trail
props.description: How long the faint trail behind each streak runs, 0 to 1.

props.name: flare

props.name: wind

props.name: onActiveChange

Keyboard: a control inside taking keyboard focus leans the rain toward it and drops a bright streak above it; blur lets the wind return. No tab stop of its own.

In a dark theme the light adds to the sky; in a light theme each streak is drawn as soft pigment of the same hue, so it reads on a pale page. Colours resolve on the element itself and are re-read when the theme changes.
Under reduced motion it is a long exposure: the streaks stand still with longer trails at the resting lean, and nothing falls or leans.

Canvas 2D: one sky blit and one sprite blit per streak a frame, sprites built once per size and look, no allocation per frame. It runs only on screen in a visible page, caps its device pixel ratio at 2 and keeps the same density per area when the box resizes.

items.title: Aether Swirl
items.tagline: Colour folded through itself, slowly.
items.description: A background of colour folded through itself like ink suspended in oil: a WebGL2 shader warps noise by noise by noise and draws four palette colours out into banded swirls that follow the folds, with hair-fine filaments where the bands meet and a soft sheen across their slopes, drifting and re-folding over tens of seconds. The folds deepen under the pointer, its place following on the springs.glide constants and its presence arriving on springs.drift, and a press winds the colour round the hand through a critically damped twist spring with the drift constants; keyboard focus on a control inside brings the hand there with a softer fold.

props.name: speed

props.name: palette

props.name: scale

props.name: detail
props.description: How much fine structure the folds carry, 0 to 1.

props.name: veins

props.name: sheen
props.description: Light on the surface, like oil, 0 to 1.

props.name: grain

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and keyboard focus deepen the folds, and a press winds the colour round.

props.name: pointerStrength

props.name: radius
props.description: How far the hand reaches, px.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the colour still; the hand still folds it.

props.name: seed

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires when the pointer or keyboard focus starts (true) or stops (false) folding the colour.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the box.

usageNotes: The swirl is decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never fold the colour.
Keyboard: a control inside taking keyboard focus brings the hand to it and gives a soft fold; blur releases it. No tab stop of its own.

Palette colours are pigments mixed 14% into the page, resolved on the element and re-read when the theme changes, so the swirl sits a shade lighter on a light page and deeper on a dark one. Put a panel or strong type over it.
Under reduced motion one still frame is drawn; the hand's deepening lands exactly where the pointer is on each move, and presses do not fold.

One fullscreen draw at two thirds of the capped device pixel ratio, scaled up by the browser; thirty frames a second while it only drifts, every frame while the hand works, nothing off screen or in a hidden page. Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still frame of the palette stands in.

items.title: Prism Spill
items.tagline: White light breaks into its colours.
items.description: A background in which a glass prism, drawn in light strokes, splits a beam of white light into its colours: the beam is traced through the prism each frame for seven wavelengths (Snell's law in, a Cauchy index whose dispersion is the spread, one internal reflection allowed, Snell's law out) and the escaping colours fan out as spectral bands that soften and diffuse into a wash across the surface. The prism sways slowly about its angle of least deviation and the fan swings with it the way a real one does; the pointer turns the prism on the springs.drift constants, heavy and without overshoot, a press sends a pulse of light down the beam and out through the spectrum, and keyboard focus on a control inside turns the prism toward it and pulses.

In a dark theme the light adds to the surface; in a light theme the bands are laid as soft pigment and the beam as a pale warm line, so both read. Colours resolve on the element and are re-read when the theme changes.

items.title: Night Veil
items.tagline: A dark veil that moves like breath.
items.description: A quiet hero background: a near-black ground with a faint coloured undertone and two to four layers of soft noise veil drifting at their own scales and headings, closed by a soft vignette, breathing slowly so a headline sits on something alive; on a light page the same recipe is a pale mist. The pointer lifts a gentle light under the veil, its place following on springs.glide and its presence arriving on springs.drift, and a press draws a deep breath in on the glide spring and out on drift that parts the veil around the hand; keyboard focus on a control inside is the hand there, with a softer breath.

The pillar leans toward the pointer, planted at the floor and bending more the higher it climbs, on springs.drift, and a press sends a surge up it through a critically damped drift-spring impulse that brightens the column, hurries the motes and rings out across the floor on the enter easing; keyboard focus on a control inside is the hand there, with a half surge.

items.title: Drape Silk
items.tagline: Silk that settles into soft folds.
items.description: A background of silk filling the box: long hanging folds that meander, fan out as they fall and drift slowly, raked by a soft key light with an anisotropic shine stretched along the threads, so the sheen slides along the folds as they move, and a fine plain weave breaking it where the screen can hold it. The hand lifts the cloth, its place following on springs.glide and its presence on springs.drift; a press takes it up higher and on release it drops on springs.recoil with two small bounces, a ripple runs out from where it fell and the folds shift into a new arrangement on drift. Keyboard focus on a control inside takes the cloth up gently there, and focus leaving lets it fall the same way.

items.title: Drift Lines
items.tagline: Thin lines floating at different depths.
items.description: A Canvas 2D background of long thin lines floating across the frame at different depths: each a gentle seeded curve drifting sideways at a pace set by its depth and bobbing on its own long period, so neighbours now and then cross, with near lines thicker, softer and lower in contrast and far ones hair-thin and crisp. The pointer shifts the parallax by depth on springs.glide, and a press racks focus to the depth of the line nearest the pointer on the glide spring, sharpening that plane and softening the rest, before it drifts back to rest on springs.drift; keyboard focus on a control inside racks focus to the line nearest it.

items.title: Window Shafts
items.tagline: Afternoon light through a tall window.

The pointer moves the sun, turning its angle and changing the patch's length on springs.drift, and a press stirs the dust into a swirl through a critically damped drift-spring impulse; keyboard focus on a control inside moves the sun toward it with a softer stir.

items.title: Crown Rays

items.title: Pixel Bloom
items.tagline: Pixels that burst open where you touch.
items.description: A background of square pixels that bloom: a ring leaves the point you press at 300 px/s and every pixel it reaches turns over about the axis facing it, onto its colour on the springs.recoil constants and on home on springs.glide after a short hold, so each pixel spins once through its colour and the bloom travels out as a ragged ring with the field closing behind it (a long hold lets the pixels land, two small bounces on their stops, and fills the bloom in). Past the reach the ring only knocks pixels on springs.snap, so the bloom fades into the field. A resting pointer blooms where it rests, the pixel under a hovering pointer warms toward the colour, soft blooms open on their own every few seconds, and keyboard focus on a control inside blooms from that control.

items.title: Color Fold
items.tagline: Bands of colour bending around each other.
items.description: A background of ribbons of paint folded round one another: each ribbon's centreline bends in two slow travelling waves, the ribbons overlap and plait over and under each other, and each one turns over along its length — pinching to a crease where it is edge-on and showing its darker back where it has turned — with a soft shadow on whatever lies beneath it. The pointer is a hand in the paint: the ribbons part around it, its place following on springs.glide and its presence arriving on springs.drift, and a press throws a fold, a ring that leaves the press and turns every ribbon right over as it passes; keyboard focus on a control inside parts the ribbons there and throws a softer fold.

props.name: twist
props.description: How far the ribbons turn over along their length, 0 (flat) to 1 (turning right over).

props.name: angle
props.description: The tilt of the whole stack, degrees, −30 to 30.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the bends travel, 0 (still) to 2.

props.name: shadow
props.description: How dark a ribbon's shadow falls on the ones beneath it, 0 to 1.

props.name: sheen
props.description: A soft light along the flat of each ribbon, 0 to 1.

props.name: grain
props.description: A whisper of grain that also hides banding, 0 to 1.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and keyboard focus part the ribbons, and a press throws a fold along them.

props.name: pointerStrength
props.description: How far the hand parts the ribbons and how hard a press folds them, 0 to 1.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the ribbons still; the hand still parts and folds them.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds every bend, twist and weave, so two folds never match.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires when the pointer or keyboard focus starts (true) or stops (false) parting the ribbons.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the box.

usageNotes: The ribbons are decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with their focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never fold.
Keyboard: when a control inside takes keyboard focus the ribbons part around it and a softer fold leaves from it; blur lets go. The background adds no tab stop of its own.
Under reduced motion one composed moment is held still — the ribbons bent and plaited, with no drift and no folds — and the hand parts them exactly where it is, with no easing travel.

One WebGL2 pass. It draws thirty frames a second while it only drifts and every frame while the hand or a fold works; paused or at speed 0 it stops once they settle, and nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page. The canvas caps its pixel ratio at 2 and resizes with its box.

Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still frame of the palette stands in; the named palettes are pigments at a fixed lightness, and every colour resolves on the element and is re-read when the theme changes.

items.title: Iris Watch
items.tagline: A vast iris that follows your every move.
items.description: A background that is one enormous iris seen close up — fibrous strands from the pupil to a darkening limbus, a warmer burst inside a zig-zag collarette, dark crypts, a deep pupil and a window of light on the cornea — that watches: the eye turns toward the pointer on a heavy, critically damped spring with the springs.drift ratio (its stiffness set by tracking), the iris sliding and foreshortening as the ball turns. The pupil breathes and narrows as the pointer comes near, a press flashes it small on a stiff spring before it opens again as the flash fades, it blinks now and then and glances about when nobody is near; keyboard focus on a control inside draws its gaze to that control.

props.name: pointerStrength

usageNotes: The eye is decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with their focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never flash it.
Keyboard: when a control inside takes keyboard focus the eye turns to look at it — the state a pointer over the control reaches; blur lets it wander again. The background adds no tab stop of its own.

Under reduced motion the eye holds still at its resting dilation — no breathing, blinking, wandering or flash — and glances to a pointer that has rested for a quarter of a second in one instant step, with no travel; focus glances at once.

One WebGL2 pass. Thirty frames a second while it only breathes, every frame while the gaze, a flash or a blink travels; with breathing at 0 or paused it stops between glances and blinks, waking on a timer. Nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page, and the canvas caps its pixel ratio at 2.

Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still eye stands in. The iris colours are pigments at a fixed lightness, the page around it is the theme's own background, and both are re-read when the theme changes.

items.title: Harp Strings
items.tagline: Lines that ring when you pluck them.
items.description: A background of horizontal strings that ring: each is a real fixed–fixed string solved by up to eight standing-wave modes, each turning at its own frequency and fading at its own rate, so a pluck is exact superposition and dies away the way a string does, treble strings shivering faster than bass ones and brightening toward their colour as they ring. A passing pointer catches the nearest string, bends it 1:1 round the hand and lets it go when the hand pushes through, so a slow pass drags each string before it twangs and a fast strum sweeps every one it crosses; a press grabs a string, the drag pulls it 1:1 with rubber-banding and the release plucks it with the hand's speed, and keyboard focus on a control inside strums the strings behind it.

usageNotes: The strings are decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with their focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never pluck.

Keyboard: when a control inside takes keyboard focus the strings behind it are strummed top to bottom, 28 ms apart — the ringing a hand passing across them makes. The background adds no tab stop of its own.

Touch: a tap plucks the string under it and a sideways-and-down drag strums; the box keeps touch-action pan-y, so an upright swipe still scrolls the page — and a swipe the page takes never plucks, because a string is only grabbed once a press has become a drag.
Under reduced motion the strings stay straight and nothing shimmers; a pluck shows as the string's colour rising at once and fading as it would have rung, and its note still plays when sound is on.

Sound is off by default. With sound on, each pluck plays its string's note from the scale, louder for harder plucks and panned to where it was plucked; plucks from a passing pointer only sound once the page has had a click, tap or key, and the breeze is silent.

Canvas 2D on typed arrays, nothing allocated per frame. With only the breeze it draws thirty frames a second; with the breeze at 0 or paused it stops once the strings are still, and nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page. The canvas caps its pixel ratio at 2.

items.title: Sweep Scope
items.tagline: A sweep that finds what is out there.
items.description: A background that is a radar scope: range rings with their numbers, faint spokes and ticks, and a beam that nods across the upper half from a centre on the bottom edge (or turns full circle from the middle), its afterglow exact — every half-degree of bearing remembers when the beam last crossed it — lighting ground clutter as it rakes it, while vessels drifting across show only where the beam last painted them, each paint fading into a dotted track. A press places a contact whose corner brackets close in on springs.snap; nothing shows there until the sweep finds it, when the blip lands on springs.recoil and a ping ring opens, and keyboard focus on a control inside places a contact at that control.

props.name: onFind

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the box.

usageNotes: The scope is decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with their focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never place a contact.

Keyboard: when a control inside takes keyboard focus a contact is placed at its centre — the same contact a press places — and the sweep finds it on its next pass; blur takes the cursor away. The background adds no tab stop of its own.

Under reduced motion the beam stands parked with its afterglow drawn as if it had just passed and every vessel at its last paint; a placed contact shows at once, lit, with its brackets closed and no ping, and onFind fires with onPlace.

Canvas 2D: the face (rings, spokes, ticks, labels) is drawn once per size or theme; a frame is one blit, a third-resolution afterglow buffer from a precomputed bearing map, and a sprite per blip, with nothing allocated per frame. Paused, it stops once the last marker settles; nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page, and the canvas caps its pixel ratio at 2.

Bearings are degrees clockwise from straight up and ranges are in rings, so onPlace and onFind can feed a readout directly; labels drop away below 280 px wide, and the mono labels are redrawn once the page's fonts have loaded.

items.title: Polar Glow
items.tagline: A soft aurora, barely there.
items.description: A background of a night sky with an aurora barely there in it: broad, blurred curtains whose lower edges fold in three slow travelling waves, their light rising from the edge and fading upward from the palette's lower colour to its upper one, brighter where a sheet folds toward you, over a faint star field that shows only on a dark page — low contrast by design, so a headline sits on it comfortably. The curtain nearest the pointer brightens around it, each curtain's light following its own springs.drift so it hands over smoothly as the hand moves (the hand itself follows on springs.glide); a press sends a surge running out both ways along the nearest curtain, and keyboard focus on a control inside brightens the curtain nearest it and sends a softer surge.

usageNotes: The sky is decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with their focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never surge.
Keyboard: when a control inside takes keyboard focus the curtain nearest it brightens and a softer surge runs along it; blur lets the light go. The background adds no tab stop of its own.

Under reduced motion one composed moment of the sky is held — no drift, no twinkle — and the hand's light comes and goes as a short fade; a press brightens the nearest curtain as a whole and lets it fade, with no travelling surge.

It is built to sit behind text: even at intensity 1 the curtains stay soft and under 0.82 opacity, and a dither of under half a level keeps the gradients free of banding. On a light page the stars vanish and the curtains read as a pale wash.

One WebGL2 pass. It draws two dozen frames a second while it only drifts and every frame while the hand or a surge works; paused or at speed 0 it stops once they settle, and nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page. Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still sky stands in.

items.title: Aurora Curtain
items.tagline: Curtains of light with rays in their folds.
items.description: A night sky with an aurora in it, drawn in one WebGL2 pass with the content on top: tall curtains of light with a sharp pink lower fringe, a body of fine vertical rays and a ragged crown, sampled through travelling folds so the rays crowd and thicken where the sheet bunches, over a low ridge and treeline. The pointer gathers the rays toward the hand, the place following on springs.glide and the presence arriving on springs.drift, and a press sets off a breakup on the nearest curtain whose rays shoot up and die away on a critically damped drift spring. It is decoration and never takes focus; keyboard focus landing on a control inside gathers the rays there with a softer flare.

usageNotes: Give the box a size (a height class, or a parent that has one); children render above the sky in their own layer and keep every click, focus and text selection. The sky itself is aria-hidden and has no focus stop.

Keyboard: when a control inside gains keyboard focus the rays gather under it and a soft flare rises; blur lets them go. Presses on the content's own controls never flare. Touch gathers the rays where a finger lands without blocking vertical page scrolling.

Reduced motion: one still sky at a composed moment, no drift or shimmer; the gather lands exactly under the pointer with no easing, and a flare is a brightening of the nearest curtain that fades without growing.

Cost: one fullscreen WebGL2 pass at 0.75 render scale, thirty frames a second while it only drifts and every frame while the hand or a flare works; nothing off screen, in a hidden tab, or once paused or speed 0 has settled. DPR is capped at dpr. Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still sky stands in and a restored context repaints.

Theming: the stars show only on a dark page, and the sky deepens or pales with the theme; colours resolve on the component's own element, so a theme switch repaints. Pass three CSS colours to palette (fringe, body, crown) to dye the light your own way.

items.title: Plasma Bloom
items.tagline: Plasma in a palette you would wear.
items.description: A background of plasma in a palette you would wear, drawn in one WebGL2 pass with the content on top: interfering sine fields, planar and radial with slowly wandering centres, mapped through five low-chroma pigments mixed in OKLab, with a soft posterise from smooth gradient to crisp printed bands and a fine grain fixed to the cloth. The pointer adds its own source of rings that interfere into a soft moiré, the place following on springs.glide and the strength arriving on springs.drift, and a press drops a ring that rides outward while its strength rises and dies away on a critically damped drift spring. It is decoration and never takes focus; keyboard focus landing on a control inside brings the rings there and drops a softer one.

items.title: Plasma Ribbon
items.tagline: A ribbon of plasma across the dark.
items.description: A background with a single ribbon of plasma crossing it on a gentle wave, drawn in one WebGL2 pass with the content on top: a glowing core, long twisting filaments flowing along it, frayed edges and sparks that leave both edges, flicker and die inside a soft halo. Its centreline is a small string integrated at 120 Hz, where tension carries a disturbance along the ribbon and a local restoring spring with the springs.drift constants brings it home without ringing; the pointer pulls the string to its own height and the far ends follow late, and a press whips it with a crest and trough that run out both ways. It is decoration and never takes focus; keyboard focus landing on a control inside lifts the ribbon to it with a softer whip.

items.title: Dust Motes
items.tagline: Dust drifting through a beam of light.
items.description: A background of dust hanging in still air, seen through a lens, with a beam of light crossing the room and the content on top: seeded flakes wander on slow currents, rise a little in the warm light and flash as they turn to it, while a thin-lens depth of field opens near and far motes into soft bokeh discs and keeps those at the focal plane crisp. The pointer leans the camera on springs.drift, so near motes slide further than far ones, and a press racks focus to the mote under the hand, the focal plane travelling to its depth on springs.glide while a thin focus mark closes on it on springs.snap. It is decoration and never takes focus; keyboard focus landing on a control inside racks focus to the mote nearest it.

props.name: children

usageNotes: Give the box a size (a height class, or a parent that has one); children render above the room in their own layer and keep every click, focus and text selection. The room itself is aria-hidden and has no focus stop.

Keyboard: when a control inside gains keyboard focus the camera leans toward it and focus racks to the nearest mote; blur racks back to focus. Presses on the content's own controls never rack. Touch racks where a finger lands without blocking vertical page scrolling, and the focus holds for a moment after the finger lifts; onFocusPull reports each rack and then null when the lens lets go.

Reduced motion: a still room with no drift, spin or parallax; a press still racks focus, because blur is not travel, as a short tween instead of a spring, and the focus mark simply stands on the mote and is taken down after a moment, with no frames in between. The hand is not reported through onActiveChange, since the camera never leans.

Cost: Canvas 2D from a prefiltered sprite atlas, at most 600 sprites a frame and nothing allocated per frame; thirty frames a second while it only drifts and every frame while the lens or camera moves; nothing off screen, in a hidden tab, or once paused or drift 0 has settled. DPR is capped at dpr. count is for a 760 by 208 box, and smaller boxes hold proportionally fewer motes.

Theming: motes glow against a dark page and read as dark flecks with a softer beam on a light one; colours resolve on the component's own element, so a theme switch repaints. Pass any CSS colour to light to warm or cool the beam.

items.title: Shutter Glow
items.tagline: Blinds of gradient turning in the light.
items.description: A background of vertical blinds built from real CSS 3D slabs, each with a front, a back and two edges turning on its long axis in one shared perspective, over a glow of light seen through the gaps and with the content on top: the fronts carry slices of one gradient and the backs slices of another, and a light from one side shades every face and puts a sheen where its reflection meets the eye. A wave of turning crosses the wall every interval, blind after blind turning half over on springs.snap with one crisp overshoot, staggered so the whole wall changes gradient inside 600 ms, and a press sends the wave out both ways from the blind under it while the blinds near the pointer part around the hand on their own snap springs. It is decoration and never takes focus; keyboard focus landing on a control inside parts the blinds around it and sends a wave from there.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the box.

usageNotes: Give the box a size (a height class, or a parent that has one); children render above the blinds in their own layer and keep every click, focus and text selection. The wall itself is aria-hidden and has no focus stop.

Keyboard: when a control inside gains keyboard focus the blinds part around it and a wave turns the wall from there; blur lets them hang again. Presses on the content's own controls never send a wave. Touch parts the blinds where a finger lands without blocking vertical page scrolling.

Reduced motion: the blinds hang still at their resting angle and nothing rotates; a press or keyboard focus cross-fades the wall from one gradient to the other, staggered and lit as the faces are, and the wall never changes on its own. The hand does not part the blinds and is not reported as parting them.

Cost: no canvas and no WebGL; at most 32 slabs of four faces (and never narrower than 18 px each, so a narrow box hangs fewer) whose angles are motion values with every shade derived from them, so nothing re-renders per frame. Between waves nothing runs at all: the idle wave is a timer that waits while the wall is off screen or the page is hidden, and never fires while paused or with interval 0.

Theming: the pigments sit at fixed lightness and 10% into the page colour, so the wall reads the same in both themes and belongs to each. Pass four CSS colours to palette (front from and to, back from and to) for gradients of your own.

items.title: Grain Mesh
items.tagline: A grainy gradient that shifts like a print.
items.description: A background printed rather than rendered, drawn in one WebGL2 pass with the content on top: a mesh gradient of four to six spot inks laid down drum by drum like a risograph, through a stochastic screen fixed to the paper so ink lands as grain where it is thin and solid where it is thick, each drum a little out of register on a stock with fibres and tooth. The points drift on slow orbits while the grain stays put; the nearest ink leans toward a hovering hand on springs.glide, a drag picks it up on springs.flick and follows the finger 1:1 with its drum slipping out of register, and a release throws it home with the release velocity, landing on springs.recoil. It is decoration and never takes focus; keyboard focus landing on a control inside draws the nearest ink to it, and blur lets it land home.

props.name: seed

props.name: dpr

props.name: onActiveChange

usageNotes: Give the box a size (a height class, or a parent that has one); children render above the print in their own layer and keep every click, focus and text selection. The print itself is aria-hidden and has no focus stop.

Keyboard: when a control inside gains keyboard focus the nearest ink is drawn to it; blur lets it recoil home. Drags start only on the paper, never on the content's controls. On touch a sideways drag pulls ink and an upright one scrolls the page.

Reduced motion: the print is still at a composed moment; the hover lean lands at once, a drag still follows the finger 1:1 because it is direct manipulation, and a release puts the ink straight home without the recoil or the register jolt.

Cost: one fullscreen WebGL2 pass with the grain computed in CSS px, so it keeps its size at any DPR; twenty-four frames a second while it only drifts and every frame while the hand works; nothing off screen, in a hidden tab, or once paused or drift 0 has settled. DPR is capped at dpr. Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS print of the inks under a halftone screen stands in and a restored context repaints.

Theming: inks multiply on light stock so overprints darken into new colours, and screen onto dark stock on a dark page; colours resolve on the component's own element, so a theme switch repaints. Pass four to six CSS colours to palette for inks of your own.

items.title: Horizon Grid
items.tagline: A perspective grid swept by light.
items.description: A background of a fine grid floor running to the horizon, the camera travelling over it so the lines flow toward you, a soft band of light sweeping across the floor and a low glow breathing on the horizon. The camera banks and turns toward the hand on springs with the springs.drift constants and levels the same way when it leaves; a press on the bare background opens a ring of light across the floor in perspective while a critically damped surge carries the camera a few cells forward. Keyboard focus on a control inside leans the camera toward it and opens a softer ring under it.

There is no tab stop of its own: keyboard focus on a control inside leans the camera toward it and opens a softer ring, the same response a hand gets.

One fullscreen WebGL2 draw at a capped pixel ratio, 30 frames a second while it only travels, and nothing at all off screen, in a hidden page, or while paused and level. Context loss shows the stand-in until the context returns.
The light takes the given colour at a fixed lightness, and the floor and haze are read from the component's own element and re-read when the theme changes, so it reads in light and dark.
Under reduced motion one still floor is drawn: the grid and the band parked, the glow steady and the camera level. A press shows its ring at full width at once and fades it by opacity only.

items.title: Stage Beams
items.tagline: Beams that sweep like a concert stage.
items.description: A background of a lighting rig along the bottom edge throwing narrow volumetric beams up through drifting haze in mirrored pairs, a lighting desk moving them through looks on springs with the springs.drift constants — a fan, crossed pairs, straight up, a lean — with motes glinting where the beams pass and light pooling on the floor. The beam nearest the pointer leaves the show and follows the hand on springs.glide like a follow spot, and a press brings every beam onto that point on springs.snap with one crisp overshoot while the rig flares. Keyboard focus on a control inside puts the nearest pair on it, crossing there.

There is no tab stop of its own: keyboard focus on a control inside points the nearest pair at it, and leaving hands the pair back to the show.

One fullscreen WebGL2 draw at half the capped pixel ratio, 30 frames a second while the show sways, nothing off screen or in a hidden page, and nothing when paused and settled. Context loss shows the stand-in until the context returns.
Palettes take their colours at a fixed lightness so the beams read the same in both themes; the hall's darkness is read from the component's own element and re-read on theme change.
Under reduced motion the rig holds its first look with no sway or drifting haze; the hand and focus still direct the beams, which land where they are sent at once.

items.title: Pixel Snowfall
items.tagline: Snow falling in quiet pixels.
items.description: A background of snow drawn as pixel art at three depths over a dithered sky, far flakes single dim cells and near ones small crosses swaying hardest in the wind, settling into a drift along the bottom edge that banks into rounded dunes and slowly melts. The pointer is a wind source that blows harder the faster it moves, and a press bursts a gust — a critically damped impulse on the springs.drift constants — that throws the nearby flakes outward and scours a crater in the drift whose snow sprays up and lands again. Keyboard focus on a control inside puffs a softer gust from it.

There is no tab stop of its own: keyboard focus on a control inside puffs a gust from it, the same response a press gets. On touch a tap bursts a gust and page scrolling stays with the page.
Canvas 2D into a buffer of cells scaled up crisp, thirty frames a second only while on screen in a visible page, nothing allocated per frame; paused holds the flakes in the air and stops the loop.
Density is set per area, so a phone card and a wide hero snow equally hard. The sky and snow colours are read from the component's own element and re-read when the theme changes.
Under reduced motion it is one still winter frame with the drift banked; a press shows the gust's end state at once.

items.title: Storm Front
items.tagline: Lightning moving through heavy cloud.
items.description: A background of a heavy storm deck seen from beneath, rolling slowly in layered, domain-warped cloud over a pale band of rain, lit from inside by seeded lightning that crawls and branches through it: a dim leader, two or three return strokes and an afterglow, the light catching the undersides of every billow and the channel glimpsed only where the cloud thins. A click calls a strike at the pointer — a discharge crawling out both ways inside the cloud, or a stroke dropping from the base below it — with thunder after the flash when sound is on, and a faint charge gathers under the hand on springs with the springs.drift constants. Keyboard focus on a control inside calls a softer, silent discharge above it.

There is no tab stop of its own: keyboard focus on a control inside calls a soft discharge above it, the same strike a click gets but quieter and always silent.
Thunder (a thud, later and lower the deeper the strike sits) only answers a visitor's click and only when sound is true; the storm's own flashes are always silent.

One fullscreen WebGL2 draw at half the capped pixel ratio, 30 frames a second while the cloud only rolls, every frame during a flash, nothing off screen or in a hidden page, and nothing when paused with no flash running. Context loss shows the stand-in until the context returns; without WebGL2 the stand-in stays.

The light takes the tint at a fixed lightness and the cloud is built from the page's own background and foreground, read from the component's element and re-read on theme change: a grey daylight storm in light, blue-black cloud in dark.
Under reduced motion the cloud holds still around one softly lit discharge with no automatic flashes; a click lights the cloud at the pointer as one still frame that fades out by opacity.

items.title: Spectrum Burst
items.tagline: A burst of light split into colour.
items.description: A background of light bursting from a point in every direction, each seeded ray split by dispersion: summed over seven wavelengths, each turned by an angle that grows away from the centre, so the colours overlap into white at the heart and fan into a spectrum toward each tip, red on one edge and violet on the other. The burst turns slowly and breathes, and its centre follows the hand on springs with the springs.drift constants; a press blooms it on springs.recoil — rays thrown out long and split wide, ringing twice as they settle — while a split ring of light leaves the centre on the enter easing. Keyboard focus on a control inside carries the centre to it and blooms softly.

There is no tab stop of its own: keyboard focus on a control inside carries the centre over it and blooms softly, and leaving returns it home.

One fullscreen WebGL2 draw at half the capped pixel ratio; each pixel weighs only the ray under it and its two neighbours, with ray shapes hashed in the shader. 30 frames a second while it only turns, every frame while a spring settles, nothing off screen or in a hidden page, and nothing when paused and settled. Context loss shows the stand-in until the context returns.

In the dark theme the light adds to the page; in the light theme it lays down as washes, the white of each ray only a faint warm shade and its split edges tinting the page. The page colour is read from the component's own element and re-read on theme change.
Under reduced motion the burst is still at a seeded moment: the centre lands where the hand puts it at once, and a press shows the bloom's peak while it is held.

items.title: Star Spiral
items.tagline: A galaxy turning slowly in the dark.
items.description: A background of a spiral galaxy built from density waves: every star rides its own closed orbit, the orbits bulging into lobes that twist with radius, so the arms stand where neighbouring orbits crowd while every star streams through them, the core turning faster than the rim. Young stars light only along the arm ridges, a bulge glows at the centre and dust rides each arm's leading edge, becoming the dark lane when the disk is seen edge on. A drag tilts the plane 1:1, rubber-banding past edge on, and on release it swings back on springs with the springs.drift constants taking the release velocity; a tap sends a ring of star formation out from the core on the enter easing as the core flares on a drift-spring impulse, and keyboard focus on a control inside tilts the plane toward it and sends a softer ring.

props.name: onTiltChange

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires when a drag or keyboard focus starts (true) or stops (false) tilting the plane.

props.description: Sizes and shapes the box.

usageNotes: The canvas and its CSS stand-in are aria-hidden and pointer-events-none; children render above them and keep every click. A press on a control is the control's: it never tilts the plane or sends a ring.

There is no tab stop of its own: keyboard focus on a control inside tilts the plane toward it and sends a softer ring, and blur lets it right itself. On touch the root is touch-pan-y, so a sideways drag tilts the plane and an upright swipe scrolls the page.

Canvas 2D with every orbit in typed arrays: a frame is a few trig calls per star and about a dozen batched fills, nothing allocated per frame. 30 frames a second while it turns, every frame while dragging, swinging back or ringing, nothing off screen or in a hidden page, and nothing when paused and settled.

In the dark theme the stars add as light; in the light theme the galaxy prints as a negative plate, ink stars on paper with the dust as pale lanes. Colours are read from the component's own element and re-read on theme change; young stars and the bulge take their colours at a fixed lightness so both themes read them.
onTiltChange reports whole degrees only when they change, so a status line can follow a drag without rendering every frame.
Under reduced motion the galaxy is still at a seeded moment: a drag sets the tilt exactly under the hand and release returns it at once, and a tap brightens a still ring at mid-disk for a moment.

items.title: Dither Dunes
items.tagline: Gradients printed in ordered dots.
items.description: A background printed like a one-bit risograph sheet: an aerial dune sea whose crests bow, split and rejoin as the field migrates downwind, drawn entirely in two or three flat inks through an ordered dither, with the key ink printing the relief and a spot ink laying large soft shapes under it on a shifted screen. The pointer is a lamp whose soft spot of light follows on the springs.glide constants and arrives on springs.drift; a press pulls a flash, a ring that prints the sheet in negative as it crosses, and the spot swells after it on springs.recoil. Keyboard focus on a control inside brings the lamp to it with a softer flash.

props.name: matrix

props.name: className

usageNotes: The print is decoration: the canvas, its CSS stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and your children sit above in their own layer with focus, clicks and selection intact. Presses on your controls never flash.
Keyboard: a control inside taking keyboard focus brings the lamp to it and pulls a softer flash from it; blur lets the light go. No tab stop of its own.

Inks resolve on the element and are re-read when the theme changes. On a light page the key ink prints the shade and the sheet rests mostly paper; on a dark page it prints the light, a negative that stays mostly dark. Pass two or three colours of your own, paper first.
Every dot is a whole number of device pixels: the canvas is the dot grid itself, scaled up nearest-neighbour, so the shader runs once per dot and the print stays crisp at any pixel ratio.
Under reduced motion one still print is drawn; the spot of light lands exactly where the hand is and a press brightens it for a moment without any ring travelling.

WebGL2: thirty frames a second while it only drifts, every frame while the hand or a flash moves, nothing off screen or in a hidden page. A lost context shows the CSS stand-in until it is restored; without WebGL2 the stand-in stays.

items.title: Relay Terminal
items.tagline: A terminal screen humming with glyphs.
items.description: A background that is a terminal screen of mono glyphs holding real-looking console output, updating in bursts: lines re-roll and settle left to right, value fields tick, and now and then the screen feeds a line, scrolling up a row on the springs.glide constants while the new line types in behind a blinking cursor. Written glyphs flare and decay through the phosphor with a fading ghost of what they replaced, a faint line screen and a slow rolling band sit over the tube, and a line occasionally tears sideways and springs back on springs.snap. The pointer is a lamp whose light follows on glide and arrives on springs.drift; a press pings the screen with a ring that flares every glyph it crosses, and keyboard focus on a control inside lights and pings from that control.

props.name: children

props.name: rate

props.name: glyphs

props.name: color

props.name: fontSize

props.name: density

props.name: decay

props.name: glitch

props.name: scanlines

props.name: glow
props.description: The halo round lit glyphs, 0 (none) to 1.

props.name: cursor

props.name: interactive

props.name: pointerStrength

props.name: radius

props.name: paused

props.name: seed

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires when the pointer or keyboard focus starts (true) or stops (false) lighting the screen.

props.name: onPing

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the box.

usageNotes: The screen is decoration: the canvas, its text stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden, and the glyphs are never read aloud. Your children sit above in their own layer with focus, clicks and selection intact; presses on your controls never ping.
Keyboard: a control inside taking keyboard focus lights the glyphs round it and pings from it; blur lets the light go. No tab stop of its own.
The phosphor resolves on the element and is re-read when the theme changes: on a dark page it glows over a tinted tube, on a light page it is drawn as ink on a pale screen, so it reads in both.

Glyphs come from an atlas built once per font, colour, theme and pixel ratio, one blit per cell a frame; block elements are drawn, not set in type, so meters join without seams. If the host's mono face is not monospaced the system's is used.
Under reduced motion the screen is still with the newest lines a little brighter; the lamp lands where the hand is and a press lights the glyphs round it, fading back without anything travelling.

Thirty frames a second while only the output runs, every frame while a tear springs, a ping travels, the screen scrolls or the hand moves; nothing off screen or in a hidden page, and paused stops the loop once the phosphor settles.

items.title: Ripple Lattice
items.tagline: A grid that ripples where you touch.
items.description: A background that is a fine square lattice of hairlines, centred in the box, whose lines are pushed by ripples: each a wave packet spreading from where it fell, a leading crest with a short train of wavelets behind, decaying with age and spreading with distance. Up to thirty-two sum as vectors, so crossing rings interfere into a moire of pinched and stretched cells, and the lines thicken and brighten at the crests. A moving pointer leaves a wake of small ripples as strong as it is quick, a press drops a stone, denting the mat under it so it bounces back twice on springs.recoil while the ring spreads with a softer echo behind it, and keyboard focus on a control inside drops one from that control.

props.name: children

props.name: spacing

props.name: strength

props.name: color

props.name: lineWidth
props.description: The lines' width, px.

props.name: wavelength

props.name: speed

props.name: decay

props.name: crest
props.description: How much the lines thicken and brighten at the crests, 0 to 1.

props.name: drizzle

props.name: trail

props.name: interactive

props.name: seed

props.name: dpr

props.name: onActiveChange

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the box.

usageNotes: The grid is decoration: the canvas, the SVG and the colour carriers are aria-hidden. Your children sit above in their own layer with focus, clicks and selection intact, and a press on one of your controls never drops a ripple.
Keyboard: a control inside taking keyboard focus drops a ripple from its centre. No tab stop of its own.

One WebGL2 fragment pass sums up to thirty-two ripples per pixel. The server renders the lattice at rest as an SVG pattern; without WebGL2, or after a lost context, that SVG stays and its lines are rebuilt from the same ripples.
The loop runs only while a ripple lives or drizzle falls, on screen and in a visible page; with drizzle at 0 the grid settles flat and costs nothing until the hand moves.
Under reduced motion nothing spreads: no drizzle and no wake, and a press draws one still ring that fades where it stands.
Colours resolve on the element and are re-read when the theme changes, so the grid reads on light and dark pages alike.

items.title: Pollen Flow
items.tagline: Specks carried on a slow current.
items.description: A background of fine specks carried on a slow breeze: a steady current plus the curl of two octaves of drifting noise, so the specks swirl and braid but never pile into knots. Each speck has a little inertia and leaves a short trail that tapers and fades behind it, and three sizes give the cloud depth. The air eddies round the hand, the eddy's place following on springs.glide and its strength arriving on springs.drift; a press shakes pollen loose, the oldest specks reborn at the press in a bright little cloud the air's drag takes into the current, and keyboard focus on a control inside brings the eddy there and shakes a smaller cloud from it.

props.name: wind

props.name: interactive

props.name: pointerStrength

props.name: radius

props.name: paused

props.name: seed

props.name: dpr

props.name: onShake

usageNotes: The current is decoration: the canvas, its seeded SVG stand-in and the colour carriers are aria-hidden. Your children sit above in their own layer with focus, clicks and selection intact, and a press on one of your controls never shakes pollen.
Keyboard: a control inside taking keyboard focus brings the eddy to it and shakes a smaller cloud from it. No tab stop of its own.
Colours are pigment, not text colour: each palette hue is drawn at a fixed lightness per theme, re-read when the theme changes, so the specks read on light and dark pages alike.

Canvas 2D: the air is a few hundred noise samples on a 20 px grid, and the specks are batched into one stroke per colour and fade band, about forty draws a frame. Typed arrays are sized on resize and count change, never per frame.
The loop runs only on screen in a visible page; paused, or speed 0 once the specks have coasted to rest, stops it. The count scales with the box's area, so a phone card is as dense as a desktop hero.
Under reduced motion the current is a long exposure: a still frame of specks with their trails traced back along the air, and a press brightens the specks round it where they stand.

items.title: Dot Tide
items.tagline: A field of dots with a tide running through it.
items.description: A background that is a regular dot grid, centred in the box, with a slow tide running through it: three long travelling waves sum into a height that raises and lowers every dot between a fine point and most of a cell, and the colour shifts along the wave from troughs washed into the page to crests in the full colour turned a little in hue. The tide rises gently under the hand, the mound following on springs.glide and arriving on springs.drift. A press sends a fast circular wave through the field, and every dot rides its own springs.recoil spring, so each dot the ring crosses pops up, overshoots back twice and settles, leaving a ringing, brightened wake; keyboard focus on a control inside raises the tide there and sends a softer wave from it.

Keyboard: a control inside taking keyboard focus raises the tide round it and sends a softer wave from it. No tab stop of its own.
The nine tones from trough to crest are mixed by the browser in OKLab against the page background and re-read when the theme changes, so the field reads on light and dark pages alike.

Canvas 2D: one arc per dot and nine fills a frame, with every dot's spring integrated in typed arrays. The tide alone draws thirty frames a second; a wave or the hand gets every frame, and nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page.
The server renders the same centred grid at rest as a CSS dot pattern, so the first paint lines up with the canvas when it takes over.
Under reduced motion the tide holds a composed moment, the rise lands under the hand without travelling, and a press tints the dots round it where they stand.

items.title: Thread Drift
items.tagline: Threads that float and tangle gently.
items.description: A background of long smooth threads drifting edge to edge, each through thirteen points riding two octaves of noise, so it bows and swings like silk in still air while neighbours cross, wrap and part again. Threads sit at their own depths over a thin stroke of the page colour, so crossings read over and under, and the bends catch the light. The hand gathers them, every point drawn toward it on its own springs.glide spring with the gather arriving on springs.drift; a press pinches them into a knot under the finger and on release they let go on springs.recoil, swinging back past their lanes twice; keyboard focus on a control inside gathers the threads to it and plucks them once.

Keyboard: a control inside taking keyboard focus gathers the threads to it and plucks them once, the same swing a press and release gives. No tab stop of its own.
Colours are pigment, not text colour: each palette hue is drawn at a fixed lightness per theme and the gap under each thread is the box's own colour, all re-read when the theme changes.

Canvas 2D: two strokes per thread plus a few sheen arcs on its bends; every control point's spring lives in typed arrays sized once. The drift alone draws thirty frames a second, the hand and a release get every frame, and nothing runs off screen or in a hidden page.
The server renders the same skein at a composed moment as an SVG traced with arithmetic-only noise, so it matches the browser to the digit.
Under reduced motion the skein holds that composed moment, nothing gathers, and a press lights the bends round it where they lie.

items.title: Night Drive
items.tagline: Streaks of light on an endless road.
items.description: A background of a highway at night seen from a moving car, drawn as a long exposure: one WebGL2 pass casts every pixel onto the road, the light plane and its mirror under the wet asphalt, so oncoming headlights stream toward you in pale trails, taillights pull away to the vanishing point in red, dashes rush past and lamps pass overhead with long reflections while the road sweeps through slow bends. The pointer steers across your lanes on the springs.glide constants, and holding a press warps — speed, trail length and field of view stretch on glide and ease back to a cruise on springs.drift. Keyboard focus on a control inside steers toward it and surges.
