usageNotes: Keyboard: the headline is one tab stop with a hint. Focus sweeps the lens along the line word by word; Left and Right move it, Home and End jump, Enter or Space sweeps again and Escape closes it. Each key move is announced politely.

The real text is the element's own transparent text node, so it sizes the box (no layout shift), selects and copies as words (selected text shows in ink), and is read once by assistive technology; the canvas is aria-hidden.
Reduced motion: no paint-on and no breathing; the dabs are painted still, the lens fades rather than springs and follows directly, and focus places it on the first word without a sweep.

Performance: Canvas 2D, one path fill per pigment per frame from typed arrays. The loop runs only on screen in a visible tab while something changes; breathing alone draws at 30 fps and stops with twinkle={0} or paused. The lattice is rebuilt on resize, font load and theme change.

The server renders the same pigments as a dotted fill clipped to the glyphs, which the paint-on wipes away, so the first frame is already the headline. Pigments sit at one fixed lightness each set, so the mix reads the same on light and dark pages.

items.title: Steam Words
items.tagline: Words rise off a warm cup and drift apart.
items.description: A cup at the foot of the frame breathes a column of steam out of which a phrase condenses: each letter leaves the coffee as a tall, thin, blurred wisp and climbs to the reading line, opening out to its place and settling on the house drift spring, centre letters first. After a moment legible, the draught shears it apart from the windward end — each letter carried off by a gust that grows with the square of its time released, skewed, stretched and split into wisps — while the next phrase rises. The cup is a real button: Space or Enter blows the phrase away and brings the next, Left and Right blow it toward that side, and a sideways swipe across the steam does the same.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The phrase in the air, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange

props.name: rise

props.name: shear

props.name: warmth

props.name: draught
props.description: Where the draught comes from.

props.name: hold
props.description: How long a phrase stays legible, ms at rise 1.

props.name: readingLine
props.description: Height of the reading line, 0 (top) to 1 (foot).

props.name: steamColor

props.name: warmColor

props.name: cupColor

props.name: color

props.name: interactive

props.name: paused

props.name: label

usageNotes: Keyboard: the cup is a real button in the tab order — Space or Enter blows the phrase away and brings the next, Left and Right blow it toward that side. The new phrase is announced only after a blow, never on the automatic cycle.
Assistive technology reads the scene's label and every phrase once from a hidden line; the letters, their wisps, the steam canvas and the cup art are aria-hidden.
Reduced motion: one phrase stands still and legible over a single drawn wisp of steam, with no loop running; a blow cross-fades to the next phrase.

Performance: one requestAnimationFrame loop drives a fixed pool of steam puffs (a cached soft sprite) and writes the letters' transforms straight to their nodes; it runs only on screen in a visible tab and stops while paused.
Give it a height; the phrase's size comes from the className (em-based). Long phrases wrap on word boundaries.

items.title: Word Hunt
items.tagline: A letter grid that rings the words that matter.
items.description: A word search: a wall of mono capitals with your words hidden in all eight directions by a seeded generator. A marker capsule hunts them one at a time, gliding to each word on the glide spring — centre, angle the short way round and length each on its own — drawing its outline round it and inking the letters in a cascade, then leaving the word tinted as it moves on. Drag across the grid to circle one yourself: the capsule follows the finger 1:1 held to the allowed directions and lands on whole cells on the snap spring, or fades if it caught nothing. The grid is one tab stop: arrow keys move the marker between found words, Home and End jump, Enter or Space circles the next hidden word.

props.name: words
props.description: The words to hide; letters only are kept and a word longer than the grid is left out.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The words found so far, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange

props.name: onFind

props.name: gridSize

props.name: rows
props.defaultValue: about 0.42 of the columns, at least 5

props.name: directions

props.name: seed
props.description: Where the words go and which letters fill the rest.

props.name: marker
props.description: The pen: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: pace
props.description: How quickly the marker hunts, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: autoplay

props.name: loop
props.description: Once every word is found, clear the tints and hunt again.

props.name: showList
props.description: Show the word list beside (or under) the grid.

props.name: label

props.name: disabled

usageNotes: Keyboard: the grid is one tab stop (role application with a hint). Arrow keys move the marker between found words, Home and End jump to the first and last, Enter or Space circles the next hidden word — the keyboard's way to find one yourself. Every find and move is announced politely.

Pointer: press on a letter and drag across a word; the capsule follows 1:1 along the nearest allowed direction. The grid uses touch-action: none so a finger can drag in any direction; the word list and page around it still scroll.
The hunt pauses while the pointer is over the grid or focus is in it, and only runs on screen in a visible tab; it is timers and springs only, no frame loop.
Reduced motion: no glide or outline draw — the marker appears round each word with a short fade and the ink swaps in; the dragged capsule still follows the finger and settles without a spring.

The grid is generated deterministically from words, size and seed, so the server and the browser render the same puzzle; the layout puts the list beside the grid from a 34rem container and under it below that.

items.title: Salon Walk
items.tagline: Walk a long corridor of hung pictures.
items.description: A long barrel-vaulted corridor in CSS 3D, every length in container units, with pictures hung alternately on both walls in gilt frames under small picture lights. Scroll walks you forward: the corridor is a real scroll container with the view sticky inside it, and the camera follows the scroll on the drift spring with a slight lean toward the picture ahead. As you draw level with a frame it swings toward you on its wire on a spring at glide stiffness whose damping falls as sway rises, so it overshoots and swings back once, while its plaque brightens and its light comes up. Arrow keys step frame to frame, Home and End go to either end, and a click on a picture walks to it.

props.name: onValueChange

props.name: spacing

props.name: lighting

props.name: wallColor

props.name: frameColor

props.name: eyeHeight

props.name: walk

props.name: label

props.name: disabled

usageNotes: Keyboard: the corridor is one tab stop (a region with roledescription gallery). Down and Right step to the next picture, Up and Left to the one before, Page Up and Page Down two at a time, Home and End to either end; each arrival is announced with its caption and note.

Scrolling is native: wheel, trackpad, touch and keys scroll a real container, and when you reach the end the page carries on scrolling. Pictures are listed once for assistive technology; the 3D dressing is aria-hidden.
Reduced motion: the camera follows the scroll directly with no spring and no lean, pictures hang flat, and the plaques and light pools still brighten beside the picture you are level with.

Performance: everything is CSS 3D on the compositor; one requestAnimationFrame loop runs only while the camera or a picture is still moving, on screen, in a visible tab, and stops when settled. No canvas.
The room is drawn in fixed pigments (plaster, salon red, gilt) so it reads the same in light and dark pages; pass wallColor and frameColor to re-hang it.

items.title: Formation Flight
items.tagline: Pictures that fly into formation on cue.
items.description: A flock of photo cards in CSS 3D holding a named formation — a tipped ring, a two-turn spiral, a globe or a grid — and turning slowly while it waits. Choosing a formation sends every card on its own cubic path through a curve the whole flock shares, departures from the flock's leading edge and arrivals packed tighter, so the flock stretches into a stream and tightens into the new shape; each card's roll comes from its real sideways acceleration on the path, so it banks into the turn and levels out as it lands. Hover a card and it comes forward on the snap spring. The picker is a radiogroup whose arrow keys cycle formations, and the flock is a listbox: arrows move between cards and bring each forward, Enter chooses one.

props.name: items
props.description: The cards in the flock.

props.name: formation / defaultFormation
props.description: The formation the flock holds, controlled or initial.

props.name: onFormationChange
props.description: Fires from the picker or the keys that asked for a new formation.

props.name: formations
props.description: Which formations the picker offers, in order.

props.name: cohesion
props.description: How tightly the flock holds together in flight, 0 (a loose stream) to 1 (one body).

props.name: bank
props.description: How hard cards roll into their turns, 0 (flat) to 1.

props.name: spin
props.description: Idle turn of the ring, spiral and globe, degrees a second; 0 holds them still.

props.name: cardSize
props.description: Card size, 0.6 to 1.6.

props.name: flightTime
props.description: A flight's length at default cohesion, ms.

props.name: showPicker
props.description: Show the formation picker.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: A card was chosen with a click or Enter.

props.name: label
props.description: The flock's accessible name.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the idle turn; a flight still flies.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The picker and the cards take no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Give it a height; the flock scales with the smaller side.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the formation picker is a radiogroup with roving focus — arrows cycle the formations, Home and End jump. The flock is a listbox with aria-activedescendant: arrows move between cards and bring the active one forward with a focus ring, Enter or Space chooses it.
Reduced motion: no flights and no idle turn — the cards fade out and back in at their new places, and a hovered or active card grows in place without travelling.

Performance: CSS 3D on the compositor with transforms written straight to the card nodes; one requestAnimationFrame loop runs while flying, turning or settling a hover, only on screen in a visible tab, and stops when settled with spin={0} or paused.

At rest the flock holds itself in the air: a loose flock (low cohesion) bobs out of line, every card rocks a little by bank, and in a turning ring or spiral the cards lean into the turn, so both knobs read before any flight.
Every length is in container units (cqmin), so the server renders the first formation exactly and the flock scales with its box; cards facing away show the back of the print.

items.title: Cyclorama Room
items.tagline: Stand inside a panorama of your pictures.
items.description: Your pictures composited into one continuous painted band — cover-fitted panels cross-faded across a blend zone so the seams dissolve — wrapped round the inside of a drum, with you at its centre behind a brass viewing rail. A Canvas 2D view draws the band in two-pixel strips from the camera, atan across and 1/cos up, so it bows toward you at the edges; curvature blends that from a flat strip and fov sets how much you see. Drag to look round 1:1 and a throw coasts on with its velocity on the drift spring; a heading strip along the base names each picture as it passes. Click a picture or press Enter and the heading glides to it and you walk up on the drift spring while the rail drops away; Escape or Step back walks you back. Left and Right turn 15°, Page Up and Page Down go picture to picture.

props.name: items
props.description: The pictures, stitched round the drum in order.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The heading at the centre of the view, degrees, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the heading a drag, throw or key is heading for, 0–360.

props.name: curvature

props.name: fov
props.description: Field of view across the frame, degrees, 50 to 110.

props.name: rail
props.description: Draw the brass viewing rail in front of you.

props.name: drift

props.name: zoom
props.description: How close walking up to a picture gets, 1.4 to 3.

props.name: blend
props.description: How wide the cross-fade across each seam is, as a share of a picture, 0 to 0.3.

props.name: showStrip

props.name: onOpen

props.name: onFrontChange

props.name: label
props.description: The view's accessible name.

props.name: dpr

props.name: disabled
props.description: No turning or walking up.

props.name: className
props.description: Give it a height.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the view is one tab stop (a region with roledescription panorama). Left and Right turn 15°, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End go picture to picture, Enter walks up to the picture in front and Escape (or the Step back button) walks back; turns and walks are announced.
Pointer: drag sideways to look round (touch-action: pan-y keeps vertical page scrolling); a click walks up to the picture under it, and another click walks back.
Reduced motion: no idle turn and no coasting — a drag turns 1:1, keys jump, and walking up is a short cross-fade.

Performance: Canvas 2D, about one drawImage per two pixels of width per frame, drawn only while turning or walking and stopped when settled; the idle turn runs only on screen in a visible tab. The panorama is composed once per item, size or blend change; gradients and sprites are built per size, never per frame. Images can come from any origin, as nothing is read back.
The room is fixed art (dark canopy, brass rail), the same in light and dark pages. The server renders a painted gradient stand-in and the heading strip, so the first frame is designed.

items.title: Paternoster Cards
items.tagline: Cards riding an endless lift, one landing at a time.
items.description: Cards ride the open cabins of an endless lift: up the left shaft, over the top on the drive wheel's half circle (receding into the machine room so close cabins pass behind each other) and down the right, the loop longer than the frame so it never stops and never jumps. The chain runs by itself and crawls while a cabin is level with the landing; there the cabin's lamp warms and its card swings out on springs.snap while it travels and grows to full size on springs.glide, its detail printing in line by line, then tucks back on an exit tween as the cabin moves on. Drag drives the chain 1:1 (up on either shaft moves the cabins under the finger), a flick settles on the nearest landing on glide with the release velocity; Up and Right bring the next cabin, Down and Left the previous, Home and End the ends, Enter or Space hold the landing card and Escape lets it go.

props.name: speed

props.name: landing

props.name: disabled

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: the shaft view is one focusable carousel — Up/Right next cabin, Down/Left previous, Home/End first and last card, Enter or Space hold the landing card, Escape release. Each card is a labelled slide; off-landing cards are hidden and inert. Moves made by the visitor are announced politely; the automatic run is not.

Pausing: the run rests while the pointer or keyboard focus is on the lift and for a few seconds after any visitor move, and the Stop / Run button on the ground floor stops it outright (pass `paused` to stop it from the host).
Reduced motion: the chain never runs by itself and lands at once; the landing card cross-fades open in place with its detail, because which card is at the landing is the information.

Performance: one requestAnimationFrame loop drives the chain, and only while it should run, the lift is on screen and the tab is visible; everything else is motion values, so React renders only when the landing changes.
Theming: the wall, shafts and cards use tokens; cabin materials and lamps are pigments derived from tokens at fixed lightness, so both themes read.

items.title: Celluloid Coil
items.tagline: A strip of film winding through space.
items.description: Pictures become frames on one long strip of film — sprocket holes cut through the base, frame numbers, stock and captions printed on the edge — wound in a loose helix through space in CSS 3D, each frame a plane on the chord between its ends so the strip never tears. The camera rides the strip and follows its turns, so travelling reads as the coil turning past you like a screw: each frame swings round to face you at the gate and curls away round the back; on first view the straight strip winds into its coil on springs.drift. Wheel, drag (1:1 at the gate) and flick travel along it and settle on the nearest frame on springs.glide with the release velocity; Left and Right step frames, Page keys step three, Home and End go to the ends.

Reduced motion: the coil is wound from the first frame and nothing glides — steps and drags land at once and the grain holds still.

Performance: every frame is posed as a rounded matrix3d in a motion value, with no allocation per frame and no loop at rest; frames beyond 1.3 turns of the gate are hidden, and the server renders the reel laid flat.
Images: pass `src` (any URL) or `art`; frames are about a third of the stage wide, so modest images are enough.

items.title: Prism Gate
items.tagline: Pictures take their colour passing through glass.
items.description: A rail of pictures runs through a glass prism at the centre of the frame: outside the glass they wear a quiet monochrome tone, behind it they are in colour, cut exactly at its faces, so a picture sliding in takes its colour from the leading edge. While it moves through, the glass splits it into colour fringes — three channel copies isolated with colour matrices and screen-blended back over black, separating along the direction of travel by `dispersion` — and they close up as it centres and holds in resolved colour. Drag follows 1:1 and rubber-bands at the ends, a flick settles on the nearest picture on springs.glide with the release velocity; Left and Right step, Page keys step three, Home and End go to the ends, and a click brings a picture to the glass.

Performance: one rail motion value; the colour layers exist only for pictures near the glass, and the channel copies only while a picture is splitting, so at rest each picture is one layer. The tone and channel filters are static SVG.
Theming: the glass, caption and frame use tokens; the monochrome tones are colour matrices, so your own pictures take them as they are.

items.title: Petal Gallery
items.tagline: Pictures as petals that close around your choice.
items.description: Pictures sit as petals in an oval bloom around an empty heart, each clipped to a petal outline and kept upright inside it. Choosing one closes the bloom like a flower at dusk: the chosen picture flies from its petal into the heart on springs.glide, its outline morphing from petal to oval, while the other petals fold up toward you about their base hinges and over its rim on springs.drift — a wave running round from the chosen petal, swirled by `curl` and paced by `bloomSpeed` — as the frame dims and pushes in. The bloom is a listbox: arrow keys move round it, Home and End jump, Enter or Space choose, and Escape or a tap on a folded petal opens the bloom again.

props.name: height

props.name: label

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer frame.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the bloom is a focusable listbox with aria-activedescendant — Right/Down move clockwise, Left/Up back, Home/End jump, Enter or Space choose, Escape opens the bloom again; the active petal lifts and takes the ring colour, and choices are announced politely.
Reduced motion: nothing folds or flies — the chosen picture cross-fades into the heart and the petals fade to their undersides, and back.

Performance: two motion values drive the whole bloom (the heart's flight and the close, which each petal reads through its own window); the clip shapes are static except while the heart morphs, and nothing runs at rest.
Pictures are cropped square inside each petal and oval in the heart, so centre the subject of your own images.

items.title: Crate Dig
items.tagline: Flip through a crate and pull out a record.
items.description: Album sleeves stand in a wooden crate seen from above at an angle, in CSS 3D. Flick, drag or scroll and they tip forward one at a time onto the front wall and each other, each a hair more upright than the last so the stack never passes through itself, while the next cover stands revealed, lifted a notch; the flip is one continuous value, so a drag riffles through 1:1 and a flick settles on a whole sleeve on springs.glide with the release velocity. Pull the revealed sleeve (drag it up, click it or Enter) and it rises to face you on glide, the record sliding out a beat later and spinning up to `spin` rpm, its label printed; Escape or Enter puts it back on an exit tween. Down and Right flip forward, Up and Left back, Home and End go to the ends, with paper sounds for every sleeve and pull when `sound` is on.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The sleeve standing revealed, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the flick, drag, wheel, key or click that revealed a new sleeve.

props.name: pulled / defaultPulled
props.description: The revealed record pulled out and turning, controlled or initial.

props.name: onPulledChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, click or key that pulled the record or put it back.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How steeply you look down into the crate, degrees.

props.name: crateDepth

props.name: spin

props.name: tipAngle

props.name: woodTone
props.description: The crate's wood.

props.name: wheel

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the paper of the sleeves. Off unless asked for.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the frame, px.

props.name: label

props.name: disabled

usageNotes: Keyboard: the crate is one focusable group — Down/Right flip forward, Up/Left back, Home/End to the ends, Enter or Space pull or put back, Escape puts back; the revealed record and the pull are announced politely, and the plate under the crate prints the title and artist.
Reduced motion: the stack re-poses at once, the record and plate cross-fade in, and the record does not turn.

Performance: the flip and pull are motion values; the spin runs on a requestAnimationFrame loop only while a record is out, the crate is on screen and the tab is visible, spinning down and stopping otherwise.
Sound: sleeves rustle as paper only after the visitor has clicked or pressed a key on the page — a wheel or scroll never starts audio.

items.title: Yearbook Grid
items.tagline: Faces in a grid that open their row and column.
items.description: A yearbook page of drawn portraits where the face under the pointer or keyboard focus grows by widening its whole column and deepening its whole row: the grid's tracks are fractions driven by where the focus is — two motion values gliding cell to cell on springs.glide — and how open it is, so the page flexes like a table and every line stays in register instead of one picture bulging like a lens. Portraits are anchored at the foot, so a wider cell shows more shoulder and a taller one more room above the head, and where the open row and column cross the name and role print in left to right with a rule drawn under them. It is a real grid: arrow keys move cell by cell, Home and End go to the row's ends (Ctrl for the first and last), and Enter, Space or a click pins someone open.

props.description: The people, in reading order: { name, role, src?, alt?, art? }.

props.name: value / defaultValue

props.name: onValueChange

props.name: onFocusChange

props.name: gap

props.name: grain

props.name: columns
props.description: A fixed number of columns; by default chosen from the width so the grid fits `maxHeight` with the fewest empty places.

props.name: ratio
props.description: Portrait width over height.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: The tallest the grid may be, px; more columns are used to stay under it.

props.name: ink

props.name: paper

props.name: captionHeight

props.name: label

props.name: disabled

usageNotes: Keyboard: role=grid with rows and gridcells and a roving tab stop — arrows move cell by cell, Home/End to the row's ends, Ctrl+Home/End to the first and last, Enter or Space pin and unpin (aria-selected); each cell is named "Name, Role" and pins are announced politely.
Reduced motion: the tracks change at once and the caption fades in without the wipe; the open cell still opens, because which one is open is information.

Performance: three motion values compose two grid-template strings — one style write per frame while a spring runs, nothing at rest; the grain is a static data-URI tile and the column count comes from a ResizeObserver.
Empty places at the end of the last row read "Not pictured"; pass `columns` to fix the count, or `src` per person for real photographs (cropped from the top quarter).

items.title: Shutter Spill
items.tagline: A burst of frames spills across a light table.
items.description: A camera on a light table fires a burst of contact prints at `cadence` frames a second: each shot blinks the lens, throws a flash across the table, and sends a print out white, developing as it travels a loose spiral on springs.glide to a seeded resting place on a golden-angle spiral, where its angle lands on springs.snap. A click lifts a print into the middle on springs.glide while the others shuffle aside in a cascade, a double click gathers the set back into the lens, and a print slides 1:1 under the finger and coasts by projection. The prints are one roving tab stop: arrows step through them (carrying a held print along), Enter picks up, Escape puts down, Shift with an arrow slides one, and the camera button fires or gathers.

props.type: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string }[]
props.description: The pictures, one print each, up to 24; prints without a src are drawn in code.

props.name: cadence

props.name: flash

props.name: swirl
props.description: How far each print curls round on its way out, in turns, 0 to 1.

props.name: tilt

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The picked-up print, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the click or key that picked a print up or put it down.

props.name: spilled / defaultSpilled
props.description: Whether the prints are out on the table, controlled or initial.

props.name: onSpilledChange
props.description: Fires from the trigger, camera, double click or key that fired or gathered the set.

props.name: trigger
props.description: What fires the first burst: coming into view, mounting, or only the camera.

props.name: light

props.name: frameSize
props.description: A print's width on the table, px.

props.name: numbered
props.description: Print frame numbers in the margins.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the spiral's jitter and the resting angles.

props.name: sound

props.name: label

props.name: disabled

usageNotes: Give the parent a height: the table fills it, fits the spiral and the picked print to the box, and clips at its edge.

Keyboard: the prints are one tab stop; arrows step through them, Home and End jump, Enter or Space picks one up, Escape puts it down, Shift with an arrow slides it 12 px; the camera button fires a burst or gathers the set (the double click's keyboard path).

Reduced motion: no travel or bounce; a burst fades the prints in at their places one by one at the same cadence, a pick cross-fades the print into the middle, and a gather fades them out while the counter still counts.

Cost: nothing runs while idle; every motion is an animation started by an event and stopped on interrupt and unmount. One IntersectionObserver serves the inView trigger and is disconnected once it fires.
Sound plays only for bursts a visitor fired (the camera, a key, a double click), never for the automatic first burst.

items.title: Book Spines
items.tagline: Pictures shelved by their spines.
items.description: Pictures shelved as books whose jackets wrap round their spines, so each spine shows a sliver of its picture under a vertical title. Resting on a spine or focusing it tips the book out of the row toward you on springs.snap and turns it on its own axis, a real CSS 3D box, to show the whole picture on its cover on springs.glide, its cover left a few degrees ajar; the neighbours lean into the gap on springs.snap, the lean running down the row. Arrow keys browse and open each book, Home and End jump, Enter holds a book open and Escape puts it back; a shelf wider than its box drags 1:1, rubber-bands and settles on springs.glide.

props.name: items
props.type: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string }[]
props.description: The books, one picture each, up to 40; the caption is the title on the spine and cover.

props.name: spineWidth

props.name: lean

props.name: shelf
props.description: The shelf's finish.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The book held open, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the click or key that held a book open or let it go.

props.name: openOn
props.description: What opens a book under a pointer; focus always opens.

props.name: delay

props.name: tip

props.name: coverRatio

props.name: bookHeight

props.name: titles

usageNotes: Give the parent a height (about 200 to 260 px reads best): books are sized from it, and the open cover is kept inside the box at both ends.
Keyboard: the books are one tab stop; Left/Right (and Up/Down) move along the shelf and open each book as it takes focus, Home and End jump, Enter or Space holds a book open, Escape puts it back.
Reduced motion: nothing tips, turns or leans; a flat cover card fades in above the book instead, and the shelf still drags under the finger without coasting.
Cost: no loop at all; springs run only on open, close and scroll, on two compositor layers per book.
A shelf wider than its box scrolls with a drag, a flick or a horizontal wheel; a vertical wheel is left to the page.

items.title: Lens Turret
items.tagline: Spin the turret; each lens holds a picture.
items.description: A cine camera's lens turret: a machined plate of lenses, each holding a picture in its glass, with the lens in the gate projected large behind it, every picture weighted by how squarely its lens sits in the gate so a spin flickers through them like a projector. A drag turns it 1:1 through a notched detent field and a flick coasts on friction while the lenses smear, then a detent spring whose stiffness and damping come from detentStrength clicks the next lens into the gate carrying the coast's velocity, and the projection racks into focus on a tween. It is a slider: arrow keys turn it one lens at a time on the same detent spring, Home and End go to the first and last lens, and a click on a lens turns it in.

props.name: items
props.type: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string }[]
props.description: The pictures, one per lens; they repeat when there are fewer than lenses.

props.name: lensCount
props.description: How many lenses the turret carries, 3 to 6.

props.name: blur
props.description: How much the lenses smear when the turret spins, 0 to 1.

props.name: detentStrength
props.description: How notchy the drag feels and how firmly a lens clicks into the gate, 0 to 1.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The lens in the gate, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, flick, click or key that brought a new lens to the gate.

props.name: friction
props.description: How soon a flick runs down, 0 (coasts) to 1 (stops short).

props.name: finish
props.description: The turret's metal.

props.name: focalLengths
props.description: Focal lengths engraved on the barrels, in millimetres.

props.name: focusRack
props.description: Rack the projection into focus after each landing.

props.name: caption
props.description: Show the projected picture's caption.

props.name: turretSize
props.description: The turret's diameter, px.

props.name: sound
props.description: Detent clicks as lenses pass and land, after a visitor's action.

props.name: label
props.description: The turret's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No turning.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the piece; it fills its parent by default (h-full w-full).

usageNotes: Give the parent a height: the projection fills the box and the turret is fitted to its foot by width and height.
Keyboard: the turret is a slider; Right/Up turn the next lens into the gate, Left/Down the previous, Home and End the first and last; the value text names the lens, its focal length and its picture.
Reduced motion: the turret jumps lens to lens and the projection cross-fades; a drag still turns it under the finger and lands on the nearest lens without coasting or ghosts.

Cost: no idle loop; rotation is one motion value read by the lenses, their two ghosts and the projection layers (transform and opacity only); a flick's run-down is a short rAF loop that hands over to a spring.
Sound: detent ticks as lenses pass the gate and a firmer one as a lens seats, only for a visitor's drag, flick, click or key.

items.title: Bokeh Orbit
items.tagline: An orbit of pictures, in focus where you point.
items.description: Pictures ride a slow elliptical orbit seen from a little above, through a thin-lens model: each picture's circle of confusion is the aperture times its distance from the focal plane, so the picture at the plane is crisp and the rest melt, their lights blooming into soft-rimmed bokeh discs that grow with the blur. The pointer's height racks the focal plane on springs.glide, read off a distance scale, and a click spins the orbit open on springs.snap with the phase kicked on springs.drift before it draws back in on springs.drift. The scale is a vertical slider: arrows rack the focus, Page keys in larger steps, Home is infinity and End the nearest, Enter or Space spins the orbit open.

props.name: items
props.type: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string }[]
props.description: The pictures on the orbit, up to 16.

props.name: aperture

props.name: radius
props.description: The orbit's size in the box, 0.4 to 1.

props.name: spin

props.name: focus / defaultFocus
props.description: The focal plane, 0 (far) to 1 (near), controlled or initial.

props.name: onFocusChange

props.name: followPointer

props.name: tilt

props.name: highlights

props.name: bloom

props.name: pictureSize

props.name: scale

props.name: paused

props.name: label

props.name: disabled

usageNotes: Give the parent a height and a surface: the orbit is fitted to the box with room for the open radius, and reads best on a card or a dark panel.
Keyboard: the distance scale is a vertical slider; Up/Right rack farther, Down/Left nearer, Page Up/Down in larger steps, Home to infinity, End to the nearest; Enter or Space spins the orbit open.
Reduced motion: the orbit holds still and never travels; focus is still information, so it follows the pointer and the keys at once, and a click racks it to the picture under it.
Cost: one rAF loop runs only while the orbit turns, on screen and in a visible tab; blur is quantised to quarter pixels so an unchanged value does not repaint; no canvas.
The pictures are a list of labelled images; the bokeh discs are decoration and hidden from assistive technology.

items.title: Seedhead Gallery
items.tagline: Pictures set like seeds in a sunflower.
items.description: Pictures set on the golden-angle spiral of a seed head: each seed keeps the angle it was born at while its distance grows with its age, so the core is dense and tiny and the rim roomy and large, every tile sized by the area its ring gives it. The emerged count is one motion value on springs.drift: as it rises new pictures emerge at the centre and push the rest outward along their rays, driven by the growth prop and by scrolling the page past the head; hover or focus enlarges a seed in place on springs.snap with its caption, and changing the angle re-spirals the head on springs.glide. The seeds are one roving tab stop: arrows walk the spiral, Home and End jump to the rim and the core, plus and minus grow and shrink it, Enter holds a seed and Escape lets it go.

props.name: items
props.type: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string }[]
props.description: The pictures, oldest first: the first sits at the rim, the newest at the core, up to 233.

props.name: angle
props.description: The divergence between one seed and the next, degrees; 137.5 is the golden angle.

props.name: growth
props.description: How much of the head has emerged at rest, 0.1 to 1.

props.name: scale

props.name: scrollGrowth

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The enlarged seed held by a click or Enter, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange

props.name: zoom
props.description: How large a hovered or focused seed grows, px.

props.name: spread

props.name: captions
props.description: Show a caption beside the enlarged seed.

props.name: trigger
props.description: What starts the first growth: coming into view, or mounting.

props.name: label

props.name: disabled

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the piece; it fills its parent by default (h-full w-full).

usageNotes: Give the parent a height: the head is fitted to the shorter side, and an enlarged seed near the rim is drawn inward so it stays inside the box.

Keyboard: the emerged seeds are one tab stop; Right/Down walk the spiral inward, Left/Up outward, Home goes to the rim and End to the newest seed; + and - grow and shrink the head by 8 seeds (the scroll's keyboard path); Enter holds a seed and Escape lets it go.
Reduced motion: the head is shown fully grown and still, scroll does not move it, and angle, growth and enlargement change at once.
Cost: no idle loop; the emerged count and the angle are motion values whose springs run only on a change; the scroll listener is passive and reads the box only while it is on screen.
Unemerged seeds are inert and hidden from assistive technology, so the tab order and the counts always match what is drawn.

items.title: Gate Rings
items.tagline: Nested rings that line up to let light through.
items.description: A small gyroscope of nested polished rings round a glowing core, drawn in Canvas 2D with real 3D: each ring tumbles about its own axle and is cut with a single gap at the axle's end, so when the axles line up the gaps sit one behind another and the core's beam passes clean out through them, whatever the tilts. A drag tumbles the rings 1:1 and its release throws each its own share; they coast on friction and, as they slow, a field draws axles and tilts home so the light flickers through and steadies as each ring locks with a detent, while a click swings them flat into one concentric halo on the springs.snap constants in a cascade. The control is a switch: Enter swings the halo in and out, Space spins the rings, Escape brakes a spin.

usageNotes: Give the parent a size: the rings are fitted to its shorter side and the beam runs from the core to the box's edge.
Keyboard: the control is a switch whose checked state is the flat halo; Enter swings it, Space spins the rings, Escape brakes a spin; a click swings and a drag spins.

Reduced motion: nothing tumbles or coasts; Space and a drag's release set a new still pose at once and Enter swaps between gyroscope and halo in one frame, and the beam still shows whenever the gaps are in line.

Cost: the rAF loop runs only while a ring moves, on screen and in a visible tab, and stops once they settle; segment geometry lives in preallocated typed arrays sorted in place, colours are made once per finish, gradients are cached per size, and the canvas caps its pixel ratio at dpr.
The server renders a still SVG of the rest pose with the beam, replaced by the canvas on its first frame.

items.title: Pause Bloom
items.tagline: Rest the cursor and colour blooms beneath it.
items.description: A sheet of wet watercolour paper behind your content that the cursor paints only when it stops: rest the pointer and a drop of pigment falls at its tip and blooms into the paper as a stack of fractal-edged translucent layers, growing on a critically damped curve (the drift spring's character, stretched to growTime) that is quick at first and slows as the paper drinks it. Move on and the bloom coasts to a stop and dries where it lies — a tide line gathers at its rim and the pigment granulates into the paper's tooth — the next rest takes the next pigment, overlapping blooms mingle, and the paper slowly dries clean. Touch blooms on a long press; with the keyboard, arrows move the brush, Space or Enter held lets a drop bloom and Delete blots the paper.

usageNotes: Keyboard: a transparent button behind the content is the paper's one tab stop. Arrow keys move the brush (Shift for longer steps), Space or Enter held lets a drop fall and bloom until you let go, Delete or Backspace blots the paper clean. A polite status says which pigment is blooming, and "Paper dry." once the visitor's painting has dried away.

Pointer and touch: only a rest paints, so the page scrolls and clicks as usual; on touch a long press (longPress) blooms and any drift past a few pixels cancels it. Rests over links, buttons and fields inside the children never drop pigment, and the painted layer never takes a click.
Under reduced motion no drop falls and nothing grows: a rest lays a dried bloom at its full size by a short crossfade, and drying clean is an opacity fade.

Canvas 2D with the device pixel ratio capped at 2: the loop runs only while a drop falls, a bloom grows or dries, or the paper is drying clean (at twenty frames a second), and stops on its own once the paper is clean, off screen or in a hidden tab. Dried blooms are baked to their own small canvas once.

Pigments are pigment colours at a fixed lightness from the token hues (light-dark keeps them readable on both themes); light paper multiplies them like paint, dark paper screens them, chosen from the paper's resolved lightness and re-read on theme change.

items.title: Bevel Gauge
items.tagline: A cursor that measures angles as you drag.
items.description: A cursor that measures angles: it carries a sliding bevel, and a press and drag slides the stock out from the press point on springs.flick while the blade opens 1:1 under the pointer and a protractor fans out between them with graduations ticking in and a live readout. Near a detent the blade catches it on springs.snap with the drag's own angular speed and a tick, letting go back to the finger on flick when pulled past; release and the bevel lifts away leaving an angular dimension whose label lands on springs.recoil. The surface is a real slider from 0 to 180 degrees — arrows turn the arm a degree, Shift a tenth, Page Up and Page Down jump detents — reading degrees, roof pitch in 12, radians or gradians.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The measured angle in degrees, 0 to 180: controlled, or drawn at first when uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drag or the key that changed the angle, with the new angle in degrees.

props.name: onMeasure
props.description: Fires when a measurement is set down: the pointer lifts, or a key turns the arm.

props.name: snapAngle
props.description: The detent spacing in degrees; 0 turns snapping off.

props.name: snapTolerance
props.description: How close to a detent the blade must come to catch it, degrees.

props.name: scale
props.description: The graduations and the readout: degrees, roof pitch in 12, radians or gradians.

props.name: ink
props.description: The ink the dimension and the protractor are drawn in: a named ink or any CSS colour.

props.name: precision
props.description: Decimals in the readout (radians add two).

props.name: radius
props.description: The protractor's radius, px; three quarters of it on a small box.

props.name: reach
props.description: The longest the blade opens, px.

props.name: graduations
props.description: Tick marks and numbers on the protractor.

props.name: pivot
props.description: Where the bevel sits before the first press, as fractions of the box.

props.name: children
props.description: What is being measured: a plan, a drawing, a photograph. Drawn under the gauge.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Pressing and dragging measures.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing measures and the keys do nothing.

props.name: sound
props.description: A tick as the blade catches each detent. Off unless asked for.

props.name: label
props.description: The gauge's accessible name.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the measuring surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the surface is one role="slider" from 0 to 180 with the reading as aria-valuetext in the chosen scale ("6.9 in 12 pitch"). Right and Up open the arm a degree, Left and Down close it, Shift fine-tunes by a tenth, Page Up and Page Down jump to the next detent, Home and End go to 0 and 180; each key sets the dimension down and reports onMeasure.

Pointer and touch: press where the angle's vertex is and drag along the second line; the box is touch-action: none while interactive, so pass interactive={false} where the page must scroll through it. A tap moves the dimension to the tap and keeps its angle. Children are drawn under the gauge and do not take the pointer.
Values reported through onValueChange and onMeasure are rounded to the readout's precision, so a host never sees 29.999; a controlled value turns the arm there on the snap spring.

Under reduced motion nothing springs: the stock and protractor appear by a short fade, the blade follows the pointer, a detent jumps exactly (the tick and the lit mark remain), and the dimension appears without its sweep or the label's landing.

Pure SVG with every coordinate rounded; the geometry lives in motion values and repaints once per frame only while something moves, so an idle gauge costs nothing. The label halo uses the card colour, so place it on bg-card or set the surrounding surface to match.

items.title: Bead Fountain
items.tagline: A chain of beads that pours after your cursor.
items.description: A long ball chain coiled in a glazed pot, its tagged end over the rim: the pointer is the hand, catching the end on a 120 ms ease and then holding it 1:1, and as you pull away the chain pours out after it and lifts into an arc above the rim — the pile kicks every leaving bead upward at a share of the pay-out speed, so the faster the pull, the higher the fountain. Click, lift a finger or leave and the chain is thrown with the hand's own speed, falls and heaps on the floor bead against bead, then the pot winds it back in over the rim, slowing for the last beads so the tag comes home. Position-based physics at 120 Hz with the rim as a pulley; arrow keys carry the end and pour it, Space or Enter takes it or lets it go, Escape lets go.

props.name: beadSize
props.description: Each bead's diameter, px (3 to 10).

props.name: length
props.description: How many beads the chain has (20 to 400).

props.name: finish
props.description: The metal: brushed steel, brass, copper or black nickel.

props.name: gravity
props.description: Gravity, as a share of the house pull (0.3 to 2).

props.name: lift
props.description: How hard the pile kicks each bead up as it leaves, as a share of the pull's speed: the fountain's height.

props.name: drag
props.description: Air drag on the beads, 0 (none) to 1 (thick air).

props.name: rewindSpeed
props.description: How fast the pot winds the chain back in, beads a second.

props.name: rewindDelay
props.description: How long the dropped chain lies still before the pot winds it in, ms.

props.name: potPosition
props.description: Where the pot stands, as a fraction of the box's width.

props.name: children
props.description: Content beside the pot: a product line, a heading. The chain passes in front of it.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and keys pull the chain.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The chain rests in its pot and nothing pulls it.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the chain where it is.

props.name: sound
props.description: Ticks as beads run over the rim and as the dropped chain lands. Off unless asked for.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The chain's accessible name, for the keyboard's way in.

props.name: onStateChange
props.description: The chain changed what it is doing: resting in the pot, being pulled, falling, or winding in.

props.name: onPour
props.description: How many beads are out of the pot, at most ten times a second.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: a transparent button behind the content is the chain's one tab stop. Arrow keys take the end (if it is resting) and carry it 24px a press, 72px with Shift, gliding so a held key pours the chain; Space or Enter takes it or lets it go; Escape lets go and is not passed on to the page. A polite status says "Pouring", "Let go" and "Back in the pot" — never per bead.

Pointer and touch: a mouse takes the resting chain as it comes in and a click lets it go; on touch, drag to pull and lift to let go. The box is touch-action: none while interactive, so set interactive={false} (or disabled) where the page must scroll through it.
Under reduced motion there is no fountain kick and no tumbling fall: the chain still follows the hand, and letting go fades it back into its pot.

Canvas 2D with the device pixel ratio capped at 2; typed arrays are allocated only when length or beadSize change. The loop runs while the chain moves, is held, falls or winds, and sleeps at rest, off screen and in a hidden tab.

Finishes and the pot are pigment colours from token hues at fixed lightness, so the metal and the glaze read the same on both themes; content passed as children sits under the chain and stays interactive.

items.title: Leaf Dapple
items.tagline: Sun through leaves, every dapple a tiny sun.
items.description: A plaster wall in the afternoon, dappled with sunlight through a swaying canopy, as a background with your content above it: every dapple is a true pinhole image of the sun, round and soft-edged, sized by how high its gap is in the canopy and stretched as a high sun grazes the wall, so raising eclipse turns all of them into crescents at once — cut from the same side, as each is the same inverted sun — and at 1 into rings. Branches sway together and leaves flutter alone, closing their gaps for a moment, and the pointer is a gust that stirs the leaves along its path, easing out on the drift spring's time scale. One WebGL2 pass; reduced motion holds a still afternoon.

props.name: children
props.description: The content on the wall: a hero line, a heading, a call to action. It stays fully interactive.

props.name: wind
props.description: The breeze, 0 (a still afternoon) to 1 (a gusty one): how far and how fast the leaves sway.

props.name: leafDensity
props.description: How thick the canopy is, 0 (sparse, the wall mostly lit) to 1 (dense, a few bright coins in deep shade).

props.name: eclipse
props.description: How much of the sun the moon covers, 0 to 1; every dapple becomes a crescent, and at 1 a ring.

props.name: sunSize
props.description: A typical dapple's diameter, px (10 to 60): how high the canopy is.

props.name: elevation
props.description: The sun's height above the horizon, degrees (0 to 75); a high sun grazes the wall and stretches every dapple.

props.name: azimuth
props.description: Which way the stretched dapples lean, degrees from vertical.

props.name: warmth
props.description: How golden the light is, 0 (white noon) to 1 (late afternoon).

props.name: plaster
props.description: How much trowel texture and grain the plaster shows, 0 to 1.

props.name: wallColor
props.description: The plaster, any CSS colour.

props.name: sunColor
props.defaultValue: a warm white from the amber token (light-dark)
props.description: The sunlight, any CSS colour.

props.name: shadeColor
props.defaultValue: a muted olive grey on light, a cool near-black on dark (light-dark)
props.description: The shade, any CSS colour: the wall under the canopy's skylight.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer is a gust that stirs the leaves near it.

props.name: pointerStrength
props.description: How strong a pointer gust is, 0 to 1.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the leaves still.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds where the gaps in the canopy fall.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the wall.

usageNotes: The wall is decoration: its canvas and still are aria-hidden and never focusable; children render above it in their own layer and keep every click and focus. Moving focus to a child sends a small gust from it.
Pointer gusts are read from the container, so nothing covers your content; set interactive={false} to keep the breeze to itself.
Under reduced motion it is a still afternoon: one frame, no sway, no flicker, no gusts, redrawn only when a prop such as eclipse changes.

One fullscreen WebGL2 pass (nine lattice cells a pixel) at three quarters of a dense screen's pixels, the device pixel ratio capped at 2. The loop runs only on screen, in a visible tab, unpaused and with wind or a gust to show, at thirty frames a second when only the breeze moves; context loss stops it and a restore rebuilds.

Colours are resolved on the element (light-dark defaults keep a warm plaster wall on light pages and a dusk wall with golden dapples on dark ones) and re-read when the theme changes. Without WebGL2 a seeded still of soft dapples, crescent-cut by eclipse, stays as the designed frame.

items.title: Gold Mend
items.tagline: Break the headline and mend it in gold.
items.description: A headline glazed like a ceramic plate — glaze pooled deeper toward each letter's foot, a glossy band across the top, a thin rim, a short soft shadow — that you break and mend: a click cracks it from that point, seeded cracks running out to the edge in 90 ms with a snap while the pieces shift a hair apart on springs.flick, then gold flows into every crack from the break point, wide enough to fill the gap, and the pieces close on springs.glide as it narrows to a bright seam and a glint runs along it. Seams are drawn only on the glaze and accumulate with every break, so the headline grows richer the more it is broken. The real text stays HTML, selectable and read once; Enter or Space breaks it at the centre.

props.name: text
props.description: The headline.

props.name: as
props.description: The element rendered.

props.name: glaze
props.description: The glaze the letters are fired in.

props.name: goldWidth
props.description: The width of a mended seam, px.

props.name: crackCount
props.description: How many cracks run out from each break (2 to 9).

props.name: branching
props.description: How many side cracks split off the main ones, 0 to 1.

props.name: part
props.description: How far the broken pieces shift apart before the gold closes them, px.

props.name: flowTime
props.description: How long the gold takes to fill the cracks, ms.

props.name: gold
props.description: The gold, any CSS colour.

props.name: shimmer
props.description: A glint runs along the new seams as a mend closes.

props.name: maxBreaks
props.description: Breaks kept; past this the oldest seams are polished away.

props.name: defaultBreaks
props.description: Breaks already mended when it first shows, as [x, y] fractions of the headline's box.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the headline breaks once by itself, to show what it does: when first seen, at mount, or never.

props.name: resetKey
props.description: Any change clears every break and seam.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Clicks and keys break the headline.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing breaks.

props.name: sound
props.description: A snap as each break cracks. Off unless asked for.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the crack patterns.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onBreak
props.description: A break cracked: how many breaks there have been.

props.name: onMend
props.description: A break was mended: how many seams the headline now carries.

props.name: className
props.description: Styles the headline: size, weight, tracking and alignment carry through to the glazed letters.

usageNotes: The text is real: the element is your heading with its words as HTML, read once by assistive technology and selectable and copyable; the canvas that draws the glaze and the gold is aria-hidden and mirrors the HTML layout word by word, so wrapping, alignment and font come from your CSS.

Keyboard: when interactive the heading is one tab stop; Enter or Space breaks it at the centre (later breaks spiral round the centre). A polite status says "Mended. 3 seams." as each mend settles, never per frame. A click that ends a text selection does not break it.
Under reduced motion nothing parts or flows: the crack and its gold arrive together by a 240 ms crossfade, and seams still accumulate.

Canvas 2D with the device pixel ratio capped at 2; the loop runs only for the second and a half a break takes and stops, and a break that lands off screen or in a hidden tab is mended at once. The plate is rebaked on resize, on font load and on theme change.
Glazes and gold are pigment colours from token hues at fixed lightness, so the plate looks the same on both themes; the server renders the same glaze as a CSS gradient on the text.

items.title: Light Wand
items.tagline: Paint with light while the shutter is open.
items.description: A dark room with your content in it and the cursor a light wand: moving it paints a glowing tube whose colour walks through the palette along its length, a hot core in a coloured halo built from additive stamps so crossings over-expose toward white like film, and fast strokes run thinner and hotter. The first movement opens the shutter and a corner readout counts the exposure down while every stroke holds; then the frame blinks once and the light fades from oldest to newest along the stroke's own timeline. Arrow keys move the wand on springs.glide and paint, Enter or Space closes the shutter, and when first seen an unseen hand paints one coiled stroke so the room never opens empty.

props.name: children
props.description: The content standing in the room: a headline, a call to action. It stays fully interactive.

props.name: exposure
props.description: How long the shutter stays open once the wand starts moving, seconds (0.5 to 30).

props.name: palette
props.description: The colours the wand walks through along its stroke.

props.name: colors
props.description: Two to eight CSS colours that replace palette.

props.name: thickness
props.description: The tube's thickness at rest, px.

props.name: colorLength
props.description: How much stroke one walk through the palette takes, px.

props.name: speedThinning
props.description: How much speed thins the tube and burns its core whiter, 0 to 1.

props.name: glow
props.description: How wide the glow round the tube spreads, 0 to 1.

props.name: fadeTime
props.description: How long the light takes to fade from oldest to newest once the shutter closes, ms.

props.name: dwell
props.description: A wand held still burns a brighter spot, as it would on film.

props.name: shutter
props.description: Show the shutter's readout in the corner.

props.name: autoPaint
props.description: When first seen, an unseen hand paints one stroke, so the room never opens empty.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and the keys paint.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing paints and the keyboard's way in is off.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the exposure where it is.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The room's accessible name, for the keyboard's way in.

props.name: onExposureStart
props.description: The shutter opened.

props.name: onExposureEnd
props.description: The shutter closed, with how much light was painted, px of stroke.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the room.

usageNotes: The room is scoped to the dark tokens (it carries the dark class), so it is a dark stage on light and dark pages alike and anything you put in it reads with the dark theme's colours.

Keyboard: a transparent button behind the content is the room's one tab stop. Arrow keys move the wand 20px (60px with Shift) on the glide spring and paint as it goes; Enter or Space closes the shutter. A polite status says "Shutter open." and "Shutter closed." for the visitor's own exposures only — never per frame, and never for the unseen hand.
Pointer and touch: a mouse paints by moving; on touch, drag to paint. The room is touch-action: none while interactive, so set interactive={false} where the page must scroll through it.
Under reduced motion the light still answers the hand, but a closing exposure crossfades out over 400 ms with no blink and no oldest-first wipe, and the unseen hand's stroke simply appears.

Canvas 2D with lighter compositing from pre-rendered tinted sprites; while the shutter is open only new stamps are drawn, full redraws happen only during the fade, and the loop sleeps once the room is dark, off screen or in a hidden tab. Stamps live in typed arrays (8,000 per exposure; a full buffer closes the shutter early). Device pixel ratio capped at 2.

items.title: Plankton Wake
items.tagline: Disturb the dark water and it glows.
items.description: Night water full of bioluminescent plankton behind your content: move the pointer through it and the water you push blooms blue-green along your wake about 70 ms after you pass, then fades back to black over glowDecay, while the hand drags the water so the lit points drift apart into a soft V. Each plankton spends a charge when it flashes, so a second pass is dimmer until it recovers, and a click sends a ring outward that is drawn only by the plankton it reaches as they flash. Arrow keys send a light of its own through the water on the springs.glide constants, stirring the same wake, and Enter or Space sends a ring from it.

props.name: children
props.description: Content laid over the water: a headline, a card, a call to action. It stays fully interactive.

props.name: density

props.name: glowDecay

props.name: hue

props.name: water
props.description: The water's colour, any CSS colour. Dark by design in both themes.

props.name: wakeRadius

props.name: sensitivity
props.description: How readily a slow hand lights the water, 0 to 1; a fast one always does.

props.name: ring
props.description: A click on the water sends a ring of light outward from that point.

props.name: ringSpeed
props.description: How fast a ring travels, px per second.

props.name: ambient
props.description: Life in the still water, 0 to 1: a slow current and the odd lone flash. 0 holds it perfectly still.

props.name: intro
props.description: When it first comes into view, something unseen swims across once and stirs a wake.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer stirs the water.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the water as it is: nothing drifts, glows on or fades.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds where the plankton float and the swimmer's path.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The water's accessible name, for the keyboard's way in.

props.name: onPulse
props.description: A ring was sent, with how many so far.

props.name: onGlowChange
props.description: The water started or stopped glowing from a disturbance.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing stirs and the keyboard's way in is off.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the water.

usageNotes: The water is decoration: its canvas is aria-hidden and takes no clicks, and pointer input is read from the box itself, so every child keeps its own clicks, focus and keys. A click that lands on a child control never sends a ring.

Keyboard: Tab to the water (it is one stop, a transparent button behind your content) and a small light appears; arrow keys send it 24 px (Shift 72 px) on the glide spring and stir a wake along the way, Enter or Space sends a ring from it, and each ring is announced once.
On touch, swipe the water sideways to stir it and tap to send a ring; the box keeps touch-action pan-y, so vertical swipes still scroll the page.

Under reduced motion the water holds a still, softly glowing wake with no drift, push or travelling ring; your hand and the keyboard still light the plankton they pass, and the glow fades back by opacity alone.

Canvas 2D with additive sprites and a quarter-resolution bloom buffer, device pixel ratio capped at 2. The frame loop runs only while something moves or glows (a slow ~20 fps while only drifting) and stops off screen, on a hidden tab, when paused, or when dark and still with ambient 0.
The water stays dark in both themes by design; set water to any CSS colour, and keep content on it light (primary-foreground reads in both).

items.title: Impasto Knife
items.tagline: Smear thick paint with a palette knife.
items.description: A primed board and a palette knife: drag and the knife lays a slab of thick oil paint with a striated swath behind the blade, a ridge squeezed out at each end and a bead pushed ahead that stays as a lump where you lift, all lit per pixel by a low raking light with an oil gloss in one WebGL2 pass. The knife scoops up the wet paint it crosses, mixing in log reflectance so yellow and blue make green, and folds that residue into the next stroke's fresh dollop, so the board builds up like a painting. A double click (or Delete) scrapes the board: an edge sweeps across on the move ease, heaping every row's paint into a banded ridge it carries off and leaving a ghost in the gesso; the drawn knife presses on springs.flick, and arrow keys plus Enter pull strokes without a pointer.

props.name: palette

props.name: colors

props.name: lightAngle

props.name: lightHeight

props.name: gloss

props.name: knifeWidth
props.description: The blade's width, px.

props.name: blend
props.description: How much wet paint the knife scoops up and folds into its load, 0 to 1.

props.name: ground
props.description: The primed board's colour, any CSS colour. A fixed gesso in both themes by default.

props.name: defaultStrokes
props.description: Knife strokes already on the board when it first shows, 0 to 4.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer paints.

props.name: clearKey
props.description: Any change scrapes the board clean.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the first strokes and each stroke's blade marks.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The board's accessible name, for the keyboard's way in.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the knife's scratch on the board. Off unless asked for.

props.name: onStroke

props.name: onClear

props.name: disabled

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: the board is one tab stop. Arrow keys move the drawn knife 16 px (Shift 48 px) and turn it to face that way, Enter or Space pulls a 120 px stroke the way it faces, Delete or Backspace scrapes the board; each stroke and the scrape are announced once.

Pointer and touch: drag to paint (the board is touch-action none, so a finger paints rather than scrolls), tap to press a short slab, double click or double tap to scrape. Inside the board a drawn palette knife replaces the mouse cursor; the system cursor returns on any key and outside the box.

The simulation runs on the CPU over 2 px cells and only while the knife moves; the light is one WebGL2 fragment pass that re-uploads just the cells the knife touched. Nothing draws at rest, and the device pixel ratio is capped at 2.
Without WebGL2, or while a lost context is being restored, the same paint is lit on the CPU and drawn smoothed onto a second canvas, so the board stays fully paintable.
Under reduced motion painting stays 1:1 under the hand, the keyboard pull lands at once and the scrape is a short fade to the clean board instead of a sweeping edge.
Pigments and the gesso are fixed lightnesses of the theme's hues, so the painting looks the same on light and dark pages; pass colors for your own palette.

items.title: Plasma Lamp
items.tagline: Touch the glass and the lightning finds you.
items.description: A desk plasma lamp: a dark glass globe on a pedestal, a hot core and filaments of plasma wandering out to the glass, each a jagged path with a slow meander and a fast crackle that forks near the glass and dips toward or away from you. Put the pointer on the glass, or press it with a finger, and the tendrils nearest that angle swing over on springs.snap and converge onto one shared path, fusing into a single bright braided arc with a flare where it lands; a press gathers two more, and letting go lets them drift back into their wander on springs.drift. The globe is a round toggle button: Enter or Space touches the glass, the arrow keys move the finger round it and in or out, and Escape lets go.

props.description: Seeds where each tendril wanders.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The lamp's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the lamp's hum while the glass is touched. Off unless asked for.

props.name: onTouchChange
props.description: The glass was touched or let go, by pointer, touch or key.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing reaches the glass and the button is disabled.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the lamp; the globe fits the box.

usageNotes: The globe is a real round button with aria-pressed: Enter or Space touches the glass and lets it go again, Left and Right move the finger 15° round the glass (Shift 45°), Up and Down move it in and out, and Escape lets go. A faint ring shows where a keyboard finger will land.

A mouse touches the glass just by resting on it and a press gathers two more tendrils; a finger or pen touches by pressing and can drag round the glass, which is touch-action none so it never scrolls the page.
The hum plays only with sound on, and only from a press, a key, or a hover once the page has had a press; it stops on release, on a hidden tab and on unmount.

Canvas 2D with the glass and pedestal painted once per size; the plasma draws at about 30 fps alone and every frame while touched, and the loop stops off screen, on a hidden tab and when paused. Device pixel ratio is capped at 2.
Under reduced motion the lamp holds one still frame with no wander or crackle; a touch redraws it with the arc already formed at the finger, and letting go redraws the still.
The lamp is an object, so it looks the same on light and dark pages; hue tints everything that glows and the pedestal takes the theme's ink at a fixed lightness.

items.title: Dart Cursor
items.tagline: A paper dart that banks into every turn.
items.description: Inside its box the cursor is a folded paper dart seen from above, nose on the pointer: a small 3D model with dihedral wings and a keel, flat-shaded from an upper-left light, whose shadow falls further and softer the higher it flies. The nose points where it flies on springs.snap, it banks into each turn by the coordinated-turn angle on springs.snap, dips its nose as it slows on springs.glide and rides higher with speed on springs.drift; circle it fast and it loops the loop, and two hairlines from its wingtips trail behind and fade. A lifted finger or a pointer that leaves throws it on to glide, bank away from the edges and land; keyboard focus on a child flies it there along a banked curve, and Enter or Space on that child salutes with a loop.

props.name: children
props.description: The area the dart flies in. Its buttons and links keep every click, focus and key.

props.name: size
props.description: The dart's length, px.

props.name: bank
props.description: How far it rolls into a turn, 0 (flat turns) to 1 (steep, knife-edge rolls).

props.name: trail
props.description: How long its wingtip trails last, seconds; 0 draws none.

props.name: color
props.description: The paper: a named tone from the theme, or any CSS colour.

props.name: loop
props.description: Circle fast and it loops the loop.

props.name: glide
props.description: A lifted finger or a pointer that leaves throws the dart on, to glide and land.

props.name: drag
props.description: How quickly a glide bleeds its speed, 0 (floaty) to 1 (heavy).

props.name: lift
props.description: How high speed carries it, 0 to 1: its shadow falls further below a fast dart.

props.name: restAt
props.description: Where it sits landed before anyone points, as fractions of the box.

props.name: restHeading
props.description: Which way it points while landed, degrees (0 is right, -90 up).

props.name: targets
props.description: Children it flies to when they take keyboard focus, as a CSS selector.

props.name: followFocus
props.description: Keyboard focus on a child flies the dart to it; Enter or Space there loops.

props.name: hideCursor
props.description: Hide the system cursor while the dart leads (never over text fields, never after a key).

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and touch fly the dart.

props.name: onLoop
props.description: It looped the loop.

props.name: onLand
props.description: It touched down after a glide or a flight.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the box.

usageNotes: The dart, its shadow and its trails are aria-hidden and take no pointer events, so every child keeps its own clicks, keys and focus ring. The system cursor is hidden only inside the box, only for mouse and pen, never over inputs, textareas, selects or contenteditable, and it returns on any key press and on leave.

Keyboard: when a child takes keyboard focus the dart flies to it along a banked curve and lands beside it pointing at it, a second focus cue beside the ring; Enter or Space on that child loops the loop.

Touch: the dart follows the finger a little above it so it stays visible, and glides on when the finger lifts. The box keeps touch-action pan-y, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the page (and simply throws the dart).
Under reduced motion the dart follows 1:1 and points where it goes, with no bank, nose dip, altitude, loop or glide; the trails still fade, and keyboard focus places it beside the control at once.

Five SVG polygons rewritten only when the pose changes (rounded to 0.1 px) and one composited transform per frame; the trails are a small canvas with the device pixel ratio capped at 2. The loop runs only while the dart moves, settles, glides, loops or a trail is fading, and stops off screen and on a hidden tab.

items.title: Magpie Cursor
items.tagline: A cursor that collects the labels you pass.
items.description: A cursor that collects: point at anything marked data-magpie and its label lifts off the item as a small paper tag, starting at the item's own box and rising toward you, then flies to the head of a string of tags hanging off the cursor in 3D. Each tag follows the one in front on its own spring with the snap character, softer down the string by lag and further back by depth, tilting with its own speed; pointing at a label already held brings it to the front, and past maxTags the oldest lets go and falls away. A click deals the stack out where you stand in a shallow arc that lands on springs.recoil, holds for a beat so you can read it, then gathers up on springs.glide and clears; keyboard focus collects, Enter or Space drops, and Escape gathers the stack away.

props.name: children
props.description: The area the magpie works in. Mark anything collectable with attribute (default data-magpie).

props.name: depth
props.description: How far apart the tags hang in depth, px: 0 is a flat pile, 60 a long string into the page.

props.name: lag
props.description: How loosely the stack trails the cursor, 0 (tight) to 1 (loose and swinging).

props.name: maxTags
props.description: The most tags it carries, 1 to 8; past that the oldest lets go and falls away.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The collected labels, newest first: controlled, or the labels it starts with.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the hover, focus, click or key that changed the stack, with the new labels.

props.name: attribute
props.description: The attribute that marks a collectable item; its value is the label, or the item's text when empty.

props.name: offset
props.description: Where the stack hangs from the pointer, px.

props.name: spread
props.description: How far the ends of a dropped arc tip, degrees.

props.name: hold
props.description: How long a dropped arc rests before it gathers up, ms.

props.name: dropOnClick
props.description: A click drops the stack where you stand.

props.name: followFocus
props.description: Keyboard focus on a tagged item collects it; Enter or Space there drops the stack.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer collects.

props.name: onPick
props.description: A label was picked up, or brought back to the front.

props.name: onDrop
props.description: The stack was dropped, with the labels it held, newest first.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the box.

usageNotes: Mark collectable items with data-magpie="Label" (or an empty data-magpie to use the item's text). The tags are aria-hidden decoration in a pointer-events none layer, so every item keeps its own role, clicks and focus ring, and the system cursor is never hidden.

Keyboard: focusing a tagged item with the keyboard collects it and the stack hangs off that item; Enter or Space on it drops the stack there; Escape gathers the stack away and is not passed on. Each pick and drop is announced once in a polite live region.
Touch has no hover: a tap on a tagged item collects it and a tap anywhere else drops the stack at that point.
Use value and onValueChange to drive a comparison tray or filter from the collected labels; onDrop hands you the labels at the moment they are laid down.
Under reduced motion the tags appear at their place with a short fade and move 1:1 with the pointer, with no swing, tilt, lift or bounce; the dropped arc appears in place, holds and fades.
