props.name: sync
props.description: How strongly their flashes fall into step with each other, 0 to 1.

props.name: color
props.description: Their light, any CSS colour.

props.name: glow
props.description: How far each one's halo spreads, 0 to 1.

props.name: size
props.description: The radius of a firefly's bright core, px.

props.name: wander
props.description: How much they bob in their spots, 0 to 1.

props.name: backdrop
props.description: A dusk panel behind them, or none to put them on your own dark ground.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When they arrive and light the words.

props.name: once
props.description: Arrive once, or each time the headline comes back into view.

props.name: play
props.description: With trigger "manual": true brings them in.

props.name: delay
props.description: Wait before they arrive, ms.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer, a touch and the keys startle them.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the scene still.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds their spots, rhythms and flights.

props.name: dpr
props.description: The most device pixels per CSS pixel the canvas draws at (never above 2).

props.name: onScatter
props.description: How many are away from their spots, whenever that changes.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: The words are whole again: every firefly is back and lit.

props.name: className
props.description: Size and layout.

usageNotes: Keyboard: a transparent button over the headline — focusing it by keyboard startles the whole line in a wave from the left, and Enter or Space startles it again; touch startles with a tap or a sideways drag.
Reduced motion: the fireflies sit still in their spots at a steady glow with no flashing; a startle blinks the near ones out and relights them in place, one by one.

Performance: one Canvas 2D layer with two pre-drawn sprites; the loop halts off screen, in hidden tabs and when paused, runs at half rate while the word is whole and resting, and stops entirely when nothing flashes or flies. The canvas caps its pixel ratio at dpr (never above 2) and resamples on resize and font load.

Theming: the dusk panel and the light are fixed pigments, the same night in both themes; with backdrop "none", put it on your own dark ground. The headline stays real, selectable text — a faint ghost the fireflies draw over.
The server renders the headline lit as a glowing word, so the first frame is finished before the fireflies arrive on the trigger.

items.title: Break Shot
items.tagline: Letters break like a rack of balls, then re-rack.
items.description: A headline racked as billiard balls on a small carom table, a lacquered ball for every letter with an ivory spot carrying it. The pointer is a cue ball: what it meets it hits as an equal mass would, with the pointer's speed and the force, and the balls run on real physics — elastic collisions, cushions that give back part of the speed, rolling resistance from the cloth — each one rolling so its letter turns over the top and comes back round. After the spread has lain still they are lifted and glide back to their slots along straight lines in reading order, a cascade apart on springs.glide, rolling upright so the letters land facing the reader. A transparent button gives the keyboard Enter or Space to break from the left and Escape to re-rack.

props.name: children / text
props.description: The headline, as children or a prop.

props.name: as
props.description: The element that carries the headline.

props.name: force
props.description: How hard the cue ball hits, as a multiple of a firm shot.

props.name: friction
props.description: How much the cloth slows the balls, 0 (slick, they run and bank) to 1 (heavy nap).

props.name: returnDelay
props.description: How long the spread lies once the last ball stops, before the re-rack, ms.

props.name: bounce
props.description: How lively the cushions are, 0 to 1.

props.name: palette
props.description: Ball colours, cycled along the headline; any CSS colours.

props.name: cloth
props.description: The cloth.

props.name: size
props.description: Ball diameter, em.

props.name: cue
props.description: A faint cue ball rides the pointer over the cloth.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer, a touch and the keys play shots.

props.name: sound
props.description: Clacks for the shots the visitor plays.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Racked and still: nothing plays.

props.name: onBreak
props.description: A shot scattered the rack.

props.name: onRack
props.description: Every ball is back in the rack.

props.name: className
props.description: Size: the table is drawn in em.

usageNotes: Keyboard: a transparent button over the table — Enter or Space breaks from the left with a cue ball off the cushion, Escape re-racks at once; a tap on the cloth shoots a cue ball from the tap at the nearest ball, and on touch a sideways sweep strikes.
Reduced motion: nothing travels or rolls — a shot is played out at once and the balls cross-fade from the rack to where they would have stopped, then cross-fade back into the rack after the delay.
Performance: one loop plays every ball at 240 Hz sub-steps and stops when the table is at rest; it halts off screen and in hidden tabs, and the rack is measured only on resize and font load.
The rack is laid out by CSS, so the server's first frame is the finished headline; the words are read once from an sr-only copy and the balls are aria-hidden.
Theming: the table, cloth and balls are fixed pigments, the same in both themes; pass palette for your own ball colours.
Sound: with sound on, ball-on-ball and cushion clacks answer the visitor's shots, louder for harder hits; it stays silent until the page has had a click, tap or key press.

items.title: Crease Swap
items.tagline: Letters fold corner to corner to show the other word.
items.description: A word in squares of origami paper, white with the letter in ink on the front and coloured with the other word's letter on the back. Hover and the squares fold over one after another from the side you came in: the near corner lifts and travels over the diagonal crease to the far corner, the leading triangle rising on springs.snap and the trailing one following on springs.glide a beat behind, so the paper creases into a V along the diagonal before it lands coloured side up and the row reads the other word; every face is shaded from its own angle and a folded square keeps a faint crease. It is a toggle button: a press latches the back word, keyboard focus folds it like a hover, and Enter or Space toggles it.

props.name: back

props.name: as
props.description: The element that carries the words.

usageNotes: Keyboard: a transparent toggle button over the word — keyboard focus folds it like a hover, Enter or Space latches or releases the back word, and aria-pressed says which; the word showing is read once from an sr-only copy.
Reduced motion: no square turns — each cross-fades from its front to its back (and back) on an opacity tween in the same staggered order, so the swap still reads.
Performance: one loop turns every square and stops when they rest; it halts off screen and in hidden tabs. Each square is two triangles with shading and the crease driven by a few CSS variables.
Words of different lengths are centred on the squares; a place where both words have a space is a gap the row can wrap at, so words never break.
Theming: the paper is a fixed pigment that reads the same in both themes; choose the coloured side with paperTone.
Sound: with sound on, a soft crinkle answers each square the visitor turns; it stays silent until the page has had a click, tap or key press.

items.title: Capillary Cursor
items.tagline: A drop of ink that fills whatever it touches.
items.description: Inside its own box the pointer is a single drop of ink, exactly at the pointer and drawn out a little along fast travel. Touch a button, link or field and the ink wicks along the control's real outline — its border box and its own four corner radii — from the point of contact in both directions, the fronts slowing as capillary flow does, then seeps inward from the wet edge at low strength until the control is filled in its exact shape, while the drop shrinks by the ink it gave; the drop's size eases on a rate as quick as springs.flick and the flood on a glide-like ease. Leave and the flood recedes and the outline drains back toward the exit point through a thread of ink that thins as it pulls and pinches off past its reach, and the drop swells again. Keyboard focus moves the ink from one control to the next, and the system cursor returns over text fields and on any key.

props.name: inkColor

props.name: wickSpeed

props.name: dotSize

props.name: strength

props.name: lineWidth

props.name: flood

props.name: stretch
props.description: How far the drop draws out when it moves fast, 0 to 1.

props.name: cling
props.description: How far the draining thread stretches before it lets go, 0 to 1.

props.name: targets

props.name: hideCursor

props.name: followFocus

props.name: interactive

props.name: onTargetChange

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: focus moves the ink — the focused control wicks from the side nearest the last one and the last drains toward it; any key press hands the pointer back its own cursor, and nothing new enters the tab order.
Touch: there is no hover on glass, so a tap inks the tapped control from the tap point and the ink stays until the next tap.
Reduced motion: the drop follows the pointer 1:1 at a constant size with no stretch, and a touched control's outline and flood fade in and out whole — no wicking, no thread.

Performance: one loop runs only while ink is moving or the drop is changing; it halts off screen and in hidden tabs. Outlines are measured only for live stains (at most four), and the painted SVG layer never takes a click.
Theming: the named inks are pigments that read in both themes (iron follows the theme's ink); pass any CSS colour or token. Mark custom targets with data-ink.

items.title: Margin Pencil
items.tagline: A paragraph marked up by a careful reader.
items.description: A paragraph of real text and a careful reader with a coloured pencil: when it comes into view the pencil marks it up mark by mark — an underline, a loop that overshoots its own start, a bracket in the gutter with a note, a phrase struck through — each built from the phrase's real line fragments so it sits on the words wherever they wrap. Every stroke is a ribbon whose width follows the hand's pressure, with a seeded wobble, and the pen travels it on a minimum-jerk profile timed from its length, lifting between strokes, while a small pencil rides the tip; notes are written line by line in a margin column, or as numbered footnotes when the container is narrow. Hovering a phrase brings its mark and note up on a short tween; there is nothing to operate, so the keyboard reads the marks and notes in place from sr-only annotations.

props.name: marks

props.name: wobble

usageNotes: Accessibility: the paragraph stays real, selectable text; each marked phrase is followed by an sr-only annotation such as “(circled; note: really every?)”, so marks and notes are read once, in place, and the drawn SVG, margin notes and footnotes are aria-hidden.
Reduced motion: the marks and notes are shown already drawn — the finished page — with no pencil and no sound.

Layout: a container query puts notes in a 7.5rem margin column from 30rem wide and turns them into numbered footnotes below it; strokes are rebuilt from the layout on resize and font load, so they always sit on the words.
Performance: one loop draws only while a run is under way, rebuilding just the stroke being drawn; it halts off screen and in hidden tabs and stops when the last mark is down.

Sound: with sound on, a pencil scratch follows the pen's pressure and speed — only for a run the visitor started (a manual play set from a click or key), never for one that starts on scrolling into view.
Theming: the named pencils are pigments that read on either theme (graphite follows the theme's ink); pass any CSS colour or token.

items.title: Night Side
items.tagline: A turning world with day sweeping over its lights.
items.description: An invented world as a dotted globe on Canvas 2D: seeded continents, a body shaded per pixel with a soft terminator and a warm twilight band, and city lights glowing on the dark half. Change the hour and the day sweeps round on springs.drift while each city switches on with its own flicker as night reaches it; routes between offices rise as arcs on springs.glide the first time the globe is seen, then pulses of light ride them and ring out on arrival. Drag turns it 1:1 and tips it with a rubber band, a throw coasts, a click brings an office round on glide; arrow keys turn and tip, Page Up and Page Down step through the offices, Home faces one and Escape lets it turn again.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the globe is one tab stop. Left and Right turn it, Up and Down tip it, Page Up and Page Down bring each office round and select it, Home faces the selected office, Escape clears the selection. A polite live region speaks the selected office's local time and daylight.

Reduced motion: nothing turns, coasts or flickers on its own; the arcs are drawn whole with a still glow, lights are simply on or off, a new hour moves the terminator at once and keys turn in instant steps.

Performance: one requestAnimationFrame loop that runs only while the globe is on screen, the page is visible and something moves; `paused` stops it. The backing store is capped at device pixel ratio 2, dots and cities are typed arrays laid out once, and every ink string is built when the theme is read, not per frame.

Theming: the day body, land and routes come from tokens; the night body and the lights are pigments at fixed lightness, so the dark half stays dark and the lights glow in both themes. Theme switches are picked up through colour carriers, with no page-level observers.
Use `nightSideReading(point, timeOfDay, season)` to print the same local time and daylight the globe shows, for a status line or a list beside it.

items.title: Turnstile Cards
items.tagline: Push the wings round to bring the next card.
items.description: Cards mounted on the glass wings of a turnstile seen from slightly above, in real CSS perspective: the wing facing you is square to the eye while the others recede behind the post and swing round in front, each shaded by its angle, a sheen sliding across its glass and its shadow turning on the floor. A push follows the hand along the arc it grabbed, and on release a fixed-step integrator carries it — inertia, friction and a soft cam detent at every wing with a damper that bites only when slow — so a gentle push settles on the next wing and a hard one spins through several before one is caught square; the landing is predicted at release and reported from the gesture. Arrow keys turn one wing on springs.snap, a click on another wing brings it round on springs.glide, and Home and End go to the first and last card.

props.name: onValueChange

props.name: glass

props.name: tilt

props.name: floor

usageNotes: Keyboard: the stage is one tab stop. Left and Right turn one wing at a time, Home and End go to the first and last card the short way round; the card is spoken politely once it is chosen. Each wing face is a labelled slide, and wings not facing you are hidden from assistive technology and inert.
Reduced motion: a drag still turns the turnstile under the hand, but every landing is an instant swap with a short dip in opacity instead of a coast, and the sheen holds still.

Performance: nothing runs at rest. One requestAnimationFrame loop integrates the turn only while it moves and only while the turnstile is on screen; every wing's angle, shade and sheen derive from one motion value, and React re-renders only when a wing behind the post picks up its next card.
Layout follows the stage by container query units, so the first server-rendered frame is already composed at any width; wings that swing past the edges are clipped by the stage.
Controlled use: a host that refuses the new card gets its own card turned back into place when the turnstile comes to rest.

items.title: Wrap Wall
items.tagline: An endless wall of pictures you throw anywhere.
items.description: An endless wall of pictures in staggered columns that wraps in every direction. Drag it anywhere and it follows 1:1; throw it and it coasts by friction, leaning with its speed. Every column trails the hand on its own spring — between springs.snap beside the column you hold and springs.drift far from it — so the wall bends round your hand and ripples straight as it slows. Enter or a click opens the picture nearest the centre, growing from its tile to fill the frame on springs.glide while the wall dims; Escape shrinks it home. Arrow keys pan a column or a row on glide, Page Up and Page Down a screen, Home returns to the start.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the wall is one tab stop. Arrows pan a column or a row, Page Up and Page Down a screen, Home returns to the start, and Enter or Space opens the picture nearest the centre, which is outlined while the wall has keyboard focus. The open picture is a modal dialog: focus moves to Close, Tab stays there, Escape closes and focus returns to the wall.

Reduced motion: the wall still pans 1:1 under the hand, but there is no coast, lean or ripple, keys jump straight to their place and a picture fades in where it opens instead of growing from its tile.

Performance: only the columns in view are rendered, and React re-renders only when one enters or leaves; per-frame positions are written straight to transforms by one loop that runs only while the wall moves and is on screen.

The first frame is laid out in CSS with container query units, so it is composed and full at any width before the wall is measured. Screen readers also get a list of every picture with a button to open it.
Pictures passed as `src` should be the size of a tile or larger; they are covered, not stretched, and the drawn defaults use tokens so the wall reads in both themes.

items.title: Band Compare
items.tagline: Several versions side by side, seams you drag.
items.description: Several versions of one picture side by side as bands across a single frame, in register, each labelled at its top. Drag any seam and it follows 1:1 while only the two bands either side give way, rubber-banding against a neighbour and landing on springs.glide with the release velocity; the grip lifts on springs.flick. Double-click a band or press its label and it widens to fill the frame as the seams sweep outward on glide, nearest first, and again sweeps them back to the shares they had. Seams are separators: Tab moves between them, arrows move them (Shift for larger steps), Home and End go to their limits, number keys widen a band and Escape shares it back.

Each seam is a vertical separator with its value, limits and both bands' shares in its value text; arrows move it, Shift moves it five times as far, Home and End go to its limits. Labels are toggle buttons that widen their band, number keys do the same from anywhere inside, Escape shares the frame back, and a seam that hides while focused hands focus to the widened label.
Reduced motion: seams jump to their places and a widened band fades in with no sweep; a drag still follows the hand and the grip does not lift.
Performance: there is no loop. Each seam is one motion value; every clip path, label position and shade derives from them, so dragging re-renders nothing.
Versions can be separate pictures (`src` per item) or one shared picture with a CSS `filter` per item; filters apply to the picture only, so labels and seams stay crisp.
Theming: seams, grips and labels use card, background and hairline tokens with a hairline ring, so they read over light and dark pictures in both themes.

items.title: Sand Furrow
items.tagline: Plough through sand to find the picture beneath.
items.description: A picture buried under fine sand, the sand a heightfield simulated on a coarse grid and shaded per pixel in WebGL2 — directional light, grain, glints, short shadows cast into the furrow and damp edges where it thins. Drag to plough: a bowl-shaped plough cuts down toward the picture and heaps what it cuts onto a bank on each side, the banks round off at their angle of repose, and about a second later they slump back in at the settle pace until the sand lies smooth and the loop stops. Double-click, Enter or Space sweeps the tray clear with a broom front that carries a ridge off the edge; Backspace pours the sand back in; arrow keys plough from a marker.

props.name: light

props.name: sandColor

props.name: cleared / defaultCleared

props.name: onClearedChange

props.name: onPlough

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the tray is one tab stop and shows a plough marker on keyboard focus. Arrows plough from the marker, drawing the furrow along the move (Shift ploughs further); Enter or Space sweeps the sand clear and Backspace pours it back. A polite live region says how much is uncovered after each stroke, when it is covered again and when it is swept.
Reduced motion: ploughing still cuts, but nothing slumps on its own; after a pause set by `settle` the sand fades back smooth, and sweeping and pouring are cross-fades.

Performance: one WebGL2 pass. The heightfield is simulated in JavaScript on a 3 px grid and uploaded only on frames where it changed; the loop runs only while ploughing, sweeping, pouring or slumping, only on screen and with the page visible, and stops once the sand is still. Device pixel ratio is capped at 2, context loss is handled, and everything is released on unmount.
Without WebGL2 (or with a picture from another origin that cannot be read) a drawn still shows the picture under sand with one shaded furrow, and the sweep cross-fades it away.

Sound plays only when `sound` is on, only for the visitor's own strokes and keys: a swish every stretch of ploughing, pitched by speed and panned by position, and a longer one for the sweep and the pour.

items.title: Sweep Studio
items.tagline: Your screen on a phone turning in a studio.
items.description: A product shot you can handle: a phone standing on a turntable on a seamless studio sweep under a light rig, its screen real content. The phone is a CSS 3D body — screen face, back plate in its finish with a camera island, and an edge band of strips that rounds every corner — every face shaded from one turn value, with rim light flashing along the edges as they pass the lamps, a highlight sliding across the glass, a contact shadow turning on the plate and a mirrored copy in the glossy floor. Drag turns it 1:1, all the way round; released, the throw is projected and it eases back to face you at the nearest copy of its rest pose on springs.drift with the release velocity. The plate is a slider: arrow keys turn it 30° on springs.snap and it eases home after a hold; Home faces it, End shows the back.

props.description: What the screen shows; real content that stays readable while it faces you. Defaults to a transit app.

props.name: lightRig
props.description: The lights: a big softbox, two rim strips, a top spot, or window light.

props.name: angle
props.description: The pose it rests in, degrees; 0 is square on.

props.name: finish
props.description: The body's finish.

props.name: autoTurn
props.description: Degrees per second of a slow showcase turn; 0 rests in the pose.

props.name: hold
props.description: How long it holds a pose turned by the keys before easing back, ms.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far above the eye sits, 0 to 20 degrees.

props.name: gloss
props.description: How glossy the floor is: the reflection's strength, 0 to 1.

props.name: perspective
props.description: Distance of the eye from the phone, px.

props.name: colors
props.description: The sweep's colours: { wall, floor }; tokens by default.

props.name: onSideChange
props.description: Fires as a turn brings the front, an edge or the back to face you.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Drag and the keys turn it.

props.name: label
props.description: The studio's accessible name.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the studio; the phone scales to it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the turntable plate is a slider ("Turn the phone") with its angle and the visible side in its value text, and a focus ring round the plate. Left and Right turn it 30°, it eases back to face you after `hold`; Home faces it at once, End shows the back.
Reduced motion: a drag still turns the phone 1:1, but every return to the rest pose is a short cross-fade instead of a swing, keys step instantly, and the showcase turn stays off.

The screen is real DOM: it stays readable and focusable while it faces you and becomes inert and hidden from assistive technology when the back is turned. The reflection renders the same content again, inert and hidden; pass content without side effects, or set `gloss` to 0 to skip the copy.

Performance: nothing runs at rest. One motion value drives every transform; face shading and highlights are written straight to styles from its change events, so a turn re-renders nothing. The showcase turn runs only on screen with the page visible.

Sizing: the phone, the plate and the edge band are laid out with container query units from the studio's box, so the first server-rendered frame is already composed at any size; screen content is set in em against a font size that scales with the phone.

items.title: Drum Plotter
items.tagline: A live line drawn by a stylus on a turning drum.
items.description: A chart recorder whose graph paper is wrapped round a drum turning about a vertical axis, drawn as a real cylinder in Canvas 2D so the squares crowd into shade at both rims while the paper carries the inked trace left, away from a pen on a rail. The pen follows each reading on the snap spring's constants scaled by penResponse, so a step is drawn with one small overshoot; a series change lifts it on flick, glides the carriage to the new level while the ink changes to the next in the rack, and drops it on recoil, where a blot spreads into the paper. Hover reads the value under the pointer as the paper passes; the drum is a slider whose arrow keys move the same readout along the trace (Page Up and Down five seconds, Home the oldest ink, End the pen, Escape to hide it), and the legend is a radio group.

props.name: series
props.type: { id: string; label: string; unit?: string; samples?: number[]; min?: number; max?: number; decimals?: number; ink?: string }[]
props.description: The series the pen can plot; samples play back in a loop when no live reading is given.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The series being plotted, by id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the legend press or key that picked a series.

props.name: reading
props.description: Live mode: the pen follows this reading, in the series' units, instead of its samples.

props.name: sampleRate
props.description: Samples per second when playing a series' samples.

props.name: paperSpeed
props.description: How fast the paper travels across the front of the drum, px per second.

props.name: inkColor
props.description: The first ink in the rack, or any CSS colour; later series take the next inks.

props.name: gridStyle
props.description: The paper: fine graph paper, ruled lines, a dot grid or plain.

props.name: penResponse

props.name: penAt

props.name: lineWidth

props.name: legend

props.name: scale

props.name: paused

props.name: onReadout
props.type: (readout: { series: string; value: number; secondsAgo: number } | null) => void
props.description: Fires when the hovered or keyboard reading changes, and with null when it hides.

props.name: label
props.description: The recorder's accessible name.

props.name: dpr

props.name: disabled
props.description: No legend, hover or keys; the drum keeps plotting.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the recorder; it is 224px tall and full width by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab reaches the legend (a radio group; arrows pick a series) and then the drum, a slider over the history: Left and Right step half a second, Page Up and Page Down five seconds, Home the oldest ink, End the pen, and Escape hides the readout. aria-valuetext reads the series, value and how long ago.

Reduced motion: the drum steps once a second instead of turning, the pen lands on each reading at once and a series change is an instant ink change with a gap; the record still grows and the readouts work the same.

Performance: the frame loop runs only while the drum is on screen, the tab is visible and paused is false; the ink lives in preallocated typed arrays keyed by paper position, the canvas is capped at dpr and resized by ResizeObserver, and history is pre-filled on mount so the paper is never blank.
Live data: pass reading and update it as values arrive (the pen interpolates on its spring); without it, each series' samples play back at sampleRate in a loop.
Theming: ink, paper, grid and metal are pigments from tokens resolved on the element and re-read on a theme change, so the paper reads in both themes.

items.title: Steel Card
items.tagline: A brushed-metal card with a weight you can feel.
items.description: A payment card in brushed metal: the brushing is fractal noise stretched along brushAngle in overlay, and its anisotropic highlight is a long streak across the grain that slides along it and turns with the tilt as the card leans toward the pointer on the glide spring. Flick it and it falls back onto the table under gravity, pivoting on its bottom edge, lands flat with one or two bounces set by bounce and a clink, then rights itself on the glide spring after rightAfter ms. Focus tilts it into a three-quarter pose, arrow keys lean it, Enter or Space drop it and Escape rights it at once.

props.name: name
props.description: The cardholder's name, etched along the bottom.

props.name: number
props.description: The card number, etched in groups of four.

props.name: expiry
props.description: Expiry, as printed.

props.name: issuer
props.description: The issuer's wordmark, top left.

props.name: metal
props.description: The metal; black steel is etched bright.

props.name: brushAngle
props.description: Direction of the brushing, degrees from horizontal.

props.name: edge
props.description: The edge: a polished bevel, a flat cut, a gilt edge or an ink-black one.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far the card tilts toward the pointer, degrees.

props.name: gloss
props.description: Strength of the brushed highlight, 0 to 1.

props.name: bounce
props.description: How much of its speed the card keeps when it hits the table, 0 to 1.

props.name: rightAfter
props.description: How long the card lies on the table before it rights itself, ms.

props.name: mask
props.description: Show only the last four digits.

props.name: chip
props.description: Draw the contact chip.

props.name: contactless
props.description: Draw the contactless mark.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the clink when it lands.

props.name: onDrop
props.description: Fires when a flick, Enter or Space drops the card.

props.name: label
props.defaultValue: issuer, metal, last four and name
props.description: The card's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No tilting, dropping or keys.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the stage; the card is up to 280px wide and centred.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the card is a button. Focus tilts it into a three-quarter pose, the arrow keys lean it, Enter or Space drop it on the table, and Escape stands it straight back up. Its name reads the issuer, metal, last four digits and the holder.

Reduced motion: the card never tilts or falls. The highlight still follows the pointer and focus, because the light is the material, and a drop is a sweep of light with the clink and the same announcements.
Performance: nothing runs at rest. Tilt and drag are motion values; the fall runs its own short integrator only while falling. The brushing is a static SVG filter rasterised once on its own layer.
Sound is off by default; with sound on, the clink plays only for a drop the visitor made, louder for a harder landing, with a quieter tick on the second bounce.
Etched text is real text inside the button, so it scales with the card (container units) from 238px on a phone plate to 280px.

items.title: Table Spinner
items.tagline: Pictures laid on a turntable you spin by hand.
items.description: Pictures lie flat on a round wooden turntable seen at an angle, built in CSS 3D. A drag turns the plate 1:1 under the finger, un-projected onto its plane, and a throw carries on by motion's inertia generator, slowing by friction with its resting angle snapped so a picture always stops at the front; arrow keys turn it a picture on the glide spring. As each picture comes round to the front it stands up off the plate, hinged on its outer edge, until it faces you, and lies back down as it moves on; a fast spin keeps them flat until it slows. The pictures are a radio group with one tab stop on the front picture: arrows turn, Home and End jump, and a press on a lying picture brings it round the short way.

props.name: items
props.type: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string }[]
props.description: The pictures, laid round the plate in order (3 to 16).

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The picture at the front, by index, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the throw, key or press that brought a new picture to the front.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How steeply you look down at the plate, degrees from face-on.

props.name: friction
props.description: How quickly a thrown plate slows, 0 (it coasts for turns) to 1 (it stops almost at once).

props.name: plateSize
props.description: How much of the box the plate fills, 0.5 to 1.

props.name: wood
props.description: The plate's timber.

props.name: stand
props.description: How far the front picture stands up, 0 (it stays flat) to 1 (it faces you).

props.name: autoTurn
props.description: Turn to the next picture by itself every this many ms while on screen and untouched; 0 never.

props.name: trigger
props.description: What starts the entrance spin.

props.name: captions
props.description: Show the front picture's caption under the plate.

props.name: label
props.description: The turntable's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No spinning, pressing or keys.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the turntable; it fills a 416px-tall box by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: one tab stop, on the front picture. Arrows turn the plate a picture at a time in the arrow's direction, Home and End jump to the first and last; focus follows the picture that comes to the front. A polite live region names it.
Reduced motion: no entrance spin and no coasting; a release or key changes the front picture at once and it is shown standing. Dragging still turns the plate 1:1, because it is the hand's own motion.

Performance: nothing runs at rest; the plate angle is one motion value, animated only by a gesture, a key or autoTurn, and every picture's 3D pose is derived from it. autoTurn's timer runs only while on screen, visible and untouched.
Layout is pure CSS: the plate is sized with container units from the box's width, height and tilt, so it fits a phone card and a desktop plate without measuring.

items.title: Glass Trio
items.tagline: Three glass beads that listen, think and speak.
items.description: An assistant's presence as three glass beads drawn as one liquid body: any two beads that come close are joined by a metaball neck, and an SVG lighting filter turns the blurred outline into a height map, so the union reads as one piece of glass with a tinted body, a refracting rim, a highlight whose sharpness is gloss and a soft caustic. Idle, they breathe apart and together on the drift spring, necks forming as they meet; listening, they slide into a line on snap and bob with the input level, each a beat behind the last; thinking, they orbit and spiral in on glide until they merge into one bead with a slow light turning inside; speaking, the bead pulses with the voice and sheds drops that fall back through a neck. It is an image named for its state, or a button when onPress is given (Enter or Space press it).

props.name: state
props.description: What the assistant is doing.

props.name: level
props.description: The input or voice level, 0 to 1: a number, or a function read every frame so a live level never re-renders.

props.name: tint
props.description: The glass's colour: cobalt, mint, amber or clear, or any CSS colour.

props.name: gloss
props.description: How wet the glass looks, 0 (a soft sheen) to 1 (a small, sharp highlight).

props.name: size
props.description: Radius of each bead, px; the trio's box is 8.4 by 6.6 radii.

props.name: breath
props.description: How long one idle breath takes, ms.

props.name: orbit
props.description: How fast the beads orbit while thinking, turns per second.

props.name: shed
props.description: How readily the speaking bead sheds drops, 0 (never) to 1 (on every syllable).

props.name: follow
props.description: Lean a little toward a pointer over the trio.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold everything still.

props.name: label
props.description: Who the trio is, for its accessible name.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Makes the trio a button (tap to talk); a press squeezes the beads together.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the trio, and a press does nothing.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the trio's box; its size comes from size.

usageNotes: Accessibility: the trio is an image named for its state ("Assistant, listening"), or a button with that name when onPress is given. A polite status announces each state change once and never the level.
Reduced motion: each state is a still pose reached at once with a short dip of light; levels still show as a glow round the beads, with no bobbing, orbit, drops or breathing.

Performance: one frame loop, only while on screen, visible and not paused (under reduced motion only while a level is shown); fixed pools of three beads and four drops; the lighting filter is sized once from size.
Live audio: pass level as a function that reads your analyser, so the trio samples it every frame without re-rendering; it is smoothed with a fast attack and a slow release.

items.title: Ambient Spill
items.tagline: The front card lights the room in its own colour.
items.description: A carousel of screen-like cards in a dark room where the front card glows and spills its colour onto the wall behind it, the glossy floor in front and the whole room. The position is one continuous motion value: every card's place, turn, dimming and glow, and the room's colour, mixed in oklab between the two cards it lies between, are functions of it, so the light dips and blooms as the next card takes the front. A drag follows 1:1 and rubber-bands at the ends, a flick is projected and settles on the glide spring with the release velocity, and a horizontal trackpad swipe scrolls it; the cards are slides with one tab stop, arrows and Home and End move it, and Enter opens the front card.

props.name: items
props.type: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string; meta?: string; color?: string }[]
props.description: The cards, in order; color is the light each throws into the room.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The card at the front, by index, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, wheel, key or press that brought a new card to the front.

props.name: spill
props.description: How much light the front card throws onto the wall and floor, 0 to 1.

props.name: roomTone
props.description: The room: a blue night, neutral ash, a plum dusk or a pale gallery.

props.name: spacing
props.description: How far apart the cards stand, in card widths.

props.name: reflection
props.description: Show each card's light on the glossy floor.

props.name: loop
props.description: Carry on from the last card to the first.

props.name: wheel
props.description: What a horizontal wheel or trackpad swipe does; vertical wheels always scroll the page.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Fires when the front card is pressed, or Enter is pressed on it.

props.name: captions
props.description: Show the title and line on each card.

props.name: label
props.description: The carousel's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No dragging, wheel, keys or presses.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the room; it fills a 544px-tall box by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the carousel has one tab stop, the front card. Left and Right move a card, Home and End jump, Enter opens the front card; focus follows the card that comes to the front and a polite live region names it.

Reduced motion: cards change places at once with no travel, while the room's colour still cross-fades over a short tween, because the colour is where you are. Drag still follows the hand and snaps on release.
Performance: nothing runs at rest. One motion value drives every card through useTransform, and the room's colour is a single CSS variable written per frame only while it moves.
Wheel: only a horizontal swipe is captured (and kept from paging the browser); vertical wheels pass straight to the page, so the room never traps scrolling.
The room is a scene, dark in both themes by default; roomTone "paper" gives a light gallery for light pages.

items.title: Year Rings
items.tagline: An archive in rings, oldest at the core.
items.description: An archive as a cross-section of a tree: items are grouped by year into concentric rings, the oldest at the core, over timber drawn from a seed whose rays, check and growth lines scale with grain. Every ring turns at its own slow pace, the pictures riding it upright; hovering or focusing a ring brakes it to a stop by constant friction while its band brightens and its year reads above the slice. A click brings a picture forward from its own rectangle on the glide spring to a framed view over the centre while the rings pause, and Escape, the close button or the scrim send it back with focus returned. Pictures share one roving tab stop: Left and Right move along a ring, Up and Down between years, Home the core and End the bark, Enter brings forward.

props.name: items
props.type: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string; year: number }[]
props.description: The archive, any order: grouped into one ring per year, the oldest at the core.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The picture brought forward, by index into items, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that brought a picture forward or sent it back.

props.name: ringGap
props.description: Space between rings, in picture widths (1.1 to 2).

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the rings turn, 0 (still) to 2.

props.name: grain
props.description: How much of the timber is drawn, 0 (a clean diagram) to 1 (rays, a check and every growth line).

props.name: alternate
props.description: Neighbouring rings turn opposite ways.

props.name: brake
props.description: Hovering or focusing a ring stops it.

props.name: wood
props.description: The timber.

props.name: captions
props.description: Show the year label above the slice.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold every ring still.

props.name: label
props.description: The archive's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No hovering, pressing or keys.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the archive; it fills a 544px-tall box by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: one tab stop across every picture. Left and Right move along a ring, Up out to newer years and Down in to older (to the picture nearest in angle), Home the core and End the outer ring; Enter or Space brings a picture forward, its close button takes focus, and Escape sends it back with focus returned to the picture.
Reduced motion: the rings stand still, hover and focus still show the year at once, and the forward view cross-fades instead of flying.

Performance: one frame loop advances the ring angles, only while on screen, visible, not paused and with speed above zero; braked rings ease to zero and the loop stops when every ring is still. Each ring is one rotating layer whose pictures counter-rotate through a shared CSS variable.
Each ring is a labelled group ("2023, 11 pictures") and each picture a button named with its caption, year and place in the ring.

items.title: Burner Card
items.tagline: A card with a gas flame breathing behind it.
items.description: A content card with a row of gas jets burning behind its top edge, drawn per pixel in WebGL2: a white-blue inner cone inside a taller translucent mantle for every port, a soft glow over the row and hot air above it that visibly wobbles the light. Hover, keyboard focus inside the card or a touch press turns the valve up on springs.snap, whose one overshoot is the roar before the taller, brighter flame settles, while the card's top edge catches the light; leaving turns it down on springs.drift to a low, steady flicker. The first time it is seen the burner lights from end to end, each jet popping alight as the front reaches it.

props.name: children
props.description: The card's content.

props.name: flameHeight

props.name: hue

props.name: flutter
props.description: How restless the flame is, 0 (steady) to 1 (nervous and dancing).

props.name: roar
props.description: How much taller the flame stands with the valve open, as a multiple of flameHeight, 1 to 3.

props.name: active
props.description: Holds the valve open (true) or low (false) whatever the pointer does; leave undefined for hover and focus to drive it.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires when hover, focus or a touch opens or closes the valve, with the new state.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Hover, keyboard focus inside the card and a touch press open the valve.

props.name: jetSpacing
props.description: Distance between the burner's ports in px; smaller is a finer, denser row.

props.name: glow
props.description: The soft glow over the burner, 0 to 1.

props.name: shimmer
props.description: How much the hot air above the flame wobbles, 0 to 1.

props.name: ignite
props.description: When the burner lights: the first time it is seen, at mount, or already lit.

props.name: focusable
props.description: Makes the card itself a tab stop, for cards with nothing focusable inside; name it with label.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the card when it is focusable.

props.name: paused
props.description: Holds the flicker still; the valve still opens and closes.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds each jet's own flicker.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's pixel ratio, at most 2; the soft flame never draws above 1.25.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root (width, margins).

props.name: cardClassName
props.description: Classes for the card box (padding, background).

usageNotes: Keyboard focus anywhere inside the card (focus-visible) opens the valve and blur closes it, exactly like hover; with no focusable content, pass focusable and label to make the card its own tab stop. Touch opens it while pressed.

The flame is one WebGL2 pass at a soft pixel ratio. It draws only while on screen and the tab is visible, at thirty frames a second while low and sixty while the valve moves, and stops when paused. Without WebGL2 a CSS flame stands in; a lost context is rebuilt.
Under reduced motion there is no flicker, ignition or roar: a still flame is drawn, and redrawn tall and bright at once when the valve opens, so the state still shows.
Colours come from hue at fixed lightness, composited so the flame reads as light on a dark page and as a saturated blue flame on a light one; the page's theme is re-read when it changes.
The root reserves headroom above the card for the full roar (about flameHeight × roar + 16 px), so nothing is clipped and nothing draws outside the component's box.

items.title: Curtain Count
items.tagline: Five ways to hold the stage while the page loads.
items.description: A full-frame loading screen over its own box in five variants driven by one progress value, which the readout follows on springs.glide: a counter whose odometer wheels rest on their digits and roll on the carry beside a filling rule, the brand word filling with colour from its baseline, five stacked bars filling over overlapping windows of the load, a split frame whose field inverts the giant percentage where its edge crosses, and a radial wipe with a clock hand riding its edge. All five end the same way: at 100 % the curtain holds a beat and says Ready, its seams crack open on springs.flick, and two halves, vertical slats or horizontal bands lift out of the box on the exit ease in a cascade while the page beneath settles from a hair's scale on springs.glide. There is nothing to press: the page is inert and marked busy until it is revealed, and one progress bar carries the value for assistive technology.

props.name: progress
props.description: How far the page has loaded, 0 to 1. At 1 the curtain holds a beat, then splits and lifts away; below 1 again, it falls back in.

props.name: variant
props.description: Which way to hold the stage, by name or by its place 1–5 in that order.

props.name: exitMotion
props.description: How the frame leaves: two halves parting at the centre, vertical slats from the centre out, or horizontal bands from the top.

props.name: accent
props.description: The fill colour, any CSS colour, taken at a lightness that reads on the curtain.

props.name: children
props.description: The page beneath, inert and marked busy until the curtain has gone.

props.name: brand
props.description: The brand on the curtain, and the word the word variant fills.

props.name: caption
props.description: A line of copy on the curtain; it reads Ready at 100 %.

props.name: stages
props.description: Labels for the bars variant's five bars.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the progress bar for assistive technology.

props.name: hold
props.description: How long the curtain holds at 100 % before it splits, in ms.

props.name: exitDuration
props.description: How long each part takes to lift away, in ms; the cascade adds to it.

props.name: slats
props.description: How many slats or bands the slats and shutter exits cut the frame into, 3 to 10.

props.name: curtainColor
props.description: The curtain's colour.

props.name: inkColor
props.description: The type on the curtain.

props.name: onRevealChange
props.description: Fires when the curtain has fully lifted (true), and when it falls back over the page (false).

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box; the curtain fills it. Give it a height.

usageNotes: Drive progress from your real loader; the readout smooths jumps on the glide spring, so a stalling request and a rush still read as one movement. A drop below 1 is a new run: the curtain fades back in and the count starts from there.

Assistive technology hears one progress bar with the value from progress (not the smoothed readout) and, on reveal, a polite '{brand} loaded.'; the page beneath is inert and aria-busy until then, and no focus is taken.
Under reduced motion the digits and fills change in place (the fill is the information) and at 100 % the curtain fades out instead of splitting.

The curtain lives inside its box: it is a size container, never fixed or sized by the viewport, so wrap a page region or a full-height app shell. The parts exist only while they lift and leave through the top edge, clipped by the box.
Nothing runs while it is settled: the readout and the exit are motion values on springs and tweens; at rest the curtain is a single sheet.

items.title: Word Window
items.tagline: Hover a word to see the picture through its letters.
items.description: A paragraph whose linked words carry pictures inside their letters. Hover a word or focus it and its ink fades so the letters become windows onto its picture, placed exactly where the preview card's picture will be and drifting a few pixels against the pointer on springs.glide. Rest on it for expandDelay and a card opens out of the word: a clip that starts as the word's own box grows to the whole card on springs.glide while the drift springs home, so the window spreads from the letters into the full picture, and the caption follows. The words are real links in real text; Escape closes the card where focus is, Enter follows the link, and a long press opens it on touch.

props.name: text
props.description: The paragraph; each [bracketed phrase] is a link carrying the next picture in links.

props.name: links
props.description: One per bracketed phrase, in order: { href?, src?, alt, caption?, scene? }. Without src a scene (flats, harbour, orchard, fjord) is drawn in code.

props.name: as
props.description: The paragraph's element.

props.name: expandDelay
props.description: How long the pointer or focus rests on a word before its card opens, in ms.

props.name: cardSize
props.description: The card's width in px; its picture is 0.62 as tall, and it shrinks to fit a smaller box.

props.name: maskTone
props.description: How the picture is toned in the letters and the card: as drawn, recoloured to the accent, grey, or deepened toward ink.

props.name: drift
props.description: How far the picture drifts behind the letters against the pointer, in px.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: How long the card waits after the pointer leaves before it closes, in ms.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The index of the link whose card is open, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires when a rest, a key or a leave opens or closes a card.

props.name: accent
props.description: The underline's colour and the duotone's hue, any CSS colour.

props.name: underline
props.description: A dotted underline marks the linked words at rest.

props.name: onLinkClick
props.type: (link: WordWindowLink, index: number, event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLElement>) => void
props.description: Fires when a linked word is clicked or activated, before it navigates.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Keeps the words as plain links: no pictures, no cards.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the box the card stays inside; size it to give the card room.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab to a linked word and it shows its picture as hover does; after expandDelay its card opens and its caption becomes the link's description; Escape closes the card and keeps focus on the word; Enter follows the link.
The text is real and selectable and read once; linked phrases never wrap (nowrap) and the font size is inherited, so the effect works from a caption to a hero line.
The card is a preview: it never takes the pointer or focus, stays inside the component's box and shrinks to fit a short box, so give the box some height around the paragraph.
Under reduced motion the picture does not drift and the card does not grow from the word: the ink cross-fades to the picture and the card fades in whole.

Drawn scenes are painted once on a canvas when the component mounts and released on unmount; pass src for real images (they are loaded once to learn their shape). Nothing runs while the paragraph is at rest.

items.title: Envelope Modal
items.tagline: Cards that open like letters into the full story.
items.description: A desk of envelopes, each closed with a seal, that open like letters into the full story. Opening one is three beats: the seal gives and the flap swings up about its hinge in perspective on springs.snap, its patterned liner showing as it turns; the folded letter slides up out of the pocket on springs.glide; then it flies to the middle and grows to fill the component's box as a modal, its panels unfolding one after another on springs.glide in a cascade, each darkening as it turns edge-on, until the real, scrollable letter takes over and focus moves into it. Closing refolds it, carries it back over its envelope and slides it into the pocket while the flap closes on springs.snap and the seal is pressed back with springs.recoil. Enter or Space opens an envelope, Escape closes the letter, and focus stays inside it while it is open.

props.name: items
props.description: The letters: { id, title, from?, date?, body, monogram? }. A string body splits into paragraphs on blank lines.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The id of the open letter, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the click or key that opens or closes a letter.

props.name: paperTone
props.description: The paper: envelope, liner and letter, fixed pigments that look the same in both themes.

props.name: foldCount
props.description: How many panels the letter is folded into, 2 to 5.

props.name: seal
props.description: What holds the flap shut: an embossed wax disc, a scalloped foil sticker, a button-and-string tie, or nothing.

props.name: sealColor
props.description: The seal's colour, any CSS colour; defaults to wax red, foil gold or string brown.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far the envelopes lie askew on the desk, in degrees either way.

props.name: scrim
props.description: How far the desk dims behind an open letter, 0 to 1.

props.name: inset
props.description: The open letter's margin inside the box, in px.

props.name: columns
props.description: A fixed number of columns; by default 2 under 480 px and 3 above.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The letter title's heading level.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the desk for assistive technology.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the desk's scatter.

props.name: sound
props.description: Plays the paper: the flap, the slide and every crease, only after the visitor's click or key.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the desk but opens nothing.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box; the desk and the open letter fill it. Give it a height.

usageNotes: The desk is a list of envelope buttons (aria-haspopup=dialog). Enter or Space opens one; the open letter is a modal dialog labelled by its title, focus moves to its close button when it arrives, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it, Escape or the close button closes it, and focus returns to its envelope.
The letter fills the component's own box, not the window: give the component the region it should take over (a section, a panel, a full-height page area). Long letters scroll inside the sheet.
Under reduced motion there is no flap swing, slide, flight or fold: the letter cross-fades in whole over the dimmed desk and out again, and the envelope shows its flap open while its letter is out.
Nothing runs at rest; each open or close is a handful of springs on motion values. The folded panels exist only while the letter folds, and the settled letter is one flat sheet.
Paper tones are fixed pigments with dark ink, so envelopes and letters look the same and stay legible on light and dark pages.

items.title: Fovea Image
items.tagline: A picture that's sharp only where you look.
items.description: A picture drawn coarse in square blocks everywhere except where you look: under the pointer it sharpens in steps, a crisp centre and rings that each halve the block, chosen block by block so the ring edges step like a real change of resolution, every block the average of the picture beneath it. The sharp spot follows the pointer as an eye does, waiting a moment and then jumping on springs.snap, whose one overshoot is a saccade's small glissade; entering closes the field in onto the gaze on springs.glide and leaving opens it out on springs.drift until the picture is sharp all over. Keyboard focus shows it sharp, the arrow keys look around it and Escape stops looking.

props.name: src
props.description: The picture's URL; without it a harbour at dusk is drawn in code.

props.name: alt
props.description: Describes the picture; it is the figure's accessible name.

props.name: blockSize
props.description: The coarse field's block size in px.

props.name: fovea
props.description: The crisp centre's radius in px.

props.name: steps
props.description: How many rings of resolution lie between the crisp centre and the coarse field, 1 to 4; each halves the block.

props.name: ring
props.description: Each ring's width as a share of the fovea, 0.2 to 2.

props.name: lag
props.description: How long the eye waits before it jumps to where the pointer went, in ms.

props.name: rest
props.description: What the picture is with no one looking: sharp all over, or coarse all over.

props.name: intro
props.description: On first view the eye glances round the picture, three fixations, before it settles.

props.name: gap
props.description: A seam between coarse blocks in px, for a tiled look.

props.name: fit
props.description: Fill the box, cropping, or fit inside it.

props.name: caption
props.description: A caption laid over the foot of the picture.

props.name: onGazeChange
props.type: (gaze: { x: number; y: number } | null) => void
props.description: Fires when the eye settles on a new point, as fractions of the picture, and with null when it stops looking.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the picture at rest and takes no input.

props.name: paused
props.description: Holds everything where it is: no intro, no saccades.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the drawn harbour.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box; the picture fills it. Give it a height.

usageNotes: The figure is one image to assistive technology, named by alt, and one tab stop. Keyboard focus shows it sharp all over; the arrow keys then look around it (24 px a press, 96 with Shift) with the same saccades, and Escape stops looking.
On touch, press and move to look and lift to let it rest; the box keeps touch-action pan-y so the page still scrolls under a vertical swipe.

One WebGL2 pass over a mipmapped texture, drawn only while the eye or the field is moving and never off screen or in a hidden tab. A lost context is rebuilt; without WebGL2 (or with a cross-origin src that cannot be read) the picture is drawn sharp on a 2D canvas.
Under reduced motion there is no intro and nothing travels: the sharp spot jumps to the pointer and entering or leaving swaps the field at once.

Pass src for your own image (it is loaded with crossOrigin anonymous so it can be sampled); the drawn harbour is painted once per seed and keeps its town and lighthouse in the middle of the frame so narrow crops still hold them.

items.title: Dealt Feed
items.tagline: New entries dealt onto the list like cards.
items.description: A live list whose new entries are dealt onto it like cards: each leaves a deck in the corner face down, flies to the top along an arc on two springs of different stiffness, turning face up and spinning a little against its travel, and slaps into place with the two bounces of springs.recoil while the rows below glide down on springs.glide to make room and jostle as it lands, and the count beside the heading rolls up a digit on springs.snap. Several arrivals are dealt one after another. A pointer or keyboard focus in the feed holds the deal so nothing moves under the reader; arrivals wait on the deck with a count, and pressing the deck (Enter or Space) deals them now.

props.name: entries
props.description: The list, newest first: { id, name, detail?, meta?, time?, hue? }. An entry with a new id at the front is dealt onto the list.

props.name: dealSpeed
props.description: How fast cards are thrown, 0.5 (a lazy toss) to 2 (a snap deal).

props.name: spin
props.description: How much a card spins in flight, 0 (it slides flat) to 1 (a spinning throw).

props.name: density
props.description: Row height, avatar size and how much each row says.

props.name: deckCorner
props.description: Where the deck sits.

props.name: max
props.description: How many rows are kept; older ones slide out at the foot.

props.name: pauseOnHover
props.description: A pointer or keyboard focus anywhere in the feed holds the deal; arrivals wait on the deck until it is pressed or the feed is left.

props.name: flip
props.description: Cards leave the deck face down and turn over in flight.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading.

props.name: total
props.description: The count beside the heading; defaults to the number of entries. It rolls up as each card lands.

props.name: totalLabel
props.description: A word after the count.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the list for assistive technology.

props.name: accent
props.description: The deck's colour and the new row's wash, any CSS colour.

props.name: onDeal
props.description: Fires as each dealt card lands.

props.name: sound
props.description: A paper slap as each card the visitor dealt from the deck lands; automatic arrivals stay silent.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Arrivals still land, but the deck cannot be pressed.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box; the feed fills it. Give it a height.

usageNotes: Push new entries onto the front of entries with fresh ids; the feed works out what is new, deals it in arrival order and announces landings politely, one sentence per burst.

The list is one tab stop and the deck the next: focus anywhere in the feed holds the deal just as a pointer over it does, so keyboard readers are never chased by moving rows and can reach the deck to deal what waits. The deck is a real button named for what waits on it; it is marked aria-disabled, never disabled, when nothing waits.
Under reduced motion there is no flight, flip, spin or slap: a new entry fades in at the top, the rows below move at once and the count changes in place.
Nothing runs while the feed is idle: each arrival is a handful of springs, rows move by transforms, and only max rows (plus the one leaving) are in the document.
Sound answers only the visitor: cards they dealt from the deck slap as they land; arrivals that deal themselves never play.

items.title: Shop Light
items.tagline: A strip light stutters on and lights what's under it.
items.description: A room in the dark with a fluorescent batten hanging over your content. On reveal the tube starts the way a cold tube does: its cathodes glow orange at both ends, it tries to strike in uneven, seeded flashes with dim swims between them, and it catches dimmer and cooler than it will be, settling to full on springs.drift while its colour warms to the chosen temperature and the content rises a nudge into the lit pool on springs.glide. The light is composited rather than tinted, so the wall and the content are multiplied by it and the pool dies into the dark below. The pull cord is a real switch that follows a downward drag 1:1 and springs back on springs.recoil with the drag's velocity; Space or Enter pulls it, and keyboard focus entering the content in the dark switches the light on.

props.name: children
props.description: The content on the wall under the light; it stays available to assistive technology in the dark.

props.name: lit / defaultLit
props.description: Whether the tube is switched on, controlled or initial.

props.name: onLitChange
props.description: Fires from the cord, the key, the reveal or the focus that switched it, with the new state.

props.name: trigger
props.description: What switches the tube on by itself: coming into view, mounting, or nothing but the cord.

props.name: once
props.description: Light once and stay lit; false puts it out when it leaves the view and strikes it again on return.

props.name: delay
props.description: Pause before an automatic strike, in ms.

props.name: flicker
props.description: How hard the cold tube fights before it catches, 0 (strikes clean) to 1 (a long preheat and five or six failed strikes).

props.name: warmth
props.description: The settled light's colour, 0 (6500 K daylight) to 1 (2700 K warm white).

props.name: falloff
props.description: How quickly the light dies below the tube, 0 (a wash to the floor) to 1 (a tight pool under it).

props.name: tubeLength
props.description: The tube's length as a share of the width, 0.3 to 0.9.

props.name: hang
props.description: How far below the top edge the fixture hangs, in px.

props.name: ambient
props.description: How much of the room shows with the tube out, 0 (pitch dark) to 0.5.

props.name: surface
props.description: The wall the content hangs on.

props.name: cord
props.description: Show the pull cord, the visitor's switch.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the stutter: the same seed fails the same way.

props.name: label
props.description: The switch's accessible name.

props.name: onSettle
props.description: Fires when a strike has settled to a steady light.

props.name: sound
props.description: Plays the cord's click and the tube's buzz on each flash, only for the visitor's own pull, key or focus.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the room but takes no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the room.

usageNotes: The cord is a role=switch button with aria-checked: Space or Enter pulls it, a drag down past 9px pulls it, and the change is announced politely. Focus moving into the content while the room is dark switches the light on, so a focus ring is never drawn in the dark.
Under reduced motion there is no preheat, stutter or rise: the light fades up over 240ms and out over 150ms, and the settled colour is used at once.

The room is its own world: the wall is a fixed pigment and the content inside is scoped to the light theme's tokens, so it reads the same on light and dark pages. Style the content with ordinary tokens.
Nothing runs once the tube has settled: a strike is a few keyframe tweens on motion values driving opacity, and the reveal is one IntersectionObserver.
Sound never plays for an automatic reveal; with sound on, the visitor's own pull clicks and each flash of the strike buzzes.

items.title: Shadow Box
items.tagline: A card built like a shadow box, deep inside.
items.description: A card built as a real box in CSS 3D: a framed window, inner walls running back to a sky panel, outside walls in the frame's colour, and layers of cut-paper scenery standing at their own depths. One side is open and the light falls in from it, so the walls are shaded by where they face, each layer's cut edge catches the light, and each casts a blurred shadow drawn on the layers behind it, which therefore moves with the surface it falls on as the box turns. The pointer tilts the box toward it on springs.glide and it drifts level on springs.drift when the pointer leaves. Keyboard focus starts a slow tour round the inside, arrow keys tilt it a quarter of the range and Home levels it.

props.name: layers
props.description: How many cut-paper layers to generate, 2 to 7, or your own layers back to front: { path (0–100 SVG path), color, depth? }.

props.name: depth
props.description: How deep the box is, in px: longer shadows, more parallax.

props.name: light
props.description: The open side the light falls in from.

props.name: lightStrength
props.description: How strong that light is, 0 (flat, no shadows) to 1.

props.name: palette
props.description: A named paper set, or five CSS colours: sky top, sky low, moon, far ridge, near ridge.

props.name: tilt
props.description: The furthest the box tilts toward the pointer, in degrees.

props.name: perspective
props.description: The viewing distance, in px: smaller is a stronger perspective.

props.name: frame
props.description: The frame's width, in px.

props.name: frameColor
props.description: The frame's colour, any CSS colour; the outside walls are it, shaded.

props.name: glass
props.description: A glass pane in the frame, its reflection sliding against the tilt.

props.name: title
props.description: The piece's name, printed on the plaque and read first.

props.name: caption
props.description: A line read after the title.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the whole box a link.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Pointer, touch and keys tilt the box.

props.name: tour
props.description: Keyboard focus starts a slow tour round the inside.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the ridges, trees and stars.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name, if it should say more than the title and caption.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the box at rest and takes no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

usageNotes: The box is a focusable group (or a link with href) named by its title and caption, with aria-roledescription="shadow box". Keyboard focus starts the tour; arrow keys tilt it, Home levels it, and Escape levels it only when it is tilted, so otherwise Escape reaches the page.
Under reduced motion the box rests at a fixed three-quarter view that shows its walls and depth; there is no pointer tilt or tour, and arrow keys set a new still view at once.

Nothing runs at rest. The pointer retargets two springs, the tour's frame runs only while focused and on screen, and the scenery and its blurred shadows are rebuilt only when size, seed, layers or palette change.
Paper colours are pigments, the same on light and dark pages; the frame defaults to ink on the page's tone, so it is near-black on a light page and gallery white on a dark one.
The box sits in from its root by as far as its outside walls can swing, so a full tilt never paints outside the component; deeper boxes sit a little smaller.

items.title: Droplet Swap
items.tagline: A rolling drop carries the next image across.
items.description: A gallery whose transition is a drop of water. A drop rolls across the picture with the next one inside it, small and upside down as a ball lens shows it, its view sliding the other way as it moves, with a dark meniscus, a highlight, a cast shadow and a caustic, squashing along its path with speed and leaving a wet trail that dries. It gathers as it rolls, and at full size it bursts into a spreading circle of the new picture, upright, on the springs.glide constants, throwing a few splash beads and leaving a sheen that dries. Drag to steer: a drop forms under the finger and follows it 1:1, carrying the next picture right or the previous one left, and a flick rolls it on by projection. Arrow keys roll next and previous, Home and End roll to the ends, and dots choose a picture.

props.name: items
props.description: The pictures, in order: { src?, alt, caption? }. Items without src get a drawn scene.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The index of the picture shown, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires when a drop has burst and a new picture fills the frame, with its index.

props.name: dropSize
props.description: How big the drop has grown when it bursts: its diameter as a share of the frame's height, 0.2 to 0.6.

props.name: rollSpeed
props.description: How fast a drop rolls across, in px/s.

props.name: refraction
props.description: The lens's power, 0 (most of the picture, a faint rim) to 1 (a close-up of its middle, a dark meniscus and a bright caustic).

props.name: trail
props.description: Leave a wet trail behind the drop that dries.

props.name: splash
props.description: Throw a few small drops when it bursts.

props.name: interval
props.description: ms between automatic swaps, 0 for none. Held while hovered, focused, hidden or off screen.

props.name: loop
props.description: Wrap from the last picture to the first and back.

props.name: indicators
props.description: Show a dot per picture to choose it.

props.name: captions
props.description: Show the caption over the picture's foot.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the gallery for assistive technology.

props.name: sound
props.description: A plip when a drop forms under the finger and a blup when it bursts, only for the visitor's own drag, tap or key.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the picture and takes no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the frame.

usageNotes: The gallery is a region with aria-roledescription="carousel"; its frame is focusable, Arrow Right and Left roll a drop to the next or previous picture, Home and End to the ends, and the new picture is announced politely after it lands. Every picture is an sr-only slide group with its alt text; only the shown one is exposed.
Under reduced motion the bead rests still and a swap is a 240ms cross-fade; a drag still moves the drop under the finger and a long enough pull cross-fades the next picture in.

Nothing runs at rest: the loop runs only while a drop rolls, is dragged or bursts, and the geometry is written to SVG attributes, never to React state per frame. Automatic swaps wait while the gallery is hovered, focused, hidden or off screen.
Pictures are cover-fitted, so any aspect works; the default scenes are drawn in code and bleed wide enough to crop well from a phone card to a wide hero.
Keys pressed during a roll are not lost: the rolling drop bursts where it is and the next one goes straight after it.

items.title: Pin Depth
items.tagline: Cards pinned at heights, shifting as you move.
items.description: Cards pinned to a cork board on pins of different lengths, each floating at its own height. The pointer is the viewer's eye: moving it slides every card against the cork by its height, the higher the further, so they pass one another in parallax, and since each shadow lies on the cork and stays put, the gap between a card and its shadow opens and closes while pin shafts show wherever the parallax uncovers them. The view follows on springs.glide and drifts level on springs.drift. Clicking a card lifts it off its pin on springs.snap, leaving the pin standing, and flies it to the middle as a close-up on springs.glide; Escape or the close button flies it home and drops it on its pin with springs.recoil. Arrow keys tilt the view and Home levels it.

props.name: cards
props.description: The cards: { id, title, body?, meta?, kind? (note, photo, swatch, ticket, sketch), tone?, pin?, height?, swatches? }.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The id of the card brought close, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the click, key or close that changed it, with the new id or null.

props.name: depth
props.description: How far the view swings as you move, 0 (flat) to 1.5.

props.name: shadow
props.description: How strong and long the shadows are, 0 to 1.

props.name: pinLength
props.description: The longest pin, in px: the highest a card floats above the cork.

props.name: columns
props.description: A fixed number of columns; by default 2 under 520px wide and 3 above.

props.name: tilt
props.description: The pointer moves the view. Keys still tilt it when off.

props.name: scatter
props.description: How far cards hang askew, in degrees either way.

props.name: corkColor
props.description: The cork's colour, any CSS colour.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the scatter and any pin length left unset.

props.name: label
