props.name: height
props.description: Height of the editor in px; its body scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be dragged, typed or saved; the editor dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the threshold handle is a role="slider" whose value text carries the would-have-alerted count. Up or Right nudge one step, Down or Left one step down, Shift with an arrow or Page Up and Page Down move ten, Home and End go to the axis ends. Comparison and duration are radiogroups (arrows), the channel is a native select, and the threshold is also a number field. Markers are one tab stop: arrows walk them, Enter opens a card with the fire time and peak, Escape closes it.

Fires are worked out from the series, not stored: a breach is a run of readings past the line that fires once, duration minutes after it starts, if it is still past the line then; a gap in the data ends a run. The same function is exported as findTripwireFires, so a host can show the count elsewhere.

Reduced motion: the line jumps to its value, markers fade in and out in place with no drop or lift, the count updates without rolling, and pills cross-fade. The recolouring past the line, the wash, the markers and the count still change, because they are the information.

Performance: nothing runs at rest. A drag writes one motion value that the handle, the clip rect and the wash read; React renders only when the stepped value changes. The chart is one stretched SVG with non-scaling strokes and the plot width is measured by a ResizeObserver bound to the node when it arrives.

States: loading keeps the axes and the rule editable; a failed load keeps the draft under a Retry banner; a failed save says so inline and leaves the draft untouched. Below a 544px container the form drops under the chart and the body scrolls inside the editor.

items.title: Rack Elevation
items.tagline: Your hardware, unit by unit, with its lights on.
items.description: A rack elevation drawn from data: each rack front-on with rails and U numbers, each host a slim drawer with power, network and health lights, its temperature and a load meter, and every free unit a dashed slot. Selecting a host slides its drawer out on its rails on springs.glide, heavy and damped and carrying the throw's velocity when it is pulled by hand, while the slot it left shows dark between two rails, a shadow grows with the pull, its tray unrolls toward the side with room and every other unit dims; an alert flashes only the one light it belongs to. The elevation is one tab stop: Up and Down walk units, Left and Right cross racks to the unit at the nearest height, Enter opens, Escape closes, and Reboot asks for a second press.

props.name: rackCount
props.description: How many racks are drawn side by side (stacked when narrow), from the start of racks.

props.name: ledStyle
props.description: How a status light is drawn: a round lamp, a slim light pipe or a hollow ring.

props.name: tone
props.description: The rack's metal, mixed from theme tokens so it reads in both themes.

props.name: racks
props.description: The racks: { id, name, units, hosts }, each host { id, name, role, u, size, state, address, temp, load, power, uptime, drained?, alert? }.

props.name: selected / defaultSelected
props.description: The open host id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fires from the press, key or pull that opened or closed a drawer.

props.name: onDrain
props.description: Drain or Undrain was pressed, with the host's new drained state.

props.name: onReboot
props.description: A reboot was confirmed with the second press of Reboot.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading draws outline units in each rack; error offers Retry.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed after the racks failed to load.

props.name: unitHeight
props.description: Height of one rack unit in px.

props.name: pull
props.description: How far a drawer slides out on its rails, in px.

props.name: tempLimit
props.description: Temperatures at or above this (°C) are drawn as warnings.

props.name: blink
props.description: Let an alert's light flash; it only does while its rack is on screen and the page is visible.

props.name: title
props.description: The room or row over the racks, and the surface's accessible name.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; the racks scroll inside it.

props.name: disabled

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the elevation is one tab stop (roving tabindex). Up and Down walk the units of a rack, Left and Right cross to the neighbouring rack at the unit nearest the same height, Home and End jump to the top and bottom unit, Enter or Space opens a drawer and Escape closes it from the drawer or anywhere in its tray, returning focus to the drawer. The tray's Drain and Reboot follow in tab order; Reboot arms on the first press and only fires on a second within three seconds.

A drawer can also be pulled: it follows the finger 1:1 sideways, rubber-bands past its stop, and a release is projected open or shut. The face carries touch-action: pan-y, so vertical scrolling still works over the racks.
Reduced motion: nothing slides. The open drawer is ringed in place, the tray fades in, other units dim, and an alert light holds steady inside a halo instead of flashing.

Performance: the only repeating work is an alert light, which flashes on a slow timer as a paint-only colour change, only while its rack is on screen (IntersectionObserver) and the page visible; everything else moves only when opened, pulled or closed. Every host name is announced with its units, health, temperature and load.
Below a 544px container the racks stack as an accordion with one rack open at a time; a closed rack shows a spine of its units so an alert is visible before it is opened.

items.title: Heartbeat Ledger
items.tagline: Scheduled jobs that check in, and the ones that don't.
items.description: A monitor for scheduled jobs that check in: each row is a job, its owner, a strip of recent check-ins drawn as slim bars whose height is the run's length (on time, late, failed, and a hatched slot wherever a run never arrived) and its next deadline. A new check-in drops into the head of its strip on springs.recoil while the strip rolls one slot left on springs.glide; past its deadline a job wears a ring that runs down its grace on a linear tween between readings of the now prop, and if the grace runs out the row tips into a warning tint that sweeps in on glide while its dot turns into a warning glyph on springs.snap. It is a role="grid" with one roving cell: arrows move, P pauses, M mutes, Enter opens the last run, and Enter on a strip steps into it to pick an older run.

props.name: stripLength
props.description: How many beats each history strip shows at wide widths; narrow widths always show the last ten.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height and bar size.

props.name: accent
props.description: On-time ticks, grace rings and the clock, any CSS colour.

props.name: jobs
props.description: The jobs: { id, name, schedule, every, grace, lastCheckIn?, owner, beats, typical? } with beats { id, at, status, duration } oldest first.

props.name: now
props.description: The time every deadline is judged against, in ms; the host advances it and the clock is never read.

props.name: paused / defaultPaused
props.description: Paused job ids, controlled or initial.

props.name: onPause
props.description: Fires from the button or the P key, with whether the job is now paused.

props.name: muted / defaultMuted
props.description: Muted job ids, controlled or initial.

props.name: onMute
props.description: Fires from the button or the M key, with whether the job's alerts are now muted.

props.name: onOpenRun
props.description: A run was opened: Enter or a press on the job, or a beat picked in its strip; null when the job has never run.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading draws skeleton rows with ghost strips; error shows its own state with Retry; an empty jobs list has its own state too.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed after the check-ins failed to load.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading and the grid's accessible name.

props.name: formatTime
props.description: Formats the clock, deadlines and beat times.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; rows scroll under the pinned header.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be paused, muted or opened; the surface dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: a role="grid" with one roving cell. Arrows move between cells and rows (hidden columns are skipped at narrow widths), Home and End go to the row's ends and Ctrl with Home or End to the corners. P pauses or resumes the focused job, M mutes it, Enter on the job opens its last run. Enter on a history strip steps into it: Left and Right pick a run (each is announced), Enter opens it, Escape steps back out.

Time is a prop. The component never reads the clock: pass now and advance it (a second at a time is enough; the grace ring tweens between readings). Missed runs are derived, not stored: any gap between check-ins longer than every plus grace is drawn as a hatched slot, and a job past its grace grows a pending one at the head of its strip that keeps its place when the late check-in lands.

Reduced motion: beats appear in place with a short fade and the strip re-seats without gliding, the ring and the warning tint jump to their state, and the warning glyph fades in. Every count, deadline and colour still changes.

Performance: there is no loop of its own. Motion happens only when now or jobs change, the grace ring tweens only while the ledger is on screen, and strips are absolutely placed slots moved by transform. A lapse is announced once, politely, from the render that sees it.
Helpers for hosts and tests: heartbeatRun, heartbeatBeats and heartbeatJobAt turn a seeded HeartbeatPlan into the beats it would have produced by a given time, which is how the demo replays a night.

items.title: Exception Triage
items.tagline: Group the errors, then decide what each one is.
items.description: An error inbox where each row is a group of exceptions sharing a fingerprint: its level, type and message, where it was thrown, a 24-hour sparkline, events, users affected, when it was last and first seen, and who owns it. Resolving plays in three beats: the sparkline's points glide flat onto the floor on springs.glide while it turns to success, the flat line writes a Resolved label uncovered left to right along it, and the row folds away on the exit ease while the rows below close up on glide; an issue that regresses slides back to the top on glide and stamps a Reopened tag on springs.recoil. It is a grid: J and K move, E resolves, I ignores, A opens the assign menu and Enter opens the issue.

props.name: sparkStyle
props.description: How each 24-hour sparkline is drawn: a line ending in a dot, bars, or a filled area.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height (54, 64 or 74px) and type size.

props.name: palette

props.name: issues

props.name: members

props.name: now

props.name: onResolve

props.name: onIgnore

props.name: onAssign

props.name: onOpen

props.name: status
props.description: Loading draws skeleton rows; error shows its own state with Retry; an empty inbox has its own state too.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed after the issues failed to load.

props.name: labelHold
props.description: How long the Resolved label holds before the row folds, in ms.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading and the grid's accessible name.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: What an empty inbox says.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; the list scrolls under its header.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be resolved, ignored or assigned; the surface dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: a role="grid" with one roving cell. J or Down and K or Up move between issues, Left and Right between cells, Home and End to the first and last issue. E resolves, I ignores, A opens the assign menu (a role="menu" of menuitemradio items: arrows, Enter, Escape returns focus) and Enter opens the issue. After a row leaves, focus moves to the issue that takes its place; each decision is announced politely.

Rows are placed by transform in a stable DOM order, so a re-sort (a regression sliding to the top) never moves a node under the keyboard. A decision shows at once and stays until the host's data for that issue changes, so the inbox works controlled or not; a fix that regresses comes back even when the host lands on the status it had before.

Below a 544px container the users count and the actions live behind each row: arrowing into them slides the face aside on springs.snap, a horizontal swipe follows the finger 1:1 with rubber-banding and a flick commits, and Escape slides it back. Rows carry touch-action: pan-y so the list still scrolls.

Reduced motion: the sparkline is simply flat and the Resolved label fades in, rows fade out without folding, regressions re-sort in place with the tag faded in, and the narrow reveal is an instant swap. Counts and states still change.

Performance: nothing runs at rest. The flatten is one motion value per resolving row that rebuilds its path; the label sweep is one clip. Compact counts are formatted by hand (1.3k) so the server and the browser print the same text.

items.title: Probe Relay
items.tagline: Check an endpoint from six stations at once.
items.description: A synthetic check runner: six stations sit on a ring round the endpoint, each joined to it by a path that bows the same way, and each holds its last latency for the active check with a slim bar against the budget. Run now sends a pulse from every station to the target at once on the move ease; while the results are out the paths turn dotted and march, and when they land a pulse returns to each station taking time in proportion to its latency, so the fastest hear back first, and each number lands at its station on springs.recoil, coloured against the budget, while its bar glides on springs.glide. Checks are a tablist, every station is its own tab stop with a details card, and R reruns the active check from anywhere inside.

props.name: pathCurve

props.name: pulseSpeed
props.description: Scales every travel time: 2 is twice as quick, 0.5 half.

props.name: accent

props.name: stations

props.name: checks

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The active check id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the tab, arrow or key that changed the active check.

props.name: onRun
props.description: Run now or R was pressed. Answer by updating the check's ranAt and results; the pulses return when they change.

props.name: onPause

props.name: onEdit
props.description: Edit was pressed.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading draws dotted paths and ghost checks; error shows its own state with Retry.

props.name: onRetry

props.name: now
props.description: The time "ran 2m ago" is measured from, in ms; never read from the clock.

props.name: formatLatency
props.description: Formats every latency and the budget.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading and the surface's accessible name.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing runs, pauses or edits; the surface dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the checks are a role="tablist" with roving focus (arrows in either direction, Home and End) that activates as it moves; each station is its own tab stop, named with its latency against the budget or its error, and opens a details card that Escape closes, returning focus. R reruns the active check from anywhere inside the surface. A finished run is announced once: how many stations were within budget and which failed.

Results are data: onRun only asks. The host runs the check and updates its ranAt and results; each station keeps its old number until its own pulse lands, so readings change in latency order. A host that never answers does not leave the run spinning: it gives up after twelve seconds.

Reduced motion: no pulse travels. The paths are dotted but still while a run is out, numbers fade to their new value and bars set without gliding; colours and the announcement still say what happened.

Performance: nothing runs at rest. Pulses animate one motion value each for the length of a run and only while the surface is on screen (off screen the results land at once); the dotted march runs only while waiting. Geometry is measured with a ResizeObserver and every coordinate is rounded.
Below a 544px container the ring becomes a list of stations with latency bars and a budget mark, and the checks become a horizontal tab row with an edge fade.

items.title: Status Dispatch
items.tagline: Write the public update and see it as customers will.
items.description: A status-page composer with the public page beside it: pick the phase, set each component's state, write the update (a slash at the start of a line offers templates) and choose who is notified, while the preview shows the page, the email or the text message as customers will get them, the draft riding at the head of the timeline as a dashed ghost. Publishing folds the ghost away on a fast exit tween, lands the real entry on springs.recoil, presses the stamp onto it a beat later on the same spring, and then the component dots change to their new states one after another on a cascade stagger; a failed publish keeps the draft and never celebrates. Ctrl or ⌘ + Enter publishes from anywhere in the composer, the phase, preview and component states are radiogroups driven with the arrow keys, and the template list follows Up, Down, Enter and Escape from the textarea.

props.name: previewMode
props.description: Which view the preview opens on: the public page, the email or the text message. Changing it moves the preview there; at narrow widths email and text also open on the Preview tab.

props.name: onPreviewModeChange

props.name: stampStyle
props.description: The mark pressed onto a posted update: a round seal, a label chip, or a tick.

props.name: accent

props.name: components
