props.name: incident
props.description: The incident being updated and its posted updates, newest first.

props.name: templates
props.description: Templates offered when a line starts with a slash; inserting one also sets the phase.

props.name: audiences
props.description: Who can be notified: { id, label, count, channel: "email" | "sms" | "webhook" }.

props.name: draft / defaultDraft
props.description: The update being written, controlled or initial: { phase, text, affected (component id → new state), notify (audience ids) }.

props.name: onDraftChange
props.description: Fires from the edit that changed the draft, with the whole draft.

props.name: onPublish
props.description: Publish was pressed (or Ctrl+Enter). Return a promise to show publishing; a rejection keeps the draft.

props.name: onSchedule
props.description: A time was chosen from Schedule; the post joins the timeline as scheduled. A rejection keeps the draft.

props.name: onSaveDraft
props.description: Save draft was pressed.

props.name: now
props.description: The current time in ms; posts are stamped with it and schedule times count from it. Never read from the clock.

props.name: pageName
props.description: The status page's name in the preview, the email and the text.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the live page has loaded. Loading shows a skeleton preview and holds Publish; error keeps the composer under a Retry banner.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed after the live page failed to load.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the composer in px; each pane scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be edited, published or scheduled; the composer dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Ctrl or ⌘ + Enter publishes from anywhere in the composer. Phase, preview view and every component's state are radiogroups (one tab stop each, arrows move). Typing / at the start of a line opens the template listbox: Up and Down move, Enter or Tab inserts, Escape closes it without leaving the stage. Schedule is a menu button: arrows move, Escape returns focus to it.

The composer owns the live page after mount: components and incident seed it, and a publish updates the live states and the timeline itself. Report the post to your backend from onPublish; return a promise and the draft stays read-only until it settles, so nothing typed meanwhile is lost.

Reduced motion: the ghost does not fold, the entry and the stamp fade in without travel or bounce, and the component dots change together with a short colour tween. States, counts and the timeline still update, because they are the information.
Below a 640px container the preview becomes a tab beside Compose, and publishing switches to it (focus moves to the Preview tab) so the landing is seen. Both panes scroll inside the fixed height.

Performance: nothing runs at rest. The publish choreography is two timeouts cleared on unmount, rolling counts are motion values rendered as text, and the state colours are CSS transitions with per-row delays.

items.title: Ghost Baseline
items.tagline: Today's line, laid over last week's shadow.
items.description: A metric explorer with a chart, a legend table and window controls, whose comparison is a ghost: turning on Yesterday or Last week lays the same window from earlier under the live lines, sliding in from the left on springs.glide while a clip sweeps across the plot on an enter tween, and the legend's comparison and delta columns roll to their figures. The axis is chosen from the live and the comparison data together, so the ghost never rescales the chart, and a failed refresh keeps the last result drawn. The plot is a slider over its buckets — Left and Right step the crosshair, Shift steps ten, Home and End jump — and [ and ] shift the window anywhere in the explorer.

props.name: ghostStyle
props.description: How the comparison is drawn: dashes, dots, or a soft area under a thin edge.

props.name: lineWidth
props.description: Stroke width of the live lines in px; the ghost is drawn at 80% of it.

props.name: palette
props.description: The series colours, from the theme's tokens.

props.name: query
props.description: The query behind the chart, shown in mono under the title.

props.name: series
props.description: The series: { id, label, points: { t, v | null }[] } with evenly spaced readings; null is a gap.

props.name: comparisons
props.description: The comparisons on offer: { id, label, short, offset } where offset is how far back it looks in ms.

props.name: compare / defaultCompare
props.description: The comparison id, controlled or initial; null for none.

props.name: onCompareChange
props.description: Fires from the press that changed the comparison.

props.name: range / defaultRange
props.description: The window, controlled or initial: { span: "1h" | "6h" | "24h" | "7d", end } in ms.

props.name: onRangeChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that moved or resized the window.

props.name: spans
props.description: The window sizes on offer.

props.name: now
props.description: The newest moment there can be data for, in ms; the window never moves past it. Never read from the clock.

props.name: unit
props.description: The readings' unit.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the result has arrived. Loading keeps the axes; error keeps the last result drawn under a Retry banner.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed after a refresh failed.

props.name: maxPoints
props.description: The most points drawn per series; the window is averaged into this many buckets.

props.name: title
props.description: The chart's name and the explorer's accessible name.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the explorer in px; its body scrolls inside it.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the window and the comparison are radiogroups (arrows move). The plot is a role="slider" whose value text names every route's reading and its comparison at the crosshair: Left and Right step one bucket, Shift steps ten, Home and End jump, Escape lets the legend return to the latest reading. [ and ] shift the window one span back or forward from anywhere inside the explorer, never past now.

Data: pass readings at their native resolution; the visible window is averaged into at most maxPoints buckets per series (an empty bucket is a gap), so a 7-day window stays one short path per series. The y axis covers the live data and every comparison together, so turning a comparison on never rescales the chart.

Reduced motion: the ghost fades in where it lies with no slide and no sweep, and the legend's figures change without rolling. The lines, deltas and crosshair still update, because they are the information.

States: loading keeps the axes and gridlines under a soft band; a failed refresh keeps the last successful window drawn (dimmed a step) under a Retry banner; stretches with no reading on any route are hatched and listed for assistive tech.

Performance: nothing runs at rest. Buckets are memoised per window, the crosshair renders only when its bucket changes, and the chart is one stretched SVG with non-scaling strokes. A comparison already on at first paint is in the server's markup and does not sweep; one that arrives after hydration does.

items.title: Pager Rota
items.tagline: Who is on call now, next, and after that.
items.description: An on-call week drawn as a dial — Monday at twelve o'clock, the week running clockwise, one ring per layer cut into wedges in each engineer's colour — with a now-hand, who is on call now, next and after that, and the selected shift's Page, Override and Swap. Adding an override opens a notch in the ring and the new wedge, in the covering engineer's colour, slides into it from 18px out along its bisector on springs.snap; when now moves the hand ticks there on springs.snap, unwrapped so it never runs backwards round the week, and time nobody covers is hatched and flagged. The dial is a grid with one tab stop: Left and Right walk the week, Up and Down change layer, Home and End jump, O overrides, S swaps and P pages, and narrow containers get a linear schedule with the same keys.

props.name: dialStyle
props.description: How the week is drawn: separate rings with gaps between shifts, rings that touch, or thin arcs with a dot at each handoff.

props.name: layerCount
props.description: How many layers are shown, outermost first (1–3).

props.name: accent
props.description: The now-hand, the selection and Override, any CSS colour.

props.name: rota / defaultRota
props.description: The rota, controlled or initial: { people: { id, name, color }[], layers: { id, label, shifts }[], overrides }.

props.name: onRotaChange
props.description: Fires from the override or swap that changed the rota, with the whole rota.

props.name: onOverride
props.description: An override was added: { id, layer, person, start, end }.

props.name: onSwap
props.description: Two shifts traded people; a and b as they are after the swap.

props.name: onPage
props.description: Page was pressed (or P) for the person on the selected segment.

props.name: now
props.description: The current time in ms; the hand points at it. Never read from the clock.

props.name: weekStart
props.description: Monday 00:00 of the week drawn, in ms.

props.name: selected / defaultSelected
props.description: The selected segment id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.description: Fires from the key or press that moved the selection.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the rota has loaded. Loading draws an empty dial; error adds a Retry banner.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed after the rota failed to load.

props.name: team
props.description: The team, in the header and the grid's name.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the rota in px; its body scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be overridden, swapped or paged.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the dial (or the linear schedule) is a role="grid" with one tab stop and aria-activedescendant: rows are layers, cells are segments named in one sentence ("Primary, Ravi Okonjo, Wed 09:00–18:00, on call now"). Left and Right walk the week, Up and Down move to the same time on the next layer, Home and End jump, O opens the override form (a dialog whose Escape returns focus to the grid), S swaps with the next shift, P pages.

Coverage is worked out, not stored: rotaSegments(layer, overrides, weekStart) is exported and returns each layer's week as contiguous shift, override and gap segments, with later overrides winning. Use it to show who is on call anywhere else in your app.

Colours: each person carries a CSS colour for their wedges. They are filled shapes, so pass pigments that read in both themes (the defaults are token hues at a fixed lightness, e.g. oklch(from var(--signal) 0.8 0.11 h)); initials sit on them in dark ink.
Reduced motion: the hand jumps to the hour, a new override fades in where it lands with no slide, and the selection is an outline with no lift. Colours, names and the now list still change.

Performance: no timers in the component. The dial is static SVG with rounded coordinates; the hand is one motion value driving its endpoints, and the pulse on its tip plays once per change of now. Below a 480px container the dial is swapped for a linear schedule by container query, so there is no layout flash.

items.title: Ghost Rows
items.tagline: Hover a template and watch the table fill.
items.description: An empty table with three ways in — import a file, connect a source, or start from a template — whose templates preview themselves in place: pointing at one, or focusing it, re-heads the table with its columns and pours its sample rows in one by one, each dropping from 12px above on springs.snap a cascade apart and settling faint with dashed rules, and moving on drains them last row first on the exit ease. Choosing the template turns the ghosts solid in a wave down the rows while the ways in fold away on springs.glide; an import in progress is a progress row and a failed one explains the file problem in plain words. The options are one tab stop — arrows move across all three groups, Home and End jump, Enter chooses — and focus is carried to Undo and back so it never falls to the page.

props.name: ghostOpacity
props.description: How faint the poured preview rows are, 0.2 to 0.7.

props.name: layout
props.description: Ways in beside the table, or as three columns above it. Narrow containers always stack.

props.name: accent
props.description: Focus and hover wash, the solid wave and the progress bar, any CSS colour.

props.name: templates
props.description: Templates a table can start from: { id, label, blurb, columns: { key, label, weight?, align?, mono? }[], rows }.

props.name: sources
props.description: Sources a table can be connected to: { id, label, detail, kind: "erp" | "sheet" | "feed" }.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The chosen template id, controlled or initial; null while the table is empty.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that chose a template, or from Undo.

props.name: preview
props.description: A template previewed without pointing at it (a guided tour, an onboarding hint); pointing or focusing takes over.

props.name: onPreviewChange
props.description: Fires when pointing or focusing changes the previewed template, with its id, or null when it leaves.

props.name: onTemplate
props.description: A template was chosen.

props.name: onImport
props.description: A file was picked or dropped on the table. Drive importState from here.

props.name: onConnect
props.description: A source was chosen. Return a promise to show connecting; a rejection says so on the option.

props.name: importState
props.description: An import in progress ({ phase: "reading", file, progress, rows }) shown as a progress row, or one that failed ({ phase: "failed", file, error }) shown as a row that explains.

props.name: accept
props.description: File types the picker offers.

props.name: ghostRows
props.description: How many sample rows pour in; the phone preview shows two.

props.name: title
props.description: The table's name and the surface's accessible name.

props.name: workspace
props.description: The workspace the table belongs to.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; its body scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be chosen, imported or connected.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: every way in is a real button in one roving set (one tab stop): arrows move across the three groups, Home and End jump, Enter or Space acts. Focusing a template previews it exactly as pointing does. Choosing one moves focus to Undo (the ways in go inert); Undo brings focus back to the template.

The ghost rows are a preview, not data: they are aria-hidden and a polite status says "Preview: Spare parts, 6 columns, 6 sample rows" once per template. Chosen rows are real table rows (role="table" with row and cell roles), so assistive tech reads them as data only after the choice.

Imports: the hidden file input and drops on the table both call onImport(file); the component never reads the file. Feed back progress through importState and, on failure, a plain-words error ("Row 14 has 9 columns; the header has 7") with Choose another file.

Reduced motion: ghosts appear in place without the drop, drain without travel, and the solid wave is a single cross-fade; the ways in collapse without the glide. Rows, columns, counts and the progress value still change.

Layout: columns past the second appear as the table itself widens (a named container query), so a template with six columns shows two at 316px, four at about 350px and all six from 480px. The split layout collapses its side column to nothing once a template is chosen, giving the table the full width.

items.title: Open Day
items.tagline: Nothing booked yet, so plan the day you want.
items.description: An empty calendar day: the working hours as a calm column, suggested blocks floating beside it, and an empty message that sits in the largest free stretch and shrinks as the day fills. A suggestion follows the finger 1:1, tucked to a compact chip while a dashed slot shows where it would land; released over the day it drops onto the slot on springs.snap with the throw's velocity and then stretches to its default length on springs.glide a beat later, and released anywhere else it flies home. Keyboard users pick a suggestion and press Enter to place it at the next free hour with the same drop and stretch, Delete dismisses it, and placed blocks move a quarter hour with Up and Down.

props.name: hourHeight
props.description: Pixels per hour of the column; the drag maps to it.

props.name: cardStyle
props.description: How blocks and suggestions are drawn: a tinted fill, a dashed outline, or solid pigment.

props.name: tone
props.description: The block colours: token hues at a fixed lightness, so they read in both themes.

props.name: date
props.description: Any time on the day shown, in ms (read in UTC).

props.name: workingHours
props.description: Working hours as whole hours; the column covers them.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: Blocks offered beside the day: { id, label, kind: "focus" | "lunch" | "review" | "inbox" | "prep", minutes }.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The placed blocks, controlled or initial: { id, suggestion, label, kind, start, end } in ms.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drop, key or press that changed the day, with every block.

props.name: onPlace
props.description: A block landed or moved. Return a promise to save it; a rejection keeps it, marked unsaved.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: A suggestion was dismissed (its × or Delete).

props.name: onRemove
props.description: A placed block was removed; its suggestion goes back beside the day.

props.name: now
props.description: The current time in ms; "next free hour" counts from it on its own day. Never read from the clock.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the day has loaded. Loading shows a skeleton column and cards; error marks every placed block unsaved under a Retry banner.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed on the sync banner; unsaved blocks are placed again through onPlace.

props.name: step
props.description: The minutes the column snaps to, and one Up or Down press.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the day in px; its body scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be placed, moved or dismissed.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the suggestions are one roving list (arrows, Home, End). Enter places the focused suggestion at the next free hour with the same drop and stretch a drag gets, then focus moves to the next suggestion; Delete dismisses it. Placed blocks are buttons: Up and Down move them a step, Delete or Backspace removes them and the suggestion returns. Every change is announced politely.

Drag: the card is captured only after 4px, so a tap still places it at the next free hour. The held block is drawn in a layer over the whole surface, so it can leave the suggestion rail or row; the slot is snapped to the step and moved on to the next free time that fits. touch-action is pan-x in the phone row (so the row still scrolls) and pan-y beside the column.

Reduced motion: no tuck, no drop and no stretch — a released or Enter-placed block fades in at its time, and the empty message changes size and place without travel. Times, the open count and the message's words still change.

States: loading shows a skeleton column and cards; a rejected onPlace (or status="error") keeps the blocks on the day, dashed and marked unsaved in their names, under a Retry banner that calls onRetry and saves them again.

Performance: no loops or timers at rest. A drag writes four motion values (position and size of the held block); React renders only when the snapped slot changes. Geometry is measured once at the start of a drag, not per frame.

items.title: Empty Room
items.tagline: A new space waiting for the people who belong.
items.description: The empty state of a space nobody has joined: a table seen from above with a dashed ghost seat for each person the directory suggests. Inviting someone turns their seat solid with a small hop — up on an enter tween, down on springs.recoil, the landing spring — while the disc grows in on springs.snap, one ring leaves the seat, the table warms toward the accent and the copy moves from waiting to welcoming; Invite all runs the hops round the table on cascade(). Seats are buttons in clockwise order, so Tab (or the arrows, Home and End) walks round the table and Enter invites; a refused invite marks its seat for a retry.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: People from the directory, { id, name, role?, reason? }, one per seat in clockwise order from the top left.

props.name: invited / defaultInvited
props.description: Ids of the people already invited, controlled or initial.

props.name: onInvitedChange
props.description: Fires with every invited id once an invite has gone through.

props.name: onInvite
props.description: A seat was pressed. Return a promise to show the invite in flight; a rejection marks the seat for a retry.

props.name: onCopyLink
props.description: The share link was copied (it is also written to the clipboard when one is available).

props.name: inviteLink
props.description: The space's share link, shown in the header and copied by Copy.

props.name: spaceName
props.description: The new space's name; also the surface's accessible name.

props.name: directory
props.description: Where the suggestions come from, used in the copy.

props.name: createdAt
props.description: When the space was created, in ms.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment ages count from, in ms; never read from the clock during render.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading draws blank breathing seats with skeleton names, and nothing can be invited.

props.name: seatCount
props.description: How many chairs the table seats, 4 to 10; the ends take a seat each from six.

props.name: seatShape
props.description: Seats as circles, rounded squares, or chairs whose backs face away from the table.

props.name: accent
props.description: The colour of a taken seat, its welcome ring and the table's warmth. Any CSS colour; seats take its hue at a fixed lightness.

props.name: inviteAll
props.description: Offer Invite all, which seats everyone left in one run round the table.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be invited or copied; the surface dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: every ghost seat is a button in clockwise order, so Tab walks round the table; the arrow keys, Home and End move between seats too. Enter or Space invites; a failed seat's Enter retries. Taken seats stay focusable (aria-disabled) so their names can still be read.
Each outcome is announced politely as one sentence ("Invited Mara Lind. 3 of 8 seats taken."), and Copy renames itself "Link copied" for 1.8 s.
Reduced motion: no hop, ring or orbit; a seat cross-fades from dashed to solid and an invite in flight shows a still dotted ring. The copy, counts and the table's warmth still change.

Performance: nothing runs at rest. The only loop is the marching ring of an invite in flight, and it runs only while the surface is on screen and the tab visible. Hops are motion values on each seat, so they cost no React renders.

Layout follows the container: from 30rem the seats sit round the table with the placard in its middle; below that the table folds into a bench with the seats in a wrapped row. Seat positions mix percent with px, so the table stretches while the seats keep their distance.

items.title: Offline Shelf
items.tagline: We can't reach the server, but here's what we kept.
items.description: A list that failed to load, shown honestly: a banner says the server cannot be reached and why, a countdown runs to the next automatic attempt, and under it sits what the device kept, each row wearing a Cached mark. The wait is one motion value running down at the rate of time; a failed attempt refills it to the next, longer delay on springs.glide. Back online, the marks lift off down the list on cascade() — a stamp rises, grows and turns as it fades on the exit ease — while the fresh rows slide in above on springs.glide, and losing the connection again presses the stamps back on with springs.recoil. R retries now from anywhere inside; the rows are one tab stop where the arrows move and Enter opens.

props.name: cachedItems
props.description: What the device kept from the last load: { id, title, place?, kind?, updatedAt }.

props.name: freshItems
props.description: What the server sent once it answered. New ids slide in above the cached rows; known ids take the fresh copy with a brief wash.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the server can be reached. Online lifts the marks and folds the banner away.

props.name: error
props.description: Why the list did not load, shown as it is with its code in mono.

props.name: cachedAt
props.description: When the cache was written, in ms; drives the stamps' age and the banner copy.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment ages count from, in ms; never read from the clock during render.

props.name: retryDelays
props.description: Seconds to wait before each automatic attempt; the last one repeats.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: An attempt starts. Resolve once the server answered and set status to "online"; reject, or return nothing, and the next wait is longer.

props.name: onOpenCached
props.description: A cached row was opened (Enter or a press) while offline.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: A row was opened while online.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the countdown where it is.

props.name: retryStyle
props.description: How the wait is drawn: a ring that drains round the seconds, a hairline bar along the banner, or ten ticks going out.

props.name: stampStyle
props.description: How a cached row is marked: a rotated rubber stamp with a double rule, a quiet tag, or a dimmed row with a clock.

props.name: tone
props.description: The banner's rule, icon, wash and wait colour.

props.name: title
props.description: The list's name; also the surface's accessible name.

props.name: source
props.description: What cannot be reached, used in the copy and the announcements.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the surface grows before its list scrolls inside, px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be retried or opened and the countdown holds; the surface dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: R retries now from anywhere inside the surface (not while typing in a field); Retry now carries aria-keyshortcuts. The rows are one tab stop with roving focus: Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Enter opens through onOpenCached or onOpen. Row names say whether they come from the cache.

The contract for onRetry: return a promise. Resolving means the server answered (flip status to "online"); rejecting — or returning nothing — counts as a failed attempt and the next wait comes from retryDelays. Each failure, each manual check and the reconnection are announced politely as one sentence; the seconds are never read out per tick.
Reduced motion: the countdown still counts (it is information) but the ring, bar or ticks step once a second; marks and rows cross-fade without lifting, pressing or sliding.

Performance: the only loop is the countdown tween, and it runs only while the surface is on screen, the tab visible, not paused and offline. The seconds are a motion value rendered as text, so a running wait costs no React renders; a render happens once per attempt.

Layout follows the container: from 34rem the banner is one row with the wait at its right; below it the wait sits under the message, and under 26rem the button shortens to Retry and the kind icons hide so titles keep their room. The list scrolls inside maxHeight with a fade at its foot while there is more below.

items.title: First Event
items.tagline: An empty chart, listening for its first point.
items.description: An analytics panel with nothing in it yet, drawn honestly: the axes, the gridlines and a listening pulse at the origin, with the install steps beside it and the minutes counted from a now prop. When the first event arrives the pulse stops, the point drops onto the y-axis and lands on springs.recoil with a ripple along the baseline, and the line begins to draw from it — a clip sweeping right to each new reading — while the scale rises on springs.glide and the steps tick off on springs.flick in a cascade. The steps' Copy buttons are one tab stop that Up, Down, Home and End move through, and silence past the timeout lists what usually goes wrong.

props.name: project
props.description: The project being wired up, named in the header.

props.name: installSteps
props.description: What to do to send the first event, in order: { id, title, detail?, code? }; steps with code get a Copy button.

props.name: events
props.description: Received buckets, oldest first. The first one to arrive plays the drop; later ones extend the line.

props.name: listeningSince
props.description: When listening began, in ms.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment the waiting minutes count to, in ms; never read from the clock during render.

props.name: timeoutMinutes
props.description: Minutes of silence before the pulse slows and the panel lists what usually goes wrong.

props.name: troubleshooting
props.type: { id: string; title: string; detail?: string }[]
props.description: What usually goes wrong, shown once listening times out.

props.name: windowMinutes
props.description: Minutes the x-axis spans from the first event; later readings slide the window.

props.name: metric
props.description: What is being counted, in the chart's words and announcements.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: A step's snippet was copied (it is also written to the clipboard when one is available).

props.name: onCheckNow
props.description: Check now was pressed. Return a promise to show the check in flight.

props.name: pulseStyle
props.description: How the origin listens: rings leaving it, a scanning sweep between the axes, or a breathing dot.

props.name: axisStyle
props.description: Full gridlines, axis lines with tick marks, or just the baseline.

props.name: accent
props.description: The pulse, the line, the points and the finished steps. Any CSS colour.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the surface grows before its body scrolls inside, px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be copied or checked; the surface dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the steps' Copy buttons are one tab stop with roving focus — Up and Down move between steps, Home and End jump, Enter or Space copies and the button renames itself "Step 2 code copied". Check now is a plain button that stays focusable while a check is in flight (aria-busy).

The chart is one role="img" with a sentence that stays current ("No events yet. Listening for 4 minutes." / "53 events since 14:08, peaking at 8 a minute."); the first arrival and the timeout are each announced once.

Reduced motion: the pulse is a still ring, sweep or halo at the origin; the first point fades in where it lands, the line is drawn whole and the scale changes at once. Counts, labels and ticks still change.

Performance: while waiting the only loop is the pulse, and it runs only while the panel is on screen and the tab visible; once data arrives nothing loops. The y-scale is one motion value the line and the points read through useTransform, and the line is revealed by a clip rect rather than a dash on a non-scaling stroke.

Layout follows the container: from 40rem the steps sit in a 272px column beside the chart; below it they stack under a shorter chart, and the body scrolls inside maxHeight. Code snippets scroll sideways inside their own box.

items.title: Theme Fitting
items.tagline: Try on a theme before you keep it.
items.description: An Appearance panel beside a miniature of the app it dresses. Choosing a theme sweeps it across the miniature as a circle growing from the chosen swatch — a clip-path on a tween of revealSpeed, stacked over the old theme and dropped once it covers — while density reflows the miniature's rows and tiles on springs.glide and an accent recolours its accent parts on a short colour tween; Revert sweeps everything back from the Revert button, and Auto follows the system setting. Theme, Density and Accent are radiogroups whose arrows move and select, the chosen ring and thumb slide on springs.snap, and a failed save keeps the choice on and says so.

props.name: themes
props.description: The app's themes, { id, name, palette: { canvas, panel, raised, ink, muted, line } }. Palettes are the app's own fixed colours, so the preview is true on a light or a dark page.

props.name: densities
props.description: Row spacing choices, { id, name, row, pad } in em of the miniature.

props.name: accents
props.description: Accent choices, { id, name, color }.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.type: { theme: string; density: string; accent: string }
props.description: The appearance being tried on, controlled or initial; theme may be "auto".

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the whole appearance from the choice, key or Revert that changed it.

props.name: savedValue
props.description: What is saved and what Revert returns to; omit it and the panel tracks its own saves.

props.name: onThemeChange
props.description: The theme changed.

props.name: onDensityChange
props.description: The density changed.

props.name: onAccentChange
props.description: The accent changed.

props.name: onSave
props.description: Save was pressed. Return a promise to show it saving; a rejection keeps the choice on and says so.

props.name: onRevert
props.description: Revert was pressed, with the saved appearance it returns to.

props.name: allowAuto
props.description: Offer Auto, which follows the system's light or dark setting and sweeps from its own swatch when the system flips.

props.name: appName
props.description: The app in the miniature and the copy.

props.name: previewScale
props.description: The miniature's zoom, 0.8 to 1.2: larger shows less of the app, bigger.

props.name: swatchShape
props.description: Theme and accent swatches as circles, rounded squares, or labelled chips.

props.name: revealSpeed
props.description: How long the circular sweep takes, ms.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the surface grows before its body scrolls inside, px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be chosen, reverted or saved; the surface dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Theme, Density and Accent are each a radiogroup with one tab stop — the arrow keys move and select (wrapping), Home and End jump. Revert and Save are buttons that stay focusable while unavailable or saving (aria-disabled, aria-busy).

The miniature is a role="img" whose name says what it shows ("Preview of Coldbrook in Night, compact rows, moss accent."); its stacked copies are hidden from assistive tech. Choices and save results are announced politely.
Reduced motion: no circular sweep — the new theme cross-fades in 150 ms; rows settle at once; the ring, thumb and tick appear without travel. The colours still change, so the preview stays truthful.

Performance: nothing runs at rest. A sweep is one motion value driving a clip-path in percent of the miniature, measured once by the handler that started it; at most three layers stack, and finished ones are dropped. The miniature is plain DOM sized in em from container units, so it scales with its box and with previewScale.

Auto reads prefers-color-scheme through useSyncExternalStore with a light server snapshot, so the server and the first client render agree. Layout follows the container: from 36rem the miniature sits beside the controls, below it above them.

items.title: Ping Matrix
items.tagline: Choose which events reach you, and where.
items.description: Notification preferences as a grid of switches, events down and channels across. Pressing a channel's heading turns the whole column on (or off when it is all on) and the change runs down the column like falling dominoes: each switch tips forward about its bottom edge on an ease-in, flips while it is down and stands back up on springs.snap, the next starting the moment it hits as the gaps close. A switch that differs from the workspace default carries a mark that pops in on springs.flick, and Reset to defaults runs every edited switch back as one diagonal run. It is a real grid with one roving tab stop — arrows, Home and End, Ctrl with Home or End, Space to toggle, Delete to reset — onChange and onReset fire per cell, and below 760px each event becomes a card of channel chips.

props.name: events
props.description: The rows, { id, label, description? }: what can happen.

props.name: channels
props.description: The columns, { id, label }: where it can reach you.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: On or off for every event and channel (value[eventId][channelId]), controlled or initial; the initial value also counts as saved.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with every preference after each cell changes, run cells included.

props.name: defaults
props.description: The workspace's defaults; a cell that differs carries the edited mark and says what the default is.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (eventId: string, channelId: string, on: boolean) => void
props.description: One cell changed — per cell, also as a column's run reaches it.

props.name: onReset
props.description: One cell went back to the workspace default — per cell, from Delete or Reset to defaults.

props.name: onSave
props.description: Save was pressed. Return a promise to show it saving; a rejection keeps the edits and says so.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading draws switch skeletons, makes the headings inert and marks the grid aria-busy.

props.name: switchStyle
props.description: A track whose knob slides on snap, a box whose tick draws on flick, or a ring whose core grows on snap.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height and how much is said: 40, 52 or 64px rows; compact hides the descriptions.

props.name: accent
props.description: The colour of a switch that is on, the edited marks and the column meters. Any CSS colour.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading and the grid's accessible name.

props.name: workspace
props.description: Whose defaults these are, in the copy and the switches' names.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the surface grows before its body scrolls inside, px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be changed or saved; the surface dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the grid is one tab stop with roving focus across the channel headings and the switches. Arrows move, Home and End reach a row's ends, Ctrl or Cmd with Home or End the corners, Space or Enter toggles a switch or runs a column, and Delete or Backspace puts a switch back to the workspace default.

Each cell is a role="switch" named like "Email for Mentions" — plus ", changed from the Basinworks default (off)" when it carries the mark. Column runs, resets and save results are announced politely as one sentence each; single toggles are left to the switch's own state.

onChange and onReset fire per cell, in the order the run reaches them, so a host can save cell by cell; onValueChange gets the whole value after each one. A failed onSave keeps every edit and says so beside Save.

Reduced motion: nothing tips; switches change in the same order with their colours, and marks fade. Performance: nothing runs at rest; a run is a few motion animations and timers, all stopped on unmount, and the skeletons breathe only while loading.

Layout follows the container: from 47.5rem (760px) it is a table with a sticky heading row; below it each event becomes a card of channel chips in two columns from 34rem and one below that, and the headings become a chip bar.

items.title: Hazard Shelf
items.tagline: Irreversible settings, with their consequences in full.
items.description: The irreversible end of a workspace's settings, where opening an action unrolls a caution-striped panel like a blind off a roll: its height runs to the measured size on springs.glide while a striped roll rides the leading edge, its stripes turning and its thickness thinning as it pays out, then each consequence count fills in from zero a cascade step apart. Typing the workspace name lights each matched letter with an underline drawn on springs.flick and a full match sweeps the confirm button's fill in on springs.snap; Escape, Cancel or opening another action rolls the panel up on the exit ease. Tab and Enter reach every step, and onTransfer, onArchive and onDelete fire only after confirmation.

props.name: actions
props.description: The actions on the shelf, top to bottom: { id, kind: "transfer" | "archive" | "delete", title, summary, touches: { id, count, one, other, note? }[], confirmLabel?, doneLabel? }.

props.name: workspace
props.description: The workspace's name: what the confirm field asks for, and the name in every sentence.

props.name: members
props.description: Who ownership can be transferred to: { id, name, role }.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The open action's id, controlled or initial; an action open at the first render is shown already unrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that opened or rolled up a panel.

props.name: onTransfer
props.description: Fires after a confirmed transfer with the new owner's id; a promise shows it pending, a rejection is reported in the panel.

props.name: onArchive
props.description: Fires after a confirmed archive; may return a promise.

props.name: onDelete
props.description: Fires after a confirmed delete; may return a promise.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the consequence counts have arrived. Loading shows placeholders and error offers Count again; nothing can be confirmed until they are in.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Count again was pressed after the counts failed.

props.name: stripeStyle
props.description: How the caution shows: a striped tape across the panel's top, a rail down its edge, a faint hatch, or a plain hairline.

props.name: density
props.description: Row padding, type size, icon tiles and figure size.

props.name: tone
props.description: The hazard hue: amber caution, red danger, or graphite. Stripes are pigment at a fixed lightness; text keeps the theme's tokens.

props.name: countDuration
props.description: How long the counts take to fill in from zero, ms.

props.name: matchCase
props.description: The typed name must match letter case too.

props.name: title
props.description: The shelf's heading and accessible name.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the shelf grows before it scrolls inside, px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Triggers and confirms are inert and the shelf dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer shelf.

usageNotes: Keyboard: each trigger is a button with aria-expanded; opening one moves focus to the panel's first step as it arrives (the owner radios for a transfer, else the name field), Enter in the field confirms once the name matches, and Escape anywhere in an open row rolls it up and returns focus to its trigger. An unarmed confirm stays focusable (aria-disabled) and sends focus back to the missing step.

Reduced motion: the panel appears at its height with the roll still, counts show their final figures at once, matched letters and the armed fill change colour without drawing. Every state still shows.

Callbacks fire only after confirmation. Return a promise to show the action pending; a rejection keeps the panel open and names what was not done, e.g. "Fernworks was not deleted. 412 documents, 18 members and 3 integrations are unchanged.", with the error's own message appended.
Theming: stripes, the roll and the armed button take the tone token's hue at a fixed lightness, so a large band never turns to mud on a light page; sentences and icons keep the plain text tokens.

Performance: no loop. Height, the roll and its stripe offset are motion values driven by one animation; counts are motion values rendered as text. The shelf scrolls inside its own box and brings an opening panel into view there, never the page.

items.title: Chord Recorder
items.tagline: Press the keys you want, and see what clashes.
items.description: A keyboard shortcut editor whose bindings become recording wells: every key pressed drops in as a keycap from above the rim on springs.snap, lit and pressed down while it is held, and the first key that is not a modifier completes the chord. A taken chord tints the well and nudges the row that owns it sideways on springs.snap, offering Swap, which trades the two bindings and drops both rows' keys in afresh. Enter starts recording, Escape cancels, Backspace clears, Up and Down walk the bindings, and modifier labels follow the platform.

props.name: commands
props.description: The commands, grouped by area: { id, label, area, binding, defaultBinding?, description? }. Bindings are platform-neutral strings such as "Mod+Shift+K" (Mod is Command on a Mac, Control elsewhere).

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Bindings by command id, controlled or initial; null is no shortcut.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with every binding after a record, clear, swap or reset.

props.name: onBind
props.description: A command got a new shortcut, or lost it (null).

props.name: onSwap
props.type: (id: string, otherId: string, binding: string) => void
props.description: A clash was settled by swapping: id took binding and otherId took what id had.

props.name: onReset
props.description: Reset was pressed for one command, or Reset all (null).

props.name: platform
props.description: Which modifier labels to draw: glyphs on a Mac, words elsewhere. Auto reads the platform after mount, so server and first render agree.

props.name: defaultQuery
props.description: Text in the search field at first.

props.name: requireModifier
props.description: A chord needs Command, Control or Option/Alt unless it is a function key; a bare key is refused with a note.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the shortcuts have loaded; loading shows skeleton rows and error offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the shortcuts failed to load.

props.name: keycapStyle
props.description: Keycap look: a raised key with a lip, a flat tile, or a hairline outline.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height, keycap size and type size.

props.name: accent
props.description: Lit keys, the recording well and search marks: a named token or any CSS colour.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a click as each key lands, a lower one when a chord commits or clashes.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading and the editor's accessible name.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the editor, px; the list scrolls inside under sticky area headings.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Bindings cannot be recorded, cleared or reset; the editor dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer editor.

usageNotes: Keyboard: every binding is a button named with its command and spoken chord. Enter starts recording; while recording, keys are captured (Escape cancels, Backspace or Delete alone clears, Tab leaves and cancels). Up and Down move between bindings, Home and End jump, and Backspace on a binding clears it. A clash moves focus to Swap as its notice arrives; Escape there cancels.
Reduced motion: keycaps appear in the well without dropping, the clashing row tints instead of sliding aside, and the recording hint stops pulsing. Lit, warn and committed states still show.

Bindings are stored platform-neutral ("Mod+Shift+K") and drawn per platform: ⌃ ⌥ ⇧ ⌘ glyphs in Mac order on a Mac, Ctrl/Alt/Shift words elsewhere. Keys are read by physical code, so Option-modified characters and keyboard layouts never change what is recorded. formatChord(binding, mac) prints one for your own copy.
Sound is off by default and only answers key presses: a click per landing keycap, pitched by its place in the chord.
Performance: no loop; the list renders plain rows and only the recording well and the clashing row animate. Search filters by label, area, description and the keys themselves.

items.title: Format Sampler
items.tagline: See dates and numbers the way you'll read them.
items.description: Locale and region settings beside a sample invoice that prints them: every weekday, day, month, year, hour, minute, separator and currency mark is a slot, and changing a setting rolls each changed slot to its new form in place — digits on counter wheels on springs.snap, words out on the exit ease and in on snap, widths gliding on springs.glide so neighbours slide aside — with an accent wash fading behind each, while the due day's highlight glides across the week strip on snap. Language, time zone, dates and numbers are type-ahead comboboxes (arrows, Enter, Escape) and time and week start are radio groups. Formats come from hand-written locale tables, so server and browser print the same sample.

props.name: locales
props.description: The languages on offer, each a full format table: month and weekday names, date and time patterns, 12/24-hour, day periods, decimal and group marks, currency placement, week start and the word between date and time.

props.name: timezones
props.description: The time zones on offer: { id, label, offset } with the offset in minutes on the sample's dates.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: { locale, timeZone, date, time, number, weekStart }, controlled or initial; the initial value is also what Discard returns to until a save.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with every setting after any change, including a discard.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires with the field that changed, its new value and every setting.

props.name: onSave
props.description: Save was pressed. A promise shows it saving; a rejection keeps every choice and says so.

props.name: sample
props.description: The invoice the sample prints: { from, reference, amount, currency, due, issued }, times in UTC ms.

props.name: detectedLocale
props.description: The visitor's locale, offered as a one-click suggestion when it differs from the chosen one. Omit to read the browser's language after mount; null offers nothing.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the settings have loaded; loading shows skeleton fields, error offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the settings failed to load.

props.name: sampleStyle
props.description: How the sample is printed: an invoice card with a week strip, one sentence at reading size, or mono receipt rows with dotted leaders.

props.name: density
props.description: Field heights, gaps and type size.

props.name: accent
props.description: The change wash, focused fields, the week highlight and Save: a named token or any CSS colour.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading and the surface's accessible name.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface, px; the body scrolls inside with the sample pinned beside the form.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Every field is read-only and Save does nothing; the surface dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the comboboxes follow the editable APG pattern — type to narrow (type-ahead), Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Enter chooses, Escape closes and then puts the chosen label back. Time and week start are native radio groups moved with the arrows. The sample is read once from an sr-only sentence; its animated slots are hidden from assistive technology, and each change is announced with the new due date.
Reduced motion: slots cross-fade in place, widths change at once and the week highlight jumps; the accent wash still flashes, because what changed is the information.

Formatting never calls Intl during render: each locale is a hand-written table (patterns like "EEEE d MMMM y" and "h:mm a"), so the server and every browser print identical markup. Time zones are fixed offsets on the sample's dates — pass the offsets your own dates need.
Performance: no loop. A digit's counter wheel exists only while it rolls, width glides are one animation per changed slot, and nothing runs at rest.
A failed save keeps every choice and the unsaved count, and Save reads Try again; Discard rolls the sample back to the last saved settings.

items.title: Token Locker
items.tagline: Create, scope and retire API keys safely.
items.description: API token management where a new token is shown once: its characters resolve in place left to right inside 600ms beside a Copy button and a ring that drains linearly, paused under the pointer, then the mask sweeps across a step per character and the panel folds back into its row on springs.glide. Revoking strikes the name through on springs.flick and, a beat later, the row slides down into Revoked as one shared-layout move on glide. Tab reaches every action, C copies the revealed secret, Escape closes a confirm or the create form, and onCreate, onRotate and onRevoke fire.

props.name: tokens
props.description: Seeds the tokens ({ id, name, scopes, created, lastUsed, expires, hint, revoked? }); the locker owns them after that and reports every change.

props.name: scopes
props.description: The scopes on offer, { id, label, group }, shown as grouped checkboxes under tri-state group boxes.

props.name: onTokensChange
props.description: Fires with every token after a create, rotate or revoke.

props.name: onCreate
props.description: Create was confirmed with { name, scopes, expiresInDays }. Return the new secret (or a promise of it); without one a seeded placeholder is minted. A rejection is reported in the form.

props.name: onRotate
props.description: Rotate was confirmed. Return the replacement secret, as for onCreate; it is shown once in the token's row.

props.name: onRevoke
props.description: Revoke was confirmed. A rejection leaves the token active and says so.

props.name: now
props.description: Now in ms, for last used, expiry and the stale flag.

props.name: revealSeconds
props.description: How long a new secret stays readable before it is masked for good, seconds.

props.name: staleDays
props.description: A token unused for this many days (or never used and this old) is flagged.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Printed before every secret and every stored hint.

props.name: workspace
props.description: The workspace the tokens belong to, named in the header and the empty state.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the tokens have loaded; loading shows skeleton rows, error offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the tokens failed to load.

props.name: maskStyle
props.description: How a secret is hidden, in the sweep and at rest: blurred, dotted out, or redacted with bars.

props.name: density
props.description: Row padding, button height and type size.

props.name: palette
props.description: The reveal panel's wash, the countdown ring, the resolve and the primary buttons.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading and the locker's accessible name.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the locker, px; the list scrolls inside.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Create, rotate and revoke are inert; the locker dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer locker.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab reaches every action. New token opens the form with focus in Name (Enter creates, Escape closes); a new or rotated token moves focus to Copy, and C copies from anywhere in the locker except a text field. Rotate and Revoke open an inline confirm whose button takes focus as it arrives; Escape there cancels and returns focus. After a revoke, focus moves to the next token before the row leaves.
Reduced motion: the secret appears whole, the mask fades in at once, folds and the move to Revoked happen without travel, and the strike line appears. The countdown still counts.

Security: the secret is shown once and only from what onCreate or onRotate returns; a stored token keeps just its prefix and last four characters. Without a returned secret the locker mints a seeded placeholder — never use that as a real credential. While shown, the secret sits in an sr-only span (the animated cells are hidden) and is dropped as the mask sweeps.

Performance: the resolve is one requestAnimationFrame loop writing text nodes directly that stops when the last character lands; the countdown is one animation, paused while the pointer rests on the panel, while the page is hidden and while the panel is off screen; the mask sweep is CSS transitions. Nothing runs at rest.
Narrow lockers (under about 42rem) turn rows into cards with a two-column field list and full-width actions.

items.title: Address Cascade
items.tagline: Pick one suggestion and the rest fills itself.
items.description: An address form under a search line: the search is a combobox that looks addresses up as you type, shows a quiet spinner only when a lookup is slow and always ends with Enter it manually. Choosing a suggestion closes the list on the exit ease and fills the fields one after another from top to bottom, staggerSpeed apart, each value sliding down into its field on springs.snap while an accent wash fades behind it and a check pops on snap and goes. Arrows move through the list, Enter picks, Escape closes then clears, and a failed lookup falls back to manual entry with what was typed in the first line.

props.name: fields
props.description: The fields under the search in reading order: { id, label, autoComplete?, span?: "full" | "half", optional?, placeholder? }.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: The addresses the built-in lookup searches: { id, label, detail, values } with a value per field id.

props.name: onSuggest
props.description: Looks addresses up for a query; a promise shows the spinner once slow, a rejection falls back to manual entry. Defaults to filterCascadeSuggestions over suggestions.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Field values by field id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with every value after an edit, a pick or a manual fallback.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (fieldId: string, value: string, values: Record<string, string>) => void
props.description: Fires for each field that changed, with its new value and every value.

props.name: onPick
props.description: A suggestion was chosen from the list.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: The form was submitted with every required field filled; a promise shows Saving…, a rejection says Not saved.

props.name: lookupDelay
props.description: Pretend latency for the built-in lookup, ms.

props.name: spinnerDelay
props.description: A lookup slower than this shows the spinner, ms; faster ones never flash it.

props.name: minQuery
props.description: Characters typed before a lookup runs.

props.name: fieldStyle
props.description: Field look: bordered boxes, an underline, or tinted wells.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns at wide widths, 1 to 3; under about 30rem the form always takes one.

props.name: staggerSpeed
props.description: Time between one field filling and the next in the cascade, ms.

props.name: accent
props.description: The landing wash, the check, the spinner and Save: any CSS colour.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading and the form's accessible name.

props.name: submitLabel
props.description: The submit button's words.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the form grows before it scrolls inside, px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Fields and search are read-only and Save does nothing; the form dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer form.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the search is an APG combobox (aria-activedescendant) — Down and Up open and move, Home and End jump, Enter picks, Escape closes and a second Escape clears. Enter it manually is always the last option and also a link under the field; it carries what was typed into the first line and focuses it. Required fields say what is missing on submit and the first takes focus inside the form, never scrolling the page.

Reduced motion: values appear in place in the same order and stagger without sliding, the wash still flashes and fades, the check appears without popping, and the spinner is a still ring with a Searching label.

The inputs hold the real values the moment a suggestion is chosen — onChange fires for each field then — and only the visible text is staggered: an overlay drawn exactly over each input's own text slides in and hands over when it lands. A field the visitor focuses mid-cascade lands at once.
Lookups are debounced (160ms) and answers that arrive after a newer query are dropped. filterCascadeSuggestions(query, suggestions) is exported for hosts that wrap their own lookup.
Fields carry autocomplete tokens (address-line1, postal-code…) so the browser's own autofill keeps working alongside the lookup.

items.title: Mend List
items.tagline: After submit, everything to fix in one place.
items.description: A long application form that gathers every problem a submit finds into a mend list dropped in above the form and pinned to the top of its scrolling body: the list opens on springs.glide while its items fall in from 8px above on springs.snap in a cascade, each naming the field and the fix. Choosing an item scrolls the body to the field on glide, re-aimed every frame so the field lands just under the pinned list, then the field pulses once with an accent ring and takes focus; from then on checking is live, and the moment a field passes its item strikes itself through on springs.flick while the count rolls down on snap. The list is a labelled nav whose heading takes focus when it drops, Next walks the unmended fields from the keyboard, and a refused submit keeps every answer.

props.name: sections
props.description: The form as sections of fields: { id, title, description?, fields }, each field { id, label, kind, required?, minLength?, pattern?, patternFix?, requiredFix?, options?, placeholder?, hint?, autoComplete?, wide?, validate? }.

props.name: values / defaultValues
props.description: The answers keyed by field id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValuesChange
props.description: Fires from the edit that changed the answers, with all of them.

props.name: onFieldChange
props.description: Fires from each edit with the field, its new value and every answer.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: A submit that passed every check. A promise shows progress on the button; a rejection keeps every answer and says so; resolving with fieldErrors puts the server's words into the mend list.

props.name: onInvalid
props.description: A submit found problems; the ids still to mend, in form order.

props.name: onSaveDraft
props.description: Save draft was pressed; a promise shows it saving, then a check.

props.name: onMend
props.description: An item in the mend list was chosen.

props.name: listStyle
props.description: How the mend list is drawn: a bordered panel of two-line items, a run of chips, or a numbered checklist with a progress bar.

props.name: density
props.description: Field height (32, 36, 40px) and the room between fields and sections.

props.name: accent
props.description: The list's checks, the pulse ring, the strike line and the button's progress, any CSS colour.

props.name: checkOnMount
props.description: Run the submit check on mount so the mend list shows from the first frame.

props.name: title
props.description: The form's heading and accessible name.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: A quiet line under the heading.

props.name: submitLabel
props.description: The submit button's label.

props.name: height
props.description: Panel height in px; the form scrolls inside it and the mend list pins to its top.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading draws placeholder fields and holds the buttons.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be edited, saved or sent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer container.

usageNotes: Keyboard: a submit with problems moves focus to the mend list's heading; each item is a button that scrolls to its field, pulses it and focuses it (the checked radio, or the first). Next walks the unmended fields in order and lands on Submit when none are left. Radios are native radio groups, so arrows move the choice.

Errors are linked to their fields with aria-describedby, aria-errormessage and aria-invalid; the list drop, each mend ("Email mended. 3 left."), a field going bad again, sending, success and failure are announced politely. Submit keeps focus while sending (aria-busy), never disabled.

Reduced motion: the list cross-fades in at full height, the scroll to a field jumps, the pulse is a still ring that fades and the strike appears whole. Counts, checks, strikes, the button's fill and every message still change.

Below 30rem the pinned list folds to one line (count, Next and a Show all toggle with aria-expanded) so it never covers more than a row of the form; choosing an item folds it again. Fields pair into two columns from 36rem.

Nothing runs at rest: one ResizeObserver measures the list, the scroll is a single spring stopped by wheel, touch or unmount, and the rules are exported (checkMendField, findMendProblems) so a host can run the same checks on its server.

items.title: Attendee Rows
items.tagline: Add guests one row at a time, and move them freely.
items.description: A registration form whose guests are rows you can add, remove and move. Add guest unfolds a new row downward out of the button — its slot opens on springs.glide while the row swings down from -72° about its top edge — and removing folds it back up on the exit ease behind an undo chip whose hairline timer drains over five seconds. A row dragged by its grip lifts and follows the pointer 1:1 while the others glide out of its way, then settles into its slot on springs.snap with the release velocity; Alt+Arrow from anywhere in the row (or plain arrows on the grip) moves it with every row travelling on glide, and focus stays where it was.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the row from any field in it, and plain Up and Down move it from its grip; each move is announced ("Theo Park moved to 1 of 4.") and focus stays on the control you were in. Remove hands focus to Undo, Undo hands it back to the row's first field, and an expiring chip returns it to Add guest.

Each row is a labelled group ("Guest 2 of 4, Theo Park"); fields are checked when you leave them after typing and on submit, link their errors with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, and a failed submit focuses the first bad field and names the guests that need fixing.

Reduced motion: rows cross-fade in and out at full height with no swing, keyboard moves are instant and neighbours swap at once; a drag still follows the finger, and the undo timer, badges and counts still change.

The undo timer is one motion animation, held while the chip is hovered or keyboard-focused; nothing else runs at rest. Drag positions live in motion values, never React state per frame, and the grip is touch-action: none so a phone can drag it.

Below 40rem each row becomes a compact card (grip, number, name and remove on top, the fields stacked under it, selects side by side); from 40rem it is a table under a pinned header row whose columns follow `fields`.

items.title: Thread Fields
items.tagline: Follow-up questions hang from the answer that asked them.
items.description: A single-page form where a follow-up question appears directly beneath the answer that asked for it. Choosing that answer opens the follow-ups to their measured height on springs.glide while a thin thread draws from the chosen option down the gutter and hooks into each new question's label, its reveal riding the same value as the height so it reaches each label as the label arrives; changing the answer pulls the thread back up on the exit ease as those questions fold away, keeping their answers, and the new answer's thread drops from its own option. Choice questions are radiogroups whose arrows move and choose, checkbox groups move by arrow and toggle with Space, and nested follow-ups indent with threads of their own.

usageNotes: Keyboard: each choice question is a radiogroup with one tab stop — arrows move and choose (wrapping), Home and End jump — so follow-ups open and fold as you arrow through the answers. Multi-choice questions are groups of checkboxes: arrows move focus, Space toggles.

Revealed and hidden follow-ups are announced politely, frozen at the moment of the change ("2 follow-up questions: How many people, Do you need equipment."); each follow-up block is a group named after the answer that opened it, and the thread itself is aria-hidden.
Only visible questions are checked and submitted, and a failed submit focuses the first one missing an answer. Hidden answers are kept, so changing your mind back brings them back filled.
Reduced motion: follow-ups cross-fade in at full height with the thread already whole, and leave at once; selection, messages and announcements are unchanged.

Nothing runs at rest: the thread is written straight to the SVG from the height animation's frames and a ResizeObserver, never through React state per frame. Below 34rem options stack and the thread runs down the form's left edge.

items.title: Receipt Reader
items.tagline: Drop the receipt; the claim fills itself in.
items.description: An expense claim that fills itself from a receipt: while your reader works a scanning line sweeps the image, and when it answers each place it read is outlined on the receipt in a cascade, then its value lifts out as a small chip that travels into its field — x on springs.glide, y on springs.snap, so the path bows — landing with an accent wash, and readings the reader was unsure of land flagged for a check. Focusing or hovering a field later lights its region again while the others dim, panning the receipt to it when it is out of view. Every value stays editable, Tab moves field to field, Choose file is a real file input, and a failed read keeps the image and falls back to a blank claim.

usageNotes: Keyboard: nothing needs a drag — Choose file opens the system picker through a real file input and Use sample reads the built-in receipt. Tab moves Merchant, Date, Amount, Category, Note, then Submit; focusing a field lights its region on the receipt and pans the receipt to it.

The outlines are decoration (aria-hidden); the information is on the fields, whose descriptions say where each value was read and how sure the reader was ("Read at 62% confidence from the item lines; check it"). Reading, success with the number to check, and failure are announced politely; a failed read moves focus to Merchant.
Reduced motion: the scan line becomes a still Reading band, outlines appear whole and values cross-fade into their fields with the same wash; flags, counts and messages are unchanged.

Performance: the scan loop runs only while reading, on screen and with the page visible; the travelling chips exist only during a landing; a dropped file's object URL is revoked when it is replaced or the component unmounts. Nothing runs at rest.
The sample receipt is drawn in SVG with fixed paper and ink colours so it reads as paper in both themes; give `receipt.src` to show a real image, with regions as fractions of that image.

items.title: Draft Keeper
items.tagline: Your edits are saved, even when someone else edits too.
items.description: A long form that keeps itself: edits queue and are sent as one save a moment after your last keystroke, with an indicator that counts the time since; offline edits pile up with a count that rolls on springs.snap, a failed save keeps the queue and offers Retry, and Ctrl or Cmd+S saves at once. When someone else edits a field you have also changed, their avatar drops onto it on springs.recoil and the field splits along its width on springs.glide into yours and theirs, each with the words the other lacks marked; keeping one slides it into the whole field as the other folds away on the exit ease. Tab reaches the choice and the arrows move between its two buttons.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Ctrl or Cmd+S anywhere in the form saves now (the browser's save dialog is prevented). A split field is a group named "Summary has two versions" holding two labelled regions and their Keep buttons; Tab reaches them and the arrows move between the two. If you were in the field when it split, focus moves to Keep yours; after a choice it returns to the field.

The save indicator's spoken status changes only with its state (saved, saving, offline with the queue, failed with the queue), never per second; the visible time ticks once a second from a timer that runs only while the panel is on screen and the page is shown, slowing to every 15 s after a minute.

Remote edits are taken in the render that brings them, so a conflict present at first load is drawn on the server too; onConflict and onValuesChange for remote edits are reported once each, after that render.
Reduced motion: the versions cross-fade in and out with no split travel, avatars appear in place and the saving dot holds still; counts, marks and messages are unchanged.
Avatars are pigment discs (oklch at a fixed lightness from each collaborator's hue), so they read the same in light and dark themes; the tone tints come from the theme's own surface tokens.

items.title: Twin Preview
items.tagline: Edit the listing and watch the card change.
items.description: A listing editor with the shop card it produces beside it, both driven by one value: the field you are on and its place on the card are lit by twin lenses that glide to each new focus on springs.glide, joined by a thin tether whose ends ride the same springs, and every edit ripples out of the region it changed while the price rolls its digits on springs.snap and new tags pop in on snap. Photos upload inside the card under a scrim whose fill glides to each report, empty required fields stand on the card as dashed ghosts that turn red when Publish refuses, and a Publish that lands brings a Live badge in on springs.recoil. Every field is a real control — photos are one list stop where arrows move, Shift with an arrow reorders, Enter makes a cover and Delete removes — Ctrl/⌘+S saves the draft, Ctrl/⌘+Enter publishes, and below a 36rem container the card waits in a peek tab that rises as a sheet.

usageNotes: Keyboard: every field is a native control. Photos are one tab stop: Left/Right move, Shift with Left/Right reorders, Enter makes the photo the cover, Delete removes it. Pot size is a radiogroup (arrows, Home, End). Tags take Enter or a comma and Backspace in an empty field removes the last. Ctrl/⌘+S saves the draft and Ctrl/⌘+Enter publishes; Escape closes the peek sheet (and is consumed).
A refused Publish names the missing fields in a banner whose links move focus to each, outlines their places on the card, and announces politely; uploads, saves and publishes are announced once each.

The card is measured from your own layout (offsets inside the panel), so lenses and the tether stay true inside scrolled or scaled containers; one ResizeObserver re-measures and nothing animates at rest.
Reduced motion: the lenses and tether jump and fade, ripples become a brief wash on the region, digits and badges swap — progress still fills and outlines still appear.
Product photos are drawn in code from a seed (wall, pot, strands, light); pass your own seeds or swap the art for real images by replacing the photo renderer.

items.title: Margin Help
items.tagline: Help that sits beside the field you're on.
items.description: A form with a help rail: focusing a field glides its help card down the rail until it sits level with that field, on a spring whose landing is springiness — from springs.glide, which settles without overshoot, to springs.recoil, which lands with two bounces — while the card's content cross-fades in one cell, its measured height glides and its notch slides along the edge to keep pointing at the field. A field without help leaves the rail empty, an error opens as a band in the card on springs.snap, the Help switch glides the rail's width away, and below a 40rem container the help becomes an expandable line under each field. Every field's help is its description for assistive technology, the help link sits in the tab order right after its field, and Escape on the link returns to the field.

Unanswered rows read Not answered and offer Answer, Send refuses until they are done, and a send runs a progress bar (the host's progress, or an eased creep) while each section's tick draws on flick, landing a receipt on springs.recoil or keeping every answer when it fails. Enter saves an open row, Escape cancels it, and focus moves to the first field on the way in and back to Change on the way out.

A refused Send names what is open or missing, announces it politely and moves focus to the first row that needs it; each save is announced with the new answer.

Committing the value sends a ripple down the records list beside the form, each record the change touches lighting in a cascade with its diff, while records that already hold the value stay still and fields left alone keep every original. A preview names how many records each change touches, Apply reports only the changed fields and turns into a bar that glides with each record's result while rows tick or cross, and failures are listed with a Retry failed; Tab and Enter work throughout and Escape takes a field back.
