props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface; give it a height and the cards scroll above the tray.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the cards are one roving group of role="checkbox" buttons; arrows travel by the measured columns, Home and End jump, Space or Enter toggle. Blocked add-ons stay focusable with aria-disabled, and their reason is part of their description.
Changes are announced politely with the new total ("Audit log added. Total $116 a month."); the rolling total sits behind a plain sr-only sentence.
Reduced motion: no flight — chips fade in and out of the tray, the total swaps, checks appear without drawing, and the price shimmer is a still bar.
List conflicts on both add-ons (conflicts: ["backup"] on one and ["residency"] on the other); an add-on with requires names the plan it needs and can never be turned on here.
The odometer reserves the width of the largest possible total, so the tray never shifts while digits roll.
Performance: the flier exists only during a flight and the shimmer runs only while prices load and the tray is in view.

items.title: Pause Instead
items.tagline: Before cancelling, see what stops and what stays.
items.description: A cancellation flow built from plan, usage and offers: the reason, what changes, then a plain choice, in a step bar whose pill slides on springs.snap while each step cross-slides 8px on springs.glide inside a box that glides to its measured height. When "What changes" comes into view the losses switch off one at a time inside the 600ms budget — a mini switch flips on snap, a strike sweeps on glide, or a tile's live bar drains — and the pause offer slides up 16px beneath on glide with a resume date that rolls as the length changes. Reasons and pause lengths are radiogroups (arrows, Home, End), every step and decision is a real button, and a step change moves focus to its heading.

props.name: formatDate

props.name: formatMoney
props.description: How a price is written.

props.name: disabled

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: reasons and pause lengths are radiogroups with roving tabindex (arrows move and select, Home and End jump); every step action and decision is a button. A step change moves focus to the new step's heading, bound when it arrives; pending decisions keep focus with aria-busy rather than disabling.

Each loss reads as one sentence ("Shared boards: 14 boards go read-only for 8 members. Switches off on 12 Nov 2026."); the switch-off and every outcome are announced once in a polite status, and a failed decision is a role="alert" strip.
The switch-off waits until the step is in view and is driven by one timer at a time, so leaving the view or a StrictMode rehearsal resumes it where it was; there are no loops.
Reduced motion: nothing travels — steps cross-fade and the offer fades in — but the losses still go off one at a time, because that order is the information.
Lays out by container: one column under 36rem (inactive step labels collapse to numbers under 26rem), losses beside what stays and the two offers side by side above it.

items.title: Credit Refill
items.tagline: Running low; top up without leaving the work.
items.description: A low-credit sheet that docks over the work it interrupts, showing what remains and how long it lasts at the current rate. Choosing a pack pours the balance gauge — a vial, a flask or a capsule of liquid — up to the new total on springs.glide while its surface leans against the pour and settles as a damped slosh, the bought share firming from a lighter band when the charge goes through; one frame loop runs only while the liquid moves. Packs are a radiogroup whose highlight slides on springs.snap, auto-recharge reveals a threshold slider that follows the pointer 1:1 and settles on its step with the release velocity, and arrows, Page keys, Home and End drive both.

usageNotes: Keyboard: packs are a radiogroup (arrows move and select, Home and End jump); the threshold is a role="slider" with valuetext (arrows step 50, Page Up and Page Down 250, Home and End); Escape inside the sheet dismisses it and focus moves to the reopen pill, and reopening focuses the sheet's heading.
The gauge is role="meter" with a valuetext sentence; Buy keeps focus while charging (aria-busy) and a declined payment is a role="alert" with the reason, the pack still chosen.

Performance: the liquid's frame loop runs only while the level or the slosh is moving and stops when settled, off screen or in a hidden tab; the paths are written through motion values, never React state.
Reduced motion: the level steps on a short tween with a still surface; the band, figures and runway still change.
No scrim and nothing inert: the work stays usable. Under a 36rem container the sheet covers the width as a bottom sheet; wider, it floats bottom-right at 24rem.

items.title: Upgrade Request
items.tagline: Ask your admin for the upgrade in one tap.
items.description: A member's upgrade request: the locked feature, the admins who can approve it as a radiogroup, and a card with the plan and a note. Send folds the card into an envelope that scales from the card's measured box on springs.glide while its flap closes on springs.snap, then flies to the chosen admin's avatar with x on glide and y on springs.drift so the path arcs, where the ring lands and a Pending chip arrives on springs.recoil. Approval unlocks the feature in place — the shackle swings open on snap and the veil lifts — and a decline shows the admin's note with a way to ask someone else; admins move with arrows, Home and End, and focus moves to Remind once the request lands.

props.name: admins

props.name: plan

props.name: feature

props.name: onRequest

props.name: onRemind

props.name: envelopeStyle

props.name: accent

usageNotes: Keyboard: admins are a radiogroup with roving tabindex (arrows, Home, End); the note is a labelled textarea whose count is its description; Send stays focusable while sending (aria-busy), and focus moves to Remind when the request lands.
The envelope layer is aria-hidden and every outcome is announced once ("Asked Priya Raman at 14:32. Pending."); each admin's name carries their role, presence and the request's state.

The flight is one set of animate() calls measured against the surface at the moment of sending, so it flies true inside any scroller; unmounting or a StrictMode rehearsal lands it rather than freezing it. Nothing runs at rest.
Reduced motion: nothing folds or flies — the card cross-fades to the pending summary and the chip fades in; the lock opens with a fade.
Lays out by container: stacked under 36rem with the preview trimmed to two versions, the locked preview beside the admins and card above it.

items.title: Passkey Enrol
items.tagline: Add a passkey so the password can retire.
items.description: A passkey setup step: a key inside a disc with rings round it, a short explanation, Create, and the devices already enrolled. While the platform prompt is open the rings draw slowly one after another on a symmetric tween and then turn very slowly, only in view and in a visible tab; success contracts every ring onto the key on springs.glide, outer ones a beat behind, into a solid mark that settles on springs.snap with a check drawn on springs.flick, while the new device slides into the list from 8px on glide with a New chip landing on springs.recoil. Rename edits in place (Enter saves, Escape cancels), Remove asks in the row, and cancelled prompts and unsupported browsers each get a plain message and a fallback.

props.name: account
props.description: Whose passkeys these are: { name, email }.

props.name: devices / defaultDevices
props.description: The enrolled devices: { id, name, kind, addedAt, lastUsedAt? }, controlled or initial.

props.name: onDevicesChange
props.description: Fires with the whole list after an enrol, a rename or a remove.

props.name: onEnrol
props.description: Opens the platform prompt; resolve with the new device, reject with { reason: "cancelled" | "unsupported" | "error" } or the platform's NotAllowedError.

props.name: onRename

props.name: onRemove

props.name: onFallback

props.name: supported

props.name: now

props.name: ringCount

props.name: drawDuration

props.name: title

props.name: maxHeight

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: Create stays focusable while the prompt is open (aria-busy); every row's Rename and Remove are buttons named with the device; Rename's field saves on Enter and Escape cancels and returns focus; after a remove, focus moves to the next device (or Create).
The rings are aria-hidden; each phase is one polite sentence, and cancelled, unsupported and failed prompts each get a plain paragraph with a fallback button.
Wire onEnrol to the platform's credential creation; a rejection with name NotAllowedError (the visitor closed the prompt) reads as cancelled, NotSupportedError as unsupported.
Performance: the ring turn runs only while the prompt is open, in view and in a visible tab; the draws are one-shot tweens and nothing runs at rest.
Reduced motion: the rings sit fully drawn and breathe in opacity while the prompt is open; success cross-fades to the solid mark and the new row fades in.

items.title: Inbox Wait
items.tagline: We've sent a link; this page will notice.
items.description: A magic-link waiting screen where an envelope rests in a slow breathing glow — a mirrored tween whose strength is glowAmount, running only while waiting, in view and in a visible tab — beside the address, a Resend that counts down and a way to change the address. The page notices the link opening through a BroadcastChannel another tab posts to, an onCheck asked when the tab regains focus, or the host's status; then the flap swings open on springs.snap, the letter rises on springs.glide and grows into the signed-in welcome through a shared layout on glide while the welcome's lines arrive in a cascade. Expired links and links opened on another device each explain the next step.

props.name: email
props.description: Where the link went.

props.name: status / defaultStatus
props.description: The page's state, controlled or initial.

props.name: onStatusChange
props.description: Fires when the page notices the link opened, the link expires, or a new link goes out.

props.name: sentAt
props.description: When the link was sent, in ms.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment the page first renders, in ms; its timers count on from it.

props.name: resendAfter
props.description: Seconds before Resend becomes available.

props.name: expiresAfter
props.description: Minutes a link stays valid; the page turns to expired when it lapses.

props.name: onResend
props.description: Resend was pressed; a promise holds the button.

props.name: onChangeEmail
props.description: A new address was saved; a fresh link is assumed to have gone to it.

props.name: onVerified
props.description: The page noticed the link was opened, and how ("channel", "check" or "host"); fires once per link.

props.name: onContinue
props.description: Continue was pressed on the welcome.

props.name: channel
props.description: A BroadcastChannel name; another tab posts { type: "verified", name? } (or "expired", "other-device").

props.name: onCheck
props.description: Asked when the tab regains focus (and every pollInterval ms while visible); resolve true once the link has been opened.

props.name: pollInterval

props.name: name
props.description: Who the welcome greets.

props.name: product

props.name: envelopeStyle

props.name: glowAmount
props.description: How strongly the resting envelope glows, 0 to 1; 0 is unlit and still.

props.name: tone
props.description: The glow, the seal and the primary action: cobalt, amber or ink.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Resend and Change email are unavailable.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface; it is max-w-sm unless widened here.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Resend is a button with aria-disabled until its timer ends and its name carries the wait ("Resend link, available in 24 seconds"); the countdown itself is announced only when it reaches zero. Change email swaps in a labelled field (Enter sends, Escape cancels) and focus returns to Change email.
A status change moves focus to the new heading only when focus was already inside (or nowhere), so a link noticed in the background never steals focus from the rest of the page.

Timers never read the clock in render: they count on from now, schedule only the next tick that changes something, pause in a hidden tab and re-sync when it is shown. The glow loop stops off screen, in a hidden tab, at glowAmount 0 and in every state but waiting.
Close the BroadcastChannel loop by posting from the page the link opens: new BroadcastChannel(name).postMessage({ type: "verified", name }).
Reduced motion: the glow is a still halo and the envelope cross-fades to the welcome; nothing travels.

items.title: Workspace Lobby
items.tagline: Choose which workspace to open.
items.description: The screen after sign-in: your workspaces as tiles with role, people and last visit, invitations in their own row, and a way to create one. Choosing a tile grows its real box from the tile's measured place to fill the panel on springs.glide while every other tile steps back on the same spring, the workspace's spaces cascade in under a loading line, and the answer resolves to a check drawn on springs.flick — or folds the tile back with the reason; a single accent plate travels between tiles on springs.snap. The tiles are a listbox: arrows walk them by their rendered rows, letters jump by name, Enter opens and Escape folds back.

props.name: invitations

props.name: onDecline

props.name: onSwitchAccount

props.name: onRetry

props.name: columns

props.name: accent

props.name: title

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the panel grows, in px, before its body scrolls.

props.name: disabled

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: the tiles are a role="listbox" with roving tabindex — Left and Right move one, Up and Down move a rendered row (columns are measured, so it works at every width), Home and End jump, letters jump by name, Enter or Space opens. While a workspace opens the list is inert, focus moves to the panel's Cancel, Escape folds it back and focus returns to the tile.
Each tile's accessible name is one sentence — name, role, members, last visit, unread — and opening, opened, failure and joining are each announced once in a polite live region.

Return a promise from onSelect to hold the expanded tile while the workspace loads; reject with an Error and its message is shown on the tile it folds back to. A late answer for a cancelled opening is ignored.
Times come from the now prop in fixed buckets ("2 h ago", "Yesterday"), so the server and the browser render the same words.
Reduced motion: nothing travels or scales — the panel cross-fades in at full size, the other tiles dim, the plate moves instantly — and the loading line still fills and the check still appears.
No loop at rest: the only repeating animation is the loading line, mounted only while a workspace is opening.

items.title: Org Discovery
items.tagline: Type your email; we find your company's sign-in.
items.description: A sign-in step that finds a company's own sign-in from the email domain. When a typed domain is recognised, a wash appears behind the domain's own letters — found to the pixel from a hidden mirror of the field's text — and lifts off them onto the field's top edge, growing into a badge with the company's mark on springs.glide while its shadow swells in flight and settles; the main button's words roll to single sign-on on springs.snap and the password folds away to its measured height on glide. Change the address and the badge drops back into the field where the domain now starts; it is a real form, so Tab, Enter and the announcements all behave as a sign-in should.

props.name: orgs

props.name: lookup

props.name: onForgotPassword

props.name: onOrgChange

props.name: error

props.name: productName

props.name: badgeStyle

props.name: density

props.name: accent

props.name: showAside

props.name: disabled

props.name: className

usageNotes: It is a real <form>: the email field is type="email" with autocomplete="username", the password field autocomplete="current-password", Enter submits, and the submit button stays focusable while busy (aria-busy). Errors are role="alert" and linked to their field with aria-describedby and aria-invalid.

The badge is decorative; the field is described by a visually hidden sentence ("Basinworks uses single sign-on through Basinworks ID.") and the change is announced once in a polite live region, from the lookup or the keystroke that caused it.

Pass lookup to ask your own service; answers that arrive after the address changed are dropped by sequence, a rejection falls back quietly to the password and code, and a failed domain is tried again the next time it is typed.
Reduced motion: nothing travels — the badge fades in and out at its resting place on the field's edge, the button's words cross-fade and the sections swap without folding.
No loop at rest: the three lookup dots breathe only while a lookup is pending, and one ResizeObserver keeps a resting badge and the domain's tether in place as the field resizes.

items.title: Recovery Route
items.tagline: Locked out? Choose the way back in.
items.description: An account recovery chooser drawn as a map: you on one side, the ways back in on the other — backup code, recovery email, trusted contact, support review — each with how long it takes. Choosing one draws the route from you to its card, revealed along its own length by a mask whose stroke runs on springs.glide with a traveller riding the leading point, and the card's notch answers with a ring on springs.snap; the steps slide in 16px from the side the choice came from under an honest wait counted from now. The methods are a real radio group — arrows choose and skip the ones not set up — and below 44rem of container the route runs down a gutter beside the list.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the methods are a role="radiogroup" with roving tabindex; arrows move and choose, skipping methods that are not set up (they stay readable with aria-disabled and their reason as the description), Home and End jump, Space and Enter choose.

Each step list is an ordered list with the current step marked aria-current="step"; inputs are labelled, errors are role="alert" linked by aria-describedby, and submit buttons stay focusable while busy (aria-busy). A choice is announced once with its wait.
The route is decorative and measured from the rendered cards by one ResizeObserver, so it lands on each card's notch at any width and density; the first draw waits until the map is on screen.
Times are counted from the now prop; pass formatTime to write them in the visitor's own zone once you are past hydration.
Reduced motion: the route appears whole without a traveller, the notch shows without its ring, and the steps cross-fade in place; ticks and the honest wait still show.

items.title: Spare Keys
items.tagline: Ten backup codes, saved before you continue.
items.description: A backup codes sheet that has to be kept before you go on. The codes are dealt onto the sheet when it comes into view — each ticket leaves a tilted deck above the grid and flies to its cell on springs.glide while its tilt settles on springs.snap, staggered by cascade — and Copy all flashes every ticket in turn as its code lands on the clipboard. Continue carries a padlock that stays shut until the box is ticked, then its shackle lifts and turns open about its right leg on springs.snap. Every action is a button: each ticket copies itself, Download saves a .txt, Print prints the codes alone, and Regenerate warns in place, strikes the old set and deals the new one.

props.name: account

props.name: issuer

props.name: columns

props.name: accent

props.name: deal

props.name: disabled

props.name: className

usageNotes: Every action is a real <button>, including each ticket (named "Code 4, h2wy 7ke6, copy"); the grid is a list labelled by the heading. The confirmation is a real checkbox, and Continue stays focusable while locked (aria-disabled, described by "Tick the box to continue") — pressing it lights the box's row instead.

Copy, download, print and regenerate results are announced once in a polite live region. Regenerate opens a warning in place of the actions with its safer button focused; Escape closes it and returns focus to Regenerate.
The clipboard write is attempted quietly: on a page without clipboard access the flash still shows and onCopy still fires, so the host can offer another way.
Reduced motion: nothing is dealt or turns — the tickets are simply there, Copy all marks every ticket at once, and the lock shows open while Continue still takes the accent.

No loop: the deal runs once per set after the sheet enters view (IntersectionObserver, disconnected after), flashes are timed animations stopped on unmount, and the print frame and download URL are removed after use.

items.title: Authenticator Pair
items.tagline: Scan, enter the code, and two-step is on.
items.description: An authenticator setup: a QR code with the secret written beside it for typing by hand, then a six-digit check. When it comes into view the QR assembles from its centre outward in square rings of modules, each fading up from 0.6 scale on springs.snap with the finder eyes landing in their ring; digits drop into their slots on springs.flick and a paste lands left to right. A correct code folds the rings back into the centre from the outside in, a disc grows on snap, a check draws across it on flick and the step marker's pill slides on to On; a wrong code nudges on a short tween and keeps the digits.

props.name: secret
props.description: The shared secret, base32, shown in groups of four for typing by hand.

props.name: account
props.description: The account the app will list.

props.name: issuer
props.description: The service the app will list.

props.name: modules
props.description: A real QR matrix from your encoder (true is dark). Omitted, a seeded 25 × 25 stand-in with real finder, timing and alignment patterns is drawn from the secret.

props.name: digits
props.description: How many digits the app shows.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The code, controlled or initial; non-digits are dropped.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from every keystroke or paste in the code field, digits only.

props.name: onVerify
props.description: Checks a full code. True turns two-step on; false keeps the digits and says so; a throw says the check failed. Omitted, any full code is accepted.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Cancel was pressed in the footer.

props.name: onCopySecret
props.description: The setup key was copied (spaces removed).

props.name: onDone
props.description: Done was pressed after two-step turned on.

props.name: autoSubmit
props.description: Check the code as soon as the last digit lands, whether typed, pasted or set by the host; each code is checked once.

props.name: assemble
props.description: When the QR assembles from its centre; the server renders it whole.

props.name: status
props.description: A still placeholder while the key is made; a message and Try again on error.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the key failed to load.

props.name: moduleStyle
props.description: Crisp squares, dots with round finders, or soft rounded squares.

props.name: density
props.description: QR size, paddings, slots and type.

props.name: accent
props.description: The step marker, the next slot, the finder eyes (deepened so they still scan), the check disc and Verify, any CSS colour.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the panel grows, in px, before its body scrolls.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be typed, copied or pressed.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the wrapper.

usageNotes: The code is one real <input inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="one-time-code"> drawn as slots, so autofill, paste and screen readers all see an ordinary field; its label is the step's heading and errors are role="alert" linked by aria-describedby. Verify stays focusable while checking (aria-busy).

The QR is an img named "QR code for Fieldline, mara@fieldline.io" and the key beside it is real, selectable text with a Copy button. Pass modules from your own encoder for a code that scans; it is always printed dark on a light plate so it scans in dark mode too.

The marker is an ordered list with aria-current="step"; success is announced once ("Two-step sign-in is on."). A refused code keeps the digits and, if the field has focus, selects them so typing replaces them — focus is never pulled into the field from elsewhere.
Reduced motion: the QR fades in whole and cross-fades to the check disc with its check drawn; digits appear without dropping and the wrong-code nudge becomes the slots' danger underline.
No loop at rest: the assembly is one path per ring (about a dozen elements, not one per module), run once after the panel enters view; the matrix is memoised per secret.

items.title: Step Up Check
items.tagline: Confirm it's you before the sensitive change.
items.description: A step-up verification standing in front of a sensitive settings panel: the panel sits behind a real backdrop-blur frost while a dialog asks for a passkey or password. Verifying opens the lock on snap, then the frost clears outward from the lock itself, its radial mask growing on glide with an accent ring riding the edge, while the opened lock flies into the header chip on the same spring and the chip counts the elevated session down; expiry closes the frost back in toward the lock on glide. Refused tries shake the field on a symmetric tween and are counted and explained, Tab wraps inside the dialog, Escape dismisses it to an Unlock button, and below 28rem the dialog becomes a bottom sheet.

props.name: action
props.description: The sensitive change, as it reads after "You're about to".

props.name: methods
props.description: The ways to verify, in the order offered; the first is the primary one.

props.name: account
props.description: Who is verifying, shown under the title.

props.name: heading
props.description: The protected section's name, in the header strip beside the session chip.

props.name: title
props.description: The dialog's title.

props.name: children
props.description: The protected content; inert and frosted until verified. A quiet placeholder panel when omitted.

props.name: verified / defaultVerified
props.description: Whether the elevated session is open, controlled or initial.

props.name: onVerifiedChange
props.description: Fires from the verification, expiry or Lock now that changed it.

props.name: onVerify
props.type: (attempt: { method, password? }) => boolean | void | Promise<boolean | void>
props.description: Checks a try. Return or resolve false, or reject, to refuse it; an Error's message is shown as the reason. Accepts every try when omitted.

props.name: onFail
props.description: A try was refused, with the tries left and the reason shown.

props.name: onExpire
props.description: The elevated session ran out and the panel locked again.

props.name: onLock
props.description: Lock now was pressed on the session chip.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Not now, or Escape, dismissed the dialog; the panel stays locked.

props.name: sessionDuration
props.description: How long the elevated session lasts, in ms.

props.name: warnAt
props.description: How long before the end the chip turns to a warning, in ms.

props.name: maxAttempts
props.description: Refused tries before verification pauses.

props.name: forgotHref
props.description: Where "Forgot password?" goes; the link is hidden when omitted.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Move focus into the dialog when it first shows. Leave off when the check renders with the page.

props.name: frostAmount
props.description: How heavy the frost is, 0 to 1: blur radius and tint strength.

props.name: lockStyle
props.description: The lock's glyph and how it opens: a shackle that swings, a key slot that turns, or a check drawn on flick.

props.name: accent
props.description: Any CSS colour for the badge, the primary button, the clearing edge and the session chip.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Every method is unavailable.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer section.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the dialog traps Tab and takes Escape (dismissing to an Unlock button that brings it back focused); Enter submits the password; after verifying, focus moves to the session chip, whose Enter is Lock now.
Reduced motion: nothing travels or shakes — the frost fades out, the lock swaps to open, the chip cross-fades — while the countdown, the counted tries and the reasons still update.

Performance: nothing runs while locked; the countdown ticks once a second only while the surface is on screen and the tab visible, expiry is one wall-clock timeout, and the frost layer is hidden once clear so no backdrop blur costs anything while elevated.
Pass your real panel as children: it stays mounted (inert while locked), so its state and scroll survive the check.
The dialog never takes focus on mount unless autoFocus is set, so a page that renders the check does not jump to it.
Colours come from tokens and the accent prop; the button text picks light or dark ink from the accent's lightness, so any accent reads in both themes.

items.title: Session Lapse
items.tagline: Still there? Stay signed in with a tap.
items.description: An idle-timeout guard for a page: before the session ends an alert dialog rises over it with a ring that drains linearly while the seconds in its middle count down, both read off one motion value. Stay signed in, Escape, or a press, key or scroll outside the dialog refills the ring on glide while it pops on snap and the seconds count back up, then the dialog leaves on the exit ease; letting it run out fades the page into a signed-out note that keeps the unsaved draft. Focus moves to Stay signed in when the warning appears, Tab wraps inside it, and the countdown is announced when the warning appears, at 30 seconds in longer warnings, and at 10.

props.name: timeout
props.description: Idle time before the session ends, in ms.

props.name: warningTime
props.description: How long before the end the warning appears, in ms; the ring counts this window down.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the warning is showing, controlled or initial.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires when the warning appears or leaves, from whatever caused it.

props.name: watch
props.description: Whose activity keeps the session alive: the whole page, only this component's box, or nothing but the button.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the idle clock (a call, a video); it restarts when released, and a showing warning holds its time.

props.name: onExtend
props.description: The session was extended, by the button or Escape, or by activity during the warning.

props.name: onSignOut
props.description: Sign out was chosen from the warning.

props.name: onExpire
props.description: The warning ran out and the session ended.

props.name: onSignIn
props.description: Sign back in was pressed on the signed-out note.

props.name: draft
props.type: { title: string; excerpt: string; words?: number } | null
props.description: The unsaved work the signed-out note promises to keep; null for none.

props.name: appName
props.description: The product's name, in the warning's sentence and the announcements.

props.name: title
props.description: The warning's title. Defaults by tone: "Still there?", "Are you still working?", "Signing out soon".

props.name: labels
props.type: { stay?: string; signOut?: string; signIn?: string }
props.defaultValue: Stay signed in · Sign out · Sign back in
props.description: The three actions' words.

props.name: ringStyle
props.description: How the countdown is drawn: a draining line, a tick per second, or a shrinking sector.

props.name: tone
props.description: The ring's colour and the title's voice: cobalt, ink, or amber turning to danger for the last ten seconds.

props.name: children
props.description: The page the session belongs to; inert while the warning or the note shows. A quiet placeholder when omitted.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer wrapper.

usageNotes: Keyboard: focus moves to Stay signed in when the warning appears (unless the visitor is busy elsewhere on the page, or the warning is off screen); Tab wraps inside the dialog and Escape stays signed in. When the note arrives, focus goes to Sign back in if it was inside.

Activity: before the warning any pointer, key or scroll activity in scope moves the clock on; once it shows only a press, a key or a scroll outside the dialog extends, so reaching for Sign out with the pointer never cancels the warning.
Reduced motion: the ring still drains and the seconds still count, because the time left is information; the refill is a jump and the dialog and note only cross-fade.

Performance: while the page is in use nothing ticks — one timeout marks when the warning is due; the drain runs only while the ring is on screen and the tab visible, and expiry is a single wall-clock timeout.
The page stays mounted (inert and faded) behind the note, so the draft's state survives the sign-out and comes back on Sign back in.

items.title: Invite Accept
items.tagline: Mara invited you to Basinworks; join in two steps.
items.description: An invitation landing whose invite is a card: the workspace, who asked, a personal line, the role with what it can do, and when it lapses. Accept turns the card over on snap — its scale dipping with the angle by exactly what perspective adds, so it never grows past its box — while the role chip lifts off on flick, travels flat to its slot on the back on glide and lands on snap, carrying the role to a sign-up form with the name and email already filled. The form is real (labels, autocomplete, Enter submits, errors under their fields, a rejected join kept on the form), focus moves to the first empty field after the turn, Escape turns back, and an expired invite offers to ask again.

props.name: invite
props.type: { inviter, workspace, role, roleSummary?, email, name?, note?, sentAt, expiresAt }
props.description: The invitation: who sent it, the workspace, the role (and what it can do), the invitee and when it lapses.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment expiry counts from, ms since the epoch; the clock is never read during render.

props.name: side / defaultSide
props.description: Which face of the card is up, controlled or initial.

props.name: onSideChange
props.description: Fires from the Accept, Back or Escape that turned the card.

props.name: onAccept
props.type: (details: { name, email, password, role }) => void | Promise<void>
props.description: The form was sent. A promise holds it pending; a rejection keeps the form with its message, or puts it under the field its `field` names.

props.name: onDecline
props.description: Decline was pressed.

props.name: onSignIn
props.description: Sign in was chosen instead, with the invite's address.

props.name: onRequestNew
props.description: A new invite was asked for, after expiry or a decline.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the invite has loaded: a skeleton while loading, a broken-link card on error.

props.name: passwordMinLength
props.description: The shortest password the form accepts; the hint ticks when it is met.

props.name: cardStyle
props.description: The card's make: a plain card, a ticket with notches and a perforated stub, or a pass with a coloured band.

props.name: flipAxis
props.description: The axis the card turns about: sideways or top over bottom.

props.name: accent
props.description: Any CSS colour for the workspace mark, primary buttons, pass band, role chip and checks.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Every action is unavailable.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer section.

usageNotes: Keyboard: every button and field is reachable; Enter on Accept turns the card and focus lands on the first empty field once it faces; Enter submits; Escape on the back turns it back with focus on Accept.
Reduced motion: the faces cross-fade without turning and the role chip simply appears in its new place; checks appear without drawing and the loading shimmer is still.
The hidden face is inert, so its fields never take Tab or reach assistive tech; errors are tied to their fields with aria-describedby and the form's own failure is a role="alert" that stays.
Pass `now` from your server (or a stable value) so the expiry line renders the same on the server and in the browser.
Performance: nothing runs at rest; the turn and the chip's flight are springs that settle, and the only loop is the loading shimmer, which exists only while status is "loading".

items.title: Cooling Lock
items.tagline: Too many tries; the lock cools before the next.
items.description: A lockout panel for after repeated failed sign-ins: frost covers a ring round the lock and thaws clockwise from the top as the wait runs down, in six-armed flakes that shrink on snap and leave a slipping droplet as the front passes, bristling hoarfrost that shortens at the front, or a glaze that drains as one arc. When the last of it melts the shackle lifts on snap and the copy gives way on glide to the sign-in form with the address kept; a new lockout freezes the ring back over on glide before the wait starts again, and a very long one points to support. Unlock by email is always offered, the countdown is announced at sensible marks, and focus moves to the password field when the form returns.

props.name: attempts
props.description: Failed sign-ins that caused the lock.

props.name: cooldown
props.description: How long the lock lasts, in ms.

props.name: lockedAt
props.description: When the lock began, ms since the epoch. A new value starts a new lockout and the frost grows back.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment the remaining time is measured from, ms since the epoch; the clock is never read during render.

props.name: email
props.description: The account being signed in to; kept for the retry and the unlock link.

props.name: onRetry
props.type: (retry: { email, password }) => boolean | void | Promise<boolean | void>
props.description: The retry was sent. Return or resolve false, or reject, to refuse it; an Error's message is shown.

props.name: onUnlockByEmail
props.description: Unlock by email was pressed; a promise holds it as sending.

props.name: onThaw
props.description: The wait ran out and the form came back.

props.name: supportAfter
props.description: Lockouts longer than this, in ms, point to support instead of counting down.

props.name: supportHref
props.description: Where Contact support goes on a long lockout.

props.name: appName
props.description: The product's name, in the sentences.

props.name: frostStyle
props.description: The frost's material: six-armed flakes, bristling hoarfrost, or a smooth glaze of ice.

props.name: density
props.description: How dense and thick the frost is, 0.2 to 1: flake and spike counts and the band's width.

props.name: tone
props.description: The voice and the lock's colour: calm cobalt, firm ink, or stern red.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The retry and the unlock link are unavailable.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer section.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Unlock by email is always reachable; when the form returns, focus moves to the password field if it was already in the panel, Enter signs in, and a refusal keeps focus in the field with the reason under it.
Announcements: the digits are hidden from assistive tech; a polite status says how long the wait is, then 5 minutes, 1 minute, 30 and 10 seconds, and when the lock has cooled.
Reduced motion: the ring still thaws by the same front, because the time left is information; flakes fade without shrinking, droplets do not slide, and the copy cross-fades in place.
Performance: the thaw and the once-a-second digits run only while the panel is on screen and the tab visible; the end is one wall-clock timeout, and a long lockout runs nothing at all.
Re-lock by passing a new lockedAt (and cooldown) from your server's answer; a refused retry the host answers with a new lockout shows the frost, not a stale error.
The frost is pigment mixed from the accent token at a fixed lightness, so it reads the same in light and dark themes.

items.title: Number Match
items.tagline: Tap the number you see to approve the sign-in.
items.description: A new-device approval drawn as the two screens it happens on: the browser signing in, showing a two-digit number, and the trusted phone asking whether it's you with three numbers to choose from. The right choice joins the screens — a line grows from the number and from the phone's frame level with the chosen key, each half on glide, and they meet in the middle where a dot lands on recoil — while both screens turn to success and a check stamps on recoil; a wrong one reaches in danger, stops short and draws back on a tween as both screens explain the block. The choices are buttons with roving focus (arrows, Home, End; Enter or Space chooses), outcomes are announced, a lifetime bar drains only while it can be seen, and the screens sit side by side, overlap or mirror, stacking in a narrow container.

props.name: request
props.type: { number, choices?, device, place, time, account }
props.description: The sign-in being approved: the number shown, the phone's choices (seeded when omitted), and what, where and when.

props.name: status / defaultStatus
props.description: Where the request stands, controlled or initial.

props.name: onStatusChange
props.description: Fires from the choice, the denial or the expiry that changed it.

props.name: onApprove
props.description: The right number was chosen.

props.name: onDeny
props.description: The request was stopped: a wrong number, or "No, it's not me".

props.name: onExpire
props.description: The request ran out of time before anyone chose.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again or Send a new request on the signing-in screen; pass a new request to start over.

props.name: expiresIn
props.description: How long the request lives, in ms.

props.name: timeZone
props.description: The time zone the request's time is shown in.

props.name: appName
props.description: The product's name, on both screens.

props.name: signInUrl
props.description: The address in the signing-in window's bar.

props.name: secureHref
props.description: Where Change your password goes after a block or a denial.

props.name: layout
props.description: The two screens side by side, the phone over the window's edge, or the phone first; they stack in narrow containers.

props.name: numberSize
props.description: The number's size on the signing-in screen, in px; the tile's padding scales with it.

props.name: accent
props.description: Any CSS colour for the number, the waiting highlights, the lifetime bar and the app marks.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The choices and the denial are unavailable.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer wrapper.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the three choices are one tab stop; Left/Right (and Up/Down) move between them, Home and End jump, Enter or Space chooses. After an outcome focus moves to the phone's outcome heading if it was on a choice.

Reduced motion: the line appears whole on a short fade — dashed when it fails — the check appears without the stamp, and only colours change; the lifetime bar still drains, because the time left is information.

Performance: the lifetime bar is a compositor transform tween that runs only while the surface is on screen and the tab visible; expiry is one wall-clock timeout, and the line's ends are measured only at the choice and on resize.
The line lands on the phone's frame level with the chosen key, so it never crosses another key or the phone's words; the choices stay in place through every outcome.
Pass request.time with a timeZone so the time reads the same on the server and in the browser; choices are seeded from the number when you don't pass them.

items.title: Screen Pairing
items.tagline: Sign in on the big screen with a short code.
items.description: A device-code sign-in for a shared screen: the code stands in wide tiles over an expiry bar that drains as one linear tween, and five waiting dots step along on the snap spring each time the screen polls. A new code stands up tile by tile on snap; when a poll approves, the dots light in a run on flick and the tiles drop away one by one on the exit ease while a clip sweeps the welcome open behind them, the avatar landing on recoil and the greeting settling on glide. Every action is a real button, the code is spoken one character at a time, and expiry, approval and new codes are announced once each.

props.name: code
props.description: The code your server issued for this screen. Omit it for a seeded placeholder of codeLength characters.

props.name: codeLength
props.description: Length of placeholder codes and loading outlines, 4 to 10. Tiles group in fours, threes or fives and wrap on narrow screens.

props.name: tileStyle
props.description: How each character is drawn: a split-flap tile, a raised keycap, an accent outline or a solid accent tile.

props.name: accent
props.description: Expiry bar, waiting dots, link underline, outline and solid tiles and the avatar; any CSS colour.

props.name: expiresIn
props.description: Seconds a code lives, counted from when it appears on screen.

props.name: poll
props.description: Asked every pollInterval while the code is live; resolve an account to sign the screen in. Each call steps the waiting dots.

props.name: pollInterval
props.description: Milliseconds between polls.

props.name: approved
props.description: Controlled sign-in: an account shows the welcome, null shows the code. Leave undefined to let poll decide.

props.name: onApproved
props.description: Fires once, from the poll that approved the screen.

props.name: onRefresh
props.description: A new code was asked for (New code, Get a new code, Try again). Placeholder codes roll by themselves.

props.name: onExpire
props.description: Fires once when the code runs out.

props.name: onSignOut
props.description: "Not you? Sign out" was pressed on the welcome; the screen returns to a fresh code.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether a code is ready: loading draws tile outlines, error offers Try again.

props.name: room
props.description: The screen's name, in the header and the headings.

props.name: url
props.description: Where people enter the code.

props.name: now
props.description: The room clock in the header, ms since the epoch (shown in UTC).

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the placeholder codes.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Pauses polling and the countdown and dims the screen.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer panel.

usageNotes: Polling, the countdown and the bar's tween stop while the screen is off view or the page is hidden, and resume from the real elapsed time, so the expiry stays true; nothing runs once the code is expired or approved.
Pass poll as an inline function freely: it is read when each poll fires, so a re-render never restarts the clock. Resolve null to keep waiting, an account to sign in.
The tile group is spoken as the code one character at a time; new codes, the one-minute warning, expiry and sign-in are announced once each in a polite status, never the per-second tick.
Under reduced motion tiles and the welcome cross-fade and the dots change colour without growing; the bar still drains and the countdown still counts.
Times are UTC by hand from the now prop, so server and browser render the same clock.

items.title: Reset Match
items.tagline: Type it twice and see each character line up.
items.description: A set-new-password form whose confirmation shows how far it agrees with the password without ever showing a character: a rail between the fields draws a dot per character on each row, and while the confirmation agrees each new dot rises to its partner on the snap spring as the joint draws on flick. At the first difference a gap opens — the dot drops hollow under a caret and the rest hang loose — and when the two agree with every rule met a highlight runs along the joints in a cascade and a Match chip lands on recoil. Requirements are checked live and spoken as they flip, toggles and the requirement list are keyboard reachable, and a refusal nudges the field on a symmetric tween with the reason.

props.name: rules
props.description: The requirements ({ id, label, test }), checked live as the new password is typed.

props.name: lineStyle
props.description: How a matched pair is joined on the rail: a short line, a cross-stitch, or one merged capsule.

props.name: density
props.description: Field heights (36, 40, 44px), gaps and the size of the rail.

props.name: accent
props.description: Joints, locked dots, the match chip and met ticks; any CSS colour.

props.name: isReused
props.description: Asked on submit before onSubmit; true refuses the password with reusedMessage.

props.name: reusedMessage
props.defaultValue: "You've used this password before. Choose one you haven't used on Fernworks."
props.description: Why a reused password is refused.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Fires with an accepted password. A returned promise shows Updating; a rejection shows its message under the field.

props.name: onContinue
props.description: "Continue to sign in" was pressed on the done panel.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: "Back to sign in" was pressed. Omit it to hide the link.

props.name: onResend
props.description: "Send a new link" was pressed on the expired-link panel.

props.name: account
props.description: Whose password this is: named under the title and offered to password managers.

props.name: status
props.description: loading: the reset link is being checked; error: it has expired; done: the password is set.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading.

props.name: submitLabel
props.description: The submit button's words.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Longest password the fields take; the rail tightens its pitch to fit it.

props.name: defaultPassword
props.description: What the new-password field starts with, uncontrolled — for a form resumed mid-way.

props.name: defaultConfirm
props.description: What the confirmation field starts with, uncontrolled.

props.name: onCheck
props.description: Fires from each keystroke with counts and positions (never characters): rules met, lengths, matched prefix, where it differs, ready.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the fields and actions.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer panel.

usageNotes: The rail is handed counts and the first difference only — characters never reach it — and assistive technology hears a position ("differs from character 7"), never a character, after a pause rather than per key.
Submitting checks the rules, then the match, then isReused (sync or async), then onSubmit; the submit button is aria-disabled while busy, never disabled under focus.
Both fields are real password inputs with autocomplete="new-password" and a hidden username field, so password managers offer to save the new one.
Under reduced motion the dots and joints appear in place, the seam lights at once and refusals flash instead of shaking; locked, gap and extra states all still show.
No loop runs at rest: the rail animates only on keystrokes, and its width is measured by a ResizeObserver bound to the rail when it mounts.

items.title: Limit Lanes
items.tagline: Columns that say no when they're full.
items.description: A kanban board whose columns say no when they are full: every header carries a work-in-progress gauge — pills, a bar or a ring — that fills as cards arrive with each pill popping in on the snap spring, and the gauge is itself a slider you scrub or key to change the limit. A dragged card lifts on flick into a copy that follows the finger 1:1 while a placeholder opens and the cards round it glide aside; over a full column the column washes danger, and a drop there springs the card back home on snap with the throw's own velocity while the gauge pulses once. Arrows walk the cards, Space lifts one and arrows carry it through the layout past full columns, Space or Enter drops it and Escape puts it back.

props.name: columns

usageNotes: Keyboard: arrows walk the cards (Up/Down in a column, Left/Right across, Home/End), Space lifts the focused card and arrows carry it, Space or Enter drops it, Escape puts it back. Carried sideways, a card passes full columns (each gauge pulses) to the next column with room; with none left that way it leans toward the first full one, springs back and onBlockedDrop fires.
Each column's gauge is a role="slider": arrows, Page keys and Home/End change the limit, and a horizontal scrub moves one step per pill's pitch so the row's end stays under the finger.
The carried copy is tracked relative to the board, so the edge auto-scroll that runs while a card is held near a scroller's edge never pulls it out from under the finger; nothing runs at rest.
Controlled cards that the host refuses to move simply land back where the host keeps them: the landing is measured after the commit.
Under reduced motion cards appear in place, landings and lifts are instant and the gauge pulse becomes a danger flash; counts, limits and refusals all still show.

items.title: Pinch Board
items.tagline: Zoom out for the shape, in for the detail.
items.description: A kanban board you zoom: cards have levels of detail — coloured dots, one-line titles, full cards with owner and due date, and open cards with a note and checklist — and a pinch, Ctrl or ⌘ with the wheel, the + and − keys or the toolbar morphs every card between them on the glide spring. The board notes the card under the focal point and where inside it the point sits, and its scroll rides the same glide spring to the offset that puts that spot back under the fingers, so the focal card holds still for the whole morph; at an edge the content is shifted instead and settles back on drift. Cards move by drag on flick and snap or by keys — Space lifts, arrows carry, Space drops, Escape puts back — and the level pill slides on snap.

props.name: cards / defaultCards

Ctrl or ⌘ with the wheel (a trackpad pinch arrives that way) and two-finger touch pinches are handled inside the board only; the page never zooms while the board does, and one-finger scrolling stays native.

The morph keeps the focal card still by animating the board's scroll on the same glide spring as the cards' layout; where no scroll is left the content shifts and settles back to the edge, and a spacer holds the scroll range so a shrinking board never clamps mid-flight.
Card faces are memoised and their handlers stable, so a drag re-renders only the placeholder and the lifted card; nothing runs at rest.
Under reduced motion the level swaps at once and the scroll jumps straight to the anchored offset, so the focal card is still where it was; lifts and landings are instant.

items.title: Patina Board
items.tagline: Cards that show how long they've been waiting.
items.description: A kanban board whose cards weather while they wait: every day still adds a faint patina — tarnish gathering at the edges first, then a mottled bloom from a seeded turbulence mask — mixed with the ink so it darkens on a light page and lifts like dust on a dark one, and a corner counter turns warn when a card goes stale and offers to nudge its owner. Moving or editing a card polishes it: a band of light crosses its face on a move-eased tween while a clip follows its edge and wipes the patina off, and the counter rolls to today on snap. The Stale filter gathers the oldest cards to the top of each column on glide; cards move by drag on flick and snap or by keys — Space lifts, arrows carry, Space drops, Escape puts back, Enter renames, N nudges.

The patina is static markup — gradients and one shared set of four SVG turbulence filters per board — recomputed only when now, a card or a tweak changes; the polish is one tween per touched card, and nothing runs at rest.
Patina colours are token pigments mixed with --ink, so they follow the theme with no theme reads; card names carry the age in words ("waiting 12 days, stale").
A dropped card is polished after it lands, so the wipe is always seen; while the Stale filter sorts by age a moved card joins the end of its new column.
Under reduced motion the patina fades instead of being wiped, nothing travels, and ages, stale marks and the filter order still show.

items.title: Blocker Chains
items.tagline: See what's stuck, and what it's stuck behind.
items.description: A kanban board whose blocked cards hang a thin chain to the card they wait on: quadratic catenaries drawn under the cards with a fixed length, so dragging a card pulls its chains taut and bringing it closer lets them droop. Moving a blocker into Done snaps its chains loose — the free end swings down from the waiting card as a damped pendulum and fades on the exit ease — while the freed card lifts on springs.snap with an unblocked glow and settles back on springs.glide, and every card that moved FLIPs to its place on glide. Cards share one roving tab stop: arrows move, Space lifts and drops, Escape puts back, B shows every chain, L links a blocker, and Tab reaches a card's chain chips where Enter jumps to the blocker as a bead runs along the chain and Delete unlinks.

props.name: columns

props.name: cards / defaultCards

usageNotes: Keyboard: cards share one tab stop. Arrows move between cards, Space lifts a card, arrows carry it across columns and positions, Space or Enter drops and Escape puts it back. L starts linking (arrows choose the blocker, Enter links), B toggles every chain, and Tab reaches the focused card's chain chips: Enter jumps to the blocker, Delete unlinks.
Touch scrolls the board from a card's face; a card is carried by its grip and linked from its link handle, both touch-action: none.

Reduced motion: chains still draw and still come off, but fade instead of swinging; cards jump to their places, the freed card glows without lifting, and the jump bead becomes a brief highlight of the chain.

Performance: the chain layer is drawn by writing path data straight to the DOM in a requestAnimationFrame loop that runs only during a drag, a settle, a fall or a resize, then stops. Nothing runs while the board is still.
Under 40rem of container width the columns stack and the chains become a "Blocked by" line on each card; summarizeBlockers(cards, columns) returns the blocked and loop counts the header shows.

items.title: Stack Carry
items.tagline: Select several cards and move them as one.
items.description: A kanban board where a selection moves as one stack. Dragging any selected card gathers the others under the pointer into a fan whose spread is fanAngle: the grabbed card follows 1:1 and each card behind it follows on its own spring, softer the deeper it sits, so a fast throw strings the deck out and a pause gathers it, while a count badge lands on springs.recoil. Dropping deals the cards into the column in their original board order on springs.glide, cascade() apart, as their dashed home slots fold shut and the cards around them FLIP to make room; refused cards fly home, shake once and say why. Shift-click selects a run, Cmd or Ctrl-click or the check tab toggles, X toggles the focused card, M opens a move menu that deals the same way, Escape clears, and a long press starts selecting on touch.

props.name: columns

Arrows move, Shift with Up or Down extends the selection, X or Space toggles, Cmd or Ctrl+A selects the column, M opens the move menu (arrows, Home, End, Enter, Escape returns focus) and Escape clears the selection.
Touch: cards pan the board until selected; a long press starts selecting, after which taps toggle, and selected cards are touch-action: none so a finger can carry them.
Partial failures: return or resolve { failed: [{ id, reason }] } from onMoveMany. Refused cards fly home, shake once, show the reason under their title and stay selected so they can be dealt with.
Reduced motion: the stack is a tidy pile at the pointer with no trailing springs, and cards appear in their new places without flying; selection, counts and refusals are unchanged.
Performance: nothing runs at rest. Per-card springs run only while carrying and dealing, and the edge auto-scroll frame loop only while a drag sits near the board's edge.

items.title: Burndown Board
items.tagline: Move a card to Done and watch the line step down.
items.description: A sprint board under its own burndown chart: the planned scope's ideal line is a faint dashed guide, the actual line runs through the end of each day, and scope added mid-sprint raises a marked step with a flag. Moving a card into Done lifts its points off the card as a token that arcs up into today's point on one spring; as it lands the line steps down on springs.glide, the dot takes the hit on springs.recoil and the points-left figure rolls its digits on springs.snap, while every card that moved FLIPs to its place on glide. Cards move by drag or by keys — one roving tab stop, arrows to move, Space to lift, arrows to carry, Space to drop, Escape to put back — and under 40rem the chart shrinks into a header strip.

usageNotes: Keyboard: cards share one tab stop. Arrows move between cards, Space lifts, arrows carry across columns and positions, Space or Enter drops and Escape puts the card back; every move is announced with the points left and the ideal.
The chart is an image with a sentence label (points left, the day, the ideal, any added scope) and a visually hidden table of points left per day.
Days come from sprint.start by hand in UTC and today from the now prop, so the server and the browser draw the same chart. Mark mid-sprint scope with addedOn on the new card.
Reduced motion: no token flight, no card travel and no dot bounce; the line moves to its new shape on a short tween and the figure swaps.
Performance: nothing runs at rest. The chart's width comes from a ResizeObserver, and its path is rebuilt only while a step glides.

items.title: Chart Recipe
items.tagline: Each step adds its layer to the chart.
items.description: A report wizard whose preview is a record of the choices: four steps — Source, Chart, Filters, Notes — sit beside a chart that builds one layer per step. Choosing a source sweeps the axes in through a clip, the chart type draws its series on through a sweeping clip (bars grow on springs.glide a cascade apart), filters thin the series they leave out and crop the window while every point glides to the new scale on glide, and notes land last, the peak pin on springs.recoil. Back peels the layers off in reverse, newest first, a beat apart, and going forward lays them down again; a slow source shows a layer skeleton. The step rail is a tablist that follows the arrow keys, sources and chart types are native radio groups, and filters and notes are native checkboxes.

The preview is an image whose label is one sentence listing every layer ("line chart of pump pressure in kPa, 4 series, 3 shown, last 6 months, mark the peak and average line"); each choice is announced once in a polite status.
Layers belong to steps: going back removes the layers of the steps after it, newest first, and going forward lays them down again, so the preview always shows the recipe up to the open step.
Reduced motion: layers cross-fade in and out in the same order with no sweeps, growth or bounces; every layer still appears and disappears.
Performance: nothing runs at rest. Every animation is a spring or tween started by a choice, and the preview's size comes from a ResizeObserver.

items.title: Spoke Wizard
items.tagline: Five tasks in any order, around one hub.
items.description: A non-linear setup drawn as a hub and spokes: a ring divided into one segment per task, each task's node at the end of its spoke. A spoke opens its short flow, grown out of the spoke's direction on springs.glide as the hub recedes; finishing returns to the hub, where that spoke's segment fills with a glide sweep from its start, the node's check draws on springs.flick, the spoke line turns solid and the count rolls on springs.snap. When every spoke is done the gaps close into one ring and the centre lands a check on springs.recoil: Ready. The spokes are a list of buttons in ring order, so Tab walks them clockwise (arrow keys too), each flow is a form where Enter moves on and Escape returns to the hub, and under 34rem the hub becomes a list with a small ring.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the tasks have loaded: loading shows a pulsing ring, error a message with Try again.

props.name: onReload
props.description: Try again was pressed after the tasks failed to load.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read-only: spokes show their state but do not open.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer container.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the spokes are a list of buttons in ring order, so Tab walks them clockwise and the arrow keys step around too. A flow is a form: Enter moves to the next question or finishes (Space toggles a switch), choices are native radio groups, a required field says why it stopped you, and Escape returns to the hub.
Focus moves into the flow's first field when its panel arrives and back to the spoke when the hub is in front again; the hub is inert while a flow is open.
The ring is decoration (aria-hidden); the count, each spoke's state and its saved answers are in text, and every completion and the Ready state are announced once.
Reduced motion: the flow cross-fades in place, segments fill on a short tween, checks appear without bounce, and Ready still swaps in.
Performance: nothing runs at rest. Each segment's fill is one value animated by a completion, and the arc is rebuilt from it only while it moves.

items.title: Dry Run
items.tagline: See what the migration would do before it does.
items.description: A data migration wizard — connect, map, rehearse, run — that shows what it would do before it writes. The rehearsal is a grey pass: one motion value walks the rows on the move ease and three counters (would create, would update, would skip) tick up as their rows pass, as figures, bars or a waffle of row batches whose cells pop as the head goes by; the real run repeats exactly the same seeded walk in colour over the grey ghost, and the actual counts land on springs.recoil beside their rehearsed figures and a delta chip. Panels swap by direction on springs.glide, the stepper's fill glides and its checks draw on springs.flick, and every step validates before Next, taking focus to whatever needs fixing.

props.name: source
props.description: The data being moved: { name, kind, location, rows, columns, sample?, target }.

props.name: fields
props.description: The target's fields: { id, label, required?, hint? }.

props.name: mapping / defaultMapping
props.description: Target field id → source column, or null to skip the field; controlled or initial.

props.name: onMappingChange
props.description: Fires from the select that changed the mapping, with the whole mapping.

props.name: results
props.description: { rehearsal, run, skipped }: the counts each pass lands on and the rows left out.

props.name: step / defaultStep
props.description: The current step, controlled or initial; opening later counts the earlier steps as passed.

props.name: onStepChange
props.description: Fires from Next, Back or the stepper with the step asked for.

props.name: onConnect
props.description: Fires when the connection is checked; return false to report the source unreadable.

props.name: onDryRun
props.description: Fires when the rehearsal starts, with the mapping it rehearses.

props.name: onRun
props.description: Fires when the real run starts, with the mapping it runs.

props.name: onPassEnd
props.description: Fires when a pass has walked every row, with that pass's counts.

props.name: onDownloadReport
props.description: Fires from Download report with source, target, mapping, both passes' counts and the skipped rows.

props.name: counterStyle
props.description: Counters as tiles of figures, long bars, or one waffle of row batches.

props.name: density
props.description: Padding, type size and figure size.

props.name: tone
props.description: The real run's colours (the rehearsal is always grey); pigments at fixed lightness.

props.name: passDuration
props.description: How long each pass takes to walk the rows, in ms.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading shows placeholders; error explains and offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry

props.name: title
props.description: The migration's name, the surface's heading.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; the step body scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be checked, mapped or run.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: every control is a native button or select. Next validates the step and, when it cannot go on, says why under the step and moves focus to what needs fixing (the Check button, or the first bad select). Step changes move focus to the new step's heading; the stepper's earlier steps are buttons.

Each pass is one motion value; every figure, bar and waffle cell derives from it, so nothing re-renders per frame and nothing runs once a pass has finished. The progressbar's value is written as it moves; the live region speaks once when a pass starts and once with the counts when it ends.

The rehearsal and the run share one seeded order of rows, so the run visibly repeats the rehearsal's walk; cells that came out differently are ringed and each counter shows a delta chip. Changing the mapping after a rehearsal marks it stale and blocks the run until it is rehearsed again; the mapping locks once the run starts.
Reduced motion: the pass still runs, in 600 ms with no cell pops, landings or panel travel; counts, fills and colours still change because they are the information.

Colours: the rehearsal is a share of the foreground and the run's tones are pigments at fixed lightness, so both read the same in light and dark. Skipped rows are hatched as well as tinted. Below a 34rem container the counters stack and the stepper drops its labels.

items.title: Instance Sizer
items.tagline: Choose the size; see the rack and the bill change.
items.description: A provisioning wizard — region, size, add-ons, summary — beside a small server rack and the monthly estimate. Choosing a size grows or shrinks the rack unit by unit: new sleds slide in from the right bottom-up on springs.snap a cascade apart, each status light blinking on springs.flick as it seats, and a smaller size pulls the extra sleds out top-down on the exit ease; add-ons take fixed slots or light the roof beacon, the estimate rolls digit by digit on snap in the direction the total moved, and provisioning sweeps every light to green. Every choice is a radio card with roving focus — arrows move and select, skipping sizes a region does not offer, whose reasons are shown and read out.

props.name: regions

props.name: addons

props.name: onProvision

props.name: accent

props.name: onRetry

props.name: height

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: each choice set is a role="radiogroup" with one tab stop; arrows move and select, wrapping and skipping sizes the region does not offer, Home and End jump. Add-ons are role="switch" buttons. Next validates (a size the new region does not offer sends you back to Size and says why), and step changes move focus to the new heading.

The rack is a role="img" with a sentence for a label ("Rack: Medium server in 2 of 12 units, with nightly backups"); the estimate has a full sr-only figure and every change is announced once with the new total.
Unavailable sizes stay visible, dimmed with their reason, and the group's description lists every reason so assistive tech hears why a card cannot be chosen.
Reduced motion: sleds and parts fade in place, lights switch without a blink, digits swap and panels cross-fade; the rack still fills and the total still changes.
Nothing animates at rest. Below a 34rem container the rack shrinks into a band above the choices; accent colours derive fills and washes in oklab, so any token reads in light and dark.

items.title: Question Trail
items.tagline: One question at a time, with your answers kept.
items.description: A conversational intake, one question at a time: each question is typed first, then its bubble rises a step from its tail corner on springs.snap, and the option you pick travels into place as your answer chip on springs.glide. Pressing an earlier chip rewinds — the later bubbles fold back up into it bottom-first in a cascade, heights closing on glide while their words lift away on the exit ease — and answering again replays the trail forward with every kept answer until a question has none, so a changed branch only asks what is new. Options are a roving group of buttons (arrows move, Enter sends, Escape keeps the old answer) and text questions are labelled fields that say what is wrong.

props.name: questions
props.description: { id, prompt, short?, kind?, options?, placeholder?, optional?, next?, validate? } — next is an id, a map from answer to id (a branch), or null to end.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Answers by question id, controlled or initial; "" is a skipped optional question. The trail opens at the first unanswered one.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press, Enter or Skip that changed an answer, with every answer kept.

props.name: onAnswer
props.description: Fires once per answer given.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Fires when the last question on the path is answered, with the path's ids — again after a rewind that completes it.

props.name: onRewind
props.description: Fires when an earlier answer is opened again.

props.name: onSave
props.description: Fires from Save for later with the answers and the question waiting.

props.name: storageKey
props.description: Writes a saved trail to this device's storage under this key and picks it up after mount.

props.name: bubbleStyle
props.description: Filled bubbles with a tail corner, hairline bubbles, or a plain transcript on a left rule.

props.name: density
props.description: Gaps, padding and type size.

props.name: accent
props.description: Answer chips, the composer's focus, progress and the save mark — any CSS colour.

props.name: typingDelay
props.description: How long the host types before a new question arrives, in ms.

props.name: host
props.description: Who is asking; named to assistive tech before each question.

props.name: title
props.description: The intake's heading.

props.name: closing
props.defaultValue: a thank-you that repeats the phone number
props.description: The host's last line once every question on the path is answered.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading shows placeholder bubbles; error explains and offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the questions failed to load.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; the trail scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be answered or changed.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: each composer takes focus when its question arrives. Options are a group with one tab stop — arrows and Home/End move, Enter or Space sends. Text questions are labelled fields: Enter sends, errors are linked by aria-describedby. Every earlier answer is a button named "Change <short>: <answer>"; while changing one, Escape keeps it (and is not passed on).

Answers off the current path are kept, not deleted: going back and choosing differently only asks the questions the new branch needs, and switching back replays the old ones with a "kept" mark. Questions reached through a branch say which answer led there.

The trail scrolls its own box to keep the newest item in view and never scrolls the page. Announcements are one sentence per answer (with how many kept answers replayed and the next question), never per typing frame.
Reduced motion: no typing dots, travel or scale — bubbles and chips fade in and out, folds collapse at once, and the replay still re-deals in order.
With storageKey the trail is written on Save for later and picked up after mount, so server and client render the same first frame; onSave hands the same payload to a host that keeps drafts itself.

items.title: Fork Wizard
items.tagline: See which path your choices take you down.
items.description: A branching wizard with a map of every step, laid out by depth so forks open and merges close. Choosing an option lights its branch: a dot travels the curve to the next step on springs.glide while the lit stroke draws behind it, every step the choice rules out fades to a dashed ghost, the arriving step's ring lands on springs.recoil, and the count of steps left updates — a range while later forks are still open. The map doubles as navigation with roving focus, answers are kept so going back costs nothing until a choice changes, choice steps are radio cards that say how many steps each leads to, and in a narrow container the map becomes a progress line with a mark at every fork.

props.name: graph
props.description: { start, steps } — each step is { id, title, short, body?, kind: "choice" | "field" | "end", options?: { value, label, hint?, next }[], field?: { label, placeholder?, suffix?, required?, validate? }, next? }.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Answers by step id (an option's value or a field's text), controlled or initial; answers off the path are kept.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the choice, keystroke or field that changed an answer.

props.name: step / defaultStep
props.defaultValue: — / the first unanswered step on the path
props.description: The current step's id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onStepChange
props.description: Fires from Next, Back, the map or the So far trail with the step asked for.

props.name: onChoose
props.description: Fires when an option is chosen — the moment its branch lights.

props.name: onBack
props.description: Fires when the visitor goes to an earlier step.

props.name: onFinish
props.description: Fires from the end step with only the answers on the path and the path's ids.

props.name: mapPosition
props.description: A small card in the corner, a labelled band across the top, or a column at the side with the map running top to bottom.

props.name: density
props.description: Padding, gaps and type size.

props.name: accent
props.description: The lit branch, the dot, rings and the primary button — any CSS colour.

props.name: travelDuration
