props.name: title
props.description: The wizard's heading.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: One line under the heading.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading shows placeholder cards; error explains and offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the steps failed to load.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; the panel scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be chosen or finished.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: each choice step is a role="radiogroup" with one tab stop — arrows move and select (lighting the branch as you go), Home and End jump. Field steps are labelled inputs where Enter is Next; Next validates and says why. The map is a nav of buttons for the steps on the path with roving focus (arrows, Home, End); step changes from Next and Back move focus to the new heading.
The map's SVG is decoration (aria-hidden); its buttons carry the names, answers and the current step (aria-current). The remaining count and each choice's destination are announced once per change.
Answers are kept when the path changes, so switching a fork back restores the old branch with its answers; onFinish receives only the answers on the finished path.
Reduced motion: the branch lights at once with no travelling dot, ruled-out steps dim at once, the ring does not bounce and panels cross-fade; the count still updates.
One motion value drives the dot and the drawn stroke, and nothing animates at rest. Below a 34rem container the map becomes a progress line whose dots navigate too.

items.title: Filed Steps
items.tagline: Finished steps file themselves away, still in reach.
items.description: A wizard of stacked cards: the current step in front with the next ones peeking above it. Finishing a step files it — a sheet the size of the card flies down to its place in the pile at the foot on springs.glide, animating position and size rather than scale so no text stretches, while the card's face fades and its summary arrives, and the pile takes the weight with a springs.recoil press while the card behind steps forward on glide. Clicking a tab lifts its card back up the same way while the current stack steps aside; Save files it again with the new summary, Cancel or Escape puts it back unchanged, and Skip for now files a card unfinished with a mark on its tab that Send points back to.

props.name: steps
props.description: { id, title, short?, description?, fields, summary?, skippable? } — fields are { id, label, kind?: "text" | "email" | "tel" | "textarea" | "choice", options?, placeholder?, required?, validate? }.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Field values by field id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the field that changed, and when Cancel restores a reopened card, with every value.

props.name: defaultFiled
props.description: Steps already filed when the wizard opens, finished or unfinished.

props.name: onStepComplete

props.name: onReopen

props.name: onFinish
props.description: Fires from Send once every step's fields are valid.

props.name: tabStyle
props.description: Folder tabs with sloped shoulders on a drawer, overlapping index strips with a coloured top edge, or rounded pills.

props.name: stackDepth

props.name: accent
props.description: The front card's edge, tab numbers, choice pills and primary buttons — any CSS colour.

props.name: density

props.name: title

props.name: subtitle
props.description: One line under the heading.

props.name: finishLabel
props.description: The last card's button.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading shows a placeholder card; error explains and offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the steps failed to load.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be filed, reopened or sent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the front card is a role="group" named by its heading, which takes focus when a card arrives; Enter in a field is Continue, choices are radio groups (arrows select). A reopened card focuses its first field and Escape cancels it (and is not passed on). The pile is an ordered list of buttons with one tab stop — Left/Right, Home and End move — each named like "Reopen Site, unfinished: Unit 4, Coldbrook Yard"; focus returns to a card's tab when it is filed again.
Send checks every step's fields, not just the marks: it names what needs finishing and moves focus to the first such tab, whose mark pops once.

The flight is one sheet animating position and size from a plain spring value, measured at the start (in the handler) and the end (after the commit that renders the target), so it runs even when its target has just mounted; nothing animates at rest and every animation stops on unmount.
Reduced motion: nothing flies — the card fades out, the tab fades in, the stack re-orders by cross-fade and the pile does not press; summaries and marks still change.
In a narrow container the card fills the width, the peeks shrink with it and the tab row scrolls sideways inside its own box with edge fades.

items.title: Pin Critique
items.tagline: Drop a numbered pin and say what you see.
items.description: A design-critique board: numbered pins on an artwork, each starting a thread in the column beside it. Clicking the artwork or pressing P drops a pin at the cursor — it falls 16px and lands on springs.recoil with two small bounces while its ground shadow grows and its numeral rolls up into the head on springs.snap just behind the touch-down — and the composer opens for what you see. Hovering or focusing a thread draws a ring around its pin on springs.glide while the pin lifts on snap; pins drag 1:1 and settle on snap with the throw, resolved pins fade to a check, and below a 40rem container the threads open as a sheet that rises on glide, follows a downward drag and pans the artwork so the pin stays in view. Pins are one roving tab stop: arrows move between them, Alt with an arrow nudges one, Shift with an arrow moves the drop cursor and Escape closes what is open.

props.name: pins / defaultPins

props.name: onPinsChange

props.name: threads / defaultThreads
props.description: Threads as { id, pinId, resolved?, comments: { id, author, at, text }[] }.

props.name: onThreadsChange

props.name: selected / defaultSelected / onSelectedChange

props.name: onPin
props.description: A dropped pin was posted with its first comment; both are already in the lists.

props.name: onReply

props.name: onResolve

props.name: artwork

props.name: aspect

props.name: pinStyle

props.name: density

props.name: accent

props.name: showResolved / defaultShowResolved / onShowResolvedChange

props.name: author

props.name: now

props.name: title

props.name: status

props.name: onRetry

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: P drops a pin at the cursor from anywhere in the board (or while the pointer rests on the artwork); Shift with an arrow moves the cursor 2%; pins are one roving tab stop where arrows move by number, Home and End jump, Alt with an arrow nudges the focused pin 1% and Enter opens its thread; Enter posts in a composer, Shift+Enter breaks a line, Escape cancels a draft, closes the sheet or the open thread (and is consumed).
Pin positions are fractions of the artwork, so the board can be any size; pass `aspect` with your own `artwork` (an with object-fit: cover, or an SVG) so the canvas fits it without letterboxing.
Reduced motion: pins appear on their spot without a fall, the ring appears whole, the sheet and the artwork's pan jump instead of gliding; every count, check and state still changes.

Below a 40rem container the thread column becomes a bottom sheet inside the board (a non-modal dialog): a pin opens it on its thread, a drop opens it on the composer once the pin has landed, and the artwork glides up so the pin clears the sheet.
No loop runs: every motion is a spring or tween that ends, and the pointer cursor writes motion values, not React state.

items.title: Timecode Notes
items.tagline: Comments that sit at the moment they're about.
items.description: Review notes pinned to moments in a clip: the clip plays in a procedural frame (or your own `renderFrame`), every note is a marker on the timeline, and the notes list sits beside the player, under it below a 40rem container. As the playhead passes a marker it pulses on springs.snap and its note rises into the foot of the frame on springs.recoil, holds, and leaves on the exit ease; choosing a note, marker or cluster glides the playhead there on springs.glide while the frame cuts to its scene, and markers closer than 14px merge into counted bubbles. Space plays, M adds a note at the playhead, and the timeline is a slider whose arrows, Page keys, Home, End and [ ] brackets move by seconds and between notes.

props.name: media
props.description: The clip: { title, kind: "video" | "audio", duration, scenes?: { at, label }[], peaks?: number[] }.

props.name: notes / defaultNotes
props.description: Notes as { id, at (seconds), author, text, createdAt, resolved? }, controlled or initial.

props.name: onNotesChange
props.description: Fires with every note after an add or a resolve.

props.name: time / defaultTime
props.description: The playhead in seconds, controlled or initial; a controlled change of more than a second seeks.

props.name: onTimeChange
props.description: Fires on every seek and once a second while playing, with whole seconds.

props.name: playing / defaultPlaying / onPlayingChange
props.description: Playback, controlled or initial, and the callback from the button, key or end of clip that changed it.

props.name: onAdd
props.description: A note was added at the playhead; it is already in the list.

props.name: onSeek
props.description: The visitor moved the playhead; `noteId` when a note, marker or cluster was chosen.

props.name: onResolve
props.description: A note was resolved (true) or reopened (false).

props.name: renderFrame
props.description: Draw the frame yourself; called with whole seconds and on every seek.

props.name: markerStyle
props.description: A hairline tick with a cap above the track, a dot on the track, or the author's initial on a stem.

props.name: density
props.description: List type and padding, and the size of the player's controls.

props.name: accent
props.description: Playhead, fill, markers and the current note's edge — any CSS colour; fills take its hue at a fixed lightness.

props.name: holdMs
props.description: How long a passed note stays risen over the frame, in ms.

props.name: author
props.description: The name new notes are written under.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment relative times count from, so server and browser render the same text.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading and the surface's accessible name.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading shows a skeleton frame and list; error shows Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the clip failed to load.

props.name: height
props.description: The surface's height in px; the player and notes scroll inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: the clip plays and notes can be read and chosen, nothing added or resolved.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Space plays and pauses anywhere in the surface except on a button (which answers Space itself); M adds a note at the playhead, pausing and focusing the composer (Enter posts, Escape cancels and returns focus); the timeline is role="slider": arrows step a second, Shift five, Page Up and Page Down ten, Home and End jump, and [ and ] move to the previous and next note.

Performance: a single animation-frame loop runs only while playing, while the surface is on screen (IntersectionObserver) and the page is visible; it writes motion values each frame and React state only when the whole second changes. Paused, nothing runs.

Markers are pointer conveniences (aria-hidden): every note is also a button in the list and on the slider's [ and ] keys. Each passed note is announced once in a polite live region; the time readout is not live.
Reduced motion: seeks jump instead of gliding, notes appear over the frame without travel or bounce and the frame holds still within a scene; playback and every count still run.
No media file is loaded: pass `media.scenes` for the drawn frames, `media.peaks` for an audio waveform, or `renderFrame` to draw the picture from your own source.

items.title: Cell Notes
items.tagline: Comments that live in the cell they're about.
items.description: A spreadsheet whose notes live in their cells: every annotated cell carries a small corner, and opening a note grows its card out of that corner — one value on springs.glide sweeps a diagonal crease across the card's clip with a lip of paper along it, so the note unfolds from the cell — while closing folds it back on the exit ease. Replies stack inside the card on springs.snap, resolving folds the corner back flat on snap, and the active cell's outline travels cell to cell on snap. It is a real role="grid" with one roving cell: arrows, Home, End and Ctrl+Home/End move, Shift+F2 opens or starts the active cell's note, Escape closes it and returns focus, and the notes sidebar becomes a sheet below a 40rem container.

props.name: onNotesChange
props.description: Fires with every note after an add, a reply or a resolve.

props.description: The active cell as a reference, controlled or initial, and the callback from the click or key that moved it.

props.name: open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange
props.description: The open note's id, controlled or initial, and the callback when a card opens or closes.

props.description: A note was added to a cell; it is already in the list.

props.description: A reply was posted on a note.

props.name: onResolve
props.description: A note was resolved (true) or reopened (false).

props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the grid has one roving cell — arrows move, Home and End reach the row's ends, Ctrl or Cmd with Home or End the sheet's corners, Shift+F2 opens the active cell's note or starts one, Enter opens an existing note; in the card, Enter posts, Shift+Enter breaks a line and Escape closes it and returns focus to its cell (consumed).

Assistive technology: each annotated cell is described by its note (author, text, reply count, resolved) through aria-describedby, the card is a labelled non-modal dialog that takes focus on arrival, and every add, reply and resolve is announced once.

The card is placed in the grid's scroll content beside its cell (flipping left near the right edge, under the cell when neither side fits) and the grid glides to keep it in view, so it never draws outside the surface.
Reduced motion: cards fade in place instead of unfolding, the active outline jumps, and corners swap flat at once; every note, count and state still changes.
No loop: the unfold is one motion value rebuilding a clip-path each frame (rounded) and releasing it to none at rest, so the open card's shadow and growth are never clipped.

items.title: Range Remarks
items.tagline: Comment on a span of lines, not just one.
items.description: A code review diff where comments cover spans of lines. Pressing in the comment gutter and dragging grows a bracket across the lines you mean — its live end under the pointer 1:1, the lines tinting as it passes them — and on release the end settles onto the last line's edge on springs.snap with the throw's velocity, then a comment box unfolds under the range, its measured height opening on springs.glide as it swings down from its top edge. Existing threads sit after their last line with their bracket in the gutter, brighten with their lines on hover or focus, carry suggested changes as mini diffs, and fold to a one-line summary on glide when resolved or outdated. The diff is a role="grid" with one roving line: Up and Down move, Shift with an arrow grows the same bracket a line at a time, Enter or C opens the box and Escape clears; long lines wrap below a 30rem container.

props.name: diff

props.name: threads / defaultThreads

props.name: onThreadsChange
props.description: Fires with every thread after a comment, a reply or a resolve.

props.name: onSuggest

props.name: onResolve

props.name: density
props.description: Line height (18/20/24px) and code type size.

props.name: wrap

props.name: now

props.name: onRetry

props.description: The surface's height in px; the diff scrolls inside it.

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: the diff is a grid with one roving line — Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Shift with Up or Down grows the range from its anchor (the bracket's keyboard path), Enter or C opens the comment box on it, Escape clears it (consumed); in a box, Cmd or Ctrl with Enter posts and Escape cancels back to the line.

Pointer: the gutter strip between the line numbers and the code is the drag handle (touch-action pan-x, so a vertical drag on a phone grows the range instead of scrolling); a tap there comments on one line.
Each line is named for assistive technology ("Line 12, added: const cap = 30_000") and marked aria-selected while in the range; every range, post and resolve is announced once.
Reduced motion: the bracket and the comment box appear at rest — no settle, no swing — and threads fold instantly; ranges, tints and counts still change.
Row geometry is measured after layout and on resize (ResizeObserver), never per frame, so wrapping lines and opening threads keep every bracket on its lines.

items.title: Sign-off Round
items.tagline: Every reviewer stamps it before it ships.
items.description: An approval round on a document: every reviewer's verdict lands as a stamp in its slot on the document's header, dropping from 1.4× and a little more turned onto its resting tilt on springs.recoil — the two small bounces of a hand stamp — while the header sinks 1.5px and springs back on springs.snap, a ring of ink spreads under it and the thock is heard at touch-down. Changes requested stamps in muted red whatever the accent and needs a comment; its stamp is a button that brings the comment into view. The progress rail fills a segment per verdict on springs.glide, and when the last stamp lands the round completes: the rail takes the outcome's colour and the chip rolls to Signed off or Changes requested. Reviewers are a list in tab order with Approve, Request changes and Remind as real buttons.

props.name: document

props.name: reviewers / defaultReviewers

props.name: onReviewersChange
props.description: Fires with every reviewer after a verdict is recorded here.

props.description: The reviewer the visitor is: only their row offers Approve and Request changes, the rest offer Remind. null records verdicts for anyone (a facilitator).

props.name: onApprove
props.description: A reviewer approved.

props.name: onRequestChanges
props.description: A reviewer requested changes, with the required comment.

props.name: onRemind

props.name: onComplete
props.description: The last verdict landed — from the press that made it, or once after the host's update that did.

props.name: stampStyle
props.description: A round seal with the verdict on an arc, a rectangular rubber stamp with the date, or a circled monogram with a verdict badge.

props.name: density

props.name: accent

props.name: remindCooldownMs
props.description: How long Remind rests (aria-disabled, reading Reminded) after a press, in ms.

props.name: now

props.name: status
props.description: Loading shows skeleton stamps, reviewers and text; error shows Try again.

props.name: onRetry

props.name: height

props.name: disabled

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: reviewers are a list in tab order; Approve, Request changes and Remind are real buttons. Request changes opens a labelled field that takes focus — Cmd or Ctrl with Enter sends, Escape closes it and returns focus to the button (consumed) — and Send stays focusable and explains itself until the field has text.

Assistive technology: stamps are named ("Approved by Ines Marlow, 14 oct"); a changes stamp is a button that moves focus to its comment; the rail is a progressbar ("2 of 4 reviewers signed"); every verdict, reminder and the completion are announced once as whole sentences.
Sound answers the visitor only: a verdict pressed here thocks at touch-down; verdicts that arrive from the host land silently.
Reduced motion: stamps fade in at rest with no drop, sink or ink ring, the rail fills at once and chips swap; every verdict, count and the outcome still show.
Each stamp's tilt and bare ink patches are seeded from the reviewer's id, so the same stamp looks the same on every render and in server markup.

items.title: Question Queue
items.tagline: The most wanted questions rise to the top.
items.description: The Q&A of a live town hall: open questions sorted by votes and an Answered section, in one feed. A vote fills its pill and rolls the count digit by digit on springs.snap; a beat later the question lifts and climbs past the ones it overtakes as a layout move on springs.glide while their ranks roll down, settles on springs.flick and pops a ▲ chip on springs.recoil. Answering opens an editor under the question on glide, publishing moves the card into Answered as a shared-layout move with a recoil stamp and the answer opening beneath; Up and Down walk the questions, U upvotes and A answers.

props.name: cardStyle

props.name: density
props.description: Type size, padding and the size of the vote pill.

props.name: accent

props.name: questions / defaultQuestions

props.name: onQuestionsChange
props.description: Fires from the vote, ask or answer that changed the list, with the whole new list.

props.name: onAsk
props.description: A question was asked from the composer; it is already in the list.

props.name: onUpvote
props.description: The viewer upvoted (voted true) or withdrew a vote.

props.name: onAnswer
props.description: The host answered a question; empty text means it was answered live.

props.name: now

props.name: title

props.name: subtitle

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: the feed has one roving stop. Up and Down walk every question across both sections, Home and End jump, Page Up and Page Down move five; U upvotes or withdraws, A opens the answer editor (host view). The vote and Answer buttons inside the active question are reachable with Tab. Escape in the editor cancels and returns focus to the question; Enter publishes.

The climb is choreographed: the count rolls first and the order on screen follows 160ms later, so the vote is seen landing before the question moves. Focus rides the question while it climbs, and a polite status says its new place ("Upvoted. Now 4th of 9, 22 votes.").
Reduced motion: nothing lifts or travels. A moved question takes its new place at once under a fading accent wash; counts, ranks and answers cross-fade. Every number still changes.
Anonymous questions are labelled "Anonymous" with a masked disc, never a blank name. An empty queue shows an invitation with a button that focuses the composer.
Performance: no loops or timers at rest. Layout moves are motion layout animations on the articles only; ref callbacks are stable so nothing remounts per render.

items.title: Zone Overlap
items.tagline: Find the hour that works in every time zone.
items.description: A find-a-time surface: a team across time zones as rows on one shared timeline, hours outside each person's day hatched, busy blocks drawn, and an Everyone lane holding the stretches where all are free. The meeting band spans every row with each person's local time on a flag; dragged it follows the pointer 1:1 and lands on a quarter hour on springs.snap with the throw's velocity, and as it enters the everyone-free stretch it blooms — one value springs up on springs.snap (down on springs.glide) and brightens the band and widens its glow from a single CSS property. The band is a slider: arrows move it fifteen minutes, brackets change its length, Enter picks and S suggests.

props.name: hourWidth

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: the band is a role="slider" whose value text reads the span and who is not free ("15:15 to 16:00 Lisbon time, everyone free"). Left and Right move fifteen minutes, Shift with them an hour, Page Up and Page Down an hour, Home and End the day's ends; [ and ] change the length, Enter picks, S suggests. A polite status announces each settled position.

Drag: the band is captured after 3px and follows the pointer 1:1 in minutes, rubber-banding past the day's ends; a flick lands where it would have come to rest. The right-edge grip changes the length. Pressing an empty part of a track moves the band there; a click, not a pointerdown, so panning the day on a phone never moves it.
Time zones are fixed offsets per person for the day shown, so server and client render the same times. Busy blocks are minutes on the person's own clock.
Reduced motion: the band moves without travel and the bloom cross-fades over 150ms; every readout, flag and Everyone capsule still changes.

Performance: one motion value per band edge and one for the bloom, all written as CSS custom properties; React renders only when the snapped quarter changes. Availability is computed once per data change in 96 quarter-hour slices.
Below 36rem the rows become a list: a day strip carries the same band slider and each person shows one local-time column.

items.title: Duration Slots
items.tagline: Change the length; the open times merge and split.
items.description: A public booking page with a host card, a length radiogroup, a time zone combobox, a month strip and the day's free times as pills. Changing the length from 30 to 60 minutes joins every pair of neighbouring pills with a liquid thread whose attach points spread and whose waist follows on springs.glide until the two are one tall pill, the times drifting together; changing back draws a seam across each pill and splits it on springs.snap. The day and length pills slide on springs.snap and a pick lands on springs.flick; the times are a listbox with arrow keys and the zone combobox has type-ahead.

props.name: pillShape

props.name: density

props.name: accent

props.name: slotMinutes

props.name: durations

props.name: onConfirm

props.name: now

props.name: status

props.name: onRetry

props.name: height

props.name: disabled

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: the times are one role="listbox" (Morning and Afternoon are labelled groups inside it); Up and Down move across both in time order, Home and End jump, Enter or Space picks. The day strip and the length are radiogroups (arrows move and select; past days are skipped). The zone box is a role="combobox": typing filters, Up and Down move, Enter chooses, Escape closes and is handled where focus is.

Longer lengths are offered back to back from the start of each run of free slots, so the day stays tidy; a slot left over that cannot hold the length keeps its place as a dashed "too short" pill (aria-disabled) and nothing below it jumps.

The join is drawn: each pair of pills is two HTML shapes whose facing corners square off and an SVG neck between them, rebuilt from one motion value per join and rounded to 2dp; a re-run (StrictMode, a quick second change) carries on from where the join was.
Reduced motion: no liquid. Joins cross-fade between apart and joined over 150ms, labels swap by fade, the day and length pills jump; picks, counts and the confirm bar still change.
A day with nothing free (or nothing long enough) points to the next open day with a button that goes there.

items.title: Shift Roster
items.tagline: Fill the week so every shift is covered.
items.description: A week's staff rota: people down the side, days across the top, an Open row of unassigned shifts, and under every day its coverage drawn as a hammock that sags below the target line when the day is short. A shift follows the pointer 1:1 over the board and lands with a FLIP from where it was let go on springs.snap carrying the release velocity; dropped on another shift the two swap. The day that gains hours springs up on springs.recoil and the day that lost them sinks on springs.glide, while clashing shifts ring each other in amber. On the keyboard Space picks a cell's shift up, arrows carry it a glide at a time and Space drops it.

props.name: palette

props.name: shifts / defaultShifts

props.name: onRetry

props.name: height

props.name: disabled

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the board is a role="grid" with one roving cell (Open, each person, each day). Arrows move; Space picks up the cell's shift and arrows carry it, each step a glide; Space or Enter drops it — onto a cell holding a shift, the two swap — and Escape puts it back, handled where focus is. Every move and drop is announced with the day's new coverage.

Drag: a block is captured after 4px (touch-action: none, so the gesture is the block's), follows the pointer 1:1 and is hit-tested against the cell under it, which is outlined; a shift under the pointer shows a swap glyph. The landing is a FLIP from the release point, measured again from the same snapshot if StrictMode re-runs the effect, so it always finishes.
Coverage is hours scheduled against each day's target: short days sag in a warn pigment proportional to the square root of the shortfall, met days are taut in success, overstaffed days turn accent.
Reduced motion: no lift, no FLIP, no spring in the bars; levels, sags, counts and clash outlines change at once.
Narrow containers (under 40rem) show one day at a time behind a day tablist with coverage dots; a held shift carried left or right takes the view with it.

items.title: Room Rail
items.tagline: Find a free room and book it in one drag.
items.description: A day of meeting rooms on one rail: rooms as rows with capacity, equipment and who holds them now, the working day across, the past dimmed behind a now-line that follows the now prop on springs.drift so a ticking clock sweeps instead of stepping. Pressing a free gap grows a booking out from that point to its default length on springs.snap with the end time riding its edge; both edges then drag 1:1 in quarter hours, rubber-band at the gap's bounds and settle on snap, and Book lands it on springs.flick. Your own bookings extend by a grip and release back to the now-line on springs.glide; arrow keys walk the free gaps, Enter grows a booking and Left and Right size it.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: Height of each room's row in px; from 56px rooms show their status line and blocks their holder.

props.name: blockStyle
props.description: How bookings are drawn: a tint with a coloured lead edge, a pigment fill, or an outline.

props.name: accent
props.description: Any CSS colour: your bookings, the draft and its readouts.

props.name: rooms
props.description: The rooms: { id, name, floor?, capacity, equipment: ("screen" | "video" | "whiteboard" | "projector")[], outOfService? (reason) }.

props.name: bookings / defaultBookings
props.description: The bookings, controlled or initial: { id, room, start, end (minutes), title, holder }.

props.name: onBookingsChange
props.description: Fires from the book, extend or release that changed the bookings, with all of them.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the rail is a role="grid" whose cells are the free gaps and your own bookings (other bookings are read in each room's row header). Left and Right walk a room, Up and Down move to the nearest cell in the next room, Home and End the row's ends. Enter on a gap grows a booking; then Left and Right move its end, Shift with them its start, Enter books and Escape cancels. On your booking ] extends it fifteen minutes and Delete releases it while it is in progress.

Pointer: a press grows the draft from the pressed quarter; a press-and-drag sets the end with the pointer instead. Edges are captured after 1px and rubber-band at the gap's bounds (a neighbouring booking, the now-line, the day's end). The gap stays mounted under its draft so the drag that creates it is never cut off.
Time is minutes from midnight and the now-line follows the now prop: drive it from your own clock (the demo ticks a simulated minute only while the rail is on screen and the page visible).
Reduced motion: the now-line jumps, the draft appears at full length, edges land without springs and a release retracts at once under a fading wash; every time and readout still changes.

Out-of-service rooms are hatched across the day with their reason and have no cells to walk. Under 36rem each room becomes a card with its next free slots as chips that open the same draft with − and + on its end.

items.title: Series Edit
items.tagline: Change one meeting, or this and every one after.
items.description: A recurring meeting's editor whose strip of upcoming occurrences always shows what Save would do. Choosing This and following cleaves the row at the chosen date: a gap opens before it and the chips after it reflow on springs.glide while a dashed rule draws down the gap on springs.flick, then the chips in scope slide to the new time — later dropping, earlier rising — each a cascade step after the one before, their times rolling on springs.snap, while earlier chips stay put; a one-off save stamps its mark in on springs.recoil. The strip is a horizontal listbox whose arrow keys move the edit (and the cleave) to another date, the scope is a radio group, and clashes with other events are listed before saving.

props.name: chipStyle
props.description: How each occurrence chip is drawn: a two-line tile, a one-line pill, or a calendar stub with a month band.

props.name: density
props.description: Chip size, gaps, padding and field height.

props.name: accent
props.description: The colour of the edit — chips in scope, the cleave, the day lane and Save — as pigments at a fixed lightness.

props.name: series
props.description: The recurring meeting: { id, title, weekday (0 is Monday), start, duration, room }.

props.name: occurrences / defaultOccurrences
props.description: Each { id, date, start?, duration?, room?, exception?: "moved" | "cancelled", split? }; controlled or initial.

props.name: onOccurrencesChange
props.description: Fires from Save with every occurrence.

props.name: busy
props.description: Other events ({ id, title, date, start, end }) checked for clashes before saving.

props.name: rooms
props.description: Rooms offered by the Room field.

props.name: now
props.description: The current time in ms; occurrences before today are not shown. Never read from the clock.

props.name: anchor / defaultAnchor
props.description: The occurrence being edited, by id; controlled or initial.

props.name: onAnchorChange
props.description: Fires from the press or arrow key that chose another occurrence.

props.name: scope / defaultScope
props.description: Which meetings the edit applies to; controlled or initial.

props.name: onScopeChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that changed the scope.

props.name: defaultChanges
props.description: Pre-fills the form ({ start, duration, room }) on top of the anchor's own values.

props.name: onEditOne
props.description: Save with scope "one": the occurrence, now a one-off, and its new values.

props.name: onEditFollowing
props.description: Save with scope "following": the first occurrence of the new series and its values.

props.name: onEditAll
props.description: Save with scope "all": the series' new values. One-off changes keep their own.

props.name: onDiscard
props.description: Discard was pressed: the form went back to the anchor's values.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading shows placeholder chips and fields; error explains and offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the series failed to load.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; the body scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be chosen, changed or saved.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the strip is one tab stop; arrows (and Home/End) move the edit to another date with selection following focus, so the cleave walks with the keys. The scope is a radio group; the fields are native selects; Discard and Save stay focusable with aria-disabled when there is nothing to save, and Save is described by the clash list when there is one.

Each chip's accessible name is one sentence — date, time, room, one-off or cancelled, where it will move, what it clashes with — and every change of anchor, scope or field is announced once, politely, with how many meetings move and how many clashes.
Reduced motion: no reflow travel, slide, ripple, roll or stamp; gaps and offsets switch at once and colours cross-fade in 150 ms. The strip still shows exactly what Save would do.

Nothing runs at rest: chip moves are layout animations measured against the body's scroller, the clash list measures its content with a ResizeObserver, and colours are CSS transitions delayed a cascade step per chip.

Colours: chips in scope, the lane slot and Save use the accent as a pigment at fixed lightness with dark ink, so light and dark themes read alike; clashes use a warn pigment ring plus words, never colour alone. Below a 34rem container the chips wrap, the fields stack and the scope turns into a vertical list.

items.title: Leave Planner
items.tagline: Request time off and see who else is away.
items.description: A time-off request surface: a balance meter of the leave type's days over one to three months of calendar, with teammates already away drawn as soft overlapping stripes on their dates. Choosing a range drains the meter a day at a time — one motion value walking about 45 ms a day on the linear ease — while the count of working days rolls and each working day in the calendar lights in the same beat; weekends and holidays inside the range stay hatched because they are skipped, the type switch slides on springs.snap and the months glide in on springs.glide. Asking for more than the balance runs the meter dry, shakes it once on a tween and explains the shortfall; each month is a grid with arrow keys, Enter for the first and last day, Shift to extend and Escape to clear.

props.name: stripeStyle
props.description: How teammates' leave is drawn: bands that join across consecutive days, diagonal hatching that crosses where two overlap, or stacked dots.

props.name: monthCount
props.description: Months side by side on a wide container, 1 to 3; below a 34rem container it is always one.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of your request and balance, as a pigment at a fixed lightness.

props.name: policies
props.description: The kinds of leave: { id, label, allowance?, noticeDays? }; no allowance means no cap.

props.name: balance
props.description: Days left of each kind, by policy id.

props.name: holidays
props.description: Public holidays ({ date, name }); never counted as leave.

props.name: team
props.description: Teammates and the spans they are already away: { id, name, away: { from, to }[] }.

props.name: requests / defaultRequests
props.description: Requests already made ({ id, type, from, to, days }); their days are held off the balance. Controlled or initial.

props.name: onRequestsChange
props.description: Fires from Request and Cancel with every request.

props.name: type / defaultType
props.description: The kind of leave, by policy id; controlled or initial.

props.name: onTypeChange
props.description: Fires from the press or arrow key that changed the kind of leave.

props.name: range / defaultRange
props.description: The selection, ms at UTC midnight, inclusive; controlled or initial.

props.name: onRangeChange
props.description: Fires from the press, drag or key that changed the selection.

props.name: onRequest
props.description: Request was pressed, with the request and its working days.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Cancel was pressed on a request.

props.name: now
props.description: Today in ms; earlier days cannot be chosen and notice counts from it. Never read from the clock.

props.name: defaultMonth
props.description: The first month shown: any ms inside it.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading shows a placeholder month; error explains and offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the calendar failed to load.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; the body scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be chosen or requested.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: each month is a grid with one date as the tab stop across all of them. Arrows move by day and week and carry the view into the next month, Home and End go to the week's ends, Page Up and Page Down a month; Enter or Space sets the first day and then the last, Shift with an arrow extends from the start, Escape clears.
Mouse and pen can press and drag across days; touch uses two taps so a finger sliding over the month still scrolls the page.

The drain is one motion value: every meter cell, every day's wash and the count derive from it, so a long selection never re-renders React per frame, and nothing runs once it settles. Announcements are made once per settled change — dates, working days, what is left and who else is away — never per day.
Reduced motion: the drain is instant, the meter does not shake and months do not glide; the counts, washes and the shortfall sentence still change because they are the information.

Colours: your request and balance use the tone as a pigment at fixed lightness with dark ink; teammates have their own soft pigments, kept apart from every tone, and are named in each day's label and in the Also away list, never colour alone.

items.title: Backward Plan
items.tagline: Set the deadline and the plan lays itself out behind it.
items.description: A deadline-first planner: every task is scheduled as late as it can be and drawn as a car on a timeline that ends at the deadline flag. Dragging the flag, or any unlocked car, pulls the train — each car's finish follows the start of the car after it through the springs.snap calibration, integrated per frame in one loop, so the pull travels back down the train and every car settles a beat after the one ahead; the release projects the throw to a whole day and the flag springs there with its velocity. Cars pushed before today turn amber, locked cars hold their dates and lean toward the pull before springing upright on springs.recoil, and the flag is a slider whose arrow keys move the deadline a day while Tab reaches every task.

props.name: barStyle
props.description: How a task is drawn: a pigment bar, a tinted bar with a strong leading edge, or a thin rail with its dates above.

props.name: dayWidth
props.description: Pixels per day on the board: the scale of the timeline (8 to 40).

props.name: accent
props.description: The bars' pigment at a fixed lightness; tasks in the past are always amber.

props.name: tasks / defaultTasks
props.description: Each { id, name, days, after?: id[], locked?, start? }; start is the first day of a locked task. Controlled or initial.

props.name: onTasksChange
props.description: Fires with every task after a lock, a pinned move or a length change.

props.name: deadline / defaultDeadline
props.description: The handover day, ms at UTC midnight; controlled or initial.

props.name: onDeadlineChange
props.description: Fires from the drag release or the key that moved the deadline, with the new day.

props.name: onTaskChange
props.description: Fires when one task's pinned dates or length change.

props.name: onLock
props.description: Fires when a task is locked (to its current dates) or unlocked.

props.name: now
props.description: Today in ms; tasks that would start before it turn amber. Never read from the clock.

props.name: range
props.description: Earliest and latest deadline, in days after now.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading shows placeholder bars; error explains and offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the plan failed to load.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; the board scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be moved or locked.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the deadline flag is a slider — Left and Right move it a day, Page Up and Page Down a week, Home and End to the range's ends — and the board scrolls to keep it in view. Tab then reaches each task's lock toggle and bar; on a bar, L locks it, Left and Right move a locked task a day, Shift with Left or Right changes its length.

One rAF loop drives the whole train while something moves and stops when every car is within a thousandth of a day and still; it never runs while the board is off screen or the tab is hidden (cars jump to their places instead) and allocates nothing per frame. Bars and couplings are written through motion values; React renders only when the snapped day changes.
Reduced motion: no train — every car jumps to its place when the deadline changes and locked cars do not lean; amber, dates, couplings and the summary still change.

A task that would have to start before a task it needs has finished (behind a locked one) is ringed, its coupling breaks into a dashed danger line and the header says what it waits on — in words, never colour alone. Below a 40rem container the board becomes a list with start dates under a deadline stepper, and a deadline change rolls the dates a cascade step per car.
Dates are whole UTC days and are formatted by hand, so the server and the browser draw the same plan.

items.title: Webhook Replay
items.tagline: See every delivery, and send a failed one again.
items.description: A webhook endpoint's delivery log where a failed delivery can be sent again. Replay sends a pulse along its row — a comet riding one motion value for 520 ms on the move ease, from the event name, under the columns, to the status chip — and if the answer is not back the head breathes at the chip until it is; then the chip flips about its horizontal axis, out on the exit ease and in on springs.snap with a soft success ring, or still failing, in on springs.flick to the new error code with the new response under the event. Rows open with Enter to the payload, headers and response at their measured height on springs.glide, Up and Down walk the rows, R replays, and the endpoint can be paused and its signing secret revealed or rotated.

props.name: chipStyle
props.description: How each status code is drawn: a tinted pill, a square tag with a leading bar, or a dot and the bare code.

props.name: payloadTheme
props.description: How payloads, headers and responses are coloured: one ink, tinted tokens, or a dark code panel in both themes.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height and type in the log.

props.name: endpoints

props.name: deliveries / defaultDeliveries
props.description: Most recent first: { id, endpoint, event, status, duration, attempt, at, payload, response?, replayAs? }; controlled or initial.

props.name: onDeliveriesChange
props.description: Fires with every delivery after a replay lands or a test event is sent.

props.name: endpoint / defaultEndpoint
props.description: The endpoint shown, by id; controlled or initial.

props.name: onEndpointChange
props.description: Fires from the tab press or arrow key that chose another endpoint.

props.name: onReplay
props.description: Replay was pressed. Return { status, duration, body? } or a promise of it; return nothing and the delivery's replayAs answers. A rejected promise reads as no answer.

props.name: onPause
props.description: Pause or Resume was pressed.

props.name: onRotateSecret
props.description: Rotate was confirmed. Return the new secret, or nothing for a generated one.

props.name: onSendTest
props.description: Send test event was pressed on an empty log; a test delivery is added and lands with its own pulse.

props.name: now
props.description: The current time in ms; delivery times are read against it. Never read from the clock.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading shows placeholder rows; error explains and offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the log failed to load.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; the log scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be replayed, paused or rotated.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: endpoints are a tablist and the filter a radio group. The log is an ordered list whose rows are disclosure buttons with one tab stop: Up and Down move between rows, Home and End jump, Enter or Space opens the payload, headers and response (a tablist), R replays a failed row. Replay is also its own labelled button, kept focusable with aria-disabled while sending or paused, and its name says why.

Status chips carry the code as text and the words in their title and in the row's accessible name ("504 Gateway timeout"); success and failure differ in colour and in words. One polite announcement when a replay starts and one with its result.

The pulse is one motion value and three tail segments derived from it; the secret's scramble is one short tween; nothing runs at rest, and both stop on unmount. The pulse's route is measured from the row when the replay starts, so it follows the wide layout or the stacked one.

Reduced motion: no pulse, flip or bloom; the chip dims while sending and cross-fades to its new code, panels open without growing and the secret swaps without scrambling. Codes, attempts and times still update.

Secrets are masked until revealed with an explicit action, and signature headers stay masked. The night payload theme is a deliberately fixed dark panel; the other two use tokens and follow the theme.

items.title: Sync Pairs
items.tagline: Pair the fields and choose which way each flows.
items.description: A two-way field mapping between two apps whose fields face each other across a gutter of soft cables. Dragging from a field draws a live cable 1:1 under the pointer; plugged into a compatible field its sag drops in slack and swings taut on springs.recoil, two visible bounces of a rope catching. Pressing a cable's knot cycles its direction — right, left, both — and the arrowhead turns on springs.flick and slides along the curve to its new end on springs.glide, a second chevron sliding out for both ways; lossy flows draw the cable in warn and name what is lost, and types that do not convert refuse to pair. Each side is a listbox: Enter opens a partner list, D turns a pair, Delete unpairs, and narrow containers turn the cables into rows with direction chips.

props.name: cableStyle

props.name: density

props.name: accent

props.name: leftApp

props.name: rightApp
props.description: The app on the right: { name, initials }.

props.name: leftFields

props.name: rightFields
props.description: The right app's fields.

props.name: pairs / defaultPairs
props.description: Each { left, right, direction: "right" | "left" | "both" }; one partner per field. Controlled or initial.

props.name: onPairsChange
props.description: Fires with every pair after a pairing, an unpairing or a direction change.

props.name: onPair
props.description: Two fields were paired; any pair it replaced is reported through onUnpair first.

props.name: onUnpair
props.description: A pair was taken apart.

props.name: onDirectionChange
props.description: A pair's direction was cycled; directions a type cannot flow in are skipped.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading shows placeholder rows; error explains and offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the fields failed to load.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; the board scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be paired, unpaired or turned.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: each side is a listbox with one tab stop — Up and Down move, Left and Right cross to the other side (to the partner when there is one). Enter or Space opens the partner list, a popover listbox that names what each type does to the values (converts, lossy and why, or doesn't convert); Enter pairs, Escape closes and returns focus. On a paired field or a knot, D turns the pair and Delete unpairs; knots are buttons in the tab order.

Pointer: drag from a field to its partner, or tap one field and then another. A drag captures only after 4px, so a press is still a tap; dragging a plugged field's cable into empty space unpairs it, and a drop the types refuse flies back to its port.

Every cable's sag, knot and chevrons are motion values driven by springs that stop when they settle; paths are rebuilt from them with useTransform, row positions are arithmetic and the gutter is measured once by a ResizeObserver — nothing runs at rest.

Reduced motion: cables appear without swinging, chevrons jump to their ends and a refused drop simply disappears; the live cable still follows the pointer because it is the gesture. Lossy pairs are named in the knot's label, under narrow rows and in the footer, never by colour alone.
Below a 36rem container the cables become rows with a direction chip that cycles, an unpair button, and an Add a pair form of two native selects.

items.title: Bulletin Composer
items.tagline: Build the newsletter, then check it on a phone.
items.description: An email layout editor: a palette of header, text, image, button and divider blocks feeds a one-column letter drawn in a device frame, and each block opens an edit panel for its content. Toggling Desktop and Phone changes the frame's width in one render and every block FLIPs to its new box on springs.glide — corners round into a phone bezel, pictures go full bleed, the call to action stretches and text slides to its new wrap without being squashed — while a ruler over the letter marks where the phone width will cut. Blocks and palette tiles drag 1:1: an accent drop line opens a gap between the blocks under it on glide and, on release, every block glides from where it is drawn to its new slot with the throw's velocity; the letter is a listbox where Up and Down move, Alt with Up or Down moves the block, Enter edits it and Delete removes it, and missing alt text is flagged on the picture, in its field and in a count that jumps to it.

props.name: blockStyle

props.name: accent

props.name: blocks / defaultBlocks

props.name: onChange

props.name: title

props.name: preheader

props.name: testAddress

props.name: onSchedule

props.name: now

props.name: status

props.name: onRetry

props.name: height
props.description: The editor's height in px; the letter scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: blocks can be browsed and previewed but not edited, moved, sent or scheduled.

props.name: className
