usageNotes: The letter is a listbox with one roving stop: Up and Down move between blocks, Home and End jump, Alt with Up or Down moves the block (the same glide as a drag), Enter opens its edit panel on the first field and Delete removes it; Escape clears the selection and is consumed only when there was one.
Only the preview toggle runs a layout animation (layoutDependency is the preview), so typing in the panel and reorders never re-measure the letter; moves use a FLIP on each block's own offset.
Under reduced motion the preview, every move and every insert land at once; the drop line and the gap still show, and every flag and count still changes.

Below a 40rem container the rail becomes a bottom sheet (a modal dialog with a focus trap, Escape and a drag-down to close) and the letter takes the full width; the compact letter type applies whenever the letter is under 27rem, as a real responsive email would.
Pictures are drawn in code from tokens and the accent; colours never come from hex values, so the letter reads in both themes.
Send test and Schedule results come from the host: return a promise from onSendTest or onSchedule to show sending, sent and failed states.

items.title: Quick Fix
items.tagline: Problems underlined, fixes one keystroke away.
items.description: A code editor panel built from code and diagnostics: every problem is underlined under its exact columns in its severity's colour, marked in the gutter and counted in the header. Applying a fix morphs the faulty token into its correction character by character — the common start and end stay, each changed slot rolls on springs.snap in a left-to-right cascade and slots that appear or vanish grow or shrink on springs.glide — while the squiggle unwinds, its coil straightening on glide before it retracts into its middle, and the count ticks down on snap. The text is a real textarea over a painted layer: F8 and Shift+F8 walk the problems, gliding the code into view and opening a peek under the line, Command or Control with period opens the fixes menu at the caret, and edits shift the problems after them.

props.name: squiggleStyle
props.description: How a problem is underlined: a sine wave, a row of dots (they close into a rule as a fix unwinds them) or a straight rule.

props.name: editorTheme
props.description: The surface and syntax colour: the card with quiet hues, a sunk slate panel with stronger hues and a tinted gutter, or no syntax colour so only the squiggles carry colour.

props.name: fontScale
props.description: Code size as a multiple of 13px; line height, squiggle size and gutter follow.

props.name: code / defaultCode
props.description: The source text.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires with the new text after typing or a fix.

props.name: diagnostics / defaultDiagnostics
props.description: Problems as { id, from, to, severity, message, rule?, fixes?: { id, title, text }[] }, where from and to are character offsets into the code.

props.name: onDiagnosticsChange
props.description: Fires after a fix, an ignore, or an edit that shifted problems or dropped one it touched.

props.name: onApplyFix
props.description: A fix was applied, with the new text.

props.name: onIgnore
props.description: A problem was ignored from the peek or the menu.

props.name: fileName
props.description: The file's path, shown on its tab; the last part names it in messages.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the file has opened: loading draws ruled lines, error offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the file failed to open.

props.name: problemsOpen / defaultProblemsOpen
props.description: Whether the problems panel is shown under the code.

props.name: onProblemsOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the count button or the panel's close button.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: The text can be read and navigated with F8, but not typed into or fixed.

props.name: height
props.description: The panel's height in px; the code scrolls inside it.

props.name: label
props.description: The editor's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be typed, fixed or ignored.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the editor's outer box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: F8 moves the caret to the next problem and Shift+F8 to the previous one, each announced once with its line, message and fix count; Command or Control with period opens a real menu of fixes plus Ignore at the caret (arrows, Home, End, Enter), and Escape closes the peek or the menu and is consumed only then. Tab leaves the editor as usual.

The editor is a real textarea over a painted layer, so caret, selection, typing and native shortcuts all work; edits shift every problem after them and drop one whose range they touch, for the host to re-check.
Under reduced motion the token cross-fades instead of rolling, the squiggle fades instead of unwinding, and the code jumps into view; counts, marks and the clean state still change.
Nothing loops at rest: the morph and the unwind are finite animations, scrolling moves the painted layer with one transform per scroll event, and one probe measures the character width per font size.
Below a 30rem container the gutter keeps its numbers but hides the marks and lightbulb, and the header folds the counts into one.

items.title: Screenshot Markup
items.tagline: Arrow it, box it, and blur what's private.
items.description: An image annotation editor: arrows, boxes, labels and redaction over a screenshot, every mark kept in the image's own pixels. Drawing an arrow, the shaft bows behind the hand — a curve whose control point trails the pointer on springs.glide — and on release it pulls taut while the head springs into place on springs.recoil with two visible bounces. The redact brush pixelates whatever passes under it: cells of a grid fill with the real mosaic of the image beneath, popping in as separate tiles on springs.flick, and when the stroke ends they settle — gaps closing and corners squaring on springs.snap in the order they were laid — into one solid mosaic. Tools have single keys, the canvas has a keyboard cursor so Enter, arrows and Enter draw any mark, [ and ] select marks, arrows nudge them and Delete removes them, and undo and redo walk a history.

props.name: strokeWidth
props.description: Stroke of arrows and boxes in image px; it also sizes arrowheads, labels and the redact brush (six times the stroke).

props.name: toolPalette
props.description: Where the tools live: a rail down the left, a pill floating over the image, or a strip under the header. Below a 36rem container they dock at the bottom whatever this is.

props.name: accent
props.description: The markup colour, taken at a fixed lightness so marks read the same over either theme.

props.name: image
props.description: The screenshot as { width, height, alt, src?, content? }: a raster src, or SVG content drawn in the image's coordinates (the default Basinworks dashboard).

props.name: annotations / defaultAnnotations
props.description: Marks in image pixels: arrow { x1, y1, x2, y2 }, box { x, y, w, h }, text { x, y, text } and redact { size, cells: [column, row][] }.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires with every mark after one is drawn, moved, nudged, edited, removed, undone or redone.

props.name: tool / defaultTool
props.description: The active tool.

props.name: onToolChange
props.description: Fires from the button or single key (V, A, B, T, R) that picked a tool.

props.name: selected / defaultSelected
props.description: The selected mark's id.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.description: Fires when a click, a bracket key or a new mark changes the selection.

props.name: onUndo
props.description: Undo was pressed or Command/Control+Z typed, with the marks it went back to.

props.name: onRedo
props.description: Redo was pressed or Shift+Command/Control+Z typed, with the marks it restored.

props.name: onExport
props.description: Export was pressed. Return a promise to show it exporting; a rejection offers Retry.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the screenshot has arrived: loading shows a ruled frame and a progress bar, error offers Try again.

props.name: progress
props.description: How much of a large screenshot has loaded, 0 to 1; omit it for an indeterminate bar.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the screenshot failed to load.

props.name: title
props.description: The editor's heading.

props.name: cellSize
props.description: The redaction grid in image px: the size of each pixelated block.

props.name: height
props.description: The editor's tallest height in px; the image letterboxes inside.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Marks can be viewed but not drawn, moved, removed or exported.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the editor's outer box.

usageNotes: The canvas is one focusable group with a keyboard cursor: arrows move it (Shift for larger steps), Enter starts a mark of the current tool there, arrows extend it and Enter ends it with the same landing as the pointer; [ and ] select marks, arrows nudge the selected one (Shift for ten pixels), Delete removes it and Escape cancels a mark or clears the selection, consumed only when it does something.

Redaction is a real mosaic: an SVG pixelate filter (blur, sample, dilate) over a use-copy of the image, clipped to the brushed cells, so it works on drawn SVG and raster src images alike; the source pixels remain in the page, so export the flattened image server-side before sharing.
Under reduced motion the arrow draws straight and its head appears in place, cells land as a solid mosaic, and moves are immediate; the pixelation and every count are unchanged.
Nothing loops at rest: the trailing control point, the head's landing and the settle are finite springs, and the brush adds cells to state only when it crosses a new one.
Arrow and box colours ride on plain groups through currentColor, so a changed accent re-colours marks that motion is animating.

items.title: Schema Table
items.tagline: Change a field's type and watch the data convert.
items.description: A database schema editor where each field's name, type and options sit above its sample column, so a change of type is something you watch. Picking a new type previews it: the column converts one cell at a time down the rows — the old drawing lifts and fades on a tween while the new one rises and grows from 0.94 on springs.snap, text becoming date chips, numbers gaining currency and cents, yes becoming a tick — and a cell that will not convert keeps its text, struck faint on a danger hatch with its reason; a confirm bar glides down on springs.glide, Convert commits and Cancel converts back bottom row first. Fields reorder by a grip that follows the hand 1:1 while the other columns slide aside on glide and land with the throw, or by Alt with an arrow on the field's button, which also opens a real menu of types (each showing how many cells would fail), rename, options, moves and remove.

props.name: typeBadge
props.description: How a field's type shows in its header: a glyph, a word, or both; the badge rolls to the new type on snap.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height (30, 36 or 44px), type size and column width; columns glide to a new width.

props.name: accent
props.description: The editor's colour: the previewed field, Convert, ticks, and where the select-chip hues start.

props.name: fields / defaultFields
props.description: Fields in column order as { id, name, type, options? }, where type is text, number, currency, date, select, checkbox or email and options carry currency, decimals, dateStyle and choices. An empty list starts with one Name field.

props.name: onFieldsChange
props.description: Fires with every field after a rename, a confirmed type change, an option, a move, an add or a removal.

props.name: sampleRows / defaultSampleRows
props.description: Sample records as { id, cells: { [fieldId]: string | number | boolean | null } }; dates are ISO strings.

props.name: onSampleRowsChange
props.description: Fires after a conversion rewrote a column, or a field was added or removed.

props.name: onFieldChange
props.description: A field was renamed, re-typed (only after Convert) or given new options.

props.name: onAddField
props.description: Add field created a field; its name input takes focus.

props.name: onRemoveField
props.description: A field was removed after its menu's second press.

props.name: totalRows
props.description: How many records the whole table holds, shown in the footer beside the sample count.

props.name: title
props.description: The table's name; also names the table for assistive technology.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the schema has arrived: loading draws skeleton rows, error offers Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the schema failed to load.

props.name: height
props.description: The editor's height in px; the table scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: fields can be browsed but not changed, moved, added or removed.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the editor's outer box.

usageNotes: Field buttons are one roving tab stop: Left and Right (Up and Down in the list view) move between fields, Home and End jump, Alt with an arrow moves the field, F2 renames it and Enter opens its menu; the menu takes arrows, Home, End and Enter, and Escape closes it (and is consumed) with focus back on the field.

A type change never applies on the first press: it previews, marks every cell that will not convert with its reason in the cell's name, and waits for Convert, which takes focus as the bar arrives; Escape on the bar cancels.
Conversion is a pure function of the column, so a preview costs one pass over the sample; drags write one motion value per field and render only when the drop slot changes.
Under reduced motion every swap is a short cross-fade with no cascade and every move lands at once; failure marks, counts and the confirm step are unchanged.
Below a 40rem container the fields become a list of cards with the same buttons, menu and conversion, and reorder vertically.

items.title: Promoter Scale
items.tagline: Zero to ten, then the one question that fits.
items.description: A score survey: zero to ten, then the one question written for the band the answer falls in. Picking a score fills the segments from zero up to it in a quick wave — each fill sweeping in on springs.snap a few milliseconds after the last, every one in the picked band's colour, draining from the top when the score drops — and a beat later the scale shrinks into a summary chip, its segments travelling on springs.glide into the chip's mini ticks while the follow-up slides in from 16px. The scale is a real radio group: arrows and Home or End move the score with the wave following, number keys pick one (1 then 0 is ten) and Enter, Space or a click confirms; the chip brings the scale back, Escape in the follow-up does too, and sending, thanked, failed and dismissed states are covered with the card's measured height gliding between them.

props.name: segmentStyle
props.description: How the scale is drawn: equal tiles that fill from the left, bars rising left to right that fill from the base, or discs that fill from the centre.

props.name: bandPalette
props.description: Band colours as pigment: danger, warn and success; the accent at three depths; or quiet greys with promoters in the accent.

props.name: cornerRadius
props.description: Corner radius in px of the segments, ticks, chip, field and buttons; the card rounds with it.

props.name: question
props.defaultValue: "How likely are you to recommend Fernworks to a friend or colleague?"
props.description: The question over the scale; it also names the radio group.

props.name: bands
props.description: Score bands low to high as { id, label, from, to, colour? }: Detractor 0–6, Passive 7–8, Promoter 9–10 by default.

props.name: followUps
props.description: The follow-up for each band id as { question, placeholder?, chips? }; chips become quick reason toggles.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The score.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires as a click, an arrow or a number key changes the score.

props.name: onScore
props.description: A score was confirmed and its follow-up opened.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Send or Skip was pressed with { score, band, comment, reasons }. Return a promise to show sending; a rejection shows the failed state with the answer kept.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: The survey was dismissed; it folds to one line with Undo.

props.name: lowLabel
props.description: Words under the low end of the scale.

props.name: highLabel
props.description: Words under the high end of the scale.

props.name: max
props.description: The top of the scale.

props.name: sendState
props.description: Controlled send state, for a host that tracks delivery itself; by default it follows the promise onSubmit returns.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The survey can be read but not answered.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the survey's outer box.

usageNotes: The scale is a radio group with one roving stop: arrows and Home or End move the score (the wave follows), number keys pick one directly with 1 then 0 inside 600ms meaning ten, and Enter, Space, a click or the Continue button confirms it; focus then moves to the follow-up field, and Escape there brings the scale back (consumed).
Each radio is named with its score and band ("8, passive") and the chip with the score and what pressing it does; sending, the result and a dismissal are announced once.
Under reduced motion the fill appears at once in the band's colour and the scale, chip and follow-up cross-fade without the shared-layout travel; the score, band and every state still show.

Nothing loops: the wave, the travel and the height are finite springs, and the only spinner runs while a send is in flight. The card's height is measured with one ResizeObserver and glides between states, so nothing reserves space.
Below a 34rem container the scale wraps into two rows (0–5 over 6–10) and the follow-up stacks its question under the chip, keeping every state inside a 232px card.

items.title: Bug Snapshot
items.tagline: Report a bug with the screen already attached.
items.description: A bug report that starts from the page it is about: Report a bug flashes the page (or closes a shutter on it, or lifts it toward you), then a copy of the page shrinks along a straight path into the form's thumbnail slot on springs.glide and drops into it on springs.recoil while the form's sections rise into place in cascade order. A drag on the thumbnail draws a highlight or an opaque redaction from the press point, the signed-in address is hidden on its own, environment rows can be removed and restored, and Send becomes its own progress bar that follows the host's progress on glide; a failed upload keeps every word, box and choice. Every box is a button that arrow keys move and Alt with an arrow resizes, Add box draws one from the keyboard, and the category and severity are radiogroups with roving focus.

props.name: page
props.description: The page the capture shows, drawn into a 16:10 frame: an <svg viewBox> or an element that fills its box.

props.name: pageLabel
props.description: Names the page in the frame's bar and the report header.

props.name: sensitiveAreas
props.description: Areas redacted automatically on every capture, as { id, kind, x, y, w, h } in percent of the page.

props.name: environment
props.description: Environment rows sent with the report as { id, label, value }; each can be removed and restored.

props.name: categories
props.description: The kinds of problem offered, as { id, label }.

props.name: severities
props.description: Severity steps, mildest first, as { id, label, tone? } with tone neutral, accent, warn or danger.

props.name: defaultDraft
props.description: The draft the form starts from: { category, severity, happened, expected }. Defaults to the first category and medium severity.

props.name: onDraftChange
props.description: Fires with the whole draft whenever a field, category or severity changes.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the report is open, controlled or initial. Opening captures the page.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the button that opened or closed the report.

props.name: onCapture
props.description: A capture has landed in the form (on open and on Retake).

props.name: onRedact
props.description: Fires with every redaction box after one is added, moved or removed, and after a capture.

props.name: onSubmit
props.type: (report: BugReport, progress: (fraction: number) => void) => void | Promise<unknown>
props.description: Send was pressed with a valid report. Return a promise to show the upload and call progress(0–1) to drive the bar; a rejection keeps the draft, a resolved string is shown as the reference.

props.name: captureStyle
props.description: How the capture announces itself: a white flash, an ink shutter closing and opening, or the page lifting toward you before it shrinks.

props.name: density
props.description: Control height (28, 32 or 36px), padding, type size and gaps.

props.name: highlightColor
props.description: Highlight strokes, washes, numbered badges and the landing flash — any CSS colour.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the surface grows before the report scrolls inside it, in px. The page frame is capped to fit it.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the environment details have been read: loading shows skeleton rows, error a line with Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the environment failed to read.

props.name: title
props.description: The report's heading and the surface's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be opened, drawn or sent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab reaches every control. Category, severity and the drawing tool are radiogroups (arrows move and select, Home and End jump). Add box draws a box in the middle of the screenshot and focuses it; on a box, arrows move it 1% (Shift 5%), Alt with an arrow resizes it, and Delete or Backspace removes it.

Reduced motion: the capture becomes a cross-fade with a soft flash on the thumbnail and nothing travels; boxes, the severity indicator and the environment rows change at once, while the upload bar still fills and the sent card still appears.

Real screen capture is the host's job: pass what was on screen as `page` (an SVG or an element that fills a 16:10 box) and the areas to hide as `sensitiveAreas`. The capture is drawn, so it costs nothing until Report is pressed.

onSubmit receives a `progress` callback: call it with 0–1 as the upload reports bytes. With no reports the bar creeps toward 90% on a long ease-out so it never looks stuck and never claims to be finished.
There is no loop: motion runs only after a press, a drag or an upload, the copy in flight exists only during a capture, and every animation and pending answer is dropped on unmount.

items.title: Similar Ideas
items.tagline: Someone may have asked already; add your vote.
items.description: An idea panel that checks the roadmap while you type: after three letters a quiet spinner turns at the end of the field, then the ideas most like yours rise 16px from below it on springs.glide in cascade order, each with its status, votes and a match strength that fills as it lands; ideas that stop matching fade out and the rest glide to their seats. Voting folds your draft into the idea as your comment — the draft lifts off the field as a pill and glides into the row's note line while the vote count rolls on snap and the comment badge lands on recoil — and with nothing similar the list gives way to a clean submit. The field is a combobox: Up and Down move through matches, Enter votes, Shift+Enter follows and Escape clears.

props.name: ideas / defaultIdeas
props.description: The roadmap's ideas as { id, title, body, status: "review" | "planned" | "shipped", votes, comments, voted?, following?, updated, shippedIn?, note? }, controlled or initial.

props.name: onIdeasChange
props.description: Fires with every idea after a vote, a follow or a post.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The draft title in the field, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires on every keystroke, and when a vote or a post clears the field.

props.name: onVote
props.type: (ideaId: string, voted: boolean, comment?: string) => void
props.description: A vote was cast (with the draft as the comment when there was one) or taken back.

props.name: onSubmitNew
props.description: Post was pressed: a new idea from the field and the details.

props.name: onFollow
props.description: The follow bell was pressed, or Shift+Enter on a highlighted match.

props.name: onMatches
props.description: A search settled, with the ids of the similar ideas it found — for counting requests that found an existing home.

props.name: matchStyle
props.description: How the match strength reads: a thin bar with its percentage, five dots, or a small ring gauge.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height, padding, gaps and type.

props.name: statusPalette
props.description: Status colours: amber, cobalt and green; three cool hues; or ink, with the dashed, half and filled glyphs telling them apart.

props.name: maxMatches
props.description: The most similar ideas shown at once.

props.name: minScore
props.description: How alike an idea must be to show, from 0 to 1.

props.name: searchDelayMs
props.description: How long the quiet spinner turns after the last keystroke before matches rise, in ms.

props.name: product
props.description: The product whose roadmap this is, named in the header.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The field's placeholder.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment ages count from, so the server and the browser print the same text.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the ideas have arrived: loading holds the field, error shows a line with Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the ideas failed to load.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the panel grows before it scrolls inside, in px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be typed, voted, followed or posted.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the panel.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the field is a combobox with aria-activedescendant. Up and Down move through the matches, Home and End jump once one is highlighted, Enter votes for it (adding your text as a comment), Shift+Enter follows it, and Escape clears the highlight, then the field. With no matches Enter posts the idea.

Reduced motion: matches appear in place with a fade, strengths are drawn at once and the draft cross-fades into its note line instead of flying; counts, statuses and the list height still change. The spinner becomes three still dots that fade.

Matching runs in the browser over the ideas you pass: each query word takes its best match in the title (or 60% of its best in the body), with stems, shared prefixes and a small synonym list. Pass your own ranked ideas through `ideas` if matching happens on a server.
Use onMatches to measure deflection — how often a request found an existing idea — and onVote's comment to keep the requester's words with the vote.
Nothing runs while idle: one timer per keystroke, cleared by the next; the spinner exists only while a search is pending; one ResizeObserver measures the list for its height glide.

items.title: Ease Check
items.tagline: One quick question, right after the task.
items.description: A one-row question for right after a task, whose effort slider is a string between two pegs: pressing rests the finger on it, dragging moves the thumb 1:1 while dragging up or down bends the string under the thumb into two straight runs with a rounded apex, and letting go settles the thumb on its step on springs.snap and plucks the string, which rings through straight on a spring with springs.recoil's character (its stiffness set by the track and the tension) carrying the release velocity. A release, a tap or Enter sends the answer; low scores open a short why field on a measured glide, others say thanks and fold the question away, and a task is never asked twice. It is a real slider: arrows step and pluck lightly, Page keys move two, Home and End jump.

props.name: question
props.description: The question, asked right after the task; it also labels the slider.

props.name: taskId
props.description: The finished task this asks about. Each task is asked once: answered or dismissed, it never returns.

props.name: stepCount
props.description: Points on the scale, 3 to 10: ticks, labels and keyboard steps.

props.name: labels
props.description: One label per point, hardest first. Defaults to a preset for 3, 5 and 7 points, else the end labels and "n of N".

props.name: minLabel
props.description: The hard end's label.

props.name: maxLabel
props.description: The easy end's label.

props.name: lowThreshold
props.description: Scores at or below this open the why field.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The score, 1 to stepCount, or null before an answer; controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the release, tap or key that chose a score.

props.name: onAnswer
props.description: An answer was sent: on release, on a tap, or on Enter.

props.name: onComment
props.type: (text: string, score: number, taskId: string) => void
props.description: The why field was sent, with the score it explains.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: The question was dismissed without an answer.

props.name: trackStyle
props.description: What the slider is made of: a fine string that rings fast, a thick cord that sways slowly, or beads on a thread, one per point.

props.name: tone
props.description: The filled run and thumb: cobalt; a colour that warms from red at the hard end through amber to green; or ink.

props.name: tension
props.description: How taut the string is, 0 to 1: tighter rings faster and settles sooner.

props.name: whyPrompt
props.description: The why field's prompt and label.

props.name: thanksMs
props.description: How long the thanks shows before the question folds away, in ms.

props.name: persist
props.description: Also remember asked tasks in localStorage, so they stay answered across visits.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The slider and buttons do nothing.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the question's outer box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the slider is role="slider" labelled by the question, with aria-valuetext such as "5 of 7, fairly easy". Arrows step from the waiting middle thumb, Page Up and Page Down move two, Home and End jump, and Enter sends; after a key the line under the string says "Enter to send". In the why field Enter sends and Escape skips.
Reduced motion: the string never bends or rings and the thumb moves to its step at once; the value, the fill, the why field and the thanks still change, and the fold is instant.

Ask once: pass a stable `taskId` per finished task. Answered and dismissed task ids are remembered for the page's life (and in localStorage with `persist`), and a question for one of them renders nothing — so it is safe to mount it after every export.
It fits one row at 316px: the question wraps to two short lines beside the slider, and the end labels appear from 30rem. Give it the width of the task's own surface.
There is no loop: the string's spring runs only after a press or a key and stops when it settles, and the path is rebuilt from two motion values with every coordinate rounded.

items.title: Point and Tell
items.tagline: Point at the part of the page you mean.
items.description: Feedback that points: Point turns the page into targets, and hovering — or Tab, which cycles through the parts while point mode is on — finds the smallest part under the pointer while one fine measuring outline travels to its box on springs.snap, with its size in a tag and guides out to the page's edges. A click or Enter pins it: a crop of the page lifts off at the part's own box and flies into its slot in the form on springs.glide on one uniform scale while the outline flashes. Crops are the page drawn again and scaled, sensitive values are masked in every crop, Escape leaves point mode, and Send shows sending, sent and failed — a failure keeps the note and every pin.

props.name: targets
props.description: The page's parts as { id, label, kind, rect: { x, y, w, h } in percent of a 16:10 page, text?, sensitive? }; each kind (header, nav, heading, field, select, button, chart, table, card, note, badge) draws itself.

props.name: pageLabel
props.description: Names the page in its frame's bar and the point-mode group.

props.name: form
props.description: The form's words: { heading, prompt, placeholder, sendLabel }, defaulting to Feedback, a one-line prompt, "What should we know?" and Send.

props.name: pointing / defaultPointing
props.description: Whether point mode is on, controlled or initial.

props.name: onPointingChange
props.description: Fires from the button, key or send that turned point mode on or off.

props.name: pins / defaultPins
props.description: The pinned target ids in pin order, controlled or initial.

props.name: onPinsChange
props.description: Fires with every pin after one is added or removed.

props.name: onPoint
props.description: A part of the page was pinned.

props.name: onSubmit
props.type: (feedback: { message: string; targets: PointTarget[] }) => void | Promise<unknown>
props.description: Send was pressed. Return a promise to show sending; a rejection shows the failure and keeps the note and pins.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Cancel was pressed; pins and note are cleared.

props.name: outlineStyle
props.description: The pointing outline: a fine box with corner ticks, guides and a size tag; a dashed box with the tag; or four corner brackets.

props.name: maskStyle
props.description: How sensitive values look in crops: blurred, covered by solid bars, or replaced by dots. The live page is untouched.

props.name: accent
props.description: Outline, guides, pin numbers, the point-mode tint and Send — any CSS colour.

props.name: maxPins
props.description: The most parts that can be pinned at once.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the surface grows before it scrolls inside, in px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be pointed at, pinned or sent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Point is a toggle button. In point mode the parts are buttons over the drawn page in reading order; focus moves to the first, Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through them (a loop until you leave), Enter or Space pins or unpins, and Escape leaves point mode from anywhere in the surface and returns focus to Point. Removing a pin moves focus to the next pin's remove button.
Reduced motion: the outline jumps to each box and fades, a pin appears in its slot with a fade instead of flying, and the sent check is drawn at once; pins, masks and the send states all still show.
Mark parts that show personal data `sensitive`: they read normally on the page and are masked in every crop and in the copy that flies, so a screenshot of the form never carries them.

The page is drawn in container units from `targets`, so it scales to any width and each crop is the same page at 640px, scaled and clipped — exact, and free of images. Pass your own parts with percent rects to point at your own screen.

Nothing runs while idle: hover hit-testing is the buttons themselves (smaller parts sit above larger ones), the outline moves only when the part under the pointer or focus changes, and the flying crop exists only during a pin.

items.title: Theme Sorter
items.tagline: Sort incoming feedback into themes that count.
items.description: A feedback inbox you sort by hand: a card lifts after 4px of travel and follows the pointer 1:1 as a copy above both columns, leaning with its speed, while the theme under it swells on springs.snap. Dropped on a theme it is squeezed in — narrowing on springs.glide and flattening 60ms behind on the same spring toward the theme's centre — the theme gulps on springs.recoil as its tally rolls up on snap, and once it is in the themes re-rank by count with a layout glide; dropped anywhere else it springs home with the release velocity. The inbox is one tab stop with roving focus: Up and Down move, T or Enter opens a theme menu with type-ahead and New theme, A or Delete archives, and a failed tag springs the card back into its slot with a note.

props.name: items / defaultItems
props.description: Feedback as { id, quote, customer, company, source: "email" | "call" | "survey" | "chat" | "review", plan, sentiment: "positive" | "neutral" | "negative", at, themeId?, archived? }, controlled or initial. Untagged, unarchived items wait in the inbox; tagged ones count toward their theme.

props.name: onItemsChange
props.description: Fires with every item after a tag, an archive or a failed tag's revert.

props.name: themes / defaultThemes
props.description: Themes as { id, name }, controlled or initial; shown most-counted first.

props.name: onThemesChange
props.description: Fires with every theme after one is created.

props.name: onTag
props.description: An item was tagged by a drop or the theme menu. Return a promise; a rejection springs the item back into the inbox with a note and rolls the tally back.

props.name: onCreateTheme
props.description: A theme was created from New theme; the item it was opened on is tagged into it.

props.name: onArchive
props.description: An item was archived without a theme.

props.name: bucketStyle
props.description: How a theme looks: a tray with its count, a share bar coloured by its sentiment mix and a percentage; a jar whose level rises with its count; or a compact row. Chips at narrow widths keep a hint of each.

props.name: density
props.description: Card padding, quote size and gaps.

props.name: sentimentPalette
props.description: Sentiment colours: green, ink and red; cobalt, ink and amber; or ink alone, told apart by the dot, ring and diamond marks.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment ages count from, so the server and the browser print the same text.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the items have arrived: loading shows skeleton cards and themes, error a line with Try again.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the items failed to load.

props.name: title
props.description: The inbox's heading and accessible name.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the surface grows before its columns scroll, in px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be dragged, tagged, created or archived.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the inbox is one tab stop with roving focus — Up and Down move between quotes, Home and End jump. T or Enter opens a theme menu on the card (arrows move, a letter jumps to the theme it starts, Enter tags, Escape returns to the card, New theme… becomes a name field); A, Delete or Backspace archives. Focus moves to the next quote when one leaves, and to the inbox itself when the last one does.

Reduced motion: nothing lifts, leans or squeezes — a tagged card fades out of the inbox, counts update, the themes re-order at once and a failed tag fades the card back; jar levels and share bars change without travel.

Touch: the grip is the drag handle (touch-action none), so a finger anywhere else on a card still scrolls the inbox. The dragged copy lives above both columns, so it can cross from the scrolling inbox to the themes without being clipped.
Themes re-rank only once a tag has landed, so the theme a card is flying into never moves out from under it; the re-rank is announced when the leader changes.
Nothing runs while idle: a drag sets motion values only, theme bounds are read as the pointer moves, and every animation and pending timer is dropped on unmount.

items.title: Macro Reply
items.tagline: Answer the ticket and set its fields in one move.
items.description: An agent's ticket view — the conversation, a customer sidebar with plan, fields and earlier tickets, and a reply box — where # opens the macros and picking one types its reply at a steady pace while every field it changes switches at its own moment: a wash sweeps the field, the old value rolls out and the new one rises on springs.snap, a set-by-macro dot pops on springs.flick, and a chip for the change lands in the reply's footer on snap, so nothing changes unseen even when the sidebar is a tab. Sent replies rise into the conversation on springs.glide. The reply is a combobox over the macro listbox (arrows, Enter or Tab to apply, Escape to close), any key finishes a typing macro, and Ctrl+Enter sends.

props.name: sidebarSide
props.description: Which side the customer sidebar sits on; at narrow widths, which side its tab sits on.

props.name: density

props.name: accent

props.name: customer

props.name: macros

props.name: agent

props.description: The moment relative times count from, ms. Never read from the clock.

props.name: status
props.description: Loading draws skeletons in the same boxes.

props.description: The reply was sent with its fields. A promise holds Send; a rejection keeps the draft and offers Retry.

props.description: The reply box's placeholder.

props.name: disabled

props.name: className

props.name: ref
props.description: applyMacro(id) applies a macro as if picked; focusReply() moves focus to the reply.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the reply textarea is a combobox over the macro listbox — # (or the Macros button) opens it, typing filters, Up and Down move, Enter or Tab applies, Escape closes. While a macro types the reply is read-only and busy, and any key finishes it at once. Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter sends.

Each macro is announced once as a sentence when it lands ("Refund duplicate charge applied: status Pending, priority Low, tag refund added."); status and priority are native selects under a drawn face, so they keep every platform's own keyboard and picker.
Below a 36rem container the sidebar becomes a tab with a badge counting unsent macro changes, and the change chips stay in the reply footer, so a narrow agent still sees everything a macro set.
Typing is one linear tween that writes the draft only when the character count changes; nothing runs at rest, and timers stop on unmount or when the ticket id changes.
Reduced motion: the macro text arrives in one step and the fields swap under a fading wash with no roll or sweep; every change is still shown and announced.
Accent colours derive from the theme tokens (accent, success, warn, ink), so all four read in light and dark.

items.title: Request Tracker
items.tagline: Where your request is, and whose turn it is.
items.description: A customer's own page for a support request: whose turn it is in words, a bead riding the stages from received to solved, the updates as headed articles and a reply box. A stage change glides the bead on springs.glide with the rail's fill on the same motion value, and the stage it reaches fills with a check drawn on springs.flick; while the request waits on you the bead breathes and the reply box's measured height opens on glide. Replying (Ctrl+Enter) lands your update at the top on glide and passes the turn back with an honest next-reply time, and a solved request asks for a rating in a radiogroup driven by the arrow keys.

props.name: density

props.name: accent

props.name: request

props.name: now

props.name: status

props.name: onReply

props.name: onClose

props.name: onReopen

props.name: onRate

props.name: onRetry

props.name: company

props.name: customer

props.name: pulse
props.description: Let the bead breathe while the request waits on you.

props.name: height

props.name: disabled

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the reply textarea follows the turn card in the tab order and is labelled by the question it answers; Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter sends, and when the box folds away focus moves to Add more detail. The rating is a radiogroup (arrows, Home, End), and the updates list is a focusable region so it scrolls from the keyboard.
The stages are one ordered list with aria-current="step" and a completed, current or to do word per stage; the bead, line and dots are decoration. Turn changes are announced once as a sentence.
The bead's breathing is the only loop and runs only while the request waits on the customer, the page is in view, the tab is visible, motion is allowed and pulse is on.

Below a 40rem container it is one column with the reply box at the foot; above it, the turn card, reply box and request details move to a side column. Under 19rem the rail names only the current stage.
Reduced motion: the bead and fill move in one step, the ring holds still at half strength and the reply box opens without travel; stage, turn and rating still change.

items.title: Before You Send
items.tagline: Answers appear while you're still writing in.
items.description: A contact form that searches the help articles as the subject is typed and slides the matches up between the subject and the rest of the form: the panel's measured height opens on springs.glide, each answer rises 8px in cascade order and its relevance bar grows on glide a beat later, and a changing query re-ranks them in place on glide. Choosing one opens it in the panel, and This solved it folds the form down to a thank-you on glide — a ring landing on springs.recoil, a check drawn on springs.flick — instead of a ticket. The subject is a combobox: Down and Up walk the answers, Enter opens one, Escape hides them, and a failed search never blocks Send.

props.name: resultStyle
props.description: How the answers are drawn: a row of cards, hairline rows with a meter and percentage, or rows whose relevance is a wash behind the title.

props.name: density
props.description: Control heights, type and gaps.

props.name: accent

props.name: topics

props.description: The draft (topic, subject, details, email), controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from every edit with the whole draft.

props.name: onSearch
props.description: A settled search. Return matches to replace the built-in scoring; a rejection shows a quiet note and never blocks Send.

props.name: onSolved
props.description: This solved it was chosen: the form closes with a thank-you and nothing is sent.

props.name: onSend

props.name: onOpenArticle
props.description: Full article was pressed in a preview.

props.name: company

props.name: responseTime

props.name: maxResults

props.name: searchDelay

props.name: height

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be typed, chosen or sent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the subject is a combobox over the answers' listbox — Down and Up move (Down also brings back answers hidden with Escape), Home and End jump, Enter opens the active answer instead of submitting, Escape hides them. A preview's heading takes focus; Escape or Back to answers returns to the subject.

Each settled search is announced once, and only when what it found changed (a count, nothing, or an outage). Field errors use aria-invalid and aria-describedby, and the first invalid field takes focus on Send.

The built-in ranking (also exported as scoreArticles) is deterministic, so server and browser agree; pass onSearch to rank on your own index. Stale answers are dropped by a sequence number, and a failing search only ever adds a quiet line.
Below a 30rem container every result style collapses to titles with a thin bar; above 36rem the cards sit three across.
Reduced motion: the panel opens at its height, answers and bars appear in place at their widths, and the thank-you cross-fades with its check already drawn.

items.title: Callback Queue
items.tagline: Wait your turn, or ask us to call you back.
items.description: A live support queue with your place, an honest wait (a likely figure and a range from the line, the average chat and the agents on shift) and the agents on shift. When the queue moves, the person at the front goes into the desk on the exit ease, everyone behind glides one place forward on springs.glide, and your place and the estimate roll down digit by digit, the estimate a beat later. Call me back opens a picker — a number and a radiogroup of times — and booking turns your token into a time chip in its place, one element whose layout glides from circle to pill; your turn, leaving, closed hours and a full queue each say what happens next.

props.name: tokenStyle
props.description: How the line is drawn: circles to the desk, numbered ticket stubs, or a lane you ride along.

props.name: density
props.description: Token size, type and gaps.

props.name: accent
props.description: Your token, the estimate and the primary button.

props.name: queue

props.name: agents

props.name: now
props.description: The moment times count from, ms. Never read from the clock.

props.name: status

props.name: hours

props.name: callbackSlots
props.defaultValue: the next three half hours, or tomorrow morning when closed
props.description: The times offered for a callback; at null means as soon as an agent is free.

props.name: defaultPhone
props.description: The number a callback goes to until it's changed.

props.name: company

props.name: onRequestCallback

props.name: onCancelCallback

props.name: onLeave

props.name: onRejoin

props.name: onJoinChat
props.description: Join chat was pressed when it was your turn.

props.name: maxTokens
props.description: The most people drawn ahead of you; the rest fold into a count.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be booked, left or joined.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: every action is a button. Call me back opens a form whose number field takes focus; the times are a radiogroup (arrows, Home, End), Enter books, and Escape cancels back to Call me back. After booking, leaving or rejoining, focus moves to the new state's heading or button once it arrives.

The line itself is decoration; one sentence carries it for assistive technology ("You're 4th in line, 3 people ahead. About 6 minutes, usually 4 to 8."), and each move is announced politely once, computed from the new place.
The component runs no loop of its own: everything moves on a prop change or a press. Drive queue.position from your server, and pause your own polling while the page is hidden.
The estimate is a figure and a range, never a promise: position × average chat ÷ agents on shift, widened to 0.8–1.3× and rounded to whole minutes.
Reduced motion: tokens re-place without travel, digits cross-fade, and the token-to-chip swap is a cross-fade; position, estimate and states still update and are announced.

items.title: Cobrowse Consent
items.tagline: Let support see your screen, and nothing private.
items.description: A screen-sharing request on the customer's own page: a card names the agent, says what they will and won't see, lists the private fields and counts down to expiry, with Allow viewing and Not now. Allowing plays three beats — the card becomes a slim bar at the top through a shared layout on springs.glide, a coloured frame draws round the page edge by edge on the move ease, and a stripe sweeps across every private field in cascade order leaving its mask behind — while the agent's pointer, when the host passes one, glides on springs.drift. Stop sharing or Escape anywhere inside lifts the masks, fades the frame on the exit ease and leaves a receipt; an unanswered request expires and explains why.

props.name: frameColor

props.name: maskStyle

props.name: density
props.description: Field rows, type and gaps.

props.name: agent

props.name: fields

props.name: maskedFields

props.name: product

props.name: onStateChange

props.name: onDecline

props.name: height

usageNotes: Keyboard: the request is a non-modal dialog whose choices are labelled buttons. Allowing moves focus to Stop sharing once it arrives (only if focus was in the page), and Escape anywhere inside stops sharing and is consumed there; the receipt's heading then takes focus.

Private fields stay readable to the customer's assistive technology, with "hidden from Ines while sharing" added to their description; the frame, stripes, masks and pointer are decoration and aria-hidden. Every state change is announced once.

The countdown ticks once a second only while a request waits and the tab is visible, the shared time only while sharing, and the live dot breathes only while sharing, on screen and in a visible tab. Nothing else runs at rest.
The masks show the customer what the agent sees; masking the agent's own view is your session service's job — pass it the same maskedFields ids.
Below a 36rem container the frame thins from 4px to 2px, fields drop to one column and the bar spans the top; under 24rem the request card stacks its buttons.
Reduced motion: the frame and the masks fade in place, the card swaps for the bar with a cross-fade, the pointer jumps and the live dot holds still; every private field is still covered.

items.title: Overage Forecast
items.tagline: Where usage will land by the end of the month.
items.description: A metered-usage panel where each meter is a small chart: history up to today, the plan's allowance as a hairline, and a forecast cone fanning from today's reading to the period's end, its share above the allowance drawn in warn. When a meter is first seen the history draws across and the cone grows out of today on springs.glide, a beat apart per meter, and turning on planned load springs every cone's ends to their new values on the same spring so each fan widens and lifts while the overage and the projected bill roll to their new figures. Each chart is a slider over the period's days: hover, a tap or the arrow keys move a cursor on springs.flick whose reading is the value text, Page keys move a week, Home and End reach the ends and Escape returns to today.

usageNotes: Each chart is a role="slider" over the period's days: Left and Right move a day, Page Up and Page Down a week, Home and End reach the ends, and Escape returns to today; its value text reads use so far or the likely range ahead, and a sentence summary is attached with aria-describedby.
Nothing loops: every movement is a motion animation that stops when it settles, geometry is derived from motion values rather than React state, and the entrance waits until a meter is in view.
Under reduced motion the history and cone are in place at once; planned load swaps the cone's ends on a short tween and figures cross-fade, because the widening is information.
Forecast fills are pigment (the accent's hue at a fixed lightness) and overage is always warn, so the cone reads the same in light and dark and never depends on the accent.
The y scale covers both forecasts, so the planned-load switch moves the cone without re-scaling the history beneath it; pass history for each elapsed day to draw the real curve.

items.title: Seat Planner
items.tagline: Add or remove seats and see the prorated cost.
items.description: A seat management panel where every seat is a chair in a row: seated members sit on theirs as initials on a disc, empty paid seats are outlines and seats added in the draft are dashed accent chairs until confirmed. Adding a seat sets a new chair into the row from 16px above, landing on springs.recoil while its shadow spreads, a cascade apart when several arrive at once, and today's prorated charge rolls up; removing one lifts the chair away on the exit ease and opens the credit on springs.glide. Waiting members drag 1:1 onto an empty chair or seat through a menu; the chairs are one roving group (Left, Right, Home, End, Enter opens a chair's menu) and the count is a spinbutton driven by the arrow and Page keys that never falls below the seats in use.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the chairs are a roving group (Left, Right, Home, End; Enter or Space opens the chair's menu), menus take the arrow keys and Escape returns focus to their trigger, and the seat count is a role="spinbutton" (arrows, Page keys, Home for the seats in use, End for the ceiling).
Every drag has a keyboard twin: a waiting member's chip opens a menu of empty chairs (and Add a seat), and an empty chair's menu lists who is waiting.
The count never falls below the seats in use: asking for less leaves it alone, says why in words and flashes the occupied chairs once.
Under reduced motion chairs and discs fade in and out in place; the drag still follows the pointer, and the chip returns home without travel.
Proration counts the calendar days left in the period from now, so the charge and the credit match what an invoice would show; a rejected confirm keeps the whole draft.

items.title: Invoice Drilldown
items.tagline: Open a line item and see what made it.
items.description: An invoice viewer with the list of invoices on one side and the chosen one in full on the other, where a metered line opens to show the usage records that made it. Opening a line grows its region to the measured height on springs.glide while the parts slide down from 8px a cascade apart and a guide rule grows down from the line; the sum lands last, saying it matches the line or what it differs by, and the line's own figure takes one accent wash so every total traces to its parts. The invoice list is a listbox (arrows, Home, End) whose selection slides on springs.snap, each line is a native disclosure button (Enter or Space toggles, Up and Down walk, Right opens, Left closes), and a paid invoice's tick draws on springs.flick.

props.name: invoices

props.name: lineItems
props.description: Every line of every invoice: { id, invoiceId, label, detail?, amount, records? }.

props.description: Fires from the press or key that chose an invoice.

props.name: expanded / defaultExpanded

props.description: Fires with every open line id after a line opens or closes.

props.name: onDispute

props.name: disabled

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: the invoice list is a listbox (arrows, Home, End) with selection following focus; each line with records is a native button with aria-expanded and aria-controls (Enter or Space toggles, Up and Down walk the lines, Right opens, Left closes).
Status is a word with a glyph — Paid, Due, Overdue, Void — never colour alone; void amounts are struck and overdue invoices say by how many days.
The sum under each opened line is checked against the line itself, so a record set that does not add up says what it differs by instead of claiming a match.
Under reduced motion regions open in place with a fade and the parts appear together; the trace's wash still shows as colour.
At phone widths the invoice list becomes a horizontal strip and the lines become cards, by container query, so the server markup is the same at every width.

items.title: Change Preview
items.tagline: Before you switch plans, see when and what you pay.
items.description: A plan-change preview with the plans as a radio group and the billing period drawn as a timeline beneath: the days used, and from the change date the credit for the unused plan and the charge for the new one. Choosing a plan slides the marker to the change date on springs.snap, then the credit and charge segments grow from it toward the period's end on springs.glide, the credit a beat ahead, while the amount due today rolls to its new figure; a cheaper plan that waits for the period's end gets a dashed marker there. Every position is a CSS variable written by a motion value, so the same values drive the horizontal timeline and the vertical one at phone widths; the radios take the arrow keys, Home and End.

props.name: currentPlan
props.description: The plan the account is on now.

props.name: plans
props.description: The plans on offer, cheapest first: { id, name, price, blurb? }.

props.name: period
props.description: The current billing period: { start, end }.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment the preview is made, in ms.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The chosen plan id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onPreview
props.description: Fires from the press or key that chose a plan; a returned promise shows Calculating…, its figures replace the computed ones and a rejection is stated.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Confirm was pressed with the quote; a returned promise holds the button.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Keep was pressed: the choice goes back to the current plan.

props.name: errors
props.description: Parts the host could not calculate, each with its reason; Confirm waits until they are known.

props.name: taxRate
props.description: Tax on what is due today, as a fraction.

props.name: downgradeAt
props.description: When a cheaper plan starts.

props.name: account

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the plans have arrived.

props.name: onRetry

props.name: timelineStyle
props.description: How the billing period is drawn: thick lanes, hairline rails, or one cell per day.

props.name: density
props.description: Padding, gaps and the plan cards' height.

props.name: accent

props.name: formatMoney

props.name: disabled

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the panel; it caps at 36rem tall and scrolls inside past that.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the plans are a role="radiogroup" with a roving tabindex (arrows move and choose, Home and End jump); Confirm and Keep are buttons, and Confirm stays focusable while it waits (aria-disabled, aria-busy).
The timeline is a figure whose caption states the whole change in one sentence; the drawn lanes are decorative, and due today is announced once per choice.

quoteChangePreview is exported, so a host can show the same figures elsewhere or check its own; pass errors to name a part that could not be calculated and it is drawn as an ink hatch and listed in words.
Under reduced motion the marker and segments are in place at once and figures cross-fade; the dashed or solid marker and every amount still change.
No frame loop: three motion values write CSS variables, and the vertical timeline at phone widths is chosen by container query alone, so server and client markup match at every width.

items.title: Failed Charge
items.tagline: The payment didn't go through; fix it right here.
items.description: An in-app banner for a payment that didn't go through, fixable in place: Retry tries the charge again and Update card opens a short form of saved methods or a new card that saves and retries in one go. While a retry is pending a tinted sweep fills across the banner on a long decelerating tween; when the charge lands it completes on springs.glide, the band turns from muted red to green, the check draws on springs.flick and the banner folds itself away on glide, while a refusal drains the sweep on the exit ease and simply states the reason. The message is a polite live region, the form is a radiogroup of methods (arrows) with labelled inputs, Enter submits and Escape closes it back to Update card.

props.name: invoice
props.description: The invoice that failed: { id, number, amount, label }.

props.name: method
props.description: The method the charge was tried on: { id, label, kind }; the label reads mid-sentence.

props.name: methods
props.description: Other saved methods to choose from in the update.

props.name: graceDays
props.description: Days the account stays active after the first failure.

props.name: failedAt
props.description: When the charge first failed, in ms.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment grace is counted at, in ms.

props.name: reason
props.description: Why the first attempt failed.

props.name: attempts / defaultAttempts
props.description: Failed attempts so far, controlled or initial; two or more shows the grace days.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed (or a new method was saved); resolve when paid, reject with the reason.

props.name: onUpdateMethod
props.description: The update form was submitted with a saved method or a new card's fields; resolve with the method to retry on.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the banner is showing, controlled or initial.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: The banner folded away: dismissed by the reader, or paid.

props.name: expanded / defaultExpanded
props.description: Whether the update form is open, controlled or initial.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Fires from Update card, Cancel or Escape with the new state.

props.name: foldDelay
props.description: How long Payment received stays before the banner folds, in ms.

props.name: bandStyle
props.description: Where the colour sits: a leading band, the whole banner, or the border.

props.name: cornerRadius
props.description: Corner radius in px.

props.name: tone
props.description: How loud the colour is.

props.name: account
props.description: The product that stays active through the grace days.

props.name: formatMoney
props.description: How money is written.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the region that holds the banner.

usageNotes: The message is aria-live="polite" and atomic, so retrying, received and declined are each spoken once; Retry stays focusable while busy (aria-disabled, aria-busy), and focus inside a folding banner is parked on its region rather than dropped to the page.

The form is keyboard complete: a radiogroup of methods (arrows, Home, End), labelled inputs with inline errors tied by aria-describedby, Enter submits, and Escape closes it and returns focus to Update card.
A new card's fields are handed to onUpdateMethod as typed; pass them straight to your payment provider and never store them.
The band's colour is one hue variable, so the turn from red to green is a plain colour transition everywhere at once; fills are pigment and read the same in light and dark.
Under reduced motion the sweep is a still, faint fill, the colour still turns, the check appears without drawing and the fold is a fade. The only timer is the fold delay, cleared on unmount.

items.title: Spend Guard
items.tagline: Set limits, and who hears when you're near them.
items.description: A budget-alerts panel for a project's cloud spend this month: one bar carries the spend as a fill, the forecast to month end as a hatch, a hairline at the budget and a marker per alert threshold with its recipients' avatars riding on its head, while a month strip below pins each threshold to the day it fired or will fire at the current pace, joined by a leader. Dragging a marker follows the pointer 1:1 and rubber-bands past the axis, the avatars follow on springs.snap and the date pin trails on springs.glide, and release snaps to a whole percent on snap with the throw's velocity; crossing what is already spent flips the head on springs.flick. Every marker is a slider (arrows one percent, Shift five, Page keys ten, Home and End), the recipients menu is a real menu, and an optional hard limit says plainly what stops.

props.name: markerStyle
props.description: How a threshold marker is drawn: a round head carrying the avatars, a flag off the stem, or a hairline tick.

props.name: barHeight
props.description: Thickness of the spend bar in px; markers and the month strip scale with it.

props.name: palette
props.description: Tone of the spend fill, forecast hatch and markers; the hard limit keeps its danger tone.

props.name: budget
props.description: The monthly budget, in the currency format prints.

props.name: thresholds / defaultThresholds
props.description: The alert thresholds, controlled or initial: { id, percent (of budget), recipients (ids) }.

props.name: onThresholdChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, key, add, remove or recipient change that changed the thresholds, with all of them and the id that changed.

props.name: recipients
props.description: Everyone who can be alerted: { id, name, role?, hue? }.

props.name: onRecipientsChange
props.description: A threshold's recipients changed, with the new ids.

props.name: hardLimit / defaultHardLimit
props.description: The amount at which spending stops, controlled or initial; null for none.

props.name: onHardLimitChange

props.name: hardLimitEffect
props.defaultValue: "New deployments pause and preview environments scale to zero. Production keeps serving, and nothing is deleted."

props.name: daily
props.description: Spend per day of the current month so far, day 1 first; the pace is the mean of the last seven.

props.name: now
props.description: The current time in ms. Dates are read in UTC; never read from the clock.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount.

props.name: onSave
props.description: Save was pressed with { thresholds, hardLimit }; return a promise to show Saving… and its outcome.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the spend data has arrived. The bar and its markers stay in every state.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the spend failed to load.

props.name: project
props.description: The project, in the heading.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; its body scrolls inside.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be moved, added or saved.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Each marker is a role="slider" whose value text is a full sentence (percent, amount, the date it fires and who hears it): arrows move it one percent, Shift five, Page Up and Page Down ten, Home and End to the axis ends. The recipients button opens a real menu of menuitemcheckbox rows; Escape closes it and returns focus.
Under reduced motion markers, avatars and date pins move instantly and the hard-limit body opens without travel; the passed state, the inspector and every date still update.
Dates are computed in UTC from the now prop and the daily series, so server and client agree; the pace is the mean of the last seven days.
Nothing runs at rest: positions are motion values that settle, the leader paths are rebuilt only while a marker or pin moves, and the only observer is a ResizeObserver on the hard-limit body.
Colours come from tokens: the palette sets --sg-fill (a pigment at fixed lightness, so a filled bar reads the same in both themes) and --sg-ink; the hard limit always uses the danger tone.
Below a 32rem container the heads drop their unit and the riding avatars become dots, so markers a few percent apart still sit side by side on a phone.

items.title: Tax Profile
items.tagline: Company details for invoices, checked as you type.
items.description: A billing-details form with a live invoice header beside it: every field a labelled native input in reading order with its error inline, the preview re-typesetting as you type and lighting the line of the field you are in. A well-formed tax ID runs a checking pulse along the field's lower edge while it is looked up; a registered number fills the legal name, which lifts out of the note under the field and glides into the invoice header on springs.glide, landing with a springs.flick settle and a wash of the accent while the Verified badge pops on springs.snap. Not-found numbers and an unanswering registry keep the entry with a note, a failed check digit is an inline error, and on a narrow container the preview folds away behind a toggle.

props.name: fieldStyle

props.name: previewStyle
props.description: The invoice header preview: seller left and title right, a large title with two blocks, or one tight strip.

props.name: accent
props.description: Any CSS colour: focus edges, the checking pulse, the landing wash and the invoice rule.

props.name: company
props.description: The legal company name the form starts with.

props.name: address

props.name: taxId

props.name: email
props.description: The billing email the form starts with.

props.name: reference

props.name: values

props.name: onValuesChange

props.name: seller

props.name: invoiceNumber
props.description: The invoice number in the preview.

props.name: now

props.name: lookup

props.name: checkDelay
props.description: How long the default lookup takes, in ms.

props.name: onValidate
props.description: Fires with every check outcome: valid (with the registered name), not-found, unreachable or invalid.

props.name: onSave

props.name: onCancel

props.name: status

props.name: onRetry

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; its body scrolls inside.

props.name: disabled

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: A real form in normal tab order: every input is labelled, errors are inline with aria-invalid and aria-describedby, the tax ID group is aria-busy while checking, and Save (a submit button associated with the form) focuses the first invalid field and announces how many need attention.

Lookups are debounced (450 ms after the ninth digit), keyed by the number and cancelled when it changes, so a stale answer never lands; pass lookup to call your own registry and read every outcome from onValidate.
Under reduced motion the pulse is a still tint with a spinner glyph, there is no flight, and the registered name cross-fades into the header; the Verified badge and every note still appear.
The preview is a document: its paper keeps a fixed light tone and ink in both themes, while the form uses theme tokens; the accent drives the focus edge, pulse, wash and the invoice rule.
Below a 44rem container the preview folds behind a Preview invoice toggle (aria-expanded, aria-controls) and opens above the form; City and Postal code share a row from 22rem.

items.title: Team Chargeback
items.tagline: Split the bill by the teams that ran it up.
items.description: A cost-allocation view for a cloud account: the month's total is one long bar already divided into its teams, with what no rule claims hatched at its end and every billed month drawn below it. Pressing the total splits it: the segments part on springs.snap, then each slides down into its own row of a ranked list on springs.glide in one cascade while its share, trend and owner arrive beside it, and the unallocated remainder stays behind in the bar; pressing again folds the rows back up. Allocation is computed from tag rules and shared-cost splits, rows open with Enter to their spend by service and the rules that claimed it, arrow keys walk the rows and the month tabs, and a narrow container shortens each bar to its percentage.

props.name: barStyle
props.description: How team bars are drawn: pigment fills, a tint with a lead edge, or outlines that fill on hover and focus.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height and bar thickness; roomy rows also show the owner's role.

props.name: palette
props.description: Team colours as pigments at fixed lightness: cool blues and teals, warm, spread hues, or ink steps.

props.name: costs
props.description: Costs per month id: { id, label (resource), service, amount, previous, tags }.

props.name: months
props.description: The months as tabs, oldest first: { id, label, long }.

props.name: month / defaultMonth
props.description: The month shown, controlled or initial.

props.name: onMonthChange
props.description: A month tab was chosen.

props.name: teams
props.description: The teams costs are charged back to: { id, name, owner, role? }.

props.name: rules / defaultRules
props.description: Allocation rules, controlled or initial: tag rules { kind: "tag", key, value, team, enabled } (key "resource" matches a cost's label) and split rules { kind: "split", key, value, method: "usage" | "even", enabled } for shared costs.

props.name: onRuleChange

props.name: onAllocate

props.name: onExport
props.description: Export was pressed: the month's allocation as CSV text and as rows.

props.name: split / defaultSplit
props.description: Whether the total bar is split into team rows, controlled or initial. A host that flips it gets the same choreography as a press.

props.name: onSplitChange
props.description: The total bar was pressed.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every amount.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the costs have arrived; a month without costs says so on its own.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the costs failed to load.

props.name: account
props.description: The account, in the heading.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the surface in px; its body scrolls inside.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be split, switched or assigned.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: The total bar is a button with aria-expanded and a sentence describing the split; rows are buttons with aria-expanded under roving focus (Up and Down, Home and End), rule switches are role="switch", the shared-cost method is a radiogroup, and the months are a tablist driven by the arrow keys.
While rows are being edited the ranking holds still, so a rule change or an assignment never pulls the row you are in out from under the focus; the next split ranks the teams again.
Under reduced motion the split is a cross-fade: no segment travels, rows appear in place and open without a height glide; every amount, share and trend still updates.
Shared layout moves run only on split and fold (each segment's layoutDependency is the phase and its amount), so expanding rows never sets off stray slides; nothing runs at rest.

Team colours are pigments at fixed lightness so the bars read the same in both themes; trends use the warn tone above +10% and the success tone for a fall, always with the sign and percentage in text.

items.title: Visitor Chat
items.tagline: Talk to the team from the corner of the page.
items.description: A website chat widget that lives in the corner of its own box, with the host page behind it. Pressing the launcher stretches it into the window on a goo layer used only while the shape moves: the window grows out of the launcher, rising on springs.snap and widening on springs.glide while its fill turns from the accent to the card and the neck between them thins until it lets go, then the crisp window takes over and its content arrives; closing runs back into the launcher on the exit ease. Inside, the header says who is on and how soon they reply, the messages are a log where an agent's reply resolves out of the typing bubble on springs.glide, the composer is a real textarea with attach and send, a failed send keeps a retry on its bubble, outside office hours the window asks for an email first, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the launcher.

props.name: launcherShape

props.name: bubbleStyle
props.description: Message bubbles: a soft tint, a solid accent for the visitor, or agents as plain text.

props.name: accent
props.description: Any CSS colour: the launcher, the visitor's bubbles, read marks and focus edges.

props.name: team
props.description: Who answers: { id, name, role?, online, hue? }.

props.name: hours
