props.name: messages / defaultMessages
props.description: The thread, controlled or initial: { id, from ("visitor" or an agent id), text, at, status?, attachment? }.

props.name: onMessagesChange
props.description: Fires from a send, a delivery change or a retry, with every message.

props.name: typing

props.name: onSend
props.type: (message: ChatMessage, meta: { email: string | null }) => void | Promise<void>

props.description: Files were picked with the attach button; the first rides on the next message.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the window is open, controlled or initial. A host that opens it gets the same stretch, without moving focus.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: The launcher, Escape or the minimise button changed the open state.

props.name: onClose
props.description: The window was closed by the visitor.

props.name: now
props.description: The current time in ms; decides office hours. Never read from the clock.

props.name: replyMinutes
props.description: How soon the team usually replies, in minutes, shown in the header.

props.name: title
props.description: The window's title and the dialog's name.

props.name: greeting
props.defaultValue: "Hi, we're the Waylight team. Ask us anything about your workspace, billing or the API."
props.description: The team's first message, always shown at the top.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the box the widget lives in, in px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be opened or sent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer box.

props.name: children
props.description: The page behind the widget.

usageNotes: The launcher is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; the window is a non-modal role="dialog" labelled by its title, opened by the visitor it moves focus into the composer, and Escape anywhere inside closes it and returns focus to the launcher.

Messages live in a role="log" (polite) holding a list; every bubble carries its author and time for assistive technology, and the visitor's carry their delivery (Sending, Sent, Seen, Not sent) as words, not colour. The typing bubble announces itself once.

The goo is an SVG blur-and-threshold filter over two plain shapes that exists only during the half second of stretching; at rest the window is plain DOM and nothing animates except the typing dots while someone types.
Under reduced motion there is no goo and no stretch: the window cross-fades in place, the typing dots hold still at three tones, and replies fade in.
Agent replies are the host's: pass typing while an agent types, then add their message in the same update that clears typing so it grows out of the indicator.
Office hours are computed from hours and now in the team's offset; outside them the window asks for an email before the first send and passes it to onSend.

items.title: Swipe Reply
items.tagline: Swipe a message to answer it.
items.description: A direct-message thread on a phone-width screen with day dividers, delivery ticks, reactions and a composer. Swiping a bubble toward the middle pulls it 1:1 for swipeDistance px and rubber-bands past it while a ring in the gap it uncovers fills with the pull and, full, arms with a springs.flick pop; letting go always snaps the bubble home on springs.snap with the release velocity, and an armed pull docks the quoted message above the composer on springs.glide with its accent edge drawing down. Keyboard users walk the messages with the arrow keys, press R to reply and the menu key (or Shift+F10) to open reactions, which land under the bubble on springs.recoil; older messages load at the top behind a spinner without moving what you were reading, and a failed message offers retry.

props.name: swipeDistance
props.description: How far a pull travels before the reply arms, in px; past it the bubble rubber-bands.

props.name: bubbleStyle
props.description: Bubble shape: a small tail on the last of a run, full pills, or squarer blocks.

props.name: accent
props.description: Any CSS colour: your bubbles, the reply ring, the dock's edge and focus edges.

props.name: messages / defaultMessages
props.description: The thread, oldest first, controlled or initial: { id, from, text, at, status?, replyTo?, reactions? }.

props.name: onMessagesChange
props.description: Fires from a send, a reaction, a retry or older messages arriving, with every message.

props.name: participants
props.description: Everyone in the thread: { id, name, hue?, presence? }.

props.name: me
props.description: Which participant is you; your bubbles sit right and swipe left.

props.name: onSend
props.description: A message was sent. Return a promise: resolved marks it sent, rejected marks it failed with a retry.

props.name: onReply
props.description: A message was picked to reply to, by swipe, R or the hover bar.

props.name: onReact
props.type: (message: SwipeMessage, reaction: SwipeReaction, on: boolean) => void
props.description: You added or removed a reaction (like, love, laugh, wow, sad, done).

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed on a failed message; it is sent again through onSend.

props.name: onLoadEarlier
props.description: The thread reached the top; return older messages (oldest first) or add them yourself.

props.name: hasEarlier
props.description: Whether older messages exist; shows the loader row at the top.

props.name: now
props.description: The current time in ms, for day dividers (read in UTC). Never read from the clock.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the screen in px; the thread scrolls inside.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be sent, swiped or reacted to.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer box.

usageNotes: Every gesture has a key: messages are a roving list inside a polite role="log" (Up and Down, Home and End, Up from the first loads earlier), R replies to the focused message, the menu key or Shift+F10 opens a real menu of reactions, and Escape clears the reply dock or closes the menu and returns focus.

Each message speaks as one sentence: author, time, what it answers, its text, its delivery (Sending, Sent, Delivered, Read, Not delivered) and its reactions by name; reactions are drawn icons, never emoji.

Bubbles are touch-pan-y, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the thread; the drag captures the pointer only after 6px sideways. Under reduced motion the bubble still follows the finger and the ring still fills (it is information), but it returns home at once and the dock fades in.
Older history is prepended with the scroll position restored before paint, so what you were reading stays put; the spinner animates only while a page is loading.
Nothing runs at rest: the pull, ring and pop are motion values on each bubble, and the hover bar is hidden while a bubble is being pulled.

items.title: Live Chatter
items.tagline: A fast chat that holds still while you read.
items.description: A live event chat that holds still while you read: while nothing holds it, the log's scroll chases the newest row on a spring derived from springs.glide whose stiffness scales with scrollSpeed², keeping its velocity across arrivals so a burst reads as one climb. Hovering, keyboard focus, Space or scrolling up freezes it in place while a pill rises on springs.snap counting the messages below the fold with rolling digits; choosing the pill or pressing End fast-forwards on a stiff glide under a brief vertical blur and draws the newest row's edge on springs.flick. Up and Down walk the rows, Space pauses and resumes, Tab reaches each row's Report, and slow mode, mutes and a dropped connection show in the composer and the log.

props.name: messages
props.description: The stream so far, oldest first: { id, author, text, at, badges?: ("host" | "mod" | "speaker" | "staff")[], kind?: "message" | "gap", missed?, until? }. The host appends; the chat follows.

props.name: title
props.description: The broadcast's name in the header; also names the log.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: A short line under the title, before the viewer count.

props.name: viewers
props.description: How many people are watching, grouped by hand so server and browser agree.

props.name: connection
props.description: Anything but live tears the log's tail with a "Connection lost" edge and holds sending with a reason in the composer.

props.name: paused / defaultPaused
props.description: The explicit pause (Space), controlled or initial. Hover, keyboard focus and scrolling up still hold on top of it.

props.name: onPause
props.description: The stream started or stopped holding still; reason is "hover", "focus", "key", "scroll", "pill" or "send".

props.name: onSend
props.description: A message was sent from the composer (Enter). Append it to messages to show it; the log goes live to see it land.

props.name: onReport
props.description: A message was reported through its row's confirm; it is already hidden for this viewer.

props.name: slowMode
props.description: Seconds between messages from one viewer. Shows a header chip, and after a send a ring on Send that empties over the cooldown.

props.name: muted / mutedUntil / mutedReason
props.description: Replaces the composer with a calm notice: until when (ms since the epoch) and why.

props.name: viewerName
props.description: Messages that @mention the viewer's first name get an accent wash.

props.name: now
props.description: The current moment in ms since the epoch, for the connection-lost stamp. Never read from the clock during render.

props.name: scrollSpeed
props.description: How briskly the log follows new rows: the follow spring's stiffness scales with its square (0.5 drifts, 2 ticks).

props.name: density
props.description: One tight line per row at 12px, a coloured dot before each name, or an initial avatar with the name and time over the message.

props.name: accent
props.description: Pill, Send, Host badge, mention wash and the newest-row edge — any CSS colour; fills take its hue at a fixed lightness.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: Rows kept in the DOM while live; a hold keeps up to three times as many so nothing you are reading is trimmed.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Characters a message may hold; a counter shows past 80%.

props.name: formatTime
props.description: How times are printed on rows, the mute notice and the connection stamp.

props.name: status / onRetry
props.description: Loading shows skeleton rows; error shows a message and Try again, which calls onRetry.

props.name: height
props.description: The surface's height in px; the log scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: no composer and no reporting; the log still reads and pauses.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer section.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab lands on the newest row and holds the chat; Up and Down walk rows, Page Up and Page Down ten at a time, Home the oldest kept row; Space pauses and resumes; End fast-forwards to the newest row and goes live; Tab from a row reaches its Report button, and Escape cancels a report confirm.
The log is role="log" with aria-live off — a fast chat read aloud is noise. Holds, jumps, sends and reports are announced once in a polite status, and the pill's name carries the count below.

Reduced motion: following and the fast-forward jump straight to the bottom with no blur, rows appear without travel and the pill fades; the count, the newest-row wash and the slow-mode countdown still show, because they are information.

Nothing runs at rest: the follow spring starts on an arrival and stops when it settles, and the slow-mode ticker exists only during a cooldown. Drive the stream from your socket; pause your own feed when the chat is off screen.
Mark what a dropped connection lost with a { kind: "gap", missed, at, until } item; it is drawn as a torn separator.

items.title: Channel Merge
items.tagline: Email, text and web chat in one thread.
items.description: A support conversation where one customer's email, texts and web chat sit in a single thread, each message carrying a thin stripe in its channel's hue — an inner edge, a rail through the gutter that changes colour where the conversation changed channel, or a top band. Choosing the reply channel slides its badge across the radio group on springs.snap while the composer reshapes: its measured height glides on springs.glide as the email subject unfolds or the text counter's segments roll in, the address cross-fades and the top stripe wipes into the new hue; Ctrl+Enter sends and the reply rises on glide with its stripe drawn on springs.flick. Arrows move through the channels and skip the ones the customer never used, the assignee menu answers to arrows, Enter and Escape, and under 44rem the customer sidebar hides behind a tab.

props.name: messages
props.description: The conversation across channels, oldest first: { id, channel: "email" | "sms" | "chat" | "social", from: "customer" | "agent", author, at, body, subject?, quoted?, status? }.

props.name: customer
props.description: Who the customer is and how to reach them: name, company, plan, email, phone, chat, social, online, location, utcOffset, since, tags, tickets.

props.name: agents
props.description: Who the ticket can be assigned to: { id, name, team? }.

props.name: assignee / defaultAssignee
props.description: The assigned agent's id, controlled or initial; null is unassigned.

props.name: onAssign
props.description: Fires from the menu choice that changed the assignee.

props.name: channel / defaultChannel
props.description: The reply channel, controlled or initial.

props.name: onChannelChange
props.description: Fires from the radio (click or arrow) that changed the reply channel.

props.name: onSend
props.description: A reply was sent with Ctrl+Enter or Send: { channel, to, body, subject? }. Append it to messages to show it.

props.name: subject
props.description: The ticket's subject, in the header and the email reply's "Re:" line.

props.name: ticket
props.description: The ticket's reference, under the subject.

props.name: now
props.description: The current moment in ms since the epoch, for the customer's local time. Never read from the clock during render.

props.name: channels
props.description: Which reply channels to offer, in order. Ones the customer never used are greyed and skipped.

props.name: channelColors
props.description: Override a channel's stripe colour with any CSS colour; defaults are pigment hues at a fixed lightness.

props.name: stripeStyle
props.description: How each message shows its channel: a 3px inner edge, a continuous rail with a glyph node per message, or a 2px top band.

props.name: density
props.description: Type size, message padding and the gaps between messages.

props.name: accent
props.description: Send, the agent's messages, the assignee and the tab indicator — any CSS colour; fills take its hue at a fixed lightness.

props.name: smsLimit
props.description: Characters in one text before it splits; split parts hold 7 fewer, as concatenated texts do.

props.name: status / onRetry
props.description: Loading shows skeleton messages; error shows a message and Try again, which calls onRetry.

props.name: height
props.description: The surface's height in px; the thread and the sidebar scroll inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: no composer and no assigning.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer section.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the checked channel is the radio group's one tab stop; arrows, Home and End move between channels the customer has used and skip greyed ones. Ctrl+Enter (or ⌘+Enter) sends from anywhere in the composer. The assignee button opens its menu with Enter or the arrows; Escape closes it and focus returns to the button.
Reduced motion: the badge, panels and composer height change at once, the stripe colour cross-fades instead of wiping, and replies appear without rising; counters and delivery states still update.
Greyed channels are the ones the customer has never written from (or has no address for); each says why in its accessible name and tooltip.
Channel hues are pigments at a fixed lightness, so the same stripe reads on light and dark themes; pass channelColors to brand them.
The layout follows its container, not the viewport: from 44rem the customer sits in a sidebar, below it behind a Conversation | customer tab pair whose hidden panel is inert.

items.title: Clip Thread
items.tagline: Short video messages you can skim.
items.description: An asynchronous video thread whose clips are procedural screen shares drawn in SVG from one time motion value, so hovering a strip thumbnail scrubs its frames under the pointer at frame rate and the cursor in each frame glides between what the speaker points at. While a clip plays its track fills linearly and the transcript lights up word by word: a capsule glides from word to word on springs.flick and across line breaks on springs.snap, and any word can be clicked to jump there; reactions land on springs.recoil as markers on the track, choosing a clip slides the frame in on springs.glide, and a finished clip's progress ring closes into a tick. Space plays, the arrows skip five seconds, the strip is a listbox walked with Left and Right, and the transcript's lines are walked with Up and Down.

props.name: clips
props.description: The thread, oldest first: { id, author, role?, at, duration, title?, scene?, transcript: { at, text }[], reactions?: { kind, count, mine?, marks? }[], replyTo?, processing? }.

props.name: selected / defaultSelected
props.description: The clip in the player, controlled or initial.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.description: Fires from the strip choice, or the auto-advance, that changed the clip.

props.name: playing / defaultPlaying / onPlayingChange
props.description: Playback, controlled or initial, and the callback from the press, key or end of clip that changed it.

props.name: onRecord
props.description: Record was pressed. Add the new clip with `processing` to clips; it shows a progress ring until you clear it.

props.name: onReply
props.description: "Reply with a clip" was pressed on the clip in the player.

props.name: onReact
props.description: A reaction ("agree" | "love" | "idea" | "question") was toggled at a moment of the clip, in seconds.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment relative times count from, in ms since the epoch. Never read from the clock during render.

props.name: title
props.description: The thread's heading.

props.name: skip
props.description: Seconds the arrow keys skip on the frame and the track.

props.name: autoAdvance
props.description: Play the next ready clip when one ends.

props.name: posterAt
props.description: Where in a clip its strip poster frame sits, 0 to 1; a skim eases back to it.

props.name: thumbShape
props.description: Strip thumbnails as 16:9 cards, squares, or circular video notes.

props.name: density
props.description: Strip thumbnail size, transcript type size and line height, and gaps.

props.name: accent
props.description: Word capsule, playhead, fill, reaction markers, rings and the chosen card — any CSS colour; fills take its hue at a fixed lightness.

props.name: status / onRetry
props.description: Loading shows a skeleton player and strip; error shows a message and Try again, which calls onRetry.

props.name: height
props.description: The surface's height in px; the transcript, and below 44rem the player column, scroll inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Watch only: no recording, replying or reacting.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer section.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the frame is a play/pause button whose Left and Right skip; the track is a slider (arrows ±skip, Page keys twice that, Home, End, Space plays); the strip is a horizontal listbox (Left, Right, Home, End, Enter or Space to play a clip); transcript lines are buttons walked with Up and Down, and Enter jumps to a line. Space anywhere outside a control plays.
Pointer: hovering a strip thumbnail skims its frames under the pointer; clicking any transcript word jumps to that word and plays.

Reduced motion: the word capsule does not travel — the current word is marked by colour and an underline — frames swap without sliding and reactions do not pop; playback, the fill, skimming and the processing ring still work, because they are content and progress.

Performance: the clock is one linear animation on a motion value that runs only while playing; frames, the fill and the readout read that value without rendering, and the active word is React state only when it changes.
Clips are drawn, not loaded: pass a `scene` per clip ("flow", "settings", "empty", "pricing", "mobile") and the transcript's line times drive both the words and where the cursor points.

items.title: Safety Numbers
items.tagline: Compare the numbers to trust the chat.
items.description: An end-to-end verification screen that lays both safety numbers side by side as grids of five-digit groups: pointing at or focusing a group lights its partner and draws a hairline between them, and the compare-aloud stepper walks the pairs one at a time with an outline that travels cell to cell on springs.snap. Marking the chat verified turns each matched pair over in 3D on springs.glide, both grids together and staggered in reading order by cascade(), to a calm tick, and once the last one lands a seal settles on the contact on springs.snap with one ring breathing out; a changed number shows its warning first. Each grid is a role="grid" walked with the arrows, Home, End and Ctrl+Home/End, and every group's name spells its digits so a screen reader reads them one by one.

props.name: yourCode
props.description: The safety number this device computed: digits, any spacing (60 digits make 12 groups).

props.name: theirCode
props.description: The number on the contact's device, as read or scanned. Groups that differ are struck through and verifying is held back.

props.name: contact
props.description: Who is being verified: { name, handle?, device? }.

props.name: youName
props.description: How this side is named over its grid.

props.name: verified / defaultVerified
props.description: The verified state, controlled or initial. A change plays the flip and the seal, whoever made it.

props.name: onVerify
props.description: "Mark as verified" was pressed and every group matches.

props.name: onReset
props.description: "Clear verification" was pressed; the ticks turn back in reverse order.

props.name: onScan
props.description: "Scan code" was pressed: open your camera flow, then set verified.

props.name: onCompare
props.description: A group was compared aloud: its index and "same" or "different".

props.name: changed / previousCode / onAcknowledgeChange
props.description: The contact's number changed: a warning shows first, and once acknowledged the groups that differ from previousCode carry a dot.

props.name: verifiedAt / now
props.description: When the chat was verified and the moment relative times count from, in ms since the epoch.

props.name: groupSize
props.description: Digits per group.

props.name: columns
props.description: Groups per row in each grid.

props.name: groupStyle
props.description: Groups as hairline cells, filled pill chips, or one small box per digit.

props.name: density
props.description: Digit size, cell height, grid gaps and card padding.

props.name: accent
props.description: Compare outline, connector, ticks and seal — any CSS colour; fills take its hue at a fixed lightness.

props.name: renderCode
props.defaultValue: a seeded picture of the digits
props.description: Draws your number as a scannable code in the card's QR view; pass your real encoder here.

props.name: status / onRetry
props.description: Loading shows skeleton grids; error shows a message and Try again, which calls onRetry.

props.name: height
props.description: The surface's height in px; the body scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: the numbers show and can be explored, nothing can be marked.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer section.

usageNotes: Keyboard: each grid is one tab stop; arrows move between groups, Home and End along a row, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End to the ends. Focusing a group lights its partner in the other grid. Compare aloud, Same, Different, Scan and Mark as verified are buttons.
Screen readers hear every group's digits one at a time ("Group 3: 4 0 2 1 3, verified"), and each step of a comparison or verification is announced once in a polite status.
Reduced motion: no 3D turn — ticks cross-fade onto each group in the same order — the compare outline jumps and the seal fades in place; every state still shows.
Verifying is held back while any group differs (the button stays focusable and says why). Pass changed with previousCode when a contact's key rotates; the warning comes first.
The QR view shows a seeded picture of your digits by default; pass renderCode to draw a real scannable code there.

items.title: Pendant Drop
items.tagline: A drop of colour that leans toward your hand.
items.description: A single drop of coloured liquid hangs from the top edge of its frame on surface tension over a shallow pool, drawn in one WebGL2 pass of signed distances joined by a smooth minimum whose reach is the viscosity and shaded as glass. Bring the pointer near and the drop leans and stretches toward it on a spring set by the viscosity, its neck thinning to a thread as the colour pools into the leading lobe; pull far enough and a droplet pinches off while the rest recoils home on the recoil spring's constants and refills from the film, and the droplet falls, is met by the pool and reabsorbed with a mound that rebounds on the same constants and ripples running out along the surface. The frame is a button: the arrow keys lean the drop and Down stretches it, Enter, Space or a click lets a drop fall, and Escape lets it hang straight.

props.name: viscosity
props.description: How thick the liquid is, 0 (runny: quick, wobbly) to 1 (thick: slow, composed, gooier joins).

props.name: reach
props.description: How far away the drop notices your hand, 0 (only right beside it) to 1 (across the frame).

props.name: palette
props.description: The liquid's colours, pale at the root to deep in the lobe: a preset, or two CSS colours of your own.

props.name: tension
props.description: How far the drop stretches before a droplet pinches off, 0 (lets go early) to 1 (holds on long).

props.name: size
props.description: The bulb's radius in px; it shrinks to fit a small frame.

props.name: anchor
props.description: Where along the top edge the drop hangs, 0 (left) to 1 (right).

props.name: gravity
props.description: How fast a droplet falls, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: gloss
props.description: The glassy highlights, rim light and caustic, 0 (matte) to 1.

props.name: pool
props.description: Draw the pool along the bottom edge that droplets fall into. Off, they fall out of the frame.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and touch pull the drop. Keys still lean it.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the liquid still.

props.name: label
props.description: The frame's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a plip as each droplet lands. Off unless asked for.

props.name: onDrip
props.description: Fires as each droplet lets go, with how many have fallen.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing reaches the drop and the frame's button is disabled.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the frame.

usageNotes: The whole frame is one button with a spoken hint: Left and Right lean the drop, Down stretches it until it lets go and Up eases it back, Shift leans twice as far, Enter, Space or a click drops one, and Escape lets it hang straight (it is only handled while the drop is leaning).

A mouse pulls the drop just by coming near; a finger or pen presses and drags, and the frame is touch-action none so the pull never scrolls the page. Move away faster than the drop can follow and it lets go of you instead of dripping.

One WebGL2 pass on a fullscreen triangle, drawn at three quarters of a dense screen's pixels with the device pixel ratio capped at 2. The loop runs only while something moves and only on screen with the tab visible; a resting drop is a single frame. Context loss is handled, and without WebGL2 a drawn still stays.
Under reduced motion the drop hangs still and the pointer does not pull it; Enter or a tap shows a still of the moment after a drip for 600 ms and onDrip still reports.
The canvas is transparent: put the frame on any surface. Palettes are pigment at a fixed lightness, so the liquid looks the same on light and dark pages; the shadow it casts takes the theme's ink.
The plip plays only with sound on and only after the page has had a press, since a hover alone is not a user activation.

items.title: Rain Lamp
items.tagline: Drops of light sliding down taut threads.
items.description: A retro rain lamp in a dim room: beads of glowing oil form at a brass crown and slide down a ring of taut threads around a small fern sculpture, accelerating toward a speed that grows with their size, merging with momentum kept where a faster bead catches a slower one, and landing in a shallow basin with a ring on the oil, while the ring turns slowly so threads pass behind the fern and across its front. Sweeping the pointer across the threads plucks every one it crosses: each rings as a decaying standing wave while its beads shiver and stall, then run on together, and the beads you shook loose plip as they land. The lamp is a button: Left and Right move a finger along the threads and Enter or Space plucks the one under it.

props.name: filaments
props.description: How many taut threads hang in the ring, 6 to 24.

props.name: dripRate
props.description: How often a bead forms at the crown, per thread per second, 0.1 to 1.5.

props.name: glow
props.description: The colour the oil glows: a preset, or any CSS colour.

props.name: turn
props.description: How fast the ring of threads turns, 0 (still) to 1 (a turn every twenty seconds).

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the beads slide, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: beadSize
props.description: How big the beads grow before they let go, 0.5 to 1.5.

props.name: merge
props.description: A faster bead that catches a slower one merges with it.

props.name: sculpture
props.description: Stand the fern sculpture in the middle of the ring.

props.name: pluck
props.description: How hard a pass of the pointer plucks the threads it crosses, 0 to 1.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and touch pluck the threads. Keys still do.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the oil and the ring still.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the beads' sizes, timing and the film's unevenness.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The lamp's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a plip as each bead you shook loose lands. Off unless asked for.

props.name: onPluck
props.description: Fires when a thread is plucked, by pointer, touch or key, with its index.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing reaches the threads and the lamp's button is disabled.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the lamp; it is drawn to fit the box.

usageNotes: The lamp is one button with a spoken hint: Left and Right move a finger along the threads (Shift moves further, Home and End go to the edges), a dotted line shows where it is, and Enter or Space plucks the thread under it. A click or tap plucks the thread nearest it.
A mouse plucks by sweeping across the threads, harder the faster it moves; touch is pan-y, so a horizontal swipe plucks and a vertical one scrolls the page.

Canvas 2D: the room, crown, basin and fern are painted once per size and colour and stamped each frame, beads are two sprite stamps each, and every bead and ripple lives in preallocated arrays. The loop runs only on screen, with the tab visible and not paused. The device pixel ratio is capped at 2.
Under reduced motion the lamp is a still lit frame with beads held on the threads; a pluck lights its thread for 600 ms instead of shaking it, and onPluck still fires.
The lamp is an object in its own dim room, so it looks the same on light and dark pages; glow tints the beads, the threads, the oil and the room, and the brass takes the warn token's hue.
The plip plays only with sound on, only for beads a pluck shook loose, and only after the page has had a press.

items.title: Redshift Jump
items.tagline: The sky crowds ahead and reddens behind as you jump.
items.description: A window onto a starfield drawn with real relativistic optics: press and hold, or hold Space or Enter, and the drive's rapidity climbs at constant thrust, so the stars bunch toward the direction of travel by aberration and shift blue, the rim thins and reddens, each star streaks by how fast it crosses the sky, and near top speed the visible sky collapses onto one bright ring where the Doppler factor is one. Let go at the peak and the ring flashes outward to white while the sky is reseeded for the next destination and the speed falls away on a critically damped curve with the glide spring's natural frequency, the new stars streaming back to their places as the destination's card rises on springs.glide; let go early and the drive spins down, and Escape aborts. A click from assistive technology flies the whole jump on autopilot.

props.name: velocity
props.description: Top speed as a fraction of light's, 0.9 to 0.999: the higher, the tighter the ring.

props.name: shift
props.description: How strongly the Doppler shift colours and dims the stars, 0 (aberration only) to 2 (vivid).

props.name: density
props.description: How many stars fill the sky, 0.2 to 1.

props.name: destinations
props.description: Where the drive can take you, in order; the last jump wraps to the first.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The destination, as an index into destinations; controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the jump that arrived somewhere, with the new index.

props.name: onPhaseChange
props.description: Fires as the drive moves between idle, charging, at the peak and jumping.

props.name: charge
props.description: How long a held press takes to reach top speed, ms, 600 to 4000.

props.name: streaks
props.description: How long the stars streak while the speed changes, 0 (points) to 1 (long trails).

props.name: aim
props.description: How far the heading leans toward the pointer while idle, 0 to 1.

props.name: card
props.description: Show the destination's name card over the window's lower edge.

props.name: label
props.description: The window's accessible name; the destination is added to it.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play rising tones as the drive charges and jumps. Off unless asked for.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the drive: presses do nothing.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds every destination's sky.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The window's button is disabled.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the window.

usageNotes: The window is one button named with where you are ("Jump drive, at Waylight Reach"): hold Space or Enter to build speed and let go at the peak to jump, Escape aborts a charge, and a click from assistive technology flies the whole jump on autopilot. Arrivals are announced once, politely.
A press and hold works with mouse, pen and touch; the window is touch-action pan-y with the long-press menu suppressed, so a held finger charges and a vertical swipe still scrolls the page.

Stars are instanced quads, up to 4,000 in one draw over a sky pass, and each destination's stars are generated once from its seed. The loop runs only while the drive charges, jumps or the aim eases, only on screen with the tab visible; idle it is one frame. Context loss is handled and the device pixel ratio is capped at 2.

Under reduced motion, and without WebGL2, the window is a static star chart with rings every 15 degrees: holding fills a progress ring round the crosshair, a full ring and a release jump to the next destination's chart with an opacity cross-fade, and onPhaseChange and onValueChange report the same way.
The sky is fixed art, deep space on light and dark pages alike; the name card is drawn on a dark glass plate so it reads over the stars.
The rising tones play only with sound on, and only from the press, key or click that drives the jump.

items.title: Bistable Sea
items.tagline: A rolling swell on a one-bit paper display.
items.description: A slim e-paper display showing an open-sea swell under a low sun, rendered at e-paper resolution as a real perspective ocean (four wave trains, sky Fresnel, a sun-glitter path, foam on steep crests, cloud bands) and error-diffused to pure ink and paper. It refreshes like e-paper rather than video: each step of the sea rolls down the panel in bands, changed pixels flipping through their inverse before they land and keeping a faint ghost of what they were, and every few partials a full refresh flashes inverse, blanks and lands clean. The pointer tilts the device toward it on the glide spring with a sheen across the glass, a horizontal drag turns the bearing 1:1, and the device is a slider whose arrow, Page and Home keys turn the sea, each turn kicking it into a small tilt that settles on glide.

props.name: refresh
props.description: Partial refreshes a second, 0.25 to 3: how often the sea steps on.

props.name: ghosting
props.description: How much of each old frame a refresh leaves behind, 0 (clean) to 1 (heavy ghosts).

props.name: swell
props.description: How big the swell runs, 0 (glassy) to 1 (heavy).

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The bearing the display faces, in degrees (0 north, 90 east); controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drag or key that turned the display, with the new bearing.

props.name: onRefresh
props.description: Fires as each refresh lands on the panel.

props.name: fullEvery
props.description: Partial refreshes between full ones, which flash and clear every ghost; 0 never.

props.name: bands
props.description: How many bands a partial refresh rolls down the panel in, 3 to 16.

props.name: dither
props.description: The error-diffusion kernel: smooth Floyd–Steinberg or crisp, lighter Atkinson.

props.name: dot
props.description: CSS px per e-paper pixel, 1 to 4.

props.name: chop
props.description: Wind chop on top of the swell, 0 to 1.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far the device tilts toward the pointer, 0 to 1.

props.name: caption
props.description: Show the readout strip at the top of the paper.

props.name: paperColor
props.description: The paper's colour, any CSS colour.

props.name: inkColor
props.description: The ink's colour, any CSS colour.

props.name: label
props.description: The display's accessible name.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer tilts and turns the display. Keys still turn it.

props.name: paused
props.description: Stop refreshing: the panel keeps its last frame.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the sea's phases and the clouds.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The display stops answering; it stays focusable and says so.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the device; its height follows from a 3:2 aspect.

usageNotes: The device is a role="slider" over 0 to 359 degrees with a spoken value ("Facing south-southwest, 200°, swell 1.9 metres"): Left and Right turn it 15 degrees, Shift or Page Up and Page Down 45, and Home faces north. It wraps past north either way.
A horizontal drag turns the display 1:1, 0.6 degrees a pixel; it is touch-action pan-y, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the page. A mouse also tilts the device and leans the view while it hovers.

There is no animation loop: a timer drives the refreshes and their bands, the sea is computed only at a refresh (a few sines a pixel at e-paper resolution) into preallocated typed arrays and one ImageData, and the timer stops off screen, on a hidden tab, when paused and under reduced motion. Any change asks for a fast partial within 120 ms, as a reader does under a finger.
Full refreshes flash at most twice in under a quarter of a second and no more than once every few seconds; set fullEvery to 0 to never flash.
Under reduced motion there are no bands, no flashes and no tilt, and the sea does not advance: one still frame, redrawn once per turn with a faint ghost of the old one.
The bezel takes the page's surface tokens, so the device belongs on light and dark pages; the paper and ink are fixed, as e-paper is, and can be set with paperColor and inkColor.

items.title: Singing Bowl
items.tagline: Rub the rim and the water stands in patterns.
items.description: A brass singing bowl full of water seen from above, drawn in one WebGL2 pass: circle the pointer round the rim, or hold Space, and the angular speed of your circling feeds energy into the water, which rises into a standing wave of petals at the wall and rings running inward whose order climbs with the speed on the drift spring's time scale, cross-fading so the petals visibly multiply. Stop and the energy drains at the damping rate while the rings let go from the centre out, the last petals dying at the wall, and the rim keeps a soft travelling glint that fades half as fast; a tap on the rim, or Enter at the keyboard's mallet, sends one clean ring across the water. The water is shaded from its height field, its slope reflecting the room and its curvature throwing caustics on the brass floor.

props.name: modes
props.description: The highest petal order rubbing can reach, 2 (four petals) to 8 (sixteen).

props.name: damping
props.description: How fast the singing dies, 0 (rings on and on) to 1 (dies at once).

props.name: metal
props.description: The bowl's metal: a preset, or any CSS colour.

props.name: sensitivity
props.description: How much each circle of the rim puts into the water, 0 to 1.

props.name: rings
props.description: How many standing rings run inward at full energy, 2 to 8.

props.name: glint
props.description: The rim's highlights and its glint, 0 (satin) to 1 (polished).

props.name: waterColor
props.defaultValue: a dark tint of the metal
props.description: The colour of the bowl's floor seen through the water, any CSS colour.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and touch rub and strike the rim. Keys still do.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the water still: the pattern stays where it is.

props.name: label
props.description: The bowl's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: Hum while the bowl sings. Off unless asked for.

props.name: onSingingChange
props.description: Fires as the bowl starts and stops singing.

props.name: onModeChange
props.description: Fires as the number of petals at the rim changes while it sings.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the brushing on the rim and the hammer marks in the floor.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing reaches the bowl and its button is disabled.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the bowl; it is a circle fitted to the box.

usageNotes: The bowl is a round button with a spoken hint: hold Space to rub the rim, faster the longer you hold, with a mallet marker circling the rim as you do; Enter strikes the rim at the mallet; Left and Right move the mallet 15 degrees (Shift 45). Space and Enter are handled on keydown and keyup, so the button's own click never doubles them, and a click from assistive technology strikes.

A mouse rubs by circling over the rim; a finger or pen presses and circles, and the bowl is touch-action none so it never scrolls the page. A tap on the rim strikes it there, and a tap on the water sends a ring from that point.

One fragment pass over a fullscreen triangle, drawn at three quarters of a dense screen's pixels with the device pixel ratio capped at 2. The loop runs only while the water, the glint or a strike wave is alive, on screen and with the tab visible; a settled bowl is one frame. Context loss is handled, and without WebGL2 a drawn still stays.

Under reduced motion the water is a still patterned surface; rubbing or holding Space redraws the still at the order you reached, a strike redraws it with one ring for 600 ms, and onSingingChange and onModeChange still report.

The hum plays only with sound on, starts only from a press, a key, or a hover once the page has had a press, follows the energy and the order, and always stops when the water is still, on a hidden tab and on unmount.
The canvas is transparent with a soft shadow in the theme's ink, so the bowl sits on any surface; the metal is pigment at a fixed lightness, so it looks the same on light and dark pages.

items.title: Crest Fringe
items.tagline: Every wave crest splits the light at its edge.
items.description: A glass tank seen side-on, a slow train of soft Stokes waves inside, lit from behind by a broad lamp: where each crest curves it acts as a prism, seven wavelengths each brightest where the surface slope meets the lamp at that colour's own angle, so every wave's edge splits into a thin spectrum that runs along the wave and drops a faint rainbow fan into the water beneath it. The lamp's height is the light's angle and the component's value — a hovering mouse or a tapping finger sets it and the displayed angle eases there on the springs.glide constants, sliding the fringes from the back slope over the crest to the front. The lamp rail is a real slider: arrows move it 2°, Page keys 10°, Home and End to the ends.

props.name: children
props.description: Content in the tank's air above the water: a hero line, a caption. It stays fully interactive.

props.name: waves
props.description: How many crests stand across the tank, 1 (long rollers) to 6 (a choppy train).

props.name: dispersion
props.description: How far each crest splits the light, 0 (one white edge) to 1 (a wide rainbow fan).

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the waves roll, 0 (still water) to 1 (brisk).

props.name: swell
props.description: How tall the waves stand, 0 to 1.

props.name: level
props.description: How much of the tank is water, 0.25 to 0.8.

props.name: lightAngle / defaultLightAngle
props.description: The lamp's angle behind the tank in degrees, −30 (below) to 30 (above); controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onLightAngleChange
props.description: Fires from the hover, tap, drag or key that moved the lamp, with whole degrees.

props.name: followPointer
props.description: A hovering mouse or pen sets the lamp's height; a finger taps it there.

props.name: glow
props.description: How strongly the lamp lights the tank from behind, 0 to 1.

props.name: waterColor
props.defaultValue: a blue from the accent token (light-dark)
props.description: The water, any CSS colour; it deepens toward the floor.

props.name: airColor
props.defaultValue: a pale or night tint of the accent token (light-dark)
props.description: The backlit air above the water, any CSS colour.

props.name: lightColor
props.defaultValue: a near-white from the accent hue
props.description: The lamp's light, any CSS colour.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the waves where they are.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the phase of the two wave trains.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The lamp control's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The lamp does not move.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the tank; it fills its parent by default.

usageNotes: The lamp knob on the right wall is the one control: role="slider" from −30 to 30 with a spoken value ("Lamp 8 degrees above level"); arrows step 2°, Page Up and Down 10°, Home and End jump to the ends. On touch, drag the rail or tap the tank at the height you want.
The scene itself is decoration (aria-hidden); children render above it in their own layer and keep every click and focus.
Under reduced motion the waves stand still at a designed phase and the lamp moves at once, without easing — the fringes still jump to their new place.

One WebGL2 pass (seven wavelength samples) at three quarters of a dense screen's pixels, the device pixel ratio capped at 2; it runs only on screen, in a visible tab and while the waves roll or the lamp eases, at thirty frames a second when only the waves move. Context loss stops it and a restore rebuilds.

Colours resolve on the element and re-read on a theme change; the light-dark defaults give a pale backlit tank on light pages and a night tank on dark ones. Without WebGL2 the server's gradient still — water, meniscus and a spectral edge on each crest — stays.

items.title: Beadwork Loom
items.tagline: A picture woven in glass beads, moving with it.
items.description: A panel of glass seed beads woven on a loom — wooden beams, warp threads between every column — whose beads take their colour from a moving picture (a slow wave, a seascape with a low sun and rolling swell, a turning flower, or any image or video), so the beadwork plays like a soft low-resolution screen, every bead shaded as a little glass barrel with its own round highlight. Each bead is also a node on a spring lattice, home on the springs.recoil constants and linked to its four neighbours: a drag grabs the warp under the finger 1:1, and on release it springs back past home in two bounces while the ripple runs along the rows, the picture bending with the beads and every highlight rolling with its bead. A tap, Space or Enter plays and pauses the picture; arrow keys tug the warp at the needle and let it go.

props.name: motif
props.description: The picture woven in when there is no src: slow diagonal bands, a seascape with a low sun, or a turning flower.

props.name: src
props.description: An image or video to weave instead of the motif (videos by file extension: mp4, webm, ogv, mov).

props.name: colors
props.description: The bead box, up to six CSS colours from dark to light-and-warm; motifs are painted from it.

props.name: snap
props.description: Every bead takes the nearest colour in the bead box, as a real beadwork chart would.

props.name: beadSize
props.description: A bead's height, px (6 to 16).

props.name: sheen
props.description: How glassy the beads are: the strength of each bead's own round highlight, 0 to 1.

props.name: spacing
props.description: The gap between columns where the warp threads show, px (0.5 to 5).

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the picture moves, 0 to 1.

props.name: tension
props.description: How taut the warp is, 0 (loose, long ripples) to 1 (taut, quick ones).

props.name: playing / defaultPlaying
props.description: Whether the picture plays; controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onPlayingChange
props.description: Fires from the tap or key that played or paused the picture.

props.name: threadColor
props.description: The warp threads, any CSS colour.

props.name: frameColor
props.defaultValue: a wood tone from the warn token
props.description: The loom's beams, any CSS colour.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Dragging tugs the warp; a mouse lifts the sheen where it hovers.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds each bead's small differences of tone and size.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The panel's accessible name; say what is woven.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No tugging and no play or pause.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the loom; it fills its parent by default.

usageNotes: The panel is one focusable group (aria-roledescription "beadwork") named by label: Space or Enter plays and pauses the picture (announced politely), arrow keys tug the warp where the pointer last was and let it go. Pausing is the WCAG pause for moving content.

Pass src for an image or a looping, muted video (it must allow cross-origin reads); it is cropped to cover the woven area, paused off screen and in hidden tabs, and falls back to the motif if it fails to load.

Under reduced motion it is a still panel: the picture holds a composed frame (a video holds its first frame), tugs do not move the beads, and Space still records play or pause for when motion is allowed.

One WebGL2 pass finds each pixel's bead among nine around a fixed-point inverse of the lattice; the lattice steps at 240 Hz only while beads move and uploads its offsets as a small half-float texture, the picture redraws at thirty frames a second, and nothing runs off screen, hidden or paused. The device pixel ratio is capped at 2.

Bead colours, thread and wood are read from the element (pigments at fixed lightness, so they hold in both themes) and re-read on a theme change. Without WebGL2 a CSS still — the motif as a gradient seen through a bead tile, with highlights and warps — stays.

items.title: Cyclone Jar
items.tagline: Swirl the jar and a funnel forms inside.
items.description: A tall glass jar of water and fine glitter, seen side-on and a little from above: drag in circles over it — the hand's travel around the jar's axis is torque, so circles spin it up and a scrub barely does — and a funnel forms down the middle, its depth following the spin on the springs.drift constants as it narrows, while the glitter, carried by a Rankine vortex and one closed secondary cell, spirals faster as it is drawn down toward the core and is thrown out under the surface. Stop and the spin dies away: the funnel slows, widens and collapses, and the flakes drift down fluttering and glinting to gather in a mound in the middle of the floor. Arrow keys push the water round (right clockwise, left anticlockwise), Enter or Space gives a full swirl, and a swish answers each half turn of the hand.

props.name: swirl
props.description: How much a circle of the hand spins the water and how deep the funnel can reach, 0 to 1.

props.name: particles
props.description: How many glitter flakes, 100 to 1500.

props.name: glass
props.description: The glass's tint.

props.name: colors
props.defaultValue: gold, silver, blue and rose pigments from the tokens
props.description: The glitter, CSS colours.

props.name: waterColor
props.defaultValue: a pale (light) or deep (dark) blue, tinted by the glass
props.description: The water, any CSS colour (translucent reads best).

props.name: fill
props.description: How full the jar is, 0.6 to 0.95.

props.name: viscosity
props.description: How quickly the spin dies away, 0 (a long, slow spin-down) to 1 (thick water, quick).

props.name: sink
props.description: How quickly the glitter settles, 0 to 1.

props.name: glint
props.description: How brightly flakes flash as they turn to the light, 0 to 1.

props.name: onStateChange
props.description: Fires when the water starts swirling, starts settling, or comes to rest.

props.name: sound
props.description: A swish for every half turn of the hand, and for each key press.

props.name: paused
props.description: Freeze the water and the glitter where they are.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds where every flake starts and how it tumbles.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The jar's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No swirling.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the piece; the jar keeps its shape and centres in it.

usageNotes: The jar is a real button named by label: arrow keys push the water round (right and down clockwise, left and up anticlockwise), Enter or Space gives a full swirl the way the last push went, and a click gives a small one. "Swirling." and "Settled." are announced politely when the state changes, never per frame.
Circles are a 2D gesture, so the jar takes touch-action: none; the swirl is read from the hand's angle around the water's axis, weighted by its reach, so a scrub across the middle barely turns it.

Under reduced motion it is a settled jar: a swirl cross-fades (a tween) to a still of the funnel formed with the glitter strewn round it, holds while the spin lasts, and cross-fades back. onStateChange still reports.

Canvas 2D with flakes in typed arrays and every colour pre-built as a string, so a frame allocates nothing; it steps at 120 Hz only while the water spins or a flake is still falling, on screen and in a visible tab, and stops once everything rests. The device pixel ratio is capped at 2; the glass and lid are SVG.

Colours resolve on the element and re-read when they change; the water defaults to light-dark tints so the jar reads on both themes, and glitter keeps nearer its colour on light pages so shaded flakes never look like grit.

items.title: Mercury Gate
items.tagline: A liquid gate that shows where it leads.
items.description: A metal ring hanging in a place, a membrane of liquid mercury across it — a WebGL2 height field shaded as a near-perfect mirror with a crisp reflected horizon, slowly wobbling — drawing a faint stream of motes in from the card's edges. Hover or focus it and ripples run out from the pointer while the mercury parts on the springs.glide constants into a clear disc with a beaded meniscus, showing the place the gate leads to; a click or Enter dives through — a breath back, then the ring rushes past on an accelerating tween with streaks pouring outward and a soft flash — and the destination fills the card as the value changes. The ring re-forms behind you on springs.glide, still clear and showing where you came from, before the mercury flows back in on springs.drift. Arrow keys on the gate, or the marks beneath it (a radiogroup with roving focus), choose where it leads.

props.name: destinations
props.description: The places the gate connects: { id, title, caption?, kind?, tone?, scene? }. Without scene a built-in painting (field, shore, dunes, peaks, grove) is drawn from tone.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Where you are: a destination id; controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires when a dive arrives, with the new place's id.

props.name: target / defaultTarget
props.description: Where the gate leads: a destination id; controlled or uncontrolled. After a dive it leads back where you came from.

props.name: onTargetChange
props.description: Fires from the key or mark that pointed the gate somewhere else, and on arrival when it turns to lead back.

props.name: onDive
props.description: Fires as a dive begins, with where from and where to.

props.name: ripple
props.description: How high the hover ripples run and how wide the mercury parts, 0 to 1.

props.name: glow
props.description: How strongly the ring glows, 0 to 1.

props.name: pull
props.description: How many motes the gate draws in, and how fast, 0 to 1.

props.name: ringSize
props.description: The ring's diameter as a share of the box's short side, 0.4 to 1.

props.name: metalColor
props.defaultValue: a cool silver from the accent token
props.description: The ring's metal, any CSS colour.

props.name: glowColor
props.description: The ring's glow and the motes, any CSS colour.

props.name: showLabels
props.description: Show where you are and where the gate leads, as text over the scene.

props.name: sound
props.description: A whoosh as you dive, and a softer one as the ring re-forms.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the mercury and the motes still.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the motes and the built-in paintings' stars and ridges.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvases' device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The gate's accessible name, before "to" and the place.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No diving and no changing where it leads.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the gate; it fills its parent by default.

usageNotes: The gate is a real round button ("Go through to Coldbrook Shore"): Enter or Space dives, arrow keys cycle where it leads, and keyboard focus parts the mercury the way a hovering pointer does. The marks under it are a radiogroup with one tab stop; the current place is marked and disabled. Arrivals and new targets are announced politely.

Under reduced motion there are no ripples, motes or streaks: hovering cross-fades the mercury to clear, and a dive is a cross-fade from place to place with the ring staying put. The values change exactly as they do with motion.

Scenes are yours: pass scene for an image, gradient or component that fills the card, or let a built-in SVG painting be drawn from kind and tone (fixed art, the same in both themes). Set showLabels={false} if your scenes carry their own type; labels are light ink with a soft shadow.

The membrane and ring are one WebGL2 pass scissored to the ring's square, the motes and streaks a Canvas 2D layer; it idles at thirty frames a second, runs full rate only while hovered or diving, and stops off screen, in hidden tabs and when paused. Device pixel ratio capped at 2; context loss stops it and a restore rebuilds. Without WebGL2 a CSS mercury disc stands in and still clears and dives.
Controlled use: a dive reports onValueChange and onTargetChange at its peak; if the host declines the move, the ring re-forms on the place it already shows.

items.title: Lumen Chorus
items.tagline: Lines of light rise from the horizon, one per value.
items.description: A glowing horizon with thin filaments of light rising from it, one per value of a data series — a quiet equaliser drawn in light, each filament a hairline core with a soft glow, a bloom at its tip, a flare where it meets the horizon and a faint reflection on the wet ground below. When new values arrive every filament's height is a spring retargeted from where it stands, released left to right in a cascade; rise picks the spring from the calibration set (springs.drift, springs.glide, springs.snap) and the tips bloom with their speed and flare softly as they land. Hovering or arrowing reads one: it brightens, the rest dim, and a readout slides above it on springs.snap while the readings cross-fade in one cell; the chorus is a slider over the index, with Home and End.

props.name: values
props.description: The series: one filament per value, left to right.

props.name: labels
props.description: A label per value, read in the readout.

props.name: colors
props.description: A ramp of CSS colours across the filaments, left to right.

props.name: warmth
props.description: The light's colour temperature: 0 is the ramp as given (cool), 1 warm amber and rose, mixed in oklab.

props.name: rise
props.description: How the filaments move to new values: 0 slow and soft (drift), 0.5 glide, 1 quick with one overshoot (snap).

props.name: spacing
props.description: How wide the chorus stands, as a share of the width it could fill, 0 to 1.

props.name: max
props.description: The value at the top of the scale.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats a value for the readout.

props.name: unit
props.description: Appended to every formatted value, e.g. "kW".

props.name: horizon
props.description: Where the horizon sits, as a share of the height, 0.55 to 0.9.

props.name: glow
props.description: How much the filaments and horizon glow, 0 to 1.

props.name: reflection
props.description: How strongly they reflect on the ground below the horizon, 0 to 1.

props.name: shimmer
props.description: Faint pulses of light climbing the filaments while idle, 0 to 1.

props.name: active / defaultActive
props.description: The filament being read, by index, or null; controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires from the hover, key or focus that changed the filament being read.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the shimmer still; new values still arrive.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The chorus's accessible name.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the panel; it fills its parent by default.

usageNotes: The chorus is a role="slider" over the index, with aria-valuetext like "14:00, 3.4 kW": arrows step one value, Page keys six, Home and End jump to the ends, and focusing it reads the latest value. Every label and value is also in a list beside it for assistive technology.

Pass values as a new array to animate: each filament springs from where it stands to its new height, in a left-to-right cascade under 600 ms. The first paint stands at the values (the server renders the same still), so a card never looks unstarted.
Under reduced motion new values cross-fade in on a short tween, the readout jumps rather than slides, and there is no shimmer or bloom pulse.

Canvas 2D with every gradient cached per filament and drawn through transforms, so frames allocate nothing; the loop runs while springs move, at thirty frames a second for the shimmer alone, and stops when settled with shimmer 0, off screen or in a hidden tab. Device pixel ratio capped at 2.

Colours resolve on the element and re-read on a theme change: on dark pages the light adds up and glows, on light pages it is drawn as clear coloured lines with soft tinted halos. Formatting is yours (format, unit); the default is a deterministic one-decimal format, safe for server rendering.

items.title: Agate Slice
items.tagline: Banded rings of colour, growing out from the core.
items.description: A thin polished slice of banded agate held up to the light, drawn in one WebGL2 pass: an irregular nodule whose bands follow its outline inward as warped, scaled copies — opaque coloured layers, milky chalcedony that glows, fine laminations — round a small druse of quartz that glints as the lamp crosses it. New bands crystallise outward from the core in a slow loop, born soft and glowing, sharpening as they travel and hardening into the rough rind at the edge; the lamp behind the slice follows the pointer on the springs.drift constants, so the clear bands near it brighten and the far ones dim. A drag turns the slice 1:1 and a throw coasts on friction; as a slider of the angle, arrows turn it 15° on springs.glide, Page keys 45°, Home back to 0, and Shift with the arrows moves the lamp.

props.name: palette
props.description: The stone's bands.

props.name: colors
props.description: Your own five band colours, CSS, pale to deep; overrides palette.

props.name: translucency
props.description: How much light the clear bands let through, 0 (opaque stone) to 1 (glowing).

props.name: pace
props.description: How fast new bands grow from the core, 0 (one every 9 s) to 1 (one every 1.6 s).

props.name: bands
props.description: How many bands fit across the slice, 0 (broad) to 1 (fine).

props.name: rind
props.description: How thick the rough rind is, 0 to 1.

props.name: core
props.description: How large the quartz core is, 0 to 1.

props.name: rindColor
props.defaultValue: a stone brown from the warn token
props.description: The rind, any CSS colour.

props.name: angle / defaultAngle
props.description: The slice's turn in degrees; controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onAngleChange
props.description: Fires when a drag, throw or key leaves the slice at a new turn, in whole degrees 0 to 359.

props.name: followPointer
props.description: The pointer moves the lamp behind the slice.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the bands still.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the nodule's outline and every band.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The slice's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No turning.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the piece; the slice centres in it as a square.

usageNotes: The slice is a role="slider" of its angle (0–359, "Turned 30 degrees"): arrows turn it 15° on springs.glide, Page Up and Down 45°, Home back to 0, End to 359; Shift with the arrows moves the lamp, and keyboard focus brings the lamp in behind the core.
A drag turns it 1:1 by the hand's angle round the centre (touch-action: none) and a throw coasts on friction; onAngleChange reports once it comes to rest, never per frame.
Under reduced motion the bands hold a composed still, turns land at once with no glide or coast, and the lamp jumps rather than eases.

One WebGL2 pass over the slice's square at three quarters of a dense screen's pixels, device pixel ratio capped at 2; it draws at thirty frames a second while the bands grow, full rate only while turning or the lamp eases, and stops off screen, in hidden tabs, paused or at pace 0. Context loss stops it and a restore rebuilds; without WebGL2 a CSS still (banded rings in the nodule, a rind) stays.
Palettes are pigments made from the tokens at fixed lightness, so a stone looks the same on light and dark pages; the soft shadow under it deepens a little on dark ones.

items.title: Pole Trails
items.tagline: The night sky drawing circles over a ridge.
items.description: A long exposure of the northern sky above a dark ridge: while the shutter is open every star traces an arc round the celestial pole at 15° per hour of sky, gathered at `exposure` minutes a second and tinted faintly by its temperature, while skyglow gathers on the horizon and an occasional meteor scores a straight streak that stays in the picture. A click, tap, Enter or Space closes the shutter — a curtain drops on springs.flick, the exposure clears and it lifts away on springs.glide over a fresh sky of points — and dragging moves the pole 1:1 so every arc re-centres live, a throw gliding on with its release velocity. Arrow keys move the pole and Home brings it back.

props.name: exposure
props.description: How fast the exposure builds, in minutes of sky per second of real time (1 to 60).

props.name: density
props.description: How many stars, 0 (a hazy night) to 1 (a dark-sky site).

props.name: horizon
props.description: The ground under the sky: a jagged ridge, rolling hills, a hill with a treeline of pines, or a flat sea horizon.

props.name: maxHours
props.description: Hours of sky an exposure gathers before it holds (1 to 12).

props.name: loop
props.description: A finished exposure closes the shutter and starts a fresh one after `hold`.

props.name: hold
props.description: How long a finished exposure is held before it loops, ms.

props.name: meteors
props.description: Meteors per minute of real time while the shutter is open; 0 for none.

props.name: pole / defaultPole
props.description: The celestial pole as fractions of the frame, [x, y]; controlled or uncontrolled. Home returns to defaultPole.

props.name: onPoleChange
props.description: Fires from the drag release or the key that moved the pole, with where it lands.

props.name: skyColor
props.description: The night sky, any CSS colour; a pigment at fixed lightness so the print reads the same in both themes.

props.name: groundColor
props.description: The ridge silhouette, any CSS colour.

props.name: starColors
props.description: Star tints [hot, neutral, cool]; every star sits between them by its temperature.

props.name: glow
props.description: Skyglow along the horizon, 0 to 1; it gathers as the exposure builds.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Drag moves the pole; a click, Enter or Space closes the shutter.

props.name: paused
props.description: Holds the exposure where it is.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the stars, the ridge and the meteors.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onShutter
props.description: A fresh exposure opened (the shutter closed and reopened).

props.name: onComplete
props.description: The exposure reached maxHours, with the hours gathered.

props.name: label
props.description: The sky's name; the button reads "<label>: start a new exposure".

props.name: disabled
props.description: No drag, no shutter: the exposure keeps running and the button is aria-disabled.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the frame.

usageNotes: The frame is a native button named "<label>: start a new exposure": Space, Enter and clicks close the shutter; arrow keys move the pole 24 px (Shift 72 px) and Home returns it; a polite live region speaks the visitor's own shutter, completion and pole moves only, never the self-looping exposure.
Drag takes the pointer only after 4 px of travel, so a plain tap is still the shutter; touch-action is none because the pole moves in two dimensions.

Under reduced motion the frame is a still of a finished exposure (75% of maxHours, one meteor recorded) and the shutter fades through dark to a fresh still; the pole still follows a drag 1:1 and keys place it instantly.

Arcs are drawn analytically from the pole in twelve batched strokes (brightness × temperature), so a rich sky stays a dozen draw calls; the ridge and skyglow are cached layers. The loop runs only while the exposure grows, the shutter or pole moves or a meteor burns, at 30 Hz when only the arcs lengthen, and never off screen, hidden or paused.
The sky and ground are pigments at fixed lightness taken from the accent hue, so the print reads as a night photograph on both light and dark pages; colours re-read on theme change.

items.title: Ghosting LCD
items.tagline: A slow screen that remembers where you moved.
items.description: A reflective monochrome LCD with visible pixel gaps that you draw on: the pointer lays a soft brush whose edges are dithered through a 4×4 Bayer matrix, and every pixel answers on the slow, smeary response of an old pocket screen — darkening on a quarter of `response` and clearing on all of it — so a quick stroke leaves a longer, fainter ghost than a slow one, and each lit pixel casts a faint shadow `depth` px onto the reflector. A press squeezes the crystal into a dark bloom whose radius rides springs.recoil out and back with two visible bounces as the glass flexes; Delete wipes the glass with a scan bar. It is a focusable screen: arrow keys draw with a blinking pen (Shift for a quicker stroke), Enter and Space press.

props.name: response
props.description: How long a pixel takes to clear once released, ms (80 to 2000): the slower it is, the longer the ghosts.

props.name: pixel
props.description: Pixel pitch in px (3 to 12).

props.name: tint
props.description: The panel's tint: the classic olive pocket screen, a calculator grey, a pager teal or a warm sepia.

props.name: colors
props.description: Overrides of the tint, as CSS colours: the panel and the lit pixels.

props.name: gap
props.description: Share of the pitch left as a gap between pixels (0 to 0.4).

props.name: depth
props.description: How far, px, each lit pixel's shadow sits below and right of it on the reflector; 0 hides the shadows.

props.name: brush
props.description: Radius of the drawing brush, in pixels (0.6 to 4).

props.name: dither
props.description: Ordered (Bayer) dither at the stroke's soft edges; off, the edge is a hard threshold.

props.name: bloom
props.description: How far a press spreads through the crystal, 0 to 1; 0 turns the press bloom off.

props.name: text
props.description: A line of pixel text the device shows in its top-left corner (A–Z, 0–9, - . : / ! ? ' +); whole words only.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer, touch and keys draw.

props.name: paused
props.description: Freezes the screen's response.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onClear
props.description: The screen was wiped (Delete or Backspace).

props.name: label
props.description: The screen's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing draws; the screen keeps what it shows, leaves the tab order and says it is disabled.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the screen.

usageNotes: The screen is a focusable group (aria-roledescription "drawing screen") with a key hint: arrow keys draw with a pen that blinks (and ghosts) only while keyboard-focused, Shift draws four pixels a step, Enter and Space press, Delete and Backspace wipe; a polite live region confirms presses and wipes from the keyboard.
Mouse and pen draw on hover; touch draws while the finger is down, so the screen sets touch-action: none. The system cursor stays (a crosshair inside the screen only).
Under reduced motion the press bloom and the wipe fade in place instead of travelling; pixels still ghost away by opacity, because what you drew is the feedback.

Only changing pixels are visited (an active list) and lit pixels are drawn in sixteen batched alpha levels; the glass, its unlit grid and the device text are a cached layer. The loop stops when nothing on the glass is changing and never runs off screen or in a hidden page.
Tints are pigments at fixed lightness taken from theme hues, so the glass looks like the same physical screen on light and dark pages.

items.title: Heading Glyphs
items.tagline: Your path, set in the characters that fit it.
items.description: A cursor trail set in monospaced type behind your content: every cell the pointer crosses takes the character that fits the stroke there — a dash, pipe or slash for its heading, a weight from dots to hashes for its speed — then cools down the ramp a character at a time while its ink walks from hot to cold, so a fast stroke lingers and a slow one is soon gone. A click stamps an asterisk whose eight rays reach out on springs.recoil, one cell past and back, and cool from the centre outward. Keyboard focus on any child draws a short underline stroke under it, and Enter or Space there stamps at its centre.

props.name: ramp
props.description: The type the trail is set in: plain ASCII, box-drawing strokes, or braille dots.

props.name: fade
props.description: How long a cell takes to cool through the whole ramp, ms (200 to 5000).

props.name: cell
props.description: Cell height in px (8 to 28); a cell is a monospaced character wide (about 0.62 of that) and the glyphs are set to fit.

props.name: colors
props.description: Inks from hot to cold, as CSS colours, mixed in oklab into eight steps.

props.name: sensitivity
props.description: Pointer speed, px/s, that reaches the heaviest weight of the ramp.

props.name: burst
props.description: Ray length of the asterisk a click stamps, in cells; 0 turns the stamp off.

props.name: focusStroke
props.description: Draw a short underline stroke under a child that takes keyboard focus.

props.name: grid
props.description: A faint dot lattice at rest, like an empty type case.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight of the glyphs.

props.name: intro
props.description: The first time the box comes into view, a stroke sets itself across it — slow, fast, slow — to show the ramp; never under reduced motion.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer, clicks and keyboard focus draw.

props.name: paused
props.description: Holds every glyph where it is.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.
