props.name: onStamp
props.description: A stamp landed, with the cell it centred on.

props.name: children
props.description: Content set above the type; it stays fully interactive.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the box.

usageNotes: The painted layer is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none, under a z-10 content layer: children keep their own semantics, focus order and clicks, and the system cursor is never hidden.

Keyboard visitors get the same marks: :focus-visible on any child draws an underline stroke under it, and Enter or Space on it stamps at its centre. Touch never draws a trail (it scrolls the page); a tap stamps.
Under reduced motion each glyph keeps the character it was given and fades by opacity over `fade`; the stamp and the focus stroke appear whole and fade.

Only lit cells are visited and every glyph is one image draw from an atlas of the ramp in eight inks; the loop stops when the last glyph is gone and never runs off screen or in a hidden page. The resting lattice is a cached layer.

Inks are text tokens mixed in oklab and re-read on theme change. Every glyph is centred in its cell by its own ink, so box-drawing characters from a fallback face still sit on the stroke; braille dots are drawn rather than set, so the dots ramp looks the same on every platform.

items.title: Sea Printout
items.tagline: A rolling sea printed one line at a time.
items.description: A strip of continuous-feed paper — sprocket holes punched down both margins, tear-off perforations, green-bar banding and a fold crease every page — rising out of a line printer as it prints a rolling sea in overstruck ASCII, one line per tick: each line is the next slice of three Stokes swells and a short chop, shaded by the slope facing the light with crests drawn as runs of tildes, the darkest tones struck twice a hair out of register. Each line arrives in a chain printer's scattered order and the paper ratchets up on springs.snap, one crisp overshoot per line; moving the pointer sideways sets the wind on springs.drift, leaning the swell and raising whitecaps. It is a real slider: arrow keys, Page Up and Down, Home and End set the wind.

props.name: swell
props.description: Height of the swell, 0 (glassy) to 1 (a heavy roll).

props.name: feed
props.description: Lines printed per second (1 to 12).

props.name: ink
props.description: Ribbon density, 0 (pale and sparse) to 1 (heavy, with more overstrikes).

props.name: wind / defaultWind
props.description: The wind, -1 (blowing from the west) to 1 (from the east); controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onWindChange
props.description: Fires from the pointer or the key that changed the wind, in steps of 0.05.

props.name: chop
props.description: How choppy the wind makes the sea, 0 to 1: short waves, spray and whitecaps.

props.name: pageLines
props.description: Lines between the paper's fold creases (8 to 66).

props.name: bars
props.description: Faint green-bar banding every three lines.

props.name: overstrike
props.description: Overstruck pairs for the darkest tones.

props.name: size
props.description: Glyph size in px (7 to 13).

props.name: colors
props.type: { paper?: string; ink?: string; bar?: string }
props.description: Paper, ribbon and bar colours, any CSS colours; pigments by default, the same in both themes.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and the keys set the wind.

props.name: paused
props.description: The printer stops (its lamp reads off line).

props.name: sound
props.description: The printer whirs while you work the wind.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the sea and the hammers' small errors.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The slider's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The wind holds and the slider says it is disabled; the printer keeps printing.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the printer.

usageNotes: The paper is a role="slider" from -100 to 100 with a spoken aria-valuetext ("Wind 40 from the east, a light chop"): Left/Right and Up/Down step 0.1 (Shift 0.25), Page Up/Down 0.25, Home and End the extremes, 0 calms it. Touch sets the wind with a sideways drag and keeps touch-action: pan-y for vertical scrolling.

Sound is off by default; with `sound`, the whir loop runs only while the visitor works the wind (never before the page has had a click, tap or key press), lifts with each struck line and stops 600 ms after the last input, on unmount, or when sound is turned off.
Under reduced motion the paper does not feed and no line is struck in order: the page is a still print for the current wind and reprints with a 240 ms crossfade once the wind rests.

Between ticks nothing runs; each tick strikes and feeds and the loop stops when the paper settles. Every printed line is drawn once into a cached bitmap in a ring buffer, so a frame is a few dozen image draws. Nothing runs off screen, in a hidden page or paused; DPR is capped at 2.
The sea is computed with arithmetic-only trigonometry, so the server prints the same first page the canvas continues from, character for character, with no hydration risk.

items.title: Dendrite Reach
items.tagline: Tendrils that reach, touch and pass a signal.
items.description: Fluorescent nerve cells under a microscope: dendrites grow slowly out from each soma by branching, their tips carrying growth cones that feel about, and when a tip meets another cell's dendrite it either pulls back along its own path and turns away, or lunges the last pixels on springs.snap and forms a junction whose bouton blooms on springs.recoil. Cells fire at `pulse` Hz — the soma flashes and a front of light runs out along every branch — and at each junction the signal crosses after a synaptic delay, runs in to the partner's soma and fires it in turn. The pointer offers a cue that nearby tips grow toward and a click stimulates the nearest cell; as a focusable group, arrow keys move the cue, Enter stimulates and Escape clears the cue.

props.name: branching
props.description: How bushy the dendrites grow, 0 (long and sparse) to 1 (densely branched).

props.name: pulse
props.description: Spontaneous firings per cell per second (0 to 2); 0 leaves the cells quiet until stimulated.

props.name: stain
props.description: The fluorescent stain: a named one, or any CSS colour.

props.name: cells
props.description: How many cells (1 to 8); 0 picks one per ~190 px of width.

props.name: growth
props.description: How fast a growth cone advances, px/s (4 to 60).

props.name: reach
props.description: Length budget of each cell's tree, 0.4 to 2.

props.name: junctions
props.description: Chance that two meeting dendrites form a junction rather than pull apart, 0 to 1.

props.name: cue
props.description: How strongly tips grow toward the pointer's cue, 0 to 1.

props.name: cueRadius
props.description: How far the cue reaches, px.

props.name: background
props.description: The field behind the cells, any CSS colour; dark in both themes, as fluorescence is.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and the keys offer a cue and stimulate.

props.name: paused
props.description: Holds growth and signals where they are.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the culture; a new seed grows a new one.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onFire
props.description: A cell fired, with its index and why: on its own, passed a signal across a junction, or stimulated by the visitor.

props.name: onJunctionsChange
props.description: The number of junctions, reported from the start and on each new one.

props.name: label
props.description: The culture's name; the group reads "<label>, N junctions".

props.name: disabled
props.description: No cue, no stimulation; the culture grows on and says it is disabled.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the field.

usageNotes: The field is a focusable group (aria-roledescription "micrograph") named with its junction count and a key hint: arrow keys move the cue (24 px, Shift 72 px), Enter or Space stimulates the cell nearest it, Escape clears it (and only then prevents the default). A polite live region speaks stimulated cells and new junctions, no more than one junction every 1.5 s.
Mouse and pen offer the cue on hover; a tap places it and stimulates. Touch keeps touch-action: pan-y so the page still scrolls over the culture.

Under reduced motion the culture is a still micrograph grown to completion in one go; stimulating a cell crossfades a glow over it and every cell it is joined to, with no travelling pulses and no growth.

Trees are baked into a cached layer as they grow; only the last ~36 px of each live tip is redrawn per frame, and meetings are found through a spatial hash. Once growth is done and no signal is in flight the loop sleeps until the next scheduled firing; nothing runs off screen, hidden or paused, and a resize grows the culture again.

Named stains are pigments at fixed lightness taken from theme hues and the field stays dark in both themes, as a fluorescence image does; onFire's cause lets a host narrate only the visitor's own stimulus.

items.title: Torus Puzzle
items.tagline: Rows and columns of dots slide until it solves.
items.description: A square of glowing dots holding a simple picture whose rows and columns slide one cell at a time on springs.snap and wrap round the edges like a torus — the dot leaving one side is drawn again entering the other — while the moving line's track lifts behind it and its dots glow with its speed. On its own it scrambles itself and then solves back in a calm, deliberate sequence, the inverse of every step; drag any row or column and it follows 1:1, wraps as far as you pull and snaps to a whole step with the release velocity, and after a quiet spell it solves from wherever you left it. Solved, the lit dots swell and land on springs.recoil in a cascade from the centre. It is a real grid: arrow keys move between dots, wrapping at the edges, and Shift with an arrow slides the row or column.

props.name: grid
props.description: Dots per side (3 to 9).

props.name: pace
props.description: Milliseconds per autoplay step while solving; scrambling runs at 0.7 of it (200 to 1500).

props.name: glow
props.description: Halo of the lit dots and their boost while moving, 0 (none) to 1.

props.name: pattern
props.description: The picture the lit dots make at home, or your own grid × grid cells, row by row.

props.name: scramble
props.description: Steps in each scramble (1 to 30).

props.name: autoplay
props.description: Scrambles and solves itself while on screen.

props.name: resumeAfter
props.description: Quiet time after your last move before autoplay solves from where you left it, ms.

props.name: colors
props.type: { lit?: string; dim?: string; track?: string }
props.description: Colours, as CSS colours: lit dots, unlit dots and home rings, and the track behind a moving line.

props.name: onMove
props.type: (move: { axis: "row" | "column"; index: number; by: number }) => void
props.description: Fires for every committed move — yours, a button's or autoplay's — with the shortest equivalent shift.

props.name: onSolvedChange
props.description: Whether the picture is home, reported from the start and on every change.

props.name: onDistanceChange
props.description: Steps from home, reported from the start and on every change.

props.name: sound
props.description: Ticks as dots cross cells, for the visitor's own moves only.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No drag and no keys; autoplay still runs.

props.name: label
props.description: The grid's name; it reads "<label>, solved" or "<label>, N steps from home".

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the square board.

props.name: ref
props.description: Imperative solve() and scramble(), played one step at a time; autoplay waits resumeAfter before taking over again.

usageNotes: The board is role="grid" with rows and gridcells ("Row 2, column 3, lit, out of place") and one roving tab stop: arrow keys move between dots and wrap at the edges, Home and End jump within a row (with Ctrl, the whole grid), Shift with an arrow slides the row or column one step with focus riding along. A polite live region speaks the visitor's own moves and "Solved"; autoplay is silent.

Drag captures only after 4 px and picks its axis from the first travel; touch-action is none on the board because a line can move either way. Sound, when on, ticks only for the visitor's drags, keys and solve/scramble calls.
Under reduced motion a step is an instant swap with a short flash of the moved line, and solved is a glow rather than a swell; autoplay keeps its pace because the state changes are the information.

Nothing runs per frame outside a step: motion values per dot (keyed by dot id) carry every position, autoplay is a timer chain that stops off screen, in a hidden page and while the visitor plays, and everything is disposed on unmount.
Every move is kept in a history that cancels inverse steps, so the puzzle always knows its way home; solving it yourself is noticed and clears the history.

items.title: Willow Shell
items.tagline: Launch a shell; it opens, droops and fades gold.
items.description: A firework display in one tall frame: a night sky over a far riverbank, the river below mirroring it in rippling strips. A click fires a shell from the bank on a real ballistic arc, shedding sparks, and at its apex it bursts with a flash that lifts the sky toward its colour: a willow hangs heavy stars whose strands droop with age and cool from white-gold to amber as they fade, a peony blooms round and twinkles out, and crossette comets split in a cross mid-flight, while smoke drifts on the wind and catches later flashes. The frame is a button: Left and Right move the aim mark along the bank on springs.snap and Enter or Space launches there; a scripted `sequence` plays a finale.

props.name: children
props.description: A headline over the sky; it takes no pointer input. The root sets --willow-ink and --willow-faint for text on the night.

props.name: shell
props.description: The burst: hanging gold willow, a round peony, crossettes that split in a cross, or each in turn.

props.name: spread
props.description: How wide the burst opens, 0 to 1; wider shells carry more stars.

props.name: gravity
props.description: How hard stars and strands droop, 0 (they hang) to 1 (they fall).

props.name: height
props.description: How high a shell bursts, 0 (just over the bank) to 1 (the top of the sky).

props.name: stars
props.description: Stars per shell, 24 to 140.

props.name: trail
props.description: How long willow strands and star streaks are, 0 to 1.

props.name: gold
props.description: The willow's gold, any CSS colour.

props.name: colors
props.description: Star colours for peonies and crossettes; defaults to four token pigments.

props.name: wind
props.description: Wind across the river, -1 to 1: carries smoke and strands.

props.name: reflection
props.description: Mirror the sky in a river under the bank.

props.name: sequence
props.description: The scripted show `playing` runs: each cue's time in ms, shell, place along the bank, height and size.

props.name: playing / defaultPlaying
props.description: Whether the show is running, controlled or initial. Turning it on starts the show from its first cue.

props.name: onPlayingChange
props.description: Fires with false when the show's last shell has faded.

props.name: trigger
props.description: What launches an opening shell by itself: coming into view, mounting, or nothing but the visitor.

props.name: onBurst
props.description: Fires as each shell bursts, with its type and where along the bank it was fired.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold everything in the air where it is and take no launches.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the stars, the bank and every burst.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The frame's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the whistle as a shell leaves and the flare as it bursts, only for the visitor's own launches (and a show the visitor just started).

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the sky but takes no launches.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the frame.

usageNotes: The frame is a native button described by a hint: Left and Right (Shift for larger steps), Home and End move the aim mark along the bank, Enter or Space launches there, and each launch is announced once, politely.

Under reduced motion every shell is a still burst: it appears fully open with its strands at their droop, cross-fades in, and holds until the next one replaces it. The frame starts on a still of the chosen shell.
The night is fixed art, dark on light and dark pages alike; star colours are pigments read from tokens on the component's own element and re-read when the theme changes.

Canvas 2D with pooled typed arrays and a pre-rendered sky and bank. The loop runs only while something is in the air or smoke is drifting, never off screen or in a hidden tab, and the backing store caps its pixel ratio at 2.
Sound never answers an automatic launch: the whistle and the flare play for the visitor's own clicks and keys, and for a show started within a moment of their press.

items.title: Play Parachute
items.tagline: A silk canopy that billows when you lift an edge.
items.description: A playground parachute seen from above at an angle: bright silk panels round a small centre hole, sagging into a shallow bowl with each panel puffed between its seams, held at the hem by handle loops over a dotted ground. The canopy is a height field running the wave equation on a polar grid; drag near the rim and the hem rises 1:1 under the finger, shake it and waves roll inward and round with a satin sheen along the weave on every crest, and let go and the hem drops on springs.recoil with the hand's velocity. A tap throws the whole canopy up into a dome that settles slowly on its trapped air, tossing the little ball that rolls on the silk; the keyboard moves a ring between handles on springs.snap, Up lifts an edge on snap and lets it fall on recoil, and Enter throws.

props.name: panels
props.description: How many silk panels make the canopy, 4 to 24.

props.name: colors

props.name: billow

props.name: sheen
props.description: The satin highlight on every crest, 0 (matte cotton) to 1 (bright silk).

props.name: tension
props.description: How taut the silk is, 0 (slow, lazy waves) to 1 (quick ones).

props.name: settle
props.description: How quickly waves and the dome die away, 0 (they roll on) to 1 (they stop soon).

props.name: tilt
props.description: The view's height above the ground in degrees, 20 (low and long) to 70 (from above).

props.name: handles
props.description: Handles round the rim, 4 to 16: the stops the keyboard moves between.

props.name: ball
props.description: A small ball rolls on the silk.

props.name: ballColor
props.description: The ball's colour, any CSS colour.

props.name: trigger
props.description: What throws a soft billow by itself: coming into view, mounting, or nothing.

props.name: onThrow
props.description: Fires when the visitor throws the canopy up.

props.name: onLift
props.description: Fires when the visitor lifts or shakes an edge, with the handle's index (0 is nearest the viewer, counting to the right).

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the silk where it is.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds where the ball starts.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The canopy's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the swish of the silk for the visitor's own throws, lifts and shakes.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the canopy but takes no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box; the canopy, its dome and a lifted edge always fit inside it.

usageNotes: The canopy is a native button described by a hint: Left and Right (Home, End) move the handle ring, Up lifts that edge and Down pulls it, Enter or Space throws the canopy up; each action is announced once, politely. The ring shows only for keyboard focus.

Drag anywhere on the canopy to hold the nearest stretch of hem: vertical travel lifts it 1:1, sideways travel slides the hold round the rim. The box uses touch-action: none so a drag never scrolls the page.
Under reduced motion the canopy rests gently domed and still; a lift or a drag lights the silk by that edge and a throw brightens the whole canopy, fading without any travel.

Canvas 2D with a colour table built once per palette and sheen, typed arrays for the field, and a pre-rendered ground. The loop runs only while the silk, the dome or the ball moves, never off screen or in a hidden tab.
Panel colours are pigments read from tokens on the component's own element, so they look the same on light and dark pages; the dotted ground follows the theme.

items.title: Shower Radiant
items.tagline: Meteors falling outward from one point in the sky.
items.description: A meteor shower over a dark conifer treeline: meteors appear at random round a radiant point and streak straight outward along fanning rays, short near the radiant where they come almost at you and long far from it, each brief and bright with a hot head, a tapering streak and a glowing train that lingers and spreads; now and then a slow fireball sheds fragments, lifts the sky and leaves a train that bends in the upper wind. Under the sky an hour scale with the night's activity curve is a real slider: dragging moves through the night 1:1 as the radiant climbs and the visible rate (the shower's rate, its activity and the radiant's altitude) rises toward the peak, and a release projects the throw and glides to a quarter hour on springs.glide with the release velocity. Arrow keys step a quarter hour, Shift and the Page keys an hour, Home and End go to dusk and dawn.

props.name: children
props.description: A headline over the sky; it takes no pointer input. The root sets --shower-ink and --shower-faint for text on the night.

props.name: rate
props.description: The shower's zenithal hourly rate at its peak: meteors an hour with the radiant overhead.

props.name: train
props.description: How long a meteor's glowing train lingers and how far it spreads, 0 to 1.

props.name: tint
props.description: The heads' colour and the trains' glow.

props.name: headColor
props.description: A head colour of your own, any CSS colour; overrides tint.

props.name: hour / defaultHour
props.description: The hour of the night as a clock hour (1.5 is 01:30), controlled or initial.

props.name: onHourChange
props.description: Fires from the drag or key that moved the hour, with the new clock hour in quarter hours.

props.name: startHour
props.description: When the scale starts, as a clock hour.

props.name: endHour
props.description: When it ends, as a clock hour (the next morning if smaller than startHour).

props.name: peakHour
props.description: When the shower peaks, as a clock hour.

props.name: fireballs
props.description: How often a slow, bright fireball comes through, 0 (never) to 1.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast meteors cross the sky, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: showRadiant
props.description: Mark the radiant with a faint ring.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the sky still.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the stars, the trees and every meteor.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The hour scale's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the sky but the scale takes no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the frame; the scale takes 76px of it.

usageNotes: The hour scale is a role=slider with aria-valuetext such as "01:30, about 84 meteors an hour, radiant 41 degrees up"; the sky is a role=img whose label says the same. Drag is horizontal with touch-action: pan-y, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the page.

Under reduced motion the sky is a still long exposure: streaks fanning from the radiant, as many as a few minutes at that hour would bring, redrawn at once as the hour changes. No streak moves and the scale jumps without the glide.

One second in the frame is a minute of the night, so a rate of 100 gives about one and a half meteors a second at the peak. showerReading(rate, hour) returns the same numbers the scale shows, for a status line or a caption.

Canvas 2D: the sky, its stars, the galaxy band and the trees are drawn once per size and theme; meteors and trains are pre-rendered sprites under a transform from fixed pools. The loop runs only on screen and in a visible tab, at half rate while nothing is in the air.
The night is fixed art, dark on light and dark pages alike; the tint and train colours are read from tokens on the component's own element and re-read when the theme changes.

items.title: Tube Rack
items.tagline: Glass tubes of colour, each filled to its value.
items.description: A rack of glass test tubes, each filled to its value with glossy coloured liquid behind a front rail: a curved meniscus climbs the glass, a shine runs down the liquid and the glass has its own long glint. Every few seconds a slow wave runs along the rack and nudges each tube as it passes, so the surfaces tilt and rock back to level in turn on a damped oscillator. Pick a tube and drag on it: a target mark follows the finger 1:1 and the liquid pours to meet it, capped at a pour rate and settling on springs.glide's constants, with a thin stream falling from the mouth as it rises and bubbles climbing as it drains; each tube is a vertical slider under one tab stop, Left and Right move between tubes, Up and Down step, Page keys move a tenth, Home empties and End fills.

props.name: values / defaultValues
props.description: One level per tube, from 0 to max, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValuesChange
props.description: Fires from the drag or key that changed a level, with every level.

props.name: labels
props.description: A short name under each tube; also each slider's accessible name.

props.name: max
props.description: The value of a full tube.

props.name: step
props.description: How far an arrow key moves a level; drags snap to it too.

props.name: palette
props.description: The liquids' colours, cycled along the rack.

props.name: colors
props.description: Liquid colours of your own, any CSS colours; overrides palette.

props.name: slosh
props.description: How far the surfaces tilt when the wave passes and how long they rock, 0 (still) to 1.

props.name: gloss
props.description: The glass's highlight and the liquid's shine, 0 (matte) to 1.

props.name: wavePeriod
props.description: How often a slow wave runs along the rack, in ms.

props.name: pourSpeed
props.description: How fast liquid pours to a new level, 0 (a slow trickle) to 1 (a quick pour).

props.name: graduations
props.description: Faint graduations at each quarter of the glass.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats a value for its chip, its label and assistive technology; defaults to a rounded number.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires when a tube is picked by a press or by focus, or with null when focus leaves the rack.

props.name: label
props.description: The rack's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the glug of the pour, rising as the tube fills, for the visitor's own changes; it stops when the pour does.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the levels but takes no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the rack; tubes are laid out in pixels from the measured width.

usageNotes: The rack is a role=group of vertical role=slider tubes under one tab stop, each named by its label with aria-valuetext such as "P3: 62". Left and Right move focus between tubes; Up, Down, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End change the focused level.
The first press on a tube picks it; pressing a picked tube pours to that height, and a vertical drag sets the level 1:1 (touch-action: pan-x, so a sideways swipe still scrolls).
Under reduced motion the surfaces stay level and a change is a 150 ms tween with no stream or bubbles; the value still changes in full.
SVG redrawn by one loop that writes path data directly and runs only while a surface moves and the rack is on screen; the next wave waits on a timer, so a settled rack costs nothing between waves.
Liquids are pigments mixed from tokens (oklch relative colours), so they read the same on light and dark pages; glass and rack follow the theme's ink and surfaces.

items.title: Forecast Glow
items.tagline: Scrub tonight's forecast and the sky answers.
items.description: A soft, heavily blurred aurora over dark hills and a still lake whose strength follows an hourly activity forecast: the glow is computed per pixel into a small buffer and left to the browser to scale and blur, a few slow curtains rising from behind the ridge, fading upward and mirrored dimmer in the water. The timeline beneath, one bar per hour coloured by its reading, is a slider through the night: a drag moves the playhead 1:1, a release projects the throw and glides to a quarter hour on springs.glide with the release velocity, and the sky follows on springs.drift's constants, growing brighter and taller and shifting from its quiet colour toward its peak colour while the hour and the reading ride the playhead above. Arrow keys step a quarter hour, Shift and the Page keys an hour, Home and End go to the first and last hour.

props.name: forecast
props.description: Hourly activity, one reading per hour from startHour, on a 0 to maxReading scale.

props.name: startHour
props.description: The clock hour of the first reading.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The position on the timeline in hours from the first reading, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drag or key that moved the timeline, in quarter hours from the first reading.

props.name: intensity
props.description: How bright the glow can get, 0 to 1.

props.name: blur
props.description: How soft the glow is, 0 (soft) to 1 (a haze): the buffer's resolution and the blur radius.

props.name: palette
props.description: The glow's colours from quiet to the peak.

props.name: colors
props.description: Colours of your own: the base of a quiet glow, its middle, and the top at the peak; overrides palette.

props.name: maxReading
props.description: The top of the reading scale.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats a reading for the readout and assistive technology; defaults to "Kp 5.3".

props.name: describe
props.description: Names a reading; defaults to quiet, active, strong and storm.

props.name: drift
props.description: How fast the curtains drift, 0 (still) to 1.

props.name: reflection
props.description: A lake under the hills that mirrors the glow.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the curtains still.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the stars, the hills and the curtains.

props.name: label
props.description: The timeline's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the forecast but the timeline takes no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the widget; the timeline takes 56px of it.

usageNotes: The timeline is a role=slider whose aria-valuetext reads the hour, the reading and its name ("23:00, Kp 5.7, strong"); the visual readout is hidden from assistive technology so nothing is said twice, and the sky is a role=img with the same sentence.
Under reduced motion the curtains are still and the sky eases to each new reading over a few frames; the playhead jumps without the glide.

The glow is a small ImageData buffer, roughly a sixth of the box, reused every frame and blurred by the compositor: the loop runs at about 30 frames a second while the curtains drift, only on screen and in a visible tab, and stops once a still sky has settled.
forecastAt(forecast, hour) is exported: the same monotone interpolation the sky uses, for a status line or a chart beside it.
The night is fixed art, dark on light and dark pages alike; the glow and bar colours are pigments read from tokens on the component's own element.

items.title: Anaglyph Card
items.tagline: A red and cyan card whose depth shows as you tilt.
items.description: An image card split into two colour channels by a depth map: one WebGL2 pass samples the picture as a left and a right view, each shifted along the tilt by its depth with a short search so edges hold, and feeds them through the two filter colours, while whatever neither filter covers comes from the centred view so the picture at rest is exactly itself. Lean in with the pointer and the channels part in proportion to depth (the near reeds fringe the most, the far sky not at all) as near and far slide against each other and the card leans a few degrees under a soft glare, the tilt following on springs.glide's constants and returning on springs.drift's. A press toggles glasses mode, folding the split shut on springs.snap so only the parallax remains; it is a real toggle button, Enter or Space toggles, arrow keys hold a tilt, and Escape or Home levels the card.

props.name: children
props.description: The caption under the picture.

props.name: src
props.description: A picture of your own (same origin, or served with CORS); defaults to a lake at dusk drawn in code.

props.name: depthSrc
props.description: Its depth map, white near and black far. Without one, depth runs from far at the top to near at the bottom.

props.name: alt
props.defaultValue: "A lake below pine ridges at dusk"
props.description: What the picture shows, for assistive technology.

props.name: depth
props.description: How far the channels part at full tilt, 0 to 1.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far the card leans toward the pointer, 0 (flat) to 1.

props.name: channels
props.description: The two filter colours.

props.name: channelColors
props.description: Two filter colours of your own, left eye then right; overrides channels.

props.name: parallax
props.description: How far near and far slide against each other as you tilt, 0 to 1.

props.name: convergence
props.description: The depth that stays put while the rest slides, 0 (far) to 1 (near).

props.name: pressed / defaultPressed
props.description: Glasses mode, controlled or initial: the colours folded back into one, only the parallax left.

props.name: onPressedChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that toggled glasses mode, with the new state.

props.name: glare
props.description: A soft glare that slides across the glass as it leans.

props.name: preview
props.description: Lean once when the card first comes into view, so its depth shows before anyone touches it.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The toggle's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the picture but takes no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the card; the picture keeps 16:9 above the caption.

usageNotes: The picture is a native button with aria-pressed, named by label and described by the alt text and a hint. Arrow keys hold a tilt so the split can be seen without a pointer; Escape (handled, so a surrounding dialog stays open) and Home level the card.
Mouse and pen tilt on hover; touch tilts with a horizontal drag (touch-action: pan-y keeps vertical scrolling) and a tap toggles glasses mode.
Under reduced motion there is no lean and no glare travel; the split still follows the tilt, because it is the information, with a short fade instead of a spring, and the glasses fold is a fade too.

One fullscreen-triangle pass drawn on demand: only while the tilt or the fold moves, and never off screen or in a hidden tab. Textures are uploaded once per size and theme; context loss shows the still picture and rebuilds on restore, and without WebGL2 the drawn picture stays as a still image.

Filter colours are optics and stay pure on every page; the drawn scene's palette is mixed from tokens and re-read when the theme changes. A src image must be same-origin or served with CORS for the GPU to read it; otherwise the drawn scene stays.

items.title: Condenser Coil
items.tagline: Light poured through a run of glass coil.
items.description: A run of clear glass tubing coiled like a condenser, drawn in Canvas 2D, with liquid light flowing through it as segmented flow: seeded slugs parted by gas gaps, small bubbles swaying across the bore as they ride, and the light glowing brighter wherever the coil doubles back on itself (a fold weight found once per shape). The pointer warms the glass, quickening the flow and raising bubbles at the warm spot; a click sends one bright slug through the whole run that launches with a flick, flashes every crossing and leaves the outlet in a flare that blooms with the springs.recoil overshoot. The keyboard's way in is a button behind the content: Enter or Space sends a slug, arrow keys move a warm hand along the glass, Escape lifts it.

props.name: flow
props.description: How fast the liquid runs, 0 (a slow seep) to 1 (a brisk run); a sent slug runs faster with it too.

props.name: bubbles
props.description: How many small bubbles ride in the slugs, 0 to 40.

props.name: hue
props.description: The liquid light's hue, 0 to 360, held at a fixed lightness for each theme.

props.name: path
props.description: The coil as an SVG path; it is fitted inside the box with its aspect kept. Defaults to a horizontal coil that fits the box.

props.name: viewBox
props.description: The coordinate box `path` was drawn in, so the server can show it before the canvas paints.

props.name: turns
props.description: Loops in the generated coil, 2 to 16. Defaults to about one for every 64 px of width.

props.name: tubeWidth
props.description: The tube's outer width, in px, 6 to 18.

props.name: glow
props.description: How much brighter the light runs where the coil doubles back on itself, 0 to 1.

props.name: warmth
props.description: How strongly the pointer warms the glass: the flow it adds and the bubbles it raises, 0 to 1.

props.name: warmColor
props.description: The colour warm glass takes on, any CSS colour.

props.name: glassColor
props.description: The glass's colour, any CSS colour; resolved on the element so it follows the theme.

props.name: children
props.description: Content above the coil: a caption, a heading, a call to action.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and keys warm the glass and send slugs.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the liquid where it stands; a sent slug still runs.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the coil for assistive technology.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the slugs' lengths and where the bubbles ride.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Fires when a bright slug is sent, from the click or key that sent it.

props.name: onArrive
props.description: Fires when a bright slug leaves the outlet, with how many have run through.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the coil flowing but takes no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the coil is one focus stop (a button behind your content). Enter or Space sends a bright slug; arrow keys move a warm hand along the glass (Shift moves three times as far); Escape lifts it. Pointer clicks and taps send a slug too, and up to six can run at once.
Reduced motion: the train stands still mid-run and warmth shows in place; a send lights the whole run at once and fades over 600 ms, so the press is still answered.

Performance: the glass is cached in two layers and only the liquid is drawn per frame; the loop runs only while the coil is on screen, the tab is visible and something moves, and stops when paused and settled. The canvas caps its pixel ratio at `dpr`.

Theming: glass follows `glassColor` (the foreground token by default) and re-reads it when the theme changes; the liquid takes `hue` at a lightness tuned for each theme, glowing by adding light on dark pages and by deepening on light ones.

Pass any SVG `path` to lay the tubing your own way; it is fitted inside the box with its aspect kept, and its own crossings glow. Give `viewBox` too if you want the server to show it before the canvas paints.

items.title: Corner Tide
items.tagline: Soft squares rounding and squaring in a tide.
items.description: A centred grid of glowing tiles drawn per pixel in one WebGL2 pass, each a superellipse whose corner exponent rides a slow travelling field of two crossing waves, so bands of tiles soften toward circles and sharpen back toward squares while keeping their size, each lit from within by a round core and a halo summed over its neighbours. The pointer pushes its own rounded patch through the grid, following on springs.glide and swelling in on springs.drift; a click sends a squaring ripple outward and each tile it passes rings back with the springs.recoil damping ratio, its core flashing as it squares. The keyboard's way in is a button behind the content: arrow keys move the patch a tile at a time, Enter or Space sends a ripple from it, Escape lifts it.

props.name: minExponent
props.description: How round the roundest tiles get: the corner exponent in the trough, 1.2 to 4 (2 is a circle).

props.name: gap

props.name: glow

props.name: cell

props.name: colors

props.name: tide

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the tide travels, 0 to 1.

props.name: patchRadius
props.description: The reach of the pointer's rounded patch, in px.

props.name: rippleSpeed
props.description: How fast a squaring ripple travels outward, in px per second.

props.name: children
props.description: Content above the tiles: a hero line, a heading, a call to action.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and keys push the patch and send ripples.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the tide where it is; the patch and ripples still answer.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the grid for assistive technology.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the tide's directions and phases, so two grids never swing alike.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onRipple
props.description: Fires when a ripple is sent, with its origin in px from the box's top left.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the tide but takes no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the grid is one focus stop (a button behind your content). On focus the patch lands on the middle tile; arrow keys move it a tile at a time, Enter or Space sends a ripple from it, Escape lifts it. A click or tap sends a ripple from where it lands.
Reduced motion: the tide is frozen in one designed swing, the patch moves without easing, and a ripple squares the tiles near it at once and lets them ease back over half a second without travelling.

Performance: one fragment pass with four superellipse lookups a pixel; the loop runs only while the grid is on screen, the tab is visible and the tide, the patch or a ripple is moving. Paused with nothing moving, it draws nothing.

Theming: `colors` are resolved on the element and re-read when the theme changes; two colours meet through their oklch midpoint so the grid never greys in the middle. Halos add light on dark pages and soften to a tint on light ones.
Content passed as children sits above the tiles and stays fully interactive; the tiles never take its clicks.

items.title: Pastel Band
items.tagline: A ribbon of chalk pastel on dark, toothy paper.
items.description: A broad ribbon of colour waving across dark pastel paper, drawn per pixel in one WebGL2 pass: the paper has real tooth (fine grain, a felted scale and a faint honeycomb) and pigment lands only where the stick's pressure reaches past it, so the core is dense and the edges grainy, the sticks lie side by side and the grain picks between them where they meet, and diagonal strokes are laid afresh several times a second while the ribbon itself moves smoothly. The pointer bends the ribbon toward it, the pull following on springs.glide and letting go on springs.drift; a drag smudges the pastel softer along its path until fresh strokes replace it, and the first sighting lays the ribbon on from left to right on the enter easing. The keyboard's way in is a button behind the content: arrow keys move a hand that bends the ribbon, Shift with the arrows smudges, Enter or Space smudges where the hand is, Escape lifts it.

props.name: width

props.name: palette

props.name: colors

props.name: paperColor

props.name: wave

props.name: speed

props.name: boil

props.name: bend
props.description: How far the ribbon bends toward the pointer, 0 to 1.

props.name: smudge

props.name: fade

props.name: grain

props.name: children

props.name: intro

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and keys bend and smudge the ribbon.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the ribbon and its strokes still; bending and smudging still answer.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the sheet for assistive technology.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the waves and the strokes, so two sheets never match.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onSmudge
props.description: Fires when a smudge is made, from the drag or key that made it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the ribbon but takes no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the sheet is one focus stop (a button behind your content). On focus a small ring marks your hand on the ribbon; arrow keys move it and bend the ribbon toward it, Shift with the arrows smudges as you go, Enter or Space smudges a short stroke where it is, Escape lifts it. Touch drags across the ribbon smudge; vertical swipes still scroll the page.
Reduced motion: the ribbon stands still in one designed wave, the strokes never boil and there is no intro; bends are drawn at once and smudges give way in still steps every 1.6 seconds.

Performance: one fragment pass at three quarters of the capped pixel ratio (the grain is drawn in CSS px, so it never shrinks). The loop runs only while the sheet is on screen, the tab is visible and something moves; with speed at 0 it draws only when the strokes boil. The smudge map is a quarter-size canvas uploaded only while smudges are fading.

Theming: the paper is a fixed dark sheet and the palettes are pigments at fixed lightness, so the sheet looks the same on light and dark pages; give its caption the dark theme (as the demo does) so the text stays light.
No WebGL2, or a lost context: the server's still ribbon shows instead, a gradient band with grain-broken edges.

items.title: Bullseye Panes
items.tagline: A view broken into old crown-glass roundels.
items.description: A view seen through a leaded window of bullseye glass, drawn per pixel in one WebGL2 pass: roundels in hexagonal rows, each spun crown glass that is thick at its centre with a pontil knob that turns its piece of the view over, swirled so the picture twists toward the middle, magnified there, rippled by spiral ridges and fringed with colour, between flatter quarries and rounded lead cames that each carry one thin highlight. The view drifts slowly behind the glass (a garden painted in code that wraps, or your own image or video), and the pointer shifts the viewpoint on springs.glide so the thick centres move most and every swirl turns with the hand; it returns, and the first sighting swings in, on springs.drift. The keyboard's way in is a button behind the content: arrow keys shift the viewpoint, Enter, Space or Escape bring it back to centre.

props.name: roundels

props.name: swirl
props.description: How hard each disc is swirled, 0 (plain lenses) to 1 (the view twists half a turn toward the middle).

props.name: lead

props.name: src
props.description: The view behind the glass: an image or video URL. A cross-origin file must allow CORS. Defaults to a garden painted in code.

props.name: kind

props.name: alt

props.name: magnify
props.description: How much the thick centres magnify, 0 to 1.

props.name: tint

props.name: leadColor
props.description: The cames' colour, any CSS colour.

props.name: drift

props.name: parallax

props.name: children

props.description: The first time the window is seen, the viewpoint swings in from the side and every swirl turns into place.

props.name: interactive

props.description: Names the window for assistive technology.

props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the window is one focus stop (a button behind your content), described by `alt`. Arrow keys shift the viewpoint a quarter of its reach per press; Enter, Space or Escape bring it back to centre and announce it. Touch drags shift the view and let go when the finger lifts; vertical swipes still scroll.
Reduced motion: nothing drifts and there is no intro; the viewpoint moves straight to where it is sent and a video holds its first frame.

Performance: one fragment pass with three texture reads a pixel. The loop runs only while the window is on screen, the tab is visible and the view drifts, the viewpoint eases or a video plays; a video plays only while seen and pauses off screen.
Your own `src`: images and videos are cover-fitted with room to swing behind the glass. A cross-origin file must be served with CORS, or the window shows the painted garden instead of failing.
No WebGL2, or a lost context: a CSS window stands in, the same view behind rows of gradient roundels sized with container units to match the count.

items.title: Colonnade Pass
items.tagline: Light and shadow strobing as you walk past columns.
items.description: A walk along a sunlit cloister, ray-cast per pixel in one WebGL2 pass: fluted columns down the left with a lawn court beyond, a coffered ceiling, a paved walk and a wall with arched doors, and the sun's light coming in between the columns to lay bars of light and shade across the floor and up the wall, each shadow's penumbra widening with the distance to the column that casts it, faint shafts in the air and the eye adjusting as you pass from sun to shade. You walk at `pace` (and with `scroll`, with the nearest scroll container), the near columns sweeping past while the far ones creep; the pointer moves the sun, across for its angle so the bars lean and up and down for its height so they lengthen, following on springs.glide, and the first sighting swings the sun in from the far side on springs.drift. It is a slider: arrows, Page Up and Down, Home and End move the sun's angle, Up and Down its height.

props.name: columns

props.name: sunAngle

props.name: pace
props.description: How fast you walk past the columns, in metres a second, 0 (standing) to 2.5.

props.name: value
props.description: The sun's angle when you control it, in degrees; pair with `onValueChange`.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the pointer or the keys that moved the sun, with its new angle in degrees.

props.name: sunHeight
props.description: The sun's height above the horizon where it starts, 12° to 65°; lower suns lay longer bars.

props.name: softness
props.description: How soft the shadows' edges are, 0 (a crisp noon sun) to 1 (thin cloud).

props.name: haze
props.description: How much the air inside the portico glows where the sun gets through, 0 to 1.

props.name: scroll
props.description: Walk with the nearest scroll container as well as on your own.

props.name: stoneColor
props.description: The stone's colour, any CSS colour. Pigment: daylight reads the same in either theme.

props.name: sunColor
props.description: The sunlight's colour, any CSS colour.

props.name: skyColor
props.description: The sky's colour, which also fills the shade, any CSS colour.

props.name: children
props.description: Content above the scene: a hero line, a heading, a call to action.

props.name: intro
props.description: The first time the colonnade is seen, the sun swings in from the far side and the bars sweep into place.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and keys move the sun.

props.name: paused
props.description: Stand still; the sun still answers.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the sun control for assistive technology.

props.name: dpr

props.name: disabled

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the sun is a slider and the scene's one focus stop. Left and Right move its angle 2°, Page Up and Down 10°, Home and End to the ends; Up and Down raise and lower it 3°. Its value text says which way the bars lean.

The walk plays on its own: give people a way to stop it with `paused` (the demo's Stop walking button) when it sits beside reading. Under reduced motion you stand still between two columns, there is no intro and the sun moves at once.

Performance: one fragment pass with eight haze samples a pixel. The loop runs only while the scene is on screen, the tab is visible and you are walking or the sun is easing; at pace 0 with the sun settled it draws nothing, and scroll walking redraws only on scroll.
Theming: stone, sun and sky are pigments, so the picture of daylight is the same on light and dark pages; restyle it with `stoneColor`, `sunColor` and `skyColor`.
No WebGL2, or a lost context: a CSS still of the walk stands in, with the wall striped by light and the floor's bars leaning with `sunAngle`.

items.title: Smoke Tunnel
items.tagline: Smoke lines streaming past a shape you can turn.
items.description: A wind tunnel's test section in Canvas 2D with threads of smoke streaming past a wing model: the flow is real potential flow around a Joukowski aerofoil with the Kutta circulation, solved in closed form, so the smoke divides at the stagnation point, hugs the upper surface and leaves the trailing edge smoothly, and puffs released together at the rake are drawn by the time smoke takes to reach each point, so the ones over the top race ahead. From the tip a tube of haze peels away with two filaments and dust spiralling through it, wound tighter the more lift the wing makes. Drag the wing (its leading edge follows the finger 1:1) or use the keys; release projects the throw and the model locks on with springs.snap, and past the stall angle the threads leave the surface and tumble on curl noise, eddies roll off the separation point and the model buffets. It is a slider: arrows step a degree, Page Up and Down five, Home and End go to the ends, and crossing the stall is announced.

props.name: flow
props.description: The tunnel's speed, 0 (a slow drift) to 1 (a brisk run): the puffs, the dust and the turbulence.

props.name: angle

props.name: smoke
props.description: How much smoke the rake lets out, 0 (a few faint threads) to 1 (many dense ones).

props.name: value
props.description: The wing's angle when you control it, in degrees; pair with `onValueChange`.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drag or the keys that turned the wing, with its new angle in degrees.

props.name: minAngle

props.name: maxAngle
props.description: The highest angle the wing turns to, in degrees.

props.name: stallAngle
props.description: The angle past which the flow over the top lets go and the smoke tumbles, in degrees.

props.name: camber

props.name: thickness

props.name: vortex
props.description: How strongly the tube of haze winds off the tip, 0 (none) to 1.

props.name: smokeColor
props.description: The smoke's colour, any CSS colour; resolved on the element so it follows the theme.

props.name: modelColor
props.description: The model's colour, any CSS colour.

props.name: children
props.description: Content above the tunnel: a caption, a heading, a call to action.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The drag and keys turn the wing.

props.name: paused
props.description: Stop the smoke where it is; the wing still turns.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the wing's angle control for assistive technology.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the turbulence and the dust, so two tunnels never tumble alike.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onStallChange
props.description: Fires when the flow stalls (true) or attaches again (false), from the drag or keys that caused it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the tunnel running but takes no input.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the wing's angle is a slider and the tunnel's one focus stop. Up and Right raise the nose a degree, Down and Left lower it, Page Up and Down move five, Home and End go to `minAngle` and `maxAngle`; its value text and a polite status say when the flow stalls and when it attaches again. Touch drags turn the wing vertically; horizontal swipes still scroll.

Reduced motion: the threads stand steady with their puffs held in place, the tip's tube and its dust are still and there is no buffet; a stalled wing still shows its tumbled smoke, frozen at one moment, because the stall is information.

Performance: the streamlines are re-traced only while the wing turns (a closed-form field, no simulation); otherwise each frame restrokes cached threads and stamps the puffs. The loop runs only while the tunnel is on screen, the tab is visible and the smoke flows or the wing settles; paused and settled it stops.
Theming: smoke follows `smokeColor` (the foreground token) and the model `modelColor`, both re-read when the theme changes, so the tunnel is white smoke on a dark page and ink on a light one.
Set `stallAngle`, `camber` and `thickness` to match the section you are showing; the flow pattern, the lift that winds the tip's tube and the puffs' race over the top all follow from them.

items.title: Root Exchange
items.tagline: One hub feeding many, in pulses you can read.
items.description: A hub feeding a ring of nodes through fine, root-like paths: neighbours share a trunk that forks half way, each trunk as thick as the flow it carries, and pulses of light leave the hub along every route at that node's share of the total, so the busy ones visibly draw more. Hovering or tabbing to a node lights its route and shows its label, value and share in a tag that rises on springs.snap; a press reverses its flow, the route's direction springing through zero on springs.snap so pulses already in flight slow, stop and run home while the node kicks on springs.recoil and its chevron turns. Arrow keys walk the ring and Enter or Space reverses the focused node.

props.name: nodes
props.type: { id: string; label: string; value: number }[]
props.description: The nodes the hub feeds; each value's share of the total sets its pulse rate and its route's thickness.

props.name: hubLabel
props.description: What the hub is, for its accessible name and announcements.

props.name: format
props.description: Prints a node's value in its tag and accessible name.

props.name: reversed / defaultReversed

props.name: onReversedChange
props.description: Fires from the press that reversed or restored a node, with the new ids.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires when hover or keyboard focus brings a node forward, or lets it go.

props.name: pulseRate
props.description: Pulses a second leaving the hub in all, shared out by value.

props.name: travel
props.description: Time for a pulse to cross an average route, ms; every pulse moves at the same speed in pixels.

props.name: curve
props.description: How far the roots wander off a straight line, 0 (schematic) to 1 (gnarled).

props.name: rootlets
props.description: How many hair-fine side rootlets the routes shed, 0 to 1.

props.name: palette
props.description: The colourway, from the theme's tokens.

props.name: colors
props.type: { route?: string; pulse?: string; hub?: string }

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds where the nodes sit and how the roots wander.

props.name: paused
props.description: Freezes the pulses where they are.

props.name: dpr

props.name: label
props.description: The node group's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nodes cannot be focused or reversed; the flow still runs.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the nodes are one tab stop with a roving focus. Arrow keys walk the ring in order, Home and End jump, Enter or Space reverses the focused node (aria-pressed), and the change is announced once from the press that caused it.
The layout is measured from the box and seeded, so server and client draw the same roots; the pulses live on a Canvas 2D layer with a fixed pool and pre-sampled routes, nothing allocated per frame.
The pulse loop runs only while the box is on screen, the page is visible, the piece is not paused and motion is allowed; the canvas's device pixel ratio is capped at 2.
Under reduced motion each route carries still beads graded toward where it flows and a chevron, and a reversal flips them at once with no kick.
Palettes are token colours (cobalt, signal, amber, ink) and read on light and dark pages; on a dark page the pulses add light, on a light one they stay the hue.

items.title: Ice Cube
items.tagline: A melting cube that bends what it slides over.
items.description: A clear ice cube slides across a picture after the pointer on a per-frame glide spring, turning with the curve of its slide, and bends the picture per pixel in one WebGL2 pass: bevelled facets displace it, the top magnifies it through frosted cracks and a cloudy core, a cold highlight runs along the top edge and a pale shadow holds a bright caustic. Sliding melts it — it shrinks, rounds and softens and lays meltwater into a ping-pong field that bends the picture too before it dries — and a click drops a fresh cube that lands on springs.recoil with a splash. Keyboard focus on anything inside parks the cube on it, and a drop button that appears on focus takes Enter or Space.

props.name: refraction

props.name: frost

props.name: tint

props.name: rest

props.name: interactive

props.name: paused

props.name: dpr

props.name: onMelted

props.name: disabled

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: focusing anything inside the box (Tab) parks the cube on it; after the children, a Drop a fresh cube button appears on focus and Enter or Space drops one where the cube is, announced once.

The children sit above the picture and stay fully interactive; clicks on links and buttons never drop a cube, and touch follows only while the finger is down (touch-action pan-y keeps vertical scrolling).

The draw loop runs only while something changes — the cube sliding, a landing, water drying — and only on screen on a visible page; at rest it stops. Water is a quarter-resolution field and the canvas's device pixel ratio is capped at 2.
Without WebGL2, after a lost context, or with a cross-origin picture that has no CORS, the picture stays plain and a glassy drawn cube still slides and drops.
Under reduced motion the cube rests still and refracting at rest, does not melt or leave water, and focus or a click moves it at once with no fall.
The drawn cloth takes its colours from the theme, so it is light gingham on a light page and a dark one on a dark page; pass image.src for your own picture.

items.title: Catseye Marble
items.tagline: Roll a glass marble and watch its ribbon turn.
items.description: A glass marble in a felt tray, ray traced per pixel in one WebGL2 pass: the studio reflected by Fresnel with a highlight as sharp as gloss, three twisted vanes found by marching the refracted ray, the felt seen magnified and flipped through the far side, and on the felt a soft shadow holding a ribbon-tinted caustic. Drag it and it follows 1:1 with its orientation integrated as true rolling, so the ribbon turns the way a real marble's does; released, it coasts on rolling friction, bounces off the wall with a soft clack and settles. Arrow keys nudge it with the same physics and Home rolls it back on springs.glide.

props.name: tint

props.name: table

usageNotes: Keyboard: the tray is one button. Arrow keys nudge the marble (Shift harder) so it rolls, coasts and bounces like a throw; Home rolls it back; when it settles after a key the tray says Resting. once.
Pointer and touch: drag anywhere to roll it 1:1 (the tray is touch-action none, so a finger rolls rather than scrolls); a tap on the glass flicks it away from the finger.
It draws only while the marble moves and once on mount, resize and theme change; the loop stops at rest, off screen and on a hidden page. The canvas's device pixel ratio is capped at 2.
Without WebGL2 or after a lost context, a drawn marble with gradients and a turning ribbon still drags, coasts and bounces.
Under reduced motion a drag still rolls it 1:1 but it stops on release, the keys step it 24 px at once and Home places it back.
The ribbon colours are fixed lightnesses of the theme's hues and the felt follows the theme's surface, so it reads on light and dark pages.

items.title: Event Lens
items.tagline: A dark mass that bends your headline into rings.
items.description: A black hole on a real headline: the browser lays out the words, each word is painted into a texture where it was set, and one WebGL2 pass lenses that picture through the point-lens equation, so the words behind the mass bend into arcs, a flipped image appears inside the Einstein radius and whatever is right behind becomes a ring round the shadow, swirled by spin, with a thin smoky accretion disc and a bright photon edge. Drag it and it follows 1:1 while its disc flares on springs.flick; release and it drifts back to rest on springs.drift carrying the throw. Arrow keys move it on springs.glide and Escape, Enter or Home let it drift home.

The headline is a real heading, always in the accessibility tree: it turns transparent, not hidden, while its lensed copy is drawn beneath it, and the words are repainted on resize, font load and theme change.
The pass draws while the mass moves or the disc turns, only on screen on a visible page and never when paused; the canvas's device pixel ratio is capped at 2.

Without WebGL2, after a lost context or with a cross-origin picture that has no CORS, the headline shows plainly with a drawn mass — shadow, photon ring and tilted disc — that still drags and drifts home.
Under reduced motion the disc is still, a drag still moves the mass 1:1 and it returns to rest at once on release; the keys step it at once.

items.title: Gel Scroller
items.tagline: Soft beams rolling through colour like stage gels.
items.description: A stage seen from the house: floor lamps throw soft washes up a cyc through drifting haze, each behind a gel scroller whose strip of taped gels rolls past the lens, so the seam between two gels travels up the beam and, with no cue held, colour chases along the row. Hovering previews the cue under the pointer and a click takes it: every strip rolls the shortest way round on a spring with the springs.snap constants capped at the motor's speed, running through the gels between and braking onto the frame together with one crisp overshoot. The cue rail is a radiogroup — arrows, Home and End take cues and Escape lets the strips roll free.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the stage.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the cue rail along the top is a radiogroup with one tab stop. Arrow keys, Home and End take a cue as they move, Escape lets the strips roll free (and is handled, so a surrounding dialog stays open); the held cue is announced once.
Pointer: the stage is divided into one zone per cue; hovering previews that cue, a click or tap takes it, and clicking the held cue again lets go. Touch keeps vertical scrolling (touch-action pan-y).
The haze is ambient: the pass runs at half resolution and only while the stage is on screen, the page is visible and it is not paused; the canvas's device pixel ratio is capped at 2.
Without WebGL2 or after a lost context the washes are blurred CSS gradients whose colours still follow the strips at the lamps.
Under reduced motion nothing chases and the haze is still; taking a cue cross-fades every wash to it in 240 ms, never rolling through the gels between.

items.title: Desk Spike
items.tagline: Notes on a spike; tear off the top to read on.
items.description: A desk spike with notes impaled on it, seen at a three-quarter angle in real CSS 3D: a heavy base, a steel needle drawn from the top slip's hole to its point, and paper slips from data turned a little about it, each curled at a corner. A click or Space tears the top slip off — it tugs up on springs.flick, slides up the needle and rips over the point, its hole tearing ragged, then flutters away on the exit ease to reveal the next — and Backspace brings the last one back over the point and down the needle to land on springs.recoil. An empty spike refills in a cascade on the next click.

props.name: slips
props.type: "orders" | "messages" | "wire" | "receipts" | { id: string; kind?: string; title: string; lines?: string[]; meta?: string; stamp?: string }[]
props.description: The notes on the spike, top first: a preset or your own (up to nine).

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far the slips turn about the needle, 0 (squared up) to 1 (a loose pile).

props.name: paperTone
props.description: The paper: white, canary, pink, or the three carbon copies in turn.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: How many slips are torn off the top, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the click or key that tore off, put back or refilled, with the new count.

props.name: onTear
props.description: Fires when a slip is torn off, with the slip.

props.name: onRestore
props.description: Fires when a slip goes back on the spike, with the slip.

props.name: curl
props.description: How far each slip's corner curls up, 0 to 1.

props.name: angle
props.description: How far the desk tips away from you, degrees, 20 to 50.

props.name: ink
props.description: The print's colour, any CSS colour.

props.name: refill
props.description: A click on the empty spike puts every slip back.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds each slip's turn, flight and torn hole.

props.name: sound
props.description: A paper rip when a slip tears free, and a soft one when it lands. Off unless asked for.

props.name: label
props.description: The spike's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing tears.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the scene.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the spike is one button named for the top slip. Space or Enter tears it off, Backspace puts the last one back, and on an empty spike Space or Enter refills it; each change is announced once with how many slips are left.
The top slip's text is real text in an article; the slips beneath and the torn ones are hidden from assistive technology until they are on top.
Pure DOM and CSS 3D transforms driven by one progress value per slip: nothing runs at rest, and every tear, put-back and refill finishes cleanly if it is interrupted.
Under reduced motion there is no tug, flight or landing: slips fade out and back in, and the torn holes and the count still change.
Paper and ink are fixed pigments of the theme's hues, so the notes read the same on light and dark pages; pass your own slips for tickets, messages or receipts.

items.title: Flambe Pan
items.tagline: Tip the pan and the flames flare off its edge.
items.description: A copper pan on a dark range, held by its handle: a drag follows the hand 1:1, up to tip the far lip toward the gas and sideways to slide it over the grate, and a release sets it back level on springs.glide with the throw's velocity. When the lip dips past the catch angle the spirit catches, a front of fire running across the sauce from the low lip, and additive tongues of flame flare up, leaning with the tilt and trailing the pan through the air while the room takes their light; a quick shake gusts them higher before they burn down to a few blue licks and go out. Enter or Space tosses the pan (a tip on springs.snap and back on glide) when it is out and shakes it while it burns.

props.name: height
props.description: How tall the flare stands, as a share of the room above the pan, 0.2 to 1.

props.name: gust
props.description: How much a quick shake feeds the flames, 0 to 1.

props.name: hue
props.description: The flame's OKLCH hue at fixed lightness: 52 brandy orange, 30 deep red, 80 gold, 140 copper green.

props.name: burnTime
props.description: Seconds the spirit burns before the last blue lick goes out, 1 to 8.

props.name: catchAngle
props.description: Degrees the far lip must dip before it catches, 6 to 24.

props.name: maxTilt
props.description: The furthest the pan tips before it rubber-bands, 16 to 40 degrees.

props.name: lean
props.description: How far the tongues lean with the tilt and trail the pan's motion, 0 to 1.

props.name: density
props.description: How full the flame is, 0.3 (a few tongues) to 1 (a dense sheet).

props.name: metal
props.description: The pan's metal.

props.name: rangeColor
props.description: The cooktop's colour.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the pan tips itself once to show the flare (silently): first seen, at mount, or never.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the flare when the visitor catches the spirit or gusts it with a shake.

props.name: onFlameChange
props.description: Fires when the flame catches, burns down to blue licks, or goes out.

props.name: label
props.description: The scene's accessible name.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the flame still where it is; the pan can still be moved.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No tipping, tossing or shaking.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the flame's tongues.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: children
props.description: Overlay content drawn above the scene; it never takes the pointer.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root; give it a size (the demo uses aspect-[16/10]).

usageNotes: Keyboard: the scene is one role=button described by a hint. Enter or Space tosses the pan past the catch and back when the flame is out or low, and shakes it (three quick slides that gust the flame) while it flares: the same end states as a drag. A polite live region says Flaring, Burning down to blue licks, and Out.
Touch: the drag is two-dimensional (tilt and slide), so the scene sets touch-action: none; a tap tosses the pan like Enter.

Reduced motion: the pan follows the hand without springs and is set level at once; a catch shows a still, seeded flame that is redrawn smaller in calm steps as it burns down, and the room's light still comes up. Feedback stays, motion goes.

Performance: one Canvas 2D layer at a capped pixel ratio, sprites pre-rendered once per hue, particles in preallocated typed arrays. The loop runs only on screen, in a visible tab and while something burns or moves; out and level, it stops.
Sound only answers the visitor: the automatic first toss (trigger) is silent, and the flare plays only when sound is on and the visitor's own tip or shake caused it.
The scene is drawn in fixed pigments (a dark range and copper), so it reads the same on light and dark pages.

items.title: Mitre Joint
items.tagline: Four lengths of frame meet at the corners.
items.description: A border for any content built like a picture frame: four lengths of moulding with mitred ends, each shaded across its own width by a flat, cove or gilt profile so a real seam shows where two meet. When first seen the lengths slide in from beyond their edges on springs.glide a stagger apart; as the last one seats the corners click, the frame settling on springs.flick with the seams flashing, and a crisp glow runs once round the bevel from the top-left corner both ways before it settles to a quiet sheen. Hover, or keyboard focus inside the content, lifts the frame on glide and turns the light toward the pointer, the lengths facing it brightening and a highlight sliding along the moulding.

props.name: children
props.description: The content inside the frame; it keeps its own semantics and focus.

props.name: profile
props.description: The moulding's profile: a flat lacquered rail, a walnut cove, or gilt with beads.

props.name: bevel
props.description: The moulding's width in px, 6 to 28.

props.name: glow
props.description: The light that runs along the bevel once the corners meet: a preset or any CSS colour.

props.name: color
props.description: The moulding's colour: the page's ink (flat), walnut (cove) or gold leaf (gilt) unless set.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the frame assembles: first seen, at mount, or only when assembled says so.

props.name: assembled
props.description: Controls the frame: true slides the lengths in, false takes them apart. Undefined lets trigger decide.

props.name: once
props.description: Assemble only the first time it is seen; false assembles again on every return.

props.name: delay
props.description: Wait before the first length moves, ms.

props.name: stagger
props.description: Time between the four lengths setting off, ms, 0 to 150.

props.name: onAssembled
props.description: Fires when the last corner clicks home.

props.name: lift
props.description: How far hover or focus inside lifts the frame, px, 0 to 6 (the shadow stays inside the root).

props.name: highlight
props.description: Strength of the highlight that follows the pointer along the moulding, 0 to 1.

props.name: sheen
props.description: The quiet sheen the glow settles to, 0 to 1.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Hover and focus lift the frame and move its light.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the click when the corners meet, only when the visitor's own action assembled it.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root (width, margins).

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Classes for the opening that holds the content (padding, background).

usageNotes: The frame is decoration: every painted layer is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none, so links, buttons and fields inside keep their own semantics, tab order and clicks. Keyboard focus inside (focus-visible) lifts the frame like hover and parks the highlight on the edge nearest the focused element.

Reduced motion: the frame fades in already assembled with no slide, settle or glow run, the sheen fades up instead, and nothing lifts; the light still turns toward the pointer because it is colour, not travel.

Performance: four clipped divs and motion values, no canvas and no loop. The glow is an SVG drawn only while it runs, measured with a ResizeObserver; geometry is calc() on a CSS variable, so any size works.
Sound only answers the visitor: an automatic assembly (in view, at mount) is silent; the click plays when sound is on and assembled flipped to true right after a click or key press.
