props.name: captions
props.description: Small name plates under the windows.

props.name: sound
props.description: A soft clack as the wheels cross each rail joint, after a visitor's drag, flick or key.

props.name: label
props.description: The carousel's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No moving.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the carriage; it fills its parent by default.

usageNotes: The root is a labelled carousel (role group, aria-roledescription carousel) and the one tab stop: Left and Right (or Up and Down) step a window, Home and End go to the ends, and a click on a window brings it to the middle. Each window is a slide labelled "3 of 6: Pine valley" holding its view as an image named by alt, and a polite live region announces the window that arrives.
Touch keeps vertical scrolling (touch-action: pan-y); a horizontal drag moves the carriage 1:1, rubber-bands past either end and is projected on release.
Under reduced motion the carriage still follows a drag, but a release or key moves it on a 150 ms tween with no jolt, no wheel spin and no sliding reflection; the parallax holds as geometry.

Everything per frame is a motion value: the carriage's x, the body's jolt, the wheels' turn and each view's offset (a transform of x, rounded to 0.01 px), so nothing re-renders while it moves and nothing runs at rest.
Sound plays only for the visitor's own drag, flick, click or key, at most every 45 ms, panned to the wheel that crossed; a host changing value moves the carriage silently.

items.title: Dichroic Wall
items.tagline: Glass tiles that change colour as you move.
items.description: A wall of dichroic glass tiles whose colours are computed from thin-film interference: each tile passes one hue and reflects its complement, and both slide with the angle you see it from, so as the pointer (your eye) moves the tiles shift colour, the eye following on springs.glide. Each tile reads where you stood a moment ago in proportion to its distance, so a change rolls across the wall as a travelling wave, and the tiles are set slightly askew so neighbours never quite match; a click, Enter or Space flashes the wall white for a beat in a ring from the click. Arrow keys move the eye from a full-surface button under the content, Escape stands you back in the centre, and the first sight sweeps the eye across once on springs.drift.

props.name: children
props.description: Content on top of the glass: a headline, a caption card, a call to action.

props.name: tiles
props.description: How many tiles fit the wall's shorter side, 3 to 12: fewer rows make larger tiles.

props.name: shift
props.description: How far a tile's colour swings with the angle you see it from, 0 to 1.

props.name: gap
props.description: The grout between tiles, px, 0 to 12.

props.name: radius
props.description: A tile's corner radius, px.

props.name: askew

props.name: film

props.name: backlight
props.description: How much light comes through the glass rather than off it, 0 to 1: high shows the transmitted colours, low their complements.

props.name: waveSpeed
props.description: How fast a change of angle travels across the wall, tiles per second.

props.name: flash
props.description: How bright a click's flash is, 0 (no flash) to 1 (full white).

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and the keys move where you stand; off, the wall holds its view.

props.name: sweep
props.description: On first sight the eye crosses the wall once, so a wave of colour runs over it.

props.name: drift
props.description: With no pointer on it, the eye wanders slowly by itself (the wall never rests).

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the wall still: nothing animates until it is unpaused.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds every tile's film, turn and tilt.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the wall's surface button.

props.name: onFlash
props.description: Fires when a click, Enter or Space flashes the wall.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No pointer, keys or flash; the wall rests at its centre view.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: a full-surface button under the content is one tab stop. Arrow keys move where you stand (Shift for longer steps), Enter or Space flash the wall, Escape returns you to the centre; where you stand is announced politely. Keyboard focus on a control inside the content moves the eye to that control.

Reduced motion: the colours still follow the pointer and keys, but they change everywhere at once (no travelling wave), the first-sight sweep and drift are off, and the flash is a short even brightening rather than a ring.

Performance: one WebGL2 fullscreen pass; every tile's film, turn and tilt are hashed in the shader, so there are no textures. The loop runs only while the eye moves, a wave is in flight or a flash fades — and only on screen in a visible page. DPR is capped at 2 and resizes go through ResizeObserver.
Without WebGL2 (or after a lost context) a CSS still of the glass stays in place and turns its hue as you move, through one filter on one layer.

Theming: grout, the reflected room and the backlight resolve from tokens on the component's own element and are re-read when the theme changes; tile colours hold their lightness so the wall reads in light and dark.
Content in children stays fully interactive; a click on a control in it belongs to the control, a click anywhere else flashes the glass.

items.title: Buoy Tags
items.tagline: Labels that bob on the water and drift to you.
items.description: A tag picker floating on water: pill-shaped toggle buttons moored on slack lines ride a gently moving surface, a slow swell lifting and rocking one float after another while a small heightfield carries every ripple. The pointer makes a current, so the tags drift toward you within the slack of their moorings and bump softly into each other as capsules that trade momentum and spin, then drift home. Pressing a tag dunks it under the water and it comes back up on springs.recoil inside a splash ring that rocks its neighbours, selected or cleared; tags are real buttons in reading order, Enter and Space dunk them, and keyboard focus pulls the current to the focused tag.

props.name: tags
props.description: The tags on the water: { id, label, color? }.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The ids of the selected tags; controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the press or key that dunked a tag, with the new selection.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Several tags may be selected; off, choosing one clears the rest.

props.name: bob
props.description: How high the swell runs, 0 (flat calm) to 1: how much the tags bob and rock.

props.name: drift
props.description: How strongly the hand's current pulls the tags and how much slack their moorings give, 0 to 1.

props.name: depth
props.description: How deep the water is, 0 to 1: its colour, the length of the moorings, how far shadows fall and how long the swell runs.

props.name: moorings
props.description: Draw each tag's mooring line down into the water.

props.name: splash
props.description: How big a dunk's splash is, 0 to 1: the rings and the waves that rock the neighbours.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The hand (pointer or keyboard focus) makes a current the tags drift on.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the water and the tags still.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the swell and the moorings.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the plips of a dunk. Off unless asked for.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's accessible name.

props.name: onDunk
props.description: Fires when a tag is dunked, with its id.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No presses; the water lies still.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the water.

usageNotes: Keyboard: each tag is a toggle button (aria-pressed) in reading order inside a labelled group; Tab moves between them and Enter or Space dunks one through the same path as a press. Keyboard focus draws the current to the focused tag, and the new selection is announced politely ("Kelp selected. 3 selected.").
Reduced motion: the water lies still, the tags sit at home with no current or collisions, and a press swaps the selected look at once with a short opacity dip and a ring that fades in place.

Performance: one requestAnimationFrame loop runs the swell, the ripple grid (8px cells) and the tag physics, only on screen in a visible page; with bob at 0 it settles and stops. The water is shaded at grid resolution and scaled up smoothly onto one Canvas 2D layer, and tag positions go to motion values rather than React state.
Layout: homes come from a centred flex-wrap cluster measured on mount and on resize, so the tags wrap naturally at any width; give the component a height (className) that fits your tag count.

Theming: water, crests and lines resolve from tokens mixed into the page background on the component's own element and are re-read on theme change; floats use pigments at fixed lightness so they read in light and dark.

items.title: Night Facade
items.tagline: A building's windows lighting and dimming at night.
items.description: A tall apartment block at night whose small square windows each keep their own seeded schedule — warm lamps, blue screens, a kitchen's tube, the stairwell's fluorescent — so it runs from a busy early evening to a handful of night owls, while rooms go dark and light again, screens flicker and figures pass behind a few lit windows at the hour you leave it on. A rail down the right side is a vertical slider: dragging it moves the moon along its arc, deepens the sky and lets the windows answer one after another, each after its own short delay, before the thumb settles on the quarter hour on springs.snap. Up and Down move a step, Page Up and Page Down an hour, and Home and End go to 18:00 and 04:00.

props.name: hour / defaultHour
props.description: The hour, 18 (6 pm) to 28 (4 am), 24 being midnight; controlled or initial.

props.name: onHourChange
props.description: Fires from the drag or key that moved the night, with the new hour on the step.

props.name: floors
props.description: Floors of windows, 4 to 18.

props.name: columns
props.description: Windows across; by default as many as the width takes at the floor height.

props.name: warmth
props.description: Lamp colour, 0 (cool white) to 1 (deep tungsten amber).

props.name: step
props.description: Minutes the rail snaps to.

props.name: silhouettes
props.description: Figures pass behind a few lit windows now and then.

props.name: flicker
props.description: Screens flicker blue and the stairwell tube stutters.

props.name: beacon
props.description: The red light on the antenna blinks.

props.name: rail
props.description: Show the hour rail down the right side.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the building still: no flicker, no figures, no rooms changing.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds who lives where and their hours.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The picture's accessible name; the hour and lit count are added to it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The rail does not move.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the rail's thumb is a vertical slider (role="slider") whose value text reads the time and the lit count; Down and Up move a step the way the thumb moves, Page Down and Page Up an hour, Home and End 18:00 and 04:00. The picture is one image whose name carries the hour and the number of lit windows.

Reduced motion: nothing flickers, no figures pass, rooms do not come and go, the beacon holds steady and the moon steps rather than glides; windows still change with the hour by short cross-fades, because the hour is the information.

Performance: the architecture is server-rendered SVG with the windows lit for the first hour, so the first paint is finished. The light is one Canvas 2D layer drawn from pre-rendered sprites; ambient life runs at 24 frames a second, transitions at full rate, and nothing runs off screen, in a hidden page or while paused.
Controlled use: pass hour and onHourChange; a host that changes hour moves the night with the same spring a key does. clockOf(hour) is exported for printing the time the same way the rail does.
The night is drawn in fixed pigments, so it is the same scene in light and dark themes; give it a rounded border from your own tokens to seat it on the page.

items.title: Guest Pointers
items.tagline: Named pointers from a session, moving live.
items.description: A shared document visited by named collaborator pointers replaying recorded paths against its measured anchors: they glide, hover, drag-select words in their own colour, leave short chat bubbles and tick boxes or press buttons, each on a loop of its own. Positions arrive the way a network delivers them, as samples a few times a second, and the smoothing prop is a critically damped follower between them, from jumpy to buttery, with each name tag trailing its tip on springs.snap. Clicking a tag or a name in the presence toolbar follows that guest — the view zooms in and pans with them on a glide-stiff, critically damped camera and the frame takes their colour — and Escape (or the chip's button) goes back to the overview.

props.name: guests
props.description: Who might be here: { id, name, color?, steps? }, steps being the recorded path against the document's anchors.

props.name: count
props.description: How many of them are here, 1 to 5.

props.name: tagStyle
props.description: How a pointer's name is worn: a pill beside it, a flag at its tip, or initials.

props.name: smoothing
props.description: How the pointers glide between the samples the network delivers, 0 (jumps) to 1 (buttery, a little behind).

props.name: following / defaultFollowing
props.description: The guest the view follows, or null for the overview; controlled or initial.

props.name: onFollowingChange
props.description: Fires from the tag, button or Escape that started or stopped following.

props.name: speed
props.description: Replay speed, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: sampleRate
props.description: Samples a second the network delivers per pointer.

props.name: bubbles
props.description: Guests leave chat bubbles.

props.name: selections
props.description: Guests select text.

props.name: followZoom
props.description: Zoom while following; never less than the overview.

props.name: title
props.description: The document's title.

props.name: paused
props.description: Stop the replay where it is.

props.name: label
props.description: The view's accessible name.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the view.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the presence bar is a toolbar with roving focus — Left and Right (or Home and End) move between people, Enter or Space follows or stops following (aria-pressed), and Escape anywhere in the view stops following. Starting and stopping are announced politely. The tags on the pointers are pointer-only duplicates of those buttons.

Reduced motion: pointers step between the places they stop instead of gliding, the camera cuts to its target instead of panning, and bubbles fade; selections, presses and following still happen, because they are what the guests did.

Performance: one requestAnimationFrame loop drives the replay, the sample followers and the camera, only on screen in a visible page and not when paused. Positions go to motion values; React renders only on discrete events (a word selected, a bubble, a press).

Layout: the board lays itself out wide or tall to suit the view and is centred by CSS for the first paint; scripts address anchors (data-anchor ids such as "p1.11", "approve", "chart"), measured after layout, so they survive font and size changes. Near the right edge tags and bubbles hang to the left of the tip.
Theming: the board uses surface and ink tokens; guest colours are pigments at a fixed lightness dark enough for white type in either theme.

items.title: Mangle Press
items.tagline: Plain pages go in; printed results roll out.
items.description: A press seen from above: plain grey pages slide in from the left, are drawn under heavy steel rollers and come out on the right as finished results — a card, a chart, a poster, a ticket, a report, a badge — that land on a fanned pile on springs.recoil. Each pair of rollers is a stage and every part of a sheet shows the stage it has passed, clipped exactly at each nip, while the rollers turn by the distance the paper moves, ride up over each sheet and drop back with a bounce. A flywheel motor drives it; winding the crank turns the rollers 1:1 and the flywheel carries the wind, and the crank is a button whose Right, Enter or Space wind one document through on springs.glide, Left winds one back and Home and End go to the first and last.

props.name: items
props.description: The documents in the queue: { id, title, kind?, input?, output? }; they go round and round.

props.name: speed
props.description: The motor's pace, 0.25× to 2×.

props.name: rollers
props.description: Rollers on the press, in pairs: 2, 4 or 6. Each pair is a stage — colour, then detail, then varnish.

props.name: palette
props.description: The inks the results come out in.

props.name: heft
props.description: How heavy the rollers are, 0 to 1: a heavy press carries a wind for longer.

props.name: squeeze
props.description: How hard the rollers press, 0 to 1: how far they ride up over a sheet and how plain the crease is.

props.name: spacing
props.description: Space between sheets in the queue, 0 to 1.

props.name: crank
props.description: Show the crank.

props.name: paused
props.description: The motor is off: the press turns only when wound or stepped.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the press's creak while you wind it. Off unless asked for.

props.name: label
props.description: The press's accessible name.

props.name: onResult
props.description: Fires when a finished result lands on the pile, with the item and its place in the queue.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No winding and no steps.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the crank is a button labelled "Wind the press". Right (or Down), Enter and Space wind one document through, Left (or Up) winds the last one back, Home and End go to the first and last of the queue; every result that lands is announced politely ("Printed: Spring catalogue, a card.").
Reduced motion: the motor is off and nothing slides; keys and crank taps swap to the next result at once with a short dip, and a wind lands on the nearest whole document.

Performance: everything — sheets, their stage clips, the rollers' knurled surfaces and the crank — derives from one feed motion value; React renders only when a sheet enters or leaves the drawn window. One requestAnimationFrame loop runs the flywheel while the press turns and on screen, and stops when paused and still.
Content: each item draws one of six results in the chosen palette, or pass input and output nodes of your own; they fill the sheet and are clipped by the stages like the drawn ones.
Sound: the creak only answers the visitor — winding or stepping — and stops when they let go or the step settles.

items.title: Petri Stack
items.tagline: A tilted stack of dishes, each with a picture.
items.description: A gallery as a tilted stack of glass petri dishes in real CSS 3D, each holding its picture like a specimen under a lid, with thin stacked rims, a glass tint, a soft shadow between layers and refraction at the rim where the picture bends into the glass. A click, a key or a flick sends the top dish off: it lifts and slides out on springs.glide with the flick's velocity, drops while the rest of the stack rises a level in a cascade, and tucks in underneath to land on springs.recoil with a glassy clack, bringing the next picture up; hovering or keyboard focus lifts the top lid on springs.snap. The stack is a focusable carousel where Right, Down, Enter and Space send the top dish down, Left and Up bring the bottom one back, Home and End jump, and a drag follows 1:1 and commits by projection.

props.name: items
props.description: The dishes, top first: { src?, alt, caption?, art? }; without src or art a specimen is drawn in code.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The dish on top; controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the click, key or drag that changed the top dish, with its index.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far the stack leans back from you, 10 to 75 degrees: low looks down on it, high sees it side on.

props.name: gap
props.description: Air between one dish and the next, px, 2 to 32.

props.name: glass
props.description: The glass's tint.

props.name: visible
props.description: How many dishes show in the stack, 2 to 7; the rest wait unseen beneath.

props.name: lift
props.description: How far hovering or focus lifts the top lid, px.

props.name: refraction
props.description: How strongly the glass bends the picture at the rim, 0 to 1.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the stage, px; the dishes size themselves to fit it and the width.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the glassy clack as a dish lands. Off unless asked for.

props.name: label
props.description: The stack's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No clicks, keys or drags.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the stack is one tab stop (role region, aria-roledescription carousel). Right, Down, Enter and Space send the top dish to the bottom, Left and Up bring the bottom dish back to the top, Home and End go to the first and last; the dish now on top is announced politely, and only it is exposed as a labelled slide.
Reduced motion: no slide, lift or cascade — the stack holds still, the dishes take their new places at once and the new top picture cross-fades in; the lid does not lift.
Performance: pure DOM and CSS 3D with motion values on each dish; nothing runs at rest, and only the top two dishes draw the refraction ring.
Images: pass src (with alt) for photographs, or art for your own drawing; the defaults are specimens drawn in seeded SVG, the same on the server and in the browser.

Controlled use: a host that changes value gets the same choreography (one step either way, or a glide for longer jumps); a host that refuses a change keeps its dish on top and the dragged dish returns.

items.title: Sand Portrait
items.tagline: A picture in sand; sweep it and it remakes itself.
items.description: A picture laid in coloured sand on a canvas: every grain keeps a home and a colour sampled from the picture, a tone of its own and a bead's highlight. Dragging sweeps an eddy along the stroke that drags grains with it and turns them the way the stroke curves, and a flick throws it on; when the stroke stops the sand flows home grain by grain from the bottom up, each on its own spring with the springs.drift constants and a sideways curl, so the picture rebuilds in curling streams. A tap swirls everything into a turning two-armed spiral on springs.glide constants while the colours turn toward the next picture, then the spiral slowly unwinds from the outside in into the new one; Right, Enter and Space swirl forward, Left back, Home and End to the ends.

props.name: items
props.description: The pictures: { src?, alt, caption? }; an item without src pours a drawn print.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The picture shown; controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the tap or key that asked for another picture, with its index.

props.name: grains

props.name: sweep

props.name: reform

props.name: curl

props.name: swirl
props.description: How many turns the spiral's arms wind when the picture changes, 0.5 to 3.

props.name: texture
props.description: Grain-to-grain variation in tone, 0 (flat colour) to 1 (coarse, mixed sand).

props.name: hold
props.description: How long the sand waits after a stroke stops before it flows back, ms.

props.name: tray
props.description: A sand-coloured floor and a shaded rim; off, the grains lie on whatever is behind.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Sweeping with the pointer and tapping for the next picture. Keys always work.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold every grain where it is.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the grain grid and its tones, so two trays never match.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the tray, px.

props.name: label
props.description: The tray's accessible name.

props.name: onStateChange
props.description: Fires when the sand starts or stops moving.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No sweeps, taps or keys; the tray dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the tray.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the tray is one tab stop, a labelled carousel. Right, Enter and Space swirl into the next picture, Left into the previous one, Home and End to the first and last; the new picture is spoken politely from the key that chose it. A sweep is transient — the picture always comes back — so it needs no key of its own.
Reduced motion: a sweep leaves a dimmed trail that fades back instead of moving grains, and a new picture cross-fades into the grains in place from the bottom up.

Performance: nothing runs at rest. One requestAnimationFrame loop steps the grains in typed arrays and stamps them into a single ImageData only while sand is loose, swirling or changing colour, and only while the tray is on screen and the page visible; it stops the moment every grain is home. The canvas caps its pixel ratio at 2.

Pictures: an item's src must be same-origin or CORS-enabled to be sampled; anything else falls back to a drawn print. Drawn prints use token pigments at fixed lightness, so they look the same in light and dark themes.
The server renders the print itself in SVG under a fine screen of grain shadows, so the first paint is already the picture; the canvas fades in over it.

items.title: Headwind Cards
items.tagline: Cards that lean into the drag like walkers.
items.description: A row of standing cards that lean into the drag like walkers into wind: the row follows the hand 1:1 and rubber-bands past its ends, and each card skews about its foot in proportion to the row's speed, the cards at the leading end furthest, each on its own spring so a change of direction runs down the row as a wave. A throw is projected to the card it would rest on and the row springs there on springs.glide with the release velocity, while every card stands back up on a spring of the given stiffness at the recoil damping ratio, rocking just past upright before it settles. Arrow keys step one card on springs.snap with half the lean, Home and End travel to the ends on springs.glide, and a click on another card brings it in.

props.name: items
props.description: The cards: { src?, alt, caption?, detail?, art? }.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The current card; controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the throw, click or key that chose a card, with the card the row will settle on.

props.name: skew
props.description: How hard the cards lean into the motion, 0 (upright) to 2.

props.name: stiffness

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between cards, px.

props.name: cardWidth
props.description: A card's width, px; held to 72% of the row on narrow screens.

props.name: aspect
props.description: A card's height as a share of its width.

props.name: maxLean
props.description: The most a card may lean, degrees.

props.name: spread
props.description: How much more the leading cards lean than the trailing ones, 0 (all alike) to 1.

props.name: friction
props.description: How quickly a throw dies away, 0 (coasts far) to 1 (stops short).

props.name: align
props.description: Where the current card rests: at the start of the row or in its middle.

props.name: streaks
props.description: Faint wind lines drifting through the gaps while the row moves fast.

props.name: label
props.description: The row's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No drags, clicks or keys; the row dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root region.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the row is one tab stop, a labelled carousel. Left and Right step one card with a smaller lean, Home and End go to the ends; the chosen card is spoken politely. Each card is a labelled slide, and cards wholly outside the row are hidden from assistive technology and inert.
Reduced motion: nothing leans and no wind lines show. A drag still moves the row under the hand, a release finishes on a short tween, and keys jump with a brief dip in opacity.

Performance: nothing runs at rest. One requestAnimationFrame loop turns the row's speed into lean targets and steps each card's spring only while the row or a lean is moving; the row's width is cached by a resize observer so the loop never reads layout.
Layout uses container units: the card width is the smaller of cardWidth and 72% of the row, so the server frame is already composed at any width and a phone shows one and a half cards.
Each card skews about its foot, so its height never changes and nothing leaves the row's box; cards lean apart rather than into each other because the leading ones lean furthest.

items.title: Cartwheel Deck
items.tagline: Each card cartwheels into place as it advances.
items.description: A row of cards standing on a floor, front card at the left and each further card a little smaller. Advancing sends the front card cartwheeling end over end along the floor to the back: it turns whole turns while it travels, always resting on its lowest corner so it rises onto each corner and drops onto each edge, shrinking to the back card's size, with a floor shadow as wide as its projection; it lands upright with a squash on the recoil spring, a hop sized by bounce and a thud, while the rest shuffle forward on springs.glide in a short cascade. The tumble runs on the glide calibration retimed to the duration, so a card tipped by hand carries its throw into it; Right, Enter and Space advance, Left reverses the tumble, and Home and End tumble through to the first and last card.

props.name: items
props.description: The cards, front to back: { src?, alt, caption?, detail?, art? }.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The card at the front; controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the click, swipe or key that moved the deck, with the new front card.

props.name: spin

props.name: bounce

props.name: gap

props.name: depth
props.description: How much smaller each card further back stands, 0 to 0.2 of the front card.

props.name: duration
props.description: Roughly how long one tumble takes at one turn, ms.

props.name: aspect
props.description: A card's width as a share of its height.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the stage, px; the cards are sized so a tumbling card always clears its top.

props.name: shadow
props.description: Shadows on the floor that stretch as a card turns.

props.name: label
props.description: The deck's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a thud as each card lands. Off unless asked for.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No clicks, swipes or keys; the deck dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root region.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the deck is one tab stop, a labelled carousel. Right, Enter and Space send the front card to the back, Left brings the back card to the front, Home and End tumble through to the first and last card one card at a time; the new front card is spoken politely and is the only slide exposed to assistive technology.
Reduced motion: no tumble or shuffle travel. The cards take their new places with a short dip in opacity, a swipe needs a real distance or flick, and the value and the thud still follow.

Hand feel: dragging right tips the front card onto its corner 1:1 under the finger, dragging left tips the back card toward the front; past a third of a card or with a flick it goes and carries the throw into the tumble, otherwise it rocks back on the recoil spring.

Performance: nothing runs at rest. Each card's position, angle, size, squash and shadow are motion values; floor contact is computed from the angle in the animation's own update, never in React state, and tumbles queue so rapid keys never stack.
Layout is pure CSS with container units, so the server frame is right at any width: natural spacing while the row fits, an even overlap like a fanned deck when it does not.

items.title: Freight Sidings
items.tagline: Pictures riding freight cars on tilted tracks.
items.description: A rail yard seen from above and turned so the tracks cross the frame on a diagonal: loaded lines alternate with empty sidings, and each line carries a train of flat cars loaded with pictures, its head car showing a marker lamp. Page scroll moves the trains in alternating directions at their own speeds, a sideways drag scrubs the yard 1:1 under the hand with a flick carried on, and left alone each train shunts slowly back and forth; every train follows its target on its own spring and slows to a crawl under the pointer or keyboard. Clicking a car rolls it to the front: it uncouples on springs.flick, switches onto the siding on springs.glide, rolls past the cars ahead while they back up, switches back at the head and couples, and the jolt runs down the train car by car on the recoil spring; the yard is a grid where arrows move between cars and Enter rolls one to the front.

props.name: items
props.description: The pictures, dealt round the trains in turn: { src?, alt, caption? }.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The picture last rolled to the front of its train; controlled or initial. Nothing is chosen until a car is.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the click or key that rolled a car to the front, with its picture's index.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far the yard is turned, degrees, -40 to 40; the tracks cross the frame on this diagonal.

props.name: speed
props.description: How far the trains travel for each pixel of scroll or drag, 0 to 2.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between coupled cars, px.

props.name: trains
props.description: How many trains run in the yard, 2 to 6.

props.name: carLength
props.description: A car's length, px.

props.name: drift
props.description: How far each train shunts back and forth on its own while you watch, 0 (still) to 1.

props.name: slow
props.description: How much a train under the pointer or keyboard slows, 0 (not at all) to 1 (to a crawl).

props.name: scroll
props.description: Scrolling the page moves the trains.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the yard, px.

props.name: label
props.description: The yard's accessible name.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play the couplers' clacks, and the rail joints under a drag. Off unless asked for.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold every train where it is; clicks still roll cars to the front.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No drags, clicks or keys; the yard dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the yard.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the yard is a grid with one tab stop. Arrow keys move between cars along a train (left and right follow the screen) and between trains, Home and End go to the first and last car, Enter or Space rolls the focused car to the front and keeps focus on it; a focused train slows and shunts so the car is in view, and the move is announced politely.
Reduced motion: no drift, no scroll or drag travel, and a car takes the head place with a short cross-fade; the marker lamp still moves and the clack still plays.

Performance: one requestAnimationFrame loop drives each train's spring and the shunt clock, only while the yard is on screen and the page visible; with drift off it stops when every train has settled. Page scroll is read from one passive capture listener, and cars are transformed elements over CSS-gradient tracks, with no canvas.
Sound answers only the visitor: couplers on a click or key, and quiet rail-joint clacks only while a hand drags the yard, never on scroll.
The yard is a window onto a longer line: trains reach past the frame's edges, and the frame clips with paint containment so nothing draws outside its box.

items.title: Core Plane
items.tagline: Type and watch each bit flip in a grid of cores.
items.description: A plane of ferrite memory cores strung on fine wires, drawn on a canvas: eight columns from bit 7 to bit 0 and as many rows as fit, each core a small ring at ±45° threaded by its row, column and sense wires, lit when it holds a 1, and each row labelled with its character and hex. Typing writes each character's UTF-8 bytes into the next row the way the real thing does: a spark runs along the row wire while sparks run down the column wire of every bit that changes, and where each pair meets the core flips with a stutter scaled by flicker and a tiny burst, a bit every few milliseconds left to right; Backspace erases the last row, older rows fade, and an idle job reads random cores with a faint blink. The writing happens in a real text input, so the keyboard is simply typing; reduced motion swaps the sparks for a short cross-fade timed on durations.base.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The text written to the plane; controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires as the visitor types, with the new text.

props.name: cores
props.description: Diameter of a core, px, 6 to 18: finer cores fit more rows.

props.name: flicker

props.name: wire
props.description: The wires' colour: a preset, or any CSS colour.

props.name: fade
props.description: How much older rows fade as new ones are written, 0 (none) to 1.

props.name: idle
props.description: Let a background job read random cores when the plane is idle.

props.name: readRate

props.name: bitDelay

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Most characters the input takes.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in the empty input.

props.name: label

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the plane, px.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a tick for every core that flips while you type. Off unless asked for.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the plane still: writes land without sparks and the idle job rests.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No typing; the plane dims.

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard and assistive technology: writing happens in a real labelled text input with a visible prompt, so typing, editing and pasting all work as usual; the plane is an image whose name lists the characters it holds, and a polite announcement gives the last character's hex and bit count once typing pauses.
Reduced motion: no sparks, stutter or idle reads. Cores cross-fade to their new values on a short tween, and labels and fades still follow every keystroke, because the bits are information.

Performance: the canvas redraws only while a write, erase or read is in flight; the idle job is a timer that schedules only while the plane is on screen, the page is visible and nothing is being typed. A long paste animates only the rows that stay visible.
Sound answers only typing: one tick per flipped core, pitched by its bit; the idle job and a host's changes to value are silent.

Theming: wires, lit cores, ferrite and sparks are token pigments resolved on the plane's own element and re-read when the theme changes; on a pale board the sparks draw as a darker hot streak so they still read.

items.title: Node Leap
items.tagline: Signals that hop from bead to bead along a strand.
items.description: A background of long soft filaments drifting through the dark on a slow current, each threaded with small beads, drawn in Canvas 2D with the content above. Signals do not flow: a signal rests on a bead, then jumps to the next in a quick streak of light, and the bead it lands on flares and cools; where two filaments drift close a faint glimmer passes between their beads, and a signal may jump across, arcing over the gap and carrying on along the other filament. The pointer is a gentle current that pushes the filaments aside, each point drifting back on a spring with the springs.drift constants, and a press sends a new signal from the nearest bead; the field is decoration and never takes focus, so the keyboard goes straight to the content above it.

props.name: children
props.description: The content above the field: a hero line, a heading, a call to action.

props.name: strands
props.description: How many filaments drift through the field, 2 to 16.

props.name: hopRate
props.description: How often a signal hops to its next bead, per second, 0.5 to 8.

props.name: glow
props.description: How far a lit bead's light spreads, 0 (bare beads) to 1 (blooming).

props.name: beads
props.description: Beads threaded on each filament, 6 to 24.

props.name: signals
props.description: Signals travelling on each filament, 1 to 4.

props.name: current
props.description: The pace of the slow current the filaments drift on, 0 (still) to 2.

props.name: cross
props.description: The chance a signal jumps across where two filaments drift close, 0 to 1.

props.name: colors
props.description: Signal colours, as CSS colours (up to four); each signal takes one.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer is a gentle current, and a press sends a new signal.

props.name: pointerStrength
props.description: How strongly the pointer's current moves the filaments, 0 to 1.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold everything still.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the filaments, their beads and the signals' walks.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: onCrossing
props.description: Fires each time a signal jumps across from one filament to another.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the box.

usageNotes: The field is decoration: the canvas is aria-hidden and never takes focus or clicks, and children render above it in their own layer, fully interactive and in the tab order. Pointer influence is read from the container, so a press on a button above the field is just a press.
Reduced motion: a still frame of the filaments at rest with beads lit as if mid-relay; no hopping, drift or pointer current.

Performance: one requestAnimationFrame loop runs only while the field is on screen, the page is visible and it is not paused; it uses typed arrays and one pre-rendered glow sprite per colour, caps the pixel ratio at 2 and resizes through a resize observer. The server renders an SVG still of the same filaments.

Theming: the ground, filaments and signal colours are tokens resolved on the component's own element and re-read when the theme changes; light adds on a dark page and draws as ink and pigment on a light one.

items.title: Geodesic Spin
items.tagline: Spin the frame; faster spins subdivide it.
items.description: A wireframe geodesic sphere you spin by hand: it turns 1:1 under a drag, coasts on the release velocity for as long as its inertia allows and eases back to a slow turntable spin, its near struts lit from a light high on the left and its front hubs catching a glint that slides from hub to hub. Past a speed every strut splits at its middle, the new hubs pushed out from the old chords to the sphere on the snap spring's one overshoot while the new struts draw out from their centres, and as it coasts down the frame merges back on glide. The arrow keys spin it (Shift for more), so repeated presses split it as a flick does, and Home brakes it.

props.name: frequency

props.name: maxFrequency
props.description: The finest frame a fast spin reaches, 2 to 8; levels double from the base frequency.

props.name: splitAt
props.description: Spin speed in rad/s that splits the first level; each further level needs 1.8 times more, and a level merges back below 0.65 of its threshold.

props.name: inertia
props.description: How long a flick coasts, 0 (it stops almost at once) to 1 (it coasts for seconds).

props.name: strut
props.description: Strut weight in px, 0.5 to 2.5.

props.name: idleSpin
props.description: The turntable spin it returns to when left alone, rad/s; 0 lets it come to rest and stop drawing.

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far the rest pose leans toward you, degrees.

props.name: glint
props.description: Strength of the specular glints on the near hubs, 0 to 1.

props.name: perspective
props.description: How much nearer struts are drawn larger, 0 (orthographic) to 1.

props.name: color
props.description: Strut colour, any CSS colour.

props.name: lightColor
props.description: The colour lit struts and glints turn toward.

props.name: readout
props.description: Show the frequency and face count in the corner.

props.name: onFrequencyChange
props.description: Fires when a split or merge completes, and once at mount, with the frequency and face count.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the frame still; a drag still turns it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No drag and no keys.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box; the sphere fits its shorter side.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the sphere is one focusable group. Arrow keys add spin about the matching axis (Shift for a bigger push), so a run of presses splits the frame exactly as a flick does; Home brakes it, and Escape brakes it only when it is spinning (otherwise Escape is left to the page). Each completed split or merge is announced once.

Meshes are built once per frequency and cached; a frame rotates the hubs with one matrix and strokes the struts as six light-binned paths, so even the 8V frame (1,920 struts) is a handful of draw calls. Nothing runs off screen or in a hidden tab, and with `idleSpin={0}` the loop stops once the sphere is still.

Under reduced motion it turns only while dragged or stepped by a key (15° a press) and never coasts; the frequency still follows the speed you give it, but levels change by a short cross-fade instead of splitting.
Colours come from `color` and `lightColor` resolved on the component, re-read when the theme changes; on a light page the glints take the light colour deepened rather than white.
The server renders a still SVG of the base frame at rest, so the first paint is finished before the canvas takes over.

items.title: Slow Sync
items.tagline: Scattered blinks that slowly fall into step.
items.description: A field of soft dots, each blinking on its own rhythm, that slowly falls into step: every dot is a pulse-coupled oscillator whose flash nudges its neighbours — a late one advanced, an early one held back — so patches agree first, waves of light sweep the field, and a weak pull toward the mean dissolves the last whirling cores until it beats as one pulse, over about a minute at the default coupling. A click scatters the timing in a patch: a ring opens on the snap spring, the dots it passes are pushed out and come home on recoil, and the patch blinks out of step until its neighbours draw it back. With the field focused, the arrow keys move the patch and Enter scatters it.

props.name: children
props.description: Content above the field; it stays fully interactive.

props.name: coupling
props.description: How strongly a flash nudges its neighbours, 0 (they never agree) to 1 (they lock in seconds).

props.name: count
props.description: How many dots on a 720 × 208 field, 20 to 600; other sizes keep the same density.

props.name: warmth
props.description: The colour of the light, cool moon-white (0) through firefly green (0.5) to amber (1).

props.name: color
props.description: Any CSS colour for the light; overrides warmth.

props.name: period
props.description: Mean time between one dot's blinks, s.

props.name: spread
props.description: How different the dots' own rhythms are, 0 to 1; more spread means more waves and slower agreement.

props.name: reach
props.description: How far a flash is felt, in dot spacings, 1 to 3.

props.name: glow
props.description: Size and strength of a flash's halo, 0 to 1.

props.name: dotSize
props.description: Dot radius at rest, px.

props.name: patch
props.description: Radius of a scatter, as a fraction of the field's width.

props.name: interactive
props.description: A click on the field, or Enter, scatters a patch.

props.name: onScatter
props.description: Fires when a patch is scattered, with its centre as fractions of the field.

props.name: onSyncChange
props.description: How in step the field is, 0 (scattered) to 1 (one pulse), rounded to 2 dp, at most four times a second.

props.name: paused
props.description: Freeze the field.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the layout, the rhythms and the starting phases.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the field.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the field is one focusable group with a hint. Arrow keys move a reticle the size of the patch, Home centres it, and Enter or Space scatters there, so the keyboard reaches the same state as a click. A scatter is announced, and "In step" is announced once when the field next agrees — never per blink.
`onSyncChange` reports the field's order parameter (the length of the mean of every dot's phase as a unit vector), so a host can narrate progress or trigger something when the field agrees.

One Canvas 2D layer of two pre-rendered sprites per dot; neighbour lists are built once per layout through a spatial hash, so a step is linear in the dot count. Nothing runs off screen, in a hidden tab or while `paused`, and the backing store is capped at `dpr`.

Under reduced motion nothing blinks: each dot glows steadily by how in step it is with its neighbours, re-read every 600 ms and cross-faded, so the field still visibly evens out and a scattered patch shows as a dim island that recovers.

On a dark page flashes are added light with a hot centre; on a light page the same dots are drawn as pigment with a softer halo, so they read in both themes. Flashes stay well under three per second per dot.

items.title: Marsh Light
items.tagline: A pale light in smoke, keeping just out of reach.
items.description: A pale light over a night marsh, keeping just out of reach: a small orb drifts above dark water wrapped in slow curls of smoke that are wound round it, lit by it and left trailing when it moves, while the water carries its long broken reflection under reeds and a low mist. Reach toward it and it slips away to the side with more room on a critically damped spring, harder the closer you come; stop, and it waits at a polite distance. Corner it against the frame and it goes out and blooms back in elsewhere, its halo swelling once on the snap spring; keyboard focus on anything in your content calls it over, and with the scene focused the arrow keys move a hand it shies from.

props.description: Content above the marsh; it stays fully interactive, wears the dark tokens, and keyboard focus inside it calls the light over.

props.name: shyness

props.name: smoke

props.name: hue

props.name: size
props.description: The bright core's radius, px.

props.name: glow

props.name: drift

props.name: waterLine
props.description: Where the water begins, as a fraction of the height.

props.name: reeds
props.description: Reeds and bulrushes along the water's edge.

props.name: summonOnFocus

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer, and the arrow keys when the scene has focus, move it; off, it only wanders.

props.name: onVanish
props.description: Fires when it is cornered and reappears somewhere else.

props.name: onStateChange
props.description: Fires when what it is doing changes.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the scene still.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds its wandering and the reeds.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name.

props.name: dpr

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the scene.

usageNotes: The light following keyboard focus is a bonus, never a requirement: your content keeps its own focus order and rings. With the scene itself focused, the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps) move a dashed hand ring that it shies from exactly as from the pointer, so the keyboard can corner it too. A vanish is announced once.

One WebGL2 pass over a fullscreen triangle; the orb is steered in JS and handed to the shader as uniforms, and the smoke is only computed near the light. The scene draws at no more than 1.25× pixel ratio, stops off screen and in a hidden tab, survives context loss, and without WebGL2 keeps a CSS still with a CSS orb that still keeps its distance.

The marsh is night in both themes (its colours come from `hue`, mixed toward black), so the component puts its content under the dark tokens: `text-foreground`, `bg-primary` and the rest read correctly on it whatever the page's theme.

Under reduced motion the smoke and water are still and the light does not drift or flee: come within its distance and it fades out and back in at the far side; focus inside the content fades it in beside the focused element.
The cursor is never hidden, and pointer tracking is read from the scene's own box, so links and buttons inside keep their clicks.

items.title: Pace Board
items.tagline: Words swap at speed, smeared by their own motion.
items.description: A display that swaps one value for the next with real motion: the new value arrives fast from the side on a spring between flick and recoil set by its overshoot, runs past its rest and on the way back is caught like a detent — locked, with a short judder — while the old one accelerates away stretching from its trailing edge. Both carry a horizontal motion blur in proportion to their own speed, an SVG blur in x only that is switched off at rest, so the faster a value moves the more it smears. Values cycle from a list or follow a live number, optionally swapping only the characters that changed; a cycling board pauses on hover, and with keyboard focus Space pauses and resumes it while Left, Right, Home and End step through it.

props.name: value

props.name: format

props.name: index / defaultIndex

props.name: onIndexChange

props.name: interval

props.name: blur

props.name: overshoot

props.name: speed

props.name: travel

props.name: from

props.name: swap
props.description: Swap the whole value, or only the characters that changed, each in its own window.

props.name: stagger

props.name: trigger

props.name: paused
props.description: Stop cycling; live values still swap.

props.name: onPausedChange
props.description: Fires when Space pauses or resumes the cycle.

props.name: progress
props.description: Draw a hairline under the value that fills until the next swap.

props.name: reserve
props.description: A sample whose width is always kept, so a growing number never shifts the layout.

props.name: align
props.description: Where the value sits in its kept width.

props.name: as

props.name: label

props.name: live
props.description: Announce each new value politely; off by default so a cycling board never chatters.

props.name: onSwap

props.name: className

usageNotes: A cycling board is a focusable group described as rotating text: Space pauses and resumes it (the pause WCAG asks of moving content), Left/Right and Up/Down step, Home and End jump, a click steps forward, and hovering pauses it. Pauses are announced; the values themselves are announced only with `live="polite"`.

The current value is in the accessibility tree exactly once; the moving layers are hidden from it. The widest value (or `reserve`) keeps its width, so the sentence around the board never shifts as words swap.

Font size, weight, colour and line height inherit, and the travel, overshoot and judder scale with the window, so it works from a caption to a hero heading. Use `tabular-nums` for numbers in `chars` mode so digits share one width.

Each moving layer gets its own SVG blur in x only, written per frame from the layer's velocity and switched off (`filter: none`) below a quarter pixel, so a resting value costs nothing and is pin sharp. The cycle timer runs only in view and while the tab is shown.
Under reduced motion the old value fades out and the new one fades in, in place, on a short tween — no travel, blur or judder — and the cycle, steps and live values still change.

items.title: Eaves Drip
items.tagline: Pixel rain on a roof, running off the eaves.
items.description: A small pixel-art cottage in quiet rain, and the water's whole way down: drops fall at the wind's angle and burst on the tiles leaving a wet glint, some of the water runs down the roof into the gutter and along it to the end, where a drop swells at the lip, lets go and falls into a puddle that slowly grows, each landing opening a ring. The pointer is the wind — lean either side of the middle and the rain leans with you, eased over a few hundred milliseconds — and a click sends a gust from that side that lifts a sheet of spray off the roof, the gutter and the puddle, which falls back as scattered drops. The scene is focusable: Left and Right step the wind and Enter sends a gust.

props.name: children

props.name: rainRate

props.name: pixel

props.name: puddle

props.name: wind

props.name: gust
