props.name: fade
props.description: How long the developed photograph takes to fade back to the live view, ms.

props.name: develop
props.description: The halation bloom that swells as the photograph develops.

props.name: speed
props.description: How fast the cars drive, 0.5 to 2.

props.name: maxExposure
props.description: The shutter closes by itself after this long, seconds.

props.name: lightColors
props.description: Headlights and tail lights, CSS colours.

props.name: stars
props.description: Stars come out as the dusk deepens.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the live traffic still (an open shutter still records).

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the mountains, the traffic and the stars.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The control's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No pressing or keys; the view dims.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the view; it fills its parent by default.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the view is a role="button" with aria-pressed for the shutter; Space opens it while held and closes it on release (repeats are ignored), Enter opens and closes it for anyone who cannot hold a key, and Escape closes an open shutter (handled, so the page never sees it). A polite live region announces each photograph once: "Exposure 4.6 seconds, 9 cars."

Reduced motion: no moving lights in the live view; holding the shutter fades in a finished long exposure (the trails laid down at once) more fully the longer you hold, and release holds the photograph and fades it out — no bloom, and the iris cross-fades.

Performance: the dusk scene is painted once per size, tone and theme into an offscreen canvas; a frame is three drawImage calls and a short line per car (typed arrays, no per-frame allocation). Live traffic draws at 30 frames a second only while on screen and visible; an exposure or a fading photograph draws every frame; paused with the shutter closed and the photograph gone, nothing runs.

A press holds the shutter open until the pointer lifts anywhere on the page; a touch that turns into a scroll closes it. The view is painted from pigments, so the dusk looks the same on a light or a dark page; the server renders a still with the road and a pair of trails.
Give it a size (it fills its parent); in a cropped box the sky gives way first so the hairpins stay in view.

items.title: Wing Scales
items.tagline: Iridescent ridges of a wing, shifting as you tilt.
items.description: A specimen of an invented blue butterfly drawn per pixel in one WebGL2 pass, zoomable from the whole insect down to the ridges of a single scale: rows of toothed scales laid like shingles, coloured by a thin-film term on their ridges, so the blue slides toward green and violet as the pointer rocks the specimen on a critically damped spring with the drift constants. The wheel (once focused), a pinch, double-click or the keys zoom about the pointer on the glide constants in log space; zoomed in, a drag pans 1:1 and a release throws by projection, and while you look the scales breathe in a slow wave that settles when you leave. Plus and minus zoom, Home and End jump to the wing or the ridges, Left and Right rock it, Shift with an arrow pans, and Escape returns to the whole wing.

props.name: zoom
props.description: Magnification shown, 1 (the whole wing) to maxZoom (the ridges of one scale); a new value glides the view there.

props.name: onZoomChange
props.description: Fires from the wheel, pinch, drag or key that changed the magnification.

props.name: maxZoom
props.description: The deepest magnification, 8 to 160.

props.name: iridescence
props.description: How strongly the ridges shine, 0 (dull pigment brown) to 1 (the full blue-green play).

props.name: tilt
props.description: How far the wing rocks toward the pointer, 0 (held still) to 1 (26° each way).

props.name: film
props.description: Thickness of the ridges' film in nanometres, 300 to 560: the colour family (gold, violet, blue, green).

props.name: ground
props.description: The pigment under the film, any CSS colour.

props.name: markings
props.description: The pattern of pigment scales: a spotted outer band, an eyespot on each hindwing, or plain.

props.name: breathe
props.description: How far the scales lift as the wing breathes while you look, 0 to 1.

props.name: wheel
props.description: When a plain wheel zooms: once the wing has focus (or with Ctrl or ⌘), always, or never. Pinch always zooms.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the scales' small irregularities.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the specimen for assistive technology.

props.name: paused
props.description: Holds the scales flat: no breathing.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the wing but takes no gestures or keys.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box (default h-56 w-full); the insect is fitted inside it.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the wing is one focusable group — + and − (or Up and Down) zoom, Page Up and Page Down by ×3, Home the whole wing, End the ridges, Enter the next level, Left and Right rock it toward the light, Shift with an arrow pans, and Escape (handled only while zoomed) returns to ×1. A polite status reads the magnification when it settles.

Wheel etiquette: with wheel="focus" a plain wheel scrolls the page until the wing is clicked or focused (a hint says so); once it is, scrolling down looks deeper toward the ridges and up backs out. Ctrl or ⌘ with the wheel, and trackpad pinches, always zoom (spread to zoom in); at either zoom limit the wheel returns to the page. Touch pinches zoom, and the page still scrolls vertically over an unzoomed wing.
Reduced motion: no breathing, no tilt following the pointer and no glides — zoom, pan and key tilts change in place — while the colour and the magnification still show.

Performance: one fullscreen triangle with no textures, drawn only while a spring, the breath or a gesture is moving, on screen and with the tab visible; DPR is capped at `dpr`, context loss rebuilds, and without WebGL2 (and as the server's first frame) an SVG still of the same insect is shown.
Theming: the insect is fixed pigment art on a transparent canvas with a black-alpha shadow, so it sits on any card in light or dark; `ground` accepts tokens and is re-read when the theme changes.

items.title: Hanging Scroll
items.tagline: Pictures on a paper scroll rolling away overhead.
items.description: A vertical gallery mounted on a long paper scroll hung from a turned rod: as its scroll container scrolls, the stage pins and the paper rolls up onto the rod, bowing off the wall before the roll while each picture bends over the front of it, foreshortening and darkening as it turns away, and the knobs on the rod turn exactly with the rolled length as the roll fattens. The shown progress follows the scroll on a critically damped spring with the glide constants, and the hanging part is a lightly damped pendulum that the roll's changes of speed kick into a slight sway, swinging quicker as the scroll shortens until the weighted bottom bar rises with the last picture. Down, Page Down and Space roll to the next picture, Up and Page Up back, and Home and End jump to either end.

props.name: items
props.type: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string }[]
props.description: The pictures, top to bottom; the default is five ink-wash views drawn in code.

props.name: curl
props.description: How far the paper bows out before it meets the roll, 0 (straight into a tight roll) to 1 (a wide lifted curl).

props.name: rodSize
props.description: Diameter of the top rod in px, 10 to 28: a slim rod bends the pictures sharply, a thick roller slowly.

props.name: paperTone
props.description: The paper the pictures are mounted on.

props.name: mount
props.description: Colour of the mounting bands and borders, any CSS colour; defaults to the tone's own.

props.name: sway
props.description: How much the weighted bottom bar swings as the roll speeds up and slows, 0 to 1.

props.name: range
props.description: Scroll distance from one picture to the next, px.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the pinned stage, px; give it the height of the scroll container it sits in.

props.name: cord
props.description: Hang the rod from a cord and a nail.

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Fires with the picture at the reading line, from the scroll or key that moved it.

props.name: onProgressChange
props.description: Fires as the paper rolls, 0 (all hanging) to 1 (rolled to the last picture).

props.name: label
props.description: Names the scroll for assistive technology.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the section.

usageNotes: Place it inside a scroll container (or the page) and give `height` that container's visible height: the section is height + range × (pictures − 1) tall and its stage sticks while the paper rolls.

Keyboard: the stage is one focusable group — Down, Page Down and Space roll to the next picture, Up and Page Up back, Home and End to the ends — by scrolling the container, so pointer and keyboard reach the same states. Every picture's description and caption is in an sr-only list, and a polite status names the picture at the reading line.
Reduced motion: nothing rolls or sways; the scroll hangs flat and the current picture's panel cross-fades to the next as the reading line passes it, with the index and callbacks still updating.

Performance: one Canvas 2D; the paper is painted to an offscreen sheet once per layout, tone or picture load, and each frame is one drawImage for the hanging part plus about one strip per CSS pixel of the bow and the roll. The loop runs only while the roll or the pendulum moves, on screen and with the tab visible; DPR is capped at `dpr`.
The paper, wood and pictures are fixed pigments, so the scroll looks the same on a light or a dark page; the server renders a DOM still of the first picture that the canvas replaces.

items.title: Drying Line
items.tagline: Prints pegged on a line, twisting as it pulls past.
items.description: Darkroom prints pegged to a sagging cord under a red safelight, on a pulley loop you pull past: a drag follows 1:1 and commits by projection to the nearest print on the glide spring with the release velocity, and the page's scroll pulls it too. Every print is a real pendulum and a torsion pendulum, swung about its peg by the line's acceleration and twisted by the air each its own way, damped by `sway`, so the glossy faces turn and a band of red light slides across them before they hang still and the loop stops. Clicking a print unclips it: the jaw opens on the flick spring and the print glides to the front with its darkroom note, and Back on the line or Escape carries it back as the jaw snaps shut on snap; Left and Right pull the line a print, Home and End go to the ends.

props.name: items
props.type: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string; note?: string; aspect?: number }[]
props.description: The prints along the line; the default is eight black-and-white photographs drawn in code.

props.name: sway
props.description: How freely the prints swing and twist, 0 (stiff, quickly still) to 1 (loose, long and wide).

props.name: sag
props.description: How deep the cord sags between its hooks, 0 (taut) to 1 (a deep curve).

props.name: pegs
props.description: What holds each print: a wooden spring peg, a steel binder clip or a film clip.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The print at the middle of the room; a new controlled value pulls the line there.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, scroll or key that brought a new print to the middle.

props.name: onUnclip
props.description: Fires when a print is unclipped to the front (its index) and when it goes back (null).

props.name: spacing
props.description: Distance between prints on the line, px; the loop is always wider than the room.

props.name: scroll
props.description: The page's scroll (or the nearest scroll container's) pulls the line too.

props.name: light
props.description: The safelight's colour, any CSS colour.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the line for assistive technology.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the line but takes no pulls, clicks or keys.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the room (default h-56 w-full).

usageNotes: Keyboard: the prints are one tab stop with roving focus — Left and Right pull the line a print and focus travels with it, Home and End go to the first and last, Enter or Space unclips. The front print is a dialog: focus moves to Back on the line, Tab stays there, and Escape (prevented) clips it back and returns focus to the print.

Gestures: a horizontal drag with `touch-action: pan-y`, so the page still scrolls vertically on touch; a sideways wheel or trackpad swipe over the room pulls the line, and with `scroll` the page's own scroll winds it half as far without ever being taken from the page.
Reduced motion: nothing swings or twists and nothing flies; the line steps to the nearest print, keys move it in place, and the unclipped print fades in and out of the front.

Performance: DOM and SVG with one rAF loop writing transforms to the print nodes only while the line, a pendulum or a peg is moving, on screen and with the tab visible; it stops at rest. The page-scroll listener is passive.

The room is fixed darkroom art (a warm near-black wall, the safelight's glow, prints tinted by its light), so it reads the same on a light or dark page; `light` changes the lamp and the tint together.

items.title: Fresnel Sheet
items.tagline: Slide a ridged lens sheet to see the picture below.
items.description: A flat plastic Fresnel magnifier lying on a printed chart, drawn in one WebGL2 pass: through its concentric ridges a second picture, the same bay from the air, shows magnified about the sheet's centre and broken into rings, each flat facet a little out of register with its neighbours and fringed with rainbow where red and blue bend differently, while the risers catch the lamp, an anisotropic sheen fans across the rings and a glare band fixed in the room slides over the plastic. The sheet follows a drag 1:1 with its shadow lifting on the flick spring, and on release slides on with the release velocity and stops on friction, meeting the edge with a soft bounce on the snap spring; a tap on the chart glides it there on glide. The arrow keys move it (Shift for larger steps) and Home centres it.

props.name: src
props.description: The picture the sheet lies on; for WebGL it must be same-origin or CORS. Defaults to a drawn chart of a bay.

props.name: alt
props.defaultValue: a description of the drawn chart
props.description: What that picture shows, for assistive technology.

props.name: revealSrc
props.description: The picture seen through the sheet, magnified about its centre. Defaults to the same bay drawn from the air.

props.name: revealAlt
props.defaultValue: a description of the drawn aerial view
props.description: What the picture through the sheet shows.

props.name: rings
props.description: How many concentric facets the sheet has, 4 (coarse steps) to 40 (fine ridges).

props.name: magnify
props.description: How much the sheet magnifies, 1.2 to 4.

props.name: glare
props.description: How bright the glare band and the ridges' sheen are, 0 (matte) to 1.

props.name: dispersion
props.description: How strong the rainbow fringes are at each facet's edge, 0 to 1.

props.name: shape
props.description: A credit-card sheet or a round one.

props.name: size
props.description: The sheet's height as a share of the stage's, 0.4 to 1.

props.name: friction
props.description: How quickly a thrown sheet stops, 0 (a long glide on smooth paper) to 1 (a quick stop).

props.name: position / defaultPosition
props.description: The sheet's centre as fractions of the stage; a new controlled value glides it there.

props.name: onPositionChange
props.description: Fires from the drag, tap or key that moved the sheet, with where it will come to rest.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the sheet for assistive technology.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the sheet but takes no drags, taps or keys.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the stage (default h-56 w-full).

usageNotes: Keyboard: the sheet is a focusable group — the arrow keys move it 4% of the stage (16% with Shift) on the glide spring and Home centres it, through the same path that reports the position; a polite status names where it settled.
Touch: only the sheet itself takes `touch-action: none`, so the page still scrolls when a finger lands on the chart around it; a tap on the chart sends the sheet there.
Reduced motion: the sheet still follows a drag 1:1, but a release leaves it where it is (no slide or bounce), keys and taps move it in place, and the lift shadow switches instead of springing.

Performance: one fullscreen pass with two textures, drawn only while the sheet, its lift or a prop changes, on screen and with the tab visible — nothing runs at rest. DPR is capped at `dpr` and context loss rebuilds.

Without WebGL2 (and as the server's first frame) a CSS sheet shows the second picture magnified by background-size, with repeating radial ring lines and a glare gradient; both default pictures are fixed art, so the stage reads the same in light and dark.

items.title: Theatre Scrims
items.tagline: Pass through painted gauzes that turn clear.
items.description: Painted gauzes hanging one behind another on a dark stage, drawn in one WebGL2 pass, with an eye that dollies through them as the page scrolls: each gauze is front-lit and solid while you are far from it, and as you approach its front light falls and the light behind it rises, so the painting fades to a faint image on glowing, uneven threads and the next scene, now lit, shows through small and deep in the frame. Passing through, the gauze billows toward you and ripples behind you, and the last painting is a solid back cloth; the shown progress follows the scroll on a critically damped spring with the glide constants, over a floor of boards with pools of light and haze lit by shafts from the flies. Down, Page Down and Space go to the next scene, Up and Page Up back, Home and End to either end.

props.name: items
props.type: { src?: string; alt: string; caption?: string }[]
props.description: The paintings, front to back; the last is always the back cloth. The default is six scenes painted in code.

props.name: layers
props.description: How many layers hang on the stage, 2 to 6: the first gauzes and the back cloth.

props.name: haze
props.description: How smoky the stage is, 0 (clear air) to 1 (beams standing in the haze).

props.name: lighting
props.description: The lighting design: warm tungsten, cool moonlight or a dusk of rose and violet.

props.name: ripple
props.description: How much a gauze billows and ripples as you pass through it, 0 to 1.

props.name: weave
props.description: How brightly the gauze's threads glow when lit from behind, 0 to 1.

props.name: range
props.description: Scroll distance from one scene to the next, px.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the pinned stage, px; give it the height of the scroll container it sits in.

props.name: proscenium
props.description: Frame the stage with a proscenium and lay a floor of boards.

props.name: onLayerChange
props.description: Fires with the scene in view, from the scroll or key that moved it.

props.name: onProgressChange
props.description: Fires as you dolly forward, 0 (the first gauze) to 1 (the back cloth).

props.name: label
props.description: Names the stage for assistive technology.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the section.

usageNotes: Place it inside a scroll container (or the page) and give `height` that container's visible height: the section is height + range × (layers − 1) tall and its stage sticks while you dolly through.

Keyboard: the stage is one focusable group — Down, Page Down and Space go to the next scene, Up and Page Up back, Home and End to the ends — by scrolling the container, so pointer and keyboard reach the same states. Each painting's description and title is in an sr-only list and a polite status names the scene on arrival.

Reduced motion: no dolly and no ripple; the current painting stands front-lit in the frame and cross-fades to the next as the scroll passes each gauze. The same cross-fade is the fallback without WebGL2 and the server's first frame.

Performance: one fullscreen pass and one atlas texture (up to six paintings), drawn only while the progress or a ripple is changing, on screen and with the tab visible; nothing runs at rest. DPR is capped at `dpr` and context loss rebuilds.
The stage is fixed theatre art (a dark house, lit paintings), so it reads the same on a light or dark page; `lighting` changes the front light, the backlight and the haze together.

items.title: Slate Courses
items.tagline: Tiles lay themselves in courses until it reads.
items.description: A roof, face on, that a roofer slates as the page scrolls: slates fly in from above and toward you and lay themselves in courses from the eaves up, each course lapping the head of the one below and breaking joint by half a slate, working left to right on one course and back on the next, so a picture with a headline painted across it reads only once the courses are on. A slate's travel glides in on the glide spring and its scale lands on recoil, a small settle with a clack when sound is on; when the last course is laid a slow sheen crosses the roof, and scrolling back lifts the slates off top course first on exit tweens. Down, Page Down and Space lay the next course, Up and Page Up lift the top one, and Home and End lift all or lay all.

props.name: headline
props.description: The words painted across the roof; also the heading assistive technology reads.

props.name: as
props.description: The element that carries the headline for assistive technology.

props.name: src
props.description: The picture the slates are cut from; defaults to a drawn farm valley at evening.

props.name: alt
props.defaultValue: a description of the drawn valley
props.description: What the picture shows, for assistive technology.

props.name: courses
props.description: How many courses the roof has, 4 (a few big slates) to 10 (many small ones).

props.name: overlap
props.description: How much of each slate the course above covers, 0.2 (a long exposed tail) to 0.6 (a deep lap).

props.name: stagger
props.description: How far apart the slates of a course land, 0 (together) to 1 (one by one across).

props.name: cut
props.description: The shape of each slate's tail.

props.name: startCourses
props.description: How many courses are on before any scroll, 0 to 3.

props.name: paint
props.description: The colour of the sign paint, a concrete CSS colour (the paint is an image, so not a var).

props.name: range
props.description: Scroll distance for the whole roof, px.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the pinned stage, px; give it the height of the scroll container it sits in.

props.name: sound
props.description: Play a clack as each slate lands.

props.name: onCoursesChange
props.description: Fires with the number of whole courses laid, from the scroll or key that changed it.

props.name: onProgressChange
props.description: Fires as the roof is laid, 0 to 1.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the section.

usageNotes: Place it inside a scroll container (or the page) and give `height` that container's visible height: the section is height + range tall and its stage sticks while the courses go on. The headline is chalked on the felt before any slate is laid, so the first frame always reads.

Keyboard: the roof is one focusable group — Down, Page Down and Space lay the next course, Up and Page Up lift the top one, Home and End lift all or lay all — by scrolling the container. The headline is a real heading and the picture's description is sr-only; a polite status says how many courses are laid and when the roof is complete.
Reduced motion: no flights, settles or sheen; slates appear in place course by course on an opacity fade and fade out when lifted, while the count and callbacks still update.

Sound: `clack` as slates land, panned to where they land and played only after the visitor has clicked, tapped or pressed a key on the page (a scroll is not an activation); one per course under reduced motion.

Performance: DOM slates sharing two background images through CSS variables (the paint SVG is regenerated only on resize or a new headline); one passive, frame-coalesced scroll listener; the laid count is the only state the scroll changes, and animations run only while slates are in flight.

items.title: Raking Light
items.tagline: A low light that skims the surface for texture.
items.description: An object on a light table, relit per pixel in WebGL2 by a lamp that lies low at its side, so the light skims the surface and every ridge throws a long shadow marched through a height map toward the lamp: the brush ridges of an oil sketch, a plate mark, an embossed fern and a blind-stamp in paper that look blank in flat light, the wedges in a clay tablet, or your own photo. The pointer's direction from the centre is the light's direction and its distance from the rim is its height, so moving in raises the light and flattens the shadows; the direction follows on springs.glide, the height on springs.drift, a click sets the lamp down with the marker landing on springs.recoil, and the first time it is seen the light comes down from overhead and the relief rises out of a flat picture. On the keyboard, Left and Right orbit the lamp and Up and Down raise and lower it.

props.name: subject
props.description: The object on the table, drawn in code: an oil sketch, a sheet of embossed paper or a clay tablet.

props.name: src
props.description: Your own photograph to relight instead (it must be readable across origins). Its height comes from depthSrc, or from its brightness.

props.name: depthSrc
props.description: A depth map for src, white for high, black for low.

props.name: alt
props.description: What the image shows, for assistive technology. Each subject has its own description by default.

props.name: inscription
props.description: The words pressed around the paper's blind-stamp.

props.name: elevation
props.description: The raking angle: how many degrees above the surface the light skims when it lies at the edge, 2 to 40.

props.name: relief
props.description: How tall the surface's ridges stand, 0 (flat print) to 1 (deep relief).

props.name: warmth
props.description: The light's colour, 0 (cool north daylight) to 1 (warm tungsten); the shadows fill with the other.

props.name: softness
props.description: The lamp's size, 0 (a pin-point with crisp shadows) to 1 (a softbox with soft ones).

props.name: gloss
props.description: How much the surface glints where it faces the light, 0 (matte) to 1.

props.name: azimuth / defaultAzimuth
props.description: The direction the resting light comes from, degrees clockwise from the top; controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: onAzimuthChange
props.description: Fires when a click, a tap or the arrow keys set the light down in a new direction, in whole degrees.

props.name: onLightChange
props.type: (light: { azimuth: number; elevation: number; held: boolean }) => void
props.description: Fires as the hand moves the lamp, with the light it is asking for, in whole degrees.

props.name: intro
props.description: The light comes down from overhead to its raking angle the first time the object is seen.

props.name: showLamp
props.description: Show a small lamp where the light comes from while it is held.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer and the keyboard move the lamp.

props.name: seed
props.description: Seeds the brushstrokes, the paper's fibres and the wedges in the clay.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the lamp control.

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes and shapes the box.

usageNotes: Give the box a height (the default is h-56 w-full). The object is laid out for the box's own aspect and baked once — on first sight, and again only when the subject, seed, inscription, image, palette or size changes (size changes wait 140 ms for the resize to stop).

Keyboard: one focus stop. Left and Right orbit the lamp 15° (PageUp and PageDown 45°) and set that direction as the rest; Up and Down raise and lower it, Home lays it low and End lifts it overhead; blur lets it sink back to elevation. A polite live region reads the light once the keys settle.

Pointer: hovering holds the lamp, a click sets it down facing that way (onAzimuthChange), leaving lets it sink back. On touch, a sideways drag moves the lamp and lifting the finger sets it down; an upright swipe still scrolls the page.

Reduced motion: no intro and no springs — the light goes straight where the pointer or keys put it and sinks back at once; the object is still fully relit, because direction and height are information.

Cost: one fullscreen WebGL2 draw per frame only while the light moves, none when settled, off screen or in a hidden tab; the height buffer is half-float where it can be rendered, DPR capped at dpr. Without WebGL2, or after a lost context, a CSS still of the object washed from the resting side stays.

Bring your own photo with src (and depthSrc for a real depth map); it must be same-origin or served with CORS, and if it cannot be read the drawn subject is shown instead. The subjects' colours are pigments at fixed lightness, so they look the same in either theme.

items.title: Monospace Pond
items.tagline: A paragraph you can stir like still water.
items.description: A paragraph of monospaced text that is also the surface of a pond: the words stay real, selectable DOM text, and a canvas redraws every character from a glyph atlas where the page laid it out, riding a damped wave equation simulated one character wide with walls that reflect. Swells shoulder the letters toward their crests and lift them, the crests turn them into denser glyphs from the ramp in the crest's ink while troughs thin the ink, and when the energy is gone the original text is drawn exactly again. The pointer drags a trough and its wake through the water as hard as it is quick; a click, a tap, Enter or keyboard focus drops a stone that falls, dents the surface and rings outward under a hairline ring while a crown of droplet glyphs hops out, and the arrow keys move a fingertip that glides between characters on springs.snap while Escape smooths the water away on springs.glide.

props.name: text
props.description: The paragraph. Line breaks in it are kept; spaces wrap as usual.

props.name: as
props.description: The element the paragraph renders as.

props.name: damping
props.description: How quickly the water settles, 0 (rings for seconds and rebounds off the edges) to 1 (settles like syrup).

props.name: ramp
props.description: The glyphs a crest turns letters into, light to dense: a named ramp or your own string.

props.name: depth
props.description: How deep the pond is, 0 to 1: deeper water carries waves faster and bends the letters further.

props.name: stir
props.description: How hard the pointer drags waves through the text, 0 to 1.

props.name: radius
props.description: The pointer's footprint in characters, 1 to 6.

props.name: stone
props.description: How big a dropped stone is, 0 to 1.

props.name: crest
props.description: How readily crests swap letters for ramp glyphs, 0 (only the highest) to 1 (any swell).

props.name: foam
props.description: Word gaps froth with the lightest glyph on strong crests, so a ring reads across them.

props.name: ring
props.description: A hairline ring rides out from every stone with the wavefront.

props.name: color
props.description: The ink of the text at rest.

props.name: crestColor
props.description: The ink the crests, the foam and the ring mix toward.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The pointer, touch and keyboard disturb the water.

props.name: paused
props.description: Freeze the water where it is; it ignores the hand until unpaused.

props.name: intro
props.description: One stone drops by itself the first time the paragraph is seen.

props.name: seed
props.description: Where the intro stone falls and how a stone's droplets fly.

props.name: dpr
props.description: Cap on the canvas's device pixel ratio, at most 2.

props.name: label
props.description: The pond's accessible name.

props.name: onStone
props.description: Fires for every stone a click, a tap, Enter or keyboard focus drops, with its line and column (from 0).

props.name: onCalmChange
props.description: Fires when the water starts to move (false) and when it is still again (true).

props.name: className
props.description: Sizes the box and sets its type: the font size is inherited.

usageNotes: The paragraph is the real text — read once by assistive technology, selectable and copyable; the canvas under it is aria-hidden and only takes over drawing once it is ready, so the server render and any failure show plain text.

Keyboard: the pond is one focus stop (role group, roledescription pond). Focus drops a gentle stone where the fingertip rests; Left and Right move the fingertip a character, Up and Down a line, Home and End to the line's ends, stirring as it goes; Enter or Space drops a stone; Escape smooths the water away (and is left alone when the water is already still).
Reduced motion: nothing travels and nothing is displaced. A stone leaves a still ring of swapped glyphs and a hairline ring that cross-fade back to the text; the pointer leaves the text alone.

Cost: the water is a few thousand cells stepped at 120 Hz and the text a few hundred atlas draws a frame, only while the water moves, on screen and in a visible tab; settled, it draws the clean text once and stops. Layout and atlas rebuild on resize, font load and colour change; DPR capped at dpr.

Type: the font size is inherited and padding is in em, so it works from a caption to a lead paragraph. Positions come from the page's own layout, so any font works, though the swapped glyphs line up best in a monospaced one. Colours default to tokens and re-read on a theme change.

items.title: Spur Columns
items.tagline: Follow any phrase into its own column.
items.description: An assistant thread where any phrase becomes its own column: choose a dotted phrase in an answer, or select any words and ask about them, and the phrase is lifted out as a chip and carried to the new column's header on springs.glide — landing exactly, because the destination comes from the computed layout rather than a mid-flight measure — while the new column grows in and the older ones narrow to readable spines on the same spring. Every column has its own skeleton, empty and failed states and its own follow-up composer, answered through answerFor (which may return a promise). Left and Right walk the columns, Escape folds the rightmost back into its phrase on the exit ease and returns focus there, and under 520px the columns become a stack that follows a sideways swipe 1:1, rubber-bands at the ends and commits by projection with the trail shown as chips.

props.name: columns / defaultColumns
props.description: Columns left to right, controlled or initial: { id, phrase?, parentId?, turns: { id, prompt, status: "loading" | "ready" | "empty" | "failed", answer?: { text, phrases? } }[] }.

props.name: onColumnsChange
props.description: Fires with every column after an open, a fold, an ask or an arriving answer.

props.name: answerFor
props.description: Answers a spur's phrase or a follow-up ({ columnId, phrase?, kind: "spur" | "ask" }). null shows the empty state; a rejected promise shows the failed state with Try again.

props.name: onAsk
props.description: A follow-up was asked in a column's composer.

props.name: onOpenSpur
props.description: A spur was opened from a suggested phrase or a selection.

props.name: onCloseSpur
props.description: A spur, and any spurs opened from it, was folded back (Escape or its close button).

props.name: active / defaultActive
props.description: The active column id, controlled or initial. The active column always stays open.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Fires from the key, spine, chip, phrase or swipe that changed the active column.

props.name: columnWidth
props.description: The width older open columns hold, in px — the newest column takes the rest — and the width a column needs to stay open; columns that no longer fit narrow to spines, oldest first.

props.name: spineWidth
props.description: A spine's width in px.

props.name: spineStyle
props.description: Spines read their phrase set vertically, show a large number with a dot per turn, or a slim accent bar under the number.

props.name: accent
props.description: Phrase marks, the carried chip, spines, the active column's edge, trail chips and Send — any CSS colour.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: Below this container width (px) the columns become a swipeable stack with a trail of chips.

props.name: allowSelection
props.description: Selecting words in an answer offers "Ask about this" above the selection.

props.name: maxPhrase
props.description: The longest selection, in characters, that can become a spur.

props.name: title
props.description: The first column's heading and the region's name.

props.name: status / onRetry
props.description: Loading shows skeleton columns; error shows a message and Try again, which calls onRetry.

props.name: height
props.description: The surface's height in px; each column scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: columns can be walked and read; nothing can be opened, folded or asked.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer section.

usageNotes: Keyboard: suggested phrases are buttons ("Ask about SSO") — the keyboard path to a spur; Left and Right walk the columns and focus each header; Escape folds the rightmost spur and returns focus to the phrase it came from. On a phone the trail chips are tabs.
Answers can be async: return a promise from answerFor and the column shows a skeleton until it settles; resolve null for the empty state, reject for the failed state with Try again.
Reduced motion: no chip flight, no width glides and no stack slide — headers appear, columns resize at once and the skeleton does not shimmer; phrase marks and column numbers still show.
Nothing runs at rest: one ResizeObserver reads the container, the layout is computed from it, and the skeleton's shimmer exists only while a column is loading.

The layout follows its container: from stackBelow up it is a row of columns and spines; below it, a stack that follows the finger 1:1 with touch-action pan-y so vertical scrolling inside a column still works.

items.title: Ask Back
items.tagline: It asks what it needs before it answers.
items.description: An assistant thread that clarifies before it writes: the open request gets two to four questions as chip sets, and each settled chip lifts off and flies into its slot on the pinned brief on springs.glide, its box morphing to the slot as the value cross-fades in. When the last answer lands the brief is stamped Complete on springs.recoil and the real answer streams in; questions deal in on springs.snap and chips press on springs.flick. Each chip set is a radiogroup (arrows move the pick, Enter settles it and moves on), Skip and Write it now answer on stated assumptions, a brief slot reopens its question and Backspace in an empty composer reopens the last one.

usageNotes: Keyboard: each chip set is one tab stop; arrow keys move the tentative pick, Enter or Space settles it and focus flows to the next open question. Brief slots reopen their question, Backspace in an empty composer reopens the last settled one, and Escape closes the narrow brief list.
Reduced motion: nothing flies or bounces — values cross-fade into the brief, the stamp fades in at rest, questions appear without travel and the answer appears whole. Counts and states still update.

Performance: no loops at rest. The stream is a 100 ms interval that runs only while the answer is incomplete, the surface is on screen and the page is visible; each flight is one element removed when it lands.

Theming: every colour is a token except `accent`, which tints chips, the flight, the brief and the stamp in both themes. Pass `briefPlacement` to suit the host layout; under 26rem the brief folds into a count badge.
Data: questions, the answer text and every decision are props and callbacks, so a host can drive the questions from its own model and stream its own answer.

items.title: Chart Talk
items.tagline: Ask a question; the chart answers and changes.
items.description: A conversation with a dataset where the answer is one living chart: each follow-up morphs the same chart on springs.glide — bars split into stacked region segments that start as the whole bar, months gather into their quarter, a filter widens the bars that stay while the rest sink on the exit ease, and lines and areas morph point by point — while the axis and the total count to the new range on the same spring. The thread keeps one line and a thumbnail per turn, its selection bar sliding on springs.snap; loading, no-rows and query errors are drawn on the chart. The thread is a listbox: arrow keys step turns and the chart follows, Home and End jump, Enter selects.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the thread is one tab stop; Up/Down and Left/Right step turns with the chart following, Home and End jump, Enter or Space selects. Suggestions and the composer ask new questions; Export is a button.

Reduced motion: geometry cuts straight to each answer and new marks fade in where they belong; leaving marks fade in place and the selection bar moves without travel. Values, labels and totals still change.
Accessibility: the chart is a role="img" with a summary sentence and an sr-only table of every value; each answer and rewind is announced once.

Performance: no loops. Marks are springs that settle; the SVG uses a fixed viewBox with non-scaling strokes, so resizing costs nothing, and axis numbers count by writing their own text nodes rather than re-rendering.
Theming: the series ramp mixes the accent toward the card colour, so stacked segments read in both themes; pass any CSS colour as `accent`.

items.title: Hint Ladder
items.tagline: Help that holds back until you ask.
items.description: A tutoring thread that answers with a ladder of hints instead of the solution: rungs are dealt face down on springs.snap in a cascade, and each turns over only when asked — a 180° flip on springs.snap with the hint on the far side of the card — while the ladder's rail fills on springs.glide with how much help was used. The worked answer waits behind a bar that fills linearly while held and drains back on springs.snap if let go, then unfolds to its measured height on springs.glide; checking the learner's working marks it line by line with ticks and crosses that draw on springs.flick. H turns the next hint, holding Space on the bar reveals the answer, and under 23rem the rungs become one deck you swipe up or press Enter on.

props.name: solution

usageNotes: Keyboard: H turns the next hint from anywhere outside a text field and focus moves on to the next Turn over button (or the hold bar); hold Space or Enter on the bar to reveal the answer; ⌘/Ctrl+Enter in the working box checks it. In the narrow deck, Enter or Arrow Up moves forward and Arrow Down goes back.

Reduced motion: cards cross-fade instead of turning, the deck swaps without travel, the hold bar still fills (it is the timer) but drains at once, and marks appear without drawing. The rail still fills.

Accessibility: a face-down card never puts its hint in the page, so assistive tech cannot read ahead; the rail is a role="meter" of help used, each mark is spoken as a sentence, and a click from assistive technology on the hold bar reveals at once.
Performance: nothing runs at rest; the hold is one linear animation stopped on release, and the deck drag goes through the shared gesture kit with capture only after 4px.
Data: checks match the last number on each line within a tolerance, so a host can teach any numeric exercise by passing its own steps and common slips.

items.title: Meeting Recall
items.tagline: Ask what was decided; jump to the moment.
items.description: Questions asked of a recorded meeting, with its waveform and transcript docked beside the thread: every claim in an answer carries a timestamp chip, and pressing one glides the waveform's playhead to the moment on springs.glide while the transcript scrolls its own box there and a highlight sweeps across each supporting line in turn. Claims arrive on springs.snap, chips press on springs.flick, and a claim nothing supports shows a dashed No source mark. Tab moves through the chips and Enter seeks, K plays and pauses, the waveform is a slider (drag, arrows, Page keys, Home/End), and under 40rem the transcript is a sheet that rises on springs.glide.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab moves through the timestamp chips and Enter seeks; the transcript is one tab stop whose lines rove with Up/Down and Home/End; K plays and pauses from anywhere outside a text field; the waveform is a role="slider" (arrows ±5 s, Page Up/Down ±30 s, Home/End). On narrow surfaces a chip raises the transcript sheet and focuses it, and Escape lowers it and returns focus to the chip.
Reduced motion: the playhead and the transcript jump instead of gliding, the highlight fades in whole, claims arrive without travel and the sheet fades. Playback still advances — it is the content.

Performance: the playhead is one motion value written straight into the clip, the line and the clock, so playing re-renders only once a second; the frame loop runs only while playing, on screen and with the page visible, and the waveform's bar count follows its width (3px a bar, the gap dropped below 2.5px).
Data: claims cite segment ids, so a host can point any answer at the exact lines that support it; a claim with no refs is drawn as unsupported rather than hidden.
Theming: every surface colour is a token; `accent` tints the chips, the played wave, the supporting bands and the sweep in both themes.

items.title: Widget Thread
items.tagline: Replies you can use, not just read.
items.description: An assistant whose replies are small live controls — a quantity stepper, a compare table, a slot picker, a confirm card — each assembling out of a skeleton block by block, every block rising a nudge on springs.snap in a cascade. Whatever is chosen inside a widget lifts out and becomes the next sent message: a copy of the chosen thing travels to the new bubble on springs.glide, its box morphing from the control to the bubble as its fill warms to the bubble colour, while the widget fades to a read-only record with the choice ticked on springs.flick. Each widget is one tab stop with its own keyboard path (radiogroup, spinbutton, roving table buttons, roving confirm buttons), so Tab leaves it for the composer, where typing an option's name answers it too.

usageNotes: Keyboard: every open widget is a single tab stop — slots are a radiogroup (arrows move, Enter or Space chooses), the stepper a spinbutton (arrows, Page keys, Home/End, Enter sends), the compare table's Choose buttons and the confirm card's buttons rove with Left/Right. Tab leaves for the composer, and focus follows into each new widget only if it was already in the thread.
Reduced motion: nothing flies or rises — your bubble appears where it lands, the skeleton swaps to the whole widget in one cross-fade, and the widget still greys into its record.

Data: widget specs are typed (slots, stepper, compare, confirm) and may carry expiresIn minutes; an open widget past its time against `now` shows an expired state with Refresh, which fires onRetry and posts it again.
Performance: no loops. The flight is one imperative animation on a single reused element, assembly is a short chain of timeouts per reply, and every timer and glide is cleared on unmount.
Narrow surfaces: compare tables scroll sideways inside their bubble with an edge fade and become focusable when they scroll; the surface itself never scrolls sideways.

items.title: Council Table
items.tagline: Several specialists, one conversation.
items.description: An AI chat answered by a council of specialists seated along an arc above the thread. When the floor changes, a baton travels round the arc to the new seat on springs.snap — position and tilt derived from one motion value, so it passes the seats between — and that seat rises on the same spring while its reply enters the thread on springs.glide; a reply that disagrees with an earlier one draws a thin bracket back up the gutter to the message it disputes on glide. The seats are a toolbar (arrows walk the arc, Enter addresses, Delete dismisses), @ in the composer opens the council as a listbox, and under 34rem the arc flattens into a row of avatars.

props.name: seatShape

props.name: density
props.description: Seat size, the arc's height, type size and spacing.

props.name: accent
props.description: Any CSS colour for the baton, the floor ring, the addressee chip, lit brackets and Send.

props.name: specialists

props.name: status

usageNotes: Seats are a toolbar with a roving tabindex: Left/Right (or Up/Down) walk the arc, Home/End jump, Enter or Space addresses a seat and moves focus to the composer, Delete dismisses it. In the composer @ opens a listbox of the council (Up/Down, Enter or Tab to pick, Escape closes), Backspace at the start clears the addressee, Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks a line.

The thread is a role="log" around an ordered list, so a turn is announced once when it arrives; floor changes and failures are announced politely as one sentence. Dispute chips are buttons that scroll to and focus the disputed message.
Under reduced motion the baton jumps to its seat, the floor is marked by its ring, and replies, summaries and brackets fade in whole; thinking dots hold still.

The baton is one motion value whose change event writes x, y and rotation, so nothing re-renders per frame; two ResizeObservers (the arc and the thread) are bound by callback ref, and nothing runs at rest.
Layout follows the component's own width through a container query: at 34rem and over the council sits on the arc, below it the arc flattens into a row of avatars with the baton on a straight track.
Colours come from tokens; `accent` takes any CSS colour and is mixed in oklab for its wash and line, so it reads in both themes.

items.title: Assumption Pins
items.tagline: Fix one assumption; only that part rewrites.
items.description: An AI answer with the assumptions it rests on pinned beside it, every sentence linked to the pins it depends on: focusing a pin lights its sentences and draws a comb across the gutter to them on springs.glide. Editing a pin re-runs the answer, but only the sentences whose words change dissolve in place on the exit ease and stream back word by word while the rest hold still, each keeping an underline that sweeps in on glide; a paragraph whose line count changed glides to its new height, and two pins that contradict are bracketed together while Use this answer waits with the reason. Pins are a roving list — arrows move, Enter edits inline, Escape cancels or reverts — and under 40rem they become a strip of chips above the answer.

props.name: highlight

props.name: accent

props.name: onReload

props.name: rerunDelay

props.name: streamSpeed

props.name: underlineHold

props.name: height
props.description: The surface's height in px; the answer scrolls inside it.

props.name: className

usageNotes: Pins are a list with a roving tabindex: arrow keys move between them, Home/End jump, Enter opens the inline editor (a radiogroup of options, or a number field), Enter commits and Escape cancels; Escape on a changed pin reverts it. Focus returns to the pin after every edit.

Each rewrite is announced once, when it settles ("Team size changed to 5 engineers. 4 sentences rewritten."), and a conflict's reason is announced with it; Use this answer stays focusable and aria-disabled with the reason while a conflict stands.
Under reduced motion a rewrite is a cross-fade with no blur or word-by-word stream, the underline appears at full width and fades, and the comb fades in; lit sentences still light.

Sentence ids must be stable across values — that is what lets only the changed sentences move. A rewrite runs one timer chain; a newer edit cancels it and starts from what is on screen, and nothing runs at rest.

Layout follows the component's own width: at 40rem and over the pins sit in a column beside the answer with the comb in the gutter; below it they become a horizontal strip of chips that edit in place.

items.title: Detail Dial

items.description: One AI answer with a depth dial beside it, from one line to a thorough brief. Turning the dial does not swap texts: every word is a layout element, so the sentences you have read glide apart on springs.glide to make room and the new ones unfurl into the gaps word by word, while the pane holds the sentence you are reading where it was; turning it down folds the extra sentences away on the exit ease and closes the gaps on the same glide. The dial is a real slider — dragged round 1:1 with a rubber band past the ends and a settle on springs.snap that carries the release velocity, or stepped with the arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down, Home, End and the number keys — and under 36rem it becomes a segmented control above the answer.

props.name: unfurlSpeed

props.name: accent

props.name: answer
