props.name: status
props.description: Loading draws skeleton lines; error offers Try again.

props.name: onReload
props.description: Try again was pressed after the answer failed to load.

props.name: model
props.description: The assistant answering, named in the header.

props.name: wordsPerMinute
props.description: Reading speed behind the time estimate under the dial.

props.name: height
props.description: The surface's height in px; the answer scrolls inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The dial cannot be turned.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: The dial is role="slider" with a spoken value ("Level 3 of 4, Full, 111 words"): Right/Up deepen, Left/Down shorten, Page Up and Page Down jump two, Home and End go to the ends, and 1–4 jump straight to a level. Below 36rem a radiogroup segmented control takes the same keys. Additions and removals are announced once, after they settle ("3 sentences added.").
Under reduced motion there is no word travel and no stagger: new text fades in whole, leaving text fades out, the knob jumps to its detent — and the reading position still holds.
Sentence ids must be stable across levels; a deeper level must contain every sentence of the shallower ones. That is what lets the text grow instead of being replaced.
Words FLIP only on a depth change; a drag writes one motion value and commits depth only when it crosses a detent's midpoint. There are no observers and nothing runs at rest.
Return a promise from onDepthChange to fetch or generate a deeper level lazily: the dial holds at the new detent with its arc pulsing and a writing line where the answer ends until it resolves.

items.title: Brief Blocks
items.tagline: Build a prompt from parts you can rearrange.
items.description: A prompt composer built from labelled blocks — role, goal, context, constraints, format — added from a rail, filled and dragged into order: the grip follows the pointer 1:1, the other blocks glide out of its way on springs.glide, and the released block settles into its slot carrying the throw. Preview threads the blocks into one readable prompt: every word is a shared layout element, so each block's text slides out of its card into its place in the sentence on glide, block after block a cascade apart, while each label flies to the margin beside its line as a faint tag; Edit slides the words back before the text fields return. Alt with the arrow keys moves a block, Cmd or Ctrl+Enter sends, empty blocks are flagged, and a brief over its limit marks the longest block as the one to cut.

props.name: blockStyle
props.description: Blocks drawn as filled cards, flush strips with a coloured edge, or bare dashed outlines.

props.name: ribbonFont
props.description: The threaded ribbon's typeface.

props.name: accent
props.description: Any CSS colour for the active block's edge, the meter, segment hovers in the ribbon and Send.

props.name: blocks / defaultBlocks
props.description: The blocks in order (id, kind, text), controlled or initial.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires from every edit, add, remove, move and preset with the whole list.

props.name: kinds
props.description: The kinds the rail offers: id, label, hint, placeholder, and whether only one is allowed.

props.name: presets
props.description: Saved starting points for the preset menu.

props.name: onSavePreset
props.description: Save as preset was confirmed with a name; the preset joins the menu.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Send (or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter) with every block filled and the brief within maxLength.

props.name: assemble
props.description: Turns the blocks into the prompt that is sent; by default labelled paragraphs.

props.name: mode / defaultMode
props.description: The block editor or the threaded ribbon, controlled or initial.

props.name: onModeChange
props.description: Fires from the Edit/Preview switch (or a press on a ribbon segment) that changed the view.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: The longest brief Send accepts, in characters; over it the meter turns red and the longest block is marked.

props.name: status
props.description: Holds Send busy while the host sends.

props.name: title
props.description: The brief's name in the header.

props.name: height
props.description: The surface's height in px; the blocks scroll inside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be edited, moved or sent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the block you are typing in (Up and Down on its grip do the same), each move announced; the rail is a toolbar walked with Up and Down, and below 40rem it becomes a + menu (arrows, Home/End, Enter, Escape). Cmd or Ctrl+Enter sends from anywhere inside; with an empty block it focuses that block instead, and over the limit it focuses the longest one.

Edit and Preview are a two-radio group; threading takes two commits (text fields become word-for-word mirrors, then the ribbon takes their words), and focus returns to the block you were in once the text fields are back.
Under reduced motion the ribbon and reorders cross-fade with no word travel, new blocks fade in and the grip lift is a shadow only.
Words exist as separate elements only while the ribbon is shown or in flight; a drag writes one motion value and nothing runs at rest.

Layout follows the component's own width: at 40rem and over the rail sits beside the blocks and the ribbon's labels stand in a margin column; below it the rail is a menu and the labels sit inline before their text.

items.title: Scribble Prompt
items.tagline: Draw what you mean, then say it.
items.description: A prompt composer with a sketch pad that opens beside the text field, where boxes, arrows and loose pen marks — drawn by pointer, by pen with its pressure, or placed with the arrow keys — become part of the request, each landing with a flick of its weight on springs.flick. Attaching docks the drawing: the paper lifts off the pad and shrinks on springs.glide into a thumbnail chip in the field with its strokes still visible, and pressing the chip grows it back out into the pad on the same spring. Cmd or Ctrl+Z undoes a stroke, an empty pad keeps Attach disabled and says why, and under 38rem the pad rises as a full-width sheet that a downward flick closes.

props.name: penWidth
props.description: Stroke width for new marks, in drawing units (the pad is 400 wide); a pen's pressure scales it.

props.name: gridStyle
props.description: The pad's paper.

props.name: accent
props.description: Any CSS colour for the active tool, the keyboard crosshair, Attach, Send and the sketch chip's ring.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The message text, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires from every keystroke with the new text.

props.name: strokes / defaultStrokes
props.description: The drawing, controlled or initial: pen marks (points) and boxes and arrows (from, to), each with a colour and width.

props.name: onStrokesChange
props.description: Fires from every stroke, undo, redo and clear with the whole drawing.

props.name: onStrokeEnd
props.description: A stroke was finished, by pointer, pen or keyboard.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the pad is open, controlled or initial; closing a pad with marks on it docks them.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the button, chip, key or drag that opened or closed the pad.

props.name: onAttachSketch
props.description: The sketch was docked into the field.

props.name: attachments / defaultAttachments
props.description: File chips in the field (name and size), controlled or initial.

props.name: onAttachFiles
props.description: Files were picked with Attach file (a real file input).

props.name: onRemoveAttachment
props.description: A file chip's remove button was pressed.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Send (or Enter) with words, a docked sketch or a file.

props.name: messages / defaultMessages
props.description: The thread above the composer, controlled or initial; an uncontrolled send appends to it, sketch thumbnail and all.

props.name: colors
props.defaultValue: ink, accent, warn and success tokens
props.description: Pen colours as CSS colours, offered as a radiogroup.

props.name: assistant
props.description: Who answers, named in the header.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The text field's placeholder.

props.name: height
props.description: The surface's height in px.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be typed, drawn or sent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: The pad is role="application" with keyboard help: arrow keys move a crosshair (Shift for big steps), P, B and A pick pen, box and arrow, Space or Enter anchors a shape and places it (the pen builds a line point by point, Enter finishes), Escape cancels an anchored shape or closes the pad, and Cmd/Ctrl+Z and Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z undo and redo. Closing returns focus to the sketch chip (or the Sketch button), and pressing the chip moves focus back into the pad.
Below 38rem the pad opens as a role="dialog" sheet that keeps Tab inside it; dragging its grab bar down (or flicking it) closes it and docks the sketch.
Under reduced motion the pad and the chip cross-fade, there is no docking flight and marks land without the flick; drawing itself is unchanged.

The live stroke writes one motion value, so drawing re-renders nothing per pointer move; the docking flight is driven entirely by motion values from a layout effect, and nothing runs while the pad is closed.
Pen colours are CSS colours applied as styles, so tokens like var(--warn) follow the theme; the thumbnail uses hairlines that keep their width at any size.

items.title: Prompt Stamp
items.tagline: One prompt, run down every row.
items.description: One prompt with {placeholders} above a small sheet of rows; Run stamps it down the sheet. A plate carrying the prompt's tokens travels down the output column on springs.glide and presses each row on springs.recoil, its tokens turning into that row's values as the mapped cells light up left to right in a cascade, then the answer streams into the cell — and a row with an empty mapped cell is pressed too but fails with the reason instead of an invented answer. Typing { opens a column picker (arrows, Enter or Tab inserts), the sheet is a grid with one roving cell where Enter edits a field and retries or expands an answer, and at phone width each row becomes a card.

props.name: stampSpeed
props.description: How fast the stamp walks the sheet and the answers stream, as a multiplier.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: Row height in px; the answer shows as many lines as fit (1 to 3), and Enter expands a row.

props.name: accent
props.description: Tokens, the stamp, lit cells, Run and done checks — any CSS colour.

props.name: template / defaultTemplate
props.description: The prompt, with {placeholders} naming columns; controlled or initial.

props.name: onTemplateChange
props.description: Fires from every edit and every column inserted from the picker.

props.name: columns
props.description: The sheet's input columns: id (the placeholder name), label and grow.

props.name: rows / defaultRows
props.description: The rows the prompt runs down, each with a value per column id; controlled or initial.

props.name: onRowsChange
props.description: Fires with every row after a cell is edited in place.

props.name: mapping
props.description: Placeholder names that read another column, e.g. { bean: "product" }.

props.name: results / defaultResults
props.description: Run state per row id (idle, queued, running, failed, done, with text and error). Controlled, the host runs the prompt and the sheet shows it.

props.name: onResultsChange
props.description: Fires whenever the built-in run changes a row's state or text.

props.name: respond
props.description: The built-in run's answer for a row and its filled prompt.

props.name: onRun
props.description: Run was pressed: every row's filled prompt.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Stop was pressed during a run.

props.name: onRetryRow
props.description: Retry was pressed on a failed row.

props.name: onExport
props.description: Export was pressed: the sheet with its answers as CSV.

props.name: concurrency
props.description: Rows the built-in run works on at once.

props.name: title
props.description: The sheet's name in the header.

props.name: outputLabel
props.description: The output column's heading.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the rows are here: loading shows a skeleton, error a Try again.

props.name: onReload
props.description: Try again was pressed after the rows failed to load.

props.name: height
props.description: The tallest the surface grows, px; past it the sheet scrolls inside.

props.name: ref
props.description: Imperative handle with run() and stop().

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be edited or run.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: in the prompt, { opens the column picker (Up and Down move, Enter or Tab inserts, Escape closes) and Cmd or Ctrl+Enter runs. The sheet is a grid with one roving cell: arrows move, Home and End jump, Enter or F2 edits a field (Enter saves, Escape cancels), and Enter on an answer retries a failed row or expands a clipped one.

Pass results to run the prompt yourself: mark a row running and the stamp presses it, stream its text through the same object, then mark it done or failed with an error. Without results the built-in run plays respond, and only ticks while the sheet is on screen in a visible tab.
A row whose mapped cell is empty is never sent: it fails with the column's name, the empty cell lights in danger, and editing the cell then Retry runs it.
Reduced motion keeps every state and the word-by-word arrival but drops the travelling stamp and the cascade: rows light in place.
Colours come from tokens and the accent prop, so the sheet reads in light and dark; the fill of Run is the accent at a fixed lightness so it holds its contrast in both.

items.title: Answer Shape
items.tagline: Say what form the answer should take.
items.description: A prompt composer with shape picks under the field — paragraph, bullets, table, email, checklist — and a skeleton of the answer's form beside it, drawn from one fixed set of bars. Choosing a shape moves every bar to its place in the new form on springs.glide, a paragraph's word groups regrouping into a table's rows and columns or folding into an envelope whose flap rotates into a V, while the selection slides on springs.snap and the length rolls on snap. The picks are a radiogroup on the arrow keys with Cmd or Ctrl and 1 to 5 from anywhere in the composer, the length is a spinbutton, a note offers to switch when the prompt itself asks for another form, and on a phone the skeleton shrinks to a live icon beside Send.

props.name: skeletonStyle
props.description: The preview's texture: filled bars, a hairline wireframe, or bars drawn as faux words.

props.name: pickSize
props.description: Icon-only picks, icon and label, or tiles with the icon over the label (icon-only on a phone at every size).

props.name: accent
props.description: Selection, the table header, the checked box and Send — any CSS colour.

props.name: shapes
props.description: The forms on offer: label, kind (skeleton and icon), unit, min, max, step, default length, words per unit, cues, and an optional custom skeleton(length, box).

props.name: shape / defaultShape
props.description: The chosen shape's id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onShapeChange
props.description: Fires from the pick, shortcut or note that changed the shape.

props.name: length / defaultLength
props.description: The answer's length in the current shape's unit, controlled or initial; each shape remembers its own.

props.name: onLengthChange
props.description: Fires with the new length and the shape it belongs to.

props.name: draft / defaultDraft
props.description: The prompt text, controlled or initial.

props.name: onDraftChange
props.description: Fires from every edit.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Enter or Send: the prompt with the form it should take.

props.name: detectConflicts
props.description: Raise a note with Use and Keep when the prompt asks for a different form.

props.name: showPreview
props.description: Show the skeleton preview, or its icon on a phone.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder for an empty field.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's accessible name.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: Lines the field grows to before it scrolls.

props.name: busy
props.description: An answer is being written: Send holds and spins.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be typed, picked or sent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the picks are a radiogroup — arrows move and choose, Home and End jump — and Cmd or Ctrl with 1 to 5 chooses from anywhere in the composer. The length is a spinbutton (Up, Down, Page Up, Page Down, Home, End). Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks the line.
The skeleton is decoration (aria-hidden); the form and length are carried by the radiogroup and the spinbutton's value text, so nothing is lost to assistive technology.
Give a shape a skeleton(length, box) that returns up to 18 bars to draw a form of your own; it morphs to and from the built-in ones on the same spring.
Reduced motion cross-fades the preview to the new form instead of morphing it; the form, the length and the conflict note still change.
Conflict detection reads the prompt's last-mentioned cue words per shape; set detectConflicts to false if your prompts often mention forms in passing.

items.title: Queued Asks
items.tagline: Line up your next asks while it works.
items.description: A composer that keeps taking prompts while the assistant is busy, stacking each as a numbered card above the field; beyond stackDepth they tuck into a deck. When the running answer finishes, the top card peels off and flies into the thread as the new prompt bubble — a shared layout transition on springs.glide that untilts as it lands — while the cards below shuffle up on glide and their numbers roll on springs.snap. Cards drag 1:1 into a new order and settle on snap with the release velocity, or edit in place; Alt with Up or Down reorders, Delete removes, Up in an empty field edits the last card, a failed run pauses the queue, and on a phone the stack collapses to a count you expand.

props.name: stackDepth
props.description: Cards that stand fanned before the rest tuck into a deck behind the last one.

props.name: cardStyle
props.description: Paper notes with a folded corner, tickets with a perforated stub, or flat lines.

props.name: accent
props.description: Numbers, your bubbles, progress, Queue and Send — any CSS colour.

props.name: queue / defaultQueue
props.description: The queued prompts, top first; controlled or initial.

props.name: onQueueChange
props.description: Fires with the whole queue after any add, move, edit, removal or peel.

props.name: job
props.description: The run in progress (prompt, status, progress, step, answer, error), or null when idle. Owned by the host.

props.name: thread
props.description: Finished turns, oldest first.

props.name: onEnqueue
props.description: A prompt was queued.

props.name: onReorder
props.type: (ids: string[], moved: { id, from, to }) => void
props.description: A card was moved by drag or by Alt with an arrow.

props.name: onEditQueued
props.description: A queued prompt was edited in place.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: A queued prompt was removed, or Stop was pressed on the run (its id).

props.name: onAdvance
props.description: The top card peeled off: start it as the new job with the same id, so it flies into the thread.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Nothing running and nothing queued: the prompt goes straight to the assistant.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed on a failed run.

props.name: onResume
props.description: Skip was pressed on a failed run; the next card peels off.

props.name: paused
props.description: Hold the queue: nothing peels until it is resumed.

props.name: advanceDelay
props.description: How long a finished answer rests before the next card peels off, ms.

props.name: maxQueue
props.description: The most prompts the queue holds.

props.name: title
props.description: The session's name.

props.name: model
props.description: The assistant's name.

props.name: workspace
props.description: Whose workspace the session is in.

props.name: placeholder
props.defaultValue: "Ask, or line up the next ask…"
props.description: Placeholder for the field.

props.name: height
props.description: The tallest the surface grows, px; past it the thread scrolls.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be typed, queued or moved.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the queue is a list with one roving card — Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Alt with Up or Down reorders, Enter or F2 edits in place (Enter saves, Escape cancels), Delete or Backspace removes, Escape returns to the field. Up in an empty field edits the last card; Enter queues while the assistant is busy and sends when it is idle.

The host owns the job and the thread. When the job turns done the component removes the top card after advanceDelay and calls onAdvance; start that ask as the new job with the same id and the card flies into the thread.
Only the card about to peel and the bubble it becomes share a layout id, and only for the flight, so the thread can reflow freely around them.
Reduced motion keeps every state: cards jump to their slots, numbers swap, the peeled ask appears in the thread without flying, and progress still fills.
The running turn's progress is a progressbar with the current step as its value text; announcements are made once per queue change or run outcome, never per progress tick.

items.title: Scope Wheel
items.tagline: Choose where it looks before you ask.
items.description: A composer with a thumbwheel at its left edge choosing where the assistant looks — this page, this project, the workspace, the open web. The drum rolls 1:1 under a vertical drag (shaped toward the nearest detent by detents) and settles into the detent the throw was heading for on springs.snap with the release velocity; as the scope lands, an outline of the searched area sweeps across a mini map of the workspace on springs.glide with a scan line running over it, the count of searchable items rolls digit by digit on snap, and the placeholder rewrites itself from the shared prefix. The wheel is a radiogroup on the arrow keys with Cmd or Ctrl and 1 to 4 from the field, locked scopes roll back with a note, and on a phone the map hides and the wheel becomes a pill menu.

props.name: detents
props.description: How notchy the wheel is, 0 to 1: 0 rolls freely and snaps on release, 1 clicks from detent to detent as you drag; the housing's notches deepen with it.

props.name: mapStyle
props.description: The map's drawing: filled tiles, a hairline blueprint, or dot-matrix tiles.

props.name: accent
props.description: Outline, notches, count and Send — any CSS colour.

props.name: scopes
props.description: The scopes on the wheel, nearest first: label, short label, area (page, section, workspace, web), count, unit, placeholder, locked and lockedNote.

props.name: map
props.description: The workspace the map draws: its sections and pages, and where the user is.

props.name: scope / defaultScope
props.description: The chosen scope's id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onScopeChange
props.description: Fires from the turn, key, wheel or menu that changed the scope.

props.name: draft / defaultDraft
props.description: The question, controlled or initial.

props.name: onDraftChange
props.description: Fires from every edit.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Enter or Send: the question and where to look.

props.name: onLockedPick
props.description: A locked scope was reached for; the wheel rolls back and shows its note.

props.name: showMap
props.description: Draw the workspace map above the field (always hidden on a phone).

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the counts are known: counting shows a spinner, error says the count is unavailable.

props.name: busy
props.description: An answer is being written: Send holds and spins.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be typed, turned or sent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the wheel is a radiogroup — Up and Down (or Left and Right) turn it a scope, Home and End jump, locked scopes are skipped with their note — and Cmd or Ctrl with 1 to 4 picks a scope from anywhere in the composer. On a phone the pill opens a menu of menuitemradios (arrows, Home, End, Enter, Escape back to the pill). Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line.

Pointer: drag the drum vertically, flick it, or turn it with a mouse wheel (a detent per notch, and the page scrolls on at either end). touch-action is pan-x on the drum so a vertical drag never scrolls the page.
Counts are formatted by hand, never with a locale or compact formatter, so the server and the browser print the same digits.
Reduced motion jumps the drum and the outline to the new scope and swaps the digits and placeholder whole; the scope, count and note still change.
The map is decoration (aria-hidden): the scope and its count are in the meta row and in each radio's name, and each change is announced once.

items.title: Paste Fold
items.tagline: Paste the whole thing; it folds itself away.
items.description: A prompt composer that recognises a large paste — a log, a table, a long email, code — and instead of flooding the field spills it in as a sheet of its first lines, then folds it on springs.glide into a labelled block showing its kind, line count and first line, with the caret already after it so you keep typing. Peeking flips the composer to the block's numbered lines with the height gliding, and Trim keeps only the lines you mark (Errors only marks a log's errors in one press); over the character limit the meter turns danger and Send holds. The message is a flow of real textareas and block chips: Left at the start of a run or Backspace there selects the block before it, Space peeks inside, Backspace removes it, and on a phone blocks wrap as full-width chips.

props.name: foldThreshold
props.description: Pastes with at least this many lines fold into a block; shorter ones land as text.

props.name: chipStyle
props.description: A tab with a kind strip and the first line, a two-line card, or a compact pill.

props.name: accent
props.description: Chips, selection, meter and Send — any CSS colour.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The message as text runs and folded blocks in order, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the whole message after every edit, fold, trim or removal.

props.name: rules
props.description: How pastes are recognised (log, table, email, code), tried in order, each with an optional one-press keep filter for the trim view; anything else folds as Text.

props.name: foldChars
props.description: Pastes with at least this many characters fold too, whatever their line count.

props.name: limit
props.description: The most characters a message may carry, blocks included; past it the meter turns danger and Send holds.

props.name: onPasteDetected
props.description: A paste was folded into a block.

props.name: onExpand
props.description: A block was opened to peek inside.

props.name: onTrim
props.description: A block was trimmed to the marked lines (indexes into its previous lines).

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Enter or Send: the parts, and the message as plain text with blocks fenced.

props.name: placeholder
props.defaultValue: "Describe the problem, or paste the log…"
props.description: Placeholder for an empty message.

props.name: label
props.description: The message's accessible name.

props.name: busy
props.description: An answer is being written: Send holds and spins.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be typed, pasted or sent.

props.name: ref
props.description: Imperative handle: paste(text) pastes as a real paste would; focus() puts the caret at the end.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Left at the start of a text run, or Backspace there, selects the block before it; Right at the end, or Delete, selects the block after. On a block, Space or Enter peeks inside, Backspace or Delete removes it and puts the caret at the join, Left and Right return to the text, Escape goes to the text after it. In the peek, the lines are a listbox (Up, Down, Home, End; in Trim, Space toggles and Shift extends) and Escape closes back to the block.
Every run is a real, auto-sizing textarea, so spell-check, IME composition and the platform's own text editing all work; only big pastes are intercepted.
A paste from the handle never takes focus or scrolls the page unless the caret is already in the composer, so a demo or a host can feed it content safely.
Reduced motion skips the spill and the fold: the block appears folded with a short highlight, and the peek cross-fades.
onSubmit hands you both the structured parts and a plain-text message with each block fenced by its kind, ready to send to a model.

items.title: Night Shift
items.tagline: The overnight run, replayed by the hour.
items.description: A morning digest of an overnight agent run, read by replaying the night: every event is a dot on an arc from dusk to dawn and a moon rides it. Drag the moon and it follows 1:1 along the arc while the event cards below slide in lockstep, because the strip's offset is the moon's place expressed as a fractional event index; let go and the throw is projected and the moon settles on springs.glide with the release velocity at the nearest event, whose dot lights with a ring that opens on springs.snap. The strip can be dragged too, and then the moon races or crawls along the arc to keep up. The moon is a real slider: Left and Right step event by event, Home and End jump to dusk and dawn, Page Up and Page Down move about an hour and Enter opens the event; failed runs are pinned above the sky, and under 30rem the arc straightens into a vertical rail.

props.name: events
props.description: The night's events { id, agent, at, title, detail?, outcome, metric? }, in any order; outcome is done, flagged or failed.

props.name: agents
props.description: The agents the events name: { id, name, role }.

props.name: night
props.description: Dusk and dawn in ms; events outside the window are left off the arc.

props.name: utcOffset
props.description: Minutes added to UTC before a time is printed, so the clock reads in the team's zone.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.defaultValue: — / the first failed event, else the first event

props.name: now

props.name: title

props.name: cardStyle

usageNotes: Keyboard: the moon is a slider — Left/Down and Right/Up step to the previous and next event, Home and End jump to dusk and dawn, Page Up and Page Down move about an hour, Enter opens the event; each landing is announced politely, never per drag frame.

Reduced motion: the moon jumps to its landing and the strip swaps instead of sliding; while dragging, the moon still follows the pointer because the visitor is moving it. Times, counts and the travelled arc still update.
Nothing runs at rest: every frame comes from a drag or a spring the visitor started, and positions live in motion values, so a scrub never re-renders the tree per frame.
Times are printed from UTC plus utcOffset with a fixed 24-hour clock, so the server and the browser render the same markup; pass your own events and window in ms.
The layout is chosen by container width: under 30rem the arc straightens into a vertical rail (drag with touch-pan-x) with the cards sliding beside it.
Colours come from tokens: done events use the accent, flagged the warn token and failed the danger token, in both themes.

items.title: Footprint Map
items.tagline: See which parts of the code agents are in.
items.description: A live map of a repository while agents work in it: folders and files laid out as a squarified treemap sized by file size, each working agent a marker that glides from file to file along a gentle arc on springs.glide as it reads and edits, its newest trail segment cut at the marker's own progress so the line is drawn out behind it, older files fading behind. Touched files are washed by read or write, by the last agent's colour or by heat; two active agents in one file open a soft warn ring on springs.snap with a possible-conflict chip, and a stalled agent holds still with a dashed ring. Tab moves through the agents, F follows the focused one and Enter opens the history of its file; the map is one tab stop whose arrow keys move spatially between files, and under 30rem the map gives way to a list of files ranked by activity.

props.name: files
props.description: Every file in the repository as { path, size }; folders come from the paths and size sets each file's area.

props.name: agents
props.description: The agents working in it: { id, name, task, state?, tint? }. Idle agents are not drawn; stalled ones hold still with a dashed ring.

props.name: events
props.description: What they read and wrote, oldest first: { id, agent, path, op, at }. Each agent sits in the file of its newest event.

props.name: repo
props.description: The repository's name, in the header and as the region's accessible name.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment the map is read, in ms; stalls are counted from it.

props.name: utcOffset
props.description: Minutes added to UTC before a time is printed.

props.name: stallAfter
props.description: An active agent whose newest step is older than this, in ms, reads as stalled.

props.name: follow / defaultFollow
props.description: The followed agent: its trail and log come forward and the others dim.

props.name: onFollowAgent
props.description: Fires from the press or key (F) that followed an agent or stopped following.

props.name: paused / defaultPaused
props.description: Whether the agents are paused; the markers dim and the header says so.

props.name: onPause
props.description: Pause agents (or Resume agents) was pressed, with the new state.

props.name: onSelectFile
props.description: A file's history was opened (Enter or a press), with its events newest first.

props.name: trailLength
props.description: How many of each agent's recent files stay joined by its trail; 0 draws markers only.

props.name: tint
props.description: How touched files are washed: by read or write (with a pen mark), by the last agent's colour, or by how often they were touched.

props.name: accent
props.description: Access and heat washes, the follow highlight and focus accents — any CSS colour.

props.name: mapHeight
props.description: The treemap's height, px.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the repository has been read; loading draws placeholders, error offers Try again.

props.name: onReload
props.description: Try again was pressed after the map failed to load.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be followed, paused or opened.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer region.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab moves through the agents; on an agent, F or Space follows it and Enter opens the history of the file it is in. The map is one tab stop — arrow keys move to the nearest file in that direction, Home and End jump, Enter opens a file's history and Escape closes it, returning focus.
The component draws what it is given: feed events and now from your agent stream (the demo plays a seeded script only while the map is on screen). Nothing animates between steps.
Reduced motion: markers jump to their file, the conflict ring and landing flash appear without scale and list rows re-rank at once; washes, counts and the inspector still update.
The treemap is measured to its box with one ResizeObserver and laid out deterministically, so the server renders the same default layout the browser hydrates.
Conflicts and stalls are announced once, politely, when they begin; follow changes and opened histories are announced too, never each step.
Under 30rem of container the map becomes a list of files ranked by activity, with the agents' monograms gliding between rows.

items.title: Run Journal
items.tagline: The run, told in plain sentences.
items.description: An agent's run written up as it goes, as a journal of short paragraphs with their times in the margin. The newest line is written by a pen nib that rides the end of the text: after each chunk arrives its target is measured from a marker at the end of the words and it moves there on springs.flick along the line and springs.glide when the text wraps, leaning with its speed, while the words it has just written arrive in the accent and dry to ink. Only the newest entries stay written out; as one ages past condenseAfter it condenses on springs.glide into its one-line summary, its measured height closing as the summary fades in, and it opens again on a press or Enter. Up and Down move between entries, Home and End jump, links stay ordinary links, and paused, failed and finished runs each have their own designed state.

props.name: entries
props.description: The journal, oldest first: { id, at, text, summary, kind? }. The newest entry is the one being written; [[artifact-id]] or [[artifact-id|words]] in the text becomes a link.

props.name: artifacts
props.description: What the prose can link to: { id, label, href, kind? }, listed again in the footer.

props.name: state
props.description: Where the run stands: the nib writes, lifts away, stops beside a danger mark, or signs off with a closing rule.

props.name: agent
props.description: Who is writing; the region's accessible name.

props.name: run
props.description: What the run is, under the agent's name.

props.name: pausedReason
props.defaultValue: "Waiting for approval of the cut-over plan."
props.description: Shown and announced while paused.

props.name: error
props.defaultValue: "Stopped: the orders table stayed locked for 30 seconds."
props.description: Shown and announced when the run has failed.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment the journal is read, in ms; the header counts the run's length to it.

props.name: utcOffset
props.description: Minutes added to UTC before a time is printed.

props.name: condenseAfter
props.description: How many of the newest entries stay written out; older ones condense to their summary line.

props.name: expanded / defaultExpanded
props.description: Ids of aged entries opened by hand.

props.name: onExpandEntry
props.description: A condensed entry was opened, or an opened one folded again.

props.name: onOpenArtifact
props.description: A link to an artifact was followed, in the prose or the footer. It stays an ordinary link unless you prevent the event.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Stop was pressed while writing or paused.

props.name: onResume
props.description: Resume was pressed while paused.

props.name: nibStyle
props.description: What writes the newest line: a fountain-pen nib, a pencil tip, or a heavy caret.

props.name: accent
props.description: Wet ink, the nib, decision marks, links and the writing pill — any CSS colour.

props.name: height
props.description: The journal's height in px; the entries scroll inside it and stay pinned to the newest line while you are there.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the journal has loaded; loading draws placeholder lines, error offers Try again.

props.name: onReload
props.description: Try again was pressed after the journal failed to load.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer region.

usageNotes: Stream the newest entry by growing its text through props; the nib follows each change and nothing animates between chunks. An unclosed [[ link is held back until it closes, so a link never shows half-typed.
Keyboard: entries are one roving tab stop — Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Enter or Space opens or folds an aged entry; links inside entries stay ordinary links in the tab order.
Announcements are polite and whole: an entry is announced (as its summary) once the next one begins, and each change of state is announced once — never per chunk.
Reduced motion: the nib sits at the end of the text without travel or lean, ink is drawn dry, condensing swaps at once and the closing rule appears whole; every word and state still shows.
Under 19rem of container the margin times move above each entry; the footer's artifact chips scroll sideways with an edge fade.

items.title: Routine Week
items.tagline: Every scheduled agent, laid out on the week.
items.description: Every scheduled agent routine on one week: days across, the small hours down, each run a block coloured by its outcome and each future slot a dashed ghost, with overlapping runs sharing the column under a notch and skipped runs hatched. The now line moves down today's column on springs.glide as now advances, and as it crosses a scheduled slot a new block buds out of the line — a sliver that opens to the block on springs.recoil, scaled from its top edge — then fills while the run executes, the fill following now on glide until the host records the outcome. The slots are a grid with one row per day: arrows move between slots (Left and Right to the nearest slot in time on the neighbouring day), Home and End jump, Enter opens a run, R runs the focused routine now and P pauses it; under 32rem the grid becomes the day's agenda under a week strip.

props.name: routines
props.description: The recurring routines: { id, name, agent, days (0 = Monday), at (minutes after midnight), duration, paused? }.

props.name: runs / defaultRuns
props.description: This week's runs: { id, routine, day, start, duration, outcome, note? }; outcome is success, failed, skipped or running. A run whose routine, day and start match a slot fills that slot.

props.name: onRunsChange
props.description: Fires with the whole list when Run now adds a running run.

props.name: weekOf
props.description: Monday 00:00 of the week, in ms.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment the week is read, in ms: places the now line and decides which slot is running.

props.name: utcOffset
props.description: Minutes added to UTC before dates are read.

props.name: hours
props.description: The hours drawn, as [from, to).

props.name: day / defaultDay
props.description: The day the narrow agenda shows, 0 to 6.

props.name: onDayChange
props.description: Fires when the week strip picks another day.

props.name: onRunNow
props.description: Run now (or R) was pressed, with the run it started at the now line.

props.name: onPause
props.description: Pause or Resume (or P) was pressed, with the new state.

props.name: onEditSchedule
props.description: Edit schedule was pressed, or Enter on a slot that has not run; null from the empty week's Add a routine.

props.name: onOpenRun
props.description: Open run was pressed, or Enter on a slot that ran.

props.name: title
props.description: The surface's name and accessible name.

props.name: team
props.description: Whose routines, under the title.

props.name: hourHeight
props.description: Height of an hour on the grid, px; the agenda's rows breathe with it.

props.name: blockStyle
props.description: Run blocks: pigment-filled, washed with a side bar, or outlined with an outcome dot.

props.name: accent
props.description: The now line, running blocks, scheduled slots, today's shading and focus — any CSS colour.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Tallest the grid's viewport grows, px, before the hours scroll inside it.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the week has loaded; loading draws placeholder columns, error offers Try again.

props.name: onReload

props.name: disabled

props.name: className

usageNotes: Keyboard: the slots are one roving tab stop in a grid with a row per day — Up and Down move within the day, Left and Right to the nearest slot in time on the neighbouring day, Home and End jump, Enter or Space opens the run (or edits a slot that has not run), R runs the routine now and P pauses it.

Drive it from your scheduler: pass now and runs; a slot whose window contains now and has no run reads as running and buds, and a recorded outcome replaces the fill. Nothing ticks inside the component.
Reduced motion: no bud and no glide — running blocks appear whole and the fill and now line move without springs; outcomes, fills and counts still update.
The bud is driven on the element itself, so a slot that starts running keeps its node and any keyboard focus on it.
Under 32rem of container the grid becomes the chosen day's agenda under a seven-day strip (a radiogroup), with the now marker between items and a progress bar on the running one.

items.title: Standup Cards
items.tagline: Each agent reports: done, next, stuck.
items.description: A daily standup for a team of agents: one card each with what it did, what it does next and what it is stuck on. When the table comes into view the cards are dealt onto it in turn on springs.snap — from a deck with a seeded tilt, dropped from above, or slid in from the left — and an unanswered blocker glows in the warn colour until someone answers it. Answering slides the item off its card: a chip lifts from the row and glides to the resolved tray on springs.glide, landing there on springs.recoil while the card closes the gap on glide, and reassigning swaps the owner on snap. Tab moves card to card, Down and Up walk a card's items, B jumps to the next blocker; the cards form two columns from 36rem and a swipeable stack under 30rem, where a projected flick sends the front card to the back.

props.name: agents
props.description: The agents at the standup, one card each in dealing order: { id, name, role, online?, lastSeen? }.

props.name: items
props.description: Every agent's items: { id, agent, kind, text, owner? }; kind is done, next or blocked, and a blocker names the owner it needs.

props.name: owners
props.description: People a blocker can need and be reassigned to: { id, name, team? }.

props.name: resolved / defaultResolved
props.description: Answered blockers, newest first: { item, answer, at }. They leave their cards and sit in the resolved tray.

props.name: onResolvedChange
props.description: Fires with the whole list when a blocker is answered.

props.name: onAnswerBlocker
props.description: A blocker was answered (Send or Enter in its field).

props.name: onReassign
props.description: A blocker was reassigned from its owner menu.

props.name: onOpenItem
props.description: An item, or a resolved chip, was pressed.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment of the standup, in ms: stamps answers and dates the header.

props.name: utcOffset
props.description: Minutes added to UTC before a time is printed.

props.name: title
props.description: The standup's name and the region's accessible name.

props.name: team
props.description: Whose agents, under the title.

props.name: dealStyle
props.description: How the cards arrive: dealt from a deck at the top with a seeded tilt, dropped into place, or slid in from the left.

props.name: density
props.description: Type size, padding and gaps of the cards.

props.name: accent
props.description: Agent marks, Answer and Send, the flight, the tray and focus accents — any CSS colour.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the cards are dealt: as soon as they mount, or when the table scrolls into view.

props.name: height
props.description: The surface's height in px; the table scrolls inside it.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the standup has loaded; loading draws placeholder cards, error offers Try again.

props.name: onReload
props.description: Try again was pressed after the standup failed to load.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be answered or reassigned.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer region.

usageNotes: Keyboard: each card is a tab stop and Tab moves card to card, stopping on a blocker's Reassign and Answer; Down and Up walk a card's items and Escape returns to the card; B anywhere in the table jumps to the next unanswered blocker (bringing its card to the front of the stack). In the answer field Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks a line and Escape closes it.
The breathing glow on unanswered blockers runs only while the table is on screen, the tab is visible and motion is allowed; under reduced motion it is a still glow.

Reduced motion: no deal travel (the cards fade in, in turn), no flight (the answered item fades from its card and the tray chip appears), and the stack swaps instead of sliding; counts and the tray still update.

The deal is driven on motion values from an IntersectionObserver and always lands — a StrictMode rehearsal or an unmount finishes it rather than freezing a card mid-air; the server renders the cards at rest.

Under 30rem of container the cards become a swipeable stack (touch-pan-y): the front card follows the finger with a slight lean, a projected flick sends it to the back, Left and Right do the same, and dots show the position.

items.title: Cause Lines
items.tagline: Trace which event set off which.
items.description: An agent activity feed drawn oldest first on a causal gutter, where selecting an event lights its chain: lines start at the selected node and grow along their own paths up to the events that caused it and down to the ones it caused on springs.glide, hop after hop, while unrelated events dim and the selected node's ring lands on springs.snap. Every link is always there as a faint ghost, a link through an event the agent filter hides is drawn dotted, and in a narrow container the gutter gives way to indented rails whose rows step in by generation. The feed is a listbox: Up and Down walk it, Shift with Up or Down jumps to the nearest cause or effect, P pins the chain and Escape unpins it.

props.name: events
props.description: The feed, any order: { id, at, agent, severity, title, detail? }. Drawn oldest first so causes sit above effects.

props.name: links
props.description: Which event set off which: { from, to }.

props.name: agents
props.description: The agents writing into the feed, in filter order: { id, name, initial? }.

props.name: severities
props.description: Severity levels: { id, label, tone } where tone is neutral, accent, warn or danger.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The selected event id, controlled or initial.

props.name: onSelectEvent
props.description: Fires from the click or key that selected an event, or with null when a filter hid it.

props.name: pinned / defaultPinned
props.description: The event whose chain stays lit while the selection moves, controlled or initial.

props.name: onPinChain
props.description: Fires from P or the Pin button with the pinned id (or null) and its lit chain in feed order.

props.name: agentFilter / defaultAgentFilter
props.description: The agent whose events show, or null for every agent.

props.name: onFilterAgent
props.description: Fires from the chip that changed the filter.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the feed is streaming, held, or has nothing to show yet.

props.name: onLiveChange
props.description: The Live / Paused pill was pressed; omit it and the pill is a label.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the feed failed to load.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment relative times count from, in ms.

props.name: reach
props.description: How many hops of causes and effects light up each way, 1 to 6.

props.name: title
props.description: The feed's heading and the listbox's name.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Under the heading, before the event count.

props.name: curveStyle
props.description: How a causal line bends into the gutter: round bows, square brackets or angled chevrons.

props.name: dimLevel
props.description: Opacity of the events outside the lit chain, 0.1 to 0.6.

props.name: accent
props.description: The chain, the selection and Live: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be selected, pinned or filtered.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface; it caps at 36rem tall and the feed scrolls inside.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the feed is a listbox with one tab stop. Up and Down walk it, Home and End jump, Shift with Up or Down jumps to the nearest cause or effect, P pins or unpins the chain and Escape unpins; every selection is announced once, as a sentence.
Rows are a fixed 52 px, so every line is computed from the row index alone: the server renders the same lines the browser draws, and nothing is measured to draw them.
Arrivals while the reader is near the bottom are followed; otherwise a "new below" pill offers them, so a live feed never yanks the event someone is reading.
Severity is a word as well as a colour: warn and error rows say it in the meta line, and the node discs use pigment at a fixed lightness so they read the same in both themes.
Under reduced motion the chain appears whole with a fade, rows re-indent in place and arrivals fade in; the dims and the lit chain still show, because they are the information.
Below an 18.75rem container the causal gutter becomes indented rails, by container query, so the markup is the same at every width.

items.title: Merge Train
items.tagline: Agent changes, coupled and checked in order.
items.description: A merge queue drawn as a train: the pull requests agents have opened are coupled cars on a line through the depot and the stations for tests, review and merge. When a car clears a station the train advances on springs.glide, the front car first and each car behind a cascade later like slack running out, a car that fails uncouples and drops onto the siding on springs.recoil while the cars behind close the gap, and a merged car pulls away on the exit ease; couplers latch on springs.flick and check pips fill as checks pass. Below 30rem the line runs down the page. The cars are a listbox: arrows walk the line, Enter opens a car's checks, Delete pulls it from the train and Alt with an arrow moves a waiting car in the queue.

props.name: changes
props.description: Every car in a stable order: { id, number, title, agent, branch?, stop, result, checks?, progress?, failedReason? }. stop is -1 in the depot.

props.name: stations

props.name: order / defaultOrder
