props.name: onReorder
props.description: Fires from Alt+Arrow or the Move buttons with the new queue order.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: The car whose checks are open below the yard.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from Enter, a click, Escape or Close with the open car or null.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry was pressed on a car standing on the siding.

props.name: onRemoveCar
props.description: Delete, Backspace or Remove pulled a car from the train; it leaves at once.

props.name: held
props.description: Hold the train: the last station's lamp turns to stop and a banner says why.

props.name: heldReason
props.description: Why the train is held.

props.name: merged
props.description: Changes merged so far today, for the header.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the train's data has arrived; an empty train draws an empty depot.

props.name: onReload
props.description: Try again was pressed after the train failed to load.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading and the listbox's name.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Under the heading.

props.name: carStyle
props.description: A card with its checks, a compact pill, or a boxcar with a roof band and wheels.

props.name: trackStyle
props.description: Rails and sleepers, one transit line with station rings, or a dashed hairline.

props.name: accent
props.description: Running cars, progress and the open car: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: cars can be walked and read but not opened, moved or removed.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface; it caps at 36rem tall and its body scrolls inside.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the cars are a listbox with one tab stop, in line order (depot queue, the line, then the siding). Arrows walk, Home and End jump, Enter opens a car, Escape closes it, Delete or Backspace pulls it from the train, Alt with an arrow moves a waiting car in the queue.

The component draws whatever `changes` says: move a car's `stop`, set `result` to failed or merged, and the train animates the difference. Every car lives in one grid in a stable DOM order, so each move is a layout animation, not a remount.
Lamps, pips and car states always carry words for assistive technology; failures, merges and moves are announced once, from the change that caused them.
Under reduced motion cars change places with a fade instead of travelling, the siding drop has no bounce, and pips, lamps and progress still update.
Below a 30rem container the yard turns: stations become rows with upright platform signs and the siding runs down the right, by container query, so the server markup is the same at every width.

items.title: Schema Mould
items.tagline: Arguments that fit the shape they should.
items.description: A tool call checked against its schema, drawn as a mould: one cavity per expected field, keyed by its type, and the agent's arguments as pieces keyed by the type of the value they actually hold. When the mould comes into view the pieces pour in a cascade apart, each falling into its cavity on springs.snap as the rim brightens; a value of the wrong type hits the rim and is thrown out beside the mould on springs.recoil with a short reason, and a missing required field leaves its cavity hollow. Every field is a tab stop, Enter edits a rejected value and a fixed value drops back in on springs.snap; below 30rem nested objects fold into rows you open.

props.name: tool
props.description: The tool being called, in mono; also the surface's name.

props.name: server
props.description: Who serves the tool.

props.name: schema
props.description: The expected fields: { name, type, required?, description?, options?, format?, fields?, items? }, nested for objects and arrays.

props.name: args / defaultArgs
props.description: The arguments the agent sent, controlled or initial.

props.name: validation
props.description: A path's reason it does not fit, or null when it fits; overrides the built-in type check for that path.

props.name: status
props.description: The call's state; rejected while anything is outside the mould, else pending, unless the host says otherwise.

props.name: result
props.description: The tool's reply once the call completed, or the error it gave.

props.name: onFixArgument
props.description: A rejected value was fixed in its editor, with its path and the value parsed by the field's type.

props.name: onRun
props.description: Run was pressed with every argument in the mould.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Copy was pressed; the arguments as JSON, also written to the clipboard when it allows.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the pieces pour into the mould.

props.name: mouldStyle
props.description: Debossed cavities in a tray, dashed blueprint outlines, or a tinted cast.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height and piece size.

props.name: accent
props.description: Fitted keys, rims, Run and the cast: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: How a value is written on its piece.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be fixed or run.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface; it caps at 36rem tall and the mould scrolls inside.

usageNotes: Keyboard: every field is a tab stop named with its path, type and verdict. Enter on a rejected or missing field opens an editor; Enter saves (the text is parsed by the field's type, and an unreadable value is refused in place with aria-invalid), Escape cancels and returns focus to the field.

Types are shapes, not only colours: each cavity and piece carries a key glyph (circle for text, square for numbers, triangle for enums, diamond for dates), so a misfit reads at a glance and in greyscale.
Validation is built in for string, number, integer, boolean, enum, date, object and array, with email format; pass `validation` to override any path with your server's own verdict.
Run stays focusable and aria-disabled while anything is outside the mould, described by the fit summary, so a keyboard user hears why.
Under reduced motion every piece appears where it ends up, in the mould or outside it, with a fade: no fall and no bounce.
Below a 30rem container the rows stack and nested objects and arrays fold into disclosure rows, by container query, so the server markup is the same at every width.

items.title: Search Fan
items.tagline: Watch it search, skim and keep what matters.
items.description: A web search tool call shown as it works: the agent's queries fan out from the call as tabs, tilted like a hand of cards and landing on springs.snap a cascade apart, and result cards stream in under each on springs.glide. A scan line skims every card in scanSpeed ms; when it reaches the bottom the agent's decision lands, a kept card lifting and flying into the Kept stack on springs.glide while a dropped card falls away on the exit ease and leaves a slim stub, with the reason on hover and focus. Cards are one roving group where arrows move by where cards really are, K keeps and D drops to override the agent; below 40rem the fan shows one query at a time.

props.name: call
props.description: The tool's name, in mono on the call pill.

props.name: topic
props.description: What the agent is researching; the surface's heading.

props.name: queries
props.description: The queries: { id, text, at, state? } where at is ms after the call starts and state is ok, no-results or rate-limited.

props.name: results
props.description: The results: { id, queryId, at, domain, title, snippet, url, decision, reason }.

props.name: playing
props.description: Run the call's clock; paused, everything holds where it is.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the clock starts.

props.name: onOpenResult
props.description: Enter or a click on a result, to open its page.

props.name: onKeep
props.description: K overrode the agent and kept a result.

props.name: onDiscard
props.description: D overrode the agent and dropped a result.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Stop was pressed: nothing more arrives and unread results stay unread.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: The last result has been skimmed.

props.name: status
props.description: auto plays the call; loading and error stand in before it starts.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the call failed.

props.name: retryAt
props.description: When a rate-limited query will try again, as shown.

props.name: fanAngle
props.description: Tilt of the outermost query tabs, in degrees, 0 to 16.

props.name: scanSpeed
props.description: How long the agent skims one result, in ms.

props.name: accent
props.description: The scan line, kept results and the call pill: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: results open but cannot be kept or dropped, and Stop is off.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface; it is 34rem tall and its columns scroll inside.

usageNotes: Keyboard: every card, stub and kept row is in one roving group with a single tab stop. Arrow keys move to the nearest item in that direction by where items really are, so the same keys work in the column layout and the one-query layout (where Left and Right off the edge switch query). Enter opens, K keeps, D drops.

The call runs on its own clock from the `at` times in the data, as one chain of timers that pauses while the surface is off screen or the page is hidden and stops once everything has landed: no animation frame loop.
A kept card flies to the stack as a measured flyer drawn over the surface, so it can travel between two scrolling columns; the stack row appears as it lands.
Every decision carries its reason: in the footer on hover or focus, and in each item's description for assistive technology. Progress is announced once per landing, not per frame.
Under reduced motion cards appear without travel, the skim is a brief tint instead of a sweeping line, and kept results appear in the stack with a fade.
Below a 40rem container the tabs stack into a fanned hand with one query in front, by container query, so the server markup is the same at every width.

items.title: Run Cell
items.tagline: Code it ran, and what came out.
items.description: A code execution tool call drawn as a notebook cell and fed by props as the call streams: new lines of code slide in on springs.glide, an execution cursor glides down the gutter as each line runs and every executed line is marked on springs.flick, and stdout rises line by line below. When a figure first arrives the Figure tab opens and the plot develops out of a blank frame, a soft blur clearing as it settles from 1.02 on springs.glide while its lines draw left to right behind a sweeping clip and the tolerance band fades in last, with its data one tab away as a real table. Failing and timed-out lines are marked in place; Tab moves from the code to the tabs to the panel, and Enter on the code re-runs it.

props.name: code
props.description: The code, in full or as far as it has arrived; appended lines slide in, replaced code starts fresh.

props.name: language
props.description: Shown on the chip; the colouring reads Python keywords, strings, numbers, comments and calls.

props.name: executedLine
props.description: How many lines have run; the line at this index is running now.

props.name: outputs
props.description: What it printed so far: { id, stream, text } with stream stdout or stderr.

props.name: figures
props.description: What it returned: { id, title, xTicks, yUnit, series, band?, summary }. A new one develops in the Figure tab.

props.name: status
props.description: Where the call is.

props.name: error
props.description: The failure: { line, name, message, trace }, line 1-based as a traceback counts.

props.name: elapsed
props.description: Run time so far, in ms.

props.name: timeout
props.description: The run's time limit in ms, shown when it is hit.

props.name: runtime
props.description: The machine that ran it.

props.name: count
props.description: The execution count shown as In [7]; a star while it runs.

props.name: tab / defaultTab
props.defaultValue: — / figure when a figure exists, else output
props.description: The open result tab, controlled or initial; a new figure selects Figure when uncontrolled.

props.name: onTabChange
props.description: Fires from the click or key that changed the tab.

props.name: onRerun
props.description: Re-run was pressed, or Enter on the code.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Stop was pressed while it ran.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Copy was pressed; the code is also written to the clipboard when it allows.

props.name: onOpenFigure
props.description: Open was pressed on a figure.

props.name: foldLines
props.description: Below 30rem the code folds to this many lines until opened.

props.name: codeTheme
props.description: The code's surface: the page's paper, a deep ink panel in both themes, or a tint of the accent.

props.name: gutterStyle
props.description: How executed lines are marked: a tick each, one bar filling down, or dots that fill.

props.name: accent
props.description: The cursor, keywords, ticks and the running state: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be re-run, stopped or copied.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the cell; it caps at 36rem tall and its code and panels scroll inside.

usageNotes: The cell draws whatever the props say, so it follows a real stream: append to `code`, raise `executedLine`, push `outputs`, add a figure, then set `status`. Nothing in the component keeps time.

Keyboard: the code is one focusable region named with its line count, executed count and any error (Enter re-runs); the result tabs are a tablist with roving arrows, Home and End; each panel is focusable so long output can be scrolled by keys.

The figure is one SVG stretched to its box with non-scaling strokes and HTML labels, so it stays crisp at any width without measuring; it carries a sentence summary, and its data is a real table with a caption.
The output is a log that does not announce every line; the run's end, an error with its line, a timeout or a stop are announced once.
Under reduced motion lines and the figure appear with a short fade, the cursor jumps between lines, and ticks still mark each executed line.
Below a 30rem container the code folds to its first lines behind a disclosure, by container query, so the server markup is the same at every width.

items.title: Rerun Bench
items.tagline: Change an argument and see what it would return.
items.description: A debugging bench for one recorded tool call: its arguments as real fields beside its response as indented rows. Editing an argument dims the response in place as stale; when the fresh run arrives one accent line sweeps down and each row's new value drops in on springs.flick as it passes, fields that differ flash once and keep a change mark that grows in on springs.snap, and the run strip's selection slides on snap. Cmd or Ctrl+Enter re-runs, Alt with Up and Down steps through earlier runs, the strip is a radiogroup on the arrow keys, and Escape in an edited field restores it.

props.name: diffStyle
props.description: How a changed field keeps its mark: a bar in the gutter, the old value struck through before the new one, or a soft wash on the row.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height, field height and type size.

props.name: accent
props.description: Selection, change marks, the sweep and Re-run — any CSS colour.

props.name: call
props.description: The tool, its server and every parameter it takes (name, type string/number/boolean/enum, options, description, required).

props.name: runs
props.description: Every run oldest first: args, response (any JSON), ms, at, from (the run it was re-run from), recorded, error.

props.name: run / defaultRun
props.description: The id of the run on the bench, controlled or initial. Uncontrolled, the bench moves to each new run as it arrives.

props.name: onRunChange
props.description: Fires from the pick or the Alt+Up/Down step that changed the run.

props.name: args
props.description: Controlled argument draft. Uncontrolled, the draft starts as the shown run's arguments and resets when the run changes.

props.name: onArgsChange
props.description: Fires from every edit, restore or run change with the whole draft.

props.name: onRerun
props.description: Re-run or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter: call the tool with these arguments. Add the result to runs to stream it in.

props.name: onRestore
props.description: Restore: the draft went back to this run's arguments.

props.name: onSaveAsTest
props.description: Save as test: keep this run's arguments and response as a test case.

props.name: status
props.description: loading shows skeleton fields and rows; running keeps the response dimmed with a scanning hairline.

props.name: error
props.description: The last re-run never came back: shown over the response with Retry.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment relative run times count from, in ms.

props.name: baseline
props.description: What a run's marks are drawn against: the run it was re-run from, or the recorded call.

props.name: streamMs
props.description: How long a fresh response takes to stream over the stale one, in ms.

props.name: label
props.description: The bench's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: nothing can be edited or re-run.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Cmd or Ctrl+Enter re-runs from anywhere inside the bench, Alt+Up and Alt+Down step through runs, the run strip is a radiogroup (arrows, Home, End), and Escape in an edited field restores that argument.

The bench never runs the tool itself: onRerun hands you the draft, and appending the result to runs (and selecting it, if you control run) is what plays the stream-over. Keep status at "running" while the call is out.
Marks compare by JSON path; fields that disappear stay as struck rows where they used to be, and each changed row tells assistive technology what it was.
Reduced motion cross-fades the values instead of sweeping and the marks appear without the flash; the stale dim, the chips and every mark still show.
Nothing loops at rest: the scanning hairline runs only while status is "running" and the sweep ends with the last row.
The surface caps its height at 34rem and scrolls its body; under 34rem of width the request and response stack.

items.title: Server Lanes
items.tagline: Every tool server, and the calls running to it.
items.description: The tool servers an assistant is connected to, each a lane branching off the assistant's spine to a card for the server, with every call a bead that runs out along the upper rail on a tween, waits at the server end behind older calls (re-packing on springs.glide as each leaves), drops to the return rail on springs.snap and runs home tinted by its result — so a slow server shows as beads bunching and a failing one sends red home, while the port pulses on springs.flick and the card's strip gains a mark on snap. Up and Down move between lanes, Enter lists a lane's recent calls under it on glide, and Space pauses it, holding new beads at the assistant end until they are released in a cascade.

props.name: beadSize
props.description: Bead diameter in px (3 to 14), and with it how tightly waiting beads pack and how far apart the rails sit.

props.name: laneStyle
props.description: Two hairline rails, a rounded tube the beads run inside, or one dotted thread with beads riding above and below.

props.name: accent
props.description: Good calls, the spine's node, the open lane and the switches — any CSS colour.

props.name: servers
props.description: One lane each: id, name, host, tools, health (healthy, degraded, disconnected), enabled and a one-line note.

props.name: calls
props.description: Every call: id, server, tool, summary, startedAt, endedAt, status (running, ok, error) and error. A new id launches a bead; a status change brings it home.

props.name: assistant
props.description: The assistant's name at the head of the spine.

props.name: paused / defaultPaused
props.description: Ids of the paused lanes, controlled or initial.

props.name: onPausedChange
props.description: Fires from Space or a lane's pause button with every paused lane.

props.name: open / defaultOpen
props.description: The lane whose recent calls are listed under it, controlled or initial.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires from Enter, a click or Escape.

props.name: onToggleServer
props.description: The switch on a server card: may the assistant call it.

props.name: onReconnect
props.description: Reconnect on a disconnected server; the lane reads Reconnecting until its health changes.

props.name: onInspectCall
props.description: A call in a lane's recent list was chosen.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment relative call times count from, in ms.

props.name: status
props.description: loading draws placeholder lanes.

props.name: slowMs
props.description: A call slower than this comes home amber, in ms.

props.name: travelMs
props.description: How long a bead takes to run the length of its lane, in ms.

props.name: recentCount
props.description: How many results the strip on each server card keeps.

props.name: label
props.description: The view's accessible name.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the lanes are one roving group — Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Enter lists the lane's recent calls (Escape closes and returns focus), and Space pauses or resumes the lane. Every lane's name reads its health, calls in flight and its last results.

Drive it from your call log: append a call with status "running" to launch a bead and set status and endedAt when it returns. Pausing is visual and reported; hold the real calls yourself while a lane is paused.
Nothing runs at rest: each bead is one tween at a time and is removed when it lands, so a quiet assistant costs nothing. Beads are capped at ten per lane.
Reduced motion keeps beads still: a running call waits at the server end and its result lands straight in the strip.
Bead colours are pigments taken from the accent, warn and danger hues at a fixed lightness, so they read the same in light and dark themes.
Under 36rem of width each lane becomes rows: the server's name and switch, the track, then the recent-calls strip.

items.title: Query Stages
items.tagline: Watch the query narrow down to the answer.
items.description: A database query call shown as the stages it runs through, in the order the database runs them: as each finishes its clause lights, its bar narrows from the previous stage's width to its own on springs.snap and its row counter falls on snap, so the stack of bars reads as a funnel, while the running clause carries a sweeping underline and the result table unfolds beneath on springs.glide with its rows in a cascade once the last clause is done. Slow stages show their time and note, an empty result names the clause that removed the last rows, and a syntax error outlines its clause and underlines the token. Tab moves between the clauses and the table, and Enter on a clause opens the rows as they stood after it.

props.name: stageStyle
props.description: Bars centred so the stack reads as a funnel, bars from the left like a chart, or a rail of stage nodes that fills as the query runs.

props.name: counterStyle
props.description: Rolling digit columns, a number that tallies down, or the share of the source rows with the count beneath.

props.name: accent
props.description: Lit keywords, bars, the running underline and the table rule — any CSS colour.

props.name: source
props.description: The tool that ran the query and the database it ran on.

props.name: statement
props.description: The statement as written; Copy writes it to the clipboard and Copy and Explain hand it over.

props.name: stages
props.description: The clauses in run order: id, clause (from, join, where, group, having, select, order, limit), text, rows left, ms, note and a sample of rows.

props.name: columns
props.description: The result's columns: key, label, align, width, and hideNarrow to drop one on a phone.

props.name: rows
props.description: The result rows.

props.name: status
props.description: Where the call is. Rendered done, the view arrives finished with no travel.

props.name: completed
props.description: How many stages have finished while running; the next one is lit as running.

props.name: error
props.description: A syntax error with status "error": the stage id, the message, the token to underline and the line.

props.name: slowMs
props.description: A stage slower than this is marked slow and shows its note, in ms.

props.name: onRerun
props.description: Re-run in the header.

props.name: onOpenResult
props.description: Open in the result's header, with every row.

props.name: onCopyQuery
props.description: Copy in the header, with the statement.

props.name: onExplain
props.description: Explain in the header, with the statement.

props.name: onInspectStage
props.description: Enter or a click opened a finished stage's rows.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats every row count and number cell.

props.name: tableRows
props.description: Result rows visible before the table scrolls inside its own region.

props.name: label
props.description: The view's accessible name.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: every clause is a button in the Tab order whose name reads its step, keyword, text, rows and time; Enter opens the rows as they stood after it and Escape closes them. The result table sits in a labelled, focusable scroll region.
Drive a live call by stepping completed as each stage reports and set status to "done" at the end; the table unfolds then. Rendered already done, counts and rows appear in place without rolling.
Bars use a log scale so a 48,000-row scan and an 8-row answer are both visible; pass format to change how counts read.
Reduced motion lights clauses and changes counts without rolling or travel, and the table opens in place; every state still shows.
Nothing loops at rest: only the running clause's underline moves, and only while status is "running".

items.title: Command Unpacked
items.tagline: Understand the command before you let it run.
items.description: An approval card for a shell command an agent wants to run: the command first shows as one plain line, then its parts — program, flags, paths, arguments, operators — lift apart on springs.glide in a cascade and hairline stems draw down to tags that name each one, packed into staggered rows so no stem crosses a tag, with anything risky (a recursive delete, a write outside the project, running as administrator, piping into a shell) outlined in the risk colour. The part in focus is explained in plain words beneath as its outline slides on springs.snap. Tab walks the parts, Enter approves (twice for a risky command), Escape denies, and under 42rem the parts wrap and stack as a list with their explanations.

props.name: partStyle
props.description: Tinted chips, plain text with a coloured underline per part, or hollow outlined boxes.

props.name: riskColor
props.description: Outline, stem, tag and callout colour for risky parts — any CSS colour.

props.name: accent
props.description: Programs, the active outline and Approve — any CSS colour.

props.name: command
props.description: The command the agent wants to run; it is tokenised into parts (quotes respected) and explained.

props.name: cwd
props.description: Where it would run; relative paths are resolved against it.

props.name: root
props.description: The project root: paths that land outside it are flagged when they are deleted or written.

props.name: agent
props.type: { name: string; task?: string; askedAt?: number }
props.description: Who is asking, why, and when it asked in ms (12 s before now when left out).

props.name: programs
props.description: What each known program does: gist, summary, flags, subcommands, flags that take values, what plain arguments mean, and whether it deletes or writes its paths.

props.name: annotations
props.description: Explanations the agent gave for particular parts, keyed by the part's text; they replace the built-in ones.

props.name: rules
props.description: What counts as risky: id, label, level (danger or caution) and test(part, ctx) returning the reason or null.

props.name: policy
props.description: A policy that blocks approval here: blocked, reason and source. Approve locks; Deny and Edit remain.

props.name: decision / defaultDecision
props.description: The decision, controlled or initial.

props.name: onApprove
props.description: Approve or Enter on a part — a second press when the command is risky and confirmRisky is on.

props.name: onDeny
props.description: Deny or Escape.

props.name: onEditCommand
props.description: The command was edited and saved; it is explained again.

props.name: onAllowSimilar
props.description: A pattern chosen from Allow similar, offered only for the parts of the command with no risk.

props.name: unpacked / defaultUnpacked
props.description: Whether the parts are lifted apart, controlled or initial.

props.name: onUnpackedChange
props.description: Fires from the Pack/Unpack toggle and from the automatic unpack.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the command first lifts apart by itself.

props.name: confirmRisky
props.description: A risky command needs a second press within 4 seconds to approve.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment the "asked 12 s ago" time counts from, in ms.

props.name: label
props.description: The card's accessible name.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Tab walks the parts and each one's explanation and risk are its description; Enter on a part approves (arming first for a risky command), Escape denies from anywhere in the card, and closes the Allow similar menu or the editor first when one is open.
parseCommand(command, cwd, root, programs) is exported, so you can run the same tokeniser and path resolution on the server before you ever show the card.
Rules are plain functions over each part and the whole command: add your own (a network call, a force push) by appending to defaultCommandRules.
The drawing is measured once per layout change with one ResizeObserver and tags are set in mono, so packing them needs no second pass; nothing animates at rest.
Reduced motion shows the parts unpacked with stems and tags fading in where they are, and the active outline jumps instead of sliding.
Under 42rem of width the command wraps and the parts stack as a list with their explanations instead of the stem drawing.

items.title: Two Keys
items.tagline: Two people turn their keys before it runs.
items.description: A two-person approval for an agent's action, drawn as two key switches beneath a summary of it: each approver turns their own key a quarter turn on springs.snap, the first key opens a window that drains as a hairline, and only when the second turns inside it do the two halves of the bar between the switches close on springs.glide, the lock swap open on springs.flick and the Run control unlock — while a lone key turns itself back on snap if the window lapses. Only the current user's key is a control: a real switch that Space or Enter turns, or a sideways drag that follows the pointer 1:1 and commits by projection; under 34rem the switches stack beside a shorter summary with the bar running down between them.

props.name: switchStyle
props.description: A key in a round keyhole plate, a throw lever swinging across an arc, or a dial whose ring fills as it turns.

props.name: windowLength
props.description: Seconds the second key has after the first one turns.

props.name: accent
props.description: Lit ticks, the key, the closed bar and Run — any CSS colour.

props.name: action
props.description: What the agent wants to do: title, amount, currency, payee, reference, reason, limitNote, requestedBy, requestedAt and expiresAt.

props.name: approvers
props.description: The two people whose keys it needs, in switch order: id, name, role, turnedAt, rejected ({ at, note }) and comment.

props.name: currentUser
props.description: Whose key is a control here; every other key is a drawing with its state in text. Someone who is not an approver is offered Withdraw.

props.name: turned / defaultTurned
props.description: Whether the current user's key is turned, controlled or initial.

props.name: onTurnKey
props.description: Fires from the press, the drag, Space or Enter — or with "lapsed" when the window ran out on the user's own key.

props.name: onReject
props.description: Reject, with the reason the approver wrote (a reason is required).

props.name: onRemind
props.description: Remind, for an approver whose key is not turned.

props.name: onWithdraw
props.description: Withdraw, offered to anyone viewing who is not an approver.

props.name: onRun
props.description: The unlocked Run control was pressed.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment times count from, in ms; while a window is open the card keeps time from it itself.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the request can still be decided; done means it ran. It also reads as expired once now passes action.expiresAt.

props.name: runLabel
props.description: The Run control's words.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats the amount.

props.name: label
props.description: The card's accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be turned or pressed.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: only the current user's key is focusable — a role="switch" that Space or Enter turns; the other approver's key state is read as text. Reject opens a labelled note field (Escape cancels, Cmd or Ctrl+Enter sends), and Run stays focusable while locked and says why.

Pass each approver's turnedAt from your own records and keep now current; both keys count only when they turned within windowLength seconds of each other, so a late second key opens a fresh window instead of unlocking.
Nothing ticks at rest: the card keeps a 250 ms clock only while a window is open, it is on screen and the tab is visible; the drain itself is one linear tween.
Reduced motion switches key poses without travel, jumps the bar shut, and steps the window line once a tick instead of draining smoothly; every state still shows.
Under 34rem of width the switches stack beside a shorter summary with the bar running vertically between them.

items.title: Wipe Preview
items.tagline: See what it will change before it does.
items.description: An approval surface for an agent action that edits many records: every affected record is drawn twice in one grid, the result in flow and today's values laid over it, and a wipe decides which shows, with every changed field ringed solid on the result side and dashed on today's. The handle follows the pointer 1:1, rubber-bands past the ends and settles on springs.snap with the throw's velocity; approving runs the wipe to the result on springs.glide and an Applied stamp lands on springs.recoil once the host answers, while a refusal glides it back. The handle is a slider (arrows, Shift, Page keys, Home, End), the records are a multi-select listbox where X or Space skips the focused one, and below 28rem the wipe becomes a Before / After toggle.

props.name: action
props.description: The proposed action: { id, agent, title, summary, scope, proposedAt }.

props.name: fields
props.description: The fields compared, in column order: { key, label, kind? } where kind is money, percent, number or text.

props.name: records
props.description: The affected records: { id, title, meta?, before, after }.

props.name: excluded / defaultExcluded
props.description: Ids left out of the action, controlled or initial.

props.name: onExcludedChange
props.description: Fires with every excluded id after an exclusion changes.

props.name: onExclude
props.description: Fires from the key or press that skipped a record (true) or put it back (false).

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The wipe position, 0 (all today) to 100 (all result), controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires when a drag, key or toggle settles the wipe.

props.name: onApprove
props.description: Approve was pressed; a returned promise holds the stamp until it resolves, and a rejection slides the wipe back and states the reason.

props.name: onReject

props.name: onEditPlan

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry simulation was pressed after a failure.

props.name: largeChangeAt
props.description: A record whose money or number field moves more than this percent counts as a large change and raises the warning.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the simulation has produced records; failed shows the failure and holds Approve.

props.name: failure
props.description: Why the simulation failed and the record it stopped on.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment ages are counted from, in ms.

props.name: wipeStyle
props.description: The wipe's edge: a hard line, a soft 40px feather, or whole fields flipping as the handle passes each column.

props.name: ringColor
props.description: The ring around every changed field: a named colour or any CSS colour.

props.name: accent
props.description: The handle, Approve and the stamp: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: formatMoney
props.description: How money is written.

props.name: height
props.description: Tallest the surface grows, in px, before its record list scrolls.

props.name: disabled

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the handle is a role="slider" (Left and Right step 5, Shift 20, Page keys 25, Home and End); the records are a multi-select listbox of what is included, where Up, Down, Home and End move and X or Space skips or includes the focused record; Escape closes the reject note.
Each record's accessible name is one sentence (title, every change from and to, included or skipped); the overlaid today layer is aria-hidden, so assistive technology reads each record once.

The wipe is one motion value writing one CSS variable: the clip, the feather mask, the per-field flips and the ring swell are computed by CSS from it, so dragging re-renders nothing and no frame loop runs at rest.
Under reduced motion the wipe never travels on its own: approving cross-fades today's layer away and the stamp fades in; a drag still follows the finger and lands without a spring.
Colours come from tokens: accent and ringColor take a named pigment or any CSS colour, and the amber ring is pigment at a fixed lightness so it reads the same in light and dark.

items.title: Edit Before Send
items.tagline: Change what it drafted, then let it go.
items.description: A review frame for a message an agent wants to send: the draft reads as tracked changes against your edits, Edit swaps it for a real textarea sized to its text, every change is a stop you can walk to and revert, and policy flags hold the send until their words are gone, their checks drawing on springs.flick when they are. Approve shrinks the message into an envelope's pocket on springs.glide, folds the flap shut on springs.snap with a seal on flick, waits sealed for the host, then slides it out of the frame on glide; a failed send opens the flap and unfolds the sheet with the reason, and Request changes shrinks the message toward the agent with your note. Cmd or Ctrl+Enter approves from anywhere in the frame, Cmd or Ctrl+Z reverts the focused change or the last edit, and at narrow widths the recipients collapse into a count.

props.name: draft
props.description: The held message: { id, agent, model, from, subject, body, heldAt }; paragraphs in body are separated by a blank line.

props.name: recipients
props.description: Who it goes to: { id, name, email, kind?: "to" | "cc" }.

props.name: attachments
props.description: Files it carries: { id, name, size } with size in bytes.

props.name: flags
props.description: What the sending policy found: { id, severity: "block" | "warn", match, message }; a block holds Approve while its words are in the text.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The message text, controlled or initial.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the text as it is typed, reverted or undone.

props.name: onEdit
props.description: Fires when an edit settles (leaving the editor, a revert, an undo) with every change against the draft as { from, to }.

props.name: onApprove
props.description: Approve and send was pressed; the envelope waits sealed until a returned promise resolves, and a rejection unfolds it with the reason.

props.name: onRequestChanges
props.description: Sent back to the agent with the reviewer's note and the text as it stands.

props.name: onDiscard
props.description: The draft was discarded after the confirm.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether a draft is here to review.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the draft failed to load.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment the hold is timed from, in ms.

props.name: trackStyle
props.description: How changes are marked: struck and underlined, the clean text with carets where words went, or the clean text with change bars and counts in the margin.

props.name: envelope
props.description: The envelope the message folds into: plain, a striped airmail border, or an address window.

props.name: accent
props.description: Insertions, Approve and the seal: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: height
props.description: Tallest the frame grows, in px, before its body scrolls.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: the message can be read, not changed or sent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the frame.

usageNotes: Keyboard: Cmd or Ctrl+Enter approves from anywhere in the frame (it leaves the editor first); each change is a roving stop where arrows, Home and End move and Enter edits it; Cmd or Ctrl+Z reverts the focused change, or the last edit when no change is focused, while inside the textarea the browser's own undo applies; Escape leaves the editor and closes the note and the discard confirm.
Pressing a flag opens the editor with the flagged words selected; a blocking flag keeps Approve focusable but aria-disabled, with the reason as its description.
The diff is word-level and memoised on the text; changes separated only by spaces are one change, so a phrase reverts as one.
Under reduced motion nothing folds or travels: the sealed envelope fades in and out, the returned message fades, and every count, check and state still changes.
Pass onApprove a promise from your send call: the envelope only leaves the frame once it resolves, so the sent receipt never claims a send that failed.

items.title: Allow Rules
items.tagline: Turn one yes into a rule you trust.
items.description: A permission prompt that can become a standing rule: Always allow opens a sentence of selects that widens one yes into a pattern (the action, the files, a cost ceiling), with a live rule chip, a reach strip that lights in a cascade the recent requests the rule would have covered, and a conflict that names the deny rule it collides with, rings that rule and holds Create. Create folds the request card on springs.glide into its rule chip while the list opens a slot on the same spring, the chip flies into that slot on glide, and the row's fire count rolls from 0 to 1 on springs.snap as the next waiting request rises in. The builder is a toolbar of select-only comboboxes (Left and Right move, Up and Down change, Enter opens), the rules are roving stops where Enter edits and R revokes after a confirm, and below 30rem the panes sit behind tabs and the chip flies to the Rules tab.

props.name: request
props.description: The permission asked for now: { id, agent, verb, path, size?, cost, reason, at }; null when nothing waits.

props.name: waiting
props.description: Requests waiting behind it, in order; each decision brings the next one in.

props.name: templates
props.description: The builder's options, narrowest first: { verbs, scopes, costs }, each { id, label, value }.

props.name: rules / defaultRules
props.description: Standing rules, controlled or initial: { id, effect, pattern, fires, daily?, lastFiredAt? }.

props.name: onRulesChange
props.description: Fires with the whole list after a rule is created or revoked.

props.name: history
props.description: Recent requests, newest first; the reach strip lights the ones a rule would have covered.

props.name: onAllowOnce
props.description: Allow once was pressed.

props.name: onDeny
props.description: Deny was pressed.

props.name: onCreateRule
props.description: A rule was created from the request; it fires once for it.

props.name: onEditRule
props.description: Enter on a rule, or Edit that rule on a conflict.

props.name: onRevokeRule
props.description: A rule was revoked after its confirm.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the permissions have loaded.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after a failure to load.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment ages are counted from, in ms.

props.name: chipStyle
props.description: How a rule is drawn: a pill with an effect dot, a notched tag, or a mono glob pattern.

props.name: listDensity
props.description: Row height of the rules list; compact drops the last-fired line.

props.name: accent
props.description: Allow rules, the builder and Create: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: formatMoney
props.description: How money is written.

props.name: height
props.description: Tallest the surface grows, in px, before its panes scroll.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the pattern builder is a toolbar with one tab stop; Left and Right move between its selects, Up and Down change one in place, Enter, Space or Alt+Down open its listbox (arrows, Home, End, Enter picks, Escape closes). Rules are roving stops: Up, Down, Home and End move, Enter edits, R opens a revoke confirm with Keep focused, and Escape keeps.

Patterns match by verb, path (an exact file, a folder ending in / and everything under it, or any file) and cost ceiling; a deny rule that overlaps the pattern holds Create and says which rule wins, and an allow rule that already covers it is named instead.
Each rule's accessible name is one sentence with its fire count and last fire; the fourteen-day strip is a single crisp SVG path, decorative.
Under reduced motion nothing folds or flies: the card fades, the new row fades in already counted, reach dots light at once, and every count still changes.
The fold and the flight are two transient ghost elements measured from the live layout and removed when they land; nothing runs at rest.

items.title: Budget Pour
items.tagline: Approve a purchase against what is left.
items.description: An agent asking to spend money, drawn against the budget it would come out of: the bar shows paid, promised and the room left, and the order sits above it as a block of its line items starting exactly where the room left starts. A cap handle at the block's end follows the pointer 1:1, rubber-bands and settles on the nearest $10 on springs.snap, and every item past it lets go of the block and strikes in the list. Approve runs one pour front across the block on springs.glide at pourSpeed: behind it the block drains down a sloped surface into a thin stream, the bar's fill grows under the stream and the room left counts down; over budget the block overhangs the bar in danger, above the second-approval line your approval waits for the second, and an expired quote holds the decision. The cap is a slider (arrows $10, Shift $100, Page keys $250, Home, End) and Enter on it approves.

props.name: request
props.description: The spend asked for: { id, agent, title, reason, vendor, quote: { id, validUntil }, items, requestedAt }; items are in priority order and the cap trims from the bottom.

props.name: budget
props.description: The budget it comes out of: { id, name, total, spent, committed }.

props.name: cap / defaultCap
props.description: Most the agent may spend on this order, controlled or initial.

props.name: onSetCap
props.description: Fires when a drag, key or Cap at what's left settles the cap.

props.name: onApprove
props.description: Your approval, with the amount and the items that fit under the cap; a promise holds the pour until it resolves and a rejection is stated.

props.name: onReject
props.description: Declined, with the reviewer's optional note.

props.name: onRequestQuote
props.description: Ask for a new quote was pressed on an expired quote.

props.name: secondApprovalAbove
props.description: Orders above this need every approver, not only you.

props.name: approvers
props.description: Who approves: { id, name, you? }; the one marked you is the viewer.

props.name: approvals
props.description: Controlled ids of approvers who have approved; the held order pours when all have. Your own approval counts as soon as you give it.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the request has loaded.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after a failure to load.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment the quote's validity is counted from, in ms.

props.name: barStyle
props.description: How the budget is drawn: a solid bar, $250 cells cut by a repeating mask, or a 4px rail with $1,000 ticks.

props.name: pourSpeed
props.description: How fast the approved amount pours, as a multiple of the glide's pace from 0.5 to 2; the damping ratio stays the glide's.

props.name: accent
props.description: The order, its pour and Approve: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: formatMoney
props.description: How money is written.

props.name: height
props.description: Tallest the surface grows, in px, before its body scrolls.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the cap is a role="slider" whose value text reads the cap, the items that fit and the room left after; Left and Right step $10, Shift $100, Page keys $250, Home and End jump, and Enter approves. Approve stays focusable when held (aria-disabled) and its description says why.

The figure is drawn from CSS variables: two motion values (the cap and the pour) write unitless numbers and calc() places the cap, drains the block and grows the bar, so dragging re-renders only when the cap crosses an item's edge.
fitUnderCap(items, cap) is exported, so a host can show the same kept items and total elsewhere.
Under reduced motion nothing pours: the block fades, the bar and the room-left figure step to their final values, and the cap still follows a drag and lands without a spring.
Status pigments (spent, the order, the overhang) are taken at a fixed lightness so the bar reads the same in light and dark; the figure also carries a one-sentence screen-reader summary.

items.title: Rewire Plan
items.tagline: Reorder the steps; the arrows follow.
items.description: A plan an agent proposes before it starts, laid out as numbered step cards in execution order with dependency arrows in a gutter beside them, packed into lanes so arrows with overlapping spans never share one. A dragged card follows the pointer 1:1, lifted on springs.flick, while the others glide out of its way on springs.glide; every arrow touching it is rebuilt each frame from the cards' motion values and the lanes re-pack on glide, and an arrow that would now point backwards turns red and dashed while the card that needs it says why. The card lands on glide with the release velocity, Approve holds until the order is legal (Fix order finds the legal order that moves least), and the approved plan takes a stamp on springs.recoil; Up and Down move between steps, Alt with Up or Down moves one, Enter edits its title and estimate, and below 28rem the arrows become indented needs lines.

props.name: steps
props.description: The proposed steps: { id, title, minutes, owner } where owner is a person's name or "agent".

props.name: dependencies
props.description: Which steps need which: { from, to, note? }; the note explains a broken order.

props.name: order / defaultOrder
props.description: Execution order of step ids, controlled or initial.

props.name: onReorder
props.description: Fires from the drag, key or Fix order that changed the order, with the step moved (null for Fix order).

props.name: onEditStep
props.description: A step's title or estimate was edited.

props.name: onAddStep
props.description: Add step created a step at the end; it opens for editing.

props.name: onApprove
props.description: Approve plan was pressed; a returned promise holds the stamp until it resolves.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the plan exists yet; drafting shows a skeleton of cards and arrows.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the plan failed to load.

props.name: title
props.description: The plan's name.

props.name: agent
props.description: Who proposes it.

props.name: proposedAt
props.description: When the agent proposed the plan, in ms.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment the plan's age is counted from, in ms.

props.name: arrowStyle
props.description: How arrows are routed: one curve out to the lane and back, orthogonal elbows with rounded corners, or metro lines with 45° turns and stop dots.

props.name: cardStyle
props.description: How steps are drawn: bordered cards, flat rows, or tickets with a numbered stub behind a perforation.

props.name: accent
props.description: Arrows of the focused or dragged step, the agent's steps and Approve: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: height
props.description: Tallest the surface grows, in px, before the plan scrolls.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the surface.

usageNotes: Keyboard: the plan is an ordered list of roving stops; Up, Down, Home and End move between steps, Alt with Up or Down moves the focused step (announced with how many dependencies now run backwards), Enter or Space edits its title and estimate, Enter saves and Escape cancels back to the card.

Each step's accessible name says its number, title, estimate, owner and what it needs, and whether that now runs later; the gutter of arrows is decorative, and below 28rem the same facts show as indented needs lines.
fixPlanOrder(order, dependencies) is exported: a stable topological sort that keeps the reviewer's order wherever it is already legal.
Positions live in motion values (one per card and per arrow lane) and each arrow's path is derived from its two cards and its lane, so dragging re-renders only when the provisional order changes.
Under reduced motion cards and lanes jump to their places, a drag still follows the finger and lands without a spring, and the red arrows, notes and stamp still change.

items.title: Token Bucket
items.tagline: Your rate limit, as water in a tank.
items.description: An API rate limit as a glass tank of water that refills at the plan's speed in a steady linear rise, where every request lifts out a slab of exactly its size that floats up on springs.glide and evaporates while the surface drops to the new level on springs.snap and sloshes. When the water is too low, requests hang above the tank as droplets that arrive on snap, a dashed line marks what the first one needs, and when the water reaches it the droplet falls in on the exit ease and its scoop leaves as it lands; a refusal throttles the key and a ring clock counts the retry down. The last ten requests sit in a real list beside the tank (behind a toggle in a narrow container) where Up and Down move, Home and End jump and Enter inspects a request.

props.name: capacity
props.description: The size of the bucket: the most tokens you can spend at once.

props.name: level
props.description: Tokens available at `now`, as the limit reports them.

props.name: refillSpeed
props.description: How fast the plan refills the bucket, in tokens per second; the tank rises at this rate between readings.

props.name: requests
props.description: Recent requests: { id, at, tokens, route, key?, status: served | queued | refused, servedAt? }. The newest are listed; queued ones hang above the tank.

props.name: throttledUntil
props.description: When the current throttle lifts (ms); the glass turns warn and a ring clock counts down.

props.name: now
props.description: The moment the reading was taken (ms). Clocks count from it; the component never reads the wall clock in render.

props.name: status
props.description: Live or paused traffic, or no reading yet.

props.name: historySize
props.description: How many requests the list keeps.

props.name: maxDroplets
props.description: Droplets drawn above the tank before the rest are counted as +n.

props.name: title
props.description: The panel's heading.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Under the heading; by default it states the refill speed.

props.name: unit
props.description: What the bucket holds, in words.

props.name: formatTime
props.description: How a request's time is printed in the list.

props.name: liquid
props.description: How the water is drawn: a translucent fill with a rippling surface, a flat solid fill, or measured cells with the top one part-filled.

props.name: slosh
props.description: How much the surface ripples when a scoop leaves, 0 to 1.

props.name: accent
props.description: The water, the threshold line and the active actions: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: listOpen / defaultListOpen
props.description: Whether the request list is open in a narrow container, controlled or initial.

props.name: onListOpenChange
props.description: Fires from the Requests toggle with the state it asks for.

props.name: onRaiseLimit
props.description: Raise limit was pressed. Omit it and the button is not drawn.

props.name: onPause
props.description: Pause or Resume was pressed, with the state it asks for. Omit it and the button is not drawn.

props.name: onInspectRequest
props.description: A request in the list was opened.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after the limit could not be read.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: actions and the list do nothing.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the panel.

usageNotes: Feed it readings, not a clock: pass level, requests and throttledUntil at now (once a second is enough), or derive them from an arrival log with the exported simulateTokenBucket. The tank extrapolates the refill between readings and owns the drawn water after the first paint.

One animation-frame loop runs only while something is moving (refilling below its cap, a drop settling, a ripple decaying), only while the tank is on screen and the page is visible; it stops when settled and wakes on the next reading.

The request list is a real ordered list with one tab stop: Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Enter or Space inspects. Each row reads its time, route, tokens and outcome. A polite status speaks only changes of state (queue forming or clearing, throttled, full), never a refill tick.
Under reduced motion the surface steps to each reading, slabs fade in place and droplets fade, but the refill still rises and every number and clock still updates.
Below a 34rem container the list hides behind the Requests toggle (aria-expanded) and replaces the readout; action labels collapse to icons with their names kept.
Colours come from tokens: the water is pigment (a fixed lightness from the accent's hue) so it reads the same in light and dark themes.

items.title: Crew Usage
items.tagline: Who uses the assistant, and for what.
items.description: A team usage table for an assistant with a row per member — requests, tokens, spend, a thirty-day sparkline on one shared scale and a thin strip of what they use it for — where switching the metric morphs every sparkline at once on springs.glide while the rows re-rank on glide and their rank numbers roll on springs.snap. Focusing or clicking a member opens their strip into a full breakdown whose measured height unfolds on glide as its segments grow in a cascade. It is a real grid with one roving cell: Up and Down move members, Left and Right move cells, Home and End jump, Enter opens the member, Space or focus opens the breakdown, Escape closes it and M cycles the metric.

props.name: members

props.name: roles

props.name: usage
props.description: Daily usage per member id, oldest first: { requests, spend, tokens } as number arrays. The window is the series' length.

props.name: tasks

props.name: mix

props.name: metric / defaultMetric

props.name: onMetricChange
props.description: Fires from the switch or the M key with the new metric.

props.name: expanded / defaultExpanded
props.description: The member whose breakdown is open, controlled or initial.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Fires when focus or a click opens a breakdown, or with null when it closes.

props.name: onOpenMember

props.name: onExport

props.name: canSeeCosts

props.name: status
props.description: Usage arrived, is on its way, or failed. A team with no usage shows the empty state.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after usage failed to load.

props.name: now
props.description: The last day of the window (ms); day labels count back from it.

props.name: title
props.description: The table's heading.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Under the heading; by default the window's dates.

props.name: formatMoney
props.description: How money is printed.

props.name: sparkStyle
props.description: How a sparkline is drawn: a line with an end dot, an area, or day bars.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height, padding and sparkline height.

props.name: accent
props.description: Sparklines, the metric pill and the hue the task colours turn from: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: disabled

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the panel.

usageNotes: No loops run: every motion is a spring or tween started by a change. Sparkline paths keep the same point count across metrics, so the morph is a pure interpolation of their numbers on one spring.

The grid has one tab stop. Up and Down move members, Left and Right move cells, Home and End jump, Enter opens the member, Space or focus opens the breakdown, Escape closes it and M cycles the metric (Escape with nothing open is left for the page).
Sparklines share one gently compressed scale so heights compare across the team; each sparkline cell is an image whose label reads the metric, its peak day and its trend.
Without billing access (canSeeCosts false) spend reads Hidden, the Spend option is unavailable with its reason, and Export sends zero spend.
Under reduced motion sparklines switch shape at once, rows reorder in place, breakdowns appear without unfolding and numbers update without rolling.
Below a 40rem container each row becomes a card with the sparkline full width and the other two numbers on the strip's line; the headers stay for assistive technology.

items.title: Cost Streams
items.tagline: Follow the spend from project to model.
items.description: Assistant spend drawn as streams flowing from projects through features to models, each as thick as its money and coloured by the project it left; switching the month drives every node and stream from where it is to the new month's layout on one springs.glide spring, carrying on from any frame a second switch interrupts, while the total rolls on springs.snap and a line names the feature that moved most. Hovering or focusing a node lifts its streams and dims the rest, and Enter or a click isolates it — the plot re-lays out with only its flows at the same money scale on the same morph. Tab moves node to node, Enter isolates, Escape releases, the months are a tablist, and in a narrow container the streams become a nested list of bars.

props.name: projects

props.name: features
