props.name: models
props.description: What bills it, top to bottom.

props.name: months
props.description: The months, oldest first: { id, label, flows: { project, feature, model, amount }[], partialThrough? }.

props.name: month / defaultMonth
props.description: The month shown, controlled or initial.

props.name: onMonthChange
props.description: Fires from the tab or arrow key that changed the month.

props.name: isolated / defaultIsolated
props.description: The node whose flows are isolated, controlled or initial.

props.name: onSelectNode
props.description: Fires when Enter or a click isolates a node, or with null when it is released.

props.name: onExport
props.description: Export was pressed. Omit it and the button is not drawn.

props.name: status
props.description: Spend arrived, is on its way, or failed. A month with no flows shows the empty state.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after spend failed to load.

props.name: title
props.description: The panel's heading.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Under the heading.

props.name: formatMoney
props.description: How money is printed.

props.name: colors
props.defaultValue: pigments turned from the accent's hue
props.description: Project colours in project order.

props.name: plotHeight
props.description: The flow's height in px.

props.name: curvature
props.description: How far each stream's handles reach: 0 a straight band, 1 a deep S.

props.name: nodeWidth
props.description: Thickness of the node bars in px; streams start at their edges.

props.name: accent
props.description: The tab indicator, the isolation chip and the hue the project colours turn from.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: months and isolation cannot change.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the panel.

usageNotes: No loops run. A month change or an isolation starts one spring whose progress interpolates every node and stream; geometry is written straight into the paths and labels per frame, never through React state.

Every node is a button in the tab order with a name that reads its kind, amount and share of the month; Enter or Space isolates it (aria-pressed), Escape releases it. The months are a tablist: arrows, Home and End select.
A partial month (partialThrough) is marked on its tab, noted above the plot, drawn with dashed stream edges, and its total is shown with the pace for the full month.
Under reduced motion months and isolation swap to the new layout at once; dimming stays a short opacity change and totals update without rolling.
Below a 36rem container the streams become a nested list of bars — projects with their features under them, then the models billed — whose rows isolate like the nodes.
The plot width is measured with a ResizeObserver; the server renders a default 696 px layout that the client re-measures without animating.

items.title: Spike Trace
items.tagline: Click a usage spike to see what caused it.
items.description: A workspace's daily usage as bars with anomalous days flagged, where pressing a spike unpacks it: the bar splits into a coloured band per cause and from each band a strand fans out across the chart to its row in a ranked list beside it, drawn by a clip that sweeps from the bar to the list on springs.glide while the rows arrive in a cascade and one line names the biggest cause. Switching between keys, people and prompts re-splits the bar and re-sweeps the strands, and Escape folds it back on the exit ease. The flagged days are a roving set of buttons — Left and Right move between them, Home and End jump, Enter or Space unpacks, Escape folds — and in a narrow container the strands become a stacked bar above the list.

props.name: days
props.description: Daily usage, oldest first: { date, total }.

props.name: attributions
props.description: What made each flagged day, by date: { keys, members, prompts } lists of { id, label, amount, detail? }.

props.name: flags
props.description: The days the detector flagged: { date, expected?, note? }. Empty shows the no-spikes state.

props.name: pending
props.description: Flagged dates whose causes are still being computed.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The unpacked date, controlled or initial.

props.name: onSelectSpike
props.description: Fires from the press or key that unpacked a spike, or with null when it folds.

props.name: dimension / defaultDimension
props.description: What the spike is unpacked by, controlled or initial.

props.name: onDimensionChange
props.description: Fires from the switch with the new dimension.

props.name: onOpenCause
props.description: A cause's Open button was pressed.

props.name: onFlagExpected
props.description: Mark expected was pressed, with the state it asks for. Omit it and the button is not drawn.

props.name: status
props.description: Usage arrived, is on its way, or failed.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after usage failed to load.

props.name: maxCauses
props.description: Causes listed before the rest are folded into one row.

props.name: title
props.description: The panel's heading.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Under the heading; by default the window and the unit.

props.name: unit
props.description: What is counted, in words.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: How an amount is printed.

props.name: strandStyle
props.description: How the strands are drawn: filled ribbons as thick as their share, fine threads, or orthogonal steps.

props.name: flagStyle
props.description: How a flagged day is marked: a pin above the bar, a ring, or a tinted band behind it.

props.name: accent
props.description: The spike, the switch and the hue the cause colours turn from.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: spikes cannot be unpacked or marked.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the panel.

usageNotes: No loops run: an unpack is one clip sweep and a cascade of row entrances. The chart's size is measured with a ResizeObserver and every coordinate is rounded, so the server renders the same markup.

Flagged days are a roving set of buttons over the chart: Left and Right move, Home and End jump, Enter or Space unpacks (aria-pressed), Escape folds. Each reads its weekday, total, multiple of the median and whether it was expected.
The causes are a real ordered list with share text; a polite status speaks the unpack ("Most came from nightly-evals, 61%") and the fold, never per frame.
Under reduced motion the bands, strands and rows appear with a short fade and nothing sweeps or travels.
Below a 40rem container the chart runs full width and the strands give way to a stacked bar of the same shares above the list.
A pending date shows a hatched bar and says its attribution is still being computed; an empty flags list says there were no unusual days.

items.title: Swap Savings
items.tagline: What it would cost on a different model.
items.description: This month's assistant spend by task and model with a what-if mode: as you move a share of a task's traffic to another model, the from-model's bar drops and the to-model's bar rises to their projected heights on springs.glide — chasing the slider so they arrive just behind your hand — over ghost outlines that hold today's heights, while the savings figure rolls on springs.snap beside a quality note that turns warn past your floor. Each share is a real slider whose thumb follows the finger 1:1 and lands on its step on snap with the release velocity; arrows step it, Page Up and Page Down move a quarter, Home and End jump, R resets every share and Flip reverses the pair. In a narrow container the chart turns horizontal.

props.name: models
props.description: The models on the bill: { id, name, short?, inputPrice, outputPrice } per million tokens.

props.name: tasks
props.description: What the traffic is for, in chart order: { id, label }.

props.name: usage
props.description: This month's tokens per task and model: { task, model, inputTokens, outputTokens }.

props.name: quality
props.description: Quality per model and task, 0–100, from your evals.

props.name: fromModel
props.description: The model traffic moves away from; Flip swaps the pair.

props.name: toModel
props.description: The model traffic moves to.

props.name: mix / defaultMix
props.description: Share of each task's traffic moved, 0 to 1, controlled or initial.

props.name: onMixChange
props.description: Fires from the slider, key or Reset that changed a share, with the whole mix.

props.name: onApplyMix
props.description: Apply mix was pressed.

props.name: onReset
props.description: Reset (or R) put every share back to today's.

props.name: onCompare
props.description: Compare was pressed. Omit it and the button is not drawn.

props.name: status
props.description: Usage is ready, loading, too thin to project from, or failed.

props.name: daysOfData
props.description: Days of traffic so far, for the not-enough-data state.

props.name: daysNeeded
props.description: Days a projection needs.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Try again was pressed after usage failed to load.

props.name: step
props.description: How far one arrow key moves a share.

props.name: qualityFloor
props.description: A drop in quality past this many points is flagged.

props.name: title
props.description: The panel's heading.

props.name: formatMoney
props.description: How money is printed.

props.name: ghostStyle
props.description: How today's heights are kept while the bars move: a dashed outline, a faint shade, or a cap line.

props.name: barWidth
props.description: Bar thickness in px; the gap between a group's bars widens for thin bars so their labels never collide.

props.name: accent
props.description: The to-model's bars, the sliders and the savings: a named pigment or any CSS colour.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Read only: shares cannot move.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the panel.

usageNotes: The projection is pure math (the exported projectSwap): moved tokens are re-priced at the new model's rates and the moved traffic's quality is weighed by the tokens moved.
No loops run. A drag writes one motion value per thumb; bars chase the stepped share on a spring through a CSS variable, so the same element stands in a column or lies in a row.

Each share is role="slider" with a value text ("40% of summaries moved to Waylight Lite"): arrows step, Page Up and Page Down move a quarter, Home and End jump, R resets every share. The savings are spoken when a change lands, never per pixel.
Apply mix stays focusable and reads aria-disabled until a share moves, so focus never falls to the page.
Under reduced motion bars and thumbs jump to their values and figures update without rolling.
Below a 36rem container the chart turns horizontal, a row per task with its slider underneath.

items.title: Command Deck
items.tagline: A palette that arms before it fires.
items.description: A command palette that arms before it fires — a deliberate fill sweeps the selected row before execution, so destructive commands never feel accidental.

props.name: commands
props.description: { id, label, hint?, icon?, section?, keywords?, destructive?, run } per command.

props.name: open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange
props.description: Controlled or uncontrolled visibility.

props.name: hotkey
props.description: Global ⌘K / Ctrl+K toggle listener.

props.name: inline / portal
props.description: Inline renders just the panel (docs/demos); portal overlays into body with focus trap and scroll lock.

props.name: recentKey
props.description: localStorage key for the five most recent command ids.

usageNotes: Full combobox semantics with focus trap and restore; Escape mid-arm cancels the sweep.
Under reduced motion the arming sweep becomes an instant fill with a deliberate 120ms pause.

items.title: Access Panel
items.tagline: Sign-in that unlocks like a vault.
items.description: Sign-in that unlocks like a vault — steps ride a gantry rail, OTP digits drop into their cells, and the right code throws a breaker bolt open.

props.name: expectedCode
props.description: The six-digit code that throws the bolt.

props.name: onVerify
props.description: Fires with the entered code on every attempt.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Fires once when the correct code lands.

props.name: email
props.description: Prefills the email field.

usageNotes: One hidden input with autocomplete="one-time-code" drives the six visual cells — the accessibility-correct OTP pattern.
Under reduced motion the rail slides become fades and the rejection nudge is skipped; the alert still announces.

items.title: Signal Center
items.tagline: An inbox that files itself.
items.description: An inbox that files itself — signals arrive on the conveyor, swipe away with real velocity, and clear-all sweeps the floor in a cascade.

props.name: signals / defaultSignals / onSignalsChange
props.description: Controlled or uncontrolled feed; Signal = { id, source, title, detail?, time, read? }.

props.name: onArchive
props.description: Fires per archived signal, including clear-all.

props.name: title
props.description: Header title next to the live unread readout.

usageNotes: Archiving is keyboard-reachable via a per-row button; swiping is the fast path, not the only path.
Under reduced motion arrivals and exits become fades and clear-all loses its stagger.

items.title: Media Console
items.tagline: A media island that unfolds into a console.
items.description: A media island that unfolds into a console — the pill morphs open into transport, a caliper timeline, and a scope-scrubbed volume.

props.name: tracks
props.description: { id, title, artist, duration } — playback is simulated; the JSDoc shows wiring a real audio element.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.description: Start as the pill or the full console.

usageNotes: Complete keyboard transport; Escape collapses the console back to the pill.
Under reduced motion the morph becomes a crossfade and the waveform holds still.

items.title: Checkout Receipt
items.tagline: Payment that prints its proof.
items.description: Payment that prints its proof — hold to pay, then a receipt feeds out of the slot line by line, tears off, and takes a PAID stamp.

props.name: items
props.description: Line items ({ name, price }) summed into the total.

props.name: currency
props.description: Price prefix.

props.name: onPay
props.description: Fires when the hold completes.

usageNotes: The receipt is real text in a definition list; only the barcode is decorative.
Under reduced motion the receipt appears whole and the stamp fades in.

items.title: Intake Tray
items.tagline: Files land, physically.
items.description: Files land, physically — dropped files fall into the tray with a squash, shingle into a stack, fill their gauge rings, and slide to the processed rail.

props.name: onFiles
props.description: Receives each accepted batch.

props.name: accept / maxFiles
props.description: Accepted types hint and tray capacity.

props.name: simulate
props.description: Hash-driven demo progress; the JSDoc documents wiring real uploads.

props.name: ref
props.description: Imperative addFiles() for programmatic intake.

usageNotes: The drop zone is a real button with a labeled native file input — fully keyboard operable.
Under reduced motion chips stack neatly with fades; the gauge rings still fill.

items.title: Readout Grid
items.tagline: Dashboard stats as instrument cards.
items.description: Dashboard stats as instrument cards — a carry-rolling counter, a self-drawing sparkline, a split-flap delta, and a needle gauge, mounted with one cascade.

props.name: metrics
props.description: Optional full override of the four cards: counter, sparkline, flap, and gauge shapes.

usageNotes: Each card is an article whose label reads naturally to screen readers; chart visuals carry sr-only values.
Under reduced motion cards render in place, the sparkline arrives fully drawn, and the needle jumps.

items.title: Launch Checklist
items.tagline: Setup steps that stamp themselves done.
items.description: Onboarding checklist where ticks draw themselves, finished steps strike through and settle to the bottom, and completing the set lands a CALIBRATED stamp.

props.name: steps
props.description: Step definitions: id, title, optional description.

props.name: completed / defaultCompleted
props.description: Controlled or uncontrolled set of completed step ids.

props.name: onCompletedChange
props.description: Fires on every toggle with the new completed set.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Fires once when the final step completes.

usageNotes: Rows are native checkboxes under the hood — the whole block is keyboard and screen-reader operable.
Under reduced motion rows reorder instantly and the stamp fades in; the progress track still reports value via ARIA.

items.title: Iris Menu
items.tagline: Actions bloom from where you pressed.
items.description: Actions bloom from where you pressed — items launch from the trigger's center to seats along the freest quadrant's arc, and fold back in on close.

props.name: items
props.description: Up to six: { id, icon, label, onSelect, disabled?, destructive? }.

props.name: placement
props.description: Auto measures the viewport and blooms into the roomiest quadrant.

props.name: radius
props.description: Distance from trigger center to each seat.

usageNotes: Arrow keys rotate focus around the ring; Escape closes and restores the trigger.
Under reduced motion items fade in already seated — no travel.

items.title: Overflow Rail
items.tagline: More actions, sprung from the dots.
items.description: More actions, sprung from the dots — the pill rail morphs open inline while primaries yield with a recoil part and secondaries cascade in.

props.name: primary / secondary
props.description: Always-visible actions and the set revealed by the ⋯ trigger.

props.name: open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange
props.description: Controlled or uncontrolled expansion.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible toolbar name.

usageNotes: One toolbar: arrows rove across every visible action; Escape collapses and refocuses the trigger.
Under reduced motion the width jumps and secondaries fade in place.

items.title: Beacon
items.tagline: One capsule, every live activity.
items.description: One capsule, every live activity — the shell morphs between timer, upload, call, and now-playing views with blur crossfades, corners pinned.

props.name: activity
props.description: Discriminated union: timer (endsAt), upload (progress), call (accept/decline), playing (title/artist); null collapses to a standby pill.

props.name: expanded / defaultExpanded / onExpandedChange
props.description: Controlled or uncontrolled detail row.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Renders a dismiss action in the detail row.

usageNotes: Call buttons are reachable while collapsed; activity changes announce once, debounced.
Under reduced motion the shell resizes instantly and the loops hold still.

items.title: Field Report
items.tagline: Feedback that files itself.
items.description: Feedback that files itself — a notch rating with a gliding indicator, a growing note field, and a submit that folds the form into a slot under a LOGGED stamp.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Fires on valid submit; rating is 1–5.

props.name: prompt / endLabels
props.description: The question and the rail's end labels.

props.name: resetAfterMs
props.description: Fades a fresh form back in after filing.

usageNotes: The rating is a real radiogroup — arrows move the indicator, and empty submits nudge with a role=alert line.
Under reduced motion the filing collapse becomes a fade and the stamp lands statically.

items.title: Not Found
items.tagline: Sweep complete. Sector empty.
items.description: Sweep complete, sector empty — a radar arc scans a quiet grid while the 404 numeral deciphers itself, with home and command-deck exits.

props.name: face

props.name: homeHref
props.description: Return-to-base link target.

props.name: onCommandDeck
props.description: Renders the ghost command-deck action when provided.

props.name: code / message
props.description: The cipher numeral and the rising subline.

usageNotes: The heading carries real text for screen readers; the cipher layer and radar are decorative.
Under reduced motion the sweep freezes mid-arc and the numeral renders plainly.

items.title: Forecast Card
items.tagline: Every vote moves every bar.
items.description: Every vote moves every bar — one commit renormalizes the whole field while percentages carry-roll and the leader tick migrates to the new front-runner.

props.name: question / options

props.description: Controlled or uncontrolled viewer vote.

props.name: closesAt
props.description: Compact mono CLOSES footer line.

usageNotes: Rows are aria-pressed buttons; each vote announces the new percentage and leadership once.
Under reduced motion widths jump and the leader tick teleports; the readouts pulse instead of rolling.

items.title: Balance Card
items.tagline: A balance with a private side.
items.description: A balance with a private side — the numeral carry-rolls behind a privacy blur, a sparkline draws itself, and the card flips to its activity face.

props.name: balance / format / delta / series
props.description: The carry-rolling amount, its delta chip, and the sparkline data.

props.name: activity
props.description: Back-face rows: { id, label, amount, time }.

props.description: Fires from the action row.

props.description: Start with the balance blurred.

usageNotes: The hidden face is inert and aria-hidden — the flip never traps focus or leaks taps.
Under reduced motion the flip is instant, the sparkline arrives drawn, and the blur toggles without a tween.

items.title: Exchange Panel
items.tagline: Two units, one clean swap.
items.description: Two units, one clean swap — the edited side is live, the computed side carry-rolls after a debounce, and swapping keeps focus while contents trade places.

props.name: units
props.description: Linear factors to a shared base unit; groups render a grouped select.

props.name: feeRate
props.description: Fraction applied to the converted side, shown as a fee row.

props.name: onChange / onDirectionChange
props.description: Conversion updates and swap events.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Delay before the computed side rolls.

usageNotes: One side holds authority; the other is always derived — swapping transfers authority with the gesture and refocuses the input.
Under reduced motion contents swap instantly and the readout uses its highlight fallback.

items.title: Agent Desk
items.tagline: The chat, assembled from its instruments.
items.description: The chat surface assembled from its instruments: tabbed threads, each a volley-thread whose agent turns can open a train-of-thought, with the prompt-well seated at the foot — models, @ sources, and / commands included. The desk contributes the tabs and the seating; every behaviour belongs to the primitive that owns it, which is the point of having primitives.

props.name: threads
props.description: Tabbed conversations; agent turns may embed a train-of-thought.

props.name: models / onSubmit
props.description: Passed to the composer; submissions carry their thread.

usageNotes: Arrival weight, trace disclosure, and composer behaviour all belong to their primitives — the desk only seats them.
Thread swaps crossfade rather than slide: tabs are peers, not a journey.
Notes under agent turns carry the read/tool/duration line, the part worth trusting.

items.title: Calendar Workroom
items.tagline: A month with a working surface under it.
items.description: The production calendar as a workroom, not a widget: a month face for shape and a week face for the coming days, category chips whose counts are derived from the events they filter, a peek panel for any event, and inline create on the chosen day. The anchor month is a prop — the grid is computed from it, never read from the clock, so the same calendar renders on the server and on every visit.

props.name: anchor
props.description: The month shown. Computed into a grid — the block never reads the wall clock.

props.name: categories / events
props.description: The chips and the entries; chip counts derive from the events, so they cannot drift.

props.name: weekAnchorDay
props.description: The day whose Monday-aligned run the week face shows.

usageNotes: Month and week crossfade rather than slide — two faces of one room, not a journey.
Inline create ends with a named commitment (“Put it on the board”), never a bare check mark.
Peek and compose share the desk below the grid, one at a time; Escape abandons a draft.

items.title: Workroom Shell
items.tagline: The rail, given a room to run.
items.description: The workbench rail composed into a room: rail on one side, a content pane on the other, and a crossfade between panes as the selection moves. The rail keeps every behaviour it already owns — the travelling highlight, the fold to a spine, the printed quota — and the shell contributes only the seating and the handoff of selection, which is the point of having primitives.

props.name: panes
props.description: One pane per primary destination; the ids line up with the rail's items.

props.name: workspace / threads
props.description: Handed to the rail untouched.

usageNotes: Pane swaps crossfade — destinations are peers, not steps.
On narrow surfaces the rail steps out entirely; that edition is the workroom drawer.
The rail's own fold-to-spine keeps working inside the shell, so the width is always recoverable.

items.title: Workroom Drawer
items.tagline: The rail steps out; the work keeps the width.
items.description: The workroom for narrow surfaces: the rail steps off-canvas into a drawer and the content keeps the full width. The drawer primitive owns everything hard — focus trap, Escape, backdrop, the edge drag — and the rail owns its furniture; this block contributes the bar, the contained stage, and the rule that picking a destination closes the drawer, because on a phone the menu is a hallway, not a room you stay in.

props.name: panes
props.description: The content behind each destination.

props.name: workspace / threads
props.description: Handed to the rail untouched.

usageNotes: Selection closes the drawer — a deliberate rule of the block, not of the primitive.
The drawer is contained (portal={false}) so the block owns its stage in docs and previews alike.
Focus trapping, Escape, and the drag-to-dismiss all belong to the drawer primitive.

items.title: Split Ledger Hero
items.tagline: The argument left, the product at work right.
items.description: An editorial split hero: the argument on the left, the product already at work on the right. The copy column arrives on the cascade; the vignette is a live day-ledger whose total carry-rolls and whose rows carry real status seals. A gradient drift held low behind everything keeps the reading line in charge.

props.name: headline / copy / eyebrow
props.description: The copy column. Headline is two lines, one per element.

props.name: rows / panelTitle / panelMetric
props.description: The vignette's schedule and its rolling total.

props.name: primaryCta / secondaryCta / onPrimary / onSecondary
props.description: Both actions; primary carries the arrow.

usageNotes: The vignette is composed from readout and status-seal, so the proof panel moves like the product, not like a screenshot.
Sections render full-bleed: give the block the page width and it manages its own column.
Under reduced motion the copy resolves in place and the drift holds still.

items.title: Launch Beacon Hero
items.tagline: One announcement, one claim, one action.
items.description: A centered launch hero: one announcement, one claim, one action. The stack lands on the cascade over a contour wavefield held at low opacity, and the proof row carry-rolls its numbers in — a number that arrives reads as measured where a printed one reads as claimed.

props.name: notice / headline / copy
props.description: Announcement chip, two-line headline, and the standfirst.

props.name: metrics
props.description: The proof row — value, suffix, label; numbers roll in.

props.name: primaryCta / secondaryCta / onPrimary / onSecondary
props.description: Both actions; secondary renders as a ghost.

usageNotes: The wavefield is atmosphere, not spectacle — held at 0.35 opacity under a grounding gradient so copy stays the brightest thing on stage.
Sections render full-bleed: give the block the page width and it manages its own column.
Under reduced motion the stack resolves in place, the field stills, and the metrics print at value.

items.title: Console Drift Hero
items.tagline: The product demonstrating itself in its own medium.
items.description: A console hero for tools that live in the terminal. Copy holds the left edge; the vignette is a framed console whose listing turns out line by line — the product demonstrating itself in its own medium — while aurora ribbons rise from the page floor, faded low so the listing stays the brightest thing on the stage.

props.name: headline / copy / eyebrow
props.description: The copy column. Headline is two lines, one per element.

props.name: code / filename / checks
props.description: The console vignette — listing, title rail, and its seals.

props.name: primaryCta / secondaryCta / onPrimary / onSecondary
props.description: Both actions; primary carries the arrow.

usageNotes: The listing is code-lathe with streaming on — every line is in the DOM from the first frame, so copy and screen readers always see whole source.
Sections render full-bleed: give the block the page width and it manages its own column.
Under reduced motion the listing is simply there, complete and still, and the ribbons hold.

items.title: Glass Rail Navbar
items.tagline: Earns its keep once content moves under it.
items.description: A glass rail that condenses as the page gets underway: tall and transparent at rest, tighter with a blur and a hairline once content scrolls under it. Desktop links share one slipstream pill that chases hover and focus; the mobile fold glides open below the rail.

props.name: brand / links / activeHref
props.description: Identity, the link set, and the current page.

props.name: cta / onCta
props.description: The rail's one action; repeated inside the mobile fold.

usageNotes: The hover pill is slipstream — one shared pill chasing hover and focus, never one per link.
The fold and the condensing are height and blur only; no layout jumps for content below.
Under reduced motion the pill parks, and the fold and condensing switch states in place.

items.title: Dock Pill Navbar
items.tagline: One dot, one home, always somewhere.
items.description: A floating pill dock moored top-center rather than spanning the page. The active page carries a seated dot; choosing another link sends the dot sliding along the pill on the snap spring via a shared layout id. On small screens the fold opens as a full sheet whose links land on the cascade.

props.name: brand / links / activeHref
props.description: Identity, the link set, and the seated page.

props.name: cta / onCta
props.description: The dock's one action; repeated inside the sheet.

usageNotes: The dot is a layoutId — it travels between links rather than blinking out and back.
The mobile sheet is a dialog: focus stays inside it and Escape-free close is the visible button.
Under reduced motion the dot seats instantly and the sheet fades in place.

items.title: Terrace Footer
items.tagline: Brand, link garden, ground line.
items.description: A terraced mega footer: brand and the ask on the top terrace, the link garden below, and the ground line — a live status pip and the fine print — at the base. The newsletter slot composes the library's own field and button, so subscribing has the same traced focus and pressed confirm as the product above it.

props.name: columns
props.description: The link garden — heading plus links per column.

props.name: newsletterTitle / onSubscribe
props.description: The ask; omit onSubscribe to run the form inert.

props.name: statusLabel / fineprint
props.description: The ground line's two ends.

usageNotes: The status line breathes through status-pip rather than claiming uptime in static text.
Subscribe validates the address shape and reports through a polite status line.
Columns collapse two-up on small screens; the ground line wraps before it truncates.

items.title: Drift Mark Footer
items.tagline: The brand at rest, still moving.
items.description: A closing footer built around the wordmark itself: the name rides a slow ticker at display size behind a hairline, dragging under hover the way the tape always has — the brand at rest, still moving. One closing ask above; a thin link line and the fine print below.

props.name: mark / headline
props.description: The riding wordmark and the closing ask above it.

props.name: cta / onCta / links / fineprint
props.description: The action, the thin link line, and the last word.

usageNotes: The moving mark is ticker-tape — friction, hover drag, and the reduced-motion park all come from it.
The tape row is aria-hidden; the brand is carried by the visible links and fine print.
Keep the mark short — it repeats four times per loop copy at display size.

items.title: Bento Field Features
items.tagline: One working cell anchors the grid.
items.description: A bento field: one working cell anchors the grid and the rest state their case at a glance. The anchor is a live throughput chart drawn by the library's own spark instrument; the smaller cells carry a rolling metric, sealed guarantees, and plain statements. Cells arrive on the cascade, largest first.

props.name: eyebrow / headline / copy

Under reduced motion rows resolve in place as they enter.

items.title: Relay Tabs Features

Under reduced motion beats print in place and the indicator parks.

items.title: Open Ledger Pricing
items.tagline: Arithmetic performed in front of you.

items.title: Signal Band Stats
items.tagline: The claim is the number.
items.description: A stats band set like a headline, not a dashboard: oversized numerals on a single rule, edge to edge, no cards and no charts. Every numeral is the library's rolling readout at display size, resolving on the cascade as the band enters.

items.title: Impact Report Stats
items.tagline: Numbers with their provenance attached.
items.description: Stats set as an impact report rather than a dashboard: a narrative column that says what changed and why it matters, beside a ledger of metric rows — each a rolling numeral, its delta seal, and a year of context drawn as a spark line right where the claim is made. items.title: Marquee Hall Logos

items.title: Dispatch Wall Testimonials
items.tagline: One lead voice, a wall of pattern.
items.description: A dispatch wall: one quotation set large on the balance instrument — its words rising and resolving in reading order — over a wall of shorter dispatches arriving on the cascade. props.name: lead
props.description: The large quotation on the balance instrument.

props.name: dispatches
props.description: The wall — quote, name, role per card.

usageNotes: The lead quote's word-by-word rise belongs to balance-quote; the wall only cascades.
Cards are figures with real blockquote and figcaption semantics.
Four across on desktop, two on tablet, one on small screens.

items.title: Standing Desk Testimonials
items.tagline: Every claim carries its number.
items.description: One testimony at a time, at a standing desk: the roster on the left, the floor given wholly to whoever holds it. Choosing a name slides their testimony in from the side it queues on, and every claim carries a proof seal — the measured thing the quote rests on — because a testimonial with a number survives skepticism better than adjectives do.

props.name: entries
props.description: Quote, name, role, and the proof line sealed beside it.

props.name: eyebrow / headline
props.description: The standfirst above the desk.

usageNotes: The roster is a real tablist; the floor is the single live panel.
Testimonies enter from the side they queue on — direction follows roster order.
Under reduced motion testimonies crossfade in place.

items.title: Launch Window CTA

Reassurances stay mono and quiet — they are footnotes, not features.

items.title: Terminal Close CTA
items.tagline: The ask is the install line.
items.description: A closing move for tools that live in the terminal: the ask is the install command itself, turned out in the console frame with copy one click away — because for this audience, get started means give me the line. A conventional button stands beside it for everyone else.

Assurances are seals, not prose: short, checkable claims.

items.title: Split Registry FAQ
items.tagline: The rail answers where; the drawers answer what.
items.description: A FAQ set like a registry: the index down a sticky left rail — one jump link per group — and the questions on the right, each group a drawer accordion whose panels glide open on the library's own spring. props.name: eyebrow / headline / copy
props.description: The rail's standfirst.

items.title: Counter Desk FAQ
items.tagline: Ask first, browse second.
items.description: A FAQ with a counter desk: ask first, browse second. The filter is the library's own traced field, narrowing the drawers live as you type — matching question, answer, and hidden keywords — and when nothing matches, the desk says so plainly and offers a person, carrying your words along.

props.name: onContact

The empty desk is a real state with a real action, not a dead end.
Filtering matches hidden keywords, so drawers surface for words their text never uses.

items.title: Launch Rail Announcements
items.tagline: One rail, every update, one dismissal.
items.description: A launch rail for the top of a page: the library's own alert bar carrying a rolling slot of updates — one line at a time, each holding just long enough to read. The bar owns the entrance, the severity stripe, and the dismissal that closes the space behind it; the slot only rolls. Dismiss it and every update goes at once, the way a rail should.

Under reduced motion the slot steps between lines without travel.

items.title: First Light Empty State
items.tagline: A runway, not an apology.
items.description: The first minute of a product, treated as a moment rather than an apology: a dashed intake frame where the work will soon live, three concrete first moves arriving on the cascade, and one primary action. No sad illustration, no nothing-here-yet — the empty state is a runway, and it says which way to take off.

props.description: Optional illustration seated above the copy; decorative.

props.name: headline / copy / primaryCta

usageNotes: Deliberately in-panel: the full-page empty state belongs to the not-found block.
First moves are buttons, not cards — every surface here does something.
Under reduced motion the moves print in place.

items.title: Gatehouse Step Form
items.tagline: Forward must earn it; back is always open.
items.description: A gatehouse for longer asks: the journey drawn by the library's own stepper — connectors filling, cleared steps stamping their check — while each stage slides in from the direction of travel. The shell's contribution is the data layer: per-step validation that blocks forward but never back, a review stage before anything sends, and a finished state that says what happens next.

Stages slide from the direction of travel; reduced motion crossfades in place.

items.title: Pressroom Newsletter
items.tagline: Show the issue, then ask.
items.description: A newsletter signup that shows the goods: the latest issue set as a pressroom proof — number, title, standfirst, read time — beside the ask. Subscribing is the library's own field and pressed confirm, and the cadence line is a commitment, not a vibe. If the preview does not earn the address, the section has honestly answered the question.

props.description: Fired with a shape-valid address.

Submit validates the address shape and reports through a polite status line.

items.title: Routing Desk Contact
items.tagline: Who answers, and when, before you write.

Artifacts are the proof layer: name what the product holds, not what it intends.

items.title: Field Passage Content

items.title: Ops Desk Data Table

items.title: Proof Strip Features

items.title: Split Doors CTA
items.tagline: Two doors, terms on both.
items.description: The close as two honest doors: self-serve and guided, given equal floor and equal typography — the primary door earns its weight through the button alone. Each door states its own micro-terms underneath, because the reader choosing a path deserves to know its cost before knocking.

props.name: doors
props.description: Kicker, title, copy, action, and the mono micro-terms per door.

props.name: headline
props.description: The line above both doors.

usageNotes: Doors get identical layout; only the button variant separates them.
Micro-terms are commitments — no card, no sequence — not feature bullets.
Two doors only; a third door is a pricing page.

items.title: Share Dial Stats
items.tagline: Point at a slice; the centre follows.
items.description: A share-of-everything stats section: the dial is the library's own donut — slices that pop out under the pointer, a centre readout that follows the active slice — beside two notes that say what the shares mean. Proportions carry this story better than counts, and the dial is built for exactly that reading.

props.name: segments / totalLabel / format
props.description: The dial, straight into donut-breakdown.

props.name: notes
props.description: What the shares mean, in two short arguments.

usageNotes: All dial behaviour belongs to donut-breakdown — pop-out, centre follow, and its announcements.
Two notes on purpose: the biggest share and the one you are shrinking.
Feed raw counts, never pre-computed percentages — the dial derives shares, and doubling them up prints twice.

items.title: Heat Year Stats
items.tagline: Not how much — when, and how steadily.
items.description: Half a year of work as weather: the library's heat calendar draws the rhythm — weekday rows, a visible mid-season push, honest quiet weekends — with the summary numbers rolling in beside it. The grid answers the question a total can't: not how much, but when, and how steadily.

props.name: days / unit
props.description: The grid, straight into heat-calendar; the default half-year is deterministic.

props.name: figures / attestation
props.description: The rolling summary numbers and the provenance line.

usageNotes: Grid interaction — roving focus, per-cell readout — belongs to heat-calendar.
The default data keeps weekends honest; a grid with no quiet reads as invented.
Say where the numbers come from; the attestation line is part of the design.

items.title: Focus Turn Testimonials
items.tagline: Touch the dots and the clock stops.
items.description: One sentence at a time, resolving from blur: each quote takes the whole stage and pulls into focus word by word on the library's focus instrument, holds long enough to land, then yields. Dots below give the reader the wheel — selecting one stops the clock, because a carousel that fights the reader loses the testimonial's whole point.

props.name: quotes
props.description: Quote, name, role — one sentence each; the resolve carries longer ones badly.

props.name: interval
props.description: Seconds each quote holds before the next resolves.

usageNotes: The resolve belongs to focus-text; the section only rotates and keys it.
Any dot press stops the auto-advance for good — reader control is one-way by design.
Keep quotes to one sentence; the whole point is a line that lands whole.

items.title: First Light Strip
items.tagline: The page pausing to say something once.
items.description: A launch moment, not a notice: a full-bleed strip between sections where the announcement gets cinematic room — a drifting gradient behind one sealed line, one sentence, one arrow. Deliberately not dismissible and deliberately not sticky; the inline bar with a close belongs to the alert instrument. This is the page pausing to say something once.

props.name: seal / headline / copy
props.description: The moment — one seal, one line, one sentence.

props.name: actionLabel / onAction
props.description: The single arrowed path onward.

usageNotes: No dismissal by design — dismissible notices belong to alert-bar and the launch rail.
Place it between sections as a full-bleed pause, not at the page top.
The drift stays behind a horizontal gradient so the line reads at both edges.

items.title: Quiet Close Footer
items.tagline: The page signing its name and stepping back.
items.description: The quiet close: one row — wordmark, links, fine print — and one human sign-off line above it. For pages whose footer's whole job is to end gracefully: no columns, no form, no wordmark theatrics, just the page signing its name and stepping back. The stillness is the design.

props.name: brand / links / fineprint
props.description: The single row's three parts.

props.name: signoff
props.description: The one human line above the legal one.

usageNotes: Deliberately still — no motion imports at all; the stillness is the point.
The sign-off is the block's voice; write it like a person, not a brand.
The row wraps in thirds on narrow screens without reordering.

items.title: Ledger Note Newsletter
items.tagline: A circulation count worth printing.
items.description: A newsletter note for between sections: one line of pitch, the field, and the circulation count rolling beside it — because join four thousand readers is only worth saying when the number is real enough to print. Compact by design; the full pressroom treatment belongs to its own section.

props.name: readers / readersLabel
props.description: The honest circulation count, on the readout.

props.name: headline / copy / cta
props.description: The one-line pitch and the ask.

props.name: onSubscribe
props.description: Fired with a shape-valid address.

usageNotes: A band, not a destination — borders top and bottom seat it between sections.
Print the readers count only if it is real; the block's honesty is its pitch.
The form collapses under the pitch on small screens.

items.title: Direct Lines Contact
items.tagline: Real inboxes, stated plainly.
items.description: Contact without a form: three direct lines, each an address you can copy verbatim — the copy control confirms in place — with who reads it, how fast, and a live pip where someone is actually on rotation now. For teams whose honest answer to contact us is an inbox with a person behind it, not a ticket funnel.

props.name: lines
props.description: Kicker, title, address, expectation, and whether someone is on rotation.

props.name: eyebrow / headline / copy
props.description: The standfirst above the lines.

usageNotes: Addresses are mailto links and copyable verbatim; the copy control confirms in place.
The pip only appears where presence is measured — an always-on pip is a lie.
A denied clipboard fails silently; the mailto link is the fallback path.

items.title: Cover Shelf Gallery
items.tagline: The active cover sits square.
items.description: A shelf of covers in perspective: the library's coverflow banks each plate in 3D as the shelf turns — drag, wheel, and keys all come with it — and the plates are typeset covers, not images, so the shelf reads in both themes at any density. The active cover sits square; its neighbours wait at an angle, the way a shelf actually looks.

props.name: covers
props.description: Kicker, title, note per typeset cover.

props.name: eyebrow / headline
props.description: The centered standfirst.

usageNotes: All shelf physics belong to coverflow — banking, drag, wheel, and keyboard travel.
The status line names the active cover politely as the shelf turns.
Swap the typeset plates for images if you must; the shelf carries either.

items.title: Split Desk Navbar
items.tagline: The top row says it is running.
items.description: A split desk header: the utility row above — small links, a live status pip, quiet on purpose — and the working row below with the brand, the primary links, and the one action. The two-level shape carries products with an operations story: the top row says the thing is running; the bottom row says what it is.

props.name: utilityLinks / statusLabel
props.description: The quiet row — small links and the live pip.

props.name: links / activeHref / cta / onCta
props.description: The working row.

usageNotes: The status pip only belongs there if presence is measured; static text is honest, a fake pip is not.
The mobile fold merges both rows into one list, utility last.
Under reduced motion the fold switches states in place.

items.title: Atlas Panel Navbar
items.tagline: One trigger, the whole atlas.
items.description: A navbar with an atlas: one trigger opens a full-width panel below the bar — grouped destinations with a detail line each, and a closing note for the thing worth announcing. The panel glides open on the same height motion as a fold, closes on escape or any exit, and holds the trigger's expanded state honestly. Small screens get the whole atlas as a plain stacked fold.

props.name: panelLabel / panelGroups / panelNote
props.description: The atlas — grouped entries with detail lines and a closing note.

props.name: links / cta / onCta
props.description: Plain links beside the trigger, and the action.

usageNotes: Escape and any outside press close the atlas; the chevron reports the true state.
Every entry carries a detail line — an atlas of bare labels is just a long menu.
The same atlas serves both the panel and the mobile fold, so content never forks.

items.title: Ribbon Tabs FAQ
items.tagline: Tabs pick the conversation; drawers answer.
items.description: A FAQ on a ribbon: topic tabs ride the gantry — its indicator gliding between groups — and each panel is a drawer accordion. Two instruments, one seam: the tabs answer which conversation you are in; the drawers answer the question. For question sets too wide for one column and too shallow for a sidebar registry.

props.name: groups
props.description: Tab value, label, and the question/answer entries per group.

props.name: eyebrow / headline
props.description: The centered standfirst.

usageNotes: Indicator travel belongs to gantry-tabs, disclosure to drawer-accordion — the section is only the seam.
Keep two to four groups; more belongs to the sidebar registry variant.
Open drawers keep their state per tab visit within the mount.

items.title: Proof Grid Logos
items.tagline: A plaque, not a parade.
items.description: The still logo wall: typographic marks in a hairline grid, resolving one after another on the cascade and then holding — for pages where the moving tape would compete with the content around it. Stillness here is a choice, not a fallback; the grid reads like a plaque, and the attestation line says what earned a place on it.

props.name: marks
props.description: Typographic wordmarks; mono switches the stack.

props.name: claim / attestation
props.description: The line above and the earned-a-place line below.

usageNotes: Deliberately still after the cascade — the moving rail is the marquee hall's job.
The attestation defines membership; a wall without criteria is decoration.
Cells share hairlines through a single bordered grid, two across on small screens.

items.title: Quiet Word Hero
items.tagline: A sentence the reader would underline.
items.description: A manifesto hero: no vignette, no backdrop, no product window — one oversized sentence carrying the whole argument, with the phrase that matters swept by the highlighter as it enters. For products whose best pitch is a sentence the reader would underline themselves.

props.name: lead / swept / tail
props.description: The sentence in three pieces; the middle one takes the sweep.

props.name: copy / cta / onCta / footnote
props.description: The standfirst, the one action, and the quiet line under it.

usageNotes: The sweep belongs to highlight-sweep — it draws once, on entry, and holds.
Resist adding a vignette; the emptiness is what makes the sentence loud.
Keep the swept phrase short — the marker reads as emphasis, not decoration.

items.title: Agent Bench Hero
items.tagline: The vignette is the composer, wired live.
items.description: A hero for agent products where the vignette is the composer itself: the real prompt well, wired live — type @ and the sources actually open, / and the commands do — framed as a bench window with a working seal. The reader's first act on the page is the product's core act, which is the entire argument an agent product needs to make.

props.name: sources / commands / onAsk
props.description: The live composer's offer sets and its submit.

props.name: headline / copy / eyebrow / vignetteTitle
props.description: The copy column and the bench window's title rail.

props.name: primaryCta / secondaryCta / onPrimary / onSecondary
props.description: Both actions.

usageNotes: The composer is prompt-well, genuinely interactive — the copy should invite trying it.
Keep the source list short and named like the reader's own files.
The seal on the window rail states what the bench is reading; keep it truthful to the source list.

items.title: Spec Sheet Features
items.tagline: Read the spec, not the pitch.
items.description: The product as a spec sheet: capabilities set like a chassis plate — grouped terms, mono values, one plain note each — rows resolving on the cascade as the plate enters. For readers who trust a specification more than an adjective, which is most of the readers worth having.

props.name: groups
props.description: Heading plus term/value/note rows per group.

props.name: plateLine
props.description: The stamped footer line on the plate.

usageNotes: Values are mono and short; the note underneath carries the prose.
Every line should be checkable — the copy promises lines come off the plate when untrue.
The double border is the plate's chassis; keep it.

items.title: Gauge Row Features
items.tagline: A needle at two-thirds beats an adjective.
items.description: Capability as headroom: three needle gauges from the library's own cluster, swept to bench-condition values with their red zones showing — because a needle sitting at two-thirds with a visible redline says more about capacity than any adjective. Two notes below say what the reader is looking at and why the honesty is the feature.

props.name: gauges
props.description: The cluster's needles — value, max, unit, redline.

props.name: notes / attestation
props.description: What the reader is looking at, and the bench conditions.

usageNotes: Needle sweep, red zones, and meter semantics belong to gauge-cluster.
Set values at honest load — needles pinned at 10% read as staged.
The attestation names the conditions; gauges without conditions are theatre.

items.title: Signature Line CTA
items.tagline: Joining as a public act.
items.description: The close as a signature line: a ledger of names instead of an email funnel — the count rolls, the latest signatures sit there as provenance, and signing asks only for a name. For communities and open registries where joining is a public act, and the page's proof is who already did.

props.name: count / countLabel / recent
props.description: The rolling count and the provenance names.

props.name: onSign
props.description: Fired once; signing increments the shown count locally.

usageNotes: Signing asks for a name only — adding an email field turns it back into a funnel.
The local increment is honest UI, not the record; wire onSign to the real ledger.
Recent names render in mono italic, like a signature, not a testimonial.

items.title: Postscript CTA
items.tagline: The page stops presenting and starts talking.
items.description: The close as a postscript: after the whole page has argued, one short paragraph in the founder's voice — set like the end of a letter, signed, with a single action and one quiet alternative. It works because it drops the register: the page stops presenting and starts talking.

props.name: postscript / signature / signatureRole
props.description: The paragraph and who signs it.

props.name: cta / onCta / altLabel / altHref
props.description: The one action and the quiet alternative.

usageNotes: Keep it under four sentences or it becomes another section.
The alternative is an inline text link on purpose — two buttons would raise the register again.
Write the P.S. in a person's voice; the drop in register is the device.

items.title: Seat Counter Pricing
items.tagline: See where the next seat gets cheaper.
items.description: Seat pricing with the arithmetic on the counter: step the seats and both numbers roll — the applicable rate, which drops at printed breaks, and the total it produces. Discrete where the usage dial is continuous: for teams who buy in people, not units, and want to see exactly where the next seat gets cheaper.

props.name: breaks
props.description: Ascending rate breaks; the active one reads full strength.

props.name: min / max / defaultSeats
props.description: The counter's range.

props.name: onCta
props.description: Fired with the counted crew and its total.

usageNotes: Stepping belongs to stepper-number — keyboard, hold-to-repeat, and clamping come with it.
The applicable rate is the whole-count rate, not banded — print the breaks so that is obvious.
Both numerals are readouts; a break crossing rolls rate and total together.

items.title: Last Word FAQ
items.tagline: Answers owed, not interactions.
items.description: The questions answered in full sentences, no drawers to open: an editorial FAQ set as a two-column read, ending on the question most FAQs avoid — what is this bad at. Everything visible at once, because a page late enough to hold a FAQ owes the reader answers, not another interaction.

props.name: entries
props.description: Numbered question/answer pairs, all visible.

props.name: eyebrow / headline / copy
props.description: The standfirst.

usageNotes: Deliberately still and drawer-free — the disclosure variants already exist three ways.
End on the concession question; it buys the other answers their credibility.
Four to six entries; more belongs in a drawer variant.

items.title: Two Mornings Use Case
items.tagline: Both mornings, visible whole.
items.description: The same morning, twice: the old one and the new one as parallel timelines, hour marks aligned so the eye can travel across and compare beat for beat. No slider, no wipe — the two columns just sit there, because the argument is strongest when both are visible whole.

props.name: before / after / beforeTitle / afterTitle
props.description: The two timelines; keep the hour marks aligned.

props.name: verdict
props.description: The one-line close under the columns.

usageNotes: Deliberately no wipe — the draggable comparison belongs to slice-compare.
Use identical times in both columns; the alignment is the argument.
Beats cascade in per column and then hold.

items.title: Scale Ladder Use Case
items.tagline: The ladder holds all the way up.
items.description: The product at three scales, set as a ladder: each rung names the size, the shape the product takes there, and — the line most pages hide — what it costs at that rung. Rungs climb in on the cascade with a rail connecting them, because the pitch is not any single rung; it is that the ladder holds all the way up.

props.name: rungs
props.description: Scale, title, copy, and the plain cost line per rung.

props.name: eyebrow / headline / copy
props.description: The standfirst.

usageNotes: The cost line is the rung's honesty; a ladder without prices is a brochure.
Three rungs read as a ladder; five read as a pricing page.
Climbing never means migrating — say so in the copy if it is true.

items.title: Day Clock How-It-Works
items.tagline: A claim with an artifact is a fact.
items.description: How it works, told as a working day: four clock marks down a rail, each with what the product did at that hour and the artifact it left behind — sealed, because a claim with an artifact is a fact. The rail is plain and the entrance is a cascade; the day itself is the mechanism on display.

props.name: marks
props.description: Time, title, copy, and the sealed artifact per mark.

props.name: eyebrow / headline / copy
props.description: The standfirst.

usageNotes: Deliberately not scroll-scrubbed — the playhead timeline belongs to timeline-spine.
Every mark should leave an artifact; a mark without one is a promise, not a mechanism.
Times set in mono against the rail; keep them plausible and ordered.

items.title: Exchange Script How-It-Works
items.tagline: The mechanism, in its own medium.
items.description: How it works, as the conversation it actually is: a scripted exchange on the library's own thread — the reader advances it turn by turn and watches the product answer, act, and file the result. The mechanism explains itself in its own medium, and the notes under each reply say what was read and what was written, which is the part worth trusting.

props.name: script / openingTurns
props.description: The exchange and how much of it starts visible.

props.name: advanceLabel / resetLabel
props.description: The reader's two controls.

usageNotes: The thread is volley-thread — arrival weight, run labels, and live semantics come with it.
Notes under replies carry the trust: what was read, what was written.
The reader advances; nothing auto-plays.

items.title: Cleared Desk Empty State
items.tagline: The emptiness is the reward.
items.description: The empty state you earn rather than the one you arrive in: nothing is left, and the section says so calmly — a tally of what it took, the time it cleared, and one quiet way onward. Deliberately no celebration; the reward is the emptiness itself, and a desk that cheers every time it clears stops meaning anything by Thursday.

props.name: art
props.description: Optional illustration seated above the copy; decorative.

props.name: tally
props.description: What the emptiness cost to earn; numerals roll on readout.

props.name: clearedAt
props.description: The stamp on the seal.

props.name: cta / altLabel
props.description: One action and one quieter one.

usageNotes: No confetti on purpose — pair it with confetti-pop only for a genuinely once-a-quarter clear.
Keep a zero in the tally when there is one; a cleared desk with nothing waiting is the whole claim.
Counts roll rather than count up from zero; feed real numbers, not animations.

items.title: One Question Step Form
items.tagline: One question, the whole frame.
items.description: The long ask, asked one question at a time: each prompt gets the whole frame, Enter carries you forward, and the rail keeps the length honest so nobody feels ambushed. A single question in flight, the answer held, the way back always open, and a summary of everything before it is sent.

props.name: onAnswerChange
props.description: Fires on every keystroke and choice, so a page can mirror answers live.

props.name: questions
props.description: Text or choice prompts; each carries a short rail label.

props.name: showHeader
props.description: Draw the eyebrow and headline above the card. Pass false when the page composes its own header — a card standing beside a preview shares its top edge only once the header is lifted out of the column.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Fired once, on the review stage.

props.name: summaryTitle / submitLabel / doneTitle / doneCopy
props.description: The last two frames.

usageNotes: Selection never auto-advances — a form that moves by itself is a form you cannot review.
Length is delegated to stage-progress; the rail is the promise that this ends.
Focus follows the frame after the first move, never on first paint — landing on the page must not yank the viewport.
Questions slide from the direction of travel, so Back reads as going back.

items.title: Open Bench Team
items.tagline: The seats you have not filled are also the team.
items.description: The bench as it actually stands: the people on it, and — in the same grid, in the same weight — the seats that are still empty. Most pages split these into a team section and a careers page, which quietly implies the team is finished. Showing both says the truer thing, and gives a small company one section where it needed two.

props.name: people / seats
props.description: The bench and the openings, rendered at the same weight.

props.name: seatsTitle
props.description: Heading over the openings; the count seals itself.

usageNotes: Seats carry a dashed border and a real href — an opening nobody can click is decoration.
Write forWhom as a person, not a requirements list; the seat is the pitch.
Initials derive from the name unless you pass them.

items.title: Case Column Testimonial
items.tagline: Depth, where the wall proves breadth.
items.description: One customer, told at length: a single narrow column of narrative with the measured results pinned in the margin and one line lifted out onto the balance instrument. The wall variants prove breadth by counting voices; this one proves depth by staying with a single yard long enough to say what actually changed, and in what order.

props.name: paragraphs / pullQuote / pullAfter
props.description: The story and where the quote is lifted out of it.

props.name: results
props.description: The margin numerals, with optional prefix and suffix.

usageNotes: The pull quote belongs to balance-quote — never re-set it as styled text.
Order the paragraphs by what changed first; a case study that lists benefits is an ad.
The margin stacks above the story below lg; keep results to three or four.

items.title: Margin Notes Content
items.tagline: Argument, not assertion.
items.description: An editorial passage with its annotations in the margin, aligned to the paragraph each one belongs to — the shape of a marked-up document rather than a marketing page. Nothing pops or reveals: the notes are simply there, beside the sentence they qualify, which is what makes a claim readable as argument instead of assertion.

props.name: passages
props.description: Paragraphs, each with an optional margin note.

props.name: standfirst / signature
props.description: The opening and the document's foot.

usageNotes: Below the margin breakpoint notes fold in under their paragraph on a rule, still attached.
Notes warm on hover through the group only — no state, no reveal; the alignment is the device.
Leave paragraphs unannotated where there is nothing to qualify; a note on every line is a footnote habit, not an argument.

items.title: Live Floor Social Proof
items.tagline: Somewhere it is 06:40.
items.description: Proof as the floor itself, running: a live feed of what is happening across every yard right now, arriving on the conveyor with the standing counts above it. Where the evidence band assembles a case from logos, metrics, and a quote, this one makes the simpler and harder argument — that the thing is in use at this moment, and here is it happening.

props.name: events
props.description: The pool the feed cycles through; keep places coarse.

props.name: interval / visible
props.description: Seconds between arrivals, and rows held before the overflow count.

props.name: counts
props.description: The standing numbers above the feed.

usageNotes: Rotation is deterministic — the server renders tick 0 and the client walks the same pool, so there is no hydration drift and no clock.
Each arrival gets a fresh row key; reusing an event id would read to the conveyor as a reorder, not an arrival.
Never name customers in the feed. Coarse places are proof; a customer list is a leak.
Ages come from row position, not timestamps — nothing here needs to be true to the second to be honest.

items.title: Two-Way Integrations
items.tagline: Which way the data actually goes.
items.description: Integrations answered honestly: not which logos we have, but which direction the data actually moves, what is read, what is written, and how often. For the buyer who has been burned by an integration that turned out to be a nightly CSV, and who will ask the question in the second call if the page does not answer it in the first.

props.name: flows
props.description: Each connection with its direction and both payloads.

props.name: caveat
props.description: The footnote most integration pages omit.

usageNotes: Deliberately unfiltered — browsing a catalogue belongs to the patch bay; this page answers one question.
Only claim two-way when both halves are live; the section's whole value is that the claim is checkable.
State sync intervals as floors, and mean it.

items.title: Run History Table
items.tagline: Where a row tells you it is in trouble.
items.description: A report grid where each row carries its own history: the latest number, the outcome, and the last eight runs plotted small beside them, so a row that is fine today but drifting is visible without opening anything. The ops desk is for working a dataset; this one is for reading a trend across rows at a glance.

props.name: rows
props.description: Name, outcome, latest duration, and the run history behind it.

props.name: durationLabel / historyLabel
props.description: Column captions, reused as the mobile labels.

usageNotes: Nothing sorts on purpose — the argument is the shape of each line, and sorting belongs to the ops desk.
Every sparkline is a real spark-chart, so each row carries its own sr-only summary sentence.
The drifting row is the point: seed a series that is fine today and clearly heading somewhere.

items.title: Compare Wipe Hero
items.tagline: The visitor proves it themselves.
items.description: A hero for products that replace something: the argument on the left, and on the right the same morning twice with a blade between them the reader drags themselves. Handing over the blade is the point — a claim the visitor proves with their own hand in the first ten seconds is worth more than any headline.

props.name: before / after
props.description: The same timeline twice; keep the times identical.

props.name: beforeLabel / afterLabel
props.description: The blade's two side labels.

usageNotes: The wipe belongs to slice-compare — never re-implement the blade or its drag.
Both panels must show the same hours, or the comparison is rhetoric rather than evidence.
Keep the after panel boring; 'no change' twice is the strongest line in it.

items.title: Gallery Wall Hero
items.tagline: The copy yields to the work.
items.description: A visual-first hero for work that has to be seen: the claim sits small above a wall of plates that runs the full bleed, scrollable by hand or by keyboard on the library's own gallery. The copy deliberately yields — on a page selling images, a headline competing with the images is a headline in the way.

props.name: plates
props.description: Each plate's face label, caption, and wash.

props.name: wash
props.description: Any CSS background; swap for real artwork and nothing else changes.

usageNotes: Scrolling, snapping, and keyboard travel come from kinetic-gallery.
Keep the headline short — it is a caption for the wall, not a pitch.
The wash is a stand-in; real images want the same aspect box and nothing more.

items.title: Price Forward Hero
items.tagline: Answer the question they arrived with.
items.description: A hero that leads with the price. Most pages spend the fold establishing that they are worth asking about; this one answers the question the visitor came with and lets the rest of the page earn the number afterwards. It only works with simple pricing and nothing hidden below.

props.name: price / currency / period
props.description: The number, on its own plate.

props.name: includes / footnote
props.description: What it covers, and the line that makes it believable.

usageNotes: A headline price with an asterisk is worse than no price at all — only use this when nothing is hidden below.
The footnote is load-bearing: say how billing ends before anyone asks.
The numeral is a readout, so a price experiment rolls rather than cuts.

items.title: Pinned Scroll Features
items.tagline: Paced by the page, not a control.
items.description: The feature tour that uses the scroll it already has: the stage pins and scenes cross-fade under it as the reader moves, so the sequence is paced by the page rather than by a control. The pinning and the hand-off between scenes belong entirely to the sticky instrument.

props.name: scenes
props.description: Each beat's step, title, copy, and mono face lines.

props.name: height
props.description: Pinned stage height in px.

usageNotes: Pinning is sticky-reveal's — never re-implement scroll pinning in the section.
Four beats is the ceiling; a pinned stage that outstays its scroll reads as a hang.
Pair with relay-tabs only if the page is long; both on one page competes for the same attention.

items.title: Quiet Grid Features
items.tagline: The one that just has to be read.
items.description: The restrained one: a plain grid of claims, numbered, with nothing moving but their arrival. Every library needs the section you reach for when the page already has three interactive ones and this part simply has to be read — a page where everything earns attention has none left to give.

props.name: features
props.description: Title and copy per claim; numbering is automatic.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns at the widest breakpoint.

usageNotes: Deliberately still — reach for the bento, the tour, or the gauge row when a claim needs proving.
Six or four claims; an odd number leaves a hole in the last row at three columns.
No icons on purpose. An icon per claim is decoration pretending to be information.

items.title: Persona Switch Features
items.tagline: What it is for depends where you stand.
items.description: The same product, argued three ways: a control picks the reader, and the claims swap for the ones that person actually cares about. It solves the real problem of a mixed audience without the usual answer — three near-identical feature sections stacked down the page.

props.name: personas
props.description: Each reader's lede and three claims.

props.name: eyebrow / headline / copy
props.description: The standfirst above the control.

usageNotes: The thumb's travel belongs to segmented-control; the section only swaps content under it.
Write genuinely different claims per persona — if two personas share a point, the section is decoration.
The control keeps its own scroll rail so long labels never widen the page at 360.

items.title: Credit Packs Pricing
items.tagline: The discount is checkable, not asserted.
items.description: Prepaid credits, with the per-credit rate computed rather than claimed: every pack prints what it actually works out to, so the discount is checkable instead of asserted. The seat counter prices people and the usage dial prices continuous volume — this is for products metered in discrete work.

props.name: packs
props.description: Credits and price per pack; the rate is derived, never authored.

props.name: unitLine / terms
props.description: What a credit buys, and what makes prepaid fair.

usageNotes: Never author the per-credit rate — it is computed, so a pack cannot quietly disagree with its own arithmetic.
Say what one credit buys in the same breath, or the numbers mean nothing.
Expiry is the whole trust question for prepaid: answer it in the terms row.

items.title: Where It Goes Pricing
items.tagline: Show the split, don't defend the number.
items.description: Not a plan chooser — a justification: where the price actually goes, one bar per line, adding to the whole. A page that only states a number invites the reader to guess what it pays for, and buyers who feel overcharged usually just mean uninformed.

props.name: slices
props.description: Each line's declared share and what it covers.

props.name: price / period
props.description: The number being accounted for.

usageNotes: Shares are declared once; bar width and printed percentage both derive from them, so the section cannot disagree with itself.
Pair it with a pricing section that actually sells — this one explains, it does not close.
Own the rounding in the footnote rather than fudging the shares to hit a hundred.

items.title: Book a Slot CTA
items.tagline: Picking a time is smaller than starting a negotiation.
items.description: The close as a specific time: real slots on real days, taken ones visibly spent, and the promise of what the half hour actually contains printed beside them. A "book a demo" button asks the visitor to start a negotiation; a grid of times asks them to pick one, which is a far smaller thing to agree to.

props.name: days
props.description: Pre-formatted day labels and their slots; taken ones strike through.

props.name: promise
props.description: What the half hour contains — the reason to pick at all.

usageNotes: Labels are pre-formatted strings on purpose: the section never touches a clock, so it can never disagree with the server about today.
Leave some slots taken. A grid where everything is free reads as a grid nobody booked.
The promise list does the persuading; the times only lower the cost of saying yes.

items.title: Last Objection CTA
items.tagline: Say the doubt out loud, then answer it.
items.description: The close that names the reason the reader has not acted, and answers it in their own words. By this point the argument is made and the only thing left is doubt — so the section says the doubts out loud, including the one about leaving. Answering the exit question honestly is what makes the other answers believable.

props.name: objections
props.description: The doubt in the reader's voice, and the answer.

props.name: cta / altLabel
props.description: The action and the softer path.

usageNotes: Write doubts in the reader's voice, not a strawman you enjoy knocking down.
Always include the exit question; it is what makes the other three credible.
Four is the ceiling — past that it reads as a page arguing with itself.

items.title: Rank Race Stats
items.tagline: Who overtook whom.
items.description: Standings that re-rank in front of you: pick a year and the bars re-order themselves, so the story is the movement rather than the values. The band and the dial both answer "how much"; this one answers "who overtook whom", which is the only question a ranked list is actually good at.

props.name: periods
props.description: Each period's standings and the line saying what changed.

props.name: unit
props.description: Trailing unit on each bar's readout.

usageNotes: Re-ranking, bar travel, and the trailing readouts all belong to bar-race — the section only swaps the standings.
Keep item ids stable across periods or nothing can be seen to overtake anything.
Every period needs its note; a re-rank the reader has to interpret alone is a chart, not a claim.

items.title: Ring Set Stats
items.tagline: Comparable at a glance, defined in plain words.
items.description: Four proportions on one scale, read as wedges rather than numerals: the radial set makes shares comparable at a glance in a way four separate percentages never are, and every wedge carries a plain sentence saying what it counts. It wants values with real spread — four numbers inside a twenty point band are indistinguishable as wedges.

props.name: data / max
props.description: The wedges and the value that reaches the outer radius.

props.name: notes
props.description: One plain sentence per wedge saying what it counts.
